Public lobby separated from bays and quarters, with crew areas controlled so visitors never pass through operational spaces.

questions.explanation: Even community-friendly facilities zone public, operational, and living spaces; openness is offered at the lobby, not through the whole building.

questions.question: A client asks whether monitoring operators should ever silence a repeatedly alarming point without a service ticket. What is the correct policy?

answers.text: Yes, whenever the point alarms three times in a shift
No; silencing requires a documented bypass with authorization, a service ticket, and a restoration check, so the point cannot be forgotten.
Only senior operators may silence points informally
Yes, if the operator notes it in a personal notebook

questions.explanation: Informal silencing is how protected points vanish; every bypass is authorized, ticketed, and restored on record.

questions.question: A consulting firm wants one global information policy, but a client's contract imposes stricter handling for that client's data than the firm's standard. How should the procedure handle it?

answers.text: Staff may choose whichever rule set they prefer per task
The client must adopt the firm's standard to do business
The firm's standard overrides client contracts for consistency
Client-specific requirements layer on top of the firm standard for that engagement: staff follow the stricter applicable rule, and the engagement record states which rules govern

questions.explanation: The governing rule for any item of information is the strictest that legitimately applies to it. Procedures must make layered obligations explicit, or staff will default to the familiar standard.

questions.question: A security manager is preparing a survey plan for a multi-site retailer. Which element most improves the survey's credibility with executives?

answers.text: Promise that the survey will produce no findings for cooperative departments
Agree on the criteria and evidence standards in advance, and tie every finding to a business asset and a potential business consequence
Express every finding as a technology purchase recommendation
Keep the criteria confidential so departments cannot prepare

questions.explanation: Pre-agreed criteria and business-framed findings make results hard to dismiss as opinion. Executives act on exposures stated in terms of assets and consequences they own.

questions.question: A security manager reports that phishing-report rates rose 40% after an awareness campaign, and a vice president calls the campaign a failure because 'incidents went up.' What is the correct interpretation?

answers.text: More phishing emails are arriving because of the campaign
Employees are reporting to avoid doing real work

Rising reports usually signal success: employees are recognizing and reporting attempts they previously clicked or ignored, and the measure that matters — successful compromises — should be tracked alongside
The campaign should be cancelled to restore lower numbers

questions.explanation: Program metrics need interpretation. A reporting rate measures vigilance, not attack volume; judging awareness work by it inverts the incentive the program wants.

garp-scr-sustainability-and-climate-risk.quiz_title: GARP Sustainability and Climate Risk (SCR) Certificate Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: What is the role of energy efficiency in the renewable transition?

answers.text: It increases total energy demand so more renewables must be built
It is unrelated, because transition policy concerns only power generation
It reduces the amount of energy services require, lowering the scale, cost, and speed of clean supply that must be built to replace fossil fuels
It works only for fossil systems and has no effect alongside renewables

questions.explanation: Efficiency shrinks the demand that clean supply must meet, making the transition faster and cheaper. It lowers rather than raises demand, applies across the whole energy system including buildings and industry, and works alongside renewables.

questions.question: A logistics firm emits 200,000 tonnes of CO2e per year. A verified efficiency and fleet program cuts emissions by 15%. How large is the annual mitigation achieved?

answers.text: 30,000 tonnes of CO2e per year
15,000 tonnes of CO2e per year
185,000 tonnes of CO2e per year
300,000 tonnes of CO2e per year

questions.explanation: Mitigation achieved is 200,000 x 15% = 30,000 tonnes per year. The 185,000 figure is the emissions remaining after the cut, not the reduction. 15,000 uses 7.5% and 300,000 misapplies the percentage to a larger base.

questions.question: A bank wants to identify where its lending has the most significant sustainability impact. Which approach is most consistent with the Principles for Responsible Banking?

answers.text: Analyze the portfolio by sector, geography, and client type to find its most significant impact areas, positive and negative
Focus only on the bank's office energy use because it is easiest to measure
Assume the largest loans automatically have the most significant sustainability impact
Ask each branch to choose an impact area without any portfolio analysis

questions.explanation: A is correct: impact analysis under the Principles looks across the portfolio, considering sectors, geographies, and technologies, to locate the most significant impacts. B addresses only operational footprint, which is usually minor for a bank compared with financed impacts. C confuses loan size with impact significance. D lacks the systematic assessment the framework expects.

questions.question: The first PRI principle commits signatories to which action?

answers.text: Divest from any company with an unresolved ESG controversy within one year
Incorporate ESG issues into investment analysis and decision-making processes
Publish the personal holdings of all portfolio managers
Vote against every management proposal at annual meetings

questions.explanation: B is correct: Principle 1 is incorporating ESG issues into investment analysis and decision-making. A describes a mandatory divestment rule the PRI does not impose. C is not part of the principles. D misstates active ownership; voting is meant to be informed and purposeful, not automatically oppositional.

questions.question: A coal-mining borrower, invented as Blackseam Resources, earns $80 million in revenue. A new carbon charge adds costs equal to 15% of revenue, with no ability to pass costs to customers. What is the annual cost increase?

answers.text: $12 million, from 0.15 multiplied by $80 million
$15 million, from using the percentage as a dollar figure
$5.33 million, from dividing $80 million by 15
$68 million, from subtracting 15 from 80

questions.explanation: Cost increase = 15% x $80m = 0.15 x 80 = $12m. B mistakes the rate for dollars, C divides instead of multiplying by the rate, and D subtracts unlike units (a percentage from dollars).

questions.question: How does transition risk most directly become credit risk for a bank?

answers.text: Borrowers' cash flows and collateral values fall, raising default probability and loss if default occurs
Borrowers demand longer branch opening hours
The bank's own office buildings use more air conditioning
Depositors ask for statements in a different language

questions.explanation: Transition raises borrowers' costs or cuts revenues and can devalue collateral, so defaults become more likely and recoveries smaller: that is credit risk. B and D are service preferences, and C is an operating cost, not the borrower transmission channel.

questions.question: A clothing brand's factories are run by independent suppliers. Why are the suppliers' factory emissions not the brand's Scope 1?

answers.text: Because clothing production creates no emissions
Because Scope 1 requires sources owned or controlled by the reporting company, and independent supplier factories do not meet that test
Because only energy companies report Scope 1
Because emissions in other countries are never counted

questions.explanation: Scope 1 is limited to owned or controlled sources; independent supplier operations are value-chain sources, typically Scope 3 for the brand. Geography and sector do not remove Scope 1 obligations for a company's own sources.

questions.question: A company owns 40% of a joint venture and has no control over it. Under the equity share approach, how are the venture's emissions treated?

answers.text: Excluded entirely because the company lacks control
Accounted for in proportion to the 40% economic interest
Accounted for at 100% because any ownership triggers full consolidation
Reported only as a memo item outside the inventory total

questions.explanation: Equity share consolidation reflects economic interest, so a 40% holding accounts for 40% of the venture's emissions. Exclusion or memo-only treatment understates that share, and 100% consolidation would overstate it because equity share follows ownership proportion, not control.

questions.question: Socioeconomic advancement and empowerment as a social category could support:

answers.text: Programmes expanding access to finance for women-owned small businesses
Speculative derivatives trading by a proprietary desk
Executive share-option schemes only
General refinancing of unrelated corporate debt

questions.explanation: Expanding equitable access and opportunity, such as finance for underserved entrepreneurs, fits socioeconomic advancement. Proprietary trading and executive schemes do not serve a target population.

questions.question: A lender shortens loan maturities and adds climate covenants for borrowers in rapidly changing sectors. As risk management, this primarily:

answers.text: Adjusts credit terms to limit exposure as transition risk evolves
Eliminates the need to monitor borrowers
Guarantees borrowers will transition successfully
Converts credit risk into underwriting risk

questions.explanation: A is correct: maturity and covenant design are credit controls matched to evolving risk. B and C overclaim, and D mislabels the risk type.

questions.question: An insurer asks what loss level has a 1% annual probability of being exceeded. In catastrophe modelling this is best read from:

answers.text: The average of the five largest historical claims
The median premium income across the portfolio
The exceedance probability curve built from the simulated event set
The most recent year's underwriting result

questions.explanation: The exceedance probability curve, derived from the stochastic event catalogue, gives loss levels at specified annual probabilities such as 1%. Historical averages and recent results are backward-looking samples and cannot support that probability statement.

questions.question: Which is an upstream Scope 3 category in concept?

answers.text: Purchased goods and services bought by the reporting company
Use of products the company sells
End-of-life treatment of sold products
Investments made by the company

questions.explanation: Purchased goods and services are upstream. Use of sold products, end-of-life treatment and investments are downstream categories.

frm-part-ii.quiz_title: FRM Part II (Financial Risk Manager) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A risk manager backtests using hypothetical (clean) P&L rather than actual P&L primarily to:

answers.text: Guarantee fewer exceptions will be counted
Isolate the market-risk model by removing fees, commissions and intraday trading effects
Avoid ever placing the model in the yellow zone
Replace the need for independence testing

questions.explanation: Actual P&L contains non-market elements that the VaR model was never designed to predict. Hypothetical P&L revalues the fixed portfolio with realised market moves, giving a cleaner test of the risk model itself.

questions.question: For a portfolio, the worst five losses out of 100 days are $120,000, $100,000, $90,000, $80,000 and $60,000. What is the expected shortfall at the 95% level?
questions.explanation: Expected shortfall is the average loss in the tail beyond VaR, not the worst loss alone. Averaging the stated tail losses (summing them and dividing by the number of tail losses) gives $90,000.

questions.question: Exogenous liquidity-adjusted value-at-risk adjusts ordinary value-at-risk by adding what?

answers.text: A fixed percentage set by the trader's judgement
The expected cost of unwinding the position, commonly half the bid-ask spread multiplied by the position size
The full bid-ask spread multiplied by twice the position size
Only the funding cost of the position

questions.explanation: Exogenous LVaR assumes the trader pays half the spread to exit at the bid against a mid-price value-at-risk: the add-on is 0.5 x spread x position size, with the spread treated as given by the market.

questions.question: A desk's standardised charges are: sensitivities-based charge $30 million, default risk charge $8 million and residual risk add-on $2 million. What is its total standardised capital before any other adjustments?

answers.text: $40 million
$240 million
$30 million
$38 million

questions.explanation: The standardised components add: $30 million + $8 million + $2 million = $40 million. The components are summed, not multiplied.

questions.question: Which statement about historical simulation VaR at the 99% level using 200 days of data is most accurate?

answers.text: It is based on 99 tail observations, so it is very precise
It cannot be computed with fewer than 1,000 observations
Its precision is unaffected by the number of tail observations
It is based on only about two tail observations, so it is imprecisely estimated

questions.explanation: At 99% confidence with 200 observations, only about 1% x 200 = 2 observations lie in the tail beyond VaR. Estimates resting on so few points have high sampling uncertainty, a limitation of historical methods in the far tail.

questions.question: The second and third principal components of yield curve moves are conventionally interpreted as what?

answers.text: Level and volatility
Slope, a steepening or flattening twist, and curvature, a change in the bend of the middle of the curve relative to its ends
Short-rate mean reversion and long-rate volatility
Credit spread and liquidity

questions.explanation: After level, slope captures differential moves between long and short ends, and curvature captures the middle of the curve moving relative to both ends; together the three explain the great majority of curve variance.

questions.question: When would a risk manager prefer full revaluation over mapping for an options book?

answers.text: When the book contains only linear forwards
When no volatility data are available at all
When payoffs are highly nonlinear and trade-level accuracy in the tail matters more than speed
When the horizon is a single day and options are deep in the money with negligible gamma

questions.explanation: Mapping linearises options and can badly miss tail payoffs where curvature dominates. Full revaluation reprices each option under each scenario, capturing gamma and vega effects at greater computational cost.

questions.question: A counterparty posts shares in its own corporate group as collateral. Why is this weak protection?

answers.text: Own-group shares always rise in value when the issuer is in distress
The collateral's value is likely to fall exactly when the counterparty weakens, so it provides least protection when it is most needed
Shares are never eligible as collateral under any agreement
The shares will be too liquid and will be sold too quickly on default

questions.explanation: Collateral correlated with the counterparty is a form of wrong-way collateral: default risk and collateral value move adversely together, undermining the mitigation.

questions.question: Harborline Bank holds a stressed liquidity buffer of $160 million and expects a net stressed outflow of $15 million per week with no inflows. For how many full weeks does the buffer last?

answers.text: 160 weeks
15 weeks
10 weeks
12 weeks

questions.explanation: Survival weeks = buffer / weekly net outflow = 160 / 15 = 10 full weeks. This simple survival horizon shows how long positive resources last under sustained stress.

questions.question: What horizon and minimum define the Net Stable Funding Ratio for Union Trust?

answers.text: A five-year horizon, with a minimum of 75%
A stressed 30-day horizon, with a minimum of 100%
A one-year horizon, with available stable funding at least 100% of required stable funding
A one-week horizon, with a minimum of 150%

questions.explanation: The NSFR is a one-year structural measure: ASF must be at least 100% of RSF. The stressed 30-day horizon defines the LCR instead.

questions.question: A portfolio returns 14% with a risk-free rate of 3% and volatility of 11%. What is its Sharpe ratio?
questions.explanation: Sharpe ratio equals excess return divided by total volatility: (14% − 3%) / 11% = 1.00. It measures return per unit of total risk, using volatility — not beta — in the denominator.

questions.question: Diversification benefit at portfolio level is best illustrated by:

answers.text: Portfolio volatility always equalling the weighted average of asset volatilities
Every asset's risk falling when it is added to a portfolio
Correlations rising toward one in a crisis
Portfolio expected shortfall being no greater than the sum of component expected shortfalls, with strict benefit when risks are not perfectly dependent

questions.explanation: Risk measures such as expected shortfall are subadditive: the portfolio figure is at most the sum of the parts. The gap between the two is the diversification benefit, which shrinks when dependence rises in stress.

frm-part-i.quiz_title: FRM Part I (Financial Risk Manager) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: In CAPM, the market portfolio is best described as:

answers.text: A portfolio containing only the largest listed stocks
An equally weighted portfolio of all stocks
A portfolio containing only domestic equities and bonds
A portfolio containing all risky assets in proportion to their market values

questions.explanation: The theoretical market portfolio includes all risky assets, weighted by market value, so that aggregate supply equals demand.

questions.question: A portfolio return is normal with mean 10% and SD 5%. Given P(Z < -2.0) = 0.0228, what is the probability the return is below 0%?
Spread widening on a corporate bond, with Treasury yields unchanged, means:

answers.text: Its price rises because investors value it more
Its coupon automatically increases
It becomes a Treasury security
Its price falls and its yield rises relative to Treasuries, reflecting higher perceived credit or liquidity risk

questions.explanation: Credit spread is the extra yield over the risk-free benchmark; widening signals the market demands more compensation, pushing price down. The contractual coupon does not change.

questions.question: Cross hedging means:

answers.text: Hedging the same asset with the identical futures contract
Using two futures contracts on the same asset at once
Avoiding hedging altogether
Hedging an exposure with a futures contract on a related but different underlying asset

questions.explanation: Example: hedging jet fuel with heating-oil futures. Cross hedging can be effective if prices are correlated, but it adds basis risk.

questions.question: Company A can borrow fixed at 10.0% or floating at benchmark + 1.0%. Company B can borrow fixed at 12.0% or floating at benchmark + 0.5%. A wants floating and B wants fixed. What is the total quality-spread gain available to share in a swap?

answers.text: 4.0%, because all four rates are added together
1.5%, because the fixed-market difference is 2.0% (12.0 − 10.0) while the floating-market difference is only 0.5% (1.0 − 0.5 in spread terms), and 2.0 − 0.5 = 1.5%
0.5%, because only the floating difference matters
2.0%, because only the fixed difference matters

questions.explanation: Quality spread differential = difference in fixed rates − difference in floating spreads = (12.0% − 10.0%) − (1.0% − 0.5%) = 2.0% − 0.5% = 1.5%. This is the pool a swap/intermediary can split so both end up better than borrowing directly in their desired markets.

questions.question: A cleared position was valued at $2000 at yesterday's settlement and at $1850 at today's settlement, from the long holder's perspective. What variation margin does the holder experience?

answers.text: Pays the full ending value as variation margin
Receives initial margin back in full each day
Pays $150, because the position lost $150 on the day's mark to market
Variation margin is only exchanged at contract maturity

questions.explanation: Variation margin settles the daily loss: starting value $2000 falls to $1850, a loss of $2000 − $1850 = $150, which the holder pays in cash that day.

questions.question: Put-call parity with known dividends D (present value) on a European option pair is written as:

answers.text: c + K e^{-rT} + PV(D) = p + S0, equivalently using S0 - PV(D) in place of S0
c + K = p + S0 + PV(D) with no discounting
c = p + K e^{-rT} regardless of spot
p + K e^{-rT} = c + S0 + PV(D)

questions.explanation: Dividends reduce the forward value of the stock to holders who do not receive them, so parity replaces S0 with S0 minus the present value of dividends. Rearranged, c + K e^{-rT} + PV(D) = p + S0.

questions.question: In a one-step binomial model, the stock can rise by factor u = 1.10 or fall by factor d = 0.90, and e^(r*dt) = 1.0513 (r = 5% for one period). What is the risk-neutral probability of an up move?
questions.explanation: Risk-neutral probability p = (e^(r*dt) - d)/(u - d) = (1.0513 - 0.90)/(1.10 - 0.90) = 0.1513/0.20 = 0.7565. Inverting the formula or using 1 - p gives the distractors.

questions.question: As a bond's yield to maturity falls, holding its cash flows fixed, what happens to its price?

answers.text: Its price falls to par
Its price falls
Its price rises
Its price is unchanged

questions.explanation: A lower discount rate raises the present value of each fixed coupon and principal payment. Hence bond prices move inversely to yields.

questions.question: A bond has modified duration 4.50 and convexity 70. Yields change by +2.00 percentage points. What is the approximate percentage price change including convexity?
questions.explanation: Change = -D_mod x dy + 0.5 x Convexity x dy^2 = -4.50 x (+0.0200) + 0.5 x 70 x (0.0200)^2 = -7.60%. Omitting the one-half convexity term or the convexity term entirely gives the distractors.

questions.question: A bond has a Macaulay duration of 5.20 years and a yield of 6%. What is its modified duration?

answers.text: 5.20 years
4.91 years
4.51 years
5.51 years

questions.explanation: Modified duration = Macaulay / (1+y) = 5.20 / 1.06 = 4.91 years. Using Macaulay directly would overstate price sensitivity.

questions.question: Why does square-root-of-time scaling become unreliable when returns are autocorrelated or volatility clusters?

answers.text: It assumes independent and identically distributed returns, so dependent returns scale differently
Volatility clustering removes all tail risk
Scaling always works regardless of dependence
Autocorrelation makes multi-day VaR smaller than one-day VaR

questions.explanation: The sqrt(t) rule follows from variances adding under independence; autocorrelation and clustered volatility break that additivity, so scaled VaR can materially misstate multi-day risk.

api-936-refractory-personnel.quiz_title: API 936 Refractory Personnel Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Why would an inspector distinguish a witness point from a hold point?

answers.text: The two terms are interchangeable and either one always stops all work
At a witness point work may proceed if the inspector is properly notified and does not attend, while at a hold point work must stop until the inspector releases it
A witness point applies only to laboratory tests, while a hold point applies only to field work
A witness point is set by the applicator, while a hold point is set only after work is complete

questions.explanation: The distinction controls whether production may continue: hold points are mandatory stops, witness points are notified opportunities to observe. The strongest distractor, that the terms are interchangeable, would erase a control the inspection plan deliberately grades by importance.

questions.question: How does the manufacturer support material qualification testing?

answers.text: By waiving all testing if the product was used before
By accepting the finished lining on behalf of the owner
By witnessing every production hold point in place of the inspector
By supplying material, product data, and technical information needed for qualification

questions.explanation: The manufacturer supports qualification by furnishing material and technical data. Prior use does not waive qualification when the program requires it, and the manufacturer does not replace the inspector or owner in acceptance.

questions.question: What is the correct response when a delivery's paperwork and physical labels disagree on the product designation?

answers.text: Trust the paperwork because it was prepared in an office
Trust the labels because they are attached to the material
Install the material under whichever designation suits the schedule
Hold the delivery and resolve the discrepancy with the supplier; neither source may be assumed correct until they are reconciled

questions.explanation: A disagreement means identity is unproven from both directions. Choosing the convenient designation, from either source, builds an unverified material into a lining and falsifies its records.

questions.question: A data sheet is missing for a delivered specialty castable, but the crew knows the product name. What is the quality-correct position?

answers.text: Proceed on the crew's general experience with castables
Use the data sheet of the most similar product on site
Properties do not matter as long as the product name matches the order
Obtain the manufacturer's data sheet for that product before relying on its properties or installation requirements

questions.explanation: The data sheet carries the specific water, placement, and property information for that formulation. General experience and a neighbor product's sheet are substitutes in name only.

questions.question: A plastic refractory workability check is performed hours after the sample was taken, during which the sample sat exposed and stiffened. The index comes back low. What must be considered before concluding the delivered material is unworkable?

answers.text: Workability never changes after sampling
The low value proves the entire shipment should be returned
The delay and exposure themselves reduce workability, so the test condition — not just the material — may explain the low index
Exposed samples should be re-wetted until they feel right and then tested

questions.explanation: Workability is time- and exposure-sensitive, so a stale, exposed sample can understate the delivered material, making C correct. B is the strongest distractor because a low index is a genuine warning, but disposition requires a test that fairly represents the material as delivered.

questions.question: After firing, a test bar originally 240.0 mm long measures 237.6 mm. A trainee asks what the calculated change of -1.0% means for lining design. Which interpretation should the inspector give?

answers.text: The material gained volume during firing and will tighten every joint
The value is a strength loss of 1.0% and can be ignored
The material shrank permanently on heating, so expansion allowances and joint design must account for that contraction
The value proves the material was under-fired and must be discarded

questions.explanation: A length change from 240.0 mm to 237.6 mm is -1.0%, a permanent shrinkage on heating, so joints and allowances must reflect contraction, making C correct. D is the strongest distractor because shrinkage can accompany firing changes, but a single permanent linear change value does not by itself prove under-firing or require discard.

questions.question: On a lining drawing, what can anchor symbols and notes tell an installer?

answers.text: Anchor type, location or pattern, and installation details intended for each area
Only the name of the company that drew the drawing
The operating temperature of a different unit
Nothing, because anchors are decided entirely in the field

questions.explanation: Drawing symbols and notes communicate type, pattern, and details by area. Field improvisation does not replace the drawing, which is the design record.

questions.question: Why can a single failed anchor area lead to loss of a larger lining section than the area itself?

answers.text: Lining sections are completely independent at every point
Adjacent lining is held only by the failed patch's colour
Lining sections depend on the support around them, so losing retention in one area can undermine adjacent material
Damage spread is impossible in refractory linings

questions.explanation: Sections interact; loss of support and exposure at an edge undermines neighbours. Linings are continuous systems, not fully independent tiles at every point.

questions.question: How should a change to a different fiber product mid-job be treated?

answers.text: As a non-event, because all fibers are interchangeable
As an opportunity to use up old stock in any proportion
Fiber changes never need documentation
As a material change requiring verification that the new fiber matches the specified type and addition for the design

questions.explanation: Fiber type and amount are design inputs, so substitution without verification can silently change lining performance. The strongest distractor, universal interchangeability, ignores that fiber alloys and forms differ in temperature capability and reinforcing behavior.

questions.question: When mixing a castable, what governs how much water should be added?

answers.text: The manufacturer's data sheet for that specific material
The installer's past habit with a different castable
The amount that makes the mix easiest to place
A single water amount used for all castables on the job

questions.explanation: The data sheet governs because each castable is formulated with its own water demand for its intended properties. The strongest distractor, using the amount that makes placement easiest, is wrong because ease of placement bought with extra water sacrifices the properties the data sheet water range is designed to protect.

questions.question: What role does trending nonconformances play during work on an FCC unit riser?

answers.text: Tracking types and frequency reveals developing systemic problems early enough to correct the process
Trends matter only after the job ends
Individual reports contain all needed information with no pattern view
Trending is only a final-report statistic

questions.explanation: Pattern visibility during the job allows intervention before a defect multiplies across the unit. The strongest distractor — "Trending is only a final-report statistic" — is wrong because waiting until the job ends forfeits the chance to stop a growing defect.

questions.question: Which combination best reflects the practical inspection approach for a monolithic lining in a rotary kiln section?

answers.text: Destructive removal of representative halves of the lining
Radiography alone with no visual examination
No inspection if the material was qualified
Visual examination as the primary method, supplemented by sounding, thickness checks, and coring where required

questions.explanation: Practical refractory inspection layers complementary surface, sounding, dimensional, and sampling methods. The strongest distractor — "Radiography alone with no visual examination" — is wrong because qualification does not eliminate the need to inspect the actual installation.

api-653-tank-inspector.quiz_title: API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Pits in Tank 1806 intersect a straight line within an 8 in. (200 mm) length with individual pit lengths of 0.55 in., 0.50 in., 0.45 in., 0.60 in. The acceptance limit for the summed pit length in any 8 in. is 2.00 in. What is the determination?

answers.text: Acceptable — summed length 2.10 in. is within the 2.00 in. limit
Acceptable — summed length 0.55 in. (largest pit only) is within the limit
Not acceptable — summed length 2.10 in. exceeds an 8.00 in. limit
Not acceptable — summed length 2.10 in. exceeds the 2.00 in. limit

questions.explanation: Add the pit lengths lying within the 8 in. (200 mm) length: 0.55 + 0.50 + 0.45 + 0.60 = 2.10 in. Compare with the 2.00 in. limit: 2.10 > 2.00 in. by 0.10 in., so the pitting pattern fails this summed-length criterion. Counting only the largest pit would incorrectly pass it.

questions.question: A tank in water service has a upper shell course with an actual thickness of 0.43 in., a required minimum thickness of 0.25 in., and a corrosion rate of 0.009 in./yr. What is the remaining life of this course?

answers.text: 20.0 years
10.0 years
40.0 years
0.0 years

questions.explanation: Remaining life = (actual thickness - minimum thickness) / corrosion rate = (0.43 - 0.25) in. / 0.009 in./yr = 0.18 in. / 0.009 in./yr = 20.0 years.

questions.question: Tank 510 (diameter 130 ft) stores gasoline (specific gravity 0.74) to a liquid height H = 42 ft in the course being evaluated. Allowable stress S = 25,000 psi and joint efficiency E = 0.90. What is the minimum required shell thickness t-min for this existing tank course?
questions.explanation: Use t-min = 2.6·D·(H-1)·G / (S·E). Substitute: t-min = 2.6 × 130 × (42-1) × 0.74 / (25,000 × 0.90) = 2.6 × 130 × 41 × 0.74 / 22,500 = 10254.9 / 22,500 = 0.4558 in., about 0.456 in. Using H without subtracting 1 ft, or dropping E, is a wrong-method result.

questions.question: How many tension tests are normally taken from a single groove-weld PQR test coupon for plate qualification?

answers.text: Four tension specimens and no bend specimens
One tension specimen only, with no bend specimens required
Tension specimens are optional when bend tests are performed
Two reduced-section tension specimens, together with the required bend specimens, from the coupon layout

questions.explanation: Two reduced-section tension specimens, together with the required bend specimens, from the coupon layout. Tension and bend testing together prove the procedure: bends show soundness and ductility, tension shows joint strength. The strongest alternative fails because it either substitutes a different property (such as toughness or hardness), waives a required test, or treats a strength failure as curable by an unrelated passing test — none of which Section IX permits.

questions.question: Mechanical results for a shell-plate procedure coupon include a tension specimen that parted in the base metal, clear of the weld, at a strength 8 percent below the specified minimum tensile strength of that base metal. The fabricator argues the result should be credited because the weld itself never broke. What is the correct disposition?

answers.text: Credit the specimen, since a break outside the weld can never fail a qualification

Fail the specimen — a base-metal break is credited only when its strength falls no more than 5 percent below the base metal's specified minimum, and at 8 percent below, this result does not meet the acceptance basis
Credit the specimen if the companion bend specimens all passed
Average this result with the second tension specimen and credit the coupon if the average clears the minimum

questions.explanation: The base-metal break allowance is narrow: when a tension specimen breaks in the base metal, the result is acceptable only if the strength is not more than 5 percent below the base metal's specified minimum. Eight percent below exceeds that allowance, so the specimen fails on its own numbers. The strongest distractor claims a break outside the weld can never fail, which ignores the 5 percent ceiling written into the allowance, and passing bends cannot rescue a failed tension result.

questions.question: What does backscatter protection and its check image confirm on a tank radiograph?

answers.text: That density is correct
That the IQI is correct
That backscatter is not degrading the image, shown by the lead letter image characteristics
That the film is expired

questions.explanation: A lead letter behind the film reveals whether backscatter is fogging the image and reducing quality.

questions.question: An inspector sets the next internal date using remaining life but does not apply any maximum-interval cap. Why is that incomplete?

answers.text: Even when remaining life is long, the code caps the interval, so the next date is the earlier of the rate-based result and the maximum allowed
Caps apply only to external inspections
Long remaining life allows any interval the inspector chooses
The cap is whichever date operations prefer

questions.explanation: Rate-based timing and the maximum cap work together; the earlier governs. Choosing a preferred date beyond the cap breaks the interval system even with a healthy tank.

questions.question: A hot tap has been cut successfully and the new branch is in service. What completion steps close out the work properly?

answers.text: Remove the tapping machine and leave the valve as the only record of the job
Account for the cut coupon, examine the fitting welds, leave the connection in its designed valved configuration, and record the tap in the tank's file
Weld the valve permanently shut so the branch cannot be disturbed
Skip weld examination because the branch is not leaking at start-up

questions.explanation: A hot tap ends as ordinary pressure-boundary work: its welds examined, its coupon accounted for so none is loose in the tank, its final configuration as designed, and its existence documented for the next inspector. The strongest distractor — 'Skip weld examination because the branch is not leaking at start-up' — fails because absence of a leak at start-up does not prove the fitting welds are sound; they are pressure-boundary welds made on a live shell and need their own examination.

questions.question: Why should the inspector note standing water on a tank bottom during internal inspection after cleaning?

answers.text: Low spots holding water indicate bottom slope/dishing and future corrosion sites, and reveal leak paths
Water on the bottom after cleaning proves the bottom is new
Standing water location is meaningless
It shows the tank was overfilled

questions.explanation: Low spots holding water indicate bottom slope/dishing and future corrosion sites, and reveal leak paths — this is correct because water pooling maps bottom contour and corrosion risk areas. The strongest alternative, 'Water on the bottom after cleaning proves the bottom is new', loses because meaningless loses because pooling locates low, corrosion-prone areas.

questions.question: Lack of fusion at the groove sidewall most directly results from which condition?

answers.text: Too much melting of the sidewall
Arc energy or manipulation that never melted the sidewall surface
Excessive root penetration
A weld pool that was too fluid and wide

questions.explanation: Sidewall fusion requires the arc to actually melt that face; insufficient energy or poor aim leaves it unfused. The strongest alternative — Too much melting of the sidewall — loses because excessive melting would fuse the wall; the defect is defined by melting that did not occur.

questions.question: In an impressed-current installation, the anodes differ from galvanic anodes mainly in that they are intended to do what?

answers.text: Be consumed rapidly to generate the system's current
Distribute current driven by the power source while being consumed very slowly, rather than serving as the current's source themselves
Dissolve into the soil to neutralize its salts
Serve as permanent reference electrodes for all surveys

questions.explanation: The key is right because impressed-current anodes are current distributors chosen for low consumption under driven current. The rapid-consumption distractor loses because that describes sacrificial anodes, the defining component of the other system type.

questions.question: Confined-space and ventilation controls during lining application inside a tank are critical chiefly because of what hazard combination?

answers.text: The lining cures too fast in open air, so the tank must stay sealed
Ventilation interferes with the lining, so it should be avoided entirely
The only hazard is noise from the ventilation fans
Solvent vapors that are both toxic and flammable can accumulate in the enclosed bottom area, endangering workers and creating an ignition risk

questions.explanation: The key is right because solvent-bearing coatings in a confined space create simultaneous health and fire hazards that ventilation and entry controls manage. The avoid-ventilation distractor loses because withholding ventilation lets vapors accumulate toward dangerous concentrations.

api-580-risk-based-inspection.quiz_title: API 580 Risk-Based Inspection Professional Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Absolute risk refers to what?

answers.text: How an item's risk compares with the risk of other items in the same study
A guarantee that no failure can occur during the interval
The actual estimated level of risk for an item, expressed on its own scale, such as expected impact per year
The risk remaining after all inspection is complete

questions.explanation: Absolute risk states the item's own risk magnitude, which can be compared with risk criteria. Relative comparison is the strongest distractor, but that is the definition of relative risk, not absolute risk.

questions.question: A seawater-cooled condenser in coastal service shows a low risk today, but the RBI team also expresses its risk as of the next turnaround five years away. Why calculate risk at that future date rather than only for today?

answers.text: To make the current risk appear larger so more inspection funding is approved
Because only the future risk value may be reported to management under an RBI program

Because active deterioration will increase the likelihood of failure over the interval, so the inspection decision must test whether risk will still meet the target before the next opportunity to inspect
Because current risk has no role in inspection planning once a future date has been chosen

questions.explanation: Risk is time-dependent when damage progresses, so an item acceptable today may exceed the risk target before the next turnaround, and the interval must be set against that future risk. Option A is the strongest distractor because the purpose is not to inflate a ranking for funding, but to avoid an interval during which undetected deterioration carries risk beyond what the organization accepts.

questions.question: What does screening mean in this context?

answers.text: It has eliminated risk from the low group permanently
It has finished the program's entire analytical work
It has screened the population; it has not completed a detailed risk analysis of the separated items
It has produced exact risk figures for every item

questions.explanation: Screening sorts for attention; detailed characterization of the flagged group is the next step, not the same step. Finished analytical work is wrong because flagged items still await the analysis screening pointed them to.

questions.question: Which option best describes scheduling and resourcing the assessment during planning in the context of API RP 580?

answers.text: Building a schedule with milestones, assigned responsibilities, and the resources the assessment requires
Announcing a completion date with no resource plan behind it
Scheduling analysis before any data collection time is allowed
Assuming team members can fit the work in without allocated time

questions.explanation: A credible plan includes timing and resourcing; RBI competes for scarce specialists whose time must be secured in advance. The strongest distractor, "Announcing a completion date with no resource plan behind it," is wrong: a date without resources is not a plan and predictably produces rushed analysis or missed scope.

questions.question: A team is reviewing RBI in relation to API 510, API 570, and API 653. Which statement captures its place in the framework correctly?

answers.text: A substitute code that overrides their requirements
A reporting format with no connection to inspection planning
A replacement that makes those inspection codes unnecessary
A supplement that helps prioritize and plan inspection work covered by those codes

questions.explanation: RBI supplements the in-service inspection codes by informing where and how inspection effort should be directed. In practice this is a foundational requirement, not an optional administrative task. The strongest distractor, "A replacement that makes those inspection codes unnecessary," is wrong: calling it a replacement is wrong; the codes still govern inspection practice, while RBI adds risk-based prioritization.

questions.question: A pressure excursion lasted only a few hours years ago. Why might the RBI team still want it documented?

answers.text: Because any excursion automatically requires retirement of the item
Short excursions can still cause damage or reveal operation beyond intended conditions that affects risk
Because excursions change the material of construction
Because only excursions lasting more than a week affect inspection planning

questions.explanation: Even brief operation outside intended conditions can initiate or accelerate damage and informs likelihood. Automatic retirement is not the consequence, which is why that stronger-sounding distractor overstates the response.

questions.question: An engineer proposes listing 'high pressure' as a damage mechanism for a vessel. What is the correct review response?

answers.text: Pressure is an operating condition and stress contributor to be considered in susceptibility, not itself a damage mechanism
Accept it, because pressure appears in the design documents
Accept it, because high pressure always causes cracking
Replace all other mechanisms with it for simplicity

questions.explanation: Conditions enable mechanisms; they are not mechanisms. Accepting it because it is in the design documents, the strongest distractor, would corrupt the mechanism list that probability assessment depends on.

questions.question: What assumption is embedded in carrying an old POF value forward unchanged for many years?

answers.text: That the item's damage state, progression, and service have all remained essentially as they were when the value was set — an assumption that becomes less safe with time
That POF values improve automatically with age
That the original team will always be available to explain the value
That consequence has also remained unchanged, which settles the matter

questions.explanation: Carrying a value forward silently asserts nothing relevant changed; over years of progression and possible service drift, that assertion needs evidence. Automatic improvement with age inverts the actual behavior of progressing damage and is the strongest distractor.

questions.question: At a corrosion rate of 0.008 inch per year, how much wall will a circuit lose over 6 years if the rate stays constant?

answers.text: 0.014 inch
0.48 inch
0.048 inch
1.33 inches

questions.explanation: Wall loss is rate multiplied by time: 0.008 x 6 = 0.048 inch. The 0.48-inch distractor is a decimal-place error from the same multiplication; checking the magnitude against the annual rate — six years at eight thousandths per year cannot approach half an inch — exposes it.

questions.question: Fire protection systems such as deluge are installed on a unit. In RBI terms, their credited benefit is mainly what?

answers.text: Preventing internal corrosion of the protected equipment
Lowering the fluid's inherent flammability to zero
Ensuring a leak will be detected before it starts
Limiting fire growth and equipment damage after ignition, thereby reducing consequence

questions.explanation: Fire protection limits escalation and damage after ignition, a consequence reduction. Preventing internal corrosion is the strongest distractor because deluge acts externally after an event, not on internal damage mechanisms.

questions.question: In a study-defined scoring exercise for the tank farm, an aboveground storage tank is given probability value 4 and consequence value 4. Using risk = probability × consequence with those given values, what is its risk value?
questions.explanation: Multiply the given values: 4 × 4 = 16. The strongest distractor, 8, adds the values, which is wrong because the stated relationship is a product, not a sum.

questions.question: What is the role of a turnaround in managing risk for a pressure vessel whose plan requires internal inspection?

answers.text: It automatically reduces the item's risk even if no planned work is done
It resets the item's probability category to the lowest value by definition
It provides the access opportunity at which the planned risk-reducing inspection or mitigation is executed
It replaces the need for a documented inspection plan

questions.explanation: A turnaround enables the planned work on the pressure vessel; risk is managed by the work performed, not by the calendar event itself. Automatic risk reduction is wrong because an opportunity unused leaves the item's condition and risk unchanged.

api-577-welding-inspection-and-metallurg.quiz_title: API 577 Welding Inspection and Metallurgy Professional Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A pipe is fixed with its axis vertical and cannot be rotated, so the circumferential groove weld is made in the horizontal plane around it. Which pipe position is this?

answers.text: 1G
2G, the position with the pipe axis vertical and the groove weld made horizontally on a fixed pipe
5G
6G

questions.explanation: For pipe, 2G means the pipe axis is vertical and the weld runs horizontally around the fixed pipe. In 5G the pipe axis is horizontal instead, which is the strongest distractor because both are fixed-pipe positions.

questions.question: In arc welding vocabulary, what is the electrode?

answers.text: The workpiece clamp that completes the circuit through the table only
Any wire stored in the shop for later use
The insulated holder the welder grips, never carrying current
The component that conducts welding current to establish the arc, which may also supply filler metal

questions.explanation: The electrode conducts current to the arc; in processes like SMAW and GMAW it is consumable and also supplies filler, while in GTAW the tungsten electrode is nonconsumable. The holder alone is not the electrode.

questions.question: Why can FCAW generally tolerate more wind than GMAW before porosity becomes a problem, even in its gas-shielded form?

answers.text: FCAW weld metal cannot absorb nitrogen or oxygen
Wind increases FCAW deposition so defects are buried harmlessly
The tubular wire is heavier, so the arc cannot be blown off course
The flux-generated gases and slag provide protection in addition to any external gas, so shielding does not depend on gas alone

questions.explanation: Redundant protection from the flux system makes FCAW less fragile in air movement than a process relying solely on a gas envelope. No weld metal is immune to atmospheric contamination, so limits still apply.

questions.question: A P-number change is proposed together with a thickness increase beyond the qualified range. How many qualification problems are present?

answers.text: Two independent essential problems, and qualification must resolve both before production
One, because the larger change absorbs the smaller
Two, but either one alone can be waived by the inspector
None, if they are made on the same day

questions.explanation: Essential exceedances do not merge or cancel. Each boundary crossed needs its own qualification resolution, and inspectors do not waive essential variables.

questions.question: During procedure qualification, what must be recorded on the Procedure Qualification Record regarding essential variables?

answers.text: Only the broad ranges the Welding Procedure Specification intends to allow in production
The actual values used when welding the test coupon
Only the nonessential variables, because essential variables are taken from the Welding Procedure Specification
The values planned for a future production weld rather than the coupon weld

questions.explanation: A PQR records what actually happened on the coupon. The WPS then states qualified ranges supported by those actual values.

questions.question: Radiography as a bend-test substitute has a notable process limitation. Which process application is excluded at framework level?

answers.text: SMAW cannot be radiographed under any circumstances
GTAW coupons dissolve under radiation
Short-circuiting transfer GMAW cannot be qualified by radiography in place of bends
No process has any limitation

questions.explanation: The code bars RT substitution for short-circuiting GMAW performance qualification because that transfer mode's characteristic lack-of-fusion risk is not reliably revealed the same way. Bends remain required there.

questions.question: Peyton's WPQ shows qualification with backing on plate in the flat and horizontal positions. A job needs vertical groove welds without backing. How many coverage gaps exist?

answers.text: None; any groove record covers all groove work
One: only the backing differs
Three: position, backing, and plate versus plate
Two: position and backing condition are both outside the record

questions.explanation: Both vertical position and no-backing condition exceed the tested variables. Counting the gaps correctly is the first step to planning the needed test.

questions.question: An image quality indicator cannot be seen clearly on a radiograph that otherwise shows the weld. What does that mean for the examination?

answers.text: The weld is automatically acceptable because the weld area is visible
The indicator is optional decoration with no role
The required sensitivity has not been demonstrated, so the radiograph does not meet the technique requirement and generally must be redone
The flaws present are all acceptable by default

questions.explanation: Without the required IQI image, technique quality is unproven and the exposure is not acceptable as an examination record. Visibility of the weld alone is not enough.

questions.question: Two plates of noticeably different thickness are butt welded without the transition the drawing requires. Why does the inspector flag the fit-up?

answers.text: The abrupt thickness change concentrates stress and offsets the joint, harming alignment and load path
Different thicknesses can never be welded together under any design
The thinner plate will always melt away completely during welding
Thickness differences only affect the weight of the finished part

questions.explanation: An unplanned abrupt transition creates misalignment and stress concentration, so the fit-up must match the design transition. Different thicknesses can be joined when the design provides a proper taper or transition.

questions.question: For finding tight surface cracks in a ferromagnetic weld after grinding a repair excavation, which pairing of purpose and method is most appropriate?

answers.text: Radiography to confirm the surface is crack-free
Visual alone because grinding always removes cracks fully
Magnetic particle or liquid penetrant surface examination to verify no crack remains before rewelding
Ultrasonic thickness readings to prove surface soundness

questions.explanation: Surface methods such as magnetic particle and penetrant are the tools of choice to verify an excavation is crack-free before rewelding. Radiography, the strongest distractor, is comparatively poor at tight surface cracks.

questions.question: Why does carbon have a much stronger effect per percent than most other elements in the carbon equivalent concept?

answers.text: Carbon is the only element present in steel
A small change in carbon strongly changes hardenability and the hardness of any martensite formed, so it dominates cracking behavior
Other elements have no effect at all on hardenability
Carbon lowers hardness more than any other element

questions.explanation: Carbon dominates hardenability and martensite hardness, which is why it carries full weight in carbon equivalent. Other elements matter, but less per percent.

questions.question: An operator suggests raising the postweld heat treatment temperature well above specification to finish faster. Why refuse?

answers.text: Higher temperature is always safe for steel
Overshooting can over-temper and weaken the material, alter structures, and in some alloys enter damaging ranges, so the specified window must be held
The specification window is only a suggestion about furnace settings
Speed is the primary quality criterion

questions.explanation: Postweld temperatures are chosen metallurgically; exceeding them trades specified properties for speed. The window is a requirement, not a suggestion.

api-571-corrosion-and-materials.quiz_title: API 571 Corrosion and Materials Professional Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Chloride stress corrosion cracking of a stainless exchanger belongs in which category?

answers.text: Uniform or localized thickness loss
High-temperature corrosion
Environment-assisted cracking
Mechanical and metallurgical failure

questions.explanation: SCC is cracking assisted by a specific environment combined with stress, the definition of environment-assisted cracking. While pits may accompany it, cracking is the failure mode that matters.

questions.question: What does HTHA stand for?

answers.text: High Temperature Hydrogen Attack - reaction of hydrogen with carbon in steel at elevated temperature and hydrogen partial pressure, forming methane and decarburizing the steel
Hydrothermal Thinning by Acid at ambient temperature
Hydrogen Trapping in Hydrided Alloys at room temperature only
High Tensile Heat Affected zone cracking

questions.explanation: HTHA is High Temperature Hydrogen Attack. It needs elevated temperature and hydrogen pressure and damages steel internally by decarburization and fissuring - very different from low-temperature aqueous hydrogen damage.

questions.question: How does prior temper embrittlement feed brittle fracture risk?

answers.text: It lowers the transition temperature
It removes all flaws from the vessel
It raises the transition temperature, so a vessel can be in the brittle regime at temperatures that were once acceptable
It increases impact toughness

questions.explanation: Embrittling mechanisms shift the toughness curve, expanding the temperature window where brittle fracture can occur. Startup limits set for unembrittled steel may no longer protect it.

questions.question: Monitoring most helpful for detecting conditions leading to steam blanketing includes:

answers.text: Pump net positive suction head calculations only
Vibration monitoring of small-bore piping only
Circulation, flow, and tube temperature monitoring in boiler circuits
Elbow thickness surveys in gas lines

questions.explanation: Boiler circulation/flow and tube temperatures reveal blanketing risk. Pump NPSH and gas-line surveys address different mechanisms.

questions.question: What morphology is characteristic of metal dusting?

answers.text: A uniform soft ferrite skin
A smooth hard nitride case with no metal loss
Deep, localized pits and rapid wastage, often with coke deposits and metal powder or dust at the attack site
Thick glassy ash deposits

questions.explanation: Localized pitting, wastage, coke, and metal dust distinguish metal dusting. A smooth hard case describes nitriding.

questions.question: What is the primary alloying defense against high-temperature oxidation?

answers.text: Increasing carbon content, which hardens the surface against oxygen
Increasing chromium content, which forms a more protective, slower-growing oxide scale
Adding sulfur to form a protective sulfide layer
Removing chromium so iron oxide can form freely

questions.explanation: Chromium is the primary defense because chromium-rich oxide scales are more protective and allow progressively higher service temperatures. Adding carbon or sulfur does not create a protective oxide, and removing chromium makes scaling worse.

questions.question: A plant proposes raising caustic strength in a carbon steel system without stress relief. What is the appropriate integrity response?

answers.text: Evaluate caustic SCC susceptibility for the new concentration and temperature and consider stress relief, material, and controls before operating
Assume dilute-service history guarantees safety at any concentration
Only check the pump capacity
Approve automatically because carbon steel is immune to caustic

questions.explanation: A chemistry change is a management-of-change integrity issue for SCC. Past safe operation at lower concentration does not transfer to hotter, stronger caustic.

questions.question: Which stress condition can drive chloride SCC even when operating pressure stress is low?

answers.text: Purely compressive stress from external supports
No stress is needed if chlorides are present
Hydrostatic test water pressure after the equipment is drained and dried
Residual tensile stress from welding, forming, or cold work

questions.explanation: Residual tensile stresses from welding and fabrication are often sufficient to drive chloride SCC. The idea that no stress is needed is the strongest distractor, but tensile stress is a required leg of the mechanism.

questions.question: A new inspector asks which single change of service would most increase amine corrosion in an existing carbon steel line. Which answer is best?

answers.text: Switching the line to dry gas service with no liquid amine
Switching the line from lean-amine service to hot rich-amine service at higher velocity
Lowering the acid gas loading and temperature in the line
Putting the line in stagnant lean-amine storage service

questions.explanation: Hot, loaded rich amine at higher velocity combines all the aggravating critical factors for this mechanism in carbon steel. Dry gas, lower loading, and stagnant lean service all move away from the corrosive environment.

questions.question: What mitigation besides metallurgy and wash water helps control bisulfide corrosion?

answers.text: Deliberately increasing salt concentration
Removing ammonia and sulfide monitoring
Allowing repeated dry-out of effluent tubes
Controlling velocity and maintaining effective wash water distribution and quantity

questions.explanation: Process control of flow and washing addresses the two main drivers without a material change. Increasing concentration moves severity the wrong way.

questions.question: How does water availability change hydrochloric acid corrosion in an overhead vapor line?

answers.text: Water prevents hydrochloric acid corrosion completely
Corrosion becomes severe where water condenses; dry vapor alone is much less corrosive to steel
Dry hydrogen chloride gas corrodes faster than aqueous acid in all cases
Water turns hydrogen chloride into a protective coating

questions.explanation: The aqueous phase is what makes hydrogen chloride a powerful corrodent. Condensation location therefore predicts damage location, while water itself is the enabler, not a protectant.

questions.question: Applied choice: For a damage-mechanism review, a team must decide which circuits get detailed HTHA screening. Which selection rule is most defensible?

answers.text: Screen circuits chosen by alphabetical order until the budget runs out
Screen only circuits that have already leaked
Screen only the newest circuits, because older ones have proven themselves

Screen every steel circuit where metal temperature and hydrogen partial pressure could approach or exceed the alloy's limit, including during credible excursions, and document why other circuits are excluded

questions.explanation: Screening follows credible exposure, including excursions, not failure history. A circuit that has not leaked may be incubating damage, and age alone proves nothing about fissuring.

api-570-piping-inspector.quiz_title: API 570 Piping Inspector Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: The elbow below the overhead condenser on the slurry oil line from the catalytic cracking unit measures 0.365 in. today. The minimum required thickness for this location is 0.250 in. What is the remaining corrosion allowance at this location?
questions.explanation: Remaining corrosion allowance = current thickness - minimum required thickness = 0.365 - 0.250 = 0.115 in. The required thickness is subtracted, not added; adding it would give 0.615 in., which is more than the wall that exists.

questions.question: A Class 3 piping circuit (natural gas feed line to the reformer) has a calculated remaining life of 21 years. What is the maximum interval for visual external inspection of this circuit?

answers.text: 5 years
10 years
3 years
41 years

questions.explanation: Visual external inspection intervals are set by piping class, not by one-half the remaining life: Class 3 piping has a maximum visual external interval of 10 years. The 21-year remaining life limits the thickness-measurement interval, not the external visual interval, so halving it is a wrong method here.

questions.question: For an LPG rundown line, the minimum required thickness is tm = 0.4375 in. The pipe specification carries a 12.5% mill (under-tolerance) allowance. What nominal wall thickness must be ordered so the delivered wall still meets tm?
questions.explanation: Nominal thickness = tm / (1 - 0.125) = 0.4375 / 0.875 = 0.5 in. Check: 0.5 x 0.875 = 0.4375 in. = tm. Multiplying tm by 1.125 adds only 12.5% of tm, which is less than the 12.5% of the larger nominal wall that the mill may remove.

questions.question: What must a PQR record about the variables used on the qualification coupon?

answers.text: The widest values the fabricator hopes to use in future production
The actual values, or actual ranges where the code permits a range, of the essential variables as they were used on that coupon
Only the values that differ from the previous PQR
The values printed in the construction code's example forms

questions.explanation: The PQR is a record of a specific welding event. Only the actual coupon values can define the envelope the resulting WPS is allowed to claim.

questions.question: A PQR coupon was 3/4 in. thick, and the resulting WPS claims a qualified base-metal range beginning at 1/16 in. What is wrong with the lower end of that range?

answers.text: Nothing, because a thick coupon qualifies all thinner material automatically
The lower limit should have been set by the welder's performance test instead
For a coupon of that thickness the qualified range begins at 3/16 in., so the 1/16 in. claim is below what the PQR supports
The claim fails only if production material is actually 1/16 in. thick

questions.explanation: Thick qualification coupons do not reach down to foil-like thicknesses: the qualified base-metal range for a 3/4 in. coupon starts at 3/16 in. The WPS must mirror the range the qualification table gives.

questions.question: A new piping circuit is about to enter service and no baseline data exist. What should the inspection program establish?

answers.text: Baseline thickness measurements at identified monitoring locations, recorded before or as the circuit enters service
No measurements until the first scheduled inspection in ten years
A single undated reading kept verbally
Baseline data only for the pumps, not the piping

questions.explanation: Without a baseline at known locations, later readings cannot produce a corrosion rate. Delaying the first measurement for years discards the reference point the whole trending system needs.

questions.question: A thinned elbow is replaced with a new elbow of the same material, size, and rating, restoring the line to its original design conditions. How is this work classified?

answers.text: An alteration, because any welding is an alteration
A rerating, because the elbow is new
A repair, because it restores the piping to its original condition without changing design conditions
New construction, because a new component was installed

questions.explanation: Restoring original condition with like-for-like components is a repair. Newness of the component does not make the work an alteration when design conditions are unchanged.

questions.question: A stagnant dead leg on a corrosive service line shows heavy internal deposits at its low point during inspection. What action best addresses the finding?

answers.text: Evaluate wall thickness in the dead leg, consider removal or periodic flushing, and monitor it as a susceptible location
Leave it because dead legs do not corrode
Only check the flange faces on the dead leg
Increase insulation thickness without examining the pipe

questions.explanation: Dead legs trap stagnant, often corrosive fluid and are classic sites for localized loss and freezing. They require thickness evaluation and a mitigation such as removal, flushing, or inclusion in monitoring.

questions.question: Why should a relief device not be gagged or have its inlet blocked as a method of stopping a leak in service?

answers.text: Gagging is an approved temporary repair
Blocking or gagging removes overpressure protection from the equipment, so a leaking device must be managed by safe isolation and replacement or repair under a controlled procedure
A gagged valve still relieves at a higher pressure
Leaks should always be stopped by gagging first

questions.explanation: A gagged or blocked device provides no protection, leaving equipment exposed to overpressure. Leaks are managed through controlled isolation and replacement, never by defeating the device.

questions.question: What is crater cracking and where does it typically occur?

answers.text: A crack running the full length of the heat-affected zone
A crack found only in the base metal before welding begins
A surface scratch caused by a wire brush after welding
A small crack, often star-shaped, in the depression left when an arc is stopped abruptly without filling the crater

questions.explanation: Stopping the arc suddenly leaves a shrinking crater that can crack. Proper technique fills the crater or uses run-out, and inspectors examine pass stops and starts for these cracks.

questions.question: Determination: Group 1.1, service 500 psig at 400 degF. Ratings at 400 degF: Class 150 = 200 psi, Class 300 = 600 psi, Class 600 = 1200 psi. Most economical class:

answers.text: Class 150 with heavier bolts
Class 300, because its 600 psi rating is the first to cover 500 psig
Class 600, because 500 is half of 1000
Class 900

questions.explanation: Class 150 (200) = 500 and is the lowest class that works, hence most economical; Class 600 works but costs more.

questions.question: A spool is closed up without anyone checking its interior. The risk created is that construction debris left inside can:

answers.text: Increase the flange pressure rating
Improve flow by scouring the pipe wall
Eliminate the need for flushing
Damage pump internals, plug small connections and contaminate the process when the system is started

questions.explanation: Cleanliness before closure is a basic erection control. Debris causes equipment damage and blockages; flushing is still required, but it is not a substitute for preventing gross debris entry.

api-510-pressure-vessel-inspector.quiz_title: API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspector Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: The actual thickness of a deaerator vessel shell location is 0.290 in. and the required thickness for the design conditions is 0.210 in. What is the remaining corrosion allowance at this location?
questions.explanation: Remaining corrosion allowance = actual thickness − required thickness = 0.290 − 0.210 = 0.080 in. This is the thickness that can still be lost before the location reaches the required thickness; it is the numerator in the remaining-life calculation.

questions.question: A depropanizer overhead drum location is 0.630 in. thick, the required thickness is 0.450 in., and the corrosion rate is 0.009 in/yr. Based on the remaining life, what is the maximum internal inspection interval?

answers.text: 20 years
5 years
12 years
10 years

questions.explanation: Step 1: Remaining allowance = 0.630 − 0.450 = 0.180 in. Step 2: Remaining life = 0.180 ÷ 0.009 = 20 years. Step 3: Internal interval = lesser of one-half the remaining life (10 years) or 10 years = 10 years. Forgetting the half-life step would incorrectly give the full remaining life.

questions.question: A hemispherical head has an inside radius of 48 in., a design pressure of 300 psi, an allowable stress of 17,500 psi and E = 0.85. What is the required thickness?
questions.explanation: For a sphere or hemispherical head, t = PR/(2SE - 0.2P) = (300 x 48) / ((2 x 17,500 x 0.85) - (0.2 x 300)) = 14,400 / 29,690 = 0.485 in. The first distractor wrongly uses the cylindrical-shell formula; a sphere's membrane stress is half the cylinder's hoop stress, so it needs roughly half the thickness.

questions.question: How many tension and bend specimens does a typical groove-weld PQR coupon require to demonstrate qualification?

answers.text: Two tension specimens and four guided-bend specimens (face/root or side bends as thickness dictates), all meeting acceptance
Two tension specimens only, with bends optional
Four tension specimens and no bends for carbon steel
One tension specimen and one bend specimen

questions.explanation: The standard groove-weld qualification coupon yields a set of specimens — reduced-section tension specimens to prove strength and a set of guided bends to prove ductility and soundness. Both families of tests must be performed and must meet their acceptance criteria.

questions.question: PQR/WPS comparison shows a deleted PWHT cycle: The PQR coupon received postweld heat treatment, but the WPS states PWHT is not required for production joints of the same grouping and thickness. What is the disposition?

answers.text: Revise the WPQ instead, since PWHT is a welder variable
Requalification is required — PWHT condition is an essential variable and the WPS must match what the PQR coupon actually received
Accept it if the tension test passed in the as-welded condition
No action — PWHT is a production decision outside the PQR

questions.explanation: Whether the coupon was postweld heat treated, and the cycle it received, are essential to the qualification: the tested properties belong to that thermal condition. Adding, deleting or materially changing PWHT takes the WPS outside its PQR and requires requalification.

questions.question: A welder's WPQ for GTAW was taken with filler metal added. Production proposes the welder make an autogenous (no-filler) GTAW joint. What is the performance-qualification issue?

answers.text: The issue is only the tungsten size
Deleting filler metal is an essential performance variable for GTAW — the backed-by-filler test does not by itself qualify autogenous welding
Autogenous welding needs no qualification of any kind
No issue — filler use is never a performance variable

questions.explanation: For GTAW performance, the addition or deletion of filler metal changes the technique the test demonstrated. A welder tested with filler has not demonstrated the autogenous technique, so the WPQ must cover that condition.

questions.question: A radiograph of a weld has acceptable density but the required essential wire of the wire IQI is not visible. The radiograph is:

answers.text: Acceptable if the weld itself looks sound
Acceptable if the density is at the high end of its range
Acceptable after the interpreter notes the wire size on the report
Not acceptable, because the required sensitivity was not demonstrated

questions.explanation: Sensitivity and density are separate requirements and both must be met. A missing essential wire means the technique did not demonstrate the required image quality, so the exposure must be corrected and repeated.

questions.question: A vessel's inspection plan is being written for a wet H2S service separator. Which factor should most strongly shape the plan's examination locations and methods?

answers.text: The colour of the vessel's external coating
The preference of the scaffolding contractor
The order in which vessels appear in the equipment list
The damage mechanisms expected in the service, such as H2S-related cracking and corrosion, and the locations where they occur

questions.explanation: Good planning starts from anticipated damage: service, materials, operating conditions and history point to the mechanisms to hunt for and the vessel regions and NDE methods most likely to find them.

questions.question: A repair uses mechanical (non-welded) means — a bolted enclosure — to seal a leaking flange joint on a vessel nozzle. Under the repair programme, this is treated as:

answers.text: A controlled repair (often temporary) requiring engineering design for pressure and bolting loads, inspector acceptance, documentation and a plan for permanent resolution
Routine maintenance needing no engineering or records
A permanent alteration of the flange design
Prohibited in all circumstances regardless of design

questions.explanation: Engineered enclosures and clamps are legitimate repair tools, but they become pressure-retaining devices themselves: they need design calculations, controlled installation, acceptance and tracking — frequently as temporary repairs pending permanent correction.

questions.question: An inspector finds that several thickness monitoring locations on a vessel were placed on weld caps and give inconsistent readings. What is the corrective practice?

answers.text: Keep taking readings on weld caps and average them
Delete the locations and reduce coverage
Relocate or supplement locations on flat parent metal adjacent to welds, and document the change and correlation readings
Grind weld caps flush to create a measurement spot without approval

questions.explanation: Weld reinforcement gives readings that do not represent shell thickness. Locations belong on representative parent metal, with changes documented so trend data remains interpretable.

questions.question: A shop test record shows a valve's as-received pop was 15 percent above set pressure after a turnaround in fouling polymer service. What interval response is appropriate?

answers.text: Extend the interval because the valve eventually opened
Shorten the test interval for that valve or service group and address the fouling cause
Leave intervals unchanged for all valves
Remove the valve from the testing program

questions.explanation: A significantly high as-received pop in fouling service is evidence the interval is too long for that service. RP 576 practice shortens intervals and mitigates fouling for such devices.

questions.question: Why is removal of slag between passes an in-process inspection concern in SMAW and FCAW?

answers.text: Slag left in place improves penetration of the next pass
