No effect at all

questions.explanation: Lien rights rest on improving the property. Materials returned and never used in the improvement generally do not support a lien.

questions.question: What is an insurance premium audit for a contractor most often based on?

answers.text: Actual payroll and classifications during the policy period, adjusted against estimated premiums
The number of permits pulled
The owner's credit score only
Future bids

questions.explanation: Workers' comp and some liability premiums are estimated up front and trued-up by audit. Keeping payroll split correctly by classification and subcontractor certificates on file prevents overcharges.

questions.question: At what height does federal construction fall protection generally become required for work on walking and working surfaces, as a core threshold concept?

answers.text: At any height above ground level, with no exceptions
Only above 50 feet
At 6 feet in general construction work, subject to specific rules for certain tasks
At 25 feet for all residential work

questions.explanation: The general construction threshold for fall protection is 6 feet, though activities such as scaffolding and steel erection have their own thresholds. Residential builders must plan systems such as guardrails, safety nets, or personal fall arrest.

questions.question: What is the licensed home inspector's role under the Commission, in principle?

answers.text: To guarantee the future condition of a home
To build homes and inspect them
To sell the homes inspected
To perform visual, non-invasive inspections of residential property and report on observed conditions for a client

questions.explanation: Home inspectors observe and report on a home's condition at the time of inspection. They do not build, sell, or guarantee the property.

questions.question: What is the break-even point for a building business?

answers.text: The revenue level at which total income exactly covers total costs, with no profit or loss
The point where a job is half finished
The maximum a bank will lend
The owner's retirement date

questions.explanation: Break-even revenue covers all fixed and variable costs exactly. Knowing it tells the contractor the minimum volume needed before any profit is earned.

texas-home-inspector-state-law.quiz_title: Texas State Law Exam (Home Inspector) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A large commercial developer hires an inspector for a portfolio of office buildings and later asserts a DTPA claim. Which consumer-status principle may limit the claim?

answers.text: Businesses can never be consumers for any purpose
Asset size never matters under any law
The DTPA has business-consumer limits, including asset and transaction-size concepts, so very large commercial claimants may fall outside its protection
Commercial claims are trebled automatically

questions.explanation: The DTPA protects business consumers within defined limits, but very large entities and transactions can exceed them. The statute is aimed mainly at consumers without equal bargaining resources.

questions.question: An inspector gives a client a glowing report, then privately tells the listing agent which defects were left out so the agent can prepare counterarguments. Which DTPA-adjacent principle is most harmed?

answers.text: None, because private conversations are exempt
Only the agents marketing plan
A rule requiring inspectors to help both sides equally
Good faith and honesty toward the consumer, because the inspector secretly undermined the very report the consumer paid for and relied on

questions.explanation: Secretly sabotaging a clients report for another partys benefit breaches the honesty at the center of DTPA and professional-conduct principles. Private side channels do not cleanse deception.

questions.question: What is the licensing principle behind continuing education for Texas inspectors?

answers.text: Education ends forever at first licensure
Only sponsors need any education
Continuing education is optional and never tracked
License holders must complete required continuing education to renew and stay current with law, standards, and practice

questions.explanation: Renewal is tied to completing required continuing education, so inspectors remain current as laws and standards change.

questions.question: A Texas applicant has a prior criminal conviction. How is that history treated in principle during licensing?

answers.text: Any conviction of any kind automatically bars licensure for life
The licensing authority may consider the conviction and its relationship to the duties and responsibilities of an inspector
Criminal history may never be considered for inspectors
Only the applicants employer may decide whether it matters

questions.explanation: Texas licensing law allows the regulator to evaluate criminal history, particularly conduct related to fitness for the occupation. It is a case-by-case fitness review, not an automatic lifetime bar for every offense.

questions.question: A Texas inspector performs work for a client who insists no report is needed, so the inspector gives only a verbal summary. Which licensing concern remains?

answers.text: Inspectors remain accountable for regulated inspection work and its required documentation regardless of a clients preference
A verbal summary converts the job into unregulated consulting
Client preference overrides licensing law in all cases
No inspection legally occurred if nothing was written

questions.explanation: A client cannot waive the regulatory framework that governs a licensed inspection. Accountability and documentation duties follow the regulated activity.

questions.question: Which examinations are part of the Texas licensing picture for an inspector candidate?

answers.text: Only a driving examination
Only an open-book quiz from an employer
The national home inspector examination content and the Texas state law examination covering Texas law and standards
A plumbing journeyman examination

questions.explanation: Texas candidates must demonstrate both general inspection competency and knowledge of Texas-specific law, rules, and Standards of Practice.

questions.question: Why do Texas rules call for a pre-inspection agreement in typical inspection practice?

answers.text: To guarantee the home will pass inspection
To define the scope, terms, and client understanding before the inspection begins
To allow the inspector to skip the standards of practice
To set the sellers asking price

questions.explanation: A pre-inspection agreement aligns expectations about scope and terms before work starts. It does not waive the standards that govern the inspection.

questions.question: A client and inspector agree in advance that a required item will not be inspected because it is not part of this transaction. What is essential?

answers.text: Keep the agreement verbal and secret
Document the agreement and the departure in the manner required so the report reader understands the limitation
Mark the item satisfactory
Delete that section from the form

questions.explanation: An agreed departure must be transparent. The report should make clear what was not inspected and why, so no reader is misled.

questions.question: An inspector runs two fixtures at once and flow drops markedly, and a toilet leaks at its base. How should this be reported?

answers.text: As satisfactory because water is present
As deficiencies in the plumbing section of the report
Only verbally to the listing agent
As a departure from the standards

questions.explanation: Deficient functional flow and active leaks are classic plumbing deficiencies that must be documented on the promulgated report form.

questions.question: On the Texas report form, what does marking an item as deficient communicate?

answers.text: The item was not present in the home
The item was inspected and found to be in need of correction, deficient, or not functioning as intended
The inspector chose not to inspect the item
The item performed exactly as intended

questions.explanation: The deficient designation flags a condition that does not function as intended or adversely affects a system and needs correction or further evaluation.

questions.question: For a typical resale home inspection in Texas, which report approach must the inspector use?

answers.text: Use the current TREC-promulgated inspection report form
Use any narrative format the inspector prefers
Give only a verbal summary to the client
Use the seller disclosure form as the report

questions.explanation: Texas requires inspectors to use the current report form promulgated by the Texas Real Estate Commission for most inspections, so reports are consistent and complete.

questions.question: What is the most important habit for deficiency reporting under the Texas standards?

answers.text: Report each observed deficiency in the correct section with the deficient designation so it is not buried or lost
Collect all deficiencies into one vague sentence
Mention deficiencies only by phone
Report deficiencies only for the most expensive system

questions.explanation: Clear, section-by-section deficiency marking is the core discipline of the Texas form and ensures the client can act on each finding.

north-carolina-home-inspector.quiz_title: North Carolina Home Inspector Licensing Examination Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which is the best example of negligence as a discipline ground?

answers.text: Failing to inspect a readily accessible required component without a valid reason and failing to report the limitation properly
Reporting that an inaccessible component could not be inspected
Using a checklist consistent with the Standards of Practice
Recommending further evaluation instead of speculating on a cause

questions.explanation: Skipping a required, accessible component without justification or proper notation is a failure to exercise the required care. Documenting inaccessibility, following a standards-based process, and referring out are diligent practice.

questions.question: An inspector performs an inspection for a client who is also the inspector's business partner in the property's sale. The central issue is:

answers.text: Whether the inspection was performed on a weekday
Whether the report used the inspector's preferred font
A conflict of interest requiring disclosure and compliance with Board requirements
Whether the home has a garage

questions.explanation: A business interest in the transaction is a textbook conflict of interest. It must be disclosed and handled as the law and rules require, regardless of report formatting or scheduling details.

questions.question: A flat roof on an NC home has extensive ponding water 48 hours after rain. What must the inspector do?

answers.text: Report the observed ponding and related drainage condition as a roofing finding
Drill a drain hole during the inspection
Ignore ponding on all flat roofs
Certify the roof membrane as sound

questions.explanation: Ponding indicates a drainage problem that stresses the membrane and is reported as observed. The inspector does not alter the roof or certify concealed membrane condition.

questions.question: Under the NC SoP, how are structural components concealed behind finished walls and ceilings treated?

answers.text: The inspector must open finished surfaces to inspect them
The inspector must report them as defective
The inspector must use X-ray equipment
They are not inspected because they are not readily accessible, and the inspection is limited to visible conditions

questions.explanation: Concealed structure is outside a visual inspection of readily accessible components. The inspector reports visible evidence, such as cracking or sagging, that suggests hidden problems.

questions.question: A client asks an NC inspector to inspect a home the inspector's own company recently renovated. What principle from the SoP framework is most relevant?

answers.text: Inspectors should inspect their own work to save the client money
Only the fee must be disclosed
The seller must choose a different client
Inspectors must avoid conflicts of interest and must not inspect property in which they have a financial interest that compromises objectivity, disclosing relevant interests

questions.explanation: Objectivity is foundational to the SoP framework. A financial interest in the property compromises the inspection and must be avoided or disclosed as the rules require.

questions.question: Penny-sized holes and sawdust-like frass appear in crawl space joists in a Wadesboro home, and a probe easily penetrates one joist's lower edge, while other joists are sound. What should the inspector report?

answers.text: Certify the home free of wood-destroying insects because most joists are sound
Identify the exact insect species from the frass alone
Report visible evidence consistent with wood-destroying insect activity and damaged wood in the affected joists, recommending evaluation by a licensed pest management professional
Ignore holes smaller than a quarter in diameter

questions.explanation: Inspectors report observed evidence of wood-destroying organisms and the resulting wood damage, referring species identification and treatment to licensed pest professionals. Sound neighbors do not cancel damaged members.

questions.question: At a propane-fired home near Boone, the copper fuel line to the furnace is kinked sharply at a floor penetration, the tank regulator vent faces downward into mulch, and there is a faint gas odor near the line. What should the inspector recommend?

answers.text: Straighten the kink personally with pliers during the inspection
Ignore fuel line condition because propane is heavier than air and settles harmlessly
Report the damaged fuel piping and odor and recommend prompt evaluation by the propane supplier or a licensed gas contractor before continued use
Spray paint the line to mark the damaged section for later

questions.explanation: A kinked fuel line is weakened and restricted, and any gas odor moves the finding into prompt-action territory. Fuel piping work belongs to the propane supplier or licensed gas fitter, not the inspector.

questions.question: A client in Mooresville asks why the report recommends 'further evaluation by a qualified professional' for a furnace heat exchanger concern instead of declaring it cracked. What explanation reflects inspection scope?

answers.text: Inspectors are forbidden from caring about furnaces
The phrase is used to avoid all responsibility for the report

Heat exchangers are largely concealed and confirming a crack requires specialized testing beyond a visual inspection, so the referral directs the client to the professional equipped to confirm the condition
Any furnace concern can be settled by looking at the thermostat

questions.explanation: Further-evaluation language is not evasion; it marks the honest boundary between visual screening and specialized diagnosis. Explaining that boundary helps the client act on the referral promptly.

questions.question: A basement bathroom in a Morganton mountain home sits below the septic tank inlet, served by a sewage ejector basin in a closet. The basin alarm float is dangling disconnected and there is a faint sewage smell. What should the inspector emphasize?

answers.text: The alarm is optional decoration on ejector systems
The smell proves the basin is working correctly
Basement fixtures never need mechanical lifting to reach septic
If the ejector pump fails without a working high-water alarm, sewage can back up into the basement fixtures, so a plumber should restore the alarm and check the pump

questions.explanation: Fixtures below the gravity drain rely entirely on the ejector pump, and the alarm is the only warning before a sewage backup. A disconnected alarm float is reported for prompt plumber correction.

questions.question: Furniture and stored boxes completely block access to a Kannapolis attic hatch and to the electrical panel area on the day of inspection. How must the inspector handle these limitations?

answers.text: Move all the owner's belongings without permission
Report the areas as not inspected due to blocked access and explain the limitation, without guessing about hidden conditions
Certify the blocked areas as satisfactory
Cancel the entire inspection and refund without a report

questions.explanation: Inspectors do not move personal property or dismantle barriers, and they never certify what they could not see. Documenting the limitation protects both client understanding and inspector defensibility.

questions.question: A rectangular crawl space in Thomasville measures 30 feet by 40 feet and its vapor retarder is sold in rolls covering 500 square feet each, with no waste allowance. How many rolls are minimally needed for single-layer full coverage?

answers.text: One roll
Two rolls
Three rolls, because 30 times 40 is 1,200 square feet and 1,200 divided by 500 rounds up to 3
Twelve rolls

questions.explanation: The area is 30 x 40 = 1,200 square feet. At 500 square feet per roll, 1,200 / 500 = 2.4, which rounds up to 3 rolls for full coverage.

questions.question: A heat pump water heater in a Raleigh garage runs but its condensate drain was never connected and drips constantly onto the slab, and the small garage closet space around it is packed with storage against its air intake. What issues should be reported?

answers.text: The unit needs a free flow of room air to extract heat and its condensate must be drained properly; blocked airflow cuts efficiency and the dripping keeps the slab wet
Heat pump water heaters work best sealed in airtight closets
Condensate from these units is designed to evaporate off the slab
Storage against the intake acts as beneficial insulation

questions.explanation: A heat pump water heater heats water by pulling heat from surrounding air, so it needs adequate air volume and clear intake, plus real condensate drainage. Both deficiencies are simple, consequential corrections.

nhie-home-inspector.quiz_title: National Home Inspector Examination (NHIE) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A patio slab has settled so its outer edge is 2 inches lower and it now pitches back toward the house. What is the MAIN risk created by this change?

answers.text: The patio furniture will slide toward the yard
The slab will no longer support its own weight
The change proves the house footing has failed
Rainwater will run toward and collect at the foundation

questions.explanation: Settlement that reverses a slab's pitch sends water to the wall instead of the yard, increasing basement or crawl space moisture risk. It does not by itself prove footing failure.

questions.question: A second-floor shower sits about 10 feet above the basement pressure gauge. About how much pressure is lost to elevation?

answers.text: About 4.3 psi, using roughly 0.43 psi per foot of rise
About 43 psi
About 0.43 psi total
No pressure is lost to elevation

questions.explanation: Water loses about 0.43 psi per vertical foot, so 10 feet costs roughly 4.3 psi. This is one reason upper-floor fixtures show weakness first in marginal systems.

questions.question: A direct-vent fireplace termination is installed 4 inches above deep snow grade and partially buried by mulch. Why should this be reported?

answers.text: Mulch improves intake air quality for the unit
Blockage of the intake or exhaust can cause shutdown, incomplete combustion, or carbon monoxide entry
Terminations are supposed to be buried to prevent freezing
Only roof terminations are subject to clearance rules

questions.explanation: Side-wall terminations must stay clear of grade, snow, landscaping, and debris so both intake and exhaust remain free. A blocked termination disrupts sealed combustion and creates a safety hazard.

questions.question: What distinguishes the inspector's role for a residential fire sprinkler system from a full sprinkler inspection?

answers.text: The home inspector must flow water from every head
The home inspector must calculate hydraulic demand
The home inspector replaces corroded heads found during the visit
The home inspector visually checks heads, valves, and obvious obstructions or damage and recommends specialist inspection for testing and maintenance

questions.explanation: Home inspection of sprinklers is visual and non-invasive: painted, corroded, damaged, obstructed heads, closed valves, and missing escutcheons are reported. Flow testing and internal maintenance are specialist work.

questions.question: What is the function of a sill pan or pan flashing beneath an exterior door or window?

answers.text: To level the unit during installation only
To insulate the rough opening from sound
To collect water that reaches the bottom of the unit and drain it back to the exterior
To anchor the unit against wind uplift

questions.explanation: Pan flashing is the safety net at the bottom of openings, catching incidental water and directing it out instead of into the wall and floor framing below.

questions.question: A homeowner added a new roof vent by cutting a hole and setting the vent flange entirely on top of the shingles with caulk. Rain now stains the ceiling below. What failed?

answers.text: The vent is too large
The attic has too much insulation
The ridge is too high
The shingle-style lap was reversed, so water running down the roof is directed under the flange

questions.explanation: Upper shingles must lap over the top of a penetration flange and the flange laps over shingles below. A flange placed wholly on top channels water underneath it.

questions.question: Above a wide window opening in a load-bearing wall, what structural member carries loads around the opening?

answers.text: A header (lintel) supported by jack studs
A single flat 2x4 laid on its side
The window frame itself
Drywall bridging

questions.explanation: Headers span openings and transfer loads to jack and king studs at the sides. Undersized or missing headers show as sagging above openings and cracked finishes.

questions.question: A homeowner replaced a fuse box with breakers but a circuit still uses an old screw-in fuse holder inline in a closet. More importantly the inspector notices a penny behind a fuse in another holder. A penny behind a fuse is what?

answers.text: An old but acceptable fuse substitute
An extremely dangerous defeat of overcurrent protection that must be flagged for immediate correction
A grounding improvement
Evidence of a 30-amp rated circuit

questions.explanation: Bypassing a fuse removes all overload protection; the conductor can overheat and start a fire without ever opening the circuit.

questions.question: A furnace filter slot with no filter installed during heating season should be reported because operating without filtration:

answers.text: Raises AFUE to condensing levels
Improves airflow with no downside
Stops condensate production
Dirties the blower and heat exchanger/coil, restricts airflow over time, and degrades performance

questions.explanation: Filters protect equipment as much as air quality; a missing filter lets dust coat the blower, exchanger, and cooling coil. It is an easy maintenance correction the inspector should flag.

questions.question: Insulation missing or displaced above a dropped ceiling or around an attic hatch causes:

answers.text: No measurable heat loss
Improved attic ventilation
A vapor barrier failure only
A thermal bypass — a concentrated area of heat loss (and summer heat gain)

questions.explanation: Continuity matters: even small uninsulated gaps, such as an uninsulated hatch, leak disproportionate heat because heat flows preferentially through the weakest path. Weatherstripping and insulating the hatch is a standard fix.

questions.question: A client asks whether a component reported as 'defective' must be replaced. The inspector's report-based answer should clarify that 'defective' in the report means:

answers.text: Replacement is legally mandatory before closing

The component did not perform its intended function, showed significant deterioration, or presented a safety concern as observed — and a qualified professional should evaluate whether repair or replacement is appropriate
The component has zero value
The seller must use the inspector's chosen contractor

questions.explanation: 'Defective' is a condition description, not a transaction order or a repair-versus-replace verdict. That determination, with options and costs, belongs to the qualified professional who evaluates it.

questions.question: A gas fireplace produces soot on the glass and the room has no carbon monoxide alarm. The damper operation is unclear. What referral is most appropriate?

answers.text: Recommend the fireplace not be used until a qualified gas fireplace or chimney professional evaluates it, and note the absence of CO detection near sleeping areas as a safety concern
Recommend using the fireplace only on weekends
Clean the glass and declare the fireplace safe
State that soot on glass is purely decorative

questions.explanation: Sooting in a gas appliance signals combustion or venting problems that can produce carbon monoxide. Suspending use pending qualified evaluation, plus flagging missing CO alarms, matches the hazard level.

nmls-safe-mlo.quiz_title: SAFE MLO — Mortgage Loan Originator Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Originator Tim advises borrower Uma to leave income off an application form even though Uma earns it, saying it will simplify review. What should Tim do instead?

answers.text: Coach the borrower if the false statement seems harmless
Never coach or encourage a borrower to make false or incomplete statements; the application must reflect what the borrower reports truthfully
Encourage omission only for debts the borrower plans to pay off soon
Help phrase a false statement so it sounds plausible

questions.explanation: Encouraging false application statements is dishonest and can involve the borrower in misrepresentation. A seemingly harmless motive is wrong; accuracy is not optional.

questions.question: A lender's fair lending training uses a case where an officer gave pricing exceptions freely to applicants he knew socially, who were overwhelmingly of one ethnic group, while strangers of another group rarely received them. What is the teaching point of the case?

answers.text: Exceptions can produce discrimination through access patterns even when each individual exception seemed friendly and informal
Social familiarity is a legitimate pricing factor
Exceptions should be given only to strangers
Training cases have no connection to real controls

questions.explanation: The case shows how informally granted exceptions can systematically favor one protected group over another without any single hostile act. Social familiarity is not a credit factor, which is why exception access itself must be monitored.

questions.question: Applicant Walter Boone relies on documented, stable Social Security and pension income that has been received for years and is expected to continue. How must the creditor treat it?

answers.text: It must consider the documented income on its stability and expected continuance, without refusing or discounting it because of the nature or source of the income
It must disregard retirement income for applicants over age 62
It may count the income only if Walter also returns to part-time work
It may require a younger co-borrower for every retired applicant

questions.explanation: Creditors must consider retirement and benefit income based on amount, history, and likely continuance, and may not penalize an applicant because income comes from retirement or public sources. Requiring work or a younger co-borrower as a blanket rule substitutes age and source for that individual analysis.

questions.question: How are funds typically advanced under a construction loan?

answers.text: The full amount is paid to the borrower on the day of closing
In draws as stages of the work are completed and inspected
Only after the certificate of occupancy is issued
In equal monthly payments to the borrower's personal account

questions.explanation: Construction funds are released in draws tied to completed, inspected stages of work, which protects the lender's collateral as value is built. Paying the full amount to the borrower at closing would leave the lender unsecured during construction.

questions.question: A purchase price is $250,000 and the contract caps the seller concession at 3% of the price. What is the maximum concession amount?
questions.explanation: The maximum concession is $250,000 x 3 / 100 = $7,500. The $2,500 option applies only 1% of the price, and $25,000 applies 10%, both ignoring the stated 3% cap.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a VA Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan?

answers.text: It is a streamlined refinance of an existing VA loan into a new VA loan, generally intended to improve the rate or terms
It is a cash-out loan that requires a full appraisal in every case
It refinances a conventional loan into a VA loan
It is available to a borrower who has never had a VA loan

questions.explanation: An IRRRL streamlines an existing VA loan into a new VA loan, typically to lower the rate or improve terms. A borrower without an existing VA loan, or seeking a conventional-to-VA refinance, is outside that streamline concept.

questions.question: Which fact pattern most suggests a borrower may need to provide business financial statements in addition to personal returns?

answers.text: The borrower is a salaried teacher with no ownership in any business
The borrower owns the majority of a company organized as a corporation that files its own return
The borrower has a small side payment from a one-time garage sale
The borrower receives only a fixed pension

questions.explanation: Majority ownership of a separately filing business means its financials are needed to judge the income available to the borrower. Salaried and pension income do not raise that need.

questions.question: A lender offers Kurt a credit of 1.25% of the loan amount on a $350000 loan. How much is the lender credit?
questions.explanation: Lender credit = loan x credit percent / 100 = $350000 x 1.25% = $4375. The credit reduces the cash the borrower must bring to closing.

questions.question: Elena Walker's appraised property value is $714,250 and the first mortgage loan amount is $623,480. What is the LTV ratio?
questions.explanation: The LTV is $623,480 divided by $714,250, times 100, which equals 87.29%. Inverting the fraction would overstate the ratio.

questions.question: An appraiser notes the subject home has a converted garage that the county records still show as a garage, and permits are not documented. What should the underwriter expect the appraisal review to address?

answers.text: Whether the conversion is legal, permitted, and typical for the market, and how it was treated in the value and in any comparable adjustments
That converted space is always valued as living area at full price with no questions
That the processor should change county records before submission
That the title policy automatically covers unpermitted work

questions.explanation: Unpermitted conversions raise legality, marketability, and valuation questions the appraisal must address. Assuming full living-area value with no questions, the strongest distractor, ignores both permit status and market reaction.

questions.question: A licensed real estate agent helps a buyer purchase a home but receives no compensation for mortgage services and performs no mortgage origination. Is an MLO license required for that real-estate-only activity?

answers.text: Yes, every real estate agent must also hold an MLO license at all times
No, real-estate-only activity without mortgage compensation does not by itself require an MLO license
Yes, unless the agent has been selling homes for more than ten years
No, but only if the buyer pays cash and signs a waiver

questions.explanation: Real estate professionals performing only real estate activities, without compensation for mortgage services, are not originating loans. Mortgage activity for compensation would change the analysis.

questions.question: A complaint turns out to be based on a misunderstanding, but the regulator still asks the originator for the file and an explanation. What must the originator do?

answers.text: Refuse, because an unfounded complaint needs no response
Cooperate fully and provide the records and information requested
Provide only a letter from the originator's attorney
Respond only if the borrower apologizes first

questions.explanation: The duty to cooperate applies whether or not the complaint ultimately has merit.

maryland-hvac-master-restricted.quiz_title: Maryland HVAC Master Restricted Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A 90,000 Btu/h furnace is served by the single-opening outdoor combustion air method. The vent connectors in the room have a combined cross-sectional area of 18 square inches. What minimum net free area must the single opening provide?

answers.text: The opening must provide 18 square inches, matching the combined cross-sectional area of the vent connectors alone
The opening must provide 90 square inches, matching the indoor-air opening ratio applied to the appliance input
The opening must provide 100 square inches, matching the indoor-air opening minimum applied to this outdoor method
The opening must provide 30 square inches, the larger of the input-based value and the vent connector area sum

questions.explanation: D is correct: the single-opening method requires the larger of 1 square inch per 3,000 Btu/h (90,000 / 3,000 = 30 square inches) and the sum of the vent connector areas (18 square inches), so 30 square inches governs. A is wrong: the connector sum is only one of the two compared values and it is the smaller one here. B is wrong: the 1 per 1,000 Btu/h ratio belongs to the indoor-air method, not this method. C is wrong: the 100 square inch floor belongs to the indoor-air openings and is never imported into the single-opening method.

questions.question: A gas furnace is rated at 80,000 Btu/h input with an 81 percent steady-state efficiency, giving 64,800 Btu/h output. With the burners firing steadily and the blower at heating speed, the measured temperature rise across the furnace is 45 degrees. Using CFM = output / (1.08 x temperature rise), what airflow is the furnace moving?

answers.text: About 1,600 cubic feet per minute, dividing the output by 1.08 and then multiplying the result by the measured 45-degree temperature rise
About 800 cubic feet per minute, dividing the rated input of 80,000 by 1.08 and then by twice the measured temperature rise
About 3,333 cubic feet per minute, dividing the output of 64,800 by 1.08 multiplied by the rise and then doubling the result to account for return air
About 1,333 cubic feet per minute, dividing the 64,800 Btu/h output by 48.6, the product of 1.08 and the 45-degree temperature rise

questions.explanation: D is correct: 1.08 x 45 = 48.6, and 64,800 / 48.6 = 1,333 cubic feet per minute. A is wrong: it multiplies by the temperature rise instead of dividing by the full 1.08 x rise product. B is wrong: it uses the input rating instead of the 64,800 Btu/h output and doubles the temperature rise without basis. C is wrong: the formula's result is not doubled for return air; return and supply airflow are the same stream measured once.

questions.question: An air handler is installed above a finished ceiling where a clogged primary drain could cause water damage. Beyond the primary drain, what overflow protection arrangement does the mechanical code call for?

answers.text: An auxiliary drain pan beneath the unit served by its own drain line, or a water-level detection device in the pan that shuts the equipment down before the pan overflows

A second trap installed in series on the primary drain line, so that a blockage in either trap is isolated from the coil's drain outlet, with both traps vented into the auxiliary pan so condensate cannot back up into the coil section under any condition

A primary drain line oversized by two pipe sizes above the unit's outlet, so debris that would clog a standard line passes through freely, a substitution the mechanical code allows wherever the unit sits directly above finished living or working space

A condensate pump with an oversized reservoir, since pumping capacity alone satisfies the code's protection requirement for units above ceilings, with the pump's discharge line piped into the auxiliary pan that the installer places beside the unit for this purpose

questions.explanation: A is correct: the mechanical code requires an auxiliary drain pan with a separate drain, or a water-level detection device that stops the equipment, where a clogged primary drain could overflow onto finished surfaces. B is wrong: two traps in series create an air lock that impedes drainage; the code's protection is a pan or a shutoff device, not a second trap. C is wrong: oversizing the primary line does not protect against the line clogging, and no such sizing substitution appears in the code. D is wrong: a pump reservoir fills and overflows like any drain failure; without a pan or a level device the protection requirement is unmet.

questions.question: An installer wires a replacement condensing unit. The nameplate lists a minimum circuit ampacity and a maximum overcurrent protective device rating. How must those two nameplate values be used?

answers.text: The branch circuit is sized from a generic table for the unit tonnage, and the nameplate values are used only for warranty records
The conductors are sized from the minimum circuit ampacity, and the breaker is sized to the maximum rating listed
The conductors are sized from the maximum overcurrent rating, and the breaker is sized to the minimum circuit ampacity
Both values are averaged, and the conductors and the breaker are each sized to that single averaged ampacity figure

questions.explanation: B is correct: minimum circuit ampacity sets the conductor size, and the maximum overcurrent protective device value sets the largest breaker or fuse permitted for the unit. A is wrong: tonnage tables do not replace the individual unit nameplate values. C is wrong: it reverses the two values and would oversize conductors while undersizing protection relative to the listing. D is wrong: the two values serve different purposes and are never averaged into one figure.

questions.question: A replacement boiler rated at 150,000 Btu/h serves a building whose calculated design heat loss is 60,000 Btu/h. The boiler fires in bursts of about two minutes, and fuel use has risen compared with the old, smaller boiler. What is the root problem?

answers.text: The circulator is moving water too slowly, trapping heat inside the boiler jacket and forcing the operating control to end each firing cycle early, a suspicion the technician confirms by measuring the temperature rise across the boiler at full fire with strap-on sensors

The aquastat's differential is set too wide, causing long off-cycles that the burner then answers with short compensating bursts of firing, which the technician corrects by narrowing the aquastat's differential to its minimum available setting

The expansion tank is undersized, so each firing cycle relieves a little water and the fill valve answers with cold water that shortens the next cycle, a pattern the owner confirms by finding small puddles beneath the relief valve's discharge pipe after cold nights
The boiler is grossly oversized for the connected load, so each firing satisfies the control temperature almost immediately and the burner never settles into efficient steady operation

questions.explanation: D is correct: a boiler with two and a half times the capacity of the design load reaches its control temperature in very short runs, and the resulting short-cycling wastes fuel in repeated startup and standby losses. A is wrong: slow circulation raises the boiler's temperature rise across the heat exchanger but does not produce this firing pattern in an oversized boiler, and the old boiler behaved on the same piping. B is wrong: a wider differential lengthens both on- and off-cycles, the opposite pattern. C is wrong: relief weeping from an undersized tank is a pressure symptom that would be visible at the relief discharge, and it does not set burner cycle length.

questions.question: After a power outage, every zone in a hot-water system stays cold even though the boiler fires and reaches its high limit. The circulator is silent, its housing is hot, and a slight hum with vibration is felt when it is energized. How do these findings discriminate the fault from an air-bound system?

answers.text: Unlike an air-bound system, which silences a whole house at once, this pattern points to a failed air separator that has passed a large air slug into the boiler, identified by bleeding the boiler's automatic air vent and watching for a long, continuous release of trapped air

Unlike an air-bound radiator, which leaves one emitter partly cold while others heat, this whole-system no-flow pattern with a humming, hot, non-rotating circulator points to a seized or failed circulator

Unlike an air-bound system, where the boiler stays cold, this pattern points to a failed zone valve end switch that has interrupted the boiler's firing circuit, which the technician confirms by checking for control voltage at the boiler's burner circuit terminals during a call for heat

Unlike an air-bound radiator, this whole-house pattern points to the expansion tank, which has lost its charge and is blocking flow at the air separator connection, a failure the technician confirms by tapping the tank and hearing a hollow ring from its upper half when struck

questions.explanation: B is correct: trapped air disables individual emitters or a high loop while the boiler and other zones keep working, but here the boiler heats to limit with no flow anywhere and the energized circulator hums without rotating — a seized rotor or failed circulator. A is wrong: an air-bound condition does not silence a whole house at once, and a failed separator cannot stop an energized circulator from rotating. C is wrong: the boiler is firing to its high limit, so its firing circuit is intact, and an end switch fault affects one zone. D is wrong: a failed expansion tank produces pressure symptoms and relief discharge; it does not block flow or stop a circulator from turning.

questions.question: A technician adjusts the thermostatic expansion valve on a medium-temperature reach-in cooler at steady load. To what evaporator outlet superheat is the valve commonly adjusted on this class of equipment?

answers.text: The valve is adjusted for about 25 degrees of superheat, keeping the suction line warm to the touch at the compressor
The valve is adjusted for zero degrees of superheat, keeping the evaporator fully flooded to its outlet at all loads
The valve is adjusted for about 20 degrees of superheat, reserving the last half of the coil as a drying safety margin
The valve is adjusted for about 10 degrees of superheat, keeping the coil effective while protecting the compressor

questions.explanation: D is correct: medium-temperature commercial evaporators are commonly adjusted for about 10 degrees of superheat at the evaporator outlet, balancing coil effectiveness against liquid floodback protection. A is wrong: 25 degrees starves much of the coil and wastes its rated capacity. B is wrong: zero superheat means liquid can leave the evaporator and reach the compressor. C is wrong: 20 degrees leaves too much of the coil doing only gas cooling and cuts capacity noticeably.

questions.question: An office space in a commercial building houses 20 occupants and has 2,000 square feet of floor area. Using the breathing-zone rates of 5 cubic feet per minute per person and 0.06 cubic feet per minute per square foot, what outdoor airflow does the space require?

answers.text: The space requires 220 cubic feet per minute, from 100 for the occupants plus 120 for the floor area served
The space requires 100 cubic feet per minute, from the occupant component alone with no floor area component added
The space requires 120 cubic feet per minute, from the floor area component alone with no occupant component added
The space requires 200 cubic feet per minute, from 10 cubic feet per minute applied to each of the 20 occupants

questions.explanation: A is correct: outdoor air = (5 x 20) + (0.06 x 2,000) = 100 + 120 = 220 cubic feet per minute, with the people component and the area component added together. B is wrong: it drops the area component and understates the requirement. C is wrong: it drops the people component and understates the requirement. D is wrong: 10 cubic feet per minute per person is not one of the stated breathing-zone rates for this occupancy.

questions.question: A contractor holds a Maryland master restricted license examined in air conditioning and is hired to replace a residential split system. Which statement describes the work this license authorizes?

answers.text: Maintain and repair air-conditioning systems only, with all installation and replacement work reserved for a limited license holder
Install, maintain, and repair heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, refrigeration, and hydronic work in every area of the trade
Install, maintain, alter, remodel, or repair air-conditioning services within the specialty area examined
Perform air-conditioning work only while working under the direction and control of a separate licensed contractor

questions.explanation: C is correct: a master restricted licensee provides services by installing, maintaining, altering, remodeling, or repairing work within the specialty area or areas examined, and air conditioning is this licensee's examined specialty. A is wrong: maintenance-and-repair-only authority describes the limited license, and a master restricted licensee may also install and replace. B is wrong: authority across every area of HVACR work belongs to the unrestricted master license. D is wrong: working only under another contractor's direction and control describes the journeyman tiers, not a contractor-tier license.

questions.question: An applicant asks for the complete set of HVACR license classes Maryland law creates. Which set is complete and accurate?

answers.text: Master, limited, journeyman, apprentice, inspector, and helper
Master, master restricted, journeyman, foreman, apprentice, and helper
Master, master restricted, limited, journeyman, journeyman restricted, and apprentice
Master, limited, journeyman restricted, trainee, apprentice, and inspector

questions.explanation: C is correct: Maryland law creates exactly six license classes: master, master restricted, limited, journeyman, journeyman restricted, and apprentice. A is wrong: helper is not a license class, and inspector is a separate appointment credential rather than one of the six classes. B is wrong: foreman and helper are job titles, not license classes, and the set omits limited and journeyman restricted. D is wrong: trainee is not a class, and the set omits master restricted and journeyman.

questions.question: A licensee's insurer sends a certificate of insurance that names the licensee's employer as certificate holder and omits the policy number. Why will the Board not accept this certificate as filed?

answers.text: Certificates are accepted only when the insurer mails them directly, regardless of what they say
The certificate is missing the licensee's registration number, the one content the Board always requires printed in the corner of the certificate next to the insurer's own file reference number
The certificate must show the licensee's name, both coverage amounts and their combined total, and the policy number and expiration date, with the Board named as certificate holder
The certificate must name the customer on the licensee's largest current job as an additional holder

questions.explanation: C is correct: a compliant certificate shows (1) the licensee's name, (2) general liability of at least $300,000, (3) property damage of at least $100,000, (4) a combined amount of at least $400,000, and (5) the policy number and expiration date — and the State Board of HVACR Contractors must be named as the certificate holder, not the employer. A is wrong: the defect here is content and holder, not the delivery route. B is wrong: the registration number is a license-display item, not one of the certificate's five required contents. D is wrong: no customer is named on the certificate; the Board is the certificate holder.

questions.question: A renewal notice from a private vendor tells a master restricted licensee to complete 16 hours of continuing education before renewing. What is the licensee's actual position?

answers.text: The hours are required, and the license cannot be renewed until a completion certificate is filed
Half the hours are required, with the balance carried into the next renewal cycle for completion
The hours are required only for licensees who also hold a master license at the same time
No continuing-education hours are required to renew a Maryland HVACR license of this class

questions.explanation: D is correct: no continuing-education requirement applies to master restricted renewal; the renewal conditions are entitlement, the renewal fee, proof of insurance, and the renewal application. The only annual course duty in this title binds HVACR inspectors, not licensees. A is wrong: the vendor's 16-hour figure has no basis in the renewal law for this license. B is wrong: there are no required hours to split or carry over. C is wrong: holding a second license class does not create a continuing-education duty for this renewal.

virginia-plumbing.quiz_title: Virginia Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Three drinking fountains on one corridor branch drain through a common segment. What load does that segment carry from the fountains alone?

answers.text: 1.5 DFU
0.5 DFU — grouped fountains share one rating
3 DFU
6 DFU

questions.explanation: Each fountain is 0.5 DFU and loads add along the flow: 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.5 DFU. Counting the group once ignores additivity, while 3 or 6 DFU would require per-fountain values of 1 or 2 DFU that the shared table does not assign.

questions.question: A terminal is measured 7 feet horizontally from an air intake and 1 foot above the top of that intake. The installer wants to fix the location by raising the terminal in place rather than moving it. How much more height, at minimum, must the raise add?

answers.text: 2 feet more, to reach at least 3 feet above the top of the intake
1 foot more, to reach 2 feet above the intake
No raise can fix it; horizontal distance is the only path
4 feet more, to reach 5 feet above the intake

questions.explanation: Staying at 7 feet horizontal keeps the terminal short of the 10-foot branch, so it must qualify under the other branch: at least 3 feet above the top of the opening. It is 1 foot above now, so at least 2 more feet of rise are needed. Raising is a valid path — the rule is an either/or — and neither 2 feet total nor 5 feet total is the stated alternative height.

questions.question: A campus building with flush-tank fixtures totals 500 water supply fixture units. Using the flush-tank reference points, what is its probable peak demand?

answers.text: 65 gpm
124 gpm
500 gpm
208 gpm

questions.explanation: At 500 WSFU the flush-tank reference demand is 124 gpm. The 65 gpm figure is the 200-WSFU point, 500 gpm would be a 1-for-1 conversion the probability method never makes, and 208 gpm is the point where the two curves converge at 1,000 WSFU.

questions.question: A 22.5° offset has a set of 10 inches. Each of the two fittings has a take-out of 2 inches. What is the cut length of the travel piece?
questions.explanation: Travel = 10 × 2.613 = 26.13 in.; cut length = 26.13 − (2 × 2) = 26.13 − 4.00 = 22.13 in. The 26.13 in. option deducts nothing, and 24.13 in. deducts only one fitting.

questions.question: A remodel used certified lead-free solder throughout, but the inspector rejects a newly installed valve on the potable system: its wetted surfaces have a weighted-average lead content of 0.4%. Why is the rejection correct?

answers.text: The inspector is wrong - lead-free solder makes the whole installation compliant
Pipe and fitting wetted surfaces are separately capped at a 0.25% weighted-average lead content - compliant solder does not cure a noncompliant fitting
The valve is fine because 0.4% is below the 0.2% solder cap
The valve must be rejected only if it is installed on a hot line

questions.explanation: The lead-free definition has two parts: solder at 0.2% lead maximum, and the weighted average of wetted pipe/fitting surfaces at 0.25% maximum. At 0.4%, the valve's wetted surfaces fail their own limit no matter how compliant the solder is - and 0.4% also exceeds, not undercuts, the solder figure.

questions.question: A sewage ejector that receives discharge from a water closet must be able to pass spherical solids up to what diameter?

answers.text: 1/2 inch
1 inch
2 inches
3 inches

questions.explanation: Pumps and ejectors receiving water closet discharge must handle spherical solids up to 2 inches in diameter. The 1/2-inch solids capability applies to pumps and ejectors that do not receive water closet discharge.

questions.question: A laundry-room ejector (not a pneumatic unit) pumps 40 gpm, and because of the ceiling layout its sump vent cannot reach the vent stack in less than 60 feet of developed length. Which is the smallest sump vent the table allows for a run that long at that pumping rate?

answers.text: 2 inches, because no smaller vent is permitted once the run passes 50 feet
1-1/4 inches, which allows up to 72 feet at that discharge rate
1-1/2 inches, because a 1-1/4-inch vent allows less than 10 feet
3 inches, because sump vents are always at least 3 inches

questions.explanation: At a 40-gpm discharge the table gives a 1-1/4-inch sump vent a 72-foot maximum developed length, which covers the 60-foot run. The less-than-10-foot figure for 1-1/4 inch belongs to the much higher 100-gpm row, and neither a 50-foot trigger for 2 inches nor a universal 3-inch sump vent exists in the table.

questions.question: An installer proposes joining a CPVC distribution line to a PVC line with solvent cement, and supporting a branch with a saddle-type fitting. How many of these two proposals are permitted?

answers.text: Both are permitted
Neither — both are on the list of prohibited joints and connections
Only the saddle fitting
Only the solvent-cement joint between the two plastics

questions.explanation: The prohibited-joints list includes solvent-cement joints between different types of plastic pipe and saddle-type fittings, along with cement or concrete joints and joints made with fittings not approved for the installation. Both proposals on this job fall on that list.

questions.question: An installer puts a neat U-bend trap in a relief discharge line so a small amount of water always stands in the pipe. What does the IPC say?

answers.text: The trap is required wherever the pipe discharges to a receptor
The trap is permitted if a cleanout is provided at its lowest point
The discharge piping must not be trapped
The trap is permitted if it holds a seal of at least 2 inches

questions.explanation: IPC discharge piping for a relief valve must not be trapped. A deep seal or a cleanout does not make a trap acceptable, and no trap is ever required in this piping.

questions.question: Three public flush-tank water closets are the only fixtures in a tank-predominant building. What is the estimated demand?

answers.text: 31.0 gpm
17.5 gpm
9.4 gpm
21.5 gpm

questions.explanation: The load is 3 x 5.0 = 15 WSFU. On the tank-predominant curve, 15 WSFU = 17.5 gpm. The 31.0-gpm option is the valve-predominant curve at 15 WSFU, the wrong curve for flush-tank fixtures. The 9.4-gpm option is the tank curve at 5 WSFU and the 21.5-gpm option is the tank curve at 25 WSFU; both are wrong-row reads.

questions.question: An applicant has completed 80 hours of formal vocational training in plumbing. How much practical experience is required for journeyman exam approval?

answers.text: 5 years of practical experience in the trade
6 years of practical experience in the trade
7 years of practical experience in the trade
4 years of practical experience in the trade

questions.explanation: The 80-hour training level pairs with 6 years of practical experience. Five years pairs with 160 hours, 7 years pairs with 40 hours, and 4 years pairs with 240 hours.

questions.question: A contractor has not furnished a state license number or evidence of exemption to a locality. What may the locality do about a local business license?

answers.text: It must issue or renew the local business license anyway, because state licensure information is irrelevant to a local license decision
It may issue the local license for one full cycle as a courtesy, because the state license number is needed only at the second renewal
It may not issue or renew a local business license to that contractor until the state license number or evidence of exemption is furnished
It must revoke the contractor's state license itself, because localities are given direct authority over state tradesman and contractor licenses

questions.explanation: A locality may not issue or renew a local business license to a contractor who has not furnished the state license number or evidence of exemption. The locality is not required to issue the license anyway, there is no courtesy cycle that defers the showing, and the locality's role does not extend to revoking state licenses itself.

texas-plumbing.quiz_title: Texas Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A master plumber checks the grade stakes for a 64-foot run of 8-inch building drain set at minimum slope. What total fall should the stakes show?

answers.text: 4 inches
8 inches
16 inches
64 inches

questions.explanation: At 1/16 inch per foot, 64 feet falls 64 x 1/16 = 4 inches. Eight inches would be the fall at 1/8 inch per foot and 16 inches at 1/4 inch per foot — both rates for smaller pipe — and 64 inches confuses the run length with the drop.

questions.question: A homeowner converts a flat roof over a garage into a sun deck with chairs and a railing. The existing vent terminal there ends 8 inches above the roof, which complied when the roof was weather-only. What does the conversion change?

answers.text: The terminal must now be raised to at least 7 feet above the roof, because the roof is used for a purpose other than weather protection
Nothing; terminal height is fixed by what complied at installation, and later changes in how the roof is used never alter it
The vent must be removed and the fixtures re-vented elsewhere, because a vent terminal cannot serve a roof that people occupy
The terminal must be lowered so deck users cannot touch it

questions.explanation: Terminal height follows the roof's use: 6 inches suffices for a weather-only roof, but once the roof becomes an occupied deck the terminal must discharge at least 7 feet above it. The change of use changes the requirement, vents may serve buildings with occupied roofs at the taller height, and lowering the terminal would put vent gas at the occupants' level.

questions.question: A campus building with flush-tank fixtures totals 500 water supply fixture units. Using the flush-tank reference points, what is its probable peak demand?

answers.text: 65 gpm
124 gpm
500 gpm
208 gpm

questions.explanation: At 500 WSFU the flush-tank reference demand is 124 gpm. The 65 gpm figure is the 200-WSFU point, 500 gpm would be a 1-for-1 conversion the probability method never makes, and 208 gpm is the point where the two curves converge at 1,000 WSFU.

questions.question: A water column stands 46.2 feet high. What pressure does it exert at its base?

answers.text: 23.1 psi
20.0 psi
10.0 psi

questions.explanation: Pressure = head × 0.433 psi per foot: 46.2 × 0.433 ≈ 20.0 psi. Multiplying by 2.31 (106.7 psi) reverses the conversion; 23.1 psi uses 0.5 psi/ft.

questions.question: A remodel used certified lead-free solder throughout, but the inspector rejects a newly installed valve on the potable system: its wetted surfaces have a weighted-average lead content of 0.4%. Why is the rejection correct?

answers.text: The inspector is wrong - lead-free solder makes the whole installation compliant
Pipe and fitting wetted surfaces are separately capped at a 0.25% weighted-average lead content - compliant solder does not cure a noncompliant fitting
The valve is fine because 0.4% is below the 0.2% solder cap
The valve must be rejected only if it is installed on a hot line

questions.explanation: The lead-free definition has two parts: solder at 0.2% lead maximum, and the weighted average of wetted pipe/fitting surfaces at 0.25% maximum. At 0.4%, the valve's wetted surfaces fail their own limit no matter how compliant the solder is - and 0.4% also exceeds, not undercuts, the solder figure.

questions.question: A branch serves a public restroom containing two 1.6 gpf water closets, two lavatories, and one standard urinal. What total load must the branch be sized to carry?

answers.text: 14 DFU
12 DFU
18 DFU
10 DFU

questions.explanation: Public water closets at 1.6 gpf count 4 DFU each, lavatories 1 DFU each, and a standard urinal 4 DFU. The 18 DFU answer overrates each closet at 6 DFU, a value that applies only above 1.6 gpf, and 12 DFU underrates the closets at the private value of 3 DFU.

questions.question: A non-pneumatic ejector discharges 500 gpm. Its sump vent is proposed at 2-1/2 inches with a 20-foot developed length. What does the sump-vent table say?

answers.text: The 2-1/2-inch vent is permitted up to 25 feet
A 2-1/2-inch vent is not permitted at that discharge; a 3-inch vent allows up to 24 feet
A 2-inch vent allows up to 97 feet at that discharge
Any size is permitted because length is unlimited at high discharge

questions.explanation: At 500 gpm, vents of 2-1/2 inches and smaller are not permitted at all; the table first allows a 3-inch vent, capped at 24 feet. The 25-foot and 97-foot figures come from the 100-gpm row for smaller vents and do not transfer to this discharge.

questions.question: Using the segmented-loss method, a fixture group sits 30 feet above the point where available pressure is measured. How much pressure is consumed by the elevation alone?

answers.text: 15 psi
About 13 psi
About 6.5 psi
30 psi

questions.explanation: The segmented-loss method computes static head at 0.433 psi per foot of elevation, so 30 feet consumes about 13 psi. The 15 psi answer uses the 0.5 psi per foot figure, which belongs to the alternative Appendix E method, not this one.

questions.question: A combined primary-and-secondary roof drain assembly is installed so both systems share one common outlet body to save piping. What does the IPC require?

answers.text: A shared outlet is permitted if it is sized for both systems together and is provided with a cleanout where the two systems join above the roof drain body
A shared inlet is permitted if the outlets are independent and each outlet is sized for the full design flow of its own drainage system
Combined primary and secondary assemblies must have independent inlets and independent outlets
Independence is required only for scuppers, not for drain assemblies, because a drain body can be rodded from the roof when it becomes blocked

questions.explanation: A combined primary-plus-secondary assembly needs independent inlets and outlets, so a failure or blockage in the primary path cannot disable the secondary path that exists to back it up. Sharing an outlet, however generously sized, defeats that independence, and the rule applies to drain assemblies as well as scuppers.

questions.question: A transit-terminal building drain at 1/4 inch per foot serves 50 public 1.6-gpf water closets and 15 urinals flushing 1 gallon per flush or less. What is the smallest building drain size for the load?

answers.text: 5 in.
4 in.
3 in.
6 in.

questions.explanation: The load is 50 x 4 + 15 x 2 = 230 DFU. A 4-in. drain at 1/4 inch per foot is capped at 216 DFU, so it is 14 DFU short despite being close. A 3-in. drain carries only 42 DFU. The next size, 5 in., carries 480 DFU and complies. A 6-in. drain complies but is not the smallest.

questions.question: An emergency floor drain is provided in a public area solely as a safeguard against flooding. How much drainage fixture unit load is it counted as when sizing the drain it connects to?

answers.text: 2 DFU
0 DFU
1 DFU
0.5 DFU

questions.explanation: An emergency floor drain is listed at 0 DFU in public and assembly use, so it adds no load to the sizing calculation. Treating it like a regular floor drain at 2 DFU overstates the load; the 0.5 DFU figure belongs to a drinking fountain.

questions.question: Below floor level, how must an island fixture vent be installed?

answers.text: With vent fittings, sloped at least 1/8 inch per foot toward the roof vent
With vent fittings, run level to the nearest partition
With drainage fittings, sloped at least 1/8 inch per foot back toward the drain
With drainage fittings, sloped at least 1/4 inch per foot back toward the drain

questions.explanation: Below the floor the island vent uses drainage fittings and must slope at least 1/4 inch per foot back toward the drain so anything entering it drains away. Vent fittings or a flatter 1/8-inch grade leave the below-floor section able to hold water and debris.

ohio-plumbing.quiz_title: Ohio Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A master plumber sizes a segment carrying a domestic kitchen sink, a domestic clothes washer, and a drinking fountain in a break room. What is the segment's cumulative load?

answers.text: 4.5 DFU
5 DFU
5.5 DFU
7 DFU

questions.explanation: Under the Ohio Plumbing Code (2021 IPC with Ohio amendments) Table 709.1, the fixture units are: kitchen sink 2 DFU, automatic clothes washer (residential) 2 DFU, and drinking fountain 0.5 DFU, for a total of 2 + 2 + 0.5 = 4.5 DFU.

questions.question: A client asks why the plumber's bathroom-group design does not run a separate dry vent up from every fixture, and whether the shared arrangement leaves any trap unprotected. Which answer is accurate?

answers.text: The shared arrangement is a shortcut that leaves the water closet trap unprotected, since no vent rises from the closet itself
The design wet-vents the bathroom group: an oversized drain serving one fixture vents another, so each trap is protected through the shared pipe
Any trap not on its own dry vent is by definition unprotected
The design relies on the building's single main vent alone to protect every trap in the group, with no local venting at all

questions.explanation: Wet venting is protection, not the absence of it: the oversized shared drain is sized so air passes above the flow, and that air path is what protects the connected traps — and a bathroom group may be wet-vented in both code families. The arrangement is a recognized method rather than a shortcut, dry vents are not the only form of protection, and the distant main vent by itself is not what protects these traps.

questions.question: Four replacement heaters are offered as examples in an apprentice class. Which one's relief installation is fully compliant?

answers.text: One whose discharge pipe matches the valve outlet size, has no valve anywhere in the relief path, drains by gravity, and terminates observably 6 inches above a floor drain, unthreaded
One whose discharge is reduced one size to fit the wall chase, with all other details correct
One with a shutoff valve ahead of the relief valve, kept locked open
One whose discharge terminates 6 inches above the drain but is threaded for a future cap

questions.explanation: Only the first installation satisfies every agreed discharge rule at once: full size, no valve between tank and relief valve or in the discharge, gravity drainage, observable termination 6 inches above the receptor, and no threads at the end. Each other example keeps exactly one prohibited feature — a reduction, an isolating valve, or a threadable end.

questions.question: A fitting is catalogued as a 1/16 bend. Using the fraction of a full 360° circle, what is its angle?
questions.explanation: Angle = 360° ÷ 16 = 22.5°. A 1/8 bend gives 360 ÷ 8 = 45°, and a 1/4 bend gives 90°.

questions.question: A homeowner reports that ever since a pressure-reducing valve was installed last year, the house pressure creeps up overnight - after the evening's water heating, with no water being used - and the heater's relief valve occasionally drips. Nothing is wrong with the PRV's daytime readings. What is happening?

answers.text: The PRV is failing open overnight and must be replaced
Thermal expansion in the now-closed system: heated water cannot push back past the PRV, so pressure builds until the relief valve drips - an expansion tank is the correction
The city raises its street pressure at night, which the PRV cannot affect
The relief valve is oversized for the heater

questions.explanation: The pattern - pressure rising specifically after heating, in a system closed by the PRV - is trapped thermal expansion, and both codes require a means of controlling it, typically an expansion tank. A PRV holds its setpoint against street pressure day and night, so neither street pressure nor a failing PRV explains a heating-linked rise.

questions.question: A janitor area has one service sink, one general floor drain, and one drinking fountain on a common branch. What is the branch's total load?

answers.text: 6 DFU
4 DFU
5.5 DFU
4.5 DFU

questions.explanation: The service sink counts 2 DFU, the general floor drain 2 DFU, and the drinking fountain 0.5 DFU, totaling 4.5 DFU. The 5.5 DFU answer overrates the fountain at a full fixture unit's worth beyond its half-unit value, and 6 DFU treats the fountain like a 2 DFU fixture.

questions.question: A fixture discharges into a 1-1/2-inch drainage pipe, and the installer fits a 2-inch trap 'for better flow.' A second fixture gets a trap smaller than its tabulated minimum. Which installation complies?

answers.text: Both comply — trap size is the installer's choice
Neither — a trap shall not be larger than the drainage pipe into which it discharges, and trap size may not be less than the tabulated minimum for the fixture
Only the oversized trap complies; bigger traps always flow better
Only the undersized trap complies; smaller traps scour better

questions.explanation: Trap sizing is bounded on both sides: the tabulated minimum sets the floor, and the trap may not exceed the size of the drainage pipe it discharges into. The 2-inch trap on a 1-1/2-inch drain breaks the ceiling, the undersized trap breaks the floor, and flow or scouring arguments override neither bound.

questions.question: Using the segmented-loss method, a fixture group sits 30 feet above the point where available pressure is measured. How much pressure is consumed by the elevation alone?

answers.text: 15 psi
About 13 psi
About 6.5 psi
30 psi

questions.explanation: The segmented-loss method computes static head at 0.433 psi per foot of elevation, so 30 feet consumes about 13 psi. The 15 psi answer uses the 0.5 psi per foot figure, which belongs to the alternative Appendix E method, not this one.

questions.question: During a rough-in inspection, a relief discharge pipe is found made of a material that softens and sags at hot-water discharge temperatures. What standard must the pipe material meet?

answers.text: The material must be the same as the building's storm drainage piping
The material must be rated for hot-water distribution service, of the materials permitted for water distribution piping or rated under ASME A112.4.1
Any drainage-weight plastic is acceptable because the pipe only carries waste
The material only needs to match the material of the relief valve body

questions.explanation: IPC discharge-pipe materials must be those permitted for hot-water distribution (the Table 605.4 materials) or rated in accordance with ASME A112.4.1, because the pipe can carry near-boiling water. Drainage-weight plastic, a body-material match, or storm-pipe material does not establish the required hot-water rating.

questions.question: A horizontal building drain inside a building runs 260 feet from its upstream cleanout to the end of the drain, and cleanout spacing may not exceed the maximum permitted interval. What is the minimum number of additional cleanouts that must be installed along the run?

answers.text: 0; cleanouts at the ends of a run are always sufficient

questions.explanation: At a maximum interval of 100 feet, a 260-foot run needs at least three segments, so at least two intermediate cleanouts are required (for example at 90 and 175 feet, giving segments under 100 feet). One intermediate cleanout leaves segments of about 130 feet, which exceeds the interval. Three cleanouts would comply but is more than the minimum asked for. End cleanouts alone leave the full 260 feet unbroken, far beyond the permitted interval.

questions.question: Under the tradesperson experience route, how much plumbing-trade experience must an applicant have, and when must it fall?

answers.text: Work as a tradesperson in the plumbing trade for not less than three years at any point in the applicant's career
Work as a tradesperson in any construction trade for not less than five years, with at least one of those years in plumbing
Work as a tradesperson in the plumbing trade for not less than five years immediately prior to the date the application is filed
Work as a tradesperson in the plumbing trade for not less than five years, so long as the five years were completed before the applicant turned 30

questions.explanation: The tradesperson route requires not less than five years as a tradesperson in the plumbing trade immediately prior to filing. Three years is the engineer route's business-experience figure, not this one, and the experience must be recent rather than at any career point. The five years must be in the plumbing trade, not any construction trade with a single plumbing year. Nothing ties the experience to completion before age 30; the timing rule is that it immediately precedes filing.

questions.question: An estimator looks in the Ohio plumbing code for the building-sewer pipe material table and the building-sewer cleanout rules. What will the estimator find?

answers.text: Ohio kept the building-sewer pipe table and the building-sewer cleanout section but renumbered both of them in its amendments, so the estimator simply needs the current Ohio section numbers to find the material table and the cleanout rules in the code

Ohio deleted only the building sewer cleanout section from the plumbing code, while the building-sewer pipe section and its material table remain in full as the governing standard for pipe selection on every building sewer installed in the state

Ohio deleted the building sewer pipe section and its pipe table, deleted the entire building-drains-and-sewers section that followed it, and deleted the building sewer cleanout section, because building sewers are regulated by the sewer purveyor or health authority

Ohio expanded the building-sewer pipe table and the cleanout rules with Ohio-specific approved materials and additional cleanout locations, because building sewers are regulated more tightly under the Ohio code than under the model text it amended

questions.explanation: Ohio deleted the building sewer pipe section and Table 702.3 (Building Sewer Pipe), deleted Section 703 in its entirety, and deleted the building sewer cleanout section (§708.1.2), leaving building sewers to the sewer purveyor and health authority, so the deletion answer is correct. The renumbering answer fails because the provisions were removed, not moved. The cleanout-only answer understates the deletions by keeping a table Ohio removed. The expansion answer reverses Ohio's direction — it stripped these provisions out of the plumbing code.

north-carolina-plumbing.quiz_title: North Carolina Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A master plumber sizes a segment carrying a domestic kitchen sink, a domestic clothes washer, and a drinking fountain in a break room. What is the segment's cumulative load?

answers.text: 4.5 DFU
5 DFU
5.5 DFU
7 DFU

questions.explanation: Under the North Carolina Plumbing Code Table 709.1, the fixture units are: kitchen sink 2 DFU, automatic clothes washer (residential) 2 DFU, and drinking fountain 0.5 DFU, for a total of 2 + 2 + 0.5 = 4.5 DFU.

questions.question: On a service call, a homeowner reports a toilet that gurgles and a nearby shower trap that empties whenever the washing machine pump discharges. What is the most likely system-level cause?

answers.text: Inadequate venting, so discharge-driven pressure swings exceed what the trap seals can withstand
A trap seal that is 3 inches deep instead of 2
Drain slope that maintains self-scouring velocity
A vent terminal extending 6 inches above the roof

questions.explanation: Pump discharge drives strong pressure swings, and vents exist to admit and emit air so seals are not subjected to more than 1 inch of water column of differential. A 3-inch seal, self-scouring slope, and a 6-inch terminal are all normal, compliant conditions.

questions.question: A supply outlet with an effective opening 1 inch in diameter terminates above a receptor. What is the minimum air gap for that outlet?

answers.text: 1 inch
1/2 inch
2 inches
4 inches

questions.explanation: The air gap must be at least twice the diameter of the effective opening: 2 x 1 inch = 2 inches. One inch is only the absolute floor that applies to smaller openings, and 1/2 inch and 4 inches are respectively below and above what the rule computes here.

questions.question: A 45° offset has a set (offset distance) of 12 inches. What is the length of the travel piece before fitting allowances are deducted?
questions.explanation: For a 45° offset, travel = offset × 1.414, so 12 × 1.414 = 16.97 in. The 12.00 in. option is the run (equal to the offset at 45°), 31.36 in. uses the 22.5° multiplier, and 8.49 in. divides by 1.414 instead of multiplying.

questions.question: A homeowner reports that ever since a pressure-reducing valve was installed last year, the house pressure creeps up overnight - after the evening's water heating, with no water being used - and the heater's relief valve occasionally drips. Nothing is wrong with the PRV's daytime readings. What is happening?

answers.text: The PRV is failing open overnight and must be replaced
Thermal expansion in the now-closed system: heated water cannot push back past the PRV, so pressure builds until the relief valve drips - an expansion tank is the correction
The city raises its street pressure at night, which the PRV cannot affect
The relief valve is oversized for the heater

questions.explanation: The pattern - pressure rising specifically after heating, in a system closed by the PRV - is trapped thermal expansion, and both codes require a means of controlling it, typically an expansion tank. A PRV holds its setpoint against street pressure day and night, so neither street pressure nor a failing PRV explains a heating-linked rise.
