questions.question: A gym shower installation totals 10 gpm through its heads and body sprays. What is its drainage fixture unit value?

answers.text: 2 DFU
5 DFU
6 DFU
3 DFU

questions.explanation: A shower flowing more than 5.7 gpm and up to 12.3 gpm is rated 3 DFU, so 10 gpm falls in that band. It is not 2 DFU, which caps at 5.7 gpm, and the 5 and 6 DFU bands start at much higher flows.

questions.question: Two trapped fixtures stand side by side on the same floor, and the designer vents both traps with a single vent instead of running two separate vents. Which method is being used, and is it permitted?

answers.text: No — every trap must always have its own separate vent with no sharing
Yes — one vent may serve any number of traps on any floors
Yes — one individual vent may serve two traps as a common vent, provided both fixtures are on the same floor level
No — two fixtures may share a vent only if one is a water closet

questions.explanation: A common vent is exactly this arrangement: a single vent protecting two traps, allowed where the fixtures sit on the same floor level. It is not a ban on sharing, it does not extend to unlimited fixtures across floors, and water closets are not a condition of the method.

questions.question: An installer proposes joining a CPVC distribution line to a PVC line with solvent cement, and supporting a branch with a saddle-type fitting. How many of these two proposals are permitted?

answers.text: Both are permitted
Neither — both are on the list of prohibited joints and connections
Only the saddle fitting
Only the solvent-cement joint between the two plastics

questions.explanation: The prohibited-joints list includes solvent-cement joints between different types of plastic pipe and saddle-type fittings, along with cement or concrete joints and joints made with fittings not approved for the installation. Both proposals on this job fall on that list.

questions.question: In a sewage ejector discharge line, a full-open valve is installed first, followed by a check valve, and both sit below the sump cover where they cannot be reached. What arrangement is required?

answers.text: The order does not matter as long as both valves are present in the discharge piping between the ejector and the gravity drainage system it serves
A check valve and a full-open valve, with the full-open valve on the discharge side of the check valve, accessibly located above the sump cover
Only a check valve is required; the full-open valve is optional and may be omitted where the discharge run to the gravity drain is short
Both valves must be below the sump cover to stay primed, and they may be serviced by removing the pump and reaching into the sump pit

questions.explanation: The discharge piping between the ejector and the gravity system requires a check valve and a full-open valve, the full-open valve on the discharge side of the check valve, accessibly located above the sump cover (or in an accessible pit with a removable cover for below-grade discharge). Reversing the order and burying the valves below the cover fails both the sequence and the access requirements.

questions.question: A mixed-use building combines three occupancies on one building drain laid at 1/4 inch per foot. The cafe serves two public 1.6 gpf water closets, two public lavatories, one service sink and one general floor drain. The office serves two public 1.6 gpf water closets, two public lavatories and one urinal flushing 1 gallon per flush or less. The residential level has two bathroom groups with 1.6 gpf water closets, two domestic kitchen sinks and two domestic dishwashers. What is the smallest permitted size for the building drain?

answers.text: 3 in.
4 in.
5 in.
6 in.

questions.explanation: Cafe: 2 x 4 + 2 x 1 + 2 + 2 = 14 DFU. Office: 2 x 4 + 2 x 1 + 2 = 12 DFU. Residential: 2 x 5 (group value) + 2 x 2 + 2 x 2 = 18 DFU. Total 44 DFU exceeds the 42 DFU a 3-inch drain carries at this slope, so 4 inches is the smallest size that works. A 3-inch drain is the result of dropping fixtures such as the two dishwashers from the count (40 DFU), and 5- and 6-inch drains are larger than the load requires.

questions.question: A licensee named on a corporation's license certificate wants to expand into a higher license classification. What does the expansion route require?

answers.text: The corporation's license expands automatically once the firm pays the required fee, with no examination of the individual licensee and no showing that the individual meets the requirements of the higher classification

The individual may be examined to expand license qualifications on payment of the required application and examination fee, provided the individual meets the requirements for the classification sought
The individual may expand qualifications without examination by documenting experience alone and paying the required fee
The individual must surrender the corporation listing and wait one year before being examined for the higher classification

questions.explanation: An individual licensee - including one named on a corporation, partnership, or trade-name certificate - may be examined to expand license qualifications on payment of the required application and examination fee, provided the individual meets the requirements for the classification sought. Expansion is not automatic on payment, experience alone does not replace the examination, and no surrender-and-wait period is imposed.

questions.question: Who may perform the initial installation or replacement of a water heater without a plumbing license?

answers.text: Any unlicensed handyperson, because water heater replacement is classified as a minor repair for all properties
A tenant in a rental dwelling, because occupants are treated the same as owners for repair purposes
A real estate agent preparing a listed property for sale, because pre-sale work is exempt from licensure
Only a property owner who personally performs the work in property not intended for sale and not used for rental purposes

questions.explanation: The initial installation or replacement of any water heater requires a plumbing license, except for a property owner who personally performs the work in property not intended for sale and not used for rental purposes. Water heater replacement is not a universally exempt minor repair, and neither a tenant in a rental property nor an agent preparing a property for sale fits the narrow owner exception.

florida-plumbing.quiz_title: Florida Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A master plumber verifies a hotel bathroom branch serving a private water closet (1.6 gpf), a lavatory, and a single-head shower on a 2-inch trap. What cumulative load should the verification show?

answers.text: 4 DFU
5 DFU
6 DFU
9 DFU

questions.explanation: Private water closet 3 + lavatory 1 + shower 2 = 6 DFU cumulative for the branch. Totals of 4 or 5 DFU omit part of a fixture's rating, and 9 DFU would require a public-use or otherwise inflated value that is not the shared value for these fixtures.

questions.question: A client asks why the plumber's bathroom-group design does not run a separate dry vent up from every fixture, and whether the shared arrangement leaves any trap unprotected. Which answer is accurate?

answers.text: The shared arrangement is a shortcut that leaves the water closet trap unprotected, since no vent rises from the closet itself
The design wet-vents the bathroom group: an oversized drain serving one fixture vents another, so each trap is protected through the shared pipe
Any trap not on its own dry vent is by definition unprotected
The design relies on the building's single main vent alone to protect every trap in the group, with no local venting at all

questions.explanation: Wet venting is protection, not the absence of it: the oversized shared drain is sized so air passes above the flow, and that air path is what protects the connected traps — and a bathroom group may be wet-vented in both code families. The arrangement is a recognized method rather than a shortcut, dry vents are not the only form of protection, and the distant main vent by itself is not what protects these traps.

questions.question: A heater's controls fail in the heating position overnight and the water temperature climbs steadily. At what temperature will a standard T&P relief valve open on temperature to protect the tank?

answers.text: 180 degrees Fahrenheit
210 degrees Fahrenheit
150 degrees Fahrenheit
250 degrees Fahrenheit

questions.explanation: The standard T&P temperature setting is 210°F, just below boiling at atmospheric pressure, so the valve opens before the tank's water can flash to steam. Settings of 150°F and 180°F are far too low, and waiting until 250°F would defeat the valve's purpose.

questions.question: Water flows at 30 gpm through a pipe with a 1.5-inch inside diameter. What is the flow velocity?

answers.text: 8.16 ft/sec
5.45 ft/sec
3.06 ft/sec
30.00 ft/sec

questions.explanation: Velocity = gpm ÷ (2.448 × ID²) = 30 ÷ (2.448 × 2.25) = 30 ÷ 5.508 = 5.45 ft/sec. The 8.16 ft/sec option uses the diameter instead of its square (30 ÷ (2.448 × 1.5)), 3.06 ft/sec uses a 2-inch diameter in the formula, and 30.00 ft/sec is the flow with no conversion at all.

questions.question: A remodel used certified lead-free solder throughout, but the inspector rejects a newly installed valve on the potable system: its wetted surfaces have a weighted-average lead content of 0.4%. Why is the rejection correct?

answers.text: The inspector is wrong - lead-free solder makes the whole installation compliant
Pipe and fitting wetted surfaces are separately capped at a 0.25% weighted-average lead content - compliant solder does not cure a noncompliant fitting
The valve is fine because 0.4% is below the 0.2% solder cap
The valve must be rejected only if it is installed on a hot line

questions.explanation: The lead-free definition has two parts: solder at 0.2% lead maximum, and the weighted average of wetted pipe/fitting surfaces at 0.25% maximum. At 0.4%, the valve's wetted surfaces fail their own limit no matter how compliant the solder is - and 0.4% also exceeds, not undercuts, the solder figure.

questions.question: Which of these cleanout installations is acceptable?

answers.text: A cleanout sealed inside a finished wall with no access panel
A cleanout plug covered over with plaster for a smooth finish
A below-grade cleanout extended up to grade, with its plug at or above grade
A cleanout left buried below grade with no extension to the surface

questions.explanation: Required cleanouts shall not be installed in concealed locations, and below-grade cleanouts must be extended to grade with the plug at or above grade. A cleanout hidden in a wall, a plug covered with plaster or mortar, and a buried cleanout all defeat the access the cleanout exists to provide.

questions.question: What venting must accompany a combination drain and vent system?

answers.text: No vent at all — the oversized pipe is its own vent in every case

A dry vent (or a connection to a drain serving vented fixtures on the same floor), with the dry vent extending at least 6 inches above the highest fixture's flood rim before offsetting; a dry vent is mandatory where the system connects to a building drain receiving only stack discharge
An air admittance valve at the highest fixture only
A wet vent taken from a different floor

questions.explanation: The combination pipe still needs a dry vent or an equivalent connection to vented fixtures on the same floor, and where it joins a building drain receiving only stack discharge the dry vent is mandatory; it must rise 6 inches above the highest flood rim before offsetting. The oversized pipe alone, a lone valve, or a vent from another floor does not meet that requirement.

questions.question: Using the segmented-loss method, a fixture group sits 30 feet above the point where available pressure is measured. How much pressure is consumed by the elevation alone?

answers.text: 15 psi
About 13 psi
About 6.5 psi
30 psi

questions.explanation: The segmented-loss method computes static head at 0.433 psi per foot of elevation, so 30 feet consumes about 13 psi. The 15 psi answer uses the 0.5 psi per foot figure, which belongs to the alternative Appendix E method, not this one.

questions.question: A floor sink receptor is installed with no trap and no vent, the installer reasoning that because all of its waste arrives indirectly, no trap is needed. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: The installer is right: indirect waste receptors never require traps, because the air gap or air break above the receptor already separates it from the drainage system and its sewer gas at all times
The receptor needs a vent but never a trap, because venting alone keeps the receptor's water seal from being siphoned by the building drain below it
Waste receptors must be trapped and vented and connected to the building drainage system, with a narrow exception for a receptor receiving only clear-water waste with no direct sanitary connection
The receptor needs a trap only if it also receives direct waste from a fixture, since indirect waste arrives already separated from the equipment it serves

questions.explanation: Receptors are trapped and vented and connect to the building drainage system; indirect delivery does not remove the trap, because the receptor itself is part of the drainage system. The only stated exception is a receptor receiving only clear-water waste with no direct connection to a sanitary drainage system, which is not this floor sink's situation.

questions.question: On the hotel's guest floors, one drainage stack serves six branch intervals. Each interval discharges exactly one bathroom group with a 1.6 gpf water closet and nothing else. What is the smallest permitted stack size?

answers.text: 2 in.
3 in.
4 in.

questions.explanation: Each interval discharges 5 DFU, so the total is 30 DFU over more than three branch intervals. A 2-inch stack allows 6 DFU per interval, which passes, but its total limit above three intervals is only 24 DFU, so it fails on total load. A 2-1/2-inch stack allows 9 DFU per interval and 42 DFU total above three intervals, satisfying both checks. A 3-inch stack also works but is not the smallest, which is why checking only the per-interval limit misleads here.

questions.question: An applicant's proven experience is recorded as 4,000 person-hours. Using Florida's conversion for the education path, how many full-time years of experience does that represent?

answers.text: One full-time year
Four full-time years
Two full-time years
One-half of a full-time year

questions.explanation: Florida counts 2,000 person-hours as one full-time year of experience, so 4,000 person-hours represent two full-time years. One year would be 2,000 person-hours rather than 4,000, four years would require 8,000 person-hours, and one-half year would be only 1,000 person-hours.

questions.question: A specification uses the phrase medical gas for a piped system. Which set of gases does that phrase cover under Chapter 5?

answers.text: Oxygen and medical air only, because the other piped gases are regulated as industrial gases outside Chapter 5 entirely
Oxygen, nitrous oxide, and carbon dioxide only, because helium and nitrogen are never carried in piped medical systems
Any gas a hospital stores on site, including fuel gases, because Chapter 5 follows the facility's own inventory list
Oxygen, nitrous oxide, medical air, carbon dioxide, helium, nitrogen, instrument air, and mixtures of those gases

questions.explanation: Chapter 5 uses medical gas and medical support gas for piped systems covering oxygen, nitrous oxide, medical air, carbon dioxide, helium, nitrogen, instrument air, and mixtures of them, with a provision naming a specific gas applying only to that gas. Limiting the phrase to oxygen and air or to three gases understates the list, and fuel gases or a facility inventory do not define the term.

arizona-plumbing.quiz_title: Arizona Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A small ejector pump serving a basement fixture group discharges continuously at 4 gpm into the drainage system. How is that flow converted for sizing?

answers.text: At 1 DFU per gpm, for 4 DFU
It is ignored because it is pumped, not gravity
At 2 DFU per gpm, for 8 DFU
At 7.5 DFU per gpm, for 30 DFU

questions.explanation: Continuous and semi-continuous flows — pumps, ejectors, and similar equipment — convert at 2 DFU per gpm, so 4 gpm counts as 8 DFU. A 1-to-1 conversion understates it, ignoring pumped flow misses the load entirely, and 7.5 is the gpm equivalent of a single DFU, not the conversion rate.

questions.question: A dry vent serves a group whose highest flood-level rim is at 40 inches above the floor. The vent is roughed to turn horizontal at 44 inches. How much higher must the vertical rise go before the turn is permitted?

answers.text: At least 2 inches more, to reach 6 inches above the rim
It may turn now; it is already above the rim
At least 6 inches more, for a full second clearance
It must rise to the ceiling regardless of rim height

questions.explanation: The vent must rise at least 6 inches above the flood-level rim of the highest fixture served: 40 plus 6 is 46 inches, and the rough-in at 44 inches is 2 inches short. Merely clearing the rim is not enough, adding a full extra 6 inches overshoots the requirement, and ceiling height plays no part in the rule.

questions.question: Two otherwise identical school buildings are being sized. One uses flush-tank water closets throughout and the other uses flush-valve water closets throughout, and both total the same number of water supply fixture units. How should their probable peak demands compare?

answers.text: The flush-tank building will show the higher peak demand in gallons per minute
Both buildings will show exactly the same peak demand
The flush-valve building will show the higher peak demand in gallons per minute
The building with fewer floors will always show the higher demand regardless of flushing method

questions.explanation: Hunter's method uses two separate demand curves, one for systems predominantly using flush tanks and one for systems predominantly using flush valves. At the same fixture-unit total the flush-valve curve always gives the higher flow, so the demands are not equal and the tank system is not the higher one.

questions.question: A pressure gauge reads 30 psi at the base of a water column. How tall is the column?
questions.explanation: Head = pressure × 2.31 ft per psi = 30 × 2.31 = 69.3 ft. The 12.99 ft option multiplies by 0.433, which is the inverse conversion, and 138.6 ft doubles the correct head.

questions.question: A homeowner reports that ever since a pressure-reducing valve was installed last year, the house pressure creeps up overnight - after the evening's water heating, with no water being used - and the heater's relief valve occasionally drips. Nothing is wrong with the PRV's daytime readings. What is happening?

answers.text: The PRV is failing open overnight and must be replaced
Thermal expansion in the now-closed system: heated water cannot push back past the PRV, so pressure builds until the relief valve drips - an expansion tank is the correction
The city raises its street pressure at night, which the PRV cannot affect
The relief valve is oversized for the heater

questions.explanation: The pattern - pressure rising specifically after heating, in a system closed by the PRV - is trapped thermal expansion, and both codes require a means of controlling it, typically an expansion tank. A PRV holds its setpoint against street pressure day and night, so neither street pressure nor a failing PRV explains a heating-linked rise.

questions.question: A new clinic's only floor sits entirely above the elevation of the cover of the next upstream manhole in the public sewer. The designer specifies a backwater valve on the building drain anyway. What is the correct ruling?

answers.text: Permitted as extra protection
Required whenever a clinic has below-grade piping
Permitted if the valve is accessible
Not permitted; fixtures above that elevation shall not discharge through a backwater valve

questions.explanation: In a new building, fixtures installed on a floor above the elevation of the next upstream manhole cover shall not discharge through a backwater valve; the existing-building exception does not apply to this new clinic. Accessibility of the valve does not change the prohibition, and no rule requires a valve where no floor is below the manhole-cover elevation.

questions.question: A circuit-vented branch receives five water closets and connects to a drainage stack that also receives waste from upper branches. What additional vent is required?

answers.text: A second circuit vent at the downstream end
A relief vent connecting between the stack and the most downstream fixture drain
An air admittance valve at each water closet
No additional vent — circuit venting is complete as installed

questions.explanation: A relief vent is required where a circuit-vented branch receives four or more water closets and connects to a stack receiving discharge from upper branches — five closets meets the trigger. It connects between the stack and the most downstream fixture drain; neither a duplicate circuit vent nor individual valves substitute for it.

questions.question: An installer proposes joining a CPVC distribution line to a PVC line with solvent cement, and supporting a branch with a saddle-type fitting. How many of these two proposals are permitted?

answers.text: Both are permitted
Neither — both are on the list of prohibited joints and connections
Only the saddle fitting
Only the solvent-cement joint between the two plastics

questions.explanation: The prohibited-joints list includes solvent-cement joints between different types of plastic pipe and saddle-type fittings, along with cement or concrete joints and joints made with fittings not approved for the installation. Both proposals on this job fall on that list.

questions.question: A combined primary-and-secondary roof drain assembly is installed so both systems share one common outlet body to save piping. What does the IPC require?

answers.text: A shared outlet is permitted if it is sized for both systems together and is provided with a cleanout where the two systems join above the roof drain body
A shared inlet is permitted if the outlets are independent and each outlet is sized for the full design flow of its own drainage system
Combined primary and secondary assemblies must have independent inlets and independent outlets
Independence is required only for scuppers, not for drain assemblies, because a drain body can be rodded from the roof when it becomes blocked

questions.explanation: A combined primary-plus-secondary assembly needs independent inlets and outlets, so a failure or blockage in the primary path cannot disable the secondary path that exists to back it up. Sharing an outlet, however generously sized, defeats that independence, and the rule applies to drain assemblies as well as scuppers.

questions.question: A 5-inch building sewer runs 320 feet from an existing cleanout at the building drain/building sewer junction. The sewer makes one change of horizontal direction greater than 45 degrees at the 160-foot point. What is the minimum number of additional cleanouts required?
questions.explanation: A cleanout is required at the change of direction, but placing one at 160 feet does not bridge the run: the stretch from the junction to the change is 160 feet, over the 100-foot interval for a sewer smaller than 8 inches, so one cleanout is needed before the change as well, and the 160-foot stretch beyond the change needs one more. Cleanouts at 100, 160 and 260 feet give segments of 100, 60, 100 and 60 feet, so three additional cleanouts is the minimum. Two cleanouts cannot satisfy the interval on both sides of the change at once.

questions.question: A CR-37 licensee tells a homeowner the dual license gives them the full residential scope of R-37 Plumbing, Including Solar. Why is that wrong?

answers.text: The dual license pairs the commercial C-37 scope with the R-37R residential scope, not with the R-37 including solar scope
The dual license covers commercial work only, and residential work needs the separate R-37 license
The dual license pairs C-37 with R-37 including solar, but solar work itself needs a C-78 license
The dual license actually pairs the C-77 scope with the R-37R scope, so the licensee has the pair backwards

questions.explanation: CR-37 combines the C-37 commercial scope with the R-37R residential scope, so its holder cannot claim the R-37 Including Solar scope through the dual license. The dual grade does include residential authority, so it is not commercial-only; its commercial side is C-37 rather than C-77; and the pairing with R-37 Including Solar that one choice assumes is precisely the pairing the Registrar's classification does not make.

questions.question: What is the renewal fee for an Arizona Specialty Commercial contractor's license for its two-year term?
questions.explanation: Specialty Commercial renewal is $480 for the two-year term. The $580 figure is the new-license total for that classification, which includes a first-time application fee that renewal does not carry; $540 and $650 are the residential and dual renewal totals.

alaska-plumbing.quiz_title: Alaska Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An estimator totals DFU for a small motel and then warns the owner that the drain will flow at exactly that many gallons per minute whenever the building is occupied. What is wrong with the warning?

answers.text: Nothing — DFU totals convert directly to a constant occupied flow
The warning understates flow; DFU must be doubled to get gpm
A DFU total is a probability-based design load, not a direct or constant flow rate
DFU applies only when the building is unoccupied

questions.explanation: The DFU system predicts probable peak load from discharge rate, duration, and interval between uses — it does not promise a constant flow whenever the building is occupied. No direct conversion or doubling rule turns a DFU total into a steady gpm figure, and the system exists precisely for occupied, intermittently used buildings.

questions.question: A client asks why the plumber's bathroom-group design does not run a separate dry vent up from every fixture, and whether the shared arrangement leaves any trap unprotected. Which answer is accurate?

answers.text: The shared arrangement is a shortcut that leaves the water closet trap unprotected, since no vent rises from the closet itself
The design wet-vents the bathroom group: an oversized drain serving one fixture vents another, so each trap is protected through the shared pipe
Any trap not on its own dry vent is by definition unprotected
The design relies on the building's single main vent alone to protect every trap in the group, with no local venting at all

questions.explanation: Wet venting is protection, not the absence of it: the oversized shared drain is sized so air passes above the flow, and that air path is what protects the connected traps — and a bathroom group may be wet-vented in both code families. The arrangement is a recognized method rather than a shortcut, dry vents are not the only form of protection, and the distant main vent by itself is not what protects these traps.

questions.question: A reduced-pressure principle assembly's relief port dribbles during a test after one check fouls with debris. Why does that discharge demonstrate the assembly is still protecting the supply?

answers.text: The port drains the supply line so pressure cannot build
The differential relief valve between the two independent checks opens and dumps the zone between them, so a fouled check cannot silently pass contamination through
The discharge proves both checks have failed and protection is lost
The relief valve is a pressure-reducing valve regulating the building

questions.explanation: The relief valve sits between the two independent checks and vents the intermediate zone when a check fouls or pressure reverses, giving the assembly its fail-safe margin beyond two checks alone. The discharge signals the protection working — not total failure — and the relief valve is not the building's pressure regulator.

questions.question: A 45° offset has a set of 9 inches. What is the travel length before fitting allowances?
questions.explanation: Travel = 9 × 1.414 = 12.726 ≈ 12.73 in. The 23.52 in. option uses the 22.5° multiplier, 9.00 in. is the run, and 6.36 in. divides by 1.414.

questions.question: A homeowner reports that ever since a pressure-reducing valve was installed last year, the house pressure creeps up overnight - after the evening's water heating, with no water being used - and the heater's relief valve occasionally drips. Nothing is wrong with the PRV's daytime readings. What is happening?

answers.text: The PRV is failing open overnight and must be replaced
Thermal expansion in the now-closed system: heated water cannot push back past the PRV, so pressure builds until the relief valve drips - an expansion tank is the correction
The city raises its street pressure at night, which the PRV cannot affect
The relief valve is oversized for the heater

questions.explanation: The pattern - pressure rising specifically after heating, in a system closed by the PRV - is trapped thermal expansion, and both codes require a means of controlling it, typically an expansion tank. A PRV holds its setpoint against street pressure day and night, so neither street pressure nor a failing PRV explains a heating-linked rise.

questions.question: An integral-trap urinal flushing 1.0 gallon per flush is installed in an assembly occupancy. What drainage fixture unit value does it carry?

answers.text: 6 DFU
5 DFU
2 DFU
3 DFU

questions.explanation: Urinals carry an assembly premium: the integral-trap 1.0 gpf urinal is 5 DFU in assembly use but only 2 DFU in private or public use. The 6 DFU assembly value belongs to the integral-trap urinal flushing more than 1.0 gpf.

questions.question: A bathroom group is laid out so a single vented lavatory provides the wet vent path for the rest of the group. Is that arrangement within the horizontal wet vent method?

answers.text: No — the wet vent for a group must always be provided by the bathtub
No — a lavatory may vent only itself and may never wet vent other fixtures
Yes, but only where the lavatory is the fixture farthest from the water closet
Yes — one or two vented lavatories may serve as the wet vent for a bathroom group

questions.explanation: The horizontal wet vent method expressly allows one or two vented lavatories to serve as the wet vent for the bathroom group. The bathtub is not the mandatory wet-venting fixture, a lavatory is not confined to venting itself under this method, and the lavatory's position relative to the water closet is not the qualifying condition stated.

questions.question: A 1-1/4-inch trap arm turns 30 degrees, then 30 degrees, then 30 degrees. With no cleanout, how much turning capacity remains?

answers.text: 30 degrees; each individual turn is counted separately
90 degrees; the cap resets after each fitting
None; the three turns already total the 90-degree limit.
45 degrees; small arms are allowed 135 degrees in total

questions.explanation: Direction change is cumulative along the arm: 30 plus 30 plus 30 reaches the 90-degree ceiling for arms under 3 inches. The 135-degree figure is reserved for larger arms, and the cap neither resets per fitting nor judges each turn in isolation.

questions.question: A specialty appliance needing a water supply does not appear in the fixture-unit table. How is its supply sizing determined?

answers.text: It is assigned 1.0 fixture unit by default until the manufacturer publishes a value
It is sized at the largest value in the table to be safe
It may be connected without sizing because unlisted fixtures carry no demand
It is sized by reference to a listed fixture having a similar flow rate and frequency of use

questions.explanation: Unlisted fixtures are sized by analogy to a listed fixture with a similar flow rate and frequency of use, so the demand estimate tracks how the appliance actually draws water. A flat default, the table maximum, or no sizing at all would each misstate the load in one direction or the other.

questions.question: Appliances in an enclosure have a combined input of 120,000 Btu/h, and combustion air is to be supplied by the standard indoor-volume method. What minimum room volume does the method require?

answers.text: 6,000 cubic feet
2,400 cubic feet
5,000 cubic feet
12,000 cubic feet

questions.explanation: The standard method requires 50 cubic feet of indoor volume per 1,000 Btu/h of total input: 120 thousands x 50 = 6,000 cubic feet. Doubling the rate gives the oversized 12,000 figure.

questions.question: What is the minimum passing score on the department's plumbing certificate examinations, and how long must a failed applicant wait before reexamination?

answers.text: 75 percent, with a 30-day wait before reexamination after failing
70 percent, with no waiting period before reexamination
80 percent, with a 90-day wait before reexamination after failing
70 percent, with a 30-day wait before reexamination after failing

questions.explanation: The minimum passing score is 70 percent, and an applicant who fails must wait 30 days before reexamination. Higher score thresholds and different waiting periods do not match the department rule.

questions.question: A restricted utility applicant claims 600 hours of military experience, 200 hours of trade-related classroom training, and 200 hours of qualifying line installation. How many hours are counted after the restricted utility caps are applied?

answers.text: 1,000 hours, because the claimed total equals the amount required
600 hours, because only the military experience is counted here
925 hours, because the classroom hours are not capped in this case
825 hours, because both capped categories are reduced to their limits

questions.explanation: For restricted utility, military or vocational experience is capped at 500 hours and trade-related classroom hours are capped at 125 hours. Counting 500 plus 125 plus the 200 installation hours gives 825 counted hours.

alabama-refrigeration.quiz_title: Alabama Refrigeration Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: How does a digital scroll compressor vary its capacity during a control cycle?

answers.text: It reverses the direction of the orbiting scroll for part of each cycle so compressed gas flows backward through the discharge port toward the suction side
It briefly separates the scrolls so compression stops for part of the cycle
It varies the voltage and frequency supplied to the motor so shaft speed changes continuously in direct proportion to the cooling load on the building
It opens and closes a hot-gas bypass valve in the discharge line while the scrolls themselves remain loaded and compressing at full displacement continuously

questions.explanation: A digital scroll uses a solenoid to axially separate the scrolls for timed intervals, so average capacity follows the loaded fraction of the cycle at constant speed. It does not reverse rotation, it is not a variable-frequency speed control, and its scrolls themselves unload rather than relying on a discharge hot-gas bypass.

questions.question: A belt-drive blower motor draws nameplate amps at its current sheave setting. A proposal would raise blower speed by 10 percent to gain airflow. What should the contractor verify before approving the change?

answers.text: Only that a longer belt is in stock, because a 10 percent speed change is small enough that motor loading can be assumed unchanged for planning purposes
That the motor has reserve capacity, since power rises about 33 percent
That the supply registers are adjustable, because register dampers alone can absorb any extra motor load created by the faster blower speed setting
That the thermostat has a fan switch, because continuous fan operation is the only approved way to keep a faster blower motor within its temperature rating

questions.explanation: Power rises with roughly the cube of speed, so 1.10 cubed is about 1.33, meaning roughly 33 percent more power for 10 percent more speed, and a motor already at nameplate amps has no reserve for that. Belt stock, register adjustment, and a fan switch do not address the motor loading the change creates.

questions.question: A system holds test pressure overall, but a slight odor near one union suggests a tiny leak to pinpoint. Which method fits propane service?

answers.text: Pass a lit lighter slowly around the union, because a small leak will lift the flame visibly before the surrounding vapor concentration can reach a hazardous level in open air
Drill a small sampling hole in the pipe beside the union, because direct access to the pipe interior gives the fastest confirmation of which side of the joint is leaking
Raise the test pressure to tank pressure with propane and listen for a hiss, because increasing the pressure is the standard way to make a suspected pinhole reveal itself
Apply approved leak-detection fluid to the joint and watch for bubbles, or use a combustible gas detector

questions.explanation: Approved noncorrosive leak fluid bubbling at a joint, or a combustible gas detector, pinpoints a leak without adding an ignition source or damaging the piping. A flame at a suspected leak is an ignition source at the worst location, drilling the pipe destroys its integrity, and raising pressure with fuel turns a search into a release.

questions.question: A helper installs a 25-foot flex duct run but leaves the inner core bunched up so the actual duct path uses only about 18 feet of stretched core, with the rest compressed into accordion folds. What is the most likely result?

answers.text: The compressed folds greatly increase friction, so delivered airflow falls well below what the same diameter of fully extended flex would deliver

Airflow increases because the compressed core makes the effective duct shorter, since the air has less distance to travel and the tight accordion folds smooth out as velocity rises during normal blower operation
Airflow is unchanged because flex duct friction does not depend on how it is installed
The run will deliver correct airflow but will be quieter than a stretched run

questions.explanation: Flex duct friction ratings assume the core is pulled fully extended; compressed accordion folds roughen the air path and can multiply the pressure drop. Option B is wrong because a compressed core does not behave like a shorter smooth duct — the folds add far more friction than the saved length removes; option C is wrong because installation condition is one of the biggest variables in flex duct performance; option D is wrong because the folds raise both friction and turbulence noise rather than quieting the run.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: A replacement furnace is connected to an existing chimney liner that is smaller than the sizing method requires for its input and connector run. Expect:

answers.text: Improved combustion, because a smaller liner speeds the flue gases and therefore guarantees complete burning of the gas at the burners
Spillage, poor draft, and possible carbon-monoxide entry
No change in operation, because the inducer or draft hood will automatically compensate for any liner size selected by the installer
Lower fuel use with no safety effect, because restricting the vent is equivalent to reducing the appliance input at the gas valve

questions.explanation: Spillage, poor draft, and possible carbon-monoxide entry. A small liner does not improve combustion or act like a gas-valve adjustment, and no appliance control can compensate for an undersized vent path.

questions.question: A 400-seat assembly hall is packed for an evening event but nearly empty most weekdays. Which ventilation approach fits this occupancy pattern?

answers.text: Demand-controlled ventilation — carbon dioxide sensing modulates outdoor air between a low base rate and full design rate with actual occupancy

Constant full-design outdoor air at all occupied hours, because variable occupancy is not a permitted reason to reduce ventilation air, with the outdoor-air dampers pinned at the design position and the carbon dioxide sensors removed to save calibration costs
Shutting outdoor air off entirely on weekdays, since a mostly empty hall needs no ventilation air whatsoever at any time
Recirculating the hall's air through a standard filter and counting the filtered portion as outdoor air for ventilation purposes

questions.explanation: CO2-based demand control matches outdoor air to the people actually present, saving energy on light days while delivering full air at events. Option B wastes energy the strategy exists to save, option C drops below the required base ventilation for the space and its building-related sources, and option D counts recirculated air as outdoor air, which it is not.

questions.question: A homeowner finished a 400-square-foot addition served by the existing system and now wants a changeout. What design step is required before selecting equipment?

answers.text: A new load calculation covering the enlarged conditioned space, rather than sizing from the original home alone
No calculation, because additions under 500 square feet are absorbed by the safety factor built into every residential system
Sizing by the addition's square footage at the same tons-per-square-foot ratio the original installer used decades ago
Selecting equipment one full ton larger than the old unit, which reliably covers any addition of this general size

questions.explanation: Added conditioned area changes the load and the room-by-room distribution, so a fresh calculation must include it. There is no automatic safety factor for additions, rules of thumb repeat old errors, and a flat one-ton bump is unrelated to the actual load.

questions.question: Lowering condenser-water temperature generally improves chiller efficiency, yet plants do not simply drive it as low as possible at all times. Why not?

answers.text: Because chiller efficiency always gets worse as condenser water gets colder, so the warmest possible water is the efficient choice, so plants should always run the warmest condenser water the tower and its controls can possibly deliver
Because refrigerant will freeze solid inside the condenser if the entering water drops even one degree below its design value
Because some chillers need a minimum condenser pressure to move refrigerant and oil properly, and extra tower-fan energy can exceed the chiller savings
Because cold condenser water makes the evaporator approach shrink to zero, which trips the chiller on low temperature

questions.explanation: There is an optimum: too little pressure differential starves refrigerant/oil management on some machines, and tower fans spend more energy than the chiller saves. Option A states the efficiency relationship backwards, option B invents a freezing failure that water temperature alone does not cause, and option D links condenser conditions to an evaporator trip that does not follow.

questions.question: What does a job-cost variance tell a contractor at the end of a project?

answers.text: Only the amount of sales tax collected, with no comparison between what was estimated and what was spent
The owner's overall satisfaction score, based on a survey sent after the final walkthrough is complete
Whether retainage will be released, based solely on the date the certificate of occupancy was issued
How actual costs compared with estimated costs, and where they differed

questions.explanation: D is correct because variance analysis compares actual job costs to the estimate to reveal overruns and savings by category. A is incorrect because sales tax collection alone does not compare estimated and actual performance. B is incorrect because a satisfaction survey is not a cost variance. C is incorrect because retainage release timing is a contract administration matter, not a cost comparison.

questions.question: A grocery operator asks a contractor to service two systems in the same store: a walk-in cooler holding dairy inventory and a packaged rooftop unit that keeps the sales floor comfortable for shoppers. Which statement correctly separates the work under Alabama's definition of refrigeration?

answers.text: Both systems are refrigeration work, because both use mechanical equipment to control temperature and both therefore fall under the refrigeration credential regardless of the purpose each system serves in the store., and the store's single mechanical permit is treated as covering both systems under one refrigeration classification for the whole premises.

The walk-in cooler work is refrigeration work, because refrigeration is the use of mechanical or absorption equipment to control temperature or humidity for the intended use of a space other than for human comfort, while the rooftop unit serves human comfort.

Neither system is refrigeration work, because equipment installed inside a retail building open to the public is classified by the building's occupancy rather than by the function the equipment performs for its owner.

The rooftop unit is the refrigeration work, because larger packaged equipment is treated as refrigeration plant, while a walk-in cooler is treated as a storage appliance that falls outside the refrigeration definition entirely.

questions.explanation: B is correct: Alabama defines refrigeration as the use of mechanical or absorption equipment to control temperature, humidity, or both, to satisfy the intended use of a specific space other than for human comfort, which captures the walk-in cooler but not the comfort-cooling rooftop unit. A is wrong because the human-comfort exclusion removes the rooftop unit from the definition even though it uses mechanical cooling. C is wrong because the definition turns on the equipment's function and purpose, not the building's occupancy class. D is wrong because equipment size does not control the classification and a walk-in cooler is core commercial refrigeration equipment.

questions.question: A corporation is being formed to install and service commercial walk-in coolers in Alabama. The owners ask how the corporation itself becomes authorized to do that work. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The corporation becomes authorized when it registers its articles of incorporation and obtains a federal employer identification number, a filing package the owners point to as proof the new corporation is fully licensed to contract.
The corporation is certified through its person in responsible charge, and the certification issues in that person's name together with the corporation's name.
Each corporate officer must separately pass the refrigeration examination before the corporation may contract for any work.
The corporation needs no individual qualifier because a corporation is treated as its own certified contractor under Alabama law.

questions.explanation: B is correct: Alabama entity certification runs through a person in responsible charge; the application names the entity and its officers, and the certification issues in the name of the person in responsible charge and includes the name of the business organization. A is wrong: Corporate registration and a tax ID create the business entity but confer no HACR certification. C is wrong: The law requires a qualified person in responsible charge, not an examination for every officer. D is wrong: A legal entity cannot qualify itself; it acts through the certified person in responsible charge.

utah-hvac.quiz_title: Utah HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: After a hermetic compressor burnout, a replacement compressor is installed. Beyond changing the liquid-line drier, what contamination follow-up protects the new compressor?

answers.text: Test the oil/system for acid and fit suction-side filtration, then recheck and remove it as cleanup is confirmed
Do nothing further, because a single liquid-line drier change always removes all acid and debris left in the system by a hermetic motor burnout
Flush the new compressor itself with solvent before startup, because flushing a hermetic unit internally is the standard way to remove burnout contamination
Raise the operating superheat substantially for the first month, because running hot is an accepted substitute for removing acid from a contaminated system

questions.explanation: Burnout leaves acid and debris throughout the system, so acid testing plus temporary suction filtration with follow-up checks is the accepted cleanup approach. One drier change rarely completes a burnout cleanup, flushing inside a new hermetic compressor is not a service procedure, and running hot does not neutralize or remove acid and can harm the new machine.

questions.question: A 3-ton R-410A split A/C cools poorly on a 92°F day. Readings: suction 98 psig, head 282 psig, suction superheat 24°F, liquid subcooling 3°F, compressor amps 78% of rated, evaporator coil clean, airflow verified at 400 cfm/ton, and no temperature drop across the liquid-line drier. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Noncondensables trapped in the condenser after a poor evacuation, which would drive head pressure and subcooling well above normal rather than low
Severely reduced evaporator airflow from a clogged filter or coil, which would pull superheat down toward 2–5°F instead of leaving it at 24°F
A restricted liquid-line filter drier, which would show a measurable temperature drop and often frost at the drier outlet while subcooling stayed high
Low refrigerant charge

questions.explanation: Low suction and head pressures together with high superheat and very low subcooling is the classic undercharge pattern: the evaporator is starved and little liquid backs up in the condenser. A drier restriction is ruled out by the absence of a temperature drop across it and by the low subcooling, low airflow would lower superheat rather than raise it, and noncondensables would raise head pressure and subcooling, the opposite of these readings.

questions.question: During a heat pump defrost cycle on a cold day, occupants feel cooler air from the registers for a few minutes. What is the system doing, and what should already be configured to limit that effect?

answers.text: The system has failed and the reversing valve must be replaced before any heat returns

The indoor blower should stop for the entire defrost so no air moves at all, leaving the coil to absorb heat with no airflow and no auxiliary tempering until the outdoor coil is completely clear of frost
The outdoor unit is temporarily in cooling to melt frost from its coil, and auxiliary heat should be energized during defrost to temper the supply air
The thermostat has switched to emergency heat permanently for the season

questions.explanation: Defrost reverses the cycle so hot gas melts outdoor frost, which means the indoor coil briefly absorbs heat, and staging auxiliary heat during defrost offsets the cold blow. Option A treats a normal cycle as a failure, option B is not the standard strategy and leaves melt conditions unmanaged while the house gets no tempered air, and option D confuses a minutes-long cycle with a manual emergency-heat selection.

questions.question: A bedroom is noisy and drafts are felt at the bed, though airflow volume is correct. The supply register is a small, high-velocity outlet aimed at the bed. What is the best correction?

answers.text: Close the register halfway and accept the reduced airflow delivered to that bedroom
Increase blower speed
Select a larger register with proper throw and spread for the CFM
Remove the return grille

questions.explanation: Correct volume delivered through too small an outlet creates excess velocity, noise, and drafts; a properly sized register with suitable throw fixes it, so C is correct. Closing it cuts needed airflow, raising blower speed worsens noise, and removing the return does not address supply selection.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: A tight new house with an atmospherically vented water heater needs mechanical ventilation. Exhaust-only ventilation is proposed, which would depressurize the house and could backdraft the water heater. What design response best addresses that concern?

answers.text: Exhaust-only systems raise indoor humidity in every climate by pulling outdoor air through the walls, so they can never be used in a tight house at all
Use balanced ventilation instead
Exhaust fans wear out faster in tight houses because they run against higher pressure, so the design concern is mainly fan service life and replacement cost
Any ventilation system makes the water heater backdraft continuously, so the only safe design is to provide no mechanical ventilation in this house

questions.explanation: Exhaust-only ventilation depressurizes a tight house and can backdraft a natural-draft water heater, so balanced ventilation, or a sealed-combustion appliance, removes that conflict. Infiltration through an exhaust-depressurized house does not raise humidity in every climate, fan wear is secondary to the combustion-safety issue, and ventilation can be provided safely with the right configuration rather than omitted.

questions.question: A Utah HVAC business asks which state agency administers contractor licensing under the Utah Construction Trades Licensing Act. Which agency is correct?

answers.text: The Utah Labor Commission, acting through its workplace safety division
A county licensing board in the county where the business is located
The Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing in the Department of Labor
The Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL), within the Department of Commerce

questions.explanation: Contractor licensing in Utah is administered by DOPL, the Division of Professional Licensing within the Department of Commerce, under the Utah Construction Trades Licensing Act and its licensing rule.

questions.question: A candidate for the Utah H100 license asks who administers the required licensing examinations. Who does?

answers.text: The Division of Professional Licensing, which writes and scores every exam itself
The Associated General Contractors of Utah, as the approved course provider
Each approved prelicensure school, at the end of its own course
Prov, Inc., the examination vendor for the Utah HVAC examinations

questions.explanation: Prov administers the Utah HVAC examinations; DOPL is the licensing regulator, not the exam vendor.

questions.question: How is an H100 HVAC Contractor license held in Utah?

answers.text: By each individual technician, who must hold a personal H100 license
By the business owner personally, with no qualifier required
By the business, through a designated H100 Qualifier
By a master HVAC tradesperson employed full-time by the business

questions.explanation: The H100 is a contractor license held by the business through a designated H100 Qualifier.

questions.question: An experienced out-of-state HVAC journeyman moves to Utah and asks about getting a Utah journeyman or master HVAC license. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: Utah has no journeyman or master HVAC license; the H100 is a contractor license
Utah issues a master HVAC license once an applicant passes the journeyman exam and documents two additional years of supervised trade experience in the state
Utah has no contractor HVAC license at all; instead, each individual tradesperson is licensed at either the journeyman or the master level
Utah issues a journeyman HVAC license through Prov, and the H100 qualifier must personally hold that journeyman license before the business can be licensed

questions.explanation: Utah has no journeyman/master HVAC trade license; H100 is a contractor license held through a qualifier.

questions.question: A crew normally installs 10 supply boots per day, but a cramped attic job is expected to slow production by 25%. How should the estimator adjust labor?

answers.text: Reduce the labor hours in the estimate, because difficult access is assumed to make experienced crews work faster
Increase estimated labor hours to reflect lower productivity
Leave labor unchanged and reduce the material quantity instead, even though the same number of boots is required
Remove the labor burden from the estimate, because burden does not apply when working conditions are difficult

questions.explanation: B is correct because lower productivity means more hours are needed to install the same quantity of work. A is incorrect because slower conditions increase, rather than decrease, the hours required. C is incorrect because the quantity of boots stays the same; it is the time per boot that changes. D is incorrect because payroll burden applies to labor regardless of site difficulty.

questions.question: A prime contractor plans to rely on a subcontractor's price in its bid. What should the prime contractor confirm before submitting that bid?

answers.text: That the subcontractor will accept a materially lower price after award in exchange for the promise of future work on other projects the prime contractor may win
That the subcontractor's price covers the assigned scope, terms, and qualifications, and that the subcontractor can perform as priced
That the subcontractor's name can be withheld from the bid documents until the contract is signed
That the subcontractor submitted the lowest price received, with no review of scope or qualifications at all

questions.explanation: Before relying on a subcontractor's number, the prime contractor confirms the price covers the assigned scope on the stated terms and that the subcontractor is able to perform. Price alone, with no scope check, invites gaps and defaults.

oklahoma-hvac.quiz_title: Oklahoma HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Why can a heat pump's seasonal heating rating not be judged from its COP at one mild rating point alone?

answers.text: Because the single-point COP is measured with the auxiliary heat fully energized, so it already includes the worst winter condition the system will ever operate under
Because mild-point COP is always lower than cold-weather COP, meaning the seasonal figure would only improve if judged across the full range of winter conditions
Because COP is a cooling-only measure and has no valid application to heat pump heating performance at any outdoor temperature or operating condition whatsoever
Seasonal performance also reflects cold snaps, defrost, and auxiliary heat use

questions.explanation: Heating COP drops as outdoor temperature falls, and a real season adds defrost cycles and auxiliary heat operation, all of which a seasonal rating integrates but a single mild point ignores. The mild point is tested without full auxiliary heat, COP is higher rather than lower in mild weather, and COP applies to heating as well as cooling.

questions.question: A system cools the air temperature adequately but humidity stays near 65%. Readings: airflow measured at 485 cfm/ton, air-side temperature split only 13°F, superheat 9°F, subcooling 10°F, pressures normal, coil clean, and condensate barely drips except on the hottest afternoons. What adjustment does the evidence support?

answers.text: Install a larger evaporator coil, a major change that does nothing about air moving too fast for moisture to condense on the coil surface
Increase blower speed further to move more air across the coil, which would raise coil temperature even more and strip off still less moisture
Add refrigerant to drop the suction pressure and coil temperature, which would corrupt the currently correct superheat and subcooling values
Reduce blower speed to lower airflow per ton

questions.explanation: Excessive airflow per ton keeps the coil too warm and the split too small for sustained condensation, which the 13°F split and 485 cfm/ton prove. Slowing the blower lowers coil temperature and lengthens moisture contact; speeding it up worsens the problem, adding charge falsifies good readings, and a bigger coil does not fix air velocity.

questions.question: Which practice is correct for oil line joints on the suction side of the system?

answers.text: Use ordinary compression fittings and canvas tape, because suction joints do not need to be airtight for the burner to prime well
Use flare fittings and avoid excess sealant in the line
Apply generous Teflon tape inside every flare nut so loose threads are packed tight and any air path is filled by the tape bulk
Solder suction joints with plumbing flux in place, because heat-sealed joints are the standard method for oil suction piping runs

questions.explanation: Suction joints must be airtight; flare fittings are the standard practice and sealant must be kept out of the oil stream where shreds can foul valves and nozzles. Option A accepts leaky compression joints that cause loss of prime, option C puts tape where it can shed into the fuel, and option D describes a nonstandard heated joint method for this piping.

questions.question: Total effective length in Manual D is best described as:

answers.text: The length of the longest duct only, ignoring all fittings, elbows, and takeoff losses along that run
The measured length of the longest supply-return path plus equivalent lengths of its fittings
The sum of every branch in the house
The length of the line set

questions.explanation: Total effective length combines the actual run length of the critical path with fitting equivalent lengths that represent their resistance, so B is correct. A ignores fitting losses, C sums non-critical branches, and D refers to refrigerant piping, not ducts.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: What is the basic purpose of whole-dwelling mechanical ventilation under residential ventilation guidance such as ASHRAE 62.2?

answers.text: To replace all mechanical heating and cooling with outdoor air throughout the year, in every season and in every climate, without any supplemental conditioning
To pressurize the house so no air can ever leave
To provide controlled outdoor air to dilute indoor pollutants and maintain acceptable indoor air quality
To remove the need for any local kitchen or bathroom exhaust

questions.explanation: Controlled outdoor air dilutes pollutants that build up in tight homes, which is the purpose of whole-dwelling ventilation. It supplements rather than replaces heating and cooling. No practical system seals a house against all exfiltration, and local exhaust for moisture and cooking sources is still required alongside whole-dwelling air.

questions.question: A trench for underground piping was inspected in the morning, and a heavy rainstorm passed through the site at midday. The crew returns to continue piping after the storm. What must happen first?

answers.text: Work resumes immediately, because a trench that passed a morning inspection remains approved for the rest of that working day under all conditions
Only the piping already installed needs checking, since rainfall affects finished pipe joints but cannot change the stability of the trench walls themselves
The crew should pump any standing water onto the spoil pile, which strengthens the pile and the trench edge for the remainder of the excavation work
The competent person re-inspects the trench before workers re-enter

questions.explanation: Rain can saturate soil and undermine walls and spoil, so the competent person must re-inspect before re-entry after a storm. A morning approval does not survive a condition change, water affects the excavation itself and not just the pipe, and dumping water on the spoil pile adds weight at the edge.

questions.question: How much upward slope must a vent connector have as it runs toward the chimney or vent?

answers.text: One-quarter inch per foot
One inch per foot
One-eighth inch per foot
No slope is permitted in a vent connector

questions.explanation: A vent connector must rise at least one-quarter inch per foot toward the chimney or vent so flue gases flow upward and do not stagnate in the connector.

questions.question: Which board licenses mechanical work in Oklahoma?

answers.text: A county licensing board in the county where the work is performed
The Oklahoma State Board of Mechanical Examiners acting alone
The Department of Labor mechanical division
The Oklahoma Construction Industries Board (CIB)

questions.explanation: Oklahoma mechanical licensing is administered by the Construction Industries Board, which licenses mechanical work under state law and rule.

questions.question: In general terms, a performance bond on a project guarantees which of the following?

answers.text: That the equipment will operate at its advertised efficiency rating in the customer's building for its full service life
That the contractor will complete the contract, backed by a surety if it defaults
That employees will receive benefits if they are injured while performing work covered under the bonded contract
That the owner will never owe progress payments until every punch-list item on the project has been fully corrected

questions.explanation: B is correct because a performance bond backs the contractor's completion of the contract, with the surety stepping in on default. A is incorrect because equipment efficiency over its life is a product performance matter, not a bond guarantee. C is incorrect because employee injury benefits are provided by workers' compensation insurance. D is incorrect because progress payment timing is a contract term, not something a performance bond eliminates.

questions.question: A lender asks a contractor to demonstrate short-term financial strength. Which measure addresses the ability to pay current obligations with current resources?

answers.text: Working capital, the excess of current assets over current liabilities
The original purchase price of the company's vehicles and shop equipment
The total dollar value of all bids the contractor currently has outstanding
Gross profit on completed contracts, stated before any overhead is deducted

questions.explanation: Working capital — current assets minus current liabilities — measures the resources available to meet the company's short-term obligations.

questions.question: The specifications state that motor starters are furnished under the mechanical division and installed under the electrical division. A starter is missing at rough-in inspection. Why does that split matter for resolving the problem?

answers.text: It defines which trade furnishes and which trade installs the starter
It means neither trade is responsible, because any item mentioned by two divisions is automatically supplied by the building owner after occupancy
It proves the starter was deleted from the project, since equipment cannot legally be furnished by one trade and installed by another trade
It transfers the inspection failure to the general contractor's safety record, after which the starter no longer needs to be provided at all

questions.explanation: Division-of-work language assigns furnishing and installing responsibility, which is exactly what resolves a missing-item dispute. Split responsibility is common and enforceable, it does not make the owner the supplier, and it does not erase the requirement after an inspection finding.

nevada-hvac.quiz_title: Nevada HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Hot-gas bypass gas is introduced directly into the suction line far from the evaporator on a system that then logs oil in the evaporator during long bypass hours. Why can the injection point matter?

answers.text: Bypass into the distributor or evaporator inlet keeps refrigerant velocity through the coil up, helping oil return, while suction-only injection can leave coil velocity too low
The injection point never matters, because hot gas entering anywhere in the low side produces identical evaporator velocities and identical oil-return behavior at all loads
Injecting into the suction line raises evaporator velocity the most, because the gas passes through the entire coil twice before it reaches the compressor inlet
Injecting at the distributor stops all oil movement in the coil, because the added gas pressure holds the oil stationary against the tube walls during bypass operation

questions.explanation: Feeding bypass gas through the coil maintains mass flow and velocity that sweep oil back, whereas suction-line-only injection satisfies the compressor while the coil itself sees very low flow and can log oil. Injection location changes coil velocity and oil behavior materially, suction-only gas does not pass through the coil at all, and distributor injection promotes rather than prevents oil movement through the coil.

questions.question: After a motor sheave is opened to raise airflow by about 20 percent on a belt-drive blower, the motor now trips its overload after an hour of running. What best explains the overload?

answers.text: The new belt is slightly longer than the old one, and the added belt length alone raises motor current steadily until the overload device opens on every run
Opening a sheave reduces motor load in all cases, so the trips must come from a failing overload device that should simply be replaced with a larger one
Fan power rises roughly with the cube of speed, overloading the motor
The overload trips because higher airflow cools the motor less effectively, since faster supply air bypasses the motor compartment on this style of blower housing

questions.explanation: By the fan laws, power rises with roughly the cube of speed, so a 20 percent speed increase demands about 73 percent more power and can overload a motor that was near its rating. Belt length does not add that load, sheave increases raise rather than reduce load, and the cooling explanation reverses how these motors are cooled.

questions.question: Tank pressure on a warm afternoon is well over 100 psi, yet the appliances need gas at inches of water column. What does the first-stage regulator in a typical two-stage system do?

answers.text: It cuts tank pressure to about 10 psi for the yard line
It raises tank pressure before the second stage, because appliance regulators need a boosted inlet pressure whenever outdoor temperature climbs in the afternoon
It delivers the final appliance manifold pressure directly, so no second regulation stage is needed anywhere between an outdoor tank and the indoor burners
It vents excess tank pressure to the atmosphere continuously, holding the yard line at appliance pressure by releasing whatever vapor the tank produces above demand

questions.explanation: The first-stage regulator reduces variable tank pressure to an intermediate pressure, commonly around 10 psi, for the line to the building. Final reduction to inches of water column is left to the second stage, and regulators reduce and control pressure rather than boosting it or venting vapor continuously.

questions.question: A technician sets the closed-position stop on non-calling zone dampers so each blade leaks a small amount of air instead of sealing fully. What is the purpose, and the cost?

answers.text: The leak prevents damper blades from sticking after long idle periods, and its cost is the motor wear caused by the panel driving the blades against the stop repeatedly
The bleed relieves some excess pressure, at the cost of conditioning zones that are not calling
The leak equalizes humidity between zones, and its cost is that satisfied zones slowly take on the moisture load of calling zones through the shared return system
The bleed raises total airflow so the smallest zone can be served without a bypass, and its cost is that the equipment must be oversized for the whole house to feed the leakage

questions.explanation: Leaving non-calling dampers slightly open gives excess air additional paths, which trims static pressure when few zones call. The trade-off is real: satisfied zones receive conditioned air they did not ask for, while blade sticking, humidity transfer, and equipment sizing are not the purpose or the cost of the setting.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: After responders clear a carbon monoxide incident, what must happen before the gas furnace returns to normal service?

answers.text: The furnace may restart immediately once the alarm stops, because silence proves the earlier reading was a transient sensor malfunction
Only the thermostat batteries need changing, since low batteries are the most common cause of genuine carbon monoxide production in furnaces
A qualified technician must find and correct the source, verify safe combustion and venting, and confirm carbon monoxide is not being produced or spilled.
The vent connector should be sealed with tape and the furnace run at high fire for an hour to burn out any residue in the heat exchanger

questions.explanation: Clearing the building air does not fix the appliance fault; the cause, such as a blocked vent, cracked heat exchanger, or negative-pressure spillage, must be repaired and verified. A silent alarm does not prove safety, batteries do not cause carbon monoxide production, and taping a vent and over-firing a suspect furnace is dangerous.

questions.question: A straight ladder must reach a roof edge 20 feet above the ground. Using the 4-to-1 setup rule, how far from the building should the ladder base sit?

answers.text: The base sits 20 feet from the building, found by matching the base distance one-for-one with the working height of the ladder.
The base sits 10 feet from the building, found by halving the working height to reach the standard setup distance for the ladder.
The base sits 2 feet from the building, found by allowing one foot of base distance for every ten feet of working height reached.
The base sits 5 feet from the building.

questions.explanation: The 4-to-1 rule sets the base out one foot for every four feet of height to the support point: 20 divided by 4 equals 5 feet from the building.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how contractor licensing and examinations are handled in Nevada?

answers.text: The Nevada State Contractors Board administers all examinations itself, and PSI's role is limited to issuing licenses to candidates the Board has approved.
Eligibility for examination is determined by PSI, and the Nevada State Contractors Board issues licenses only after PSI approves each candidate's experience.
PSI determines which applicants are eligible for licensure, while the Nevada State Contractors Board only administers the examinations at its own testing centers.
The Nevada State Contractors Board governs licensing under state law and determines eligibility for examination, while PSI administers the examinations.

questions.explanation: The Board governs licensing and decides who is eligible to test, and PSI is the testing service that administers the examinations. Fact 1 assigns eligibility to the Board and administration to PSI.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the scope of subclassification C-21b Air Conditioning?

answers.text: C-21b covers the installation, repair, service and maintenance of equipment using evaporation, refrigeration, boilers or combustion to control air temperatures in structures, including related ductwork and controls.
C-21b covers only the repair and replacement of parts of existing air-conditioning units, and it never covers new equipment installation work.

C-21b covers the fabrication and installation of sheet metal products, including ducts, louvres, patented chimneys and metal roof systems for buildings, together with the fabrication and installation of metal roof systems, patented chimneys, flashings and gutters for those structures.
C-21b covers controlling air temperatures below 50 degrees Fahrenheit in refrigerators, refrigerated rooms and insulated storage spaces only.

questions.explanation: C-21b covers the installation, repair, service and maintenance of equipment using evaporation, refrigeration, boilers or combustion to control air temperatures in structures, including related ductwork and controls. It is not limited to repair of existing units, it is not the sheet-metal subclassification, and it is not limited to refrigeration below 50 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.question: An estimator adds a modest contingency line inside a bid for a retrofit with concealed conditions. What is the contingency meant to cover?

answers.text: Reasonable unforeseen conditions within the defined scope
The contractor's entire annual overhead shortfall if billable hours fall below the forecast for the year
Profit the contractor wants to protect even if no additional cost of any kind is ever encountered
Work the owner has already described as a definite extra that should be listed as a separate line item

questions.explanation: A is correct because contingency addresses uncertainty in conditions that fall within the defined scope of the work. B is incorrect because overhead shortfall is recovered through the overhead rate, not job contingency. C is incorrect because profit is a separate bid component, not the purpose of contingency. D is incorrect because a known, definite extra should be priced explicitly rather than buried in contingency.

questions.question: SCENARIO: A technician's gross wages for a week are $1,600. The employer's payroll burden given for that week — employer payroll taxes, workers' compensation and benefits combined — totals 25 percent of gross wages. What is the employer's total labor cost for that technician for the week?

answers.text: The total labor cost is $2,400, since the burden adds 50 percent of gross wages to the week's payroll.
The total labor cost is $2,000, since the burden adds $400 to the $1,600 in gross wages.
The total labor cost is $1,600, since the burden is withheld from the technician's own paycheck in full.
