The total labor cost is $1,840, since the burden adds 15 percent of gross wages to the amount the technician earns that week, and the remaining share of the burden is billed to the customer as a separate direct charge.

questions.explanation: Burden = 25 percent of $1,600 = $400, and $1,600 + $400 = $2,000 in total labor cost. The key carries that computation.

questions.question: A duct section drawing gives the bottom of a main at 9 feet 6 inches above the floor, and the reflected ceiling plan shows a ceiling at 9 feet. The electrical plan places light fixtures in the same bay. What problem does comparing these drawings reveal?

answers.text: No problem exists, because ductwork drawn above a ceiling line can always pass through light fixtures as long as the fixtures are recessed types
The ceiling must be raised above the duct by the ceiling contractor without any coordination, since ceiling height always yields to mechanical drawings
The fixtures are at fault by default, because electrical drawings are drawn last and therefore carry the lowest priority in every space conflict on a project
Only 6 inches separate duct bottom from ceiling, leaving a tight coordination zone

questions.explanation: Comparing the section, ceiling plan, and electrical plan shows just 6 inches between the duct bottom and the ceiling for fittings, hangers, and fixtures to share. Duct cannot pass through fixtures, ceiling heights are a coordinated design decision, and drawing order does not set conflict priority.

new-mexico-hvac.quiz_title: New Mexico HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: On a pressure-enthalpy diagram for a vapor-compression cycle, what do the two axes represent?

answers.text: Temperature on the vertical axis and entropy on the horizontal axis, so every heat transfer process in the cycle is read as a change in entropy alone
Pressure on the horizontal axis and volume on the vertical axis, with enthalpy calculated afterward from a separate table for each plotted state point
Suction pressure on one axis and discharge pressure on the other, so compressor ratio can be read directly without knowing any heat content values at all
Pressure vertically and enthalpy horizontally

questions.explanation: A pressure-enthalpy chart plots pressure on the vertical axis against enthalpy on the horizontal axis, letting cycle work and refrigeration effect be read as enthalpy differences. Temperature-entropy and pressure-volume diagrams are different charts, and the two pressures alone do not define the cycle states.

questions.question: A 3-ton R-410A split A/C cools poorly on a 92°F day. Readings: suction 98 psig, head 282 psig, suction superheat 24°F, liquid subcooling 3°F, compressor amps 78% of rated, evaporator coil clean, airflow verified at 400 cfm/ton, and no temperature drop across the liquid-line drier. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Noncondensables trapped in the condenser after a poor evacuation, which would drive head pressure and subcooling well above normal rather than low
Severely reduced evaporator airflow from a clogged filter or coil, which would pull superheat down toward 2–5°F instead of leaving it at 24°F
A restricted liquid-line filter drier, which would show a measurable temperature drop and often frost at the drier outlet while subcooling stayed high
Low refrigerant charge

questions.explanation: Low suction and head pressures together with high superheat and very low subcooling is the classic undercharge pattern: the evaporator is starved and little liquid backs up in the condenser. A drier restriction is ruled out by the absence of a temperature drop across it and by the low subcooling, low airflow would lower superheat rather than raise it, and noncondensables would raise head pressure and subcooling, the opposite of these readings.

questions.question: Why does a cubic foot of propane need far more combustion air by volume than a cubic foot of natural gas, even though air needs per unit of heat are similar?

answers.text: Propane molecules contain no carbon, so extra air is needed to supply carbon for a stable flame at the burner ports during normal operation
Each cubic foot of propane carries much more heat and fuel to burn
Natural gas burners use no primary or secondary air at all, so the comparison is between propane burners that need air and natural gas burners that burn in a vacuum jacket
Propane air requirements are set by the tank pressure alone, so a cubic foot from a warm tank needs more air than the same cubic foot from a cold tank in winter

questions.explanation: Combustion air follows the amount of fuel burned, and a cubic foot of propane contains more than twice the fuel energy of a cubic foot of natural gas. Per unit of heat released the air requirement is broadly similar for the two gases, propane does contain carbon, and tank temperature changes pressure rather than the chemistry of a cubic foot of vapor.

questions.question: One bedroom is always warm in cooling while the rest of the house is comfortable. Its register delivers about 18 CFM against a design of roughly 95 CFM; all other registers measure near design, system static pressure is normal, and the branch damper is verified open. In the attic, that bedroom's flex duct makes a sharp bend at a truss and is visibly crushed where it crosses it. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: The kinked and crushed flex branch duct serving that room
A system-wide airflow shortage from the blower, which would depress airflow at every register in the house rather than leave all but one branch at its design flow
A closed zone damper starving one side of the house, ruled out because the branch damper is verified open and neighboring branches on the same trunk measure normally
An undersized supply trunk for the whole system, which would show elevated static pressure and broadly weak registers instead of one crushed branch at normal static

questions.explanation: Only the one branch is starved, total static is normal, and the physical inspection finds that branch kinked and crushed at a truss, throttling its roughly 95 CFM design flow down to 18 CFM. A blower or trunk problem would depress many registers and change static pressure, and the branch damper is proven open.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: What defines a dedicated outdoor air system (DOAS)?

answers.text: It is any rooftop unit whose nameplate includes the word 'dedicated' in the manufacturer's model number designation
It is a transfer fan that moves air from a corridor into restrooms so those rooms need no exhaust duct of their own
It is the kitchen makeup-air unit only, because no other system in a commercial building is ever dedicated to a single air stream
A separate system that handles the outdoor (ventilation) air — often conditioning it to a neutral, dehumidified state — while other equipment handles the space's sensible loads

questions.explanation: A DOAS decouples ventilation from space conditioning, delivering treated outdoor air while terminal or local equipment meets sensible loads. Option A makes a nameplate word the definition, option C wrongly limits the concept to one kitchen appliance, and option B describes transfer air, not a system that conditions the building's outdoor air.

questions.question: Refrigerant piping passes through wood framing and runs exposed where it can be struck in a garage. What protection is required?

answers.text: No protection is needed once the system holds pressure, because a passing pressure test also proves the piping can withstand vehicle impact
Soft copper may be notched into the face of a stud without a plate, provided the notch is filled later with construction adhesive
Piping in a garage should be buried in the concrete slab without a sleeve so vehicles cannot reach it under any circumstances
Shield plates at framing penetrations where piping is close to the edge, and guards or placement that protects piping from physical damage.

questions.explanation: Piping near a framing edge must be shielded from nails and screws, and exposed piping subject to impact must be protected. A pressure test says nothing about impact resistance, unshielded notching invites fastener damage, and unsleeved burial is not the required protection method.

questions.question: Air moves through a duct at 800 feet per minute, and the duct cross-sectional area is 1.5 square feet. What is the airflow volume?

answers.text: The airflow volume is 800 cubic feet per minute.
The airflow volume is 1,000 cubic feet per minute.
The airflow volume is 12,600 cubic feet per minute.
The airflow volume is 1,200 cubic feet per minute.

questions.explanation: Airflow equals velocity multiplied by area: 800 feet per minute × 1.5 square feet = 1,200 cubic feet per minute.

questions.question: Which state office licenses HVAC contractors in New Mexico?

answers.text: The Construction Industries Division of the Regulation and Licensing Department licenses HVAC contractors in New Mexico
HVAC contractors in New Mexico are licensed by the Public Regulation Commission through its transportation and utilities bureau
HVAC contractors in New Mexico are licensed directly by the State Personnel Office under a general occupational permit program
HVAC contractors in New Mexico are licensed by each county clerk in the county where the contractor maintains its main office

questions.explanation: New Mexico places contractor licensing in the Construction Industries Division of the Regulation and Licensing Department.

questions.question: Why should a contractor compare the estimate with final job costs on every completed project?

answers.text: To satisfy a supplier requirement that estimates be filed with the wholesaler before the next material order is placed
To set the amount of retainage on the next unrelated project for a different owner in a different market
To improve future estimates and identify recurring cost errors
To determine each employee's income tax withholding for the final payroll of the completed project

questions.explanation: C is correct because estimate-versus-actual review feeds lessons back into future pricing and exposes repeated estimating errors. A is incorrect because suppliers do not require filing internal estimate reviews to place orders. B is incorrect because retainage on another project is set by that project's contract, not this review. D is incorrect because withholding is a payroll function based on tax rules, not a post-job cost review.

questions.question: SCENARIO (computed): A job's total cost is $80,000. The contractor wants a selling price that yields a 25 percent margin on the selling price. What price achieves that margin?

answers.text: A price of $96,000 achieves a 25 percent margin on the selling price for a job costing $80,000 in total, since adding one quarter of cost is the standard margin formula
A price of $100,000 achieves a 25 percent margin on the selling price, since cost divided by one minus the margin gives the required price for this job's figures
A price of $106,667 achieves a 25 percent margin on the selling price
A price of $120,000 achieves a 25 percent margin on the selling price, since margin is computed by doubling the markup percentage and adding it to cost

questions.explanation: Margin is measured on the selling price: price = cost / (1 − 0.25) = $80,000 / 0.75 = $106,667, and $26,667 is 25 percent of that price. Adding 25 percent of cost ($100,000) yields only a 20 percent margin.

questions.question: On a duct layout, a small diamond symbol on a branch duct is noted as a volume damper, and the branch serves a room that is overheating. What does that symbol tell the balancing technician?

answers.text: An adjustable damper at that location can throttle the branch
The branch contains a fire damper that must be removed from the airstream before any additional cooling can reach the overheated room
The diamond marks a test port where static pressure is recorded once at startup and the branch airflow itself can never be adjusted afterward
The branch is a spare takeoff capped inside the main, and the overheating must be corrected by increasing total fan speed for the whole system

questions.explanation: The symbol identifies an adjustable volume damper the technician can throttle to reduce airflow to the overheating room. It is not a fire damper, a fixed test port, or a capped spare, and raising total fan speed would add air where it is not wanted.

new-jersey-hvac.quiz_title: New Jersey HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A moisture indicator in the sight glass has turned its wet color, and the system has just been opened for a compressor change. Which action set correctly responds to the indication?

answers.text: Ignore the color for the first month, because a moisture indicator always shows wet immediately after any repair until the refrigerant has circulated for several weeks
Add a liquid drying agent chemical to the charge, because chemical driers are the preferred substitute for evacuation and a new filter drier after the system has been opened
Replace the liquid-line drier, evacuate deeply and verify with a micron gauge and decay check, then recheck the indicator after operation
Raise the head pressure by blocking condenser airflow until the indicator dries out, because heat alone drives moisture out of a system that remains sealed and pressurized

questions.explanation: A wet indication after an open repair calls for a fresh drier and a verified deep vacuum to actually remove the moisture, with the indicator rechecked once running. The color reflects real moisture rather than a normal month-long artifact, chemical additives are not a substitute for evacuation and filtration, and heating a sealed wet system does not remove water from it.

questions.question: A 5-ton system serves a 1,250 sq ft home whose calculated load is 2 tons. It satisfies the thermostat in 6-minute cycles, indoor humidity sits at 68%, supply air is cold, and all pressures, superheat, subcooling, and airflow per ton are normal. Occupants complain the home feels clammy. What is the correct diagnosis?

answers.text: Oversized equipment short-cycling
A blower speed set far too low, which would lengthen runtimes and wring out more moisture, the opposite of the 6-minute cycles observed
A dirty evaporator coil reducing dehumidification, which would distort airflow and superheat readings that here are entirely normal
Low refrigerant charge causing poor latent removal, which is contradicted by the normal superheat, subcooling, and pressures measured on this call

questions.explanation: Normal refrigerant readings with very short cycles and high indoor humidity are the signature of gross oversizing: sensible load is met before the coil runs long enough to remove latent load. Charge, blower speed, and coil condition all show normal measurements, and low blower speed would extend runtime rather than shorten it.

questions.question: In a zone-valve hydronic system, how is heat delivered to only the zone that is calling?

answers.text: One circulator per zone runs while all zone valves stay open, and each zone is heated in turn by timers in the boiler control rather than by its own thermostat
A single boiler pump reverses direction for each zone
Each zone has a motorized valve opened by its own thermostat, while a shared circulator moves water through whichever valves are open
Each zone has its own boiler controlled by one thermostat

questions.explanation: Zone-valve zoning uses one circulator and a valve per zone; a calling thermostat opens its valve and the end switch or control starts the circulator. Option A describes circulator zoning, the alternative arrangement. Option B is wrong because circulators do not reverse to select zones. Option D multiplies boilers instead of zoning one boiler's output.

questions.question: A branch run to a quiet bedroom hisses at the register even at moderate airflow. The balancing damper was installed in the register boot, fully in the airstream near the grille. What relocation fixes the noise while keeping balance control?

answers.text: Move the damper into the return grille, since return air makes no noise

Remove balancing dampers entirely, because throttling never makes noise at a trunk takeoff, and branches will balance themselves through their natural friction differences once the system runs long enough at steady airflow in normal operation
Replace the damper with a smaller register so the air speeds up and sounds smoother
Move the balancing damper back to the branch takeoff at the trunk, so the throttling turbulence occurs far from the grille and the branch duct length helps dissipate the noise

questions.explanation: Throttling noise is generated where the air is restricted; putting that restriction at the takeoff gives the branch run distance to absorb it before the air reaches the room. Option A is wrong because return grilles can be just as noisy, and a supply branch cannot be balanced from the return side; option B is wrong because throttling always generates some turbulence — distance from the listener, not absence of noise, is the fix; option C is wrong because a smaller register raises velocity and jet noise at the grille, making the complaint worse.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: Under federal refrigerant practice, what must be done before a refrigeration system is opened for service or disposal?

answers.text: The charge must be vented slowly at the service valves until only oil vapor remains in the system piping and components
Refrigerant must be recovered into approved containers to the prescribed recovery level for the appliance type
The charge must be transferred into the building drain system after being mixed with water to neutralize its effect on the piping
The system must be pressurized with shop air so any remaining refrigerant is diluted before the fittings are loosened for service

questions.explanation: Federal practice requires refrigerant to be recovered into approved containers to the prescribed recovery level for the appliance type before the system is opened. Recovery to the prescribed level is the keyed step, stated as federal practice only.

questions.question: After passing the examination, what surety bond must the applicant submit, and what alternative satisfies it?

answers.text: A $500,000 surety bond, with no alternative filing recognized for an applicant who already holds a bond filed with another board
A $3,000 surety bond, and a $3,000 bond already filed with the State Board of Examiners of Master Plumbers satisfies it on proof of submission
A $3,000 surety bond, and a general liability certificate in any amount satisfies it instead of filing proof of the plumbers board bond
No surety bond at all if the applicant will work only as an employee, since the bond applies solely to owners of HVACR businesses

questions.explanation: After passing, the applicant submits a surety bond in the sum of $3,000. A $3,000 bond already filed with the State Board of Examiners of Master Plumbers satisfies this requirement on proof of submission.

questions.question: Which body administers Master HVACR Contractor licensing in New Jersey?

answers.text: The State Board of Examiners of Heating, Ventilating, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVACR) Contractors
The New Jersey Board of Master Plumbers acting jointly with local code officials in each municipality for all HVACR work performed anywhere in the state
The Division of Codes and Standards acting alone without a separate HVACR examiners board
A county licensing board appointed by the municipality where the contractor has its principal office

questions.explanation: Licensing is administered by the State Board of Examiners of Heating, Ventilating, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVACR) Contractors. That Board sits in the Division of Consumer Affairs.

questions.question: A business receives a written customer complaint alleging a promised item was not installed. What is the best first business response?

answers.text: Delete the complaint and the job file, so the dispute is limited to each side's recollection of the original conversation
Review the signed contract, proposal, and change orders to verify what was promised
Offer the customer a discount on a future unrelated project without checking whether the item was in this contract
Tell the customer that verbal recollections by the sales staff override the signed documents in every disagreement

questions.explanation: B is correct because the signed contract, proposal, and change orders are the authoritative record of what was promised. A is incorrect because destroying the complaint and file removes the evidence needed to resolve the dispute fairly. C is incorrect because offering compensation before verifying the promise may pay for work that was never contracted. D is incorrect because signed documents, not later recollections, generally govern what was agreed.

questions.question: A shop's annual overhead is $120,000 and it expects 6,000 billable labor hours for the year. What overhead recovery rate per billable hour should estimating use?

answers.text: $2.00 per hour, found by dividing annual overhead by total calendar days rather than billable hours
$120.00 per hour, found by treating the entire annual overhead as a single-hour charge
$20.00 per hour
$12.00 per hour, found by dividing overhead by an assumed 10,000 hours that the shop does not expect to bill

questions.explanation: C is correct because $120,000 divided by 6,000 billable hours equals $20.00 per hour. A is incorrect because calendar days are not the allocation base for labor overhead recovery. B is incorrect because it fails to spread overhead across the expected billable hours. D is incorrect because it uses 10,000 hours instead of the stated 6,000 hours.

questions.question: Scenario: a bid is built from direct labor of $4,200 and materials of $3,800. Overhead is 15 percent of direct cost, and profit is 10 percent of the cost after overhead. What is the bid price?

answers.text: $9,200 bid price, stopping at total cost after overhead with no profit added on top of the completed cost figure
$9,660 bid price, applying the profit percentage to the direct cost only rather than to the cost after overhead was added
$10,120 bid price
$11,960 bid price, applying the overhead and profit percentages to a base that counts the direct costs twice in the build-up

questions.explanation: Direct cost is $4,200 plus $3,800, which is $8,000. Overhead at 15 percent adds $1,200 for a total cost of $9,200, and profit at 10 percent of that cost adds $920, giving a bid price of $10,120.

questions.question: A plan shows a thermostat symbol on an interior wall of a classroom, but the installer's rough-in placed the sensor on an exterior wall in direct afternoon sun. Why does the symbol location matter?

answers.text: It does not matter, because modern thermostats recalibrate themselves to cancel out solar heat gain on any wall within the first day of operation
The exterior wall placement is actually preferred, since a warmer sensor location makes the cooling system run longer and dehumidify the room better
Sensor location affects control accuracy, and sun exposure skews readings
The symbol only shows where the display screen will be viewed from, while the actual temperature sensor is always located inside the air handler

questions.explanation: A sensor reads the air and surface conditions around it, so sun exposure on an exterior wall skews the reading and the control response. Thermostats do not self-correct for solar gain, a warmer location causes false calls rather than better control, and the wall device is the sensing point shown.

mississippi-hvac.quiz_title: Mississippi HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Unsteady cooling. Superheat hunts between 8 and 28 degrees F over a single steady call, subcooling sits at 14 degrees F, and suction pressure swings with the superheat. In the air handler, the expansion valve sensing bulb is found hanging loose beside the suction line, its strap broken and insulation tape fallen away. Warming the bulb by hand drives superheat down promptly. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A moisture-contaminated system freezing at the valve orifice intermittently, which would block flow in longer episodes and would not respond immediately to hand-warming a sensing bulb hanging in the airstream
A detached expansion valve sensing bulb sensing air temperature instead of suction-line temperature
An undercharge making the valve hunt for refrigerant, which would hold subcooling low rather than at the healthy 14 degrees measured during the hunting
A compressor whose valves leak on a repeating cycle, which would produce a steady capacity loss and pressure pattern rather than superheat that answers directly to bulb temperature

questions.explanation: The loose bulb senses warm cabinet air instead of the suction line, so the valve opens and closes against the wrong signal and superheat hunts widely; hand-warming it changes superheat on cue, confirming the diagnosis. Moisture icing blocks flow in longer episodes and ignores the bulb, an undercharge cannot hold 14 degrees of subcooling, and leaking compressor valves cause a steady loss, not bulb-responsive hunting.

questions.question: After a motor sheave is opened to raise airflow by about 20 percent on a belt-drive blower, the motor now trips its overload after an hour of running. What best explains the overload?

answers.text: The new belt is slightly longer than the old one, and the added belt length alone raises motor current steadily until the overload device opens on every run
Opening a sheave reduces motor load in all cases, so the trips must come from a failing overload device that should simply be replaced with a larger one
Fan power rises roughly with the cube of speed, overloading the motor
The overload trips because higher airflow cools the motor less effectively, since faster supply air bypasses the motor compartment on this style of blower housing

questions.explanation: By the fan laws, power rises with roughly the cube of speed, so a 20 percent speed increase demands about 73 percent more power and can overload a motor that was near its rating. Belt length does not add that load, sheave increases raise rather than reduce load, and the cooling explanation reverses how these motors are cooled.

questions.question: Tank pressure on a warm afternoon is well over 100 psi, yet the appliances need gas at inches of water column. What does the first-stage regulator in a typical two-stage system do?

answers.text: It cuts tank pressure to about 10 psi for the yard line
It raises tank pressure before the second stage, because appliance regulators need a boosted inlet pressure whenever outdoor temperature climbs in the afternoon
It delivers the final appliance manifold pressure directly, so no second regulation stage is needed anywhere between an outdoor tank and the indoor burners
It vents excess tank pressure to the atmosphere continuously, holding the yard line at appliance pressure by releasing whatever vapor the tank produces above demand

questions.explanation: The first-stage regulator reduces variable tank pressure to an intermediate pressure, commonly around 10 psi, for the line to the building. Final reduction to inches of water column is left to the second stage, and regulators reduce and control pressure rather than boosting it or venting vapor continuously.

questions.question: Why does a cubic foot of propane need far more combustion air by volume than a cubic foot of natural gas, even though air needs per unit of heat are similar?

answers.text: Propane molecules contain no carbon, so extra air is needed to supply carbon for a stable flame at the burner ports during normal operation
Each cubic foot of propane carries much more heat and fuel to burn
Natural gas burners use no primary or secondary air at all, so the comparison is between propane burners that need air and natural gas burners that burn in a vacuum jacket
Propane air requirements are set by the tank pressure alone, so a cubic foot from a warm tank needs more air than the same cubic foot from a cold tank in winter

questions.explanation: Combustion air follows the amount of fuel burned, and a cubic foot of propane contains more than twice the fuel energy of a cubic foot of natural gas. Per unit of heat released the air requirement is broadly similar for the two gases, propane does contain carbon, and tank temperature changes pressure rather than the chemistry of a cubic foot of vapor.

questions.question: A homeowner expects zoning dampers to cure weak airflow that exists today with all rooms calling, on an undersized common trunk. Why will zoning alone disappoint?

answers.text: Zoning increases the capacity of the common trunk, so weak airflow with all zones calling proves the trunk is oversized rather than undersized for the equipment
Dampers add resistance and only redistribute air; they do not enlarge a trunk that is already too small for total airflow
Weak airflow with all zones calling is caused by the zone panel withholding blower speed, and removing the panel restores full trunk capacity without any duct change at all
Zoning cures total airflow problems whenever one room is weak, because closing other branches permanently is an accepted substitute for sizing the common duct to the equipment

questions.explanation: Dampers redistribute the air the blower delivers and add resistance of their own, so they cannot cure a common trunk that is already too small when every zone calls together. Zoning can send a larger share to one area by restricting others, but total airflow capacity still depends on the trunk, the blower, and total static pressure.

questions.question: Where is the return-air enthalpy sensor most usefully placed in a differential-enthalpy economizer system?

answers.text: In the supply duct downstream of the cooling coil, where the air is coldest and has already mixed with outdoor air and passed through the coil
Outdoors next to the weather station, so both sensors read the same air
In the return airstream before it mixes with outdoor air, so it represents the air that would otherwise be recirculated
In an occupied room far from the unit, where temperature swings are largest

questions.explanation: The control needs a true sample of unmixed return air to compare against outdoor air. Supply air after the coil no longer represents return conditions, duplicating the outdoor sensor defeats the comparison, and a distant room sensor responds slowly and does not sample the airstream the unit handles.

questions.question: A CSST installation is complete but unbonded, and the inspector asks for the bond before approval. The installer's correct response is:

answers.text: Explain that bonding is optional on short runs, because tubing under a certain length cannot develop a damaging voltage difference in a storm
Bond the system as required by the listing and manufacturer instructions before calling it complete
Bond the tubing to the nearest cold-water pipe at any convenient point, regardless of where the manufacturer directs the connection to be made
Wait until the first lightning storm shows whether arcing occurs, because bonding is a corrective measure rather than part of the installation

questions.explanation: Bond the system as required by the listing and manufacturer instructions before calling it complete. Bonding is not optional by length, not placed at any arbitrary pipe point, and not deferred until damage demonstrates the need.

questions.question: A 95% AFUE furnace is vented with PVC and produces a steady stream of water at its drain during heating. A homeowner worries the heat exchanger is leaking. What should the technician explain and verify?

answers.text: Any water at the drain indicates a cracked heat exchanger, so the furnace must be condemned and shut down immediately without checking the drain, trap, or venting system
Condensation is normal for this appliance; verify the condensate drain and trap are clear and properly routed
The water is humidifier overflow and the furnace drain should be plugged
PVC venting causes rain to enter, so the vent should be switched to B-vent

questions.explanation: High-efficiency furnaces condense water vapor from flue gas by design, so the task is confirming drainage works. Condensate alone is not evidence of a crack. Plugging the drain would flood the appliance, and replacing low-temperature venting with B-vent would be wrong for a condensing, positive-pressure system.

questions.question: A condensate drain line is installed dead level for a long run and plugs with slime every season. What installation defect is most likely?

answers.text: The line was made from approved drain material instead of thin-wall tubing that stays warmer and therefore resists biological growth
The drain terminates at an approved receptor instead of discharging directly onto the roof membrane below the condensing unit
The trap was installed at the unit rather than at the far end of the run near the floor drain, where traps are most effective
The line lacks continuous downward slope in the direction of flow.

questions.explanation: Condensate drains must fall continuously, about an eighth inch per foot, so water and debris do not stand in the line. Approved material and an approved receptor are correct practice, not defects, and the trap belongs at the unit to prevent air issues.

questions.question: Before leaving a new installation, which combustion-related checks belong on the startup record for a gas furnace?

answers.text: Only that the burners lit on the first attempt
Only the color of the flame as seen through the sight glass
Manifold pressure, temperature rise against the nameplate range, vent draft or pressure-switch operation as applicable, and a carbon monoxide check of the supply air or flue as directed
Only the gas meter size and the length of the gas line

questions.explanation: A complete combustion startup verifies fuel pressure, heat-exchanger airflow by temperature rise, proper venting operation, and the absence of carbon monoxide where the maker directs the check. Option A proves ignition only, option B relies on appearance, which cannot confirm safe combustion, and option D records supply piping facts without any operating verification.

questions.question: Which body administers both Mississippi's commercial Certificate of Responsibility and its residential contractor licensing?

answers.text: The State Board of Contractors administers both licensing tracks.
The State Board of Contractors administers only residential contractor licensing.
A separate heating and air-conditioning board administers both licensing tracks.
The State Board of Contractors administers only commercial contractor licensing.

questions.explanation: One Board, the State Board of Contractors, runs both the commercial and residential tracks. The distractors wrongly limit that Board to one track or invent a separate board.

questions.question: What is the balance point of an air-source heat pump heating system?

answers.text: It is the outdoor temperature at which the heat pump must be shut down and removed from service for the rest of the winter heating season
It is the indoor temperature at which the thermostat switches the system from cooling over to heating at the start of the heating season
It is the outdoor temperature where heat pump capacity just equals the building heating load
It is the refrigerant temperature at which the reversing valve changes position to start a defrost cycle on the outdoor coil in cold weather

questions.explanation: At the balance point the heat pump's output exactly matches the building's heat loss at that outdoor temperature. Below it, capacity falls short of the load and supplemental heat makes up the difference; it is not a shutdown point, a changeover setting, or a defrost trigger.

michigan-hvac.quiz_title: Michigan HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A technician must adjust TXV superheat on a stable, fully loaded system. Which procedure is correct?

answers.text: Turn the stem several full turns at once and read the superheat immediately, because a TXV reaches its new equilibrium within a few seconds of any adjustment
Measure the superheat at the compressor inlet after a long suction line, because pressure drop and heat gain along that line have no effect on the reading obtained
Adjust the valve while the system is pumped down and off, counting stem turns from fully closed, because superheat cannot be set under actual operating load conditions
Measure superheat at the bulb location, turn the stem in small increments, and allow the system to stabilize between adjustments

questions.explanation: Superheat is set at the evaporator outlet where the bulb sits, in small steps with stabilization time, under steady load. Large instant adjustments overshoot a slow-responding system, a compressor-inlet reading includes line pressure drop and heat gain and misrepresents evaporator superheat, and a valve cannot be meaningfully set while the system is off and pumped down.

questions.question: A system cools the air temperature adequately but humidity stays near 65%. Readings: airflow measured at 485 cfm/ton, air-side temperature split only 13°F, superheat 9°F, subcooling 10°F, pressures normal, coil clean, and condensate barely drips except on the hottest afternoons. What adjustment does the evidence support?

answers.text: Install a larger evaporator coil, a major change that does nothing about air moving too fast for moisture to condense on the coil surface
Increase blower speed further to move more air across the coil, which would raise coil temperature even more and strip off still less moisture
Add refrigerant to drop the suction pressure and coil temperature, which would corrupt the currently correct superheat and subcooling values
Reduce blower speed to lower airflow per ton

questions.explanation: Excessive airflow per ton keeps the coil too warm and the split too small for sustained condensation, which the 13°F split and 485 cfm/ton prove. Slowing the blower lowers coil temperature and lengthens moisture contact; speeding it up worsens the problem, adding charge falsifies good readings, and a bigger coil does not fix air velocity.

questions.question: A furnace overheats on limit most cycles. Temperature rise is 88°F, the filter is clean, ducts are open, the blower motor runs but sounds labored and its capacitor measures 3.1 µF against a 10 µF rating; motor amps are elevated and the motor shell is very hot after short runs. Gas input is correct. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A weak blower run capacitor
A limit switch weakened by age and opening early, which is contradicted by the genuinely high measured supply temperature at each trip
Closed supply registers throughout the house, which were all found open during the airflow survey of the duct system
An overfired burner section, which is excluded because the clocked gas input matches the nameplate firing rate exactly

questions.explanation: A capacitor at one-third of its rating leaves the blower turning slowly and hot, so airflow falls and temperature rise climbs to 88°F at a correct firing rate. Overfiring is excluded by the clock test, the limit trips at a real overtemperature, and the registers were verified open.

questions.question: A heat pump compressor fails in mid-winter and the technician sets the thermostat to emergency heat while parts are ordered. What changes in system operation?

answers.text: The heat pump runs at double capacity to compensate
Defrost cycles double in frequency to protect the coil
The compressor is locked out and the auxiliary heat becomes the sole heat source
The reversing valve is removed from the refrigerant circuit permanently and replaced with a straight section of copper tubing

questions.explanation: Emergency heat locks out the compressor and runs auxiliary (usually electric strip) heat alone, option C, which is why it is costly and meant for backup only. A failed compressor cannot run at double capacity (A), defrost (B) is irrelevant with the outdoor unit locked out, and the reversing valve (D) stays installed for return to normal service.

questions.question: A homeowner expects zoning dampers to cure weak airflow that exists today with all rooms calling, on an undersized common trunk. Why will zoning alone disappoint?

answers.text: Zoning increases the capacity of the common trunk, so weak airflow with all zones calling proves the trunk is oversized rather than undersized for the equipment
Dampers add resistance and only redistribute air; they do not enlarge a trunk that is already too small for total airflow
Weak airflow with all zones calling is caused by the zone panel withholding blower speed, and removing the panel restores full trunk capacity without any duct change at all
Zoning cures total airflow problems whenever one room is weak, because closing other branches permanently is an accepted substitute for sizing the common duct to the equipment

questions.explanation: Dampers redistribute the air the blower delivers and add resistance of their own, so they cannot cure a common trunk that is already too small when every zone calls together. Zoning can send a larger share to one area by restricting others, but total airflow capacity still depends on the trunk, the blower, and total static pressure.

questions.question: For reliable building pressure control, where should the indoor pressure sensor reference be placed?

answers.text: Inside the supply duct, where pressure is highest and easiest to read
In a representative interior location away from doors, diffusers, and direct drafts, referenced to a stable outdoor pressure tap shielded from wind
Directly in the blast of an entrance door that opens frequently
Outdoors on the roof in a fully exposed location where wind gusts strike the pressure tap directly and the reading follows every change in wind speed and direction

questions.explanation: Space pressure sensing must reflect the building, not local air movement, and wind on the outdoor reference corrupts the differential. Duct pressure is a different, much larger variable. Door drafts and wind gusts are exactly the disturbances good placement avoids.

questions.question: An appliance shutoff must be serviceable after the furnace is set in a tight closet. Best placement is:

answers.text: Behind the furnace against the rear wall, because a shutoff is considered accessible if it can be reached after the appliance is pulled out
In the attic above the closet, because the valve only needs to be reachable by a technician carrying a ladder during an emergency shutoff
Downstream of the flexible connector at the valve inlet, because placing it there shortens the length of pipe that remains live during service
Upstream of the connector, in the same room, reachable without moving the appliance

questions.explanation: Upstream of the connector, in the same room, reachable without moving the appliance. A valve that requires moving the appliance or climbing into another space is not readily accessible, and placing it downstream of the connector leaves the connector live.

questions.question: An ERV's measured outdoor airflow has fallen 25% over a year while fan energy has risen, and the wheel still rotates freely. What is the most likely service finding?

answers.text: The wheel has absorbed so much moisture that it has become heavier, and drying it with a heat gun restores the original airflow, a drying service the manufacturer supposedly recommends performing at every seasonal changeover without exception
Loaded filters and a fouled energy-transfer core are raising pressure drop, so the fans move less air against the added resistance
The exhaust and supply fans have exchanged rotation directions, which always shows up gradually over about a year's operation
The outdoor-air intake has grown larger through damper wear, letting in more air than the flow station was designed to measure

questions.explanation: Fouled media and filters are the routine cause of creeping pressure drop, falling airflow, and rising fan work. Option A proposes a drying procedure for a symptom fouling explains better, option C describes a wiring fault that would appear suddenly, not gradually, and option D claims more intake area reduces measured flow, which is the opposite of the finding.

questions.question: A crew is about to work from a scaffold erected beside an air handler. Which condition must be met before the scaffold is used each shift?

answers.text: The scaffold only needs a fresh inspection when it is first erected, after which daily conditions such as weather and impacts cannot affect its safety
Workers may use the scaffold while it is still being moved into position, provided they hold the frame and keep their weight near the casters
Guardrails can be left off the top level whenever ductwork is being passed up, because material handling temporarily overrides fall protection needs
A competent person inspects it and footing and planking are sound

questions.explanation: Scaffolds are inspected by a competent person before each shift and after events that could affect them, with firm footing and proper planking and guardrails. One-time inspection misses later damage, riding a moving scaffold is prohibited practice, and material handling never suspends fall protection.

questions.question: A customer wants the new high-efficiency outdoor unit paired with their 15-year-old indoor coil to save money. What is the most accurate contractor response?

answers.text: The full rated efficiency will still be achieved because efficiency is determined entirely by the outdoor unit's compressor design
The combination will actually exceed its rating, since older coils have heavier copper that transfers heat better than new coils
The system may run, but the rated efficiency and capacity cannot be claimed and performance and warranty coverage are at risk
Efficiency will be unaffected as long as the refrigerant type is the same in both the old coil and the new outdoor unit

questions.explanation: An unlisted pairing has no tested rating, and an old coil's size, metering, and condition can compromise capacity and coverage. The outdoor unit alone does not set system efficiency, heavier old copper does not guarantee better transfer, and matching refrigerant does not restore a rating.

questions.question: Which set lists work classifications for which a Michigan mechanical contractor's license is issued?

answers.text: Electrical contracting, plumbing, and building contracting are among the ten classifications
Elevator installation, boiler inspection, and fire alarm work are among the ten classifications

General contracting, residential building, and maintenance and alteration work are among the ten classifications, together with the limited and unlimited service classifications issued under the administrative rules
Hydronic heating and cooling and process piping, HVAC equipment, ductwork, and refrigeration are among the ten classifications

questions.explanation: The ten classifications include hydronic heating and cooling and process piping, HVAC equipment, ductwork, and refrigeration, along with the limited and unlimited service classifications, fire suppression, and specialty. The other sets name licenses from different regulatory schemes.

questions.question: Appliances totaling 80,000 Btu/h use the outdoor two-opening method with vertical ducts. What is the minimum free area of each opening?

answers.text: Each opening needs at least 40 square inches of free area with vertical ducts
Each opening needs at least 80 square inches of free area with vertical ducts
Each opening needs at least 20 square inches of free area with vertical ducts
Each opening needs at least 100 square inches of free area with vertical ducts

questions.explanation: For outdoor air through vertical ducts or openings, the rate is 1 square inch per 4,000 Btu/h, so 80,000 Btu/h divided by 4,000 equals 20 square inches per opening. The 40-square-inch figure is the horizontal-duct rate for the same input.

tennessee-hvac.quiz_title: Tennessee HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An accumulator-equipped system returns with a low crankcase oil level, a suction accumulator that is cold and heavy with liquid, and normal superheat at the evaporator outlet. What accumulator fault fits these findings?

answers.text: The accumulator is installed in the liquid line instead of the suction line, which is why it is cold and full while the evaporator superheat remains normal
The accumulator's oil-return orifice at the bottom of its U-tube is plugged
The accumulator's internal U-tube has grown longer with age, so it now holds more liquid than the compressor crankcase can supply with oil during operation
The accumulator is too small, because an undersized vessel returns oil to the compressor faster than a correctly sized vessel and empties the crankcase promptly

questions.explanation: The small orifice at the U-tube bottom meters oil (and some liquid) back; when it plugs, oil collects in the accumulator and the crankcase starves while evaporator operation can look normal. A suction accumulator belongs where it is described and its cold, full condition follows the plugged return, the U-tube does not change length with age, and an undersized accumulator risks liquid carryover rather than quietly storing the system's oil.

questions.question: A system moves 1,200 CFM. To keep filter face velocity near 300 feet per minute, about how much filter area is needed, and what does that imply for the rack?

answers.text: About 0.4 square feet, so a very small rack is best because higher velocity forces dust deeper into media for better capture
About 40 square feet, so the return must be built as a filter wall covering most of one side of the mechanical room itself
About 12 square feet, calculated by dividing velocity by airflow rather than airflow by the target face velocity value given
About 4 square feet of filter area

questions.explanation: Area equals airflow divided by velocity: 1,200 divided by 300 is 4 square feet, roughly a 20-by-30-inch filter, so the rack must be generously sized. Option A is off by a factor of ten and raises pressure drop, option B is off by a factor of ten the other way, and option C reverses the division.

questions.question: Which fitting choice generally creates the least resistance for a branch takeoff?

answers.text: A sharp 90-degree tap with no radius, cut straight into the side of the trunk
A smooth, gradual takeoff with a turning vane or radius throat
A crushed flex duct bend
A completely closed damper

questions.explanation: Smooth, gradual fittings keep air attached and reduce turbulence, giving the lowest equivalent length, so B is correct. Sharp taps and crushed flex add turbulence and resistance, and a closed damper blocks flow entirely.

questions.question: Why must a technician avoid performing a standard megohm (insulation) test through a connected inverter drive on a compressor?

answers.text: The test gives a falsely high reading, which is merely an accuracy inconvenience and poses no risk to any component in the drive circuit
Test voltage far above what inverter semiconductors tolerate can destroy the drive electronics connected in the circuit
The drive automatically reverses the test, sending line voltage back into the meter, which is a concern only for the meter's batteries
Compressors on inverter systems have no insulation to test, because their windings are potted in a material that makes insulation testing unnecessary

questions.explanation: Megohm test voltages far exceed what inverter semiconductors tolerate, so the compressor is isolated from the drive before insulation testing. The hazard is destroyed electronics rather than a small reading error, the drive does not throw line voltage back at the meter in that manner, and inverter compressor windings still require insulation assessment when tested correctly.

questions.question: A furnace clocks at an input 20% above its rating plate after a gas-valve replacement. The most likely setup causes are:

answers.text: Manifold pressure set too high or wrong-size orifices installed
A vent connector one size larger than the minimum, because a larger vent increases draft and pulls extra gas through the burner orifices
A sediment trap with a long capped leg, because the trap volume adds a reserve of gas that the meter counts as additional furnace input
A thermostat set several degrees above room temperature, because a larger temperature difference makes the gas valve deliver more fuel per hour

questions.explanation: Manifold pressure set too high or wrong-size orifices installed. Vent size, trap volume, and thermostat setting do not change firing rate; excessive manifold pressure or oversized orifices do.

questions.question: A long rooftop refrigerant run vibrates, ticks against its supports in changing weather, and a rigidly clamped section has cracked at a braze joint. Contributing installation faults most likely include:

answers.text: Too many access ports were installed on the run
The suction line was insulated with a sealed vapor barrier
Supports spaced for the pipe size with room for thermal movement and vibration isolation where needed were not provided
Nitrogen was used during brazing

questions.explanation: Long runs expand, contract, and transmit compressor vibration, so correct support spacing, freedom for thermal movement, and vibration control prevent fatigue cracking. Option A names a service convenience, not a fatigue cause, and options B and D describe good practices that protect the system rather than crack joints.

questions.question: A bathroom without an operable window has a noisy exhaust fan that occupants never use, and mirrors and paint show chronic moisture damage. What is the best correction?

answers.text: Install a larger mirror and advise shorter showers only
Recirculate the exhaust fan discharge into the attic space above the bathroom to save energy and avoid cutting a vent termination through the roof
Seal the bathroom door so moisture stays in one room
Provide effective, quiet local exhaust vented outdoors, controlled so it actually runs during and after showers

questions.explanation: Moisture must be captured and discharged outdoors by exhaust occupants will tolerate and controls that ensure run time. A bigger mirror does nothing about moisture load. Venting into an attic deposits moisture in the structure, and sealing the door traps humid air against finishes.

questions.question: A furnace blower is rated to deliver design airflow at a maximum total external static pressure of 0.80 in. w.g. The wet evaporator coil drops 0.28, the filter drops 0.12, and the supply and return grilles together drop 0.08. How much static pressure remains available for the ductwork itself?

answers.text: 0.48 in. w.g., because only the coil loss is subtracted from the blower rating
0.80 in. w.g., because component losses are included in the blower rating already
0.20 in. w.g., because the filter loss must be subtracted twice, once per side

questions.explanation: An external static budget subtracts every non-duct component from what the blower can overcome; what is left is what the duct runs may consume. Option A is wrong because subtracting only the coil leaves the filter and grille losses unaccounted for, so the ducts would be sized with pressure that does not exist; option C is wrong because the blower rating is a total budget for everything external to the unit, not a duct-only allowance; option D is wrong because the filter is a single component with one pressure drop, counted once.

questions.question: Why must a refrigerant cylinder never be heated with an open flame or filled beyond its rated capacity?

answers.text: It improves charging accuracy
Overfilling or heating can raise pressure to rupture, and flame can decompose refrigerant into toxic gases
It only affects the cylinder paint
Cylinders are designed for any pressure

questions.explanation: Heat and overfilling can raise cylinder pressure to rupture, and flame contact can create highly toxic decomposition products, so B is correct. A is false because these practices are dangerous, not helpful, C trivializes the hazard, and D contradicts cylinder pressure ratings.

questions.question: Refrigerant cylinders delivered to a jobsite will be stored for several days before use. Which storage practice is correct?

answers.text: Cylinders secured upright, caps on, away from heat and traffic
Cylinders laid on their sides in a sunny corner of the parking lot so the liquid inside stays warm and ready to flow quickly during charging
Cylinders stacked horizontally in the exit corridor, where they are easy to grab and the building occupants can step around them during the day
Cylinders stored valve-down in an unventilated electrical closet so they stay out of sight and cannot be tampered with by other trades

questions.explanation: Stored cylinders belong upright, secured against tipping, with valve caps on and away from heat and traffic damage. Lying in sun overheats them, a corridor blocks egress and invites impact, and an unventilated closet valve-down risks leaks pooling where ignition sources exist.

questions.question: A variable-speed drive slows a chilled-water pump to 90% of full speed. Using the pump affinity laws, about how much pump power is saved?

answers.text: About 3%, because pump power falls only in direct one-to-one proportion to the drop in pump rotational speed
About 10%, because pump power falls in proportion to the square of the speed ratio at reduced flow conditions
About 19%, because pump head and pump power always change by exactly the same percentage as each other
About 27%, because power varies with the cube of speed: 0.9 cubed is about 0.73 of full power

questions.explanation: Power follows the cube law: 0.9^3 = 0.729, so roughly 27% of the power is saved. Option A uses the flow relationship, option B uses the head (square) relationship, and option C wrongly equates head and power changes, which follow different exponents.

questions.question: Running horizontal 3/4-inch steel fuel-gas pipe along the joists of a Jackson basement, a crew spaces its hangers by the support table for steel pipe. What maximum spacing applies to supports for that pipe?

answers.text: Supports may be spaced up to 12 feet apart, because steel pipe of any trade size is rigid enough to span that distance without sagging between hangers
Supports may be spaced up to 6 feet apart, because the smallest steel size sets the spacing that must then be used for every larger size in the run
Supports may be spaced up to 10 feet apart, because that spacing governs all steel gas pipe from 3/4 inch through the largest residential sizes used
Supports may be spaced up to 8 feet apart, which is the table spacing for 3/4-inch and 1-inch steel pipe in horizontal runs

questions.explanation: D is correct: the fuel-gas support table spaces horizontal steel pipe supports at 6 feet for 1/2-inch, 8 feet for 3/4-inch and 1-inch, and 10 feet for 1-1/4-inch and larger, so 3/4-inch pipe takes 8-foot spacing. A is wrong because 12 feet exceeds every spacing in the steel-pipe table. B is wrong because the 6-foot figure belongs to 1/2-inch pipe; spacing increases with pipe size rather than defaulting to the smallest. C is wrong because the 10-foot spacing starts at 1-1/4-inch pipe, above this run's size.

virginia-hvac.quiz_title: Virginia HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A mountain-town home at 4,500 feet has sticky, humid summers and long mild shoulder seasons. Which equipment reasoning best fits all three conditions together?

answers.text: Pick the largest single-stage unit available so altitude losses are covered by raw tonnage, accepting short shoulder-season cycles as a minor comfort tradeoff overall
Size by nameplate sea-level capacity alone, because humidity control and part-load behavior matter far less at elevation than they do for lowland installations nearby
Use derated capacity, favor modulation for part load and humidity control
Choose equipment by its heating rating first and let cooling size fall where it may, since mountain homes are heating-dominated and summer loads rarely govern equipment selection

questions.explanation: The selection has to start from altitude-derated capacity, and a modulating system handles the long part-load shoulder seasons efficiently while sustaining the runtime humid monsoon weeks demand for moisture removal. Raw oversizing wrecks humidity control, nameplate sea-level sizing ignores the derate, and heating-first sizing abandons the stated summer design conditions.

questions.question: A homeowner asks why the new R-454B air handler runs its blower for a while after a leak sensor trips, even though cooling has stopped. What is the correct explanation?

answers.text: The blower is removing residual heat from the electric heat strips, a normal cool-down sequence that happens to coincide with the sensor alarm event
The blower pressurizes the duct system so refrigerant vapor is forced back through the leak point into the coil, resealing the system temporarily
The blower dilutes and disperses leaked refrigerant through the duct system so room concentration stays low
The blower run is a fault in itself, because mitigation design requires the air handler to shut down every moving part the instant a sensor trips

questions.explanation: Leak mitigation uses indoor airflow to dilute and disperse refrigerant so concentration in the occupied space stays low. The run is not a heat-strip cool-down, airflow cannot push vapor back into a leaking coil or reseal it, and the blower operation is an intended mitigation response rather than a second fault.

questions.question: A system has correct refrigerant readings for its metering type but a temperature split of only 11°F across the evaporator on a humid day with a heavy latent load confirmed normal. Static pressure is low and the blower is set one tap higher than specified for the installed coil. Which explanation best fits a persistently low sensible split after the latent load is accounted for?

answers.text: Excessive airflow moving air across the coil too fast for full sensible heat exchange per cubic foot
A refrigerant undercharge, which always lowers the temperature split first, before any other measurement is taken on the system
A clogged condensate drain raising the coil temperature
A TXV sensing bulb that has completely lost its charge

questions.explanation: Too much airflow reduces the temperature change of each unit of air passing over the coil, shrinking the measured split even when the refrigeration circuit is healthy. Option B is contradicted by the correct refrigerant readings given in the scenario. Option C affects drainage, not the air temperature change across the coil, and option D would starve the evaporator and disturb the superheat readings, which are stated to be correct.

questions.question: A cabin hydronic system uses glycol for freeze protection and is serviced after five years with no fluid records. The essential fluid checks before winter are to test:

answers.text: Only the water pressure at the boiler gauge, checked once while the system is hot and again after it cools, with no testing of the glycol itself if the pressure has remained stable since the last service visit
Only the color of the fluid against a new sample
Freeze-point concentration with a refractometer and inhibitor/pH condition, topping up or replacing fluid whose freeze or corrosion protection has degraded
Glycol ratio by measuring boiler stack temperature

questions.explanation: Glycol protection is only as good as its concentration and inhibitor package, both of which drift with age, leaks, and dilution, so both must be measured before relying on them. Option A says nothing about the fluid itself. Option B is unreliable because color does not quantify freeze point or inhibitor reserve. Option D measures combustion, which cannot reveal fluid concentration.

questions.question: A homeowner wants a much finer filter, but the existing 1-inch filter rack already shows a high clean-filter pressure drop and airflow is marginal. What is the soundest way to gain filtration without starving the system?

answers.text: Install the finer filter and raise blower speed two taps, because higher speed always restores airflow without any penalty in noise, energy use, or coil velocity
Increase filter face area
Remove the filter during mild weather to bank static-pressure margin, then reinstall the fine filter only for the hottest weeks of the cooling season
Stack two fine filters in series in the same rack so each one catches part of the load, which lowers the combined pressure drop compared with a single filter

questions.explanation: A larger, deeper media filter presents more face area, so air velocity through the media falls and pressure drop stays acceptable while filtration improves. Raising blower speed carries noise, energy, and velocity penalties and may not overcome the drop, removing filtration exposes the coil, and filters in series add their pressure drops together instead of lowering them.

questions.question: A gas appliance has an input rating of 132,000 Btu/h, and the gas supply delivers about 1,000 Btu per cubic foot. What volume of gas must the piping deliver to the appliance each hour?

answers.text: 13.2 cubic feet per hour, because the input is divided by 10,000 to convert Btu directly into piping flow units

66 cubic feet per hour, because only half the nameplate input is used when converting a rating into hourly gas flow, on the theory that appliances draw only their average firing rate across a full day of operation
132 cubic feet per hour, because the hourly input divided by the heat content per cubic foot gives the hourly volume
1,320 cubic feet per hour, because an extra zero is added to account for the pressure drop along the piping run

questions.explanation: C is correct: 132,000 Btu/h / 1,000 Btu per cubic foot = 132 cubic feet per hour of gas flow. A is wrong because it divides by 10,000, understating the flow tenfold. B is wrong because the full nameplate input is converted; no half-input convention exists. D is wrong because pressure drop affects pipe sizing selection, not the arithmetic that converts input rating into required volume flow.

questions.question: What is the basic purpose of whole-dwelling mechanical ventilation under residential ventilation guidance such as ASHRAE 62.2?

answers.text: To replace all mechanical heating and cooling with outdoor air throughout the year, in every season and in every climate, without any supplemental conditioning
To pressurize the house so no air can ever leave
To provide controlled outdoor air to dilute indoor pollutants and maintain acceptable indoor air quality
To remove the need for any local kitchen or bathroom exhaust

questions.explanation: Controlled outdoor air dilutes pollutants that build up in tight homes, which is the purpose of whole-dwelling ventilation. It supplements rather than replaces heating and cooling. No practical system seals a house against all exfiltration, and local exhaust for moisture and cooking sources is still required alongside whole-dwelling air.

questions.question: Windows condense heavily on cold winter mornings in a tight new home with a large family, showers, and cooking. Indoor humidity reads 48%. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: The humidifier is undersized, so raising indoor humidity further will warm the window glass and stop the condensation from forming
The windows are leaking refrigerant, because condensation on glass is a recognized sign of a cooling-system charge problem in winter
The furnace is oversized for cooling, which explains winter window moisture even though the cooling system is not operating at all
Indoor moisture generation exceeds removal, so humidity must be lowered and ventilation or exhaust increased rather than adding humidification.

questions.explanation: Condensation means indoor dew point exceeds the cold glass temperature; the fix is less indoor moisture and more removal through ventilation and exhaust. Adding humidity makes it worse, windows contain no refrigerant, and cooling sizing is irrelevant to a winter moisture balance.

questions.question: A replacement water heater is installed with no readily accessible gas shutoff valve serving it. What is required?

answers.text: An accessible shutoff valve in the same room, within the prescribed reach of the appliance, ahead of its union or connector.
A valve at the gas meter is sufficient for every appliance in the building, no matter how far the heater is from the meter location
A shutoff is required only on appliances over a certain input, so smaller heaters may rely on turning off the main building valve
The valve may be hidden behind the heater's jacket panel, provided a sticker on the front tells a technician that it is located inside

questions.explanation: Each appliance needs its own accessible shutoff nearby so it can be isolated quickly for service or emergency. A distant meter valve does not serve that purpose, the requirement is not limited to large inputs, and a valve behind a jacket panel is not accessible.

questions.question: All zones in a house are lukewarm. The boiler control display reads 182°F and stops firing, but a calibrated thermometer strapped to the supply pipe reads 143°F, zones call continuously, the circulator runs, and the boiler temperature sensor's resistance measures well off its published chart for the actual water temperature. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: An aquastat/limit set too low by the installer, when the control believes it is reaching 182°F and the setting itself was verified correct
A drifted boiler temperature sensor
Air binding in every zone simultaneously, which would leave the boiler itself hot and short-cycling rather than genuinely producing 143°F water
A failing circulator moving too little water, which is contradicted because a lazy circulator makes boiler water hotter, not cooler, than the display claims

questions.explanation: The control stops firing because a drifted sensor tells it the water is 182°F when it is truly 143°F — proven by the independent thermometer and the off-chart resistance. Low flow overheats boiler water, the setting was verified, and system-wide air binding leaves the boiler hot, not tepid.

questions.question: A job will cost $800 to perform. The contractor wants a 25% gross margin on the selling price, not a 25% markup on cost. What selling price achieves that margin?

answers.text: $1,000.00, found by adding a 25 percent markup directly onto the $800 cost of the work
$960.00, found by adding a 20 percent markup even though a different margin was requested
$1,600.00, found by doubling the cost on the assumption that margin and markup are interchangeable terms

questions.explanation: D is correct because price equals cost divided by one minus the desired margin, or $800 divided by 0.75, which is $1,066.67. A is incorrect because $1,000 reflects a 25 percent markup and yields only a 20 percent margin. B is incorrect because it applies neither the requested markup nor the requested margin. C is incorrect because it greatly overstates the divisor formula for a 25 percent margin.

questions.question: A Virginia firm is offered a single HVAC installation contract priced at $175,000 and expects about $600,000 in total work for the year. Which contractor class does the single-contract value require?

answers.text: Class A, because a single contract of $150,000 or more places the work in the Class A range regardless of the firm's yearly total
Class B, because any firm whose yearly total stays below $1 million remains in the Class B range even on a very large single job
Class C, because HVAC installation is a specialty trade and specialty work is classified by trade rather than by contract value
No class applies, because licensing classes are set by the number of employees a firm carries rather than by the value of its contracts

questions.explanation: A is correct: a Class A contractor performs or manages work based on a single contract or project of $150,000 or more, and $175,000 clears that line on its own. B is wrong because the Class B single-contract range tops out below $150,000. C is wrong because class is determined by contract value, not by trade specialty. D is wrong because headcount plays no part in the class definitions.

south-carolina-hvac.quiz_title: South Carolina HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: On a new condensing furnace, the PVC exhaust vent runs 18 feet horizontally to the sidewall. How should that horizontal run be pitched, and why?

answers.text: Pitched away from the furnace so condensate runs outdoors, where it can drip freely off the termination fitting
Pitched back toward the furnace
Pitched exactly level so condensate can sit in the pipe and evaporate slowly during the off cycle between calls for heat
Pitched away from the furnace on the first half and back toward it on the second half, forming a shallow low point in the middle

questions.explanation: The exhaust is pitched back toward the furnace, typically about 1/4 inch per foot, so condensate formed in the vent drains to the furnace drain system. Option A sends acidic condensate outdoors to drip and freeze at the termination, option C lets water pool and block vent area, and option D creates a trap in the middle that can fill and trip the pressure switch.

questions.question: A supply outlet measures 600 FPM average velocity through a free area of 1.0 sq ft. How much air is it delivering?

answers.text: 60 CFM
160 CFM
600 CFM

questions.explanation: CFM = velocity x area = 600 FPM x 1.0 sq ft = 600 CFM, so D is correct. A divides by ten incorrectly, B adds unrelated numbers, and C overstates the product by nearly three times.

questions.question: A 3-ton system whistles at the return grille and delivers weak cooling. The only return is a single 14-inch flex duct and one filter grille. Return-side static measures -0.42 in. w.c., total external static is 0.98 in. w.c., delivered airflow is about 880 CFM against the roughly 1,200 CFM the system needs, and the cooling temperature split is a high 24 degrees F. Coils and filter are clean. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: An overcharged refrigeration circuit raising the temperature split, which would show high subcooling and head pressure rather than a return static of -0.42 in. w.c. and a whistling grille
An undersized return air path
A blower motor running backward after a capacitor change, which would collapse airflow at every register and show near-zero static rather than a strongly negative return side
A supply duct leak in the attic losing conditioned air, which would lower supply static and delivered air without driving the return side to -0.42 in. w.c. or making the grille whistle

questions.explanation: One 14-inch return cannot carry 1,200 CFM quietly; the return side pulls -0.42 in. w.c., total static reaches 0.98 in. w.c., airflow falls to about 880 CFM, and the low airflow inflates the temperature split to 24 degrees. Overcharge changes refrigerant readings, not return static, a backward blower would show weak static everywhere, and a supply leak does not make the return grille whistle or pull the return side strongly negative.

questions.question: An ECM constant-airflow blower holds its programmed CFM as its filter loads up, but the homeowner notices higher electric bills and more blower noise. What explains this?

answers.text: Motor power rises to hold airflow
The motor holds airflow by drawing less current at higher speed, and the noise and bills both come from the thermostat calling for longer cooling cycles instead
Constant-airflow motors maintain CFM by opening a bypass damper around the filter, so the added noise is air rushing through the bypass opening
The filter is cleaning the air so well that the coil loads with the trapped dirt, and the extra energy use is the compressor working against that coil fouling

questions.explanation: To hold CFM against rising static pressure, a constant-airflow ECM increases speed and torque, which raises watt draw and noise until it reaches its limit. Such a motor draws more, not less, power under higher static, it has no filter bypass damper, and dirt trapped by the filter loads the filter itself rather than migrating onto the coil.

questions.question: A condensate drain runs 30 feet horizontally from an air handler to its receptor, pitched at the minimum slope of 1/8 inch per foot. How much total fall does the run accumulate over that distance?

answers.text: The run falls 3.75 inches in total: 30 feet x 1/8 inch per foot = 3.75 inches of fall from the unit outlet to the receptor connection point
The run falls 30 inches in total, because each foot of horizontal run contributes a full inch of fall under the minimum slope requirement for condensate piping
The run falls 0.375 inch in total, found by dividing the slope by the run length instead of multiplying the slope by the number of feet in the run
The run falls 7.5 inches in total, because the minimum slope for a condensate drain of this length is figured at 1/4 inch per foot over the whole distance

questions.explanation: A is correct: total fall is slope times length: 30 ft x 0.125 in/ft = 3.75 inches. B is wrong because the slope is 1/8 inch per foot, not 1 inch per foot. C is wrong because fall accumulates with length; dividing slope by length understates it. D is wrong because 1/4 inch per foot is double the minimum slope used in this calculation.

questions.question: When soft-soldering (sweating) a copper joint for HVAC water-side work, what sequence produces a sound joint?

answers.text: Clean and flux the surfaces, assemble, heat the fitting, and let capillary action draw solder into the joint
Heat the solder rod directly with the torch until it drips and runs onto a cold, uncleaned fitting that was never fluxed or prepared
Apply flux after the joint has cooled to seal the outside
Melt solder into the gap with no flux on oxidized tubing

questions.explanation: Soldering depends on clean, fluxed surfaces and heating the fitting so capillary action pulls molten solder through the joint, option A. Heating solder over a cold dirty fitting (B) produces a weak surface blob, flux after cooling (C) cannot clean oxides or promote flow inside the joint, and omitting flux on oxidized copper (D) prevents wetting and bonding.
