questions.question: In a hot-humid climate, a vented crawlspace gets wetter in summer the more its vents are opened, and ducts there sweat heavily. Why does ventilation worsen it?

answers.text: Vent air adds moisture that condenses
Opening vents raises crawlspace temperature above the dew point of the outdoor air, which forces moisture out of the soil and into the framing
Wind through the vents pressurizes the crawlspace and squeezes liquid water out of the soil through the foundation walls into the space
The vents admit insects whose activity generates the extra moisture, and the duct sweating is a separate refrigerant-side problem

questions.explanation: Humid outdoor air entering the crawlspace contacts ducts and framing cooled by the house above, falls below its dew point, and deposits moisture, so more ventilation means more condensation. Ventilation does not heat surfaces above dew point in a way that draws water from soil, wind pressure does not squeeze liquid water through foundation walls, and insects do not generate this volume of moisture.

questions.question: A Manual J block load for a Hilton Head office is 36,000 Btuh of total cooling. Under the equipment selection method, single-stage cooling equipment is limited to 115 percent of the total load. What is the largest total cooling capacity that may be selected?

answers.text: The largest selectable capacity is 36,000 Btuh exactly, because the selection method forbids any capacity above the calculated block load under every circumstance
The largest selectable capacity is 54,000 Btuh, because the selection method allows equipment up to 150 percent of the load so the system can recover quickly from setbacks
The largest selectable capacity is 72,000 Btuh, because the next nominal equipment size above the load may always be chosen, even when it doubles the calculated requirement for the space
The largest selectable capacity is 41,400 Btuh: 36,000 Btuh x 1.15 = 41,400 Btuh, so the equipment's total capacity may exceed the load by no more than 15 percent

questions.explanation: D is correct: the selection limit is 115 percent of the total calculated load: 36,000 x 1.15 = 41,400 Btuh of total cooling capacity. A is wrong because the method permits a modest margin above the load, up to the 115 percent limit, to fit available equipment sizes. B is wrong because 150 percent far exceeds the selection limit and would short-cycle and dehumidify poorly. C is wrong because nominal size availability does not authorize doubling the calculated load.

questions.question: A duct section being hoisted slips in its rigging and falls to the ground, narrowly missing a worker. No one is hurt and nothing is damaged. Why should the near miss still be formally reported?

answers.text: Reporting is only a formality for insurance files, and the rigging practice that allowed the slip does not need to change because no loss actually occurred
The report protects the rigger from discipline, since a documented near miss legally prevents the company from correcting the worker who rigged the load
Reporting exposes the failed practice so it can be corrected before someone is hurt
The near miss should be reported only to the equipment rental company, because dropped rental straps are a warranty matter rather than a site safety matter

questions.explanation: A near miss reveals the same failed practice that will eventually cause an injury, and reporting it triggers correction of the rigging method. It is not empty insurance paperwork, it does not shield anyone from retraining or correction, and the hazard belongs to the site safety program rather than a rental warranty file.

questions.question: Why is the expansion tank connection often called the 'point of no pressure change' in a hydronic system?

answers.text: Because the tank is the one place where system pressure is zero whenever the circulating pump is running at full speed
Because the tank connection is always the highest point in the system and therefore sees only atmospheric pressure
Because no water ever moves in or out of the tank once the system has been filled and vented for the first time
Because pump operation cannot change the pressure at that connection point, so fill and pressure relationships stay stable when the pump is piped away from it

questions.explanation: At the tank connection the pump adds no pressure differential, which anchors system pressurization and prevents cavitation or air ingestion elsewhere. Option A is wrong because the point carries full static and fill pressure, option C is wrong because the tank continuously accepts and returns water with temperature changes, and option B confuses elevation with the pressure relationship.

questions.question: A contractor marks up a $1,000 job cost by 20% to set the price. What is the resulting price and its gross margin?

answers.text: $1,200 price; about 16.7% margin
$1,200 price and a 20.0 percent margin, because markup on cost and margin on price are always identical
$1,250 price and a 20.0 percent margin, found by using the margin divisor formula instead of the stated markup
$1,020 price and a 2.0 percent margin, found by adding the markup rate as a flat dollar amount

questions.explanation: A is correct because a 20 percent markup gives $1,200, and the $200 profit divided by $1,200 is about 16.7 percent margin. B is incorrect because a 20 percent markup does not produce a 20 percent margin. C is incorrect because it prices with the margin formula when the problem states a markup. D is incorrect because it treats 20 percent as $20 rather than 20 percent of $1,000.

questions.question: A Georgia-licensed heating and air contractor applies for the South Carolina residential HVAC license and asks for a waiver of the technical examination based on her Georgia credential. What should she expect?

answers.text: A full waiver, because the Commission maintains technical-waiver agreements with every state that borders South Carolina, and Georgia is a bordering state with its own licensing exam

No technical waiver on that basis, because the Commission's technical-portion waiver agreements are only with Alabama, North Carolina, and Mississippi, and the business and law examination is required in any event

A waiver of both examinations, because an applicant licensed by examination in another state is excused from all South Carolina testing when she documents five years of licensed practice, submits her out-of-state examination scores, and files proof of good standing from her home board
No waiver, but for a different reason: waiver agreements exist for Georgia, yet they apply only to the business and law portion, which is the portion she would still have to pass here

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Commission has examination-waiver agreements for the technical portion only with Alabama, North Carolina, and Mississippi; Georgia is not among them, and the South Carolina Business Management and Law examination is still required in waiver cases. A is wrong because the agreement list is those three states, not every bordering state. C is wrong because no route waives both examinations on an out-of-state credential alone. D is wrong because it reverses the portions — where a waiver exists it covers the technical portion, never the business and law examination.

ohio-hvac.quiz_title: Ohio HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An electronic expansion valve system holds superheat poorly after a controller replacement. The pressure transducer reads correctly, but the temperature sensor strapped to the suction line is loose and reading warm room air part of the time. What will the controller tend to do?

answers.text: It will calculate superheat that is too low and close the valve completely, because a warm sensor makes the suction vapor appear colder than it really is
It will calculate superheat that is too high and open the valve too far, risking floodback
It will ignore the temperature input entirely and hold the valve at a fixed opening, because EEV controllers do not use suction temperature to compute superheat
It will switch the stepper motor to reverse rotation permanently, because a loose sensor changes the electrical polarity seen by the controller inputs

questions.explanation: EEV superheat comes from measured pressure converted to saturation temperature compared with the actual suction temperature sensor; a sensor reading warm air inflates apparent superheat, so the controller opens the valve and can flood the coil. The error drives the valve open rather than closed, temperature is an essential superheat input, and a sensor fault does not reverse stepper polarity.

questions.question: A homeowner reports the indoor blower starts at the exact instant the burners light and blows cold air for a long time. In a normal modern furnace sequence, when should the indoor blower start and stop relative to the burners?

answers.text: It should start before the inducer motor begins its pre-purge and then stop again before ignition so the heat exchanger stays completely cold at light-off
It should run continuously whenever the house is occupied
It should start after a short heat-up delay following ignition and continue briefly after burner shutdown to harvest residual heat
It should start only after the thermostat is fully satisfied

questions.explanation: Modern controls delay indoor-blower start until the heat exchanger warms and keep it running briefly after burner shutdown to capture residual heat, which is option C. Starting before the inducer (A) reverses the safety sequence, continuous running (B) is a fan setting rather than the heating sequence, and waiting until the thermostat is satisfied (D) would leave heat in the exchanger undistributed.

questions.question: A boiler's burners shut off at the aquastat setting but the circulator continues to run and the rooms keep warming past the thermostat setting, with the thermostat no longer calling. Which interpretation best fits?

answers.text: The aquastat has failed because it should also stop the circulator in every design
Stored heat in the boiler and continued circulation can carry heat to the emitters after burner shutdown; control wiring and the circulator control must be checked against the designed sequence
The expansion tank is forcing hot water into the radiators
The low-water cutoff is overheating the building

questions.explanation: Boilers hold substantial stored heat, and whether the circulator should run on after burner shutdown depends on the control design, so option B - compare actual operation to the designed sequence before condemning parts - is correct. Many aquastats control the burner and limit only, so (A) overstates their role, the expansion tank (C) exerts no pumping force, and a low-water cutoff (D) is a safety switch that does not circulate water.

questions.question: A designer specifies external insulation on a metal supply duct crossing a hot attic instead of an internally lined duct. Which pairing of benefits and cautions is correct?

answers.text: External insulation raises airflow velocity so the duct can be downsized one full size
External insulation leaves the full duct area open to airflow and keeps fibers out of the airstream, but its outer jacket must be sealed as a vapor barrier and protected where it can be damaged
External insulation needs no vapor barrier because attic air is always dry

Internal lining and external insulation perform identically in every respect, so the choice is purely cosmetic, with the same effect on duct free area, airstream cleanliness, vapor control, and long-term maintenance access whichever side of the metal the insulation is placed on

questions.explanation: Wrapping the outside preserves the duct's internal dimensions and air quality while moving the vapor-control duty to the jacket, which must then be sealed and kept intact. Option A is wrong because insulation location does not change the velocity for a given duct size and airflow enough to justify downsizing; option C is wrong because attic air in humid weather can carry heavy moisture loads, which is exactly why the jacket must be sealed; option D is wrong because lining reduces the duct's free area and puts a fiber surface in the airstream — real differences, not cosmetic ones.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: A condensing furnace's condensate drain has a long flat section that sags, and the furnace intermittently locks out with water backing up into the collector box. What correction best addresses the cause?

answers.text: Raise the gas manifold pressure well above the manufacturer's specification so the furnace runs hotter and dries itself out from the inside during every cycle
Plug the secondary drain port so water cannot back up
Re-pitch the drain so it slopes continuously downhill to its termination, support it so it cannot sag, and keep required traps in place
Connect the condensate line directly into a gas vent

questions.explanation: Condensate must flow by gravity through a continuously sloped, supported drain with its required trap, option C; a sagging flat run pools water that eventually backs up and trips the furnace. Manifold pressure (A) has nothing to do with drainage, plugging a drain port (B) worsens backup, and tying condensate into a gas vent (D) mixes drainage with combustion venting and is prohibited practice.

questions.question: Winter inspection finds condensation and mold inside exterior wall cavities of a house whose indoor RH is high and whose envelope measures positive with respect to outdoors on the upper floor while the blower and exhaust systems run. What mechanism is at work?

answers.text: Cold outdoor air is being drawn into the walls at the top of the house and condensing its moisture on the warm interior drywall surface
Plumbing vents inside the walls are releasing sewer moisture that condenses on the cold sheathing in every exterior bay inspected
Positive pressure drives vapor outward
The wall insulation is absorbing moisture from the soil by capillary action through the foundation and releasing it at the upper floor cavities

questions.explanation: Positive indoor pressure pushes warm, moisture-laden indoor air outward through envelope leaks, and that air condenses when it reaches cold layers inside the wall. At the top of this house air is moving outward, not inward, plumbing vents do not wet every exterior bay, and capillary rise from soil does not deliver moisture to upper-floor wall cavities.

questions.question: A 95% AFUE furnace is vented with PVC and produces a steady stream of water at its drain during heating. A homeowner worries the heat exchanger is leaking. What should the technician explain and verify?

answers.text: Any water at the drain indicates a cracked heat exchanger, so the furnace must be condemned and shut down immediately without checking the drain, trap, or venting system
Condensation is normal for this appliance; verify the condensate drain and trap are clear and properly routed
The water is humidifier overflow and the furnace drain should be plugged
PVC venting causes rain to enter, so the vent should be switched to B-vent

questions.explanation: High-efficiency furnaces condense water vapor from flue gas by design, so the task is confirming drainage works. Condensate alone is not evidence of a crack. Plugging the drain would flood the appliance, and replacing low-temperature venting with B-vent would be wrong for a condensing, positive-pressure system.

questions.question: A meter shows a capacitor in a de-energized unit still holding charge. What should the technician do before handling its terminals?

answers.text: Touch both terminals together with bare fingers to drain off the stored charge as quickly as possible
Safely discharge the capacitor through an appropriate resistor and verify zero volts
Assume it drained because power is off
Hit it with a screwdriver handle

questions.explanation: Capacitors store charge after power is removed and must be discharged through a suitable resistor and verified at zero volts, so B is correct. Touching terminals risks shock and burns, assuming drainage is unsafe, and striking the part can damage it and still leave charge.

questions.question: A new draw-through air handler on a cooling coil pulls air across the coil, so its drain pan is under negative pressure. It is piped with a straight pipe from the pan to the drain with no trap, and at startup air is sucked up the drain line and condensate overflows the pan. What was missed?

answers.text: The drain needed a larger diameter so air could enter faster
A trap of adequate depth is needed so its water seal resists the negative pressure and lets condensate drain instead of being held in the pan
The pan needed a safety switch instead of any trap

The drain should have been connected to the liquid line to equalize pressure, tying the condensate piping directly into the sealed refrigerant circuit so the two pressures balance each other at startup

questions.explanation: On a draw-through unit the fan can draw air up an untrapped drain and hold water in the pan until it overflows; a trap with enough depth holds a seal against that pressure difference. Option A would admit more air, option C adds protection against overflow but does not make the drain work, and option D would join condensate piping to refrigerant piping, which is never correct.

questions.question: A job will cost $800 to perform. The contractor wants a 25% gross margin on the selling price, not a 25% markup on cost. What selling price achieves that margin?

answers.text: $1,000.00, found by adding a 25 percent markup directly onto the $800 cost of the work
$960.00, found by adding a 20 percent markup even though a different margin was requested
$1,600.00, found by doubling the cost on the assumption that margin and markup are interchangeable terms

questions.explanation: D is correct because price equals cost divided by one minus the desired margin, or $800 divided by 0.75, which is $1,066.67. A is incorrect because $1,000 reflects a 25 percent markup and yields only a 20 percent margin. B is incorrect because it applies neither the requested markup nor the requested margin. C is incorrect because it greatly overstates the divisor formula for a 25 percent margin.

questions.question: A firm whose qualifier holds an Ohio HVAC contractor license is asked to install a complete heating and cooling system in a newly built single-family house. How does the license apply to that job?

answers.text: The license does not cover the job, because the credential applies to commercial construction projects and residential buildings are outside that scope.
The license covers the job, because a commercial contractor license also authorizes mechanical work in any residential building the firm accepts.
The license covers the job if the homeowner signs a disclosure acknowledging that the installing firm normally performs commercial work only.

The license does not cover the job, but only because a separate refrigeration license is required for any system that contains refrigerant piping, even when the same arrangement has been used on the parties' earlier commercial projects without objection.

questions.explanation: A is correct: Ohio contractor licensure under this chapter reaches construction projects on buildings subject to the state building code, but residential buildings are expressly excluded from the definition of a construction project, so the license is a commercial credential and this house job sits outside it. B is wrong because the exclusion of residential buildings is categorical and is not cured by the firm's willingness to accept the work. C is wrong because no homeowner disclosure or waiver expands the statutory scope of the license to residential buildings. D is wrong because the job is outside scope because the building is residential, not because of the refrigerant piping in the system.

louisiana-hvac.quiz_title: Louisiana HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: After a hermetic compressor burnout, a replacement compressor is installed. Beyond changing the liquid-line drier, what contamination follow-up protects the new compressor?

answers.text: Test the oil/system for acid and fit suction-side filtration, then recheck and remove it as cleanup is confirmed
Do nothing further, because a single liquid-line drier change always removes all acid and debris left in the system by a hermetic motor burnout
Flush the new compressor itself with solvent before startup, because flushing a hermetic unit internally is the standard way to remove burnout contamination
Raise the operating superheat substantially for the first month, because running hot is an accepted substitute for removing acid from a contaminated system

questions.explanation: Burnout leaves acid and debris throughout the system, so acid testing plus temporary suction filtration with follow-up checks is the accepted cleanup approach. One drier change rarely completes a burnout cleanup, flushing inside a new hermetic compressor is not a service procedure, and running hot does not neutralize or remove acid and can harm the new machine.

questions.question: A homeowner asks why the new R-454B air handler runs its blower for a while after a leak sensor trips, even though cooling has stopped. What is the correct explanation?

answers.text: The blower is removing residual heat from the electric heat strips, a normal cool-down sequence that happens to coincide with the sensor alarm event
The blower pressurizes the duct system so refrigerant vapor is forced back through the leak point into the coil, resealing the system temporarily
The blower dilutes and disperses leaked refrigerant through the duct system so room concentration stays low
The blower run is a fault in itself, because mitigation design requires the air handler to shut down every moving part the instant a sensor trips

questions.explanation: Leak mitigation uses indoor airflow to dilute and disperse refrigerant so concentration in the occupied space stays low. The run is not a heat-strip cool-down, airflow cannot push vapor back into a leaking coil or reseal it, and the blower operation is an intended mitigation response rather than a second fault.

questions.question: A 15 kW electric furnace has three equal 5 kW elements. On a heat call all sequencer contacts close, supply voltage is correct, but total current draw equals only two-thirds of the expected value and supply air is cooler than normal. What is the most likely fault?

answers.text: One heating element is open and producing no heat
The sequencer is energizing an extra element
The blower is running too fast for any heating to occur
The thermostat is set to emergency heat on a gas furnace

questions.explanation: Losing exactly one of three equal elements removes one-third of capacity and current while voltage and controls remain normal, matching option A. An extra element (B) would raise current above expected, blower speed (C) affects temperature rise but not element current, and the system described (D) is electric resistance heat, not a gas furnace.

questions.question: Which set of duct locations must all be included when a duct system is sealed to its specified class?

answers.text: Only the transverse joints, because longitudinal seams are factory-sealed
Transverse joints, longitudinal seams, and branch tap-ins and other duct wall penetrations
Only the connections at the air handler, because the rest of the system leaks negligibly
Only fittings, because straight duct sections never leak at their seams

questions.explanation: Leakage occurs at every discontinuity in the duct wall, so the sealing class applies to joints, seams, taps, and penetrations alike. Option A is wrong because longitudinal seams such as Pittsburgh and snap-lock seams do leak and are explicitly part of sealing requirements; option C is wrong because field joints throughout the run typically outnumber and out-leak the equipment connections; option D is wrong because straight sections are joined by longitudinal seams, which are a primary leakage path when left unsealed.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: CSST runs through a house with several metal systems. The bonding jumper for the CSST is installed primarily to:

answers.text: Carry the normal return current of the HVAC circuits, so that a separate equipment grounding conductor is no longer needed for the furnace
Replace the grounding electrode conductor for the whole house, because bonding the gas tubing satisfies every grounding requirement by itself
Equalize electrical potential and reduce arcing damage from induced voltage
Prevent corrosion of the tubing by draining stray direct current from the gas line into the soil outside the building foundation wall

questions.explanation: Equalize electrical potential and reduce arcing damage from induced voltage. Bonding does not carry circuit return current, replace the service grounding system, or serve as a corrosion drain to soil.

questions.question: A system is verified to have solid liquid at the sight glass with correct subcooling, yet the moisture indicator shows wet. The correct response is:

answers.text: Ignore it, because a clear glass proves the system is dry under all conditions, including after the system has been opened for service, evacuated briefly, and returned to operation with its original drier still in place
Replace the liquid-line drier (and investigate how moisture entered), because the indicator reports moisture independently of bubbles
Remove charge until bubbles appear
Replace the expansion valve with a larger size

questions.explanation: Bubbles and moisture are separate indications: a clear glass can coexist with wet refrigerant, and the remedy is renewed drying capacity plus finding the moisture source. Option A discards a valid warning, option C deliberately creates the flashing the glass is used to detect, and option D changes feed capacity for a contamination problem it cannot fix.

questions.question: Windows condense heavily on cold winter mornings in a tight new home with a large family, showers, and cooking. Indoor humidity reads 48%. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: The humidifier is undersized, so raising indoor humidity further will warm the window glass and stop the condensation from forming
The windows are leaking refrigerant, because condensation on glass is a recognized sign of a cooling-system charge problem in winter
The furnace is oversized for cooling, which explains winter window moisture even though the cooling system is not operating at all
Indoor moisture generation exceeds removal, so humidity must be lowered and ventilation or exhaust increased rather than adding humidification.

questions.explanation: Condensation means indoor dew point exceeds the cold glass temperature; the fix is less indoor moisture and more removal through ventilation and exhaust. Adding humidity makes it worse, windows contain no refrigerant, and cooling sizing is irrelevant to a winter moisture balance.

questions.question: A new refrigerant line set is to be pressure tested for leaks before evacuation. Which medium and practice are correct?

answers.text: Use oxygen from a cutting torch tank
Use compressed shop air without a regulator
Use dry nitrogen with a regulator, test at the specified pressure, and use an electronic detector or bubbles to check joints
Pressurize with refrigerant alone to maximum pressure

questions.explanation: Regulated dry nitrogen is inert and standard for pressure testing, with joints checked by detector or bubble solution, so C is correct. Oxygen can cause explosive combustion with oil, unregulated shop air adds moisture and uncontrolled pressure, and refrigerant alone is not the proper test medium.

questions.question: Why do many manufacturers require product registration within a set window after installation for extended parts coverage?

answers.text: Registration is purely a marketing enrollment that has no effect on the duration or terms of the equipment's parts coverage
Registration links the serial number to the install date and owner, activating the longer registered warranty term
The unregistered warranty is longer, so registration is offered mainly to shorten coverage in exchange for email promotions
Registration transfers the warranty to the installing company, so the homeowner no longer owns the coverage on their equipment

questions.explanation: For many brands the longer parts term applies only when the product is registered on time with its installation details. It is a coverage condition rather than mere marketing, registration extends rather than shortens the term, and coverage stays with the equipment owner rather than transferring to the installer.

questions.question: A variable-speed drive slows a chilled-water pump to 90% of full speed. Using the pump affinity laws, about how much pump power is saved?

answers.text: About 3%, because pump power falls only in direct one-to-one proportion to the drop in pump rotational speed
About 10%, because pump power falls in proportion to the square of the speed ratio at reduced flow conditions
About 19%, because pump head and pump power always change by exactly the same percentage as each other
About 27%, because power varies with the cube of speed: 0.9 cubed is about 0.73 of full power

questions.explanation: Power follows the cube law: 0.9^3 = 0.729, so roughly 27% of the power is saved. Option A uses the flow relationship, option B uses the head (square) relationship, and option C wrongly equates head and power changes, which follow different exponents.

questions.question: Two estimators price the same furnace change-out. One counts every fitting and hanger from the drawings; the other guesses quantities from memory. What practice distinguishes the first estimator?

answers.text: Applying a single company-wide markup before any quantities for the specific job have been determined at all
Relying on the supplier to set the contract price after the proposal has already been presented to the owner
Performing a quantity takeoff
Using last year's material prices without checking whether sizes, counts, or current costs have changed

questions.explanation: C is correct because a quantity takeoff counts the actual materials and components needed from the plans and scope. A is incorrect because markup is applied after costs are built, not before quantities exist. B is incorrect because delegating pricing to a supplier after proposal abandons the estimator's takeoff duty. D is incorrect because stale prices and uncounted quantities are the guessing approach the question contrasts.

kentucky-hvac-journeyman.quiz_title: Kentucky HVAC Journeyman Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: On a 45-degree rainy day a heat pump defrosts every 30 minutes even though the outdoor coil shows little frost, wasting energy and cycling the strip heat each time. The coil sensor is firmly clipped to its tube and its wiring is intact. What control behavior is the journeyman checking?

answers.text: Whether the defrost control is a demand type reading a mis-scaled sensor value, or a time-temperature type set to initiate on elapsed time regardless of frost need
Whether the indoor thermostat is calling for cooling between heating cycles and forcing the valve to shift over, using the values and conditions given in the problem statement itself
Whether the crankcase heater is oversized and warming the coil sensor through the outdoor unit's base pan metal
Whether the outdoor fan blade is pitched for summer duty and pushing frost-forming air across the coil too fast

questions.explanation: A is correct: Frequent defrosts on a mild day with little frost point at the initiation logic, a demand-defrost sensor reading out of scale, or a time-temperature board initiating on its timer interval whether frost exists or not; the control type and sensor value are verified against the manufacturer's chart before parts are replaced. B is wrong because the unit stays in heating and defrosts on its own control, not on cooling calls. C is wrong because a crankcase heater warms the compressor shell, not the coil sensor clipped on its tube. D is wrong because fan blade pitch does not command defrost initiation timing.

questions.question: A split system is factory-charged for a 15-foot line set. The installed line set measures 40 feet, and the manufacturer instructions direct adding 0.6 ounce of refrigerant per foot of line beyond 15 feet. How much additional charge must be weighed in?

answers.text: 24 ounces, figured by applying the per-foot rate to the entire 40-foot length of the line set
15 ounces, figured by applying the per-foot rate to the 25 feet beyond the factory-charged length
9 ounces, figured by applying the per-foot rate only to the 15 feet covered by the factory charge
40 ounces, figured by adding one full ounce for every foot of line set installed at the home

questions.explanation: B is correct: Extra length = 40 - 15 = 25 ft. Added charge = 25 ft x 0.6 oz per ft = 15 oz. A is wrong because it charges for the first 15 feet, which the factory charge already covers. C is wrong because it applies the rate to the covered length instead of the excess length. D is wrong because the specified rate is 0.6 ounce per foot, not 1 ounce per foot.

questions.question: A heat pump air handler is located in an attic. In addition to an access opening large enough to remove the appliance, what working provision is required at the appliance?

answers.text: A permanent ladder bolted to the ceiling joists directly below the attic access opening for the life of the unit
A hoist beam rated for the weight of the appliance, installed over the unit for future compressor change-outs
A second access opening at the far end of the attic so the technician can exit without turning around
A level working platform at least 30 inches by 30 inches in front of the service side of the appliance

questions.explanation: D is correct: Attic appliance installations require a level working platform not less than 30 inches by 30 inches in front of the control/service side, along with the access opening and passageway. A is wrong because a permanent ladder is not the required working provision. B is wrong because no hoist beam is required for attic appliances. C is wrong because a second exit opening is not required; the platform is.

questions.question: A supply duct must run underground beneath a slab-on-grade addition. Which construction is required?

answers.text: Standard galvanized duct wrapped in plastic sheeting, laid level so condensate can collect evenly along the run
Unsealed fiberboard duct, because soil moisture keeps the board pliable and prevents it from cracking over time
Approved watertight, corrosion-resistant material with sealed joints, sloped to drain to an accessible point
Flexible duct pulled through a larger PVC sleeve, with the annular space left open as an insulation air gap

questions.explanation: C is correct: Underground ducts must be of approved material suitable for burial — watertight and corrosion resistant — with sealed joints, installed to slope so any moisture drains to an accessible point rather than pooling. A is wrong because plastic-wrapped standard duct is not an approved underground system and a level run traps water. B is wrong because fiberboard deteriorates in soil moisture. D is wrong because an open annulus invites water and pests and the flex duct itself is not an approved underground duct.

questions.question: A combustion air opening must provide 50 square inches of net free area and will be covered by a wood louver. Wood louvers may be assumed to have 25 percent free area. What gross louver area is required?

answers.text: 200 square inches of gross louver area to deliver the required 50 square inches of net free area
100 square inches of gross louver area, figured by doubling the required net free area once
67 square inches of gross louver area, figured with the free-area percentage used for metal louvers
50 square inches of gross louver area, treating the louver face area as fully open to airflow

questions.explanation: A is correct: Gross area = net free area / free-area fraction = 50 / 0.25 = 200 sq in. B is wrong because doubling assumes 50 percent free area, which is not the wood louver assumption. C is wrong because about 67 sq in. uses the 75 percent metal louver figure for a wood louver. D is wrong because a louvered opening is not 100 percent free area.

questions.question: What is the maximum developed length permitted for a residential clothes dryer exhaust duct, before any reduction for fittings, where the manufacturer's instructions do not specify a different length?

answers.text: 25 feet, a limit borrowed from the maximum length allowed for a dryer's flexible transition duct assembly, measured from the back of the dryer cabinet to the wall cap
15 feet, because dryer ducts are limited to the same developed length as a bathroom exhaust fan duct run
35 feet from the dryer transition duct connection to the outdoor termination, before fitting reductions apply
50 feet, provided the duct is one size larger than the dryer outlet for the entire length of the exhaust run

questions.explanation: C is correct: The dryer exhaust duct maximum equivalent length is 35 feet measured from the transition duct connection to the termination, with reductions then taken for each elbow. A is wrong because 25 feet is not the base allowance. B is wrong because bathroom fan ducts have no such 15-foot dryer limit. D is wrong because upsizing the duct does not extend the 35-foot base limit to 50 feet.

questions.question: A digital thermostat resets and clicks the contactor in and out whenever the cooling call is heavy, and the problem began when the old mercury thermostat was replaced without adding a wire. The transformer and contactor test good. What is the likely wiring deficiency?

answers.text: The thermostat has no dedicated common (C) conductor, so it power-steals through the load and browns out under call load
The thermostat cable has one conductor too many landed, which forces the control board to share its fuse with the stat, checked against the manufacturer's data for the equipment on site
The outdoor unit is missing its equipment ground, which makes the thermostat display reset on every cooling cycle
The thermostat is mounted level, which prevents a digital stat from holding a steady supply voltage during calls

questions.explanation: A is correct: Many digital thermostats need a dedicated common (C) wire for steady power; without one they power-steal through the contactor coil circuit, and the resulting voltage sag under load resets the stat and chatters the contactor, so the fix is to provide a common conductor (spare wire or an approved add-a-wire device). B is wrong because an extra landed conductor does not create this load-dependent brownout pattern, and the board tested good. C is wrong because the equipment ground is a safety path, not the thermostat's power supply. D is wrong because leveling matters for mercury stats, not for powering a digital display.

questions.question: A journeyman joins two copper refrigerant tubes with a filler metal that melts at 1,100 degrees Fahrenheit and flows into the closely fitted joint by capillary action. How is this joining process classified, and what follows for the joint?

answers.text: It is soldering, since any filler that flows by capillary action into a copper joint is classified as a solder
It is brazing, since the filler melts above 840 degrees, and the joint is made with a nitrogen purge flowing during heating
It is welding, since the base copper tubes themselves melt and fuse together at the joint during the heating cycle
It is soft soldering with a high-temperature alloy, classified by the torch used rather than by the filler melting point, with the system running steadily under the stated operating load

questions.explanation: B is correct: Brazing is defined by a filler metal melting above 840 degrees Fahrenheit (and below the base metal's melting point); at 1,100 degrees this joint is brazed, and refrigerant piping is brazed with a low nitrogen purge flowing so oxide scale does not form inside the tube. A is wrong because soldering is the below-840-degree process, regardless of capillary flow, which both processes use. C is wrong because in brazing the base tubes are not melted and fused; only the filler melts. D is wrong because classification follows the filler's melting temperature, not the torch or a trade nickname.

questions.question: At commissioning, a blower is rated to deliver the design airflow at 0.50 inch water column total external static. The wet coil drops 0.20 inch and the filter drops 0.08 inch at design airflow. How much static pressure remains for the duct system itself?

answers.text: 0.22 inch, found by subtracting the coil and filter drops from the blower's rated total external static pressure
0.78 inch, found by adding the coil and filter drops on top of the blower's rated total external static pressure
0.50 inch, since the duct system always receives the full blower rating regardless of the devices in the airstream
0.12 inch, found by subtracting only the filter drop from a coil rating that was never part of the static budget

questions.explanation: A is correct: Duct budget = 0.50 - 0.20 - 0.08 = 0.22 inch w.c. left for supply and return duct friction at design airflow; ducts are then sized (friction rate) to live inside that remainder. B is wrong because component drops consume the blower budget rather than adding to it. C is wrong because the coil and filter sit in the airstream and their drops are charged against the same 0.50 inch. D is wrong because it omits the coil drop, the largest single device drop in this budget.

questions.question: A condensate line drains by gravity to its termination. A running trap sits at the unit outlet, and an open vent tee stands on the downstream side of the trap. How is this arrangement judged?

answers.text: It is wrong, since a vent placed anywhere in a condensate line breaks the trap seal and must be removed entirely
It is wrong, since the vent must stand between the unit outlet and the trap to let pan air escape ahead of the seal
It is correct, since the vent downstream of the trap lets the line drain freely while the trap seal stays intact
It is correct only in cooling season, since in heating season the same vent must be capped to hold the trap prime

questions.explanation: C is correct: A vent (where used) belongs downstream of the trap: the trap at the unit outlet holds its water seal against the unit's pressure, and the open vent beyond it prevents siphoning and lets the gravity line drain freely. A is wrong because a correctly placed downstream vent does not break the seal; the seal is on the unit side of the trap. B is wrong because a vent ahead of the trap is exactly the placement that defeats the seal, especially on a negative-pressure coil. D is wrong because trap-and-vent function does not change with the season on a shared drain.

questions.question: A licensed journeyman wants to advertise under a personal business name and sign a contract directly with a homeowner for a system change-out. What is the correct position?

answers.text: It is permitted, because a journeyman license carries the same right to advertise and contract as a master license holds
It is permitted if the journeyman carries the required insurance, because insurance alone confers contracting authority
It is permitted for jobs under a set dollar amount, because small residential change-outs fall outside the contracting rules

It is not permitted: a journeyman performs HVAC work under a master's supervision, direction, and responsibility, and only a licensed master may advertise and practice HVAC contracting and obtain the permits for the work

questions.explanation: D is correct: The journeyman license authorizes performing HVAC work under the supervision, direction, and responsibility of a master contractor; advertising and practicing HVAC contracting, including obtaining necessary permits, belongs to the master license, and using a title implying master status without that license is prohibited. A is wrong because the two licenses confer different authority. B is wrong because insurance is a practice condition, not a grant of contracting authority. C is wrong because no small-job dollar exception to the contracting rule exists.

questions.question: A 19-year-old resident alien who is authorized to work in the United States asks whether the basic personal qualifications bar applying for a Kentucky journeyman HVAC mechanic license. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: Yes, because only a United States citizen may hold any Kentucky HVAC license, regardless of work authorization status
Yes, because the minimum age for a journeyman applicant is 21 years, even though the applicant is work-authorized
No — an applicant who is at least 18 and is a citizen or a resident alien authorized to work in the United States meets those qualifications

No, because there is no age or work-authorization qualification at all for the journeyman license in Kentucky's scheme, and the department may still license the applicant on a provisional basis while the paperwork is reviewed by the licensing branch

questions.explanation: C is correct: A journeyman applicant must be at least 18 years old and be a U.S. citizen or a resident alien authorized to do work in the United States; this applicant meets both. A is wrong because the qualification expressly includes authorized resident aliens, not citizens only. B is wrong because the minimum age is 18, not 21. D is wrong because both an age qualification and a citizenship/work-authorization qualification do exist.

kentucky-hvac.quiz_title: Kentucky HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An accumulator-equipped system returns with a low crankcase oil level, a suction accumulator that is cold and heavy with liquid, and normal superheat at the evaporator outlet. What accumulator fault fits these findings?

answers.text: The accumulator is installed in the liquid line instead of the suction line, which is why it is cold and full while the evaporator superheat remains normal
The accumulator's oil-return orifice at the bottom of its U-tube is plugged
The accumulator's internal U-tube has grown longer with age, so it now holds more liquid than the compressor crankcase can supply with oil during operation
The accumulator is too small, because an undersized vessel returns oil to the compressor faster than a correctly sized vessel and empties the crankcase promptly

questions.explanation: The small orifice at the U-tube bottom meters oil (and some liquid) back; when it plugs, oil collects in the accumulator and the crankcase starves while evaporator operation can look normal. A suction accumulator belongs where it is described and its cold, full condition follows the plugged return, the U-tube does not change length with age, and an undersized accumulator risks liquid carryover rather than quietly storing the system's oil.

questions.question: A homeowner asks why the new R-454B air handler runs its blower for a while after a leak sensor trips, even though cooling has stopped. What is the correct explanation?

answers.text: The blower is removing residual heat from the electric heat strips, a normal cool-down sequence that happens to coincide with the sensor alarm event
The blower pressurizes the duct system so refrigerant vapor is forced back through the leak point into the coil, resealing the system temporarily
The blower dilutes and disperses leaked refrigerant through the duct system so room concentration stays low
The blower run is a fault in itself, because mitigation design requires the air handler to shut down every moving part the instant a sensor trips

questions.explanation: Leak mitigation uses indoor airflow to dilute and disperse refrigerant so concentration in the occupied space stays low. The run is not a heat-strip cool-down, airflow cannot push vapor back into a leaking coil or reseal it, and the blower operation is an intended mitigation response rather than a second fault.

questions.question: A fixed-orifice system's suction pressure corresponds to an evaporator saturation temperature of 40°F, and the suction line at the evaporator outlet measures 52°F. What is the evaporator superheat?

answers.text: 12°F, found by subtracting the saturation temperature from the suction-line temperature
92°F, found by adding the two temperatures
52°F, because superheat equals the suction-line temperature itself, at the evaporator outlet coil
40°F, because superheat equals the saturation temperature itself

questions.explanation: Superheat is the vapor temperature above saturation, so 52 minus 40 gives 12 degrees of superheat. Option B adds the values, which is not how any refrigerant temperature difference is calculated, and options C and D each substitute a single temperature for the required difference.

questions.question: At commissioning, a combustion analyzer shows rising carbon monoxide and unstable readings as the furnace runs longer. What is the appropriate response?

answers.text: Stop and investigate before leaving it in service
Raise the gas pressure to burn the carbon monoxide more completely and recheck only if the customer reports symptoms later on
Note the readings as normal break-in behavior for new exchangers and leave without further testing or documentation at all
Disable the analyzer alarm and run the furnace longer, because extended operation usually cleans a new exchanger by itself fully

questions.explanation: Rising, unstable carbon monoxide is not a leave-in-service finding; the installer must stop, investigate causes such as venting, combustion air, overfiring, or exchanger problems, and correct them. Option B worsens a possible overfiring or venting fault, option C dismisses a safety measurement as break-in, and option D silences the instrument instead of the hazard.

questions.question: A homeowner calls because the outdoor unit is steaming, the outdoor fan has stopped, and a whoosh was heard, while the unit is heating on a frosty morning. What should the technician explain first?

answers.text: The compressor has failed and the unit should be shut off at the breaker immediately
The refrigerant charge is escaping as steam and the area should be evacuated
This is a normal defrost: the reversing valve shifted, the fan stopped, frost is melting into visible vapor, and the cycle will end and heating will resume in a few minutes
The unit has mistakenly switched to cooling for the rest of the day

questions.explanation: Steam-like vapor, a stopped outdoor fan, and the reversing-valve whoosh are the classic signs of a normal defrost melting accumulated frost. Option A declares a failure without any fault evidence, option B mistakes water vapor for refrigerant, which is not visible as steam in this way, and option D overstates a minutes-long defrost as a day-long mode change.

questions.question: With a blower door holding the house at -50 Pa with respect to outdoors, an attached garage zone reads -25 Pa with respect to outdoors. How should this zonal reading be interpreted?

answers.text: The garage is connected only to the house, because any reading below zero means the zone has no openings at all to the outdoors or to other zones
The garage is connected only to outdoors, since an intermediate reading is produced when a zone is fully vented and the gauge averages house and outdoor pressure
Garage connects to both sides
The reading is a gauge error, because a zone can only ever read either the full house pressure or zero, never a stable value in between the two

questions.explanation: A reading halfway between house and outdoor pressure indicates the garage has meaningful connections to both the house and outdoors, splitting its pressure between them. A house-only connection would read near -50 Pa, an outdoors-only connection would read near zero, and stable intermediate zonal readings are a normal, informative result of the method.

questions.question: Why are resistance temperature detectors (RTDs) often chosen for critical duct and water temperature sensing over basic thermistors?

answers.text: They offer stable, repeatable accuracy over time and a wide temperature range, which suits trend and control decisions
They need no wiring and transmit temperature by line pressure
They change resistance so erratically from minute to minute that the controller must average hundreds of readings per second just to get a usable value
They are always the lowest-cost sensor, so accuracy is not a factor in the choice

questions.explanation: RTD stability and repeatability support reliable control and trending in critical locations. RTDs are wired devices, not pressure transmitters, their resistance changes predictably with temperature, and they typically cost more than thermistors, so the choice is performance-driven, not price-driven.

questions.question: A homeowner upgrades from a MERV 8 to a MERV 13 filter of the same size, and the system begins tripping the furnace limit and freezing the cooling coil. What is the most likely link?

answers.text: The finer filter raised pressure drop and reduced airflow below what the equipment needs
The MERV 13 filter added heat to the airstream
The filter removed so many particles that the blower oversped
Higher MERV filters always damage heating and cooling equipment whenever they are installed, regardless of filter size, airflow, or the system's actual pressure drop

questions.explanation: Reduced airflow from added filter resistance explains both overheating in heat and coil freezing in cooling. Filters do not add meaningful heat or cause blower overspeed by cleaning the air. A properly selected high-MERV installation with adequate filter area works fine, so the rating alone is not inherently damaging.

questions.question: A balancer finds a zone that cannot reach design airflow even with its dampers fully open, while the fan and other zones have capacity to spare on paper. What is the most professional handling in the report?

answers.text: Record the design value as achieved so the report shows full compliance
Document the shortfall with measured data, identify the apparent restriction or design limitation, and refer it for correction rather than falsifying a passing value
Close the dampers serving several other zones permanently so air is forced into the short zone, and report that forced condition as the final balanced result for the whole system
Omit the zone from the report so the deficiency is not visible

questions.explanation: A TAB report must state actual measured results and flag deficiencies for the responsible party to resolve. Recording unachieved values is falsification, robbing other zones is not a legitimate final balance, and omitting the zone conceals a known defect from the owner and design team.

questions.question: Why does the furnace or air handler blower matter to a cooling system's rated combination?

answers.text: The blower matters only for heating season, because cooling capacity is set entirely at the outdoor unit and airflow is secondary
Blower airflow across the coil is part of the tested combination, and wrong airflow changes capacity, efficiency, and dehumidification
A stronger blower always raises the rating, so oversizing the air handler is a reliable way to gain extra efficiency points
Blower selection affects only noise level, since the coil removes the same moisture regardless of the air volume crossing it

questions.explanation: Rated performance assumes a specified airflow; too much or too little distorts sensible and latent capacity. The blower is central in cooling as well as heating, more airflow is not automatically better, and moisture removal is strongly airflow-dependent.

questions.question: A contractor asks which authority currently administers Kentucky HVAC licensing, conducts examinations, and maintains the list of licensees. Which answer is correct?

answers.text: The Kentucky Board of HVAC Contractors, which still issues all licenses and conducts every examination
The Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction, through its Division of HVAC
Prov, the outside testing vendor, which administers licensing and keeps the licensee register
Each county government, which issues its own HVAC contractor license for work in that county

questions.explanation: B is correct: Kentucky HVAC licensing is administered by the Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction through its Division of HVAC, which promulgates rules, conducts examinations, and maintains licensee and apprentice records. A is wrong because the former board was repealed in 2017 and no longer licenses. C is wrong because the examinations are developed and administered by the department or its designee, not by a named outside vendor as licensor. D is wrong because licensure is statewide under the department, not issued county by county.

questions.question: A gas piping system serves appliances totaling 200,000 Btu per hour input. The gas has a heating value of about 1,000 Btu per cubic foot. The design flow the piping must deliver is:

answers.text: 200 cubic feet per hour, found by dividing the total input of 200,000 Btu per hour by 1,000 Btu per cubic foot
20 cubic feet per hour, found by dividing the total input by the heating value and then again by a factor of ten
2,000 cubic feet per hour, found by multiplying the total input in thousands by the heating value in thousands
100 cubic feet per hour, found by assuming only half the appliances can ever operate at the same time by code

questions.explanation: A is correct: Flow = 200,000 Btu/h / 1,000 Btu per cu ft = 200 cu ft/h, the value entered into the sizing tables with the applicable length and pressure drop. B is wrong because the extra division by ten understates demand. C is wrong because that multiplication overstates demand tenfold. D is wrong because the sizing basis is the total connected load unless a documented diversity basis applies, which the stem does not give.

hawaii-c52-hvac.quiz_title: Hawaii C-52 HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Where should a suction-line filter be used, and what caution applies to leaving it in place permanently?

answers.text: It is required permanently on every new installation, because suction filtration is the only protection a compressor has against moisture in the refrigerant charge
It is mainly a temporary cleanup device after a burnout or contamination event, and a permanent one can cause excessive suction pressure drop
It belongs in the liquid line ahead of the drier, because suction filters and liquid driers perform the same job and are installed in the same location interchangeably
It should never be used after a burnout, because the acid and debris from a burnout can only be removed by replacing the compressor and the evaporator coil

questions.explanation: Suction filters excel at catching burnout debris and acid before the new compressor, but their pressure drop penalizes capacity, so they are monitored and often removed after cleanup. They are not a universal permanent requirement on clean new systems, they are suction-side devices distinct from liquid driers, and burnout cleanup is a primary use for them rather than a prohibited one.

questions.question: A homeowner asks why the new R-454B air handler runs its blower for a while after a leak sensor trips, even though cooling has stopped. What is the correct explanation?

answers.text: The blower is removing residual heat from the electric heat strips, a normal cool-down sequence that happens to coincide with the sensor alarm event
The blower pressurizes the duct system so refrigerant vapor is forced back through the leak point into the coil, resealing the system temporarily
The blower dilutes and disperses leaked refrigerant through the duct system so room concentration stays low
The blower run is a fault in itself, because mitigation design requires the air handler to shut down every moving part the instant a sensor trips

questions.explanation: Leak mitigation uses indoor airflow to dilute and disperse refrigerant so concentration in the occupied space stays low. The run is not a heat-strip cool-down, airflow cannot push vapor back into a leaking coil or reseal it, and the blower operation is an intended mitigation response rather than a second fault.

questions.question: An air handler above a finished ceiling cools normally for hours, then stops with its condensate safety switch open, restarting after the water level slowly falls. The primary drain flows freely when tested with a full pan of water poured in at once. What subtle fault best fits intermittent trips under real operation?

answers.text: The switch is defective whenever it opens, so it should be replaced without further checks, without inspecting the drain line, the trap, or the water level in the pan itself
The refrigerant charge rises during the day and forces water out of the pan
The unit is producing no condensate, so the switch must be reading a false level
A partially restricted drain or marginal trap holds drainage just behind production during long humid runs, slowly raising the level until the switch trips

questions.explanation: A drain that passes a quick pour test can still lag behind steady condensate production if it is partly restricted or the trap and slope are marginal, which matches trips after long humid runtimes. Option A assumes the switch is lying when its behavior matches a genuinely rising water level. Option B invents a link between charge and pan level that does not exist, and option C is contradicted by water visibly reaching the switch in a humid-climate cooling run.

questions.question: Besides compressor speed control, which coordinated controls does a typical inverter ductless system use to match capacity smoothly?

answers.text: A fixed orifice and a single-speed outdoor fan switched only on and off, with no modulation of either airflow or refrigerant flow as the compressor changes speed to follow the changing load
A gas valve that stages burners to assist the compressor
A mechanical timer that forces full-speed runs every ten minutes
Variable-speed indoor and outdoor fans and an electronic expansion valve, all adjusted by the control board together with compressor speed

questions.explanation: Inverter systems modulate the whole refrigeration and air side together, with fan speeds and electronic valve opening following compressor speed under board control. Option A describes fixed-capacity hardware, option B adds a furnace that a ductless system does not have, and option C contradicts the continuous modulation these systems are built for.

questions.question: A 96% AFUE furnace is installed in a basement. Its flue gases are relatively cool and the vent system is designed to operate under positive pressure with a condensate drain at the furnace. How should its venting be handled?

answers.text: Vent it into an existing unlined masonry chimney with no corrosion-resistant liner, relying on the chimney's natural draft to carry the cool flue gases out
Use a single-wall metal connector into a Type B vent shared with a water heater
Vent it with the manufacturer-approved sealed plastic vent system and drain the condensate as directed
Let it vent into the basement and rely on dilution air to carry products out

questions.explanation: A 96% unit is a condensing, positive-pressure (Category IV) appliance, so it needs the manufacturer-approved sealed vent material and condensate handling in option C. Cool, moisture-laden flue gas would condense in and damage an unlined masonry chimney (A), Type B/common venting (B) is for negative-pressure non-condensing appliances and risks spillage, and venting into the space (D) is a carbon-monoxide hazard.

questions.question: A return grille that is too small for the required CFM will most likely cause:

answers.text: Lower velocity and quieter operation
No change in static pressure
High velocity, noise, and increased pressure drop
Higher refrigerant superheat directly, with no change in airflow or noise

questions.explanation: Forcing required CFM through too little free area raises velocity, which creates noise and pressure drop, so C is correct. A and B describe the opposite of the actual effect, and superheat is a refrigeration measurement not directly set by grille size.

questions.question: Three compressors serve a process cooling load. The lead compressor runs continuously while the others short-cycle. What staging change best evens wear and stabilizes capacity?

answers.text: Disable the lag compressors so the lead machine handles every load alone
Rotate the lead position on a schedule or by run hours and enforce anti-short-cycle timing between starts
Remove all start delays and anti-short-cycle timers so lag machines can start instantly whenever suction pressure moves even slightly
Wire all three contactors together so every compressor starts and stops at the same instant

questions.explanation: Lead-lag rotation balances run hours and timing delays prevent damaging rapid cycling. Disabling lag machines sacrifices capacity, removing delays worsens short-cycling, and starting all machines together creates demand spikes and simultaneous wear rather than staged control.

questions.question: A furnace clocks at an input 20% above its rating plate after a gas-valve replacement. The most likely setup causes are:

answers.text: Manifold pressure set too high or wrong-size orifices installed
A vent connector one size larger than the minimum, because a larger vent increases draft and pulls extra gas through the burner orifices
A sediment trap with a long capped leg, because the trap volume adds a reserve of gas that the meter counts as additional furnace input
A thermostat set several degrees above room temperature, because a larger temperature difference makes the gas valve deliver more fuel per hour

questions.explanation: Manifold pressure set too high or wrong-size orifices installed. Vent size, trap volume, and thermostat setting do not change firing rate; excessive manifold pressure or oversized orifices do.

questions.question: A protective-environment room for an immunocompromised patient needs the opposite relationship from an isolation room. What is it, and why?

answers.text: It is kept negative so any microbes generated by the patient are drawn inward and cannot reach the supply diffuser in the ceiling
It is kept positive with well-filtered supply air so corridor air and its contaminants are kept out of the room.
It is kept at exactly the same pressure as the corridor, because pressure differences of any kind are prohibited around immunocompromised patients
It is ventilated only with unfiltered outdoor air, because filtration removes the natural microbes that help such patients build immunity

questions.explanation: Protective environments use positive pressure and high-quality filtered supply to shield a vulnerable patient from outside contaminants. Negative pressure would draw corridor air in, neutral pressure gives no protective flow direction, and unfiltered air is the opposite of the room's purpose.

questions.question: A new refrigerant line set is to be pressure tested for leaks before evacuation. Which medium and practice are correct?

answers.text: Use oxygen from a cutting torch tank
Use compressed shop air without a regulator
Use dry nitrogen with a regulator, test at the specified pressure, and use an electronic detector or bubbles to check joints
Pressurize with refrigerant alone to maximum pressure

questions.explanation: Regulated dry nitrogen is inert and standard for pressure testing, with joints checked by detector or bubble solution, so C is correct. Oxygen can cause explosive combustion with oil, unregulated shop air adds moisture and uncontrolled pressure, and refrigerant alone is not the proper test medium.

questions.question: When placing an outdoor condensing unit, which placement practice best supports reliable operation and service access?

answers.text: Set it level on a stable pad, keep the coil clear of obstructions and discharge-air recirculation, and leave the clearances the maker specifies for airflow and service
Tilt it toward the house so condensate and rain run toward the building
Push it tight against two walls to shield it from wind on all sides
Set it directly on bare soil so the pad cannot crack in freezing weather

questions.explanation: A level unit on a stable pad with specified clearances gets full airflow, avoids recirculating hot discharge air, and can be serviced safely. Option B risks water at the building and an unlevel compressor, option C starves the coil and blocks service, and option D allows settling and tilting as soil shifts.

questions.question: A single-phase compressor hums, draws high current, and trips its overload without starting, while a second identical unit on the same panel starts normally. The run capacitor tests well below its rated capacitance. What is the correct repair?

answers.text: Replace the run capacitor with one of the same capacitance and voltage rating and retest starting
Replace the compressor, because a humming compressor that trips overload has locked rotors in every such case
Install a larger breaker, because raising the trip point lets the compressor pull through its difficult starting period
Add refrigerant to lower the starting load, because low charge is the usual reason a compressor hums without starting

questions.explanation: A is correct: a run capacitor far below rating robs the start winding of phase shift and torque, producing the hum-and-trip pattern, so a same-rating replacement is the repair. B is wrong because a proven capacitor fault explains the symptom without condemning the compressor. C is wrong because enlarging protection masks the fault and endangers the wiring. D is wrong because charge level does not create this electrical starting failure.

iowa-hvac.quiz_title: Iowa HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A mountain-town home at 6,000 feet has high summer humidity during monsoon weeks and long mild shoulder seasons. Which equipment reasoning best fits all three conditions together?

answers.text: Pick the largest single-stage unit available so altitude losses are covered by raw tonnage, accepting short shoulder-season cycles as a minor comfort tradeoff overall
Size by nameplate sea-level capacity alone, because humidity control and part-load behavior matter far less at elevation than they do for lowland installations nearby
Use derated capacity, favor modulation for part load and humidity control
Choose equipment by its heating rating first and let cooling size fall where it may, since mountain homes are heating-dominated and summer loads rarely govern equipment selection

questions.explanation: The selection has to start from altitude-derated capacity, and a modulating system handles the long part-load shoulder seasons efficiently while sustaining the runtime humid monsoon weeks demand for moisture removal. Raw oversizing wrecks humidity control, nameplate sea-level sizing ignores the derate, and heating-first sizing abandons the stated summer design conditions.

questions.question: A belt-drive blower motor draws nameplate amps at its current sheave setting. A proposal would raise blower speed by 10 percent to gain airflow. What should the contractor verify before approving the change?

answers.text: Only that a longer belt is in stock, because a 10 percent speed change is small enough that motor loading can be assumed unchanged for planning purposes
That the motor has reserve capacity, since power rises about 33 percent
That the supply registers are adjustable, because register dampers alone can absorb any extra motor load created by the faster blower speed setting
That the thermostat has a fan switch, because continuous fan operation is the only approved way to keep a faster blower motor within its temperature rating

questions.explanation: Power rises with roughly the cube of speed, so 1.10 cubed is about 1.33, meaning roughly 33 percent more power for 10 percent more speed, and a motor already at nameplate amps has no reserve for that. Belt stock, register adjustment, and a fan switch do not address the motor loading the change creates.

questions.question: A furnace trips its rollout switch repeatedly. Flames are visibly rolling out of the burner compartment when the blower starts. Which cause should be investigated first?

answers.text: A thermostat with a short cycle timer that repeatedly stops and restarts the furnace during a single call for heat, long before any flame or venting problem could develop in the burner compartment
An oversized gas orifice in one burner
Low gas supply pressure at the inlet tap
A cracked or plugged heat exchanger, or blocked flue passage, that lets blower air or flue pressure push flames outward

questions.explanation: Rollout on blower start points to a breached or restricted heat exchanger or flue passage disturbing burner flames, a serious safety condition requiring shutdown and inspection. Option A affects cycling, not flame shape. Option B can distort one flame but does not explain rollout tied to blower operation. Option C causes weak flames and ignition problems, not rollout.

questions.question: When a heating or cooling cycle ends and no zone is calling, many panels drive all zone dampers to the open position. Why?

answers.text: To use the closed duct system as storage for conditioned air, holding the cooled or heated air in the branches until the next zone thermostat begins a call
To test each damper motor at full travel after every cycle, because a damper that is not exercised to both stops on every cycle loses its panel calibration
To raise static pressure in the idle system, which keeps dust from settling in the branches while the blower is off between equipment cycles
So the next call, fan-only operation, or purge starts with an unrestricted air path

questions.explanation: Parking dampers open at the end of a cycle leaves the duct system unrestricted for the next call, a fan-only request, or a post-purge, instead of starting against closed branches. Idle ducts do not store conditioned air usefully, the move is a system state rather than a motor exercise routine, and raising idle static pressure serves no purpose.

questions.question: A 24 V contactor coil measures 15 ohms. Using Ohm's law, about how much current does the coil draw when energized?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 24/15 = 1.6 A. Dividing resistance by voltage inverts the formula and gives 0.63. Adding or multiplying voltage and resistance produces values far beyond what a small control coil draws.

questions.question: A technician brazes a copper refrigerant joint and the filler metal balls up and refuses to flow into a properly cleaned joint. The flame was held mostly on the filler rod, heating the tubing unevenly. What technique correction is needed?

answers.text: Add large amounts of additional flux all around the joint and keep applying it until the filler finally melts and flows into place on its own without further heating
Quench the joint with water so the filler hardens faster
Use a smaller flame and keep heating only the rod
Heat the fitting and tubing evenly to proper brazing temperature and let the heated joint melt the filler, drawing it in by capillary action

questions.explanation: In brazing, the base metal - heated evenly to temperature - melts the filler and capillary action draws it through the joint, option D; heating mainly the rod leaves the joint too cold to flow. Excess flux (A) cannot substitute for joint temperature, quenching (B) ruins an incomplete joint, and a smaller flame on the rod alone (C) repeats the original error.

questions.question: A large commercial restroom with a row of water closets needs a makeup-air path for its exhaust fan. Which arrangement works?

answers.text: Seal the restroom completely — undercut, grille, and gaps all closed — so the exhaust fan can pull the room to its deepest possible vacuum, caulking every wall joint and fitting a sealed, gasketed door with a closer that pulls it fully shut against the frame
Vent the exhaust fan into the corridor ceiling so the corridor, rather than the restroom, receives the odors being removed
Provide transfer air — a door undercut, transfer grille, or ducted path sized so makeup air can enter as the fan exhausts, keeping the room slightly negative to contain odors
Supply the restroom with more air than the fan exhausts so odors are pushed out into the corridor whenever the door is opened

questions.explanation: Exhaust can only remove the air that can get in; a sized transfer path keeps flow moving and the room negative to its neighbors. Option A starves the fan so it moves little air, option B relocates the contaminant to another occupied space, and option D pressurizes the odorous room in exactly the wrong direction.

questions.question: In proportional balancing, a branch reads 60 percent of design flow while the main reads 90 percent of design. What does proportional method direct the balancer to do first?

answers.text: Close the main damper until the main also reads 60 percent so everything matches

Set the branch reading 60 percent to exactly 100 percent of its design flow by opening its damper fully and leaving it there, regardless of how short the total system flow is or what happens to every other branch
Work with the ratios: set the outlets in proportion to each other starting from the least-favored run, rather than forcing any single outlet to full design flow while the total is short
Abandon the job, because any branch below design means the fan must be replaced

questions.explanation: Proportional balancing equalizes percentages so that a final fan adjustment brings all outlets to design together. Throttling the main to the lowest ratio wastes capacity, forcing one branch to design while the total is low starves the rest, and a short branch is a distribution problem to correct, not automatic grounds for a new fan.

questions.question: A new 3-ton system is commissioned and total external static pressure measures well above the blower table limit at the selected tap, while delivered airflow is low. What is the correct commissioning response?

answers.text: Add refrigerant until the temperature split looks normal despite the low airflow, adding charge in repeated increments and rechecking the split after each addition until it appears acceptable at the registers
Raise the cooling charge target to compensate for the duct system
