Testing it with oxygen at high pressure

questions.explanation: Mainstream fuel-gas practice and CSST manufacturers require bonding of the piping system, in part to address lightning energy, option A. Painting for appearance (B) provides no safety function, unprotected burial through concrete (C) violates protection requirements, and oxygen testing (D) is prohibited because oxygen creates a severe fire and explosion hazard.

questions.question: Mold grows on an exterior wall behind a large bookcase, while the room's measured RH is a moderate 45% and nearby open wall areas are clean. What explains the localized growth?

answers.text: The bookcase is leaking stored moisture from its wood into the wall, so the mold is feeding on water released by the furniture rather than on humidity
Mold behind furniture indicates a plumbing leak inside that wall, because room humidity at 45% can never support mold growth under any surface condition
The wall behind the bookcase is warmer than the open wall because the bookcase insulates it, and mold prefers that warmth regardless of surface moisture
Cold wall surface raises local RH

questions.explanation: Blocked air circulation lets that wall section run colder, and air at the cold surface reaches a much higher local RH than the room average, supporting mold there alone. Furniture does not leak meaningful water into walls, moderate room RH absolutely can support mold on a cold enough surface, and the covered wall is colder, not warmer, than the open wall.

questions.question: Before raising an aerial lift to set a curb adapter, the operator walks around the machine and finds a hydraulic leak and a worn tire. What should the operator do?

answers.text: Operate the lift at reduced height all day, because hydraulic leaks and tire wear only become dangerous when the platform is near its maximum elevation
Tag the lift out of service and report the defects before use
Top off the hydraulic fluid and proceed, since a leak that can be refilled during the shift does not count as a defect requiring the lift to be removed
Swap the lift's parking spot with another crew's machine without mentioning the defects, letting the next operator discover the problems during their own work

questions.explanation: A pre-use inspection that finds defects like hydraulic leaks or damaged tires takes the lift out of service until repaired. Reduced height does not make a failing lift safe, refilling does not fix a leak, and silently passing a defective machine to another crew just moves the hazard.

questions.question: A system has always short-cycled and left the home humid, and the owner asks for 'the same size again.' What should the contractor do?

answers.text: Install the same size, because the equipment that was there longest defines the correct size for that house by precedent
Go one size larger so the system satisfies the thermostat faster, which is the usual cure for humidity complaints in summer
Run a load calculation and select from its results, because repeating the old size perpetuates the oversizing problem
Go two sizes smaller without a calculation, since humidity complaints always mean the system is exactly two sizes too big

questions.explanation: Documented short-cycling and poor dehumidification are classic oversizing symptoms that a calculation can quantify and correct. Long service does not validate a wrong size, larger equipment short-cycles worse, and arbitrary downsizing without numbers risks undercapacity on design days.

questions.question: How many examinations must a Division II contractor such as a Class A air-conditioning applicant pass to be licensed?

answers.text: A Division II applicant must pass one examination, the general trade knowledge examination for the category sought.
A Division II applicant must pass three examinations covering business, contract administration, and project management topics.
A Division II applicant must pass four examinations covering trade knowledge, business, safety, and building code topics.
A Division II applicant must pass two examinations, business and finance and general trade knowledge for the category.

questions.explanation: D is correct: Division II contractors must pass two examinations, Business and Finance and General Trade Knowledge. A is wrong because it omits the Business and Finance examination. B is wrong because three examinations (Business & Finance, Contract Administration, and Project Management) is the Division I pattern, not Division II. C is wrong because no four-examination pattern of that composition applies to Division II applicants.

questions.question: A concealed condensate line from a fuel-burning appliance terminates in a Miami mechanical closet, and the inspector cannot tell which drain it serves. Under the current Florida mechanical code, how must that termination be identified?

answers.text: It must be painted safety yellow for its entire concealed run through the closet and ceiling space above it
It must be marked to show whether the piping connects to the primary drain or to the secondary drain system
It must be tagged with the appliance serial number and the date the condensate piping was pressure tested
It must be wrapped in insulation that is printed with the name of the installing mechanical contractor

questions.explanation: The termination of concealed condensate piping must be marked to indicate whether it is connected to the primary or the secondary drain. A requires a paint scheme the code does not impose, C substitutes equipment data for the primary/secondary identification, and D addresses insulation and contractor naming rather than drain identification.

texas-hvac.quiz_title: Texas HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A gauge reads the suction pressure of a system where a liquid-vapor mixture exists in the evaporator. Using the pressure-temperature chart for that refrigerant, the technician can directly determine:

answers.text: The temperature of the air leaving the supply registers after it has passed through the duct system, plenums, and diffusers into the conditioned space
The exact charge weight in the system
The saturation temperature at which refrigerant is boiling in the evaporator
The temperature of the compressor discharge gas

questions.explanation: For a given refrigerant, pressure and saturation temperature correspond one-to-one wherever liquid and vapor coexist, so suction pressure gives evaporator saturation temperature. Option A is an air measurement, option B cannot be read from a pressure-temperature chart, and option D is superheated vapor well above saturation and must be measured directly.

questions.question: A homeowner asks why the new R-454B air handler runs its blower for a while after a leak sensor trips, even though cooling has stopped. What is the correct explanation?

answers.text: The blower is removing residual heat from the electric heat strips, a normal cool-down sequence that happens to coincide with the sensor alarm event
The blower pressurizes the duct system so refrigerant vapor is forced back through the leak point into the coil, resealing the system temporarily
The blower dilutes and disperses leaked refrigerant through the duct system so room concentration stays low
The blower run is a fault in itself, because mitigation design requires the air handler to shut down every moving part the instant a sensor trips

questions.explanation: Leak mitigation uses indoor airflow to dilute and disperse refrigerant so concentration in the occupied space stays low. The run is not a heat-strip cool-down, airflow cannot push vapor back into a leaking coil or reseal it, and the blower operation is an intended mitigation response rather than a second fault.

questions.question: On a millivolt wall furnace, the pilot stays lit but the main burner will not open. Open-circuit voltage at the generator reads near its rated value, yet voltage collapses under load. What does that pattern indicate?

answers.text: The thermostat is calling correctly and the only fault is a dirty main burner that needs brushing before any electrical checks are worth completing on the unit
The pilot flame is too large and is overheating the generator, so reducing pilot gas alone will restore full load voltage to the gas valve operator circuit
The gas supply pressure is excessive at the inlet tap, which forces the valve regulator to lock out the main burner while leaving the pilot burning normally
A weak generator or a high-resistance connection in the circuit

questions.explanation: A generator that shows rated open-circuit voltage but collapses under load cannot deliver the current the valve operator needs, and corroded or loose connections produce the same collapse. Burner cleanliness, pilot size, and inlet pressure do not explain a load-dependent voltage drop in the millivolt loop.

questions.question: A technician ohm-tests a cad cell in a brightly burning oil flame and reads a very high resistance, nearly the same as in darkness. The burner locks out on safety shortly after light-off. The correct conclusion is:

answers.text: The cad cell or its sighting/wiring is faulty, so the control cannot see a flame that is actually present
The nozzle is oversized for the firing rate, delivering more oil than the chamber was designed for and producing an oversized flame that overheats the cad cell
The stack draft is excessively high
The oil supply contains too much air

questions.explanation: A good cad cell in flame should read low resistance, typically a few hundred to about 1,500 ohms; a dark-level reading in flame means the cell is dirty, misaimed, failed, or its leads are open. Option B changes firing rate but would not keep cell resistance high. Option C affects combustion efficiency, not light sensing. Option D causes flame sputter, not a stable flame the cell cannot see.

questions.question: A system moves 1,200 CFM. To keep filter face velocity near 300 feet per minute, about how much filter area is needed, and what does that imply for the rack?

answers.text: About 0.4 square feet, so a very small rack is best because higher velocity forces dust deeper into media for better capture
About 40 square feet, so the return must be built as a filter wall covering most of one side of the mechanical room itself
About 12 square feet, calculated by dividing velocity by airflow rather than airflow by the target face velocity value given
About 4 square feet of filter area

questions.explanation: Area equals airflow divided by velocity: 1,200 divided by 300 is 4 square feet, roughly a 20-by-30-inch filter, so the rack must be generously sized. Option A is off by a factor of ten and raises pressure drop, option B is off by a factor of ten the other way, and option C reverses the division.

questions.question: A flex duct run is supported with thin wire pulled tight at wide intervals, and the duct sags deeply between supports with the core choked where the wire bites in. Name the correct support practice and its purpose.

answers.text: Support it only at the two ends, since flex duct is self-supporting over any span

Use the tight wire, but add more of them, since choking the core is how flex is secured, with each additional tight wire pinching the duct further into place so the run cannot shift, sag, or pull loose between supports over time in service
Hang flex duct from its outer jacket only, letting the inner core hang free inside

Support flex duct at close intervals with wide straps that cradle the duct without cutting into it, keeping sag minimal, because sag and choked spots add friction and can collect condensate in low points

questions.explanation: Flex duct is not self-supporting: broad, closely spaced supports preserve its round shape and smooth bore, while wire bite and deep sag both raise pressure drop. Option A is wrong because long unsupported spans sag severely and are outside every manufacturer's installation instructions; option B is wrong because adding more choking points multiplies the restrictions instead of fixing them; option C is wrong because the support must carry the whole duct assembly; hanging by the jacket alone lets the core slip and bunch.

questions.question: An ECM blower does not run. Line power is present at the motor, but no control signal arrives at the motor connector. The correct conclusion is:

answers.text: Replace the motor and module as a set, because an ECM motor that has power but does not run is always internally failed regardless of its input signal
Do not condemn the motor; find why the control signal is missing
Replace the module only, because the module generates its own control signal internally and does not depend on a signal from the furnace control board
Install a PSC motor in its place without changing the controls, because an ECM motor and a PSC motor respond to the same inputs at the motor leads

questions.explanation: Do not condemn the motor; find why the control signal is missing. Power alone does not prove a motor failed, the module depends on the board signal, and a PSC motor is not a drop-in substitute for ECM control inputs.

questions.question: In January a house shows heavy window condensation and RH of 55% indoors at 70°F, with no plumbing or roof leaks found. What is the most likely explanation?

answers.text: Outdoor winter air leaking in is humidifying the house, because cold outdoor air holds more moisture than warm indoor air and releases it at the windows
The windows are defective and are generating moisture at the glass, which is why condensation appears there first instead of anywhere else in the rooms
The furnace humidifier has failed empty and is somehow adding moisture, since window condensation in winter is a standard symptom of too little indoor humidity
Indoor vapor condensing on cold glass

questions.explanation: At 55% RH the indoor dew point is high enough that cold window glass falls below it, so indoor-generated vapor condenses on the coldest surface. Winter outdoor air is dry and dilutes indoor moisture when it leaks in, glass does not generate moisture, and a failed-empty humidifier would lower rather than raise indoor humidity.

questions.question: A crew is about to work from a scaffold erected beside an air handler. Which condition must be met before the scaffold is used each shift?

answers.text: The scaffold only needs a fresh inspection when it is first erected, after which daily conditions such as weather and impacts cannot affect its safety
Workers may use the scaffold while it is still being moved into position, provided they hold the frame and keep their weight near the casters
Guardrails can be left off the top level whenever ductwork is being passed up, because material handling temporarily overrides fall protection needs
A competent person inspects it and footing and planking are sound

questions.explanation: Scaffolds are inspected by a competent person before each shift and after events that could affect them, with firm footing and proper planking and guardrails. One-time inspection misses later damage, riding a moving scaffold is prohibited practice, and material handling never suspends fall protection.

questions.question: A new three-phase scroll compressor starts but is unusually loud, draws low amperage, and produces almost no pressure difference between suction and discharge. What is the most likely cause and correction?

answers.text: The compressor is running in reverse because two power leads are swapped; correct the phase order and recheck operation
The system is overcharged; recover half the charge and restart it
The metering device is stuck closed; replace it before running the compressor again
The condenser fan is cycling; replace the fan control and leave the compressor wiring alone, then run the system again to see whether the pressure difference returns once fan operation is corrected

questions.explanation: A scroll running backwards cannot build pressure, sounds harsh, and draws low amps, and swapping any two line leads restores the correct rotation. Option B would create an undercharge without changing rotation, option C would still leave a reversed compressor unable to pump, and option D addresses the fan while the symptoms point to compressor rotation.

questions.question: Marcus holds a Class B contractor license and is asked to replace a single 30-ton rooftop cooling unit. What should he do?

answers.text: Accept the job because the building's total combined load is what matters for licensing, not the size of any single unit being replaced
Decline that unit because a Class B licensee is limited to cooling systems of 25 tons and under per unit
Accept the job if he also holds general liability insurance at Class A limits
Decline only if the heating side exceeds 2 million BTU per hour on that same job

questions.explanation: Key B is correct: Class B cooling is limited to 25 tons and under. A is wrong because the limit is per complete individual unit, not building total. C is wrong because insurance limits do not expand license class. D is wrong because the heating limit is 1.5 million BTU/hour and the cooling limit alone already bars this unit.

questions.question: A gas piping system is being sized with a sizing table using the longest length method. The outlets are at different distances from the meter. On what length must every section of this system be sized?

answers.text: On the length from the point of delivery to the most remote outlet in the system, applied to each section being sized
On the length of each individual section only, measured fitting to fitting, with no allowance for the rest of the piping system
On the length from the point of delivery to the nearest outlet, because that outlet controls the pressure available to all the others
On the average of the lengths to all outlets, calculated by adding the outlet distances together and dividing by the number of outlets

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: under the longest length method, all sections are sized using the total developed length from the point of delivery to the most remote outlet, which guarantees adequate pressure at the farthest appliance. Option B sizes sections in isolation and can starve remote outlets, option C uses the shortest run and undersizes the system, and option D uses an averaging method that appears in no sizing table procedure.

alabama-hvac.quiz_title: Alabama HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A standard cooling rating point uses hot outdoor conditions. As outdoor temperature climbs well above that point on an extreme afternoon, what happens to a fixed-speed system's capacity and power draw?

answers.text: Capacity climbs steadily with outdoor temperature because the compressor pumps refrigerant faster as discharge pressure rises against the hotter condenser airstream
Power draw falls to its seasonal minimum at extreme temperatures, which is exactly why utilities schedule demand charges around mild-weather operating hours instead
Capacity falls while power draw generally rises
Both capacity and power stay locked at their rating-point values, because nameplate ratings are guaranteed performance figures at every outdoor temperature a system may face

questions.explanation: Hotter condensing conditions raise the pressure lift the compressor works against, so it moves less refrigerant, delivers less capacity, and draws more power doing it. Capacity does not climb with head pressure, extreme heat is the high-draw condition rather than the minimum, and ratings describe one test point rather than a guarantee at all temperatures.

questions.question: No-heat call on a 90 percent condensing furnace. The inducer starts, the furnace fires and heats for about eight minutes, then shuts down on a pressure-switch fault and retries. When the condensate trap is removed, roughly a pint of backed-up water drains out, and gurgling is heard in the drain during operation. Vent piping is clear and correctly pitched. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A cracked heat exchanger tripping the pressure switch, which would present with rollout or flame disturbance and would not release a pint of backed-up water when the trap is pulled
A partially clogged condensate trap
A weak inducer motor that cannot develop vacuum, which would fail the pressure switch at the start of the call before ignition rather than after eight minutes of firing as water accumulates
A gas valve that closes early in the cycle, which would stop the burners without opening the pressure switch and without any water backing up in the drain system

questions.explanation: The furnace runs until condensate production fills the drain path; a partially clogged trap backs water up toward the inducer and pressure port until the switch opens, and pulling the trap releases the stored pint. A cracked exchanger does not store condensate, a weak inducer fails the switch before ignition rather than minutes into a firing cycle, and a closing gas valve would not produce a pressure-switch fault or drain backup.

questions.question: A corridor ceiling assembly requires smoke control, and the designer specifies a damper that stays open during normal operation but closes on a signal from the building smoke detection system, with a rated limit on air passing the closed blade. Which device and reasoning fit?

answers.text: A smoke damper: it is actuated by a detection signal rather than by heat alone, and its leakage rating describes how much air passes when it is closed
A standard fire damper, because its fusible link responds faster than any detector
A backdraft damper, because its gravity blades stop smoke whenever the fan stops

A balancing damper wired to the alarm panel, since any damper in the duct can serve as the smoke damper once its handle is connected to the alarm relay and the panel can signal it to close during an event anywhere in the building

questions.explanation: Smoke dampers are listed for detector or system actuation and carry a leakage class for the closed position, which is what a smoke-control design is specifying. Option B is wrong because a fusible link only responds after hot gases reach it and gives no detector-controlled closure or leakage class; option C is wrong because a backdraft damper is an unlisted gravity device with no rated leakage performance or alarm actuation; option D is wrong because a balancing damper is a manual volume device with no listing, actuator rating, or leakage class for smoke duty.

questions.question: After replacing one component of a communicating system with a non-matching generic part, the system runs but loses staging and diagnostic features. What principle does this illustrate?

answers.text: Any ordinary 24-volt replacement part performs identically in a communicating system once power is applied, including full staging control and complete fault reporting
Diagnostics are stored in the thermostat only and never involve the other components
Losing features proves the replacement part has higher capacity than the system needs
Communicating components exchange model and operating data, so matched components are needed for full features and correct configuration

questions.explanation: Model-specific data sharing is what enables staging, configuration, and shared faults, and a generic substitute cannot participate fully. Basic power alone does not restore data exchange, diagnostics involve the outdoor and indoor units as well as the control, and feature loss reflects incompatibility, not excess capacity.

questions.question: A furnace clocks at an input 20% above its rating plate after a gas-valve replacement. The most likely setup causes are:

answers.text: Manifold pressure set too high or wrong-size orifices installed
A vent connector one size larger than the minimum, because a larger vent increases draft and pulls extra gas through the burner orifices
A sediment trap with a long capped leg, because the trap volume adds a reserve of gas that the meter counts as additional furnace input
A thermostat set several degrees above room temperature, because a larger temperature difference makes the gas valve deliver more fuel per hour

questions.explanation: Manifold pressure set too high or wrong-size orifices installed. Vent size, trap volume, and thermostat setting do not change firing rate; excessive manifold pressure or oversized orifices do.

questions.question: An enclosed parking garage is ventilated on demand instead of running fans continuously. Which control strategy is sound?

answers.text: Run the fans only when the garage lighting is on, because vehicle activity and light switch operation always coincide exactly, with the time clock overridden only during the annual fire-department inspection walk-through of the garage
Shut the fans off whenever the outdoor temperature is mild, because vehicle exhaust gases are harmless in cool weather
Sense carbon monoxide (and nitrogen dioxide where diesel vehicles operate) and stage or modulate the fans to hold concentrations at safe levels
Sense carbon dioxide at the ceiling and use it as the direct measure of vehicle exhaust concentration at bumper height

questions.explanation: CO (with NO2 for diesel) is the contaminant vehicle exhaust produces, so sensing it lets fans track actual need. Option A ties safety ventilation to an unrelated lighting schedule, option B suspends protection based on weather rather than gas levels, and option D picks the wrong gas and the wrong sensing location for vehicle exhaust.

questions.question: A critical duct path measures 70 feet of straight duct. On that path are three elbows rated at 20 feet of equivalent length each and one branch takeoff rated at 15 feet. What is the total effective length of this path?

answers.text: 105 feet, counting only one elbow because identical fittings share one equivalent length
90 feet, because takeoffs are not counted in effective length
70 feet, because equivalent length applies only to flex duct

questions.explanation: TEL adds every fitting on the critical path at its equivalent length: 70 + 60 + 15 = 145 feet. Option A is wrong because each fitting the air actually passes through adds its own loss, so all three elbows count; option B is wrong because a takeoff on the critical path is a fitting with a real equivalent length and must be included; option D is wrong because equivalent length is a general duct-design concept for metal duct as well as flex.

questions.question: In proportional balancing, a branch reads 60 percent of design flow while the main reads 90 percent of design. What does proportional method direct the balancer to do first?

answers.text: Close the main damper until the main also reads 60 percent so everything matches

Set the branch reading 60 percent to exactly 100 percent of its design flow by opening its damper fully and leaving it there, regardless of how short the total system flow is or what happens to every other branch
Work with the ratios: set the outlets in proportion to each other starting from the least-favored run, rather than forcing any single outlet to full design flow while the total is short
Abandon the job, because any branch below design means the fan must be replaced

questions.explanation: Proportional balancing equalizes percentages so that a final fan adjustment brings all outlets to design together. Throttling the main to the lowest ratio wastes capacity, forcing one branch to design while the total is low starves the rest, and a short branch is a distribution problem to correct, not automatic grounds for a new fan.

questions.question: A changeout installs a two-stage outdoor unit, but the retained indoor coil has a fixed-orifice meter. What performance problem should the contractor anticipate?

answers.text: No problem at all, because staging is controlled entirely by the thermostat and the metering device plays no part in it
The system will gain efficiency on low stage because a fixed orifice always overfeeds at reduced compressor capacity
The fixed orifice cannot adjust feed between stages, so capacity control and efficiency will suffer versus the rated TXV pairing
The coil will freeze solid on high stage within minutes regardless of airflow, charge, or outdoor conditions on every call

questions.explanation: A fixed orifice sized for one condition cannot track the very different mass flow of low stage, unlike a TXV. The thermostat does not meter refrigerant, overfeeding degrades rather than improves low-stage performance, and instant freezing is an overstatement rather than the predictable effect.

questions.question: A contractor bills monthly based on the percentage of work completed and approved. What is this billing approach called?

answers.text: Allowance billing, where each month's invoice is limited to the placeholder amounts listed for undecided selections
Unit billing, where each invoice must restate the original per-foot rate regardless of the amount actually installed
Progress payments
Retainage billing, where the withheld percentage is invoiced first and the earned amount is billed only at closeout

questions.explanation: C is correct because progress payments bill periodically for work completed and approved during that period. A is incorrect because allowances are placeholders for selections, not the basis of monthly earned-value billing. B is incorrect because unit billing measures installed quantities, not overall percentage complete. D is incorrect because retainage is withheld from progress payments, not billed ahead of earned amounts.

questions.question: A person in Alabama spends most working days, for hire, installing new residential split systems and servicing and repairing systems installed earlier. Which description fits the credential this person must hold?

answers.text: A refrigeration contractor certification, because any equipment that contains refrigerant falls under refrigeration contracting rather than heating and air conditioning contracting, whatever the customers use the equipment for in their buildings.
A certified heating and air conditioning contractor certification, because the person is engaged in the business of heating and air conditioning contracting, installation, and service and repair.

No state certification at all, because residential heating and cooling work performed for homeowners in their own houses is treated as private household work lying outside the state's contractor certification system for this trade.

Either state certification the person prefers, because the heating and air conditioning and refrigeration credentials are interchangeable for any mechanical work a person chooses to offer to the public in Alabama.

questions.explanation: B is correct: Alabama defines a certified heating and air conditioning contractor as a person engaged in the business of heating and air conditioning contracting and installation or service and repair, which describes this install-and-service work exactly. A is wrong because refrigeration contracting is a separate business of refrigeration contracting, servicing, installation, and repair, not a catch-all for equipment that contains refrigerant. C is wrong because performing this work for hire is the regulated activity; it is not exempt merely because customers are homeowners. D is wrong because the two certifications are distinct credentials for distinct lines of contracting, not interchangeable options.

questions.question: After completing a system replacement, a certified contractor receives a Board request for the paperwork behind the design. Which records must the contractor be able to provide on request?

answers.text: Only the customer's signed contract and the final invoice, because the Board's interest in a completed job is limited to the commercial terms agreed between the contractor and the customer, and design documents are the contractor's private property.

No design records at all, because load calculations, duct designs, and gas piping plans are the contractor's trade secrets, and the rules expressly shield such material from Board inspection requests however the request is framed.

Copies of all heat gain and heat loss calculations, duct design plans, gas piping plans, other load calculations, drawings, and any information used pertaining to the installation, service, or repair performed.

Records only for jobs that generated a customer complaint, because the Board's authority to demand design and load records is triggered solely by a formal complaint filed against the contractor by a dissatisfied customer.

questions.explanation: C is correct: every certified heating and air conditioning and refrigeration contractor must provide the Board, on request, copies of all heat gain, heat loss, and duct design plans, gas piping plans, other load calculations, drawings, and any information used pertaining to the installation, service, and/or repair performed. A is wrong because the duty reaches the design records, not just contract and invoice. B is wrong because no trade-secret shield overrides the Board's request authority. D is wrong because the duty applies on Board request generally, not only after a complaint.

pmp.quiz_title: PMP Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Two regional depots in a hybrid equipment-maintenance program each expect the program's single new specialist crew to be based at their depot, and both have planned work around that assumption. Which actions facilitate alignment of these expectations? (Select TWO.)

answers.text: Bring both depot managers together with the demand data for each region and facilitate agreement on a basing and scheduling arrangement both can plan around
Base the crew at the depot whose manager raised the matter first
Split the crew permanently into two half-crews, one at each depot
Let the sponsor decide without a joint discussion, and notify both depots of the outcome
Agree a shared scheduling protocol with both depots, including how peak clashes are prioritised, and record the agreed arrangement

questions.explanation: Alignment comes from a joint, evidence-based conversation and a recorded working arrangement: reviewing regional demand together lets both managers see the same picture, and an agreed scheduling protocol with clash priorities turns the settlement into something both can plan around. Basing by who complained first rewards escalation rather than need. Splitting the crew permanently halves its capability to satisfy an assumption neither depot has yet examined. A sponsor decision handed down without discussion settles the location while leaving both depots' underlying expectations, and their resentment, untouched.

questions.question: A nonprofit's board envisions a service program measured by how many communities it reaches, while field staff envision depth of support in a few communities, and local plans are diverging. What should the project manager do?

answers.text: Split the work into two independent programs, one for each interpretation
Direct field staff to follow the board's reach definition because the board funds the program
Survey donors and let donor preference settle the vision
Facilitate a joint session to agree a shared vision that states the intended balance between reach and depth explicitly

questions.explanation: The keyed session produces one shared vision with the reach-versus-depth trade-off made explicit, which is what diverging local plans need. Imposing the board's definition ignores the field knowledge that depth may be what makes reach valuable. Splitting the program institutionalizes the disagreement instead of resolving it. Donor preference is an input, not a substitute for alignment among those who govern and deliver the work.

questions.question: A product team has just had a release fail in production. Morale is low, priorities for the recovery are disputed, and the team is looking for clear direction for the next two weeks. Which leadership approach fits best?

answers.text: Remain fully hands-off so the team can demonstrate resilience
Facilitate open-ended exploration of long-term product strategy during the recovery
Provide clear short-term direction on recovery priorities and daily coordination, while involving the team in diagnosing the failure, then ease back as stability returns
Announce that the failed release will be investigated to identify who is responsible

questions.explanation: A temporarily more directive style — clear recovery priorities and tight coordination, with the team involved in diagnosis — matches a team that is asking for direction in a crisis, and it eases as stability returns. Hands-off leadership abandons a team explicitly seeking direction. Long-term strategy exploration diverts the recovery window. A blame investigation destroys the morale and candor the diagnosis needs.

questions.question: Stakeholders on a mobile app project say status emails are technically accurate but useless because they cannot tell what changed or what is needed from them. What should change?

answers.text: Increase email frequency so changes are smaller in each message
Reshape reports around changes since last time, impact, and explicit requests or decisions needed from each audience
Attach the full project plan to every status email for completeness
Copy more senior managers into the emails to raise their importance

questions.explanation: Reports organized around change, impact, and needed actions match what stakeholders said they expect. More frequent unhelpful emails multiply the problem. Attaching the full plan adds volume, not clarity. Wider copying raises pressure, not usefulness.

questions.question: A buyer enters a three-round negotiation for laboratory equipment. In round one the seller offers a small discount and asks what else the buyer needs. The buyer's negotiator is inclined to list every concession she wants at once, to appear transparent. What does sound negotiation strategy say instead?

answers.text: List all desired concessions at once, since transparency obliges the seller to grant them
Refuse to concede anything across all three rounds to project strength
Concede the buyer's largest item first to build momentum and goodwill
Plan concessions in advance, trade them one at a time in exchange for movement from the seller, and keep a record of what has been traded so nothing is conceded twice or for free

questions.explanation: Planned, traded concessions preserve negotiating value across rounds: each concession buys movement and the record prevents double-counting. Listing everything at once gives the seller the full map while committing it to nothing. Refusing all concessions makes agreement unlikely and signals inflexibility rather than strength. Giving away the largest item first spends the strongest currency before the hard issues are reached.

questions.question: A hospital group's project to cut patient discharge delays defines its benefit clearly, but reviews of actual discharge performance happen only when someone complains. The sponsor asks how she can be confident the benefit is sustained. What should the project manager put in place?

answers.text: A scheduled benefits review rhythm with the measure, data source, and owner agreed, and a route to act when performance drifts
A one-time benefits report at project closure confirming the target was met on that day
A larger initial improvement target so later drift still leaves the project ahead
An instruction to ward staff to work harder whenever discharge delays are mentioned

questions.explanation: A measurement system that verifies sustained benefit needs a recurring review: an agreed measure, source, owner, and a way to respond to drift. A single closure-day report proves a moment, not sustainment. Inflating the target games the measure instead of tracking performance. Exhorting staff is not measurement and gives governance nothing to act on.

questions.question: A haulage firm must choose between building its own fleet-tracking platform over nine months and configuring a commercial product that could be live at one depot in six weeks with most needed functions, though dispatchers dislike its interface. Leadership needs evidence of fuel and idle-time benefit within this budget year. What should the project manager recommend evaluating first?

answers.text: Pilot the configurable product at one depot and measure fuel and idle-time results before deciding on wider adoption or a custom build
Commission the custom build, because a perfect functional fit is always worth the wait
Buy the commercial product for every depot immediately to capture the earliest possible date
Postpone the decision until a complete requirements document for the custom build is finished

questions.explanation: Piloting the configurable product at one depot produces measured benefit evidence inside the budget year while keeping both wider adoption and a custom build open as informed choices. Committing to the custom build spends the year with no evidence. Buying for every depot immediately converts an untested option into a full commitment. Finishing a requirements document first delays the evidence leadership needs without testing either option.

questions.question: A buyer is contracting for an equipment-testing program whose scope is well defined and stable. The buyer wants the seller to share in cost control: if testing comes in under the target cost, both gain; if it overruns, the seller absorbs part of the excess, and the fee adjusts by a formula agreed in advance. Which contract type fits?

answers.text: Firm fixed price, because any incentive formula complicates administration
Cost plus fixed fee, because the fee stays constant whatever the cost outcome
Cost plus incentive fee, because the fee is tied by formula to actual cost against the target
Time and materials, because labor rates are easy to compare between bidders

questions.explanation: A cost plus incentive fee arrangement is designed exactly for this: a target cost with a formula that shares savings and overruns, motivating the seller to control cost. Firm fixed price gives cost certainty but no shared-savings formula of the kind described, and fits where the buyer wants no cost visibility at all. A fixed fee does not vary with cost performance, removing the incentive. Time and materials pays for effort, not outcomes, and weakly disciplines cost.

questions.question: An agile release plan, sprint goals, and a stakeholder roadmap for a membership system have drifted apart over three releases: the roadmap promises a renewals feature the release plan dropped two releases ago, and stakeholders keep asking for it. What should the project manager do?

answers.text: Remove the roadmap so stakeholders stop referring to it
Reconcile the roadmap, release plan, and sprint goals into one maintained position and communicate the corrected renewals expectation to stakeholders
Promise the renewals feature in the next sprint to close the gap
Let each document be corrected by its owner at its next natural update

questions.explanation: Reconciling all three artefacts and correcting the stakeholder expectation restores one maintained plan instead of three divergent ones. Removing the roadmap destroys a communication tool rather than fixing its content. Promising the feature next sprint commits delivery to repair a documentation failure. Unsynchronized natural updates guarantee the documents continue drifting apart.

questions.question: A mining company with a strong site-autonomy culture is introducing centralized maintenance planning that site managers may see as head-office control. Before rollout, what should the project manager assess?

answers.text: Only the technical readiness of the new planning software
Whether head office can mandate the change without consultation
The maintenance backlog figures for the last financial year
How site managers currently make and defend decisions, where autonomy is valued, and which parts of the change will be read as loss of control

questions.explanation: Assessing how site managers currently make and defend decisions, where autonomy is valued, and which parts of the change will be read as loss of control examines the culture the change must land in. Software readiness says nothing about whether people will use the system as intended. Mandating power answers a legal question, not the adoption question. Backlog figures describe workload, not the values that will shape the response to centralization.

questions.question: A project manager cleared a customs-documentation impediment in March by adding a broker review step. In June, shipments are again being held, and the log shows the impediment as closed. What does this reveal and require?

answers.text: The June holds must be a different impediment because the March one is closed
The log is correct and the June holds are an operational matter outside the project
The broker should be replaced without further analysis
The fix addressed the immediate instance but not its cause, so the impediment should be reopened and the broker step itself examined

questions.explanation: Reopening the impediment and examining the broker step itself is required because recurrence after a fix indicates the cause survived; continual reassessment treats recurrence as evidence, not coincidence. Declaring it a different impediment by definition destroys the history that reveals the pattern. Dismissing shipping holds as operational removes a project-blocking problem from project view. Replacing the broker without analysis may change the actor while keeping the defective process.

questions.question: A shared-services migration's steering group receives risk reports as a single green-or-red traffic light per project. The migration lead believes the board is missing slow deterioration: one project's top risk has worsened slightly at each of the last four reviews while staying amber throughout. What should the lead change about the communication?

answers.text: Change the project's light to red immediately, to make the board pay attention
Keep the traffic light but present it in a larger font at steering meetings
Stop reporting the project until its rating actually changes colour

Report the trend and its drivers alongside the current rating: four reviews of worsening, what is driving it, the point at which the risk becomes critical, and the decision the board may face if the trend continues

questions.explanation: A static rating hides trajectory, and trajectory is what lets a board act before a risk becomes critical; communicating the trend, its drivers, the critical point, and the coming decision gives the board the real picture. Forcing the light red misstates the current rating to buy attention. Presentation size changes nothing about content. Silence until the colour changes guarantees the board learns of the deterioration at the worst moment.

ccrn.quiz_title: CCRN Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An Impella device's placement signal changes from a ventricular waveform to a flat aortic-type waveform, motor current rises, and flows fall. Echocardiography is being arranged. What does this pattern most likely indicate and require?

answers.text: Normal weaning physiology, so the device can be removed at the bedside without imaging
A purge-system problem only, so changing the purge fluid will restore flows
Suction from hypovolemia, so a large fluid bolus alone will correct the signal
Device migration/malposition — the inlet is no longer correctly placed in the left ventricle — requiring prompt imaging-guided repositioning

questions.explanation: Loss of the ventricular placement signal with an aortic waveform, rising motor current, and falling flows indicates the catheter has migrated (for example into the aorta or against a structure) and needs echocardiography/fluoroscopy-guided repositioning. It is not normal weaning (A). The purge system (B) affects purge pressures, not the placement signal morphology. Suction (C) typically shows flow fluctuation with a still-ventricular signal and low filling, not conversion to an aortic waveform.

questions.question: A 68-year-old man with chronic heart failure who takes carvedilol daily is admitted with acute decompensated heart failure and cardiogenic shock. His blood pressure is 84/56 mmHg, heart rate is 108/min, extremities are cool and mottled, and urine output is 15 mL/hr. Cardiac index is 1.6 L/min/m2, pulmonary artery wedge pressure is 26 mmHg, and central venous oxygen saturation is 48%. Despite escalating dobutamine, his cardiac index and perfusion have not improved. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.text: Switch to milrinone, which increases contractility without beta-receptor stimulation
Continue escalating dobutamine indefinitely until cardiac index normalizes fully
Start phenylephrine as a primary inotrope to increase cardiac contractility directly
Stop all inotropic therapy because beta blockade makes inotropy completely ineffective

questions.explanation: Option A is correct: milrinone is a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor that raises intracellular cyclic AMP downstream of the beta receptor, so it increases contractility and promotes vasodilation even when chronic carvedilol blunts beta-receptor responsiveness, making it useful when dobutamine response is poor in cardiogenic shock with low cardiac index and high filling pressures. Option B is wrong because dobutamine acts mainly through beta-1 stimulation, so continued escalation in a chronically beta-blocked patient yields diminishing inotropy while increasing tachycardia, myocardial oxygen demand, and arrhythmia risk without correcting the receptor-level problem. Option C is wrong because phenylephrine is a pure alpha-1 vasoconstrictor with no direct inotropic effect; raising afterload alone can further reduce stroke volume in a failing ventricle. Option D is wrong because beta blockade does not make all inotropy ineffective; agents that bypass the beta receptor can still improve contractility, and withdrawing inotropic support in persistent cardiogenic shock allows hypoperfusion to progress.

questions.question: A patient with severe COPD on volume-control ventilation has measured intrinsic PEEP of 9 cm H2O. Over 20 minutes his blood pressure falls from 118/72 to 88/54 mmHg, his heart rate rises, and his plateau pressures climb, with no pneumothorax on examination and no new bleeding or sepsis source. What mechanism best explains the hypotension?

answers.text: Progressive air trapping has raised intrathoracic pressure, reducing venous return and cardiac output
The set PEEP of 5 cm H2O is directly compressing the heart in the same way as pericardial tamponade fluid
COPD has caused acute pulmonary vasodilation, dropping systemic vascular resistance throughout the body
The hypotension is unrelated to ventilation because intrinsic PEEP affects only the airways, never circulation

questions.explanation: Key (A): Dynamic hyperinflation from auto-PEEP raises intrathoracic and alveolar pressure throughout the cycle. That pressure is transmitted to the great veins and heart, venous return falls, and cardiac output and blood pressure drop - a recognized cause of hypotension in ventilated obstructive disease that the team must recognize and report urgently. B misattributes the effect to the small set PEEP rather than the trapped volume. C reverses the physiology. D is false: severe auto-PEEP has major hemodynamic effects.

questions.question: On admission, a 74-year-old immobile woman has an intact sacral area of deep purple-maroon discoloration with a blood-filled blister. The skin is intact, the area is painful, and it feels boggy compared with surrounding tissue. How should the nurse classify this finding?

answers.text: Stage 1 pressure injury, because the skin surface is still intact
Stage 2 pressure injury, because a blister is present over the sacrum
Deep tissue pressure injury from damage to underlying soft tissue
Unstageable pressure injury, because the wound bed cannot be seen

questions.explanation: C is correct: intact skin with persistent deep red, maroon, or purple discoloration, a blood-filled blister, pain, and a boggy texture indicate deep tissue pressure injury — damage to muscle and deeper tissue from intense or prolonged pressure/shear that declares itself at the surface and often evolves rapidly into full-thickness loss. A is wrong: stage 1 injury is intact skin with nonblanchable erythema in a lighter red/pink tone, without purple discoloration or a blood blister. B is wrong: stage 2 is partial-thickness loss with a pink wound bed or a serum-filled blister; a blood-filled blister signals deep tissue damage instead. D is wrong: 'unstageable' applies when slough or eschar obscures an open wound bed; here the skin is intact and the presentation itself defines the category.

questions.question: A 44-year-old man has 2 weeks of worsening dyspnea and fatigue. He now coughs up blood, his urine is tea-colored with dysmorphic red cells and red-cell casts on microscopy, oxygen saturation is 89% on room air, and creatinine has risen from 0.9 to 3.1 mg/dL in 4 days. Chest imaging shows diffuse bilateral infiltrates. How should the nurse frame this, and what should be anticipated?

answers.text: Pulmonary-renal syndrome with rapidly progressive glomerular injury: urgent nephrology involvement, serologic workup, and biopsy evaluation
Ordinary community-acquired pneumonia with dehydration: antibiotics alone, with kidney recheck as an outpatient in 2 weeks and no imaging ordered
Acute heart failure with cardiorenal syndrome: aggressive diuresis first, and kidney consultation only if diuresis fails after a full week
A simple urinary infection with hematuria: oral antibiotics and fluids, because casts in the urine are usually contamination

questions.explanation: A is correct: hemoptysis with diffuse infiltrates plus an active glomerular urine sediment (dysmorphic red cells and red-cell casts) and a creatinine that has tripled in days define a pulmonary-renal presentation - alveolar hemorrhage with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, framed here within the AKI head categories; it is a same-day emergency requiring urgent nephrology and pulmonary involvement, serologic testing, and rapid movement toward biopsy and immunosuppressive therapy, sometimes with plasma exchange, because glomeruli are lost permanently while treatment waits. B is wrong: pneumonia does not explain red-cell casts or this creatinine trajectory, and a 2-week delay forfeits kidney recovery. C is wrong: the sediment is glomerular, not congestive, and diuresis does not treat alveolar hemorrhage or glomerular inflammation. D is wrong: red-cell casts form inside kidney tubules and are never contamination; they localize bleeding to the glomerulus.

questions.question: A severely malnourished 45-year-old starts parenteral nutrition after 12 days of minimal intake. Thiamine was given. On day 2, phosphate falls from 3.2 to 1.1 mg/dL, potassium and magnesium also fall, and the patient develops weakness and shallow breathing. What is the priority response to this refeeding pattern?

answers.text: Increase the feeding rate to replace the lost electrolytes faster
Stop all electrolyte replacement and obtain a bone density study
Reduce or pause feeds, replace electrolytes, and monitor closely
Give a large insulin bolus to drive phosphate back into the cells

questions.explanation: Key C is correct: a sharp fall in phosphate with falling potassium and magnesium shortly after refeeding a malnourished patient is refeeding syndrome; feeds are reduced or paused, electrolytes are aggressively replaced, and cardiorespiratory status is monitored. A is wrong because increasing feeds worsens intracellular shifts and further lowers serum phosphate. B is wrong because stopping replacement leaves life-threatening hypophosphatemia untreated and bone density is irrelevant acutely. D is wrong because insulin drives electrolytes further intracellularly and worsens serum levels.

questions.question: Twenty hours after return of spontaneous circulation, a 62-year-old man remains comatose and develops brief generalized myoclonic jerks. A family member asks whether the jerking means recovery is impossible and care should be withdrawn now. What is the best response and plan?

answers.text: Agree that early myoclonus proves a hopeless outcome, and recommend withdrawal at the next family meeting today
Explain that myoclonus alone this early must not drive withdrawal; continue care, obtain EEG, and prognosticate multimodally at 72 hours or later
Explain that myoclonus is actually a favorable sign, so the family can be reassured that full recovery is now the expected outcome
Recommend immediate deep sedation to hide the jerking from the family, because its appearance is the main problem to be solved

questions.explanation: Early post-anoxic myoclonus was once treated as uniformly ominous, but it is no longer considered a reliable stand-alone predictor of poor outcome — some patients with early myoclonus recover. Prognostication after cardiac arrest must be multimodal and deferred until at least 72 hours, with EEG used to characterize the jerks. It is neither proof of futility nor a favorable sign, and sedating to conceal movements does not address prognosis.

questions.question: A 46-year-old woman with Guillain-Barre syndrome is on day 12 of ascending weakness. Her vital capacity has fallen from 1.8 L to 1.2 L to 0.9 L over 24 hours, and her negative inspiratory force has weakened from -42 to -19 cm H2O. Her oxygen saturation is 97% on room air, respiratory rate is 24/min with shallow breaths and a weak cough, and her heart rate swings between 52 and 128/min with labile blood pressure. What is the most appropriate action?

answers.text: Reassure the team that the normal oxygen saturation shows her ventilation is adequate, continue routine shift checks, and repeat the measurements at the end of the week
Document the values, continue hourly vital signs, and recheck her respiratory measurements on the next morning round unless her saturation falls below 90%
Notify the provider now of the falling vital-capacity and inspiratory-force trend and the autonomic instability, increase monitoring, and anticipate airway support
Encourage vigorous incentive spirometry, coughing exercises, and ambulation to the chair several times daily to reverse the declining measurements

questions.explanation: C is correct: in Guillain-Barre syndrome, serial vital capacity and negative inspiratory force track neuromuscular respiratory reserve; a vital capacity falling toward 20 mL/kg and an inspiratory force weaker than about -30 cm H2O signal impending ventilatory failure, and wide heart-rate and blood-pressure swings show autonomic instability — together they demand urgent escalation even though oxygen saturation is still normal, because saturation falls late in pure ventilatory failure. A is wrong: a normal saturation does not exclude failing respiratory mechanics. B is wrong: the trend is rapid and waiting overnight risks unplanned respiratory arrest. D is wrong: exercise cannot reverse ascending paralysis and exertion may worsen fatigue.

questions.question: A 48-year-old man has been ventilated for 5 days with propofol running at 75 mcg/kg/min. His serum now looks lipemic, triglycerides are 890 mg/dL, arterial pH is 7.18 with a rising lactate, creatine kinase is 18,400 units/L, urine output is falling, and he has had new bradycardic episodes. Which action is best?

answers.text: Continue the same propofol dose, because rising triglycerides are an expected and harmless finding during prolonged sedation in a ventilated patient
Increase the propofol rate to deepen sedation and simply repeat the triglyceride level in one week without other changes
Stop the propofol infusion now, switch to a different sedative, and support organ function while treating the rhabdomyolysis
Treat the triglycerides with an insulin infusion alone and keep the propofol infusion running at its current high rate

questions.explanation: Key C is correct: prolonged high-dose propofol with hypertriglycerides, metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, renal dysfunction, and bradycardia is propofol infusion syndrome, a potentially fatal complication whose essential first step is stopping propofol immediately, changing to an alternative sedative, and supporting failing organs while the muscle injury and acidosis are treated. A is wrong because these triglycerides in this clinical picture are a warning sign of the syndrome, not a harmless expectation, and continued exposure can be lethal. B is wrong because raising the dose intensifies the toxicity and a week is far too long to wait. D is wrong because insulin does not treat the syndrome and leaving the causative infusion running allows it to progress to cardiovascular collapse.

questions.question: A 68-year-old man is found outdoors in winter with core temperature 28.5 C, heart rate 32/min, BP 82/48 mmHg, and slow respirations. He is moved to the ICU for rewarming. Which statement about his care is correct?

answers.text: Defibrillation and resuscitation drugs work the same below 30 C as at normal temperature
Rapid rough handling is safe because the hypothermic heart is stable
Rewarming should be delayed until a full neurologic examination is normal
Handle gently, rewarm, expect poor drug response below 30 C

questions.explanation: Key D is correct: the severely hypothermic heart is irritable and prone to ventricular fibrillation with rough handling, and below about 30 C defibrillation and vasoactive drugs are less effective, so gentle handling and active rewarming take priority while resuscitation continues. A is wrong because drug metabolism and defibrillation success are reduced at very low temperatures. B is wrong because rough handling can precipitate fibrillation. C is wrong because rewarming must not wait for a normal neurologic examination, which hypothermia itself distorts.

questions.question: A quality dashboard shows a funnel plot of infection rates. A small unit's raw rate is higher than the hospital average, but its plotted point lies inside the 95% control limits, and the limits around small units are very wide. What is the most defensible interpretation?

answers.text: The small unit is the hospital's worst performer and should be ranked last.
The wide limits are a plotting error and should be narrowed until the point falls outside them.
A point inside the limits is consistent with common-cause variation; the small denominator makes the rate imprecise, so ranking this unit as an outlier is not justified.
Any unit above the average line requires immediate corrective action, regardless of the limits.

questions.explanation: Funnel plots exist precisely to prevent over-reading raw rates: control limits widen as volume falls, reflecting the imprecision of small samples, and a point inside the limits behaves like common-cause variation rather than a true outlier signal. Ranking by raw rate, acting on any above-average point, or narrowing limits to manufacture a signal all recreate the misinterpretation the funnel plot is designed to avoid.

questions.question: Ana, a 38-year-old transgender woman admitted to the ICU after trauma, takes prescribed estrogen therapy at home. The team proposes stopping it indefinitely 'because she is not eating,' without discussing it with her. She is awake, has decision-making capacity, and tells the nurse she is distressed about the plan. What is the nurse's best action?

answers.text: Prompt a provider and pharmacist review of the therapy's risks and benefits for her, include her preferences, and document a time-limited plan with a reassessment point.

Agree to stop the therapy indefinitely without discussion, since it is unrelated to trauma care, and note the discontinuation in the medication list without setting any date for it to be reconsidered.
Bring in her home estrogen supply and give it secretly so the team is not troubled, documenting the doses as though they had been ordered through the usual medication reconciliation process.

Reassure her that hormone therapy is irrelevant in the ICU and change the subject, explaining that questions about long-term medications can be raised again at her first outpatient appointment after discharge.

questions.explanation: Key (A): Hormone-therapy continuation is a clinical decision, not a default deletion: it deserves the same risk-benefit review, patient involvement, and time-limited documented plan as any other home therapy, weighing her real thrombotic risk factors. B is wrong because indefinite discontinuation without review or discussion disregards both the therapy's significance to her and standard medication-reconciliation practice. C is wrong because secretly administering a non-reconciled medication is unsafe and dishonest. D is wrong because dismissing her stated distress abandons advocacy for a concern the team has not actually evaluated.

fnp.quiz_title: FNP Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A 7-week-old infant is brought in after 10 days of worsening cough. She has bursts of rapid, repeated coughs followed by apnea and bluish discoloration of the lips, yet she is afebrile, feeds between bursts, and has a clear chest examination. Her white blood cell count is markedly elevated, predominantly lymphocytes. Her older sibling has had a mild cough for 3 weeks. Which condition does this assessment most strongly suggest?

answers.text: Viral bronchiolitis from respiratory syncytial virus
Pertussis in its paroxysmal stage
Bacterial pneumonia of the right lower lobe
Laryngomalacia with secondary feeding difficulty

questions.explanation: Correct: paroxysmal coughing bursts with apnea and cyanosis in a young infant who is afebrile with a clear chest between episodes, a marked lymphocytosis, and a coughing household contact is the classic assessment picture of pertussis — infants often lack an inspiratory whoop and present with apnea instead. A is wrong because bronchiolitis causes continuous wheezing, crackles, and increased work of breathing rather than discrete coughing bursts with apnea and a normal examination between them, and it does not produce marked lymphocytosis. C is wrong because bacterial pneumonia would be expected to cause fever and focal chest findings. D is wrong because laryngomalacia produces chronic inspiratory stridor from the first weeks of life, not episodic coughing bursts with apnea.

questions.question: A 16-year-old at 10 weeks of gestation has had severe nausea and vomiting for 2 weeks, cannot keep fluids down, has lost 5% of her pre-pregnancy weight, and has ketones in her urine. Which acid-base and electrolyte pattern is characteristic of this degree of vomiting?

answers.text: Hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis
Hypernatremic respiratory acidosis
Hypokalemic metabolic acidosis with an elevated anion gap from starvation alone
Hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis

questions.explanation: D is correct: persistent vomiting loses hydrogen and chloride from gastric fluid and causes volume-depletion alkalosis with potassium loss — hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis, the pattern seen in hyperemesis gravidarum. A is wrong because vomiting lowers, rather than raises, potassium and produces alkalosis, not acidosis. B is wrong because the primary disturbance is metabolic, not respiratory. C is wrong on the potassium and chloride direction and on the primary acid-base process, even though ketosis can coexist.

questions.question: An 80-year-old woman recovering from hip surgery is examined because she cannot pass stool or flatus and her abdomen is distended. When she strains at stool in the clinic bathroom, tissue protrudes from the anus showing concentric rings of folds around a central opening, then retracts. She reports months of fecal urgency and mucus leakage. Which examination interpretation best fits this finding?

answers.text: A thrombosed external hemorrhoid, which presents as concentric full-thickness rings of protruding tissue with mucus leakage and fecal urgency in an older woman after abdominal surgery
An internal hemorrhoid that has prolapsed and will reduce spontaneously
Full-thickness rectal prolapse — protrusion of the entire rectal wall, identified by concentric folds, distinct from mucosal hemorrhoidal prolapse
A rectal polyp on a stalk presenting at the anal verge

questions.explanation: Full-thickness rectal prolapse protrudes the entire rectal wall through the anus, producing the diagnostic concentric rings of folds; it is associated in older women with pelvic floor weakness, chronic straining, fecal urgency, and mucus discharge, as here. A is wrong: a thrombosed external hemorrhoid is a tense, painful, bluish perianal lump, not concentric rings. B is wrong: prolapsing internal hemorrhoids show radial folds of mucosa rather than concentric full-thickness rings and typically present with bleeding and tissue that slips back. D is wrong: a pedunculated polyp is a discrete mass on a stalk without circumferential folds.

questions.question: A 52-year-old man who was born in a country with a high tuberculosis burden has a positive interferon-gamma release assay on pre-employment screening. He has no cough, fever, night sweats, or weight loss, his chest radiograph is normal, and he has never been treated for tuberculosis. Which diagnosis best fits these findings?

answers.text: Active pulmonary tuberculosis
A false-positive result requiring no further consideration
A positive result caused by his childhood BCG vaccination
Latent tuberculosis infection

questions.explanation: Key D is correct: a positive interferon-gamma release assay with no symptoms and a normal chest radiograph, after exclusion of active disease, defines latent tuberculosis infection, which carries a lifetime risk of reactivation and is an indication to consider preventive treatment. A is wrong because active pulmonary tuberculosis typically produces symptoms and radiographic abnormalities, both absent here. B is wrong because epidemiologic risk plus a positive assay cannot be dismissed as false positive without evidence, and latent infection warrants a treatment discussion. C is wrong because, unlike the tuberculin skin test, interferon-gamma release assays are not affected by prior BCG vaccination.

questions.question: A 58-year-old man with 30 years of heavy daily alcohol use (roughly 10 drinks a day) reports progressive exertional dyspnea and orthopnea. Echocardiography shows a dilated left ventricle with diffuse hypokinesis and an ejection fraction of 28%. Coronary angiography shows no obstructive disease, and there is no valve lesion or history of chemotherapy. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Ischemic cardiomyopathy from silent coronary disease
Hypertensive heart disease with concentric remodeling
Alcohol-induced dilated cardiomyopathy
Tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy

questions.explanation: C is correct: decades of heavy alcohol exposure with a dilated, diffusely hypokinetic ventricle and clean coronary arteries identify alcohol-induced dilated cardiomyopathy, a diagnosis of exclusion supported by the exposure history. A is wrong because angiography excludes obstructive coronary disease and the wall-motion abnormality is global rather than territorial. B is wrong because hypertensive heart disease produces concentric hypertrophy and usually a small, stiff ventricle, not dilation with an ejection fraction of 28%. D is wrong because there is no history of a persistent tachyarrhythmia to drive tachycardia-mediated dysfunction.

questions.question: A 30-year-old woman has recurrent itchy hand and forearm dermatitis that flares after using fragranced lotions and cleaning products at work and improves during vacations. Which plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Prescribe repeated courses of oral corticosteroids as the long-term strategy
Start a strict food elimination diet as the primary intervention
Continue the same products and simply increase the potency of her steroid cream indefinitely
Identify and avoid the suspected allergens, switch to fragrance-free substitutes and protective gloves, use emollients and appropriate topical therapy, and refer her for patch testing

questions.explanation: D is correct: a work- and product-linked pattern suggests allergic contact dermatitis, whose plan centers on identifying and avoiding the allergen, using fragrance-free substitutes and barrier protection, and confirming the trigger with patch testing. A is wrong because repeated systemic corticosteroids are not a safe long-term strategy and do nothing about ongoing exposure. B is wrong because food elimination does not address a contact exposure pattern that tracks with products and work. C is wrong because escalating steroid potency indefinitely while exposure continues treats symptoms only and adds skin atrophy risk.

questions.question: A 48-year-old man who immigrated 2 years ago reports 6 weeks of cough, drenching night sweats, a 12-lb weight loss, and one episode of blood-streaked sputum. A chest radiograph obtained today shows a right upper lobe cavitary infiltrate. Which plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Prescribe a 5-day course of azithromycin and recheck in 1 month
Order spirometry and a smoking cessation referral as the only plan
Schedule a routine outpatient bronchoscopy in 6 weeks
Place him in airborne isolation, obtain sputum for acid-fast smear, culture, and nucleic acid amplification testing, and notify public health

questions.explanation: D is correct: prolonged cough with night sweats, weight loss, hemoptysis, and an upper lobe cavitary infiltrate is highly suggestive of active pulmonary tuberculosis, which requires airborne isolation, sputum acid-fast smear, culture, and nucleic acid amplification testing, plus prompt public health notification because it is a reportable, transmissible disease. A is wrong because a short macrolide course does not treat tuberculosis and a month of delay exposes contacts. B is wrong because spirometry and cessation support, while generally healthy, ignore a probable infectious emergency. C is wrong because waiting 6 weeks for bronchoscopy delays diagnosis and infection control when sputum testing should begin immediately.

questions.question: A 26-year-old man with sickle cell disease presents with fever of 101.3 F, cough, chest pain, oxygen saturation of 89% on room air, and a new infiltrate on chest radiograph, consistent with acute chest syndrome. Which treatment package is most appropriate?

answers.text: Oral fluids and acetaminophen with discharge home
Oxygen, ceftriaxone plus azithromycin, incentive spirometry, and urgent hematology consultation regarding simple or exchange transfusion
High-dose corticosteroids alone
Therapeutic heparin as the sole treatment, because the infiltrate represents pulmonary embolism

questions.explanation: Acute chest syndrome is a leading cause of death in sickle cell disease and is treated with oxygen, broad-spectrum antibiotics covering typical and atypical organisms (a cephalosporin plus a macrolide), incentive spirometry, careful fluids and analgesia, and hematology involvement for transfusion decisions, with exchange transfusion for severe or worsening hypoxemia. Discharging a hypoxemic patient with oral fluids is unsafe. Steroids alone do not treat infection or sickling and can precipitate rebound vaso-occlusion. Heparin alone ignores the infectious and vaso-occlusive drivers and is not the treatment for acute chest syndrome.

questions.question: A 41-year-old woman has had four episodes of vulvovaginal candidiasis in the past 12 months, each confirmed by culture as Candida albicans and each responding to a single fluconazole dose before recurring. She is not pregnant, has no diabetes, and is not immunocompromised. Which regimen should the FNP implement to control her recurrent disease?

answers.text: Fluconazole 150 mg orally every 72 hours for 3 doses, followed by fluconazole 150 mg once weekly for 6 months
A single fluconazole 150 mg dose repeated for each new episode as it occurs, with no maintenance phase no matter how many episodes accumulate
Daily topical antifungal cream applied indefinitely as the preferred suppressive strategy, reserving oral therapy only for treatment failures
Simultaneous antifungal treatment of her asymptomatic partner plus complete abstinence during and for a week after each of her episodes

questions.explanation: A is correct: recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (four or more episodes in a year) due to C. albicans is managed with an induction course of oral fluconazole every 72 hours for three doses followed by weekly suppressive fluconazole for 6 months, which keeps most patients in remission during therapy. B is wrong because episodic single-dose treatment is exactly the strategy that has already failed to prevent her recurrences. C is wrong because long-term daily topical therapy is less effective and less acceptable than oral maintenance for albicans disease. D is wrong because vulvovaginal candidiasis is not managed as a sexually transmitted infection; routine partner treatment is not recommended.

questions.question: An 82-year-old frail man is 3 months past a stroke and has painful shoulder and elbow spasticity in the affected arm that limits dressing and hygiene. He is unsteady and takes several sedating medicines. Which spasticity plan should the FNP implement first?

answers.text: Start high-dose oral baclofen as the sole first step and stop all other spasticity measures while it takes effect
Start daily stretching, positioning, and splinting with therapy referral; consider focal injections for focal spasticity
Advise the family to keep the affected arm fully immobilized in a sling at all times, day and night, indefinitely
Schedule surgical tendon release of the affected arm as the initial intervention before any conservative therapy

questions.explanation: Key B is correct: post-stroke spasticity management starts with stretching, positioning, splinting, and therapy, with focal botulinum toxin considered for focal function-limiting patterns; systemic agents such as baclofen cause sedation and weakness that are especially hazardous in a frail fall-prone patient. A is wrong because high-dose baclofen first risks falls, confusion, and weakness. C is wrong because constant immobilization worsens contracture. D is wrong because surgery is a last resort after conservative measures.

questions.question: A 27-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome started immediate-release metformin 2 months ago. Her hemoglobin A1C improved from 6.1% to 5.8% and cycles are more regular, but she has bothersome diarrhea after morning doses taken without food. She wants to continue metformin. What is the best modification?

answers.text: Stop metformin permanently because gastrointestinal effects mean it is unsafe for her
Switch to extended-release metformin taken with food and titrate gradually, while continuing metabolic follow-up
Take metformin only on days she feels her glucose is high
Double the immediate-release dose to overcome the diarrhea

questions.explanation: The key is B: extended-release metformin taken with meals and titrated gradually commonly reduces gastrointestinal intolerance while preserving the metabolic benefit she is already seeing. A is wrong because manageable gastrointestinal effects in a patient who wants to continue do not make the drug permanently unsafe.
