C is wrong because intermittent, symptom-guided use undermines steady metabolic effect and glucose cannot be reliably felt. D is wrong because increasing the immediate-release dose would worsen diarrhea.

questions.question: A school district asks the family nurse practitioner to help design its vision-screening program for adolescents. Which program element is most essential for the screening to actually benefit students?

answers.text: A reliable referral and follow-up pathway so students who do not pass screening receive a comprehensive eye examination and needed correction
Screening only students whose teachers suspect a vision problem
Using the screening result itself as the final diagnosis
Screening once, in the final year of school, to save resources

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: screening only creates value when a failed screen reliably leads to definitive evaluation and treatment; a tracked referral and follow-up loop is the essential system element. B misses asymptomatic students screening is meant to find. C confuses a screening test with a diagnostic examination. D delays detection for years, during which uncorrected vision can impair learning.

minnesota-mpje.quiz_title: Minnesota MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A prescriber needs a commercially available drug for a patient, but the drug currently appears on the FDA shortage list and cannot be obtained from the manufacturer. May a pharmacy compound a copy of that drug?

answers.text: No, because a compounded copy of a commercial product is barred in every circumstance
Yes, but only if the pharmacy first obtains a patent waiver from the manufacturer
Yes, because drugs on the FDA shortage list may be compounded even though they are commercially available products
Yes, but only for veterinary patients, never for human patients

questions.explanation: A compounded copy of a commercially available drug is permitted when the drug appears on the FDA shortage list, which is an exception to the general bar on copying commercial products. The bar is therefore not absolute, no manufacturer patent waiver is the mechanism for the shortage exception, and the exception is not confined to veterinary use.

questions.question: Marta, the pharmacist-in-charge of a community pharmacy that dispenses controlled substances, is setting the pharmacy's federal registration renewal calendar. How often must the pharmacy renew its DEA registration?

answers.text: Every year
Every three years
Every two years
Every five years

questions.explanation: A pharmacy's DEA registration is renewed on a three-year cycle. An annual cycle understates that period, a two-year cycle confuses registration with the biennial controlled-substance inventory and the two-year federal record-retention floor, and a five-year cycle has no basis in the federal registration rule.

questions.question: During a routine visit to Harborview Pharmacy, board inspectors ask to review the store's controlled-substance dispensing records and to count selected controlled-substance stock against those records. The manager wonders whether that material is within the inspectors' reach. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: The inspectors may look at general store areas only, never at drug records or stock
Controlled-substance records and inventory fall within the scope of a board inspection
Inspectors may view inventory counts but are barred from any underlying records
Controlled-substance material may be inspected only by a pharmacist employed at the store

questions.explanation: Board inspection authority during business hours reaches the prescription department and its records, including controlled-substance records and the inventory those records account for. Limiting inspectors to general areas, separating inventory from the records that verify it, or reserving inspection to store employees would defeat the board's entry and inspection power.

questions.question: A Schedule IV prescription was written seven months ago and has been refilled three times. The patient requests another refill, noting that refills remain on the label. What must pharmacist Ben Carter do?

answers.text: Dispense it because fewer than five refills were used
Dispense it if the prescriber's office is closed
Dispense a 72-hour emergency supply of the controlled substance
Require a new prescription, because the six-month refill period has expired

questions.explanation: Schedule IV refills are limited to five refills within six months, and expiry of the six-month period ends refill authority even if fewer than five refills were used. A closed prescriber office does not extend the period, and the non-controlled emergency-refill concept does not supply controlled-substance refill authority here.

questions.question: A prescription for tablets names the patient and prescriber, is dated and signed, and gives the drug, strength, and directions to take one tablet twice daily, but it never states how many tablets are to be dispensed. What is the defect?

answers.text: The directions are missing because a dosing interval is stated
The prescription is complete because the pharmacist can infer a quantity from the directions
The prescriber must rewrite it as an electronic prescription before any quantity can be accepted
The quantity to be dispensed is a required element and is missing

questions.explanation: The quantity is one of the required elements of a valid prescription, so an order that never states how much to dispense is incomplete. Directions stating how to take the drug do not themselves supply the amount to be dispensed, and converting the order to an electronic format does not create the missing quantity.

questions.question: A patient picks up a prescription for a drug the patient has never taken before. What counseling duty applies under the Board's rules?

answers.text: The pharmacist need only make a verbal offer to counsel and stop if the patient does not respond
After reviewing the patient record, the pharmacist shall personally initiate discussion of the matters that in professional judgment enhance or optimize therapy
A technician may provide the full consultation in the pharmacist's place
Counseling is required only if the patient asks a question first

questions.explanation: For a new prescription, after reviewing the patient record, the pharmacist shall personally initiate discussion of the matters that in professional judgment enhance or optimize therapy. A bare offer that ends without engagement understates the affirmative duty, the initiation belongs to the pharmacist personally, and the duty is not triggered only by a patient's question.

questions.question: Indigo asks which dispensing-related subjects fall within the Board's statutory powers. What is correct?

answers.text: The Board regulates the identity, labeling, purity, and quality of drugs dispensed, measured against the standards in the United States Pharmacopeia and National Formulary or in federal standards
The Board sets the retail price of every drug dispensed in Minnesota
The Board approves the marketing claims manufacturers make for each drug
The Board determines which drugs physicians may prescribe for each diagnosis

questions.explanation: The Board regulates the identity, labeling, purity, and quality of drugs dispensed, using the standards in the United States Pharmacopeia and National Formulary or federal standards. Retail price setting, manufacturer marketing approval, and control over physicians' prescribing choices are not among the Board's stated powers.

questions.question: A pharmacist repeats the same CE program three times in one period and asks how many times it may be credited. What does the rule provide?

answers.text: The same program may be credited once for each time it is taken
The same program may be credited twice per period
The same program may never be credited in consecutive periods
The same program may be credited only once per period

questions.explanation: The same program may be credited only once per period. Crediting each repetition and crediting twice both multiply a single program's value, and the limit is within a period rather than a bar across consecutive periods.

questions.question: A Schedule II prescription presented to pharmacist Henrik Weiss is dated ten days in the future. The prescriber, contacted by Henrik, confirms the date is a clerical error, the prescription was written today, and it is meant to be filled today. What may Henrik do?

answers.text: Change the date on the prescription to today's date after that prescriber consultation and fill it
Fill it today but leave the future date untouched so the record matches the paper
Hold the prescription for ten days, because a date error can never be corrected
Backdate the pharmacy's fill record to the written date once the ten days pass

questions.explanation: The date is among the elements a pharmacist may change on a Schedule II prescription after consulting the prescriber, so a prescriber-confirmed date correction may be made and the prescription filled. Filling while leaving a known-wrong future date in place preserves an inaccurate record, the error does not impose an uncorrectable ten-day hold, and backdating a fill record misstates when dispensing occurred.

questions.question: Pharmacist Nadia Brooks compounds a water-based oral liquid for a child. The formula contains no preservative and there is no product-specific stability study to rely on. Refrigerated storage is planned. What is the default beyond-use limit for this preparation?

answers.text: 14 days, refrigerated
35 days, refrigerated
90 days at room temperature
180 days at room temperature

questions.explanation: For a non-preserved aqueous nonsterile preparation without supporting stability data, the default cap is 14 days under refrigeration. The 35-day period applies to a preserved aqueous preparation, and the 180-day period applies to non-aqueous formulations and solid dosage forms, so none of those longer periods fits a non-preserved water-based liquid.

questions.question: A billing specialist asks pharmacist Kenji Sato how much patient information she may pull from profiles when submitting claims and running operations reports, and whether the same limit governs a pharmacist sharing information to treat a patient. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: The minimum-necessary limit applies equally to treatment, payment, and operations, with no exceptions
The minimum-necessary limit applies to treatment only, because treatment involves the most sensitive information
No minimum-necessary limit applies to any pharmacy use of patient information
The minimum-necessary standard applies to payment and health care operations uses, but not to treatment

questions.explanation: The minimum-necessary standard applies to uses and disclosures for payment and health care operations, so staff should limit those uses to the information needed for the purpose. Treatment is not subject to that standard, because clinicians coordinating care need access to the information the care requires.

questions.question: Pharmacist-in-charge Laura Bennett discovers that the prescription department's door code has been shared with delivery drivers and the store's overnight cleaning crew so they can come and go without staff present. What must she do about access to the department?

answers.text: Leave the arrangement in place, since deliveries and cleaning are legitimate business needs
Post the code at the register so any employee can admit visitors when asked
Change the code only if a theft is later traced to an unauthorized entry
Limit the access codes and keys to authorized personnel only

questions.explanation: Only authorized personnel may have access to the pharmacy and prescription department, so codes and keys must be limited to those personnel. Delivery and cleaning needs do not create an exception for unsupervised access, posting the code widens access still further, and waiting for a theft before acting leaves the department unsecured in the meantime.

maine-mpje.quiz_title: Maine MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Maine's opioid prescribing rules set dosage limits but exempt a patient who is on an active taper from those limits for a limited period. Under the rule, how long may an active taper continue before the limits apply again?

answers.text: An active taper may continue for two years before the limits apply
An active taper ends the limits' application permanently
The active taper exemption lasts a maximum taper period of six months, after which the limits apply unless another exception applies
The taper period is thirty days at most

questions.explanation: The rule caps the active taper exemption at a maximum period of six months, after which the limits apply unless another exception fits. Two years overstates the period, permanent exemption ignores its end, and thirty days understates it.

questions.question: Marta, the pharmacist-in-charge of a community pharmacy that dispenses controlled substances, is setting the pharmacy's federal registration renewal calendar. How often must the pharmacy renew its DEA registration?

answers.text: Every year
Every three years
Every two years
Every five years

questions.explanation: A pharmacy's DEA registration is renewed on a three-year cycle. An annual cycle understates that period, a two-year cycle confuses registration with the biennial controlled-substance inventory and the two-year federal record-retention floor, and a five-year cycle has no basis in the federal registration rule.

questions.question: Pharmacist Dana Whitaker faces board charges over repeated recordkeeping violations. Rather than contest the charges at a formal hearing, she is offered a written agreement that resolves the case if she accepts probation, a monetary fine, and periodic record audits. May board charges be resolved in this way?

answers.text: Only if a criminal court approves the agreement first
Yes. A licensee may resolve board charges through a consent agreement or consent order that imposes conditions such as probation, a fine, and monitoring
No. Every board charge must be decided at a full contested hearing, even when the licensee agrees to the outcome
Yes, but a consent agreement may only dismiss the charges outright and can never include conditions

questions.explanation: A licensee may settle board charges through a consent agreement or consent order, accepting enforceable conditions such as probation, a fine, and monitoring instead of litigating the case. Criminal-court approval is not part of this administrative resolution, a contested hearing is unnecessary when the licensee voluntarily agrees to the terms, and an agreement that imposed no conditions at all would fail to address the violations that prompted the charges.

questions.question: Under the rule, what must a compliant monitoring check review about the amount of opioid therapy?

answers.text: Only the equivalents of the new prescription, ignoring current therapy
The equivalents of prescriptions filled in the previous seven days only
A simple count of opioid tablets dispensed in the past year
The person's aggregate morphine milligram equivalents, including the anticipated new prescription

questions.explanation: A compliant check reviews the person's aggregate morphine milligram equivalents including the anticipated new prescription. Looking only at the new prescription or only at the past week understates the aggregate, and a tablet count is not the equivalents review the rule describes.

questions.question: A prescription for tablets names the patient and prescriber, is dated and signed, and gives the drug, strength, and directions to take one tablet twice daily, but it never states how many tablets are to be dispensed. What is the defect?

answers.text: The directions are missing because a dosing interval is stated
The prescription is complete because the pharmacist can infer a quantity from the directions
The prescriber must rewrite it as an electronic prescription before any quantity can be accepted
The quantity to be dispensed is a required element and is missing

questions.explanation: The quantity is one of the required elements of a valid prescription, so an order that never states how much to dispense is incomplete. Directions stating how to take the drug do not themselves supply the amount to be dispensed, and converting the order to an electronic format does not create the missing quantity.

questions.question: Pharmacist Carla Nguyen wants to contact a patient's prescriber about a possible interaction she spotted during prospective review. The patient objects that he never signed any form authorizing the pharmacy to talk to his prescriber about his medications. What is correct?

answers.text: She must obtain his signed authorization before any communication with the prescriber
She must abandon the interaction concern, because the objection ends her review duties
She may communicate only if the patient pays for a consultation visit first
She may communicate with the prescriber for treatment without his authorization, because treatment communications do not require it

questions.explanation: Protected health information may be used and disclosed for treatment without patient authorization, and coordinating with the prescriber about a possible interaction is a treatment communication. A signed form is therefore not a precondition, and no consultation fee creates the permission. The objection does not cancel the pharmacist's prospective review responsibilities, which the prescriber communication serves.

questions.question: A patient starting a prescribed course of an oral antibiotic tells pharmacist Paul Grant she plans to stop taking it as soon as her fever is gone, probably on day three, and save the rest for a future illness. Which counseling response addresses the duration point correctly?

answers.text: Agree that stopping when symptoms resolve is the usual plan
Explain that she should take the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if she feels better sooner, and not save or reuse leftover doses on her own
Tell her to double the remaining doses so the course finishes sooner
Tell her duration does not matter as long as each dose is taken with food

questions.explanation: Duration is a required counseling point, and for a prescribed course the patient needs to know to continue for the full duration rather than stopping when symptoms ease. Stopping early and saving leftovers for self-treatment defeats the prescribed course, and doubling doses to finish sooner changes the regimen without authority. Food instructions, whatever they may be for a given drug, do not make duration irrelevant.

questions.question: Priya is revising a training manual and needs the size of the Maine Board of Pharmacy. How many members does the Board have?

answers.text: Seven members
Nine members
Five members
Eleven members

questions.explanation: The Board has seven members in total. Nine, five, and eleven do not match the number of seats the law creates.

questions.question: A new licensee asks where the Maine Board of Pharmacy sits and what it exists to do. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The Board is established within the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation and has the duties, powers and authority granted by and necessary to enforce the Maine Pharmacy Act
The Board is a fully independent agency outside any department and enforces all of Maine's health laws
The Board sits within the Department of Health and Human Services and administers the prescription monitoring program
The Board is a private professional association that advises the Legislature on pharmacy bills

questions.explanation: The Board is established within the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation to enforce the Maine Pharmacy Act. Independence outside any department misstates its placement, the health and human services department houses the monitoring program rather than the Board, and the Board is a state licensing body rather than a private association.

questions.question: A trainer is listing the transfer-related duty in the Board's license-required list for technicians. Which transfer duty is listed?

answers.text: Receipt of a transferred prescription for a Schedule II controlled substance
Receipt of a transferred prescription for a noncontrolled drug
Initiating a transfer of a prescription to another pharmacy on the technician's own authority
Verifying the clinical appropriateness of a transferred prescription

questions.explanation: The license-required list names receipt of a transferred prescription for a noncontrolled drug. A Schedule II transfer receipt is not the listed duty, initiating transfers on the technician's own authority adds a power the list does not grant, and clinical verification is a pharmacist function rather than a technician duty.

questions.question: Blair takes a two-credit approved college course and asks how much continuing education credit it can yield in one calendar year. What is correct?

answers.text: The course yields thirty hours that year, because the per-credit rate has no cap
The course yields no credit, because academic courses never count
The course yields seven and one-half hours, because academic credit is halved
Credit runs at fifteen hours per college credit but is capped at fifteen hours in any one calendar year, so the course yields fifteen hours that year

questions.explanation: An approved pharmacy course earns credit at fifteen hours per college credit, capped at fifteen hours in any one calendar year, on proof of successful completion. An uncapped thirty hours ignores the ceiling, academic courses do count through this route, and no halving rule applies to the credit.

questions.question: A Governor's aide is assembling a slate of pharmacist appointees drawn entirely from hospital practice and asks whether the slate satisfies the appointment rules. What is correct?

answers.text: No, because at appointment the pharmacist members must include at least one hospital pharmacist, at least one chain pharmacist, and at least one independent pharmacist
Yes, because any five licensed pharmacists satisfy the appointment rules
Yes, if at least one appointee has worked in a chain or independent setting at some earlier point
No, because the pharmacist members must all come from independent practice

questions.explanation: The appointment rules require at least one hospital, at least one chain, and at least one independent pharmacist among the pharmacist members, so an all-hospital slate fails. Any five pharmacists ignores the setting conditions, earlier work in a setting is not the same as holding that practice at appointment, and an all-independent slate would break the same rule from the other side.

massachusetts-mpje.quiz_title: Massachusetts MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A prepared medication was never dispensed because the patient never picked it up, and a technician starts pouring it back into the manufacturer's stock bottle. What is wrong?

answers.text: Nothing, because the stock bottle is where returned medication belongs
The only error is that a pharmacist must do the pouring personally
The error is that never-dispensed preparations must be destroyed in every case
Never-dispensed preparations returned to stock may not go back into the manufacturer's stock bottle, and they are kept in a labeled container instead

questions.explanation: Return-to-stock handling for a never-dispensed preparation uses a labeled container rather than the manufacturer's stock bottle. Pouring back into the stock bottle is exactly what the rule forbids, the defect is the container choice rather than who pours, and never-dispensed preparations are not automatically destroyed when the return-to-stock conditions are met.

questions.question: Noor asks how many of the pharmacist seats are reserved for academic practice. What is the correct number?

answers.text: Two seats
One seat
Three seats
No seat is reserved for academic practice

questions.explanation: One of the eight pharmacist seats is for academic practice. Two and three both overstate the single academic seat, and saying no seat is reserved overlooks the academic place built into the distribution.

questions.question: A staff pharmacist repeatedly notices that a colleague arrives smelling of alcohol, slurs words during counseling, and once nearly dispensed the wrong medication before being stopped. The store manager urges the staff pharmacist to stay quiet because reporting would leave the store short-staffed. What does the prevailing professional obligation require?

answers.text: Staying quiet, because staffing needs outweigh concerns that have not yet caused harm
Reporting only if the colleague is caught diverting drugs, since impairment alone is a private matter
Waiting until a patient is actually harmed so the report rests on a completed injury
Reporting the impaired colleague through the board or its impairment program channels, because the duty to act on a colleague's impairment is not cancelled by staffing concerns

questions.explanation: The prevailing professional and ethical obligation is to report an impaired practitioner so the concern reaches the board or its recovery and monitoring channels; a manager's staffing worries do not cancel that duty. The obligation attaches to observed impairment affecting practice, not only to proven diversion, and it does not wait for a patient to be harmed first. Near-miss dispensing errors are precisely the warning signs the duty is meant to catch.

questions.question: Pharmacist Grace Liu begins counseling a patient who is picking up a new prescription and has several similar-looking medications at home. Which opening points belong at the start of this counseling session?

answers.text: The pharmacy's return policy and the price of the medication
The name of the medication and a description of what it is and what it is for
The name of the wholesaler that supplied the medication
The schedule for the pharmacy's next inventory count

questions.explanation: The name and description of the medication are core counseling points, and identifying the drug at the outset helps the patient distinguish it from other medications at home. Price and return policy are transaction matters rather than clinical counseling content, and wholesaler or inventory details are pharmacy operations that do not help the patient use the drug safely.

questions.question: Riley has practiced pharmacy for six straight years and asks whether they meet the experience condition for a pharmacist seat on the Board. What is correct?

answers.text: Yes, because five consecutive years of practice is enough
Yes, because any three years of practice, consecutive or not, is enough
No, because a pharmacist member must have been engaged in the practice of pharmacy for at least seven consecutive years immediately before appointment
No, because ten consecutive years of practice is required

questions.explanation: A pharmacist member must show at least seven consecutive years of pharmacy practice immediately preceding the appointment, so six years falls short. Five years reflects the superseded pre-2014 figure, three nonconsecutive years ignores both the length and the consecutiveness conditions, and ten years adds a requirement that does not exist.

questions.question: Noor's pharmacist license has been lapsed for two and a half years, and Noor asks what examination step returning to practice requires. What is required?

answers.text: Noor must take and pass the state jurisprudence examination
Noor must retake the national licensure examination only
No examination is required, because conditions are the only tool for any lapse
Noor must complete a second full internship before any examination

questions.explanation: A lapse over two years requires the licensee to take and pass the jurisprudence examination. The national examination is not the stated requirement for a simple lapse of this length, conditions alone do not substitute for the examination at this tier, and no second internship is part of the lapse rule.

questions.question: Pharmacist Aisha Grant dispensed a Schedule II medication under the emergency oral authorization rule. What must the prescriber do next?

answers.text: Deliver a written or electronic prescription to the pharmacy within 7 days
Deliver a written prescription within 30 days
Telephone the pharmacy again within 72 hours to confirm the order
File the follow-up prescription only with the state board

questions.explanation: After an emergency oral Schedule II dispensing, the prescriber must deliver a written or electronic prescription within 7 days. Thirty days is too long, a second telephone call does not substitute for the required written or electronic prescription, and filing only with a board does not satisfy the duty to deliver it to the pharmacy.

questions.question: Evidence suggests a licensee's continued practice poses an immediate and serious threat to public health and safety, and Reese asks whether the Board must hold a full hearing before acting. What applies?

answers.text: Yes, because no license action of any kind may precede a full hearing
No, because the Board may act first only for paperwork violations
No, because the Board may suspend the license or refuse renewal before a hearing in that situation
Yes, because a threat finding must wait for a criminal conviction

questions.explanation: Where a licensee poses an immediate and serious threat, the Board may suspend or refuse renewal ahead of a hearing, with a prompt necessity hearing to follow. A full-hearing-first rule would nullify the summary power, the power is aimed at dangerous practice rather than paperwork lapses, and it does not depend on a criminal conviction.

questions.question: A prescription arrives for a drug whose Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program requires pharmacies to be specially certified to dispense it. This pharmacy has never enrolled in that program, though its pharmacists have dispensed similar drugs for years. What must happen first?

answers.text: The pharmacy may dispense once and complete enrollment afterward
Any licensed pharmacist on staff may dispense it because licensure satisfies the program
The pharmacy must be enrolled and certified in the drug's REMS program before it may dispense the drug
The pharmacy may dispense if the prescriber confirms enrollment is unnecessary

questions.explanation: Where a REMS program conditions dispensing on pharmacy certification, enrollment and certification are prerequisites that must be in place before the pharmacy dispenses the drug. Dispensing first and enrolling later reverses that order, general pharmacist licensure does not substitute for program certification, and a prescriber cannot waive a dispensing condition the program imposes on the pharmacy.

questions.question: A pharmacy student asks Alex who appoints every member of the Board. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: The Governor appoints all of the members
The Board elects its own members from among licensed pharmacists
The Commissioner of Public Health appoints all of the members
Each professional association appoints the member for its own field

questions.explanation: Every Board member is appointed by the Governor. Self-election by the Board, appointment by the Commissioner of Public Health, and appointment by professional associations all place the appointing power somewhere the law does not put it.

questions.question: Marlowe is counting the non-pharmacist, non-clinician seats and asks how many seats a pharmacy technician and a public representative each hold. What is correct?

answers.text: Two seats each
One seat each
The technician holds two seats and the public representative holds none
Neither role has a seat on the Board

questions.explanation: The pharmacy technician and the public representative each hold one seat. Two seats each would double both allocations, giving the technician two seats while denying the public representative any seat misstates both, and both roles are in fact represented.

questions.question: A pharmacy completed its last biennial controlled-substance inventory fourteen months ago, and the pharmacist-in-charge is scheduling the next one. Which statement about the timing is correct?

answers.text: The next biennial inventory may be taken on any date within two years of the previous inventory
The next biennial inventory must fall on exactly the same calendar date, two years later, with no flexibility
A full controlled-substance inventory must be taken every year on January 1
An inventory is required only in a year when the DEA asks the pharmacy for one

questions.explanation: After the initial inventory, the biennial inventory may be taken on any date within two years of the previous inventory date. It does not have to land on the exact anniversary date, and the cycle is every two years rather than an annual January count. The obligation runs on the pharmacy's own schedule and does not wait for a DEA request.

louisiana-mpje.quiz_title: Louisiana MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Four matters come before a state board on the same day. In which one is expedited summary suspension of the pharmacist's license the fitting response?

answers.text: A pharmacist filed a renewal application two weeks late but has practiced without incident
A pharmacist is documented working while impaired, diverting controlled substances, and is scheduled to practice as the sole pharmacist tonight
A pharmacy's exterior sign lists hours that differ slightly from the hours filed with the board
A technician's registration renewal paperwork contains a typographical error in a street address

questions.explanation: Summary suspension is reserved for imminent danger, and an impaired pharmacist who is diverting controlled substances and about to practice alone presents exactly that immediate risk to patients. A late renewal, a signage discrepancy, and a clerical typo are ordinary matters handled through the board's normal processes, not emergencies justifying suspension before the usual proceedings run their course.

questions.question: Marlowe works 60-hour weeks in the pharmacy and asks how many of those hours can be credited toward the candidate experience requirement each week. What is the cap?

answers.text: All 60 hours count, because every hour on site is creditable
Only 20 hours per week may ever be credited
The cap is 40 hours, matching a standard full-time schedule
A maximum of 50 hours per week is creditable toward the candidate's practical experience

questions.explanation: Creditable candidate experience is capped at 50 hours per week, so the extra ten hours in a 60-hour week do not count. Counting every hour on site ignores the cap, and neither a 20-hour nor a 40-hour figure states the credit limit the rule sets.

questions.question: A district manager builds a renewal wall chart for a pharmacist license, a pharmacy permit, a technician certificate, an emergency drug kit permit, and a benefits-manager permit. Which chart is right?

answers.text: Pharmacist license and pharmacy permit expire December thirty-first, the technician certificate expires June thirtieth, the drug kit permit expires July first, and the benefits-manager permit runs two years to its anniversary
Every credential on the chart expires December thirty-first
The technician certificate and drug kit permit both expire December thirty-first, and the rest run two years
The pharmacy permit expires June thirtieth and the pharmacist license expires July first

questions.explanation: Louisiana runs several cycles at once: December thirty-first for pharmacist licenses and pharmacy permits, June thirtieth for technician certificates, July first for emergency drug kit permits, and a two-year anniversary term for benefits-manager permits. A single shared date erases the technician, kit, and benefits-manager cycles, and the swaps misassign the June and July dates.

questions.question: A dated, signed prescription identifies the patient and prescriber, states a quantity and directions, and reads only 'the usual antibiotic tablets' with no medication name and no strength stated. Pharmacist Grace Liu cannot dispense it as complete. Which elements are missing?

answers.text: Only the dosage form, because naming the drug is optional
The patient's address, which is the sole defect whenever a drug is described generally
The prescriber's signature, even though the order is signed
The drug name and strength, which must be stated on a valid prescription

questions.explanation: A valid prescription must state the drug name and strength, and a general description such as 'the usual antibiotic tablets' supplies neither. The dosage form is a separate element and does not excuse the missing name, the patient's identifying elements are stated on these facts, and the signature that is present is not the defect.

questions.question: Alex is updating a compliance manual and needs the total number of members on the Louisiana Board of Pharmacy. What total is correct?

answers.text: Seventeen members
Nine members
Thirteen members
Twenty-five members

questions.explanation: The Board has seventeen members in total. Nine and thirteen both undercount the seats the membership law creates, and twenty-five overcounts them by adding seats that do not exist.

questions.question: A relief pharmacist working a single weekend shift at pharmacist-in-charge Karen Doyle's pharmacy dispenses a prescription without the required review, and an inspector later traces the lapse to that weekend. Karen tells the board the error belongs entirely to the relief pharmacist and that, as pharmacist-in-charge, she answers only for her own fills. Which response is correct?

answers.text: Karen remains accountable to the board as pharmacist-in-charge for the pharmacy's overall compliance and supervision, even though a subordinate made the underlying error
Karen is correct, because pharmacist-in-charge accountability attaches fill by fill to whoever physically dispensed
Karen is answerable only if she was physically present in the pharmacy at the moment of the error
Karen's accountability ended for that weekend when she scheduled a licensed pharmacist to cover it

questions.explanation: The pharmacist-in-charge is responsible for the pharmacy's compliance, security, records, and supervision of personnel, so regulatory accountability for the operation does not stop at errors the pharmacist-in-charge personally committed. Scheduling a licensed relief pharmacist does not transfer the designated role's accountability for that period. Physical presence at the moment of the error is not the measure of the role's responsibility to the board.

questions.question: A prescription for a 4-year-old weighing 16 kg directs an antibiotic dose that matches a typical adult dose and far exceeds the weight-based dose for a child of that size. What does prospective review require of pharmacist Nina Brooks?

answers.text: Catch the age- and weight-inappropriate dose on review and address it before dispensing
Dispense as written, because dose selection is solely the prescriber's role
Dispense half the prescribed quantity as a compromise
Ask the parent to give smaller spoonfuls at home

questions.explanation: Prospective review screens for incorrect dosage, including doses inappropriate for the patient's age and weight, so a pediatric dose far above the weight-based range must be caught and addressed before dispensing. Dispensing as written, halving the quantity, or shifting dose adjustment to the parent all leave the inappropriate dose unresolved.

questions.question: Taylor asks how much continuing education a Louisiana pharmacist must complete each year to renew. What is the baseline amount?

answers.text: 10 hours of continuing education per year
30 hours of continuing education per year
15 hours of continuing education every two years
15 hours of continuing education per year

questions.explanation: The annual requirement is 15 hours, which is one and one-half continuing education units. Ten hours undercounts the annual load, thirty hours doubles it, and spreading the same 15 hours over two years halves a requirement that is measured every year.

questions.question: A pharmacy's refrigerator failed over a weekend, and stock inside was exposed to heat until some products visibly degraded. A staff member asks whether the affected medication can still be dispensed if the expiration date has not passed. How is the degraded stock classified and handled?

answers.text: It is merely misbranded and may be dispensed once relabeled
It is adulterated because it has decomposed and degraded, and it may not be dispensed
It remains fully usable because an unexpired date guarantees quality
It may be dispensed at a discount with a warning to the patient

questions.explanation: A drug that has decomposed or degraded, including through damaging storage conditions, is adulterated, and adulterated stock may not be dispensed. The defect concerns the product's condition rather than its labeling, so relabeling cannot cure it, an unexpired printed date does not restore a degraded product, and price or warnings do not make adulterated medication dispensable.

questions.question: A nonresident pharmacy's proposed PIC held a Louisiana license years ago but let it lapse, and the pharmacy argues past licensure should count. What applies?

answers.text: Past Louisiana licensure counts for five years after it lapses
It does not count, because the nonresident PIC must be currently licensed by the Louisiana Board
The PIC may serve while a renewal application is merely being considered, with no current license
Current licensure is required only for resident pharmacy PICs, never for nonresident ones

questions.explanation: The nonresident rule requires a pharmacist-in-charge who is currently licensed in Louisiana, so a lapsed license does not qualify. No five-year grace period extends a lapsed license for this purpose, service cannot begin on a pending application without current licensure, and the current-license requirement applies to the nonresident PIC expressly.

questions.question: Casey wants to know who appoints Board members and what check applies to those appointments. What is correct?

answers.text: The Board elects its own members, with no confirmation by any other body
The secretary of the health department appoints the members, subject to approval by the Board president
District pharmacists appoint the members directly, and the governor only certifies the result
The governor appoints the members, every appointment is subject to Senate confirmation, and appointments must reflect diversity across race, gender, ethnicity, and geography

questions.explanation: Board members are appointed by the governor and every appointment is subject to Senate confirmation, with diversity across race, gender, ethnicity, and geography required. Self-election by the Board removes both the gubernatorial appointment and the confirmation check, appointment by the health secretary misplaces the appointing authority, and direct appointment by district pharmacists confuses the nomination role with the appointment itself.

questions.question: A new pharmacist-in-charge, Carla Nguyen, is reviewing how the pharmacy protects electronic and paper patient information, including who can enter record systems and how data is protected in transmission. Which set correctly describes the safeguard categories she must maintain?

answers.text: Financial, marketing, and staffing safeguards
Only physical safeguards, because locked doors are the sole required protection
Only technical safeguards, because paper records fall outside privacy protection
Administrative, physical, and technical safeguards, such as access controls and encryption

questions.explanation: Privacy and security protection rests on administrative, physical, and technical safeguards, which include measures such as access controls and encryption for electronic information. Financial, marketing, and staffing categories are not the safeguard framework, and neither physical measures alone nor technical measures alone cover the full obligation, which also reaches paper records.

kentucky-mpje.quiz_title: Kentucky MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A pharmacy blames a data processor's negligence for months of improper prescription records. How is that defense treated?

answers.text: The defense succeeds if the vendor admits fault
The defense succeeds for the first occurrence only
Computer malfunction or a data processor's negligence is not a defense to improper recordkeeping
The pharmacy's duty pauses until the vendor fixes the system

questions.explanation: Neither a computer malfunction nor a data processor's negligence excuses improper recordkeeping. A vendor's admission, a first-occurrence allowance, and a pause in the pharmacy's duty are all versions of the rejected defense.

questions.question: Taylor has served one full term as a pharmacist member of the board and asks how much longer they may continue to serve in that role. What limit applies?

answers.text: Terms are four years, with a maximum of two full terms
Terms are two years, with no limit on reappointment
Terms are six years, with a maximum of one full term
Terms are four years, with a maximum of three full terms

questions.explanation: A board term lasts four years and a member may serve no more than two full terms. A two-year term with unlimited reappointment invents both a shorter term and an absent cap, a six-year single term misstates both figures, and a three-term allowance exceeds the two-full-term maximum.

questions.question: A prescriber telephones a community pharmacy with a new prescription for a patient. The pharmacist is verifying orders beside pharmacy intern Sarah Lindqvist, who is practicing under the pharmacist's direct supervision. How may the call be handled?

answers.text: Only a technician may take the call, because telephone work is a mechanical task
The call must be declined until the prescriber sends a written prescription, because interns may never receive telephone orders
Sarah may receive the telephone order and reduce it to writing while practicing under the pharmacist's direct supervision, with the pharmacist responsible for the order as dispensed
Sarah may receive the order and dispense from it without any pharmacist involvement, because receiving an order makes it her prescription to fill

questions.explanation: Receiving a prescriber's telephone order and reducing it to writing is a pharmacist function that an intern may perform under direct supervision, with the supervising pharmacist responsible for the resulting dispensing. Telephone intake of a clinical order is not a technician's mechanical task, a supervised intern is not barred from receiving telephone orders, and intern authority never extends to dispensing independently of the pharmacist.

questions.question: How must records of prescriptions received electronically be retained?

answers.text: Electronically for no less than five years
As hard copy for three years, then electronically
Printed and filed for one year
In whatever form is cheapest each year

questions.explanation: Electronic prescriptions are retained electronically for no less than five years. The three-plus-two hard-copy split governs written, oral, and facsimile receipts rather than electronic ones, a one-year printout understates the period, and yearly cost-based format changes ignore the electronic-retention requirement.

questions.question: A buyer purchases a pharmacy and assumes the seller's permit automatically transfers with the business assets. Is that assumption correct?

answers.text: Yes, because permits transfer automatically on sale
Yes, if the sale price is reported to the board
No, because a pharmacy permit is not transferable
Yes, for 30 days after the sale while paperwork is completed

questions.explanation: A pharmacy permit is not transferable, so it does not pass automatically with a sale. Reporting the price does not create transferability, and no automatic 30-day transfer window exists apart from the separate pending-application arrangement.

questions.question: Pharmacist Laura Chen checks the prescription drug monitoring program before dispensing a benzodiazepine, finds a concerning pattern, calls the prescriber, and the prescriber confirms the therapy and explains the pattern. Laura dispenses. What documentation completes her handling of the check?

answers.text: Only a note that the prescription was filled, because the prescriber's confirmation needs no record
No documentation, because a resolved concern is treated as though the check never raised one
A note kept in her personal planner, so the pharmacy record stays clean
Documentation of the check and of the prescriber contact and resolution in the pharmacy's records

questions.explanation: Pharmacists document monitoring program checks, and where a check raises a concern that is resolved before dispensing, the record should show both the check and how the concern was resolved, here the prescriber contact and confirmation. A fill notation alone does not show the mandated review or its outcome. A personal planner is not the pharmacy's record, and a resolved concern still needs a record precisely because dispensing proceeded on the strength of that resolution.

questions.question: A patient's profile documents an allergy to a sulfonamide antibiotic. A new prescription arrives for that drug, and the patient says, 'I took something similar last year and felt fine, so I think I outgrew it.' No prescriber has addressed the documented allergy. What should pharmacist Tom Alvarez do?

answers.text: Dispense, because the patient's own report removes a documented allergy
Delete the allergy from the profile and dispense without further inquiry
Dispense a single test dose at the counter to confirm the allergy is gone
Keep the documented allergy in place and resolve the conflict with the prescriber before dispensing, rather than acting on the patient's unverified belief

questions.explanation: A documented allergy on the profile is part of the information prospective review relies on, and a patient's unverified belief that an allergy has resolved does not erase it or clear the prescription. Deleting the allergy destroys safety information, and a counter test dose exposes the patient to the very risk the screen identified. The conflict must be resolved with the prescriber, with the profile updated only on a reliable basis.

questions.question: An inspector finds a drug shipment that poses an imminent danger to public health sitting on a pharmacy's shelves. What may the board do about that product?

answers.text: Seize the drug or device that constitutes an imminent danger to public health
Only post a warning notice and wait for the pharmacy to volunteer removal
Nothing until a full disciplinary hearing concludes months later
Require the pharmacy to discount and sell through the stock quickly

questions.explanation: The board may seize a drug or device that constitutes an imminent danger to public health. A warning-only response and waiting for a hearing both leave an imminent danger in place despite the seizure power, and selling through dangerous stock would compound the hazard the power exists to stop.

questions.question: At day's end, what must happen to the daily record of prescription data generated by the computer system?

answers.text: It may be discarded once the system backs up
It must be verified, dated, and signed by the pharmacist or pharmacists who filled the prescriptions, and kept at least five years in readily retrievable form
Only the pharmacist-in-charge signs it, monthly
Verification is optional if no errors were reported

questions.explanation: The daily prescription-data record must be verified, dated, and signed by the filling pharmacist or pharmacists and retained at least five years, readily retrievable. Backup does not replace verification and signature, the duty is daily rather than a monthly pharmacist-in-charge task, and absence of reported errors does not make verification optional.

questions.question: Pharmacist Priya Nair is deciding whether a generic product may be interchanged for a prescribed brand product. The generic contains the same active ingredient but is made with a different salt form and carries no AB rating. A staff member argues the shared active ingredient is enough. What is correct?

answers.text: The shared active ingredient alone is not enough; interchangeability rests on the Orange Book therapeutic equivalence rating, such as an AB rating
Any product with the same active ingredient is automatically interchangeable for the brand
A different salt form is interchangeable whenever the strengths are numerically equal
The pharmacist may interchange the products if the patient has taken the generic before without complaint

questions.explanation: Therapeutic equivalence is determined through the Orange Book ratings; an AB-rated product is the interchangeable equivalent. Sharing an active ingredient, matching a numerical strength across a different salt form, or a patient's past tolerance does not establish therapeutic equivalence. Without the equivalence rating, the product cannot simply be interchanged for the prescribed brand.

questions.question: A licensee moves to a new home and updates the pharmacy's internal roster but never tells the Board. By when was Board notice of the home-address change due, and what is the status of the omission?

answers.text: Notice was due within thirty days, as a courtesy only
Notice was due within fourteen days of the change, and the failure is itself a discipline ground
Notice was due within sixty days, and only a fee applies
No notice is due because the employer has the new address

questions.explanation: The home-address notice runs to the Board within fourteen days, and missing it is a stated ground for discipline. Thirty days is the conviction self-report period rather than this one, the duty is a regulatory obligation rather than a courtesy or a fee item, and an employer's roster does not discharge notice owed to the Board.

questions.question: A sealed non-refrigerated drug is brought to a different pharmacy three weeks after dispensing. Why does it fail the return conditions on two grounds?

answers.text: Returns may go to any pharmacy within thirty days
It must be returned to a pharmacist of the dispensing pharmacy within fourteen days
The fourteen-day period runs from the prescription's written date, to any pharmacist
Location matters but timing never does

questions.explanation: A qualifying return must reach a pharmacist of the dispensing pharmacy within fourteen days, and this return is both late and at the wrong pharmacy. Any-pharmacy returns within thirty days misstate both conditions, the window is tied to the return rule rather than a written-date-to-any-pharmacist formula, and timing plainly matters.

hawaii-mpje.quiz_title: Hawaii MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: What must a wholesale distributor do with incoming and outgoing shipments?

answers.text: Inspect only shipments that look damaged
Open every incoming container and recount every unit by hand
Inspect outgoing shipments only once a month
Visually examine each incoming outside shipping container on receipt and carefully inspect each outgoing shipment

questions.explanation: Each incoming outside shipping container is visually examined on receipt, and each outgoing shipment is carefully inspected. Inspecting only suspicious shipments and monthly outgoing checks leave most shipments unexamined. The rule calls for visual container examination rather than a universal hand recount, and the carrier's work does not replace the distributor's duty.

questions.question: A licensee's renewal check is dishonored on first deposit, though the paperwork arrived on time. What happens to the license under the general act?

answers.text: It stays active while the licensee sends a replacement check within a year
It is automatically forfeited
Nothing; payment problems never affect a timely filing
It converts to inactive status until payment clears

questions.explanation: Automatic forfeiture follows failure to timely renew, failure to pay all required fees, a check dishonored on first deposit, or failure to meet any other legal renewal requirement. A dishonored check is not excused by timely paperwork, does not produce a short automatic suspension or inactive conversion, and cannot be cured on a year-long timeline.

questions.question: A patient with no prior contraceptive prescription and no regular prescriber asks a pharmacist to prescribe contraceptive supplies. May the pharmacist proceed if otherwise qualified?

answers.text: Yes, the pharmacist may prescribe and dispense contraceptive supplies whether or not the patient shows evidence of a previous prescription from a physician, advanced practice nurse, or other primary care provider
No, a previous prescription from a physician is always required first
No, the patient must first obtain a referral from a primary care provider
Yes, but only if the patient is already a patient of this pharmacy

questions.explanation: Pharmacist contraceptive authority applies regardless of whether the patient has evidence of a previous prescription from a physician, advanced practice nurse, or other authorized primary care provider. Requiring a prior prescription or a referral would recreate a barrier the authority removes. Pharmacy-patient status and a one-time-only limit are not conditions of the service.

questions.question: A pharmacy staff member drafts a MedWatch Form 3500 for a serious event that occurred shortly after a vaccine was administered at the pharmacy and asks pharmacist Samuel Price to submit it as drafted. What should Samuel do?

answers.text: Submit the form as drafted, because the seriousness of the event determines the form
Discard the report entirely, because vaccine events are never reported federally
Redirect the report to the vaccine adverse-event reporting system, VAERS, which is the channel for vaccine events
Hold the report until the pharmacy can prove the vaccine caused the event

questions.explanation: Vaccine adverse events are reported through VAERS, the vaccine-specific system, rather than on the MedWatch drug form, so the draft must be redirected to the correct channel. Seriousness alone does not choose the form, and vaccine events are federally reportable rather than discarded. Reporting does not wait for proof of causation before the event is submitted through the proper system.

questions.question: A prescription says nothing about how many times it may be refilled, and the patient asks for a refill. What must the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Not refill it unless the practitioner subsequently authorizes the refill
Refill it once as a courtesy fill
Refill it up to five times under a default rule
Refill it if the patient has taken the drug for years

questions.explanation: If a prescription does not indicate the number of refills, the pharmacist shall not refill it unless subsequently authorized by the practitioner. A courtesy fill, a five-refill default, and long use history each invent authorization the prescriber never gave. Transferring the prescription does not create refill authority either.

questions.question: A prescription directs a dose well above the usual range and a duration far longer than appropriate for the stated therapy. Which prospective review screens are triggered?

answers.text: Only allergy and therapeutic duplication
Incorrect dosage and incorrect duration
Only age and gender contraindications
Only abuse and misuse

questions.explanation: Prospective review includes screening for incorrect dosage and incorrect duration, both of which are presented by an excessive dose paired with an excessive treatment length. Allergy, duplication, age, gender, abuse, and misuse are separate screens and do not describe a dose-and-duration problem on these facts.

questions.question: Which item must the floor plan in a pharmacy permit application show for drug storage security?

answers.text: A locked cabinet among the counters, shelves, and storage cabinets diagrammed for the prescription area
An unlocked open bin for all prescription stock
A locked cabinet only in the front retail aisle
No storage detail, because security is inspected later

questions.explanation: The floor plan must diagram counters, tables, drawers, shelves, and storage cabinets including a locked cabinet, along with the library, sink, sewage outlet, and refrigeration. An unlocked bin defeats the security the plan must show, and a cabinet in the retail aisle or at a home is not prescription-area storage. Storage detail belongs in the application itself.

questions.question: Pharmacist Carla Jensen is reviewing over-the-counter analgesics and finds one product, properly manufactured and in date, whose labeling gives no usable directions telling a layperson how much to take, how often, or for how long. How is that product classified?

answers.text: Adulterated, because weak directions lower the product's quality
Acceptable, because store staff can explain dosing verbally at the register
Recalled, because inadequate directions automatically trigger a recall
Misbranded, because over-the-counter labeling that lacks adequate directions for use is misbranded

questions.explanation: An over-the-counter product whose labeling lacks adequate directions for use is misbranded, because a layperson cannot use it safely from its labeling alone. Verbal help at the register does not cure the labeling defect, adulteration concerns the drug's condition or quality, and a recall is a separate removal action rather than this classification.

questions.question: A compounding pharmacy prepares an oil-based oral liquid for patient Andre Boateng. The formulation contains no water and the pharmacy has no stability data for it. A technician proposes dating it 180 days because the batch is large. What is the correct default beyond-use date?

answers.text: 90 days, the default limit for a non-aqueous liquid without stability data
14 days refrigerated, the default for any compounded oral liquid
35 days, the default for any liquid that contains a preservative
180 days, the default limit for a non-aqueous formulation without stability data

questions.explanation: Under USP , a non-aqueous compounded formulation without supporting stability data carries a default beyond-use date of 180 days, and batch size does not change that limit. The 14-day refrigerated default applies to non-preserved aqueous preparations and the 35-day default to preserved aqueous preparations; this formulation contains no water, so neither shorter period applies.

questions.question: A registration holder discovers reason to believe controlled substances in inventory were diverted by fraud. What reporting sequence is required?

answers.text: Immediately report verbally to the administrator, then submit a written report as soon as practicable
File a written report within 30 days, with no verbal step
Report verbally within a week, then in writing at renewal
Wait until the annual inventory confirms the loss

questions.explanation: A holder who in a professional or official capacity has reason to believe inventory was stolen, embezzled, or obtained by fraud or diversion must immediately report verbally to the administrator and then submit a written report as soon as practicable, including the suspected perpetrator's name and address if known and the nature and extent of the loss. A 30-day written-only route, a week's delay, police-only reporting, and waiting for inventory all miss the immediate verbal step. The duty arises on reason to believe, not proof after a count.

questions.question: A licensee is disciplined by another jurisdiction in March and notifies the Hawaii authority the following January, explaining that they reported it at renewal time. What is wrong with that timing?

answers.text: Nothing, because reporting is due only at the next biennial renewal
The report was due within 10 days, so January is late for a different reason
Reports of out-of-state discipline are optional courtesies between boards
The general act requires written reporting of another jurisdiction's disciplinary decision within 30 days, and late reporting is itself a disciplinary ground

questions.explanation: A licensee must report another jurisdiction's disciplinary decision in writing within 30 days, and failure to do so is itself a ground for discipline. Renewal-time reporting months later misses that deadline. The general-act reporting window is 30 days rather than 10, and the duty is mandatory, not a courtesy.

questions.question: Pharmacist Elias Roth can supply only 12 of the 30 tablets on an outpatient's Schedule II prescription and dispenses 12 as a partial fill. A technician prepares a record showing only the full quantity of 30 tablets 'as written.' What documentation does the partial fill require?

answers.text: No special record, because the original prescription already shows the quantity
A record in the patient's general correspondence file noting that the fill 'went fine'
A record showing the quantity actually dispensed as the partial fill and the remaining balance, so the record reflects what was supplied and what remains subject to the short remainder window
A second prescription from the prescriber documenting the 12 tablets before any record is made

questions.explanation: A partial fill record must document what actually happened at dispensing: the quantity supplied in the partial fill and the balance remaining, because the remainder can be supplied only within the limited window before it is void. Recording only the quantity as written misstates the dispensing, a correspondence note is not the dispensing record, and no second prescription is needed to document a partial fill of the existing prescription.

delaware-mpje.quiz_title: Delaware MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: When a prescribed drug is out of stock, pharmacist Rachel Kim dispenses a different drug that was never authorized by the prescriber, labels the vial as though it contained the prescribed drug, and tells no one. A colleague discovers the switch a week later. How is Kim's conduct best characterized?

answers.text: Permissible generic substitution, because a pharmacist may always choose an alternative when stock runs out
A minor labeling error with no professional-conduct implications
Unprofessional conduct, involving both dispensing a drug without authority and deceiving the patient and the record about what was dispensed
Proper emergency practice, because keeping the patient on some therapy is always preferable

questions.explanation: Dispensing a different, unauthorized drug and deliberately concealing the substitution is unprofessional conduct, a recognized ground for board discipline. Lawful generic substitution involves an interchangeable equivalent the prescriber has not prohibited, not a different drug passed off under a false label, the deliberate mislabeling makes this far more than a clerical slip, and no emergency principle authorizes deceiving the patient about the medication actually dispensed.

questions.question: How much continuing education must a Delaware pharmacist acquire in each biennial licensure period?

answers.text: 20 hours, equal to 2.0 units
30 hours, equal to 3.0 continuing education units
30 hours every single year
15 hours per biennium

questions.explanation: The requirement is 3.0 units, which is 30 hours, per biennial licensure period. Twenty and fifteen hours fall short of the total, and 45 hours exceeds it. The 30 hours are spread across the two-year period rather than owed annually.

questions.question: A community pharmacy's facility permit expired at the end of last month, and the owner's renewal paperwork is still being processed. Every pharmacist on staff holds a current personal license, and the owner proposes keeping the pharmacy open as usual until the permit comes through. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The pharmacy may operate, because current pharmacist licenses are the only credentials that matter
The pharmacy may operate for thirty days after any permit expiration without consequence
The pharmacy may operate as long as it stops dispensing controlled substances during the gap
The pharmacy may not operate on an expired permit; the location itself must hold a current board-issued permit, separate from the pharmacists' personal licenses

questions.explanation: A pharmacy location operates under its own board-issued facility permit, which must be current; personal pharmacist licenses do not substitute for it, and dispensing under an expired permit is unlawful operation. No general grace period follows a permit expiration, and dropping controlled substances does not cure the missing permit for the pharmacy's other dispensing.

questions.question: After speaking with the prescriber, pharmacist Laura Nguyen learns the prescribed dosage form of a Schedule II drug is unavailable and the prescriber agrees to a different dosage form of the same drug. May the pharmacist make that change?

answers.text: No, dosage form can never be changed on a Schedule II prescription
Yes, after consulting the prescriber, the pharmacist may change the dosage form
Yes, without contacting the prescriber, whenever stock is short
Yes, and the pharmacist may also change the drug to a different therapeutic agent

questions.explanation: For a Schedule II prescription, dosage form is among the elements a pharmacist may change after consulting the prescriber. The change is not categorically barred, prescriber consultation is required rather than optional, and changing to a different drug altogether goes beyond a dosage-form change of the same drug.

questions.question: A pharmacist authorized to administer injectables and immunizations renews their license. How much of the biennial continuing education must address that practice area, and how can the duty end?

answers.text: At least 2 hours of the 30-hour requirement each period must be in that practice area, unless the pharmacist notifies the Board in writing that they no longer administer those products
No dedicated hours are required for immunizers
Ten dedicated hours are required every year
The duty ends automatically when the pharmacist changes jobs

questions.explanation: Immunizers dedicate a minimum of 2 hours of the 30-hour biennial requirement to the injectables and immunizations practice area. Relief comes only through written notice to the Board that the pharmacist no longer administers those products, not through a job change. Ten annual hours overstates the figure.

questions.question: A hospice patient in a long-term care facility needs a Schedule II medication, and the pharmacy can supply only part of the quantity today. Over what period may the remaining partial fills be provided for this patient?

answers.text: Only within 72 hours, with no exception
Only on the day the prescription was written
Up to 6 months from the issue date
Up to 60 days, because terminally ill and long-term care patients have an extended partial-fill period

questions.explanation: For terminally ill and long-term care facility patients, Schedule II partial fills are permitted over 60 days. The ordinary 72-hour remainder rule does not govern this patient category, same-day-only filling is not the standard, and six months is the refill window for lower schedules rather than this partial-fill period.

questions.question: A pharmacy intern offers to counsel a patient on a new prescription while the supervising pharmacist has stepped out of the pharmacy to run an errand and is not present or reachable. The intern has counseled before when the pharmacist was nearby. What is correct?

answers.text: The intern may counsel, because prior supervised experience carries over to this occasion
The intern may counsel if a technician remains in the department
The intern may counsel on directions but must save side effects for the pharmacist
The intern may not counsel on this occasion, because intern counseling occurs under pharmacist supervision, which is absent here

questions.explanation: Intern counseling is permitted as practice under a pharmacist's supervision, and that supervision is a condition of the occasion, not a credential earned once from earlier supervised sessions. A technician's presence does not supply pharmacist supervision. Splitting the counseling topics does not cure the missing supervision, so the counseling must wait for the pharmacist.

questions.question: Pharmacist Carla Jensen is reviewing over-the-counter analgesics and finds one product, properly manufactured and in date, whose labeling gives no usable directions telling a layperson how much to take, how often, or for how long. How is that product classified?

answers.text: Adulterated, because weak directions lower the product's quality
Acceptable, because store staff can explain dosing verbally at the register
Recalled, because inadequate directions automatically trigger a recall
Misbranded, because over-the-counter labeling that lacks adequate directions for use is misbranded

questions.explanation: An over-the-counter product whose labeling lacks adequate directions for use is misbranded, because a layperson cannot use it safely from its labeling alone. Verbal help at the register does not cure the labeling defect, adulteration concerns the drug's condition or quality, and a recall is a separate removal action rather than this classification.

questions.question: A sterile compounding trainee at pharmacist Laura Bennett's facility dons gown and sterile gloves first, then walks to the sink to wash her hands before entering the compounding area, planning to keep the gloves on while washing. The preceptor intervenes. What sequence does sterile compounding competency require?

answers.text: Garbing first and hand hygiene last, so the gloves are washed along with the hands
Either order, because garbing and hand hygiene are unrelated tasks
Hand hygiene performed before garbing, with garbing then completed before compounding begins
Hand hygiene only at the end of the shift, because garb protects the hands all day

questions.explanation: Hand hygiene comes before garbing in the sterile compounding sequence, so hands are cleaned before garb and gloves go on and aseptic work begins. Washing already-gloved hands defeats the purpose of sterile gloves, the two steps are linked parts of one competency, and deferring hand hygiene to the end of the shift leaves compounding to start with uncleaned hands.

questions.question: The Governor moves to remove a Board member for neglect of duty, and the member also faces a disciplinary hearing of their own. Which statements are correct?

answers.text: The Governor may suspend or remove a member for misfeasance, nonfeasance, malfeasance, misconduct, incompetency, or neglect of duty; a member facing a disciplinary hearing is disqualified from Board business until the charge is resolved, and the member may appeal a suspension or removal to the Superior Court
Only the Board itself may remove a member, by a unanimous vote
A member facing charges keeps voting until a court convicts them
Removal decisions are unreviewable by any court

questions.explanation: Removal authority sits with the Governor on the listed grounds, which include neglect of duty and incompetency. A member under a disciplinary charge is disqualified from Board business pending adjudication rather than voting through it. Superior Court appeal is expressly available, so the decision is reviewable.

questions.question: A licensee under a temporary suspension order demands a live evidentiary hearing before the suspension can continue pending the final hearing. What does the procedure actually provide?

answers.text: A full live trial must precede any temporary suspension
The licensee gets no opportunity to respond until the final hearing

The licensee receives written notice of the suspension and the supporting findings and an opportunity to be heard only on written submission as to why the license should not be temporarily suspended pending the final hearing
The licensee may present live witnesses but no documents

questions.explanation: The interim procedure is paper-based: written notice with findings, and a chance to be heard solely through written submissions on the temporary question. No live interim trial is provided, but the licensee is not left without any response opportunity either. Live witnesses are outside the written-submission format.

questions.question: Sam is applying for pharmacist licensure and must show completion of graduation requirements from an accredited pharmacy program. How must that evidence be presented?

answers.text: Verified by oath and satisfactory to the Board, showing graduation from a program accredited by the national pharmacy education accrediting body
By an unsworn photocopy the Board must accept at face value
By a letter from any employer confirming pharmacy experience
By proof of passing a technician certification examination

questions.explanation: The applicant must submit evidence, verified by oath and satisfactory to the Board, of completing graduation requirements at a school or college accredited by the national accrediting body for pharmacy education. An unsworn copy the Board must accept, an employer's experience letter, a memory recital, and a technician examination each fail to supply the sworn accredited-education proof required.

district-of-columbia-mpje.quiz_title: District of Columbia MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A neighborhood pharmacy compounds customized, patient-specific preparations in response to individual prescriptions and does not register as an outsourcing facility. Which regulator primarily oversees this traditional compounding activity?

answers.text: The DEA, because all compounding involves controlled substances
The state board of pharmacy
The federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services
No regulator, because patient-specific compounding is unregulated

questions.explanation: Traditional compounding pharmacies operating on a patient-specific basis under the 503A framework are regulated primarily by the state board of pharmacy. The DEA's role centers on controlled substances rather than compounding generally, Medicare and Medicaid program agencies do not license compounding practice, and patient-specific compounding is regulated rather than unregulated.

questions.question: A newly licensed pharmacist asks which authority sets the standards of pharmacy practice that govern her day-to-day professional conduct as a licensee. Which answer is correct?

answers.text: The Drug Enforcement Administration, through its controlled-substance registration program
The Food and Drug Administration, through its drug-approval process
Her employer's corporate policy manual, which supersedes government standards
The state board of pharmacy, which sets and enforces the standards of pharmacy practice for its licensees

questions.explanation: Standards of pharmacy practice for licensees are set and enforced by the state board of pharmacy.
