questions.explanation: Direct gas withdrawal is limited by how fast the container's own liquid can absorb heat and vaporize; heavy frosting is the sign that limit is reached. An evaporator takes liquid chlorine and heats it under control, sustaining gas rates the containers alone cannot.

questions.question: An operator fills a sand drying bed nearly to the boards with liquid digested sludge in one application, and weeks later it is still wet and odorous underneath. What application practice was violated?

answers.text: Sludge should be applied in a shallow lift that can drain, dry, and crack in reasonable time
Sludge should be applied only on rainy days so the surface stays soft
Sludge should be mixed with filtrate to keep it liquid longer
Sludge should be applied over the previous cake to save removal labor

questions.explanation: Drying beds work by drainage followed by evaporation through a lift thin enough for air to reach; a very deep lift seals over, stays wet and anaerobic underneath, and generates odor. Removing dried cake and applying shallow lifts keeps the bed cycling.

texas-wastewater-operator-class-d.quiz_title: Texas Wastewater Operator Class D Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A wastewater operator license remains valid for what period of time before renewal comes due?

answers.text: One year only
Two years only
Five years only
Three years

questions.explanation: A wastewater operator license is valid for three years. The shorter periods would force renewal too early and the longer one overstates the term.

questions.question: While crews are cleaning up a wastewater spill, a reporter asks an operator on site what caused it and how much spilled. The cause is not yet known. What is the most appropriate response?

answers.text: Offer a best guess about the likely cause so the news story can run on time tonight anyway
State a spill volume figure even though it has not been measured
Decline to speculate and refer the reporter to the utility's designated spokesperson
Tell the reporter that no spill occurred

questions.explanation: Unconfirmed causes and volumes are not guessed at on site; the reporter is referred to the designated spokesperson. Denying a visible spill would damage the utility's credibility as well.

questions.question: What does the average daily flow of a treatment plant describe?

answers.text: The total flow received over a period divided by the number of days in that period
The highest flow rate that the plant reaches during any single hour of operation
The flow that happens to be measured at exactly midnight on each day of the period
The rated flow capacity that is printed on the nameplate of the plant's largest pump

questions.explanation: Average daily flow spreads the total flow for a period evenly across its days. A peak-hour value, a midnight reading, and a pump rating are each different measures.

questions.question: A force main loses capacity over several weeks, pump run times lengthen, and the trouble traces to the highest point on the profile. What appurtenance at that high point addresses the cause?

answers.text: A gate valve left partly closed at the low point
An air release valve that vents trapped air from the high point
A cleanout cap on the nearest lateral
A check valve installed at the pump discharge only and nowhere else on the run

questions.explanation: Air collects at force main high points and air-binds the line, cutting capacity until it is vented by an air release valve. Valves at low points or on laterals do not remove trapped air at the crest.

questions.question: Grit and solids keep building up on the floor of the screen channel ahead of the bars, narrowing the channel between cleanings. What flow condition causes that?

answers.text: Approach velocity too low to keep the material carried through the channel
Approach velocity too high, scouring the channel clean rather than letting material drop out in it
Bar spacing wider than the channel itself
Rake cycles running more often than designed

questions.explanation: When approach velocity falls too low, heavy material drops out in the channel instead of reaching the bars and grit unit. Higher velocity would scour the channel rather than fill it.

questions.question: Three mechanics will service a clarifier drive together, and the equipment must stay de-energized until every one of them is clear. How does a group lockout accomplish that?

answers.text: The shift supervisor holds the only lock key in a desk drawer and promises the crew he will not start it until they report back to him in person
Each worker applies a personal lock to a multi-lock device, so the equipment cannot be re-energized until all locks are removed
One lock is applied and each worker keeps a photograph of it
The breaker is taped open and a note is left on the panel

questions.explanation: In a group lockout every worker's own lock must come off before the equipment can be restarted, so no one can be caught by an early start while still working. A single lock controlled by someone else, tape, or a note leaves each worker's safety in another person's hands.

questions.question: A rectangular primary tank measures 28 ft long by 14 ft wide, and the wastewater in it is 7.5 ft deep. How many gallons does it hold?

answers.text: 21,991.20 gallons
2,940 gallons
29,321.60 gallons
10,995.60 gallons

questions.explanation: Volume = 28 x 14 x 7.5 = 2,940 cu ft, and 2,940 x 7.48 = 21,991.20 gallons. The 29,321.60 figure uses a depth of 10 ft instead of the stated 7.5 ft.

questions.question: A pond cell is found to be losing level faster than evaporation explains, and a crack is suspected in its liner. Why is repairing the liner a water-quality priority?

answers.text: A leaking liner lets pond wastewater seep downward where it can contaminate groundwater supplies
A leaking liner lets groundwater flow upward and dilute the pond contents beyond permit limits
A leaking liner mainly wastes treated water that the plant had planned to sell for irrigation
A leaking liner allows algae to escape the pond and take root in the surrounding native grasses

questions.explanation: The liner is the barrier between stored wastewater and the soil below; a breach lets wastewater seep toward groundwater. The flow through a crack is outward and downward, not groundwater rising in to dilute the pond.

questions.question: A return rate is left low all weekend. On Monday the clarifier sludge smells septic and chunks of it are rising to the surface. What caused this?

answers.text: Sludge sat too long in the clarifier, turned septic, and gas lifted pieces of it
The sludge settled too well over the weekend and became too heavy to pump out
Fresh influent diluted the contents of the clarifier more than usual that week
The clarifier received far too much return flow all weekend from the basin

questions.explanation: Settled sludge that is not drawn off ages in the clarifier, and oxygen-free breakdown in it forms gas that buoys pieces to the surface. The return rate was too low, not too high, so excess return flow cannot explain sludge that sat and turned septic.

questions.question: A laboratory report lists an effluent result in milligrams per liter and a sludge cake result as a percent. An operator comparing the two numbers directly would be making what mistake?

answers.text: Reading the report from the top down instead of from the bottom up
Comparing results from two samples that were collected on different days
Using a report that the laboratory printed rather than wrote out by hand
Ignoring the units, which describe different kinds of quantities that cannot be compared as written

questions.explanation: Milligrams per liter and percent solids are different kinds of quantities, so the printed numbers cannot be compared until the units are accounted for. The order, dates, and printing of the report are not the problem; the unlike units are.

questions.question: Which statement about chlorine dioxide as a wastewater disinfectant is correct?

answers.text: It is the only disinfectant that leaves a chlorine residual in stored effluent
It disinfects by light energy, so its output falls as its lamps age
It must be stored as a pressurized gas in cylinders between uses
It remains effective over a wider range of pH values than free chlorine does

questions.explanation: Chlorine dioxide keeps its disinfecting strength across a broader pH range than free chlorine, whose form and strength shift markedly with pH. It is a chemical disinfectant, not a light-based one, and it is generated for use rather than stored as cylinder gas.

questions.question: An effluent filter is placed after secondary treatment at a plant that needs a cleaner discharge. What is its primary job?

answers.text: To add back a chlorine residual that the secondary treatment step removed
To remove suspended solids that carried over from secondary treatment
To grow a new biological population to replace the secondary process
To thicken waste sludge before it is sent to digestion

questions.explanation: Tertiary filtration is a polishing step that captures suspended solids remaining after secondary treatment. It does not grow a replacement biological process, which happens in the upstream treatment units.

texas-water-operator-class-a.quiz_title: Texas Water Operator Class A Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which set lists the required core training courses for the Class A license?

answers.text: Basic Waterworks Operation; Resiliency Overview; Surface Water Production I; Surface Water Production II; Groundwater Production; Water Distribution; Water Laboratory; Water Utility Management; Water Utility Safety

Basic Waterworks Operation; Resiliency Overview; Surface Water Production I; Groundwater Production; Water Distribution; Water Laboratory; Water Utility Management; Water Utility Safety; Wastewater Operations

Basic Waterworks Operation; Surface Water Production I; Surface Water Production II; Groundwater Production; Water Distribution; Water Laboratory; Water Utility Management; Water Utility Safety; Chlorinator Maintenance

Resiliency Overview; Surface Water Production I; Surface Water Production II; Groundwater Production; Water Distribution; Water Laboratory; Water Utility Management; Water Utility Safety; Pump and Motor Maintenance

questions.explanation: The Class A core is the nine-course set that includes both Surface Water Production courses and ends with Water Utility Management and Water Utility Safety. Each other set drops a required core course and adds a course that is not in the Class A core.

questions.question: Under the workplace safety responsibilities the Class A safety program is built on, what is the employer's core responsibility?

answers.text: To provide a workplace free of recognized hazards, along with the training and protective equipment the work requires
To transfer all safety responsibility to employees once they have been given a copy of the written program and have signed an acknowledgment that they received and read it
To provide protective equipment only after an injury shows it was needed
To limit its role to investigating injuries after they occur

questions.explanation: The employer's responsibility is preventive: a workplace free of recognized hazards, with the training and protective equipment the work requires, provided before harm occurs. Handing employees the program, or acting only after injuries, does not discharge that responsibility.

questions.question: Your conservation reporting shows a large gap between water produced and water billed, but no one knows how much is leakage, meter error, or authorized unbilled use. Which program step do you order as executive?

answers.text: A system water audit that separates real losses from apparent losses and authorized use, so conservation work is aimed at the losses that actually exist
A customer conservation campaign urging shorter showers, sized to close the entire gap, and credit all savings from the campaign against the gap whether or not the gap itself changes
A rate increase that recovers the cost of the unbilled water from billed customers
Replacement of every customer meter in the system before any audit is performed

questions.explanation: A water audit divides the gap into real losses, apparent losses, and authorized unbilled use, and each kind has a different remedy. Option B aims household conservation at a gap that may be mostly leakage or meter error, which household savings cannot close.

questions.question: During a compliance review, the executive finds one entry point where finished groundwater enters distribution is not represented in routine sampling records. What is the correct management response?

answers.text: Backdate sampling records to cover the missing period so the file appears complete when the records are reviewed at the next inspection
Correct the sampling arrangement, document the gap and the fix, and verify the entry point is covered going forward
Average the results from other entry points and report them for this one
Remove the entry point from the system's facility list

questions.explanation: The executive corrects the arrangement, documents both the gap and the remedy, and verifies future coverage. Backdating or substituting other results misrepresents compliance.

questions.question: You are approving the design of a fluoridation installation. Which design feature most directly limits how much fluoride chemical could ever reach the water in a feed malfunction?

answers.text: A second bulk storage tank so more chemical can be kept on site
A day tank sized to hold only a small, bounded supply between bulk storage and the feeder
A larger feeder capable of delivering chemical at several times the normal rate before any further changes are made to the program
A longer feed line between the storage area and the injection point

questions.explanation: A small day tank bounds the inventory available to any single malfunction, so an overfeed event is limited by design. A larger feeder, as in option C, increases the amount that could be delivered in the same failure.

questions.question: Hydrant flow testing across the system is complete for the year. How should the Class A executive use the results at the system level?

answers.text: File the results with the maintenance records for the year, note that the testing requirement has been satisfied, and take no further planning action from the readings
Direct retesting of every hydrant that flowed well, to confirm the favorable readings
Use the flow data to identify areas with deficient capacity and carry those areas into capital planning
Publish the readings to customers as evidence that every part of the system is adequate

questions.explanation: Flow-test data earns its keep when the executive uses it to find capacity-deficient areas and program capital work there. Filing the data unused, or treating favorable readings as proof everywhere is adequate, wastes the program's diagnostic value.

questions.question: Before committing a surface-water system to an alternative disinfectant, a Class A executive designs the pilot study. Which pilot design gives a defensible basis for the adoption decision?

answers.text: Run the pilot for two weeks during the mildest raw-water conditions of the year, when the new process is most likely to perform at its best, as a standing practice for every system the executive oversees
Run the pilot only at average flow, because peak-flow and low-flow performance can be projected reliably from average-condition results
Judge the pilot on finished-water appearance and operator preference, because inactivation and by-product data take too long to accumulate
Run the pilot across the seasonal range of raw-water quality the plant actually faces, measuring inactivation performance and by-product formation throughout, before deciding on full-scale adoption

questions.explanation: An alternative method must be validated under the conditions the system actually faces, including seasonal raw-water variation, with inactivation and by-product performance measured rather than assumed. A short best-case pilot, average-flow-only testing, or appearance-based judgment cannot support a system-wide adoption decision.

questions.question: Why does the sampling program require chain-of-custody documentation?

answers.text: It orders samples alphabetically for the analyst's convenience
It tracks each sample from collection through analysis so the result can be defended as belonging to that sample
It allows samples to be held indefinitely before analysis, in any container, without documenting who handled them during storage or transport
It replaces the need to label sample containers

questions.explanation: Chain of custody documents who held the sample at each step, tying the reported result defensibly to the sample collected. It supports, and never replaces, labeling and timely analysis.

questions.question: An operator files a grievance claiming a supervisor applied the overtime roster unfairly. What is the best executive handling?

answers.text: Listen to the grievance, investigate the roster records and the supervisor's account, decide on the facts, and answer the operator through the established process with the reasons

Deny the grievance immediately to support the supervisor's authority, without examining the roster records, hearing the supervisor's account of how the roster was applied, or giving the operator a chance to present supporting records
Grant the grievance immediately to end the complaint, without any investigation
Ask the operator to withdraw the grievance in exchange for extra overtime

questions.explanation: A grievance is handled by listening, investigating the records and both accounts, deciding on the facts, and answering through the established process. Denying or granting it without investigation protects or pleases one side while teaching both that the process does not matter.

questions.question: A Class A executive oversees several systems whose chiefs sign monthly disinfection records. Which supervision system best protects the record?

answers.text: Chiefs sign records as submitted, trusting each sampler completely and reviewing the underlying field results only if a problem is reported by a customer
The executive personally collects every residual sample at every system, so no chief's verification step is needed in the record chain of records
Chiefs verify field residual results before signing, and the executive spot-checks records and field results across systems on a set cycle
Records are reviewed only when a regulator asks for them, with no routine verification by chiefs or spot-checks by the executive's office during the year

questions.explanation: Verification before signing, backed by the executive's own spot-checks, is the supervision system that catches bad data while it can still be corrected. Signing as submitted removes the control, and collecting every sample personally is neither supervision nor a workable use of the executive's role.

questions.question: A section has a cross-sectional area of 2.15 square feet and the water velocity is 3.1 ft/s. What is the flow in gallons per minute?
questions.explanation: Flow is area times velocity times 448.8: 2.15 times 3.1 times 448.8 is about 2,991.25 gpm. Stopping at cubic feet per second, before the 448.8 conversion is applied, understates the flow.

questions.question: A system treats 2.15 MGD and applies a dose of 1.9 mg/L. How many pounds of chemical are fed per day?

answers.text: 34.07 lb/day
28.5 lb/day
40.85 lb/day
4.09 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day equals 2.15 times 1.9 times 8.34, which is about 34.07 lb/day. The 4.09 figure results from stopping before the 8.34 conversion is applied.

texas-water-operator-class-b.quiz_title: Texas Water Operator Class B Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which set of articles may a candidate use during a Class B computer-based test?

answers.text: Personal notes, a programmable calculator, and a cell phone kept face down on the desk
A textbook, scratch paper supplied by the candidate, and a smart watch worn on the wrist
A pencil or pen, scratch paper provided by the proctor, and a non-programmable calculator
A dictionary, a translator device, and a programmable calculator borrowed from the center

questions.explanation: The articles allowed during the exam are a pencil or pen, scratch paper provided by the proctor and collected afterward, and a non-programmable calculator. Books, notes, phones, and similar devices in the distractor sets are prohibited in the examination room.

questions.question: Before an analyst uses a new laboratory reagent for the first time, what precaution does the safety program require?

answers.text: Testing a drop of the reagent on a small skin area first to check whether it causes any reaction or irritation
Asking a coworker whether the reagent seemed strong last time
Reviewing the reagent's safety data sheet for its hazards, handling, and first-aid information
Diluting the reagent by half so it is safer to handle

questions.explanation: The safety data sheet is the authoritative source for a chemical's hazards, handling precautions, and first aid, and the program requires reviewing it before first use. Guessing from a coworker's impression or diluting the reagent is not a substitute.

questions.question: A chief operator is assigning a week's distribution work: a main repair, routine flushing, meter change-outs, and a storage inspection assist. What supervision principle governs the assignments?

answers.text: Any available employee may be assigned any of the tasks if the chief operator is busy with other duties elsewhere in the system
Tasks are matched to each worker's license and competence, with the chief directing and checking subordinate operators' work
The most senior employee chooses their own tasks and supervises themselves
Contract crews need no direction once their contract is signed

questions.explanation: Employee supervision at the Class B level means matching work to each operator's license and competence and directing and checking subordinate operators' work, including Class C and D staff. Self-assignment and unsupervised contract work abandon that directing duty.

questions.question: Which verification duty belongs to the Class B chief operator before system reports leave the plant?

answers.text: Verifying that sampling results, records, and report entries agree before the report is signed and submitted
Checking that only the final summary page is retained and that all supporting records are discarded as soon as the report is filed
Signing reports prepared by others without reviewing the underlying entries
Having an unlicensed trainee reconcile any differences found in the entries

questions.explanation: The chief verifies that sampling results, records, and report entries agree before a report is signed and submitted. Signing without review passes unverified information forward as if the chief had confirmed it.

questions.question: After a well starts, the discharge runs milky white, then clears from the bottom of a sample glass upward within a minute or two. What is the chief operator actually looking at?

answers.text: Fine silt passing the screen that must be filtered out at the plant
Precipitated hardness forming because the water was warmed in the line, based on the readings recorded in the current operating log
Chlorine gas coming out of solution because the dose is set too high
Entrained air entering through the well or suction side and escaping from the water

questions.explanation: Water that clears bottom-up is shedding tiny air bubbles, which points the chief to air entry at the well or suction side, such as cascading water or a suction leak. Silt and precipitate settle or persist rather than clearing upward in a minute.

questions.question: A Class D operator wants to change a coagulant feed at a surface plant. When may the operator make that adjustment?

answers.text: Whenever the shift log shows a turbidity change
Only after routine weekly approval from any operator while keeping the current settings in place until the next scheduled staff review meeting is held
Only when a Class C or higher surface water operator is present and has issued specific instructions
At any time if the chief is reachable by phone

questions.explanation: A Class D operator may adjust surface treatment only when a Class C or higher surface operator is present and has given specific instructions. A phone call or log entry does not replace that presence and direction.

questions.question: A groundwater system sees a rising pattern of pinhole leaks in customer plumbing and red-water complaints, while its wells produce water the laboratory describes as unstable and corrosive. As chief operator, what program response is appropriate?

answers.text: Advise customers that pinhole leaks are a private plumbing matter only
Increase distribution flushing frequency across the whole system and consider the matter addressed for the year
Direct a corrosion investigation tying corrosiveness measurement of the source water to a control strategy
Replace the system's oldest water mains on an emergency basis

questions.explanation: A system-wide pattern of pinhole leaks and red water tied to unstable, corrosive source water calls for a corrosion investigation and control strategy at the chief's level. Flushing alone does not change the water's corrosiveness.

questions.question: Why can an elevated storage tank maintain distribution pressure during a period when no pumps are running?

answers.text: The tank's altitude valve pumps water uphill into the distribution system
Water stored at elevation flows by gravity, and its height provides the pressure in the system below it
The tank's overflow pipe pressurizes the mains whenever the pumps stop for any length of time during the day or night at the station
Compressed air in the tank expands and pushes water into every main at once

questions.explanation: An elevated tank stores water at height, so gravity delivers it to the system and the height of the water provides pressure while pumps are off. An altitude valve controls filling and draining; it does not pump water.

questions.question: Trihalomethane results are trending upward while distribution residuals are compliant. A staff operator proposes cutting the plant dose below what holds the far-point minima. What does the chief operator direct instead?

answers.text: Approve the cut, because by-product results outrank the minimum residual requirements and the far points can be allowed to run below their minima during the warm months of the year, provided the entry point residual is checked weekly and the change is noted in the operating log

Control formation on the precursor and exposure side, through treatment that removes organic precursors, chlorine optimization, and reduced water age, while still holding every required residual minimum
Stop disinfecting on weekends so the weekly average dose falls, and make up the lost disinfection by feeding a larger dose on Mondays when the plant staff returns to work
Dilute the finished water with an undisinfected purchased supply at the edge of the system to lower the measured by-products, and report the blended results as the system's own

questions.explanation: By-products form from chlorine reacting with organic precursors over time, so the chief attacks precursors, dose efficiency, and water age rather than surrendering the protective residual the rules require. Intermittent disinfection and blending with undis infected water both abandon continuous disinfection.

questions.question: In the plant laboratory, what does ultraviolet absorbance measured at 254 nanometers on a raw-water sample chiefly indicate for the chief operator?

answers.text: A surrogate measure of aromatic organic matter — the precursor load that drives coagulant demand and by-product formation potential
A direct count of coliform organisms in the sample, obtained from the light those organisms absorb as the beam passes through the cell
A direct measure of the sample's hardness, obtained from the calcium and magnesium that absorb the beam in proportion to their concentration
A direct measure of the sample's turbidity, reported in the same units a nephelometer produces when it reads scattered light instead

questions.explanation: Ultraviolet absorbance at this wavelength rises with aromatic organic matter, so the chief reads it as a surrogate for precursor load and tracks its trend for coagulant and precursor-removal decisions. It counts no organisms — bacteriological examination does that — and it is not a hardness or turbidity measurement, which have their own methods.

questions.question: Which setup correctly expresses percent removal across a treatment step?

answers.text: Percent removal equals the outlet value divided by the inlet value, times 100 while keeping the current settings in place until the next scheduled staff review meeting is held
Percent removal equals inlet minus outlet, with no comparison to the inlet
Percent removal equals the drop from inlet to outlet, divided by the inlet value, times 100
Percent removal equals the inlet value divided by the drop, times 100

questions.explanation: Percent removal compares the drop across the step to the starting inlet value, times 100. Using the outlet alone or skipping the inlet comparison misstates performance.

questions.question: A plant treats 0.83 MGD and applies a dose of 2.35 mg/L. How many pounds of chemical per day are required?

answers.text: 13.02 lb/day
16.27 lb/day
19.51 lb/day
1.95 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow in MGD x dose in mg/L x 8.34, so 0.83 x 2.35 x 8.34 = 16.27 lb/day. The 1.95 lb/day figure omits the 8.34 conversion.

texas-water-operator-class-c.quiz_title: Texas Water Operator Class C Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: How does the Class C level differ from Class D in license structure?

answers.text: Class C splits into three separate specialty licenses: Groundwater, Surface Water, and Water Distribution
Class C combines all specialties into a single combined license for the first time at the higher levels of licensing
Class C adds a fourth specialty for wastewater collection systems
Class C keeps one license but adds an endorsement for each specialty

questions.explanation: Class C is where the specialty split begins, with separate Groundwater, Surface Water, and Water Distribution licenses and exams. Class D below it is the single combined license.

questions.question: A coworker suffers a deep cut from a broken fitting and is bleeding heavily. What is the correct first response?

answers.text: Apply firm direct pressure to the wound and get emergency help
Have the coworker walk to the office and rest until the bleeding slows down on its own
Wash the wound thoroughly before applying any pressure
Apply a tourniquet above every bleeding wound first

questions.explanation: Severe bleeding is controlled first with firm direct pressure on the wound while emergency help is obtained. Delaying pressure to wash the wound first allows continued blood loss.

questions.question: Why does a surface water operator expect more day-to-day adjustment than a groundwater operator?

answers.text: Surface water is always cleaner, so adjustments are only for paperwork, regardless of the season, the weather, or the time of day or night
Groundwater changes hourly, while surface water stays constant
Surface water quality changes with weather, runoff, and seasons, so treatment must be adjusted as the source changes
Surface plants are larger, and size alone explains the adjustments

questions.explanation: Surface water characteristics shift with weather, runoff, and season, driving frequent treatment adjustment. Groundwater is comparatively stable, which is the opposite of the pattern in the second option.

questions.question: In the hydrologic cycle, what is transpiration?

answers.text: Water soaking down through the soil and rock layers into an underground aquifer formation
Water vapor cooling and changing into liquid droplets
Surface water turning directly into vapor and rising
Water taken up by plants and released to the atmosphere from their leaves

questions.explanation: Transpiration is the release of water to the atmosphere through vegetation after plants take it up from the soil. Soaking into the ground describes infiltration, a different step in the cycle.

questions.question: You direct operations for a groundwater system with 180 connections that now serves 800 people after a subdivision is added. The operator on site holds a Class D license. What is the correct licensing outcome?

answers.text: The Class D operator remains sufficient because connections stayed below 250
The Class D operator remains sufficient until connections also pass 300
The system needs a Class C-or-higher groundwater operator because it serves 750 or more people
The population figure matters only for surface water systems, not groundwater and note the decision in the plant logbook for the next shift

questions.explanation: The population trigger is independent of the connection trigger: a groundwater system serving 750 or more people requires a Class C-or-higher operator. Staying below 250 connections does not excuse the system once the population threshold is met.

questions.question: Before a gas chlorinator is started up after maintenance, which pair of room safeguards must the operator verify is working?

answers.text: The ventilation system and the chlorine leak detection equipment
The eyewash station and the plant's portable fire extinguisher by the door
The floor drain and the room's overhead lighting
The sample tap and the discharge pressure gauge

questions.explanation: Chlorine gas is heavier than air and hazardous, so ventilation and leak detection are the room safeguards verified before a chlorinator is placed in service. The other items matter for general safety but do not control a chlorine release.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the flocculation step in surface water treatment?

answers.text: To mix chemicals violently so particles dissolve completely, no matter what conditions the plant happens to be facing at the time
To disinfect the water before it reaches the filters
To provide gentle, slow mixing so destabilized particles collide and grow into settleable floc
To settle the heaviest grit before chemicals are added

questions.explanation: Flocculation uses gentle, slow mixing so destabilized particles collide and grow into floc large enough to settle. Violent mixing would shear the floc apart, and disinfection is a separate step.

questions.question: Several customers in one neighborhood report low pressure, but no break has been found. What do you direct the crew to check first?

answers.text: Excavate the largest main in the neighborhood to look for a hidden failure, since no break has shown itself at the surface
Tell customers the pressure is normal for their elevation and close the calls
Replace the booster pumps, since low pressure always means pump failure
Check the storage level, booster pump operation, and whether a valve has been left partly closed

questions.explanation: Low pressure across a neighborhood most often traces to a low storage level, a pump problem, or a partly closed valve, so the directing operator checks those operating causes before assuming a main failure. Excavating or replacing pumps first spends heavily on the least likely cause.

questions.question: A new commercial service will feed a facility whose processes can contaminate its own plumbing. Before continuous service begins, what do you direct?

answers.text: Require the customer to sign a waiver accepting responsibility for any contamination
Direct the crew to install a plain check valve selected from the truck stock and record it in the file as sufficient protection for the service
Require approved backflow protection isolating the premises and an initial test of the assembly before service is activated
Activate service now and schedule any backflow work for the next budget year

questions.explanation: Where an on-site hazard exists, the directing operator protects the public main at the service connection with an approved, tested assembly before the service goes live. Delaying protection, taking a waiver, or substituting an untested plain check valve leaves the cross-connection open.

questions.question: Reviewing a system's disinfectant records, you find the running annual average free chlorine residual in the distribution system has reached 4.3 mg/L. What do you direct?

answers.text: Treat it as an exceedance of the 4.0 mg/L maximum residual disinfectant level, bring the feed down, and verify the average returns below the limit
Take no action, because that limit is judged on a single daily reading and one low reading tomorrow will cancel the high average and replace it entirely
Raise the chlorine feed slightly, because a higher residual always means a larger margin of safety for the distribution system
Recalculate the average using only the entry-point readings, because distribution readings are not the ones the limit is based on

questions.explanation: The maximum residual disinfectant level for free chlorine or chloramine within the distribution system is 4.0 mg/L on a running annual average, so an average of 4.3 mg/L is an exceedance to correct at the feed, not a paperwork problem. The limit is built from distribution readings over the year, so neither a single low day nor an entry-point-only recalculation removes it.

questions.question: Raw water enters treatment at 260 units and finished water leaves at 19 units on the same scale used for a removal check. What is the percent removal?

answers.text: 85.69 percent
89.69 percent
92.69 percent
95.69 percent

questions.explanation: Percent removal is the drop divided by the incoming value, times 100: 241 divided by 260 times 100 equals 92.69 percent. Dividing the drop by the outgoing value instead inflates the result well past the correct one.

questions.question: When computing percent removal across a treatment step, the drop in a substance is compared to which value?

answers.text: The value leaving the step
The average of the entering and leaving values
The value entering the step
The plant's total daily flow

questions.explanation: Percent removal divides the drop by the incoming value, because removal is measured against what the step received. Dividing by the outgoing value overstates the removal percentage.

michigan-real-estate.quiz_title: Michigan Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: For exam purposes, judgment lien is defined as:

answers.text: a lien arising from a court money judgment, attaching to the debtor's property.
a charge against property as security for a debt.
a lien attaching to all of the debtor's property rather than one parcel.
a lien attaching to one particular parcel of property.

questions.explanation: A judgment lien arises when a court awards a money judgment and that judgment becomes a charge against the judgment debtor's property. A generic security charge describes liens broadly, while liens covering all property or only one parcel describe general and specific liens instead.

questions.question: An appraiser adjusts a $360,000 comparable for size: the subject is 200 square feet larger than the comparable, at $100 per square foot, what is the adjusted price?
questions.explanation: Because the subject is larger than the comparable, the comparable's price is adjusted upward: 200 extra square feet at $100 per square foot adds $20,000. Adding that to $360,000 gives an adjusted price of $380,000.

questions.question: An exam question asks for an illustration of seven-day waiting period (TRID). The best answer is:

answers.text: a title company's illegal referral payment to an agent.
a closing delayed because the estimate went out late.
a lender's TILA disclosure package.
an APR disclosure on a loan.

questions.explanation: The waiting-period idea is about timing before a loan may close, so a closing pushed back because the required early estimate went out too late illustrates it. A kickback concerns referral payments, and a disclosure package or APR figure alone does not show a delay caused by a mandatory wait.

questions.question: An exam question asks for an illustration of subordination (lease). The best answer is:

answers.text: a lease recorded after the mortgage.
a drugstore lease with the tenant paying all three.
a retail lease with the tenant paying taxes and insurance.
an apartment lease with utilities included.

questions.explanation: A lease that sits behind the mortgage in priority, as when the lease is recorded after the mortgage, illustrates subordination of the lease to the lien. The drugstore and retail examples describe leases where the tenant pays taxes, insurance, and similar charges, and the apartment example describes a gross arrangement with utilities included.

questions.question: A note has a principal of $16,276 at 6.95% simple annual interest. The interest accruing over 8 months is:
questions.explanation: Annual interest on $16,276 at 6.95% comes to about $1,131.18, and eight months is two-thirds of a year, producing $754.12. Quoting a full year of interest overstates what accrues during the shorter eight-month span.

questions.question: An investor bought a property for $312,750 and later sold it for $389,430 (ignoring costs). The appreciation as a percentage of the purchase price is:
questions.explanation: The property gained $76,680 over its $312,750 cost, and that gain divided by the cost is about 24.52%. Halving or doubling the computed rate, or basing it on the sale price, yields the distractors.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes fireplace disclosure?

answers.text: property with a psychological stigma such as a past crime or death.
chimney and fireplace condition.
a hidden defect not discoverable by ordinary inspection.
a fact that could affect a buyer's decision or the property's value.

questions.explanation: Fireplace disclosure concerns the physical condition of the chimney and fireplace, whether they are safe and functional. Stigma, latent defects, and the general definition of material fact describe other disclosure categories.

questions.question: A home sells for $512,840. The seller pays a 5.5% commission and pays off an existing loan balance of $318,275 at closing (ignoring other costs). The seller's net before other closing costs is:
questions.explanation: Start with $512,840, subtract the 5.5% commission of $28,206.20, then subtract the $318,275 loan payoff, leaving $166,358.80 before other closing costs. Leaving out the commission or the payoff produces the higher distractors.

questions.question: Which term is characterized by the following statement? it includes client follow-up.

answers.text: post-closing
closing day
1031 (practice)
transaction coordinator

questions.explanation: Post-closing work happens after the transaction wraps up, and staying in touch with clients through follow-up belongs to that phase. Closing day names the event itself, while the other labels point to unrelated roles or exchanges.

questions.question: A buyer purchases a home for $438,000 and finances a loan of $359,160. The buyer's down payment percentage is:
questions.explanation: The loan covers $359,160 of the $438,000 price, which is 82 percent financed, leaving 18 percent paid in cash as the down payment. The 82 percent figure is the loan share, not the buyer's contribution, and the other percentages do not match the loan-to-price ratio.

questions.question: A broker sells a rental they own and never mentions being licensed. The licensee-seller must disclose licensed status to the buyer. This situation best illustrates which concept?

answers.text: licensee buying listed property (MI)
personal interest in transaction (MI)
dual capacity disclosure (MI)
licensee selling own property (MI)

questions.explanation: A licensee who sells property they own must reveal that licensed status to the buyer; keeping silent about being licensed is exactly the failure this concept targets. Michigan also requires a licensee-owner to disclose the ownership interest and licensure in writing before an offer is signed.

questions.question: Deed restrictions (MI) is best described as which of the following?

answers.text: Michigan condo buyers should review the master deed, bylaws, budget, and meeting minutes.
Michigan summer resort and park associations are a unique form of seasonal community governance.
Michigan homeowners associations enforce deed restrictions and collect assessments.
Michigan deed restrictions limit how property may be used.

questions.explanation: Deed restrictions are private limits on how a parcel may be used, running with the land through its recorded documents. Reviewing condominium papers, describing seasonal resort associations, and describing association enforcement each touch related structures without defining the restriction itself.

washington-real-estate.quiz_title: Washington Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Regarding estates, ownership forms, and encumbrances, which of the following situations illustrates mineral estate?

answers.text: A court orders a sale in a divorce.
A buyer takes possession before closing with permission.
A widow receives the home for her lifetime.
A developer reserves mineral rights.

questions.explanation: A mineral estate appears when a developer reserves mineral rights, severing the subsurface mineral interest from the surface estate. A court-ordered divorce sale, early possession by permission, and a widow's lifetime interest show other property concepts.

questions.question: Eric Whitfield analyzes a rental with gross income $94,000, 3% vacancy/collection loss, $19,000 other income, and $63,000 operating expenses. Regarding net operating income, what is it?
questions.explanation: Vacancy and collection loss of three percent removes $2,820 from the $94,000 gross income, leaving $91,180, and adding $19,000 of other income gives $110,180. Subtracting $63,000 of operating expenses yields net operating income of $47,180.

questions.question: Regarding debt-to-income ratios, david Bell earns $12,750/month, with housing expense $3,700 and other monthly debts $1,325. Regarding the back-end debt-to-income ratio, what is it?
questions.explanation: The back-end ratio counts all monthly debts, so housing expense of $3,700 plus other debts of $1,325 totals $5,025 in obligations. Dividing $5,025 by monthly income of $12,750 gives a back-end ratio of about 39.4 percent.

questions.question: Omar Young introduced the buyer to the property, but the buyer then signed with another broker who wrote the offer. Regarding procuring cause, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The seller always decides who is paid
Procuring cause never matters
Both brokers are always paid in full
The broker may still be the procuring cause if their actions set off the chain.

questions.explanation: Procuring cause turns on who set in motion the unbroken chain of events that led to the sale, so the broker who introduced the buyer to the property may still qualify. That credit is not lost merely because a second broker later wrote the offer, and it is not decided simply by the seller or split in full between both brokers.

questions.question: Where a buyer wants the seller to credit a leaseback for 30 days after closing, regarding purchase agreements, leases, and multiple offers, which statement of the rule is correct?

answers.text: A contract signed under duress is fully binding.
A leaseback lets the seller remain as tenant after closing.
Oral agreements for the sale of land are fully enforceable.
A counteroffer keeps the original offer alive.

questions.explanation: A leaseback is an arrangement written into the deal that lets the seller stay in the home as a tenant for a set period after closing, here thirty days in exchange for the credit the buyer negotiates. It is a real post-closing tenancy, distinct from duress, from oral land contracts the writing requirement bars, and from a counteroffer, which replaces rather than preserves the original offer.

questions.question: Regarding fiduciary duties and agency relationships, which of the following situations illustrates breach of confidentiality?

answers.text: A seller authorizes the agent to accept $400,000.
A buyer signs an exclusive buyer agency agreement.
An agent commingles the client's deposit.
A broker discloses the seller's motivation to the buyer.

questions.explanation: Confidentiality requires keeping a principal's private information private, and revealing the seller's motivation hands the buyer negotiating information the seller expected to stay protected. Accepting an authorized price, signing an agency agreement, and mishandling a deposit each involve different duties, not this disclosure breach.

questions.question: Regarding seller disclosure duties, which of the following situations illustrates septic condition?

answers.text: A property has a failing septic system.
A seller checks 'unknown' for every item.
A flipper who never lived in the home sells it.
A buyer receives the disclosure and rescinds within 3 business days.

questions.explanation: A failing septic system is a concrete septic condition, a defect in the property's waste-disposal system that a buyer needs to learn about through disclosure. Checking unknown down the whole form or flipping a home are seller behaviors, and rescission after delivery is a remedy, none of which is itself a septic condition.

questions.question: Where a buyer records before the seller's prior mortgage, regarding deeds and recording, which statement of the consequence is correct?

answers.text: The legal description changes by itself.
Timing determines priority.
The grantee owns nothing.
The grantor retains full title.

questions.explanation: Recording order matters because priority among competing interests turns on the timing of recording and notice; a buyer who records promptly protects position against later-recorded claims. The legal description does not rewrite itself, and the grantor does not keep full title after conveying.

questions.question: Regarding code of ethics, a REALTOR who refuses to show homes to buyers of a certain race violates the Code of Ethics, which requires REALTORS to provide equal professional service without discrimination. Regarding the duty, which statement is correct?

answers.text: REALTORS have no such duty
The duty is optional
The duty applies only to clients
REALTORS must provide equal professional service without discrimination.

questions.explanation: Equal professional service is a core ethical duty: a REALTOR must serve buyers of every race on the same terms, without steering or refusal. The duty is mandatory rather than optional, and it extends beyond people who have already become clients.

questions.question: Regarding transfer taxes, peter Reed sells for $740,000 where the transfer tax is $1.5 per $1,000 of sale price. Regarding the transfer tax due, what is the amount?
questions.explanation: At $1.50 per $1,000 of price, a $740,000 sale contains 740 thousands, and 740 times $1.50 equals $1,110. The larger figures come from misplacing the decimal or applying a percentage instead of the per-thousand rate.

questions.question: Regarding Washington license administration, in a situation where a licensee is also an appraiser, which of the following statements is NOT correct?

answers.text: Conflicts must be managed
Roles blend freely
The roles must be kept distinct
Separation is required

questions.explanation: Holding an appraisal credential alongside a brokerage license does not let the two roles blend freely; conflicts must be managed and the roles kept distinct so clients know which capacity the licensee serves. The statement permitting free blending is therefore the incorrect one.

questions.question: Regarding trust accounts, which of the following situations illustrates branch trust supervision?

answers.text: A buyer and seller both claim the $5,000 earnest money.
A managing broker supervises trust handling at a branch office.
A broker refuses a DOL request to examine trust account records.
A broker accepts a promissory note as earnest money with the seller's written approval.

questions.explanation: Branch offices operate under a branch manager who must be a managing broker, and that supervision extends to how trust funds are handled at the branch, under the designated broker's ultimate responsibility for trust administration. Refusing an examination of trust records would be a violation, not supervision.

maryland-real-estate.quiz_title: Maryland Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Seller Steven Young in Annapolis wants to take an item from the bungalow, but the buyer objects. Which of the following is real property the seller may NOT remove?

answers.text: It is personal property the seller may take.
A deck bolted to the house — A permanent improvement; real property.
It is a trade fixture the tenant may remove.
It does not convey unless the deed names it.

questions.explanation: A deck bolted to the house is a permanent improvement and therefore real property, so the seller may not simply remove it after sale. It is neither loose personal property nor a tenant's removable trade fixture, and it conveys even though the deed does not name it item by item.

questions.question: A Towson home's replacement cost new is $380,000, depreciation is 30%, and the site is worth $65,000. The cost-approach value is

answers.text: the land alone.

questions.explanation: Depreciated replacement cost is $380,000 times 70%, which is $266,000, and adding the $65,000 site value gives $331,000 by the cost approach. The $316,000 and $346,000 figures misapply the depreciation or site value, and the land alone omits the improvements.

questions.question: A Ellicott City loan taken by Emily Moore of $217,000 amortizes at $6.32 per $1,000 of loan. What is the monthly principal and interest payment?
questions.explanation: Multiplying 217 thousands by the $6.32 amortization factor gives a monthly principal and interest payment of $1,371.44. The halved figure prices only half the loan, and the largest figure multiplies a monthly payment across a year.

questions.question: Kenneth Moore of Bowie ignores a bounced earnest check; the correct legal result is

answers.text: The seller must close despite the bounced check.
A bounced earnest check must be addressed immediately; the buyer is in breach and the seller has default remedies.
Bounced checks may be ignored.
A bad check satisfies the deposit duty.

questions.explanation: An earnest-money check that bounces must be confronted immediately because the buyer has failed to fund the deposit and is in breach, giving the seller default remedies. Ignoring the bad check does not satisfy the deposit duty, and the seller is not forced to close as if payment had been made.

questions.question: Daniel Rodriguez, studying in Salisbury, reads that 'transaction broker' means: a licensee who assists both sides without representing either, where allowed The term being defined is

answers.text: transaction broker
contingency
competent parties
valid contract

questions.explanation: A licensee who helps both sides complete a deal without representing either one, where that role is allowed, is a transaction broker. Contingencies and competent parties are contract concepts, and a valid contract is the document produced, not the licensee's role.

questions.question: Maria Thomas of Towson tells parties all agencies are irrevocable. What does agency law provide?

answers.text: All agencies are irrevocable once created.
Only a court can end an agency relationship.
Revocability is a basic agency principle; the licensee must correct the misstatement.
Revocation requires the agent's written permission.

questions.explanation: Agency is not permanent by default: a principal can generally revoke the agent's authority, so telling parties every agency is irrevocable misstates the law and no court order or agent permission is ordinarily required to end it.

questions.question: Which statement about lead-based paint disclosure is TRUE?

answers.text: Sellers and landlords of pre-1978 housing must disclose known lead-based paint.
Buyers get no inspection opportunity.
It applies only to commercial property.
It applies to all homes.

questions.explanation: For housing built before 1978, sellers and landlords must disclose known lead-based paint and provide the related information; that duty targets the older housing stock where the hazard is concentrated. It does not extend to every home regardless of age or only to commercial buildings.

questions.question: An Annapolis transfer tax is 1.25% of the $900,000 price. The tax is

answers.text: 1% of the commission.

questions.explanation: The stem fixes the Annapolis transfer tax rate at 1.25%, and 1.25% of the $900,000 price is $11,250. The larger figures come from applying a higher rate than the one given, and the tax is computed on the sale price — not as a percentage of anyone's commission.

questions.question: Which term matches this description? competitors agreeing on commission rates or fees

answers.text: price fixing
RESPA
fair housing
franchise

questions.explanation: Competitors agreeing among themselves on the commission rates or fees they will charge is price fixing, an antitrust violation. It has nothing to do with settlement-procedure law, fair-housing rules, or franchising.

questions.question: A property is worth $572,000. It is encumbered by a first mortgage of $510,000 and a second mortgage of $17,000. What is the owner's equity?
questions.explanation: Equity is what remains of value after debts secured by the property are removed: $572,000 − $510,000 − $17,000 = $45,000. Adding the two mortgages together gives $527,000, which is the total owed, not the owner's stake.

questions.question: A Rockville buyer agency agreement sets the broker's compensation at 3% of the purchase price. The seller offers the buyer's broker 1%. On a $270,000 purchase, the buyer may owe the broker

answers.text: $0 — nothing is owed.

questions.explanation: The buyer's broker is promised three percent of $270,000, or $8,100, while the seller covers only one percent, or $2,700 — leaving the buyer to owe the $5,400 difference under the agreement. The buyer does not owe the full $8,100 because the seller's contribution offsets part of it.

questions.question: Nancy Scott of Cumberland fails to explain dual agency before seeking consent; the written policy manual should

answers.text: stay oral.
be hidden.
cover this area with clear procedures.
omit it.

questions.explanation: Consent to dual agency is meaningful only after the arrangement is explained, so the brokerage manual should set clear procedures for that explanation before consent is sought. A hidden, oral-only, or omitted procedure makes uninformed consent more likely in a relationship Maryland allows only with written informed consent from all parties.

montana-real-estate.quiz_title: Montana Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which concept matches this situation? A city zoning ordinance limiting building heights

answers.text: police power
due process
escheat
a taking

questions.explanation: A city zoning ordinance limiting building heights is an exercise of police power, the government's authority to regulate land use for public health, safety, and welfare. It is not a taking, which requires compensation, nor escheat, which is the state taking property when no owner exists.

questions.question: A licensee gives a buyer written permission to walk the listed acreage. How does it differ from an easement?

answers.text: it creates no property interest and is revocable
no difference
it is a lien
it is stronger

questions.explanation: The walk-on permission differs from an easement because it creates no property interest and is revocable by the owner at will. An easement, by contrast, is an actual interest in the land; the permission is not a lien and is weaker, not stronger, than an easement.

questions.question: In Dillon, Kyle selects comparable sales that are the most recent, proximate, and similar to the subject early in the transaction. Why?

answers.text: the subject is the benchmark; comparables are adjusted to it
market conditions changed between the sale date and the valuation date
differences in rooms affect value
comparables should be recent, nearby, and similar

questions.explanation: Kyle chose comparables that are recent, nearby, and similar because those qualities make a sale a reliable indicator of the subject's value, with adjustments then made to the comparable. A sale chosen for unrelated reasons, such as a change in market conditions alone, would not serve that benchmark role as well.

questions.question: Tom in Helena explains the inspection contingency. Must notice be given?

answers.text: as the contract requires
only the agent
nothing
never

questions.explanation: Rights and duties under an inspection contingency are exercised as the contract requires, including any notice the contract specifies. The contingency is a contract term, so neither silence nor an agent's personal choice replaces its procedure.

questions.question: The photos market the acreage well. What governs drone use?

answers.text: nothing
the Montana Board of Realty Regulation
the MLS
FAA rules

questions.explanation: Commercial drone flights used to photograph and market acreage are governed by Federal Aviation Administration rules. Neither a tax, nor the listing service, nor no authority at all regulates that airspace use.

questions.question: A broker's personal data is breached. What if breached?

answers.text: notify as the law requires
nothing
hide it
notify only the other brokers in the office

questions.explanation: When client data is breached, the broker must notify as the law requires rather than hide the incident or do nothing, because affected people need the chance to protect themselves.

questions.question: While working in Livingston, Omar sees the option holder exercise before the deadline. Another licensee witnesses the conversation. Why?

answers.text: exercise within the period creates a purchase contract
it is triggered only if the seller decides to sell
it binds the seller while the buyer may choose
it employs the broker to market the property

questions.explanation: Exercising an option within its period is the act that converts the option into a purchase contract on the option's terms, obligating both sides to the sale. Before exercise the holder may choose; once exercised on time, the contract exists.

questions.question: A lender quotes 6.5 percent with two points versus 6.875 percent with no points. What tradeoff is shown?

answers.text: a tax
paying points for a lower rate
a scam
nothing

questions.explanation: The lender's two quotes show paying points for a lower rate: paying two points up front buys the rate down from 6.875 percent to 6.5 percent. The tradeoff is higher closing cost now in exchange for lower interest over time, which is a standard pricing exchange rather than a scam.

questions.question: A $400,000 purchase is financed with a $225,000 loan. The down payment is
questions.explanation: Subtracting the $225,000 loan from the $400,000 price leaves $175,000 paid down, and $175,000 divided by $400,000 is 43.75 percent. Pairing that same dollar figure with 21.88 percent understates the share, while $225,000 is the amount borrowed rather than the amount put down.

questions.question: In Kalispell, Omar continues acting for a seller who properly terminated the agreement. May the agent keep acting after proper termination?

answers.text: only to collect commission
yes
only for 30 days
no

questions.explanation: Once the seller has properly terminated the agreement, the agent's authority to act for that seller ends. The agent may not keep representing the seller afterward, whether to pursue a commission or for a short extra period.

questions.question: In Havre, Marcus takes a listing from a tenant purporting to act for an absent owner, without checking. Whose authority counts for listing purposes?

answers.text: the title company
the listing agent's assistant
the owner or someone with legal authority to convey
any interested neighbor

questions.explanation: For listing purposes, authority counts only from the owner or someone with legal authority to convey, so a tenant's unverified claim to act for an absent owner is not enough. A title company, an assistant, or an interested neighbor cannot confer that authority.

questions.question: A power of attorney is arranged. What should the broker do?

answers.text: ignore it
nothing
verify its validity
file it with the county clerk and recorder before any showing

questions.explanation: Before relying on a power of attorney, the broker should verify its validity so the person signing actually has authority to bind the absent party. Ignoring the document risks a closing built on unauthorized signatures.

north-carolina-real-estate.quiz_title: North Carolina Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true of a section?

answers.text: it is a six-mile by six-mile square containing 36 sections
a unit of the government survey system: one square mile containing 640 acres
a township is divided into 36 sections
sections are numbered beginning in the northeast corner of the township

questions.explanation: A six-mile-by-six-mile square containing 36 sections describes a township, not a section. A section is one square mile containing 640 acres, a township is divided into 36 sections, and sections are numbered beginning in the township's northeast corner.

questions.question: Grace Mercer's instructor describes "the status of a tenant who remains after a lease expires without the landlord's consent" Which term is being described?

answers.text: cooperative
estate at sufferance
tenancy by the entirety
separate property

questions.explanation: A tenant who stays after the lease expires without the landlord's consent holds an estate at sufferance, exactly as the stem describes. A cooperative is an ownership form, tenancy by the entirety is a married co-ownership form, and separate property is a classification of ownership, not a holdover tenancy.

questions.question: In a Salisbury office meeting on financing concessions comparables, which statement is true?

answers.text: market value means the maximum imaginable price
financing concessions in comparables require adjustment
mass appraisal values one property
negotiation is irrelevant

questions.explanation: In the sales comparison approach, financing concessions in a comparable sale require adjustment because favorable financing can inflate the price paid. Market value is a probable price under typical conditions, not the maximum imaginable price, and mass appraisal values many properties rather than one.

questions.question: A broker studying appraisal contingency mechanics asks which statement is false. Which is it?

answers.text: the buyer may renegotiate or exit if value falls short
the seller may reduce the price to appraised value
the buyer may add cash to cover the gap
waiver has no consequences

questions.explanation: The false statement is that waiving an appraisal contingency has no consequences; waiving it gives up the protection of renegotiating or exiting if value falls short. The buyer may instead reduce the gap with added cash or the seller may lower the price to the appraised value.

questions.question: David Judd's instructor describes "a licensee treated as self-employed for tax purposes, common for sales agents affiliated with brokers" Which term is being described?

answers.text: earnest money deposit
Americans with Disabilities Act
cloud on title
independent contractor

questions.explanation: The stem describes an independent contractor: a licensee treated as self-employed for tax purposes rather than as an employee of the brokerage. Earnest money, disability law, and a cloud on title are unrelated concepts.

questions.question: An exam candidate reviews seller and broker disclosure duties. Which statement is false?

answers.text: sellers must still be honest
the disclosure does not substitute for inspections
basement water intrusion is material
discovered defects can be ignored

questions.explanation: Discovered defects cannot be ignored; a broker who learns of a material defect such as basement water intrusion must disclose it, and the disclosure form does not substitute for inspections. Sellers likewise must answer honestly even when a disclosure is involved.

questions.question: A loan has a fixed interest rate for five years, then adjusts annually. What type of loan is this?

answers.text: a fixed-rate mortgage
a reverse mortgage
a graduated payment mortgage
a hybrid adjustable-rate mortgage, such as a 5/1 ARM

questions.explanation: A loan that is fixed for an initial period and then adjusts on a schedule is a hybrid adjustable-rate mortgage; the five-year fixed start followed by annual adjustments matches the 5/1 ARM pattern. It is not fully fixed, not a reverse mortgage, and not a graduated-payment loan, whose payments rise on a set schedule.

questions.question: A $170,000 sale in Concord produces a 6% total commission split 50/50 between the firms. How much does the selling firm (the 50% side) receive?
questions.explanation: Total commission is $170,000 times 6 percent, or $10,200. The selling firm's 50 percent share of that commission is $5,100.

questions.question: With respect to tenant placement versus ongoing management, which of the following is accurate?

answers.text: compensation is identical regardless
placement automatically includes full management
placement-only services have a defined limited scope
trust duties apply to neither model

questions.explanation: Tenant placement and ongoing management are different service models: a placement-only engagement has a defined, limited scope that ends with placing the tenant. Placement does not automatically expand into full management, and compensation follows the services actually agreed to.

questions.question: With respect to NCREC audits and investigations, which of the following is accurate?

answers.text: audits are prohibited
cooperation is optional
the Commission can audit trust accounts
records may be withheld

questions.explanation: The Commission can audit trust accounts, and it may inspect trust-account records periodically without prior notice. Cooperation is not optional, and records may not be withheld.

questions.question: An adjustable-rate loan has an index of 4% and a margin of 2.75%. What is the fully indexed rate?

answers.text: 6.75%: the index plus the margin
4%, the index alone
2.75%, the margin alone
1.25%, the index minus the margin

questions.explanation: A fully indexed adjustable rate is the index plus the margin: 4% plus 2.75% equals 6.75%. Using the index alone, the margin alone, or subtracting the margin gives the wrong rate.

questions.question: A broker studying the NC statute of limitations for contracts asks which statement is true. Which is it?

answers.text: attorneys are unnecessary
documentation is irrelevant
the broker should not give legal conclusions
contract claims never expire

questions.explanation: A broker must not give legal conclusions, even when studying time limits for contract claims, because advising on legal rights is the practice of law. Documentation matters, attorneys are sometimes necessary, and contract claims do expire, which is why the broker refers the question instead of answering it.

virginia-insurance.quiz_title: Virginia Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: What single question best separates first-party from third-party bad faith?

answers.text: Was the loss caused by fire or by water, as governed by the policy language applicable to the period in which the event occurred, and as the form itself provides?
Whose claim against whom created the duty — the insured's own benefits claim, or a claim against the insured that the insurer failed to settle?
Did the policy include a deductible?
Was the adjuster a staff employee?

questions.explanation: First-party claims involve benefits owed to the insured; third-party claims involve settling another person's claim against the insured. The adjuster's employment type does not drive the distinction.

questions.question: A business consultant's flawed inventory forecast leads a client to over-order perishable stock that must be discarded. The client has no bodily injury and no damage to tangible property belonging to others, only a pure financial loss. Which coverage is designed for this claim?

answers.text: Commercial general liability insurance, because every business loss is a premises loss
Workers compensation insurance, because the stock belonged to an employer
Commercial property insurance, because discarded stock is always a covered peril
Errors and omissions insurance, because it responds to financial loss from negligent professional advice

questions.explanation: Errors and omissions coverage is built for a client's financial loss caused by negligent advice or services, even without bodily injury or property damage. General liability coverage is generally triggered by bodily injury or property damage, not pure economic loss from advice.

questions.question: A business buys an auto mid-term under a specifically described autos policy and timely asks for coverage on day 12. From what date does the newly acquired auto coverage for that auto run?

answers.text: From day 30, when the reporting window closes
From the acquisition date, because the request was made within the 30-day condition
From the next audit date only
From the date the auto is first driven on a public road

questions.explanation: A timely request within the 30-day condition preserves coverage from the date the business acquired the auto. A late request would not receive that backdating.

questions.question: Under a directors and officers policy, which people are insured in their capacity as leaders of the organization?

answers.text: Customers who bought the company's products last year
Past, present, and duly elected or appointed future directors and officers acting in that capacity
Outside vendors who supply the company's office paper
Shareholders solely because they own one share and never serve

questions.explanation: Individual insureds under directors and officers coverage are the organization's directors and officers, including past and future holders of those roles acting in that capacity. Merely being a customer or vendor does not make a person an insured director or officer.

questions.question: A directors and officers policy has a single $2,000,000 limit shared by its coverage parts. A covered Side C securities settlement of $1,200,000 is paid from that limit. How much of the shared limit remains for other covered claims in the same period, ignoring any retention or defense payments?
questions.explanation: A shared limit is reduced by amounts paid under any part: $2,000,000 minus $1,200,000 equals $800,000 remaining. The settlement does not leave the full limit intact, which is why $2,000,000 is wrong.

questions.question: A building insured for an agreed value of $800,000 suffers a partial fire loss causing $90,000 of damage. What does the agreed value provision do with this partial loss?

answers.text: It pays the full $800,000, because any covered loss triggers the agreed amount
The partial loss is settled on the applicable loss basis for the damage done, not by paying the full $800,000 agreed amount
It pays nothing, because agreed value responds only after the building is repaired and final repair invoices are submitted for the damaged building
It pays $800,000 minus the building's remaining value as a bonus

questions.explanation: The agreed amount is the measure for a total loss; a partial loss is paid according to the damage actually sustained. Paying $800,000 for $90,000 of damage would grossly overcompensate the loss.

questions.question: A regional carrier hauls freight for customers every week throughout the year and wants one cargo arrangement for the continuing flow of loads. Which arrangement matches that need?

answers.text: A trip policy that must be rewritten from scratch after every delivery
A policy that covers only one named load on one named date
A policy that ends automatically when the first shipment is delivered
An annual motor truck cargo policy covering shipments made during the policy period

questions.explanation: An annual cargo policy is designed for a continuing stream of shipments during the year. A trip policy is limited to the single shipment it describes, so it would not fit weekly operations.

questions.question: A producer discovers, before submission, that a client understated the number of wood stoves in a home on a draft application. What action best honors utmost good faith?

answers.text: Submit it as written because the client signed it
Correct the application to state the true number before it is submitted to the insurer
Remove the question from the application
Submit it and correct it only if a fire occurs

questions.explanation: Correcting known false material information before submission upholds the duty of honesty both parties owe. Waiting until after a loss, or submitting a known understatement, breaches that duty.

questions.question: Under a residential NFIP contents policy, covered personal property includes belongings of the named insured and

answers.text: Any neighbor who stored items in the home temporarily
Customers of a business run from the home
The prior owner's property left behind years ago
Members of the insured's household who live at the insured location

questions.explanation: Residential contents coverage extends to the household's own property at the insured location. It is not a catch-all for neighbors' goods or business customers' property.

questions.question: An excess policy lists a specific underlying primary policy that the insured is required to keep in force during the excess policy's term. The insured lets that primary policy lapse and then suffers a loss. What problem has the insured created?

answers.text: The insured may have to bear the underlying layer personally, because the excess policy was priced and written to attach above that primary limit
The loss is automatically uninsured in every possible respect
The excess policy automatically becomes a primary policy at no charge and pays from the ground up at the same premium, deductible, and terms as though the required primary policy were still in force
The former primary insurer must pay even though its policy lapsed

questions.explanation: Excess conditions commonly require maintaining the scheduled underlying coverage. If it is missing, the excess layer still attaches at its stated point and the gap falls on the insured.

questions.question: A tenant's sofa and clothing are damaged by a covered peril inside the insured rental house. The landlord asks whether those items are part of the landlord's Coverage A loss. What is the correct answer?
