answers.text: No, because Coverage A insures the structure, and contents are addressed, if at all, under Coverage C for property the policy covers
Yes, because everything inside the dwelling is Coverage A property, as reflected in the renewal review completed before the expiring policy was extended
Yes, but only up to 10 percent of the Coverage A limit
No, because tenant property is paid under Coverage D

questions.explanation: Coverage A is structure coverage for the dwelling and attached structures, not a contents coverage. Tenant belongings are not the landlord's Coverage A property, and any contents analysis belongs under Coverage C and its covered-property rules.

questions.question: An insurer's direct gross premium income for flood insurance is $8,000. Its assessment for the dam safety and flood protection fund is:
questions.explanation: The flood assessment is 1 percent of flood premium income — $80 here — but when the 1 percent amount is under $100, a contribution of $100 is assessed. All collections go to the dam safety and flood fund.

ohio-insurance.quiz_title: Ohio Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Underinsured motorist coverage has 100/300 split limits. One insured person has $260,000 in bodily injury damages caused by an underinsured driver, before any offset required by applicable rules. What is the most this coverage can pay toward this one person's damages, at the limit-application level?
questions.explanation: At the concept level, uninsured and underinsured motorist bodily injury limits work like split liability limits: a single person's recovery is first measured against the per-person limit. The claim of $260,000 compared with the $100,000 per-person limit gives $100,000; the $300,000 figure is the per-accident total for all persons, not this one person's cap.

questions.question: A homeowner owns a small sailboat and a small outboard fishing boat used only for family recreation. Where is liability for these craft commonly found?

answers.text: Under a personal auto policy, because boats are treated as automobiles on water
Under a liquor liability policy, because marinas often sell fuel
Under the homeowners policy, because small recreational watercraft within its size and power boundaries may be covered there
Under a surety bond posted with the marina

questions.explanation: Homeowners coverage commonly extends liability to small recreational boats within its limits on type, size, and power; an auto policy does not treat a boat as an automobile.

questions.question: A night janitor employed by a cleaning firm under contract, not by the store, steals the store's cash. For the store's Employee Theft agreement, how is the janitor treated?

answers.text: As a non-employee as to the store, so the taking is not Employee Theft under the store's policy
As a custodian, which makes every taking an Employee Theft loss
As a messenger, because the janitor carried keys
As the store's employee, because the theft happened inside the store

questions.explanation: Explanation: Employment is measured against the named insured, so a contractor's worker is not the store's employee for the store's Employee Theft agreement. Location inside the store and carrying keys do not create that employment relationship.

questions.question: A worker's general health insurer suggests it should pay first for emergency care after a clearly covered work injury. Which statement is most accurate?

answers.text: Workers compensation is the source of benefits for covered work injuries, not the worker's general health coverage
General health insurance always pays work injuries before Part One
The worker must exhaust personal health benefits before filing a claim
Part One pays only bills the health insurer has already denied twice

questions.explanation: Part One is the benefit source for work-related injuries and diseases covered by the act. Routing the worker through general health coverage first misplaces a compensable work injury.

questions.question: A home's replacement cost is $500,000, so 80% of replacement cost is $400,000. The owner carries $320,000, and a covered partial loss is $60,000. The actual cash value of the damaged part is $44,000 and the deductible is $1,000. What does the insurer pay under the homeowners greater-of settlement?
questions.explanation: Proportionate share = ($320,000/$400,000) x $60,000 = $48,000, which is greater than the $44,000 ACV, so the insurer pays $48,000 - $1,000 deductible = $47,000. The $59,000 option wrongly grants full replacement cost even though the 80% threshold was missed.

questions.question: A sporting goods store carries a $240,000 business personal property limit and qualifies for the seasonal increase. During peak season, a covered loss totals $275,000, ignoring any deductible. What is the most the insurer will pay for that loss under the increased limit?

answers.text: $240,000, because the stated limit can never change
$264,000, because only a 10 percent increase is allowed
$275,000 plus an added 25 percent bonus on the loss itself
$275,000, because the effective peak-season limit is $300,000 and the loss is below it

questions.explanation: A 25 percent increase on a $240,000 limit produces a $300,000 effective limit, and the $275,000 loss falls below it, so the loss amount is payable subject to other terms. The increase raises the limit rather than adding a bonus to the loss, which is why the bonus option is wrong.

questions.question: An additional insured landlord demands that the tenant's insurer send it all cancellation notices exactly as a mortgagee would receive them, based only on its additional insured endorsement. What is the sound response?

answers.text: No party except the first named insured ever receives any notice for any reason
The landlord is right, but only for renewals, not cancellations
Notice rights for an additional insured depend on what the policy and endorsement provide; the mortgage clause's independent notice promise belongs to mortgagees

The landlord is right; additional insured and mortgagee notice rights are identical in every respect, so the tenant's insurer must give the landlord every notice promise the mortgage clause gives a lender

questions.explanation: A mortgagee's notice promise comes from the mortgage clause itself. An additional insured has only the notice rights its endorsement or the policy actually grants, so the two statuses cannot be treated as identical.

questions.question: An insured incurs $3,500 in covered identity fraud restoration expenses. The endorsement limit is $15,000 and a $250 deductible applies. How much is reimbursed?
questions.explanation: Covered expenses of $3,500 minus the $250 deductible equals $3,250, which is within the $15,000 limit. The limit is a maximum, not the amount paid for every claim.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding superintendent must study UM UIM market availability and competition in Ohio?

answers.text: UM availability is never reviewed by the state
Insurers may refuse all data requests for the study
Reports are prepared by the registrar of motor vehicles
Periodic market studies and reports, backed by insurer data calls

questions.explanation: The superintendent studies availability and competition, issues periodic status reports to state leaders, and may compel insurers and rating organizations to collect and submit the needed data.

questions.question: Which of the following actions, related to no nonrenewal solely because of age, is prohibited under Ohio law?

answers.text: Nonrenewing with proper notice for a permitted reason unrelated to age alone
Charging a lawful rate that reflects filed rating factors
Nonrenewing a policy solely because of the insured's age
Offering a mature-driver course discount

questions.explanation: An insurer may not fail to renew solely because of the insured's attained age.

questions.question: Regarding contempt for disobeying regulator process, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Cancel the investigation automatically
Seek a court order compelling obedience through contempt proceedings
Fine the person without any court involvement
Transfer the inquiry to a private arbitrator

questions.explanation: Enforcement runs through the court of common pleas, which can treat disobedience like disobedience of a court subpoena.

questions.question: An applicant asks a producer about title escrow records must be kept for ten years and accounts opened to oversight. Which response states the Ohio rule correctly?

answers.text: Agents may refuse insurer access to escrow accounts
Only closed accounts are open to oversight
Records may be destroyed after three years
Reasonable account access for the superintendent and represented insurers, with records retained at least ten years

questions.explanation: The agency must allow reasonable access to its escrow accounts and supporting information, and must keep its records for at least ten years after the transactions.

arizona-insurance.quiz_title: Arizona Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A forklift the claimant rented out is struck by the insured's truck and is out of service for repairs for ten days. The rental owner's claim for those ten days is best characterized as what?

answers.text: Bodily injury to the rental company
Damage to electronic data
Loss of use resulting from physical injury to tangible property
Loss of use of property that was not physically injured

questions.explanation: The forklift was physically injured, and the downtime flows from that injury, placing it in the first branch. The second branch is reserved for property that was not physically injured.

questions.question: A claimant is 99 percent at fault for a collision causing $200,000 in damages in a pure comparative negligence jurisdiction. How much can the claimant recover from the defendant who was 1 percent at fault?
questions.explanation: The defendant is responsible for 1 percent of $200,000, which is $2,000, and the pure system lets the claimant collect that sliver. The $198,000 figure reverses the percentages, paying the claimant's own share back to the claimant.

questions.question: What narrow exception allows policy rights to pass without the usual prior written consent?

answers.text: Transfer to a creditor whenever a loan is made
Transfer to a named insured's legal representative upon the named insured's death, until a replacement is appointed or the period ends
Transfer to any buyer of the insured's furniture
Transfer to an employee who uses the insured property of the insured during the policy period, and an employee who regularly uses insured property may take over the policy by assignment

questions.explanation: Death of a named insured triggers the legal-representative exception. A routine sale of furniture does not transfer the policy, making that distractor wrong.

questions.question: An insured negligently strikes a parked car owned by a stranger and also crushes a suitcase the insured had borrowed and was carrying in the trunk. The stranger's car is paid under Part A. How is the borrowed suitcase treated?

answers.text: It is paid on the same basis as the stranger's car
It is paid only under Part D as damage to the insured auto
It is excluded under Part A as property in the insured's care being transported by the insured
It is paid if the suitcase owner gives written permission after the loss

questions.explanation: Explanation: Borrowed property being transported by and in the care of the insured falls within the owned or transported property exclusion, unlike the stranger's car, which is ordinary third-party property damage. Later permission from the owner does not remove an exclusion that applied at the time of loss.

questions.question: A policy has a $25,000 aggregate deductible for the period. Covered claims so far have absorbed $18,000 of it. A new covered claim of $40,000 arises. How much deductible remains to be applied to the new claim?
questions.explanation: The remaining aggregate deductible is $25,000 minus $18,000 already absorbed, which equals $7,000. Only that remainder, not a fresh $25,000, applies to the new claim.

questions.question: Two identical condominium units sit in different buildings. In one building the association documents make owners responsible for interior fixtures; in the other the association insures them. What most determines each owner's Coverage A need?

answers.text: The unit's resale price alone
The association documents and master policy, which allocate which building items each owner must insure
The number of parking spaces assigned to the unit, for purposes of the coverage determination presented in the situation described
The owner's automobile insurance deductible

questions.explanation: Coverage A need follows the legal split of insuring responsibility in the declaration and master policy, not market price or unrelated policy terms. Two physically identical units can need very different limits because that split differs.

questions.question: An insurer finds that predictions for a class become steadier as it goes from insuring a handful of similar delivery vans to insuring many thousands of them. This experience most directly supports which element?

answers.text: A large number of similar exposure units
A catastrophic concentration of exposures
An intentional loss by each insured
An unaffordable premium for each van

questions.explanation: More similar units produce more stable aggregate predictions, which is why a large number of similar exposure units is required. Concentrating catastrophic exposure would work against insurability.

questions.question: An apartment building with a value of $540,000 is subject to 90% coinsurance and is insured for $324,000. A fire causes a covered partial loss of $54,000; the deductible is $1,000. Determine the amount payable.
questions.explanation: Should = $540,000 x 90% = $486,000. Payment = ($324,000/$486,000) x $54,000 - $1,000 = $36,000 - $1,000 = $35,000. The $53,000 option ignores the coinsurance penalty and pays the loss as if the requirement had been met.

questions.question: What is an endorsement in policy structure terms?

answers.text: A verbal assurance from an agent that supplements the contract
A written change to the policy that becomes part of the contract it modifies
A separate policy that replaces the original in all respects
A notice from a third party claiming an interest in the policy

questions.explanation: An endorsement is the written instrument by which policy terms are changed, and once attached it is part of that policy. A verbal assurance is not an endorsement.

questions.question: An insured demands a refund of all premiums after a claim-free policy period, arguing the exchange was one-sided. How does the aleatory nature of insurance answer the demand?

answers.text: The insured is entitled to a full refund plus interest
The insurer must convert the premiums into a savings account for the insured, crediting every premium dollar to an account the insured may withdraw after any claim-free period ends
The exchange was the premium for the insurer's promise and protection during the period, so a claim-free period does not make the contract fail
The policy was void because no loss occurred

questions.explanation: The insured received exactly what was bargained for: the insurer stood ready to pay covered losses throughout the period. Aleatory exchange means an unequal outcome does not undo a valid contract.

questions.question: A landlord is endorsed as an additional insured on a tenant's property policy for the landlord's interest in the building. The tenant's own stock is destroyed by a covered peril. Can the landlord claim payment for the tenant's stock as an additional insured?

answers.text: No, because additional insureds can never present any claim of their own
Yes, if the landlord's name appears before the tenant's on the endorsement
No, the landlord's additional insured interest is the building, not the tenant's stock
Yes, additional insureds share in every property loss under the policy

questions.explanation: Additional insured coverage follows the interest described in the endorsement, here the landlord's building interest. It does not extend to the tenant's separate stock, although an additional insured can claim for loss to its own described interest.

questions.question: What is the statutory fee range for an examination on the laws and one kind of insurance?
questions.explanation: The one-kind examination range is $8 to $25. The $15 to $45 range applies when the examination covers two or more kinds.

cbcs.quiz_title: CBCS Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A patient reviewing a copy of their own billing record tells the billing and coding specialist that a statement shows a service date they believe is wrong, and asks that the record be changed on the spot to match their recollection. Regarding a patient's request to amend their PHI, what is the specialist's best response?

answers.text: Alter the date immediately so the copy matches what the patient remembers
Delete the disputed statement from the record so there is no disagreement

Route the request through the facility's amendment procedure so it can be reviewed against the documentation, explaining that the patient may also submit a statement of disagreement if an amendment is denied
Refuse to note the request anywhere because billing records can never be questioned

questions.explanation: C is correct: amendment requests are reviewed through the facility procedure against the supporting documentation rather than changed on demand, and a patient whose request is denied may place a statement of disagreement in the record. A is wrong because altering a record on recollection alone, without review, undermines record integrity. B is wrong because deleting the disputed entry destroys the record instead of following the amendment process. D is wrong because patients do have a right to request amendment and to have the request addressed.

questions.question: Regarding implied consent in a routine outpatient encounter, which statement best describes how this type of consent is established?

answers.text: The patient presents voluntarily for care and cooperates with routine treatment, so consent is inferred from their actions
The patient signs a detailed form that lists every risk, benefit, and alternative before any care occurs
A family member verbally agrees to treatment on the patient's behalf while the patient is unavailable
The provider documents consent after treatment because the patient was unable to communicate

questions.explanation: A is correct because implied consent is inferred when a patient voluntarily seeks care and cooperates with routine, noninvasive treatment. B is wrong because a signed form detailing risks, benefits, and alternatives describes written informed consent, not implied consent. C is wrong because agreement by a family member describes surrogate or proxy decision-making, not consent implied by the patient's own actions. D is wrong because documenting consent after the fact does not create implied consent, which rests on the patient's conduct before and during care.

questions.question: For one date of service, verified benefits show a $35 copayment for the office visit and, for a separate covered laboratory service with an allowed amount of $400, 10% coinsurance with the deductible already met. Regarding the patient's total responsibility for that date of service, which amount is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct: the patient owes the $35 visit copayment plus 10% of the $400 allowed amount, which is $40, for a total of $75. B is wrong because $40 is only the laboratory coinsurance and omits the visit copayment. C is wrong because $35 is only the visit copayment and omits the laboratory coinsurance. D is wrong because $435 adds the full allowed amount to the copayment instead of the 10% coinsurance share.

questions.question: A batch eligibility file returns results for a clinic session, and one response matches the patient's name but carries a different date of birth and member number than the account it was returned for. Regarding applying batch verification results to accounts, what should the billing and coding specialist do?

answers.text: Hold that result off the account, investigate the identifier mismatch, and re-run verification with the correct subscriber and patient identifiers before relying on it
Post the active status to the account because the name matches
Change the patient's date of birth in the account to match the response
Apply the result to a different patient with a similar name

questions.explanation: A is correct: eligibility results may only be applied when the identifiers match the account; a mismatched date of birth and member number mean the response cannot be trusted for that patient until the discrepancy is resolved and verification is re-run. B is wrong because a name match alone does not establish that the coverage belongs to this patient. C is wrong because the account demographics should be corrected from source documents, not overwritten to fit a mismatched response. D is wrong because applying one person's coverage result to another patient corrupts both accounts.

questions.question: For an office visit being leveled by time, the provider's documented time is 12 minutes reviewing records the day before the visit, 14 minutes face-to-face with the patient plus 6 minutes reviewing results and documenting on the encounter date itself, and 9 minutes coordinating care the day after the visit. How much time counts toward selecting this visit's level by time?

answers.text: 20 minutes, counting only the provider's documented time spent on the encounter date itself
41 minutes, counting the provider's documented time on all three days together
32 minutes, counting the day before and the encounter date but not the day after
29 minutes, counting the encounter date and the day after but not the day before

questions.explanation: A is correct: 14 plus 6 equals 20 minutes, and time-based level selection counts only the billing provider's qualifying activities performed on the calendar date of the encounter. B is wrong because adding all three days (12 + 20 + 9 = 41) counts work done on other dates, which the time rules exclude. C is wrong because the 12 minutes from the day before do not count even though they concerned the same patient. D is wrong because the 9 minutes from the day after likewise fall outside the encounter date and cannot be added.

questions.question: One highly complex, life-threatening procedure requires several surgeons of different specialties working simultaneously, together with specialized staff and equipment, and the record documents why that coordinated team was medically necessary. Regarding the surgeons' reporting for this case, which modifier action is correct?

answers.text: Append the co-surgeons modifier to every claim, because it covers any number of surgeons
Append modifier 66, surgical team, to the procedure on the team members' claims, supported by the documentation of medical necessity
Append the assistant-at-surgery modifier for a nonphysician practitioner to every claim
Report the procedure as unlisted, because no single surgeon performed all of it

questions.explanation: B is correct because modifier 66 identifies surgical team services for highly complex procedures requiring several surgeons and specialized resources, with documentation supporting medical necessity. A is wrong because the co-surgeons modifier describes two primary surgeons sharing one procedure, not a multi-surgeon team case. C is wrong because that modifier describes a nonphysician practitioner assisting at surgery, not the surgical team as a whole. D is wrong because the procedure itself has a code; the team circumstance is conveyed by the modifier, not by abandoning the code.

questions.question: Provider documentation identifies an infectious condition as caused by a specified bacterial organism, and an instructional note for the condition's code directs the coder to use an additional code to identify the organism. Regarding that note, which action follows it?

answers.text: Report the organism code as the principal diagnosis instead of the condition code
Disregard the note, because instructional notes in the Tabular List are optional suggestions
Assign the organism code as an additional code that supplements the condition code by identifying the infectious agent
Assign the organism code only if a second, separate infection is also documented

questions.explanation: C is correct: a 'use additional code' instruction requires a secondary code that adds the organism's identity to the primary condition code, completing the clinical picture the note calls for. A is wrong because the organism code cannot replace the code for the condition being treated as principal. B is wrong because Tabular instructional notes are mandatory conventions, not optional advice. D is wrong because the note is triggered by the documented cause of this infection, not by the presence of another infection.

questions.question: Regarding HCPCS unit reporting, the HCPCS descriptor printed on the encounter states that the drug code reports each 10 mg. The provider documents a single administration of 30 mg of the drug, with none wasted. How many units of the HCPCS code should the specialist report?

answers.text: 1 unit, because the drug was administered only once
10 units, matching the milligram amount in the code descriptor
30 units, matching the total milligrams documented
3 units, because 30 mg divided by the 10 mg descriptor equals 3

questions.explanation: D is correct because HCPCS units are calculated from the code descriptor: 30 mg administered ÷ 10 mg per unit = 3 units. A is wrong because the number of administrations does not set the units when the descriptor is dose-based. B is wrong because 10 is the descriptor increment, not the quotient. C is wrong because reporting the raw milligram total as units would overstate the quantity by tenfold.

questions.question: Regarding the provider signature and date entered on a CMS-1500 before submission, what does that signature assure?

answers.text: That the patient has already paid their full balance for the visit
That the services were rendered as reported and the information on the claim is attested to by the provider or supplier
That the payer has guaranteed payment at the billed charge
That the patient's authorization to release information is no longer needed

questions.explanation: B is correct because the provider or supplier signature attests that the services shown were provided as billed and that the claim information is true. A is wrong because the signature does not record patient payment. C is wrong because a signature cannot guarantee how a payer will adjudicate the claim. D is wrong because the patient's release authorization is a separate patient signature function and is not cancelled by the provider signature.

questions.question: A claim is denied with reason code CO-29, stating the time limit for filing has expired. The practice's clearinghouse report shows the claim was transmitted before the deadline, but it was rejected for a data error and never corrected until after the deadline. Regarding this timely-filing denial, what is the strongest resolution path?

answers.text: Bill the patient in full because the deadline has passed
Submit a new claim with a different date of service inside the filing window
Gather the transmission and rejection history and appeal with proof of the original timely submission, explaining the rejection, per the payer's timely-filing appeal process
Write off the balance without checking the submission history

questions.explanation: C is correct because documented proof of a timely original transmission, presented through the payer's appeal process, is the legitimate basis for overturning this denial. A is wrong because shifting a practice follow-up failure to the patient is improper where the original filing was timely. B is wrong because changing the date of service misrepresents when care occurred. D is wrong because it forfeits a recoverable claim without reviewing evidence the practice already holds.

questions.question: Using the National Physician Fee Schedule amount given in a payer's pricing screen, the allowed amount for a service is $150 and the payer pays 80% of the allowed amount after the deductible has been met. Regarding the expected payer payment, what amount should the billing and coding specialist anticipate?
questions.explanation: D is correct because 80% of the $150 allowed amount equals $120. A is wrong because $150 is the full allowed amount before the payer's 80% payment percentage is applied. B is wrong because $30 is the remaining 20% coinsurance share, not the payer's payment. C is wrong because $80 confuses the payment percentage with a dollar amount and does not follow from the figures given.

questions.question: A charge-capture review finds the same pattern across many encounters for one service line: a documented administration service is repeatedly missing from encounter forms, while the related product charge is captured. Which response addresses the pattern within timely-filing limits?

answers.text: Treat each omission as isolated and make no changes
Correct the affected accounts where documentation supports the charge and filing deadlines allow, and fix the encounter-form or workflow step causing the omission
Backdate new encounter forms so the missed charges appear original
Add the administration charge to future encounters whether or not it is documented

questions.explanation: B is correct because a repeated omission is a process defect: supported charges on affected accounts are corrected while timely filing still allows, and the form or workflow causing the pattern is fixed. A is wrong because identical repeated omissions show a systemic problem that will keep recurring if ignored. C is wrong because backdating forms falsifies the charge-capture record. D is wrong because charges may only be captured when the service is documented for that encounter.

cehrs.quiz_title: CEHRS Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Regarding a vendor update that must be withdrawn shortly after go-live, which information should the specialist's rollback notice contain?

answers.text: Only the vendor's apology, with no practice-specific instructions
That the update is being reversed, when the reversal occurs, which workflow returns to its prior steps, and what users should do with work started under the update
A statement that nothing has changed, so users do not become confused
Technical server details that only information technology staff can act on

questions.explanation: B is correct: when an update is withdrawn, users need to know the change is reversing, the timing, which workflow steps return, and how to handle work already started, so they do not keep following withdrawn steps. A is wrong because an apology gives users no instructions for their work. C is wrong because the workflow is changing back, and denying it leaves users following the wrong steps. D is wrong because server detail does not tell end users what to do in their own workflow.

questions.question: The EHR specialist has charts for two different patients open in separate tabs and is about to enter information from the current encounter. Applying identifier verification at the point of documentation, what should they do first?

answers.text: Enter the information in the tab that was opened first and sort out any mismatch later
Rely on the appointment reason shown in the schedule to decide which tab to use
Check the identifiers in the header of the active chart against the patient and encounter in front of them, and document only when they match
Close both charts and re-enter the information from memory after the visit ends

questions.explanation: C is correct: with more than one chart open, verifying the active chart's header identifiers against the patient and encounter in front of them is what prevents documenting in the wrong record. A is wrong because tab order says nothing about which patient the information belongs to, and later cleanup cannot undo a wrong-chart entry reliably. B is wrong because a visit reason can be shared by many patients and does not identify a chart. D is wrong because documenting from memory after the visit invites errors and still does not verify the chart.

questions.question: Several devices in the inventory are leased rather than owned, and the lease term for a group of workstations is ending. Analyzing the inventory's role in the lease return, which use of the inventory is best?

answers.text: Return whichever workstations are oldest, regardless of what the inventory shows
Keep the leased workstations in service past the term because they still work
Use the inventory's ownership, serial number, and location details to identify exactly the leased units due back, verify each unit against the lease list, and document their removal from service
Delete the leased units from the inventory as soon as the term ends, before they are collected

questions.explanation: C is correct: the inventory's ownership and identifying details pinpoint exactly which units are leased and due for return, each is verified against the lease list, and removal is documented as it happens. A is wrong because age does not determine lease status, and returning owned units by mistake is a real loss. B is wrong because retaining leased equipment past its term breaches the lease arrangement. D is wrong because deleting records before collection erases accountability for devices still on the premises.

questions.question: At today's visit, a patient describes their pain in their own words, giving a number on the pain scale plus the quality and location of the pain. Regarding entering that assessment in real time, what should the EHR specialist do?

answers.text: Convert the patient's report into the severity category the specialist considers most accurate and chart only that category
Enter the reported score, quality, and location in the structured pain fields as the patient stated them, without substituting the specialist's interpretation
Chart only the number, discarding the patient's descriptive words as non-clinical
Ask the patient to choose a different number that better matches the practice's pain poster

questions.explanation: B is correct: pain is a patient-reported measure, and the structured entry must preserve the score, quality, and location the patient actually reported so later comparisons reflect the patient's experience. A is wrong because recategorizing the report substitutes the specialist's judgment for the patient's own assessment. C is wrong because quality and location are clinically useful parts of the assessment, not noise. D is wrong because coaching a patient to a different score corrupts the measurement.

questions.question: An immunization record transferred from another clinic includes the vaccine, the date given, and the lot number. Regarding documenting that historic immunization, what should the EHR specialist enter?

answers.text: Only the vaccine name, because lot numbers are billing details
The vaccine, date administered, and lot number in the immunization record, along with the source of the information, so the entry is complete and traceable
The lot number in the allergy section so it is easy to find
A note that an immunization probably occurred, without dates or lot details

questions.explanation: B is correct: a complete historic immunization entry preserves the vaccine, administration date, and lot number — the lot number lives in the immunization record — with the source identified for traceability. A is wrong because lot numbers support safety recalls and verification, not billing. C is wrong because lot information filed under allergies misplaces the data and implies a reaction that did not occur. D is wrong because a vague note without the available specifics wastes verified source information.

questions.question: Concerning what point-of-care EHR support includes during a live encounter, which description is most accurate?

answers.text: It is limited to resetting passwords and replacing workstation hardware
It helps the user navigate the chart, locate data, and work through system problems in the moment, while the clinician keeps authorship of the clinical content
It means the specialist reviews every closed chart at the end of the day for billing errors
It transfers the encounter note to the specialist whenever the clinician falls behind

questions.explanation: B is correct: point-of-care support is in-the-moment help with navigation, data location, and system use during care, and the clinician remains the author of the note. A is wrong because password and hardware work is general IT support, not the full point-of-care role. C is wrong because end-of-day chart review is a monitoring function, not support during the encounter. D is wrong because support never transfers authorship of clinical documentation to the specialist.

questions.question: As a medication is being entered during a visit, the EHR fires an allergy alert tied to the patient's recorded allergies. Regarding the specialist's response to that alert, what is correct?

answers.text: Override the alert quietly so the visit is not interrupted
Stop, bring the alert to the provider's attention, and let the provider decide how to proceed while the alert and response remain part of the record
Delete the allergy from the chart so the alert stops appearing
Change the medication entry to a similar drug the specialist prefers

questions.explanation: B is correct: an allergy alert is a safety signal for the ordering clinician; the specialist surfaces it and the provider — not the specialist — decides the clinical response. A is wrong because overriding a safety alert to save time defeats its purpose and exceeds the specialist's role. C is wrong because removing a recorded allergy erases safety information and can cause harm. D is wrong because substituting a different drug is a prescribing decision outside the specialist's scope.

questions.question: A scheduled imaging service has an allowed amount of $180 in the EHR. The patient's verified benefits show the deductible is already fully met, and the patient pays 25% coinsurance on the allowed amount for this service. Regarding the estimated patient cost for this service, which amount should the specialist provide?

answers.text: $0, because the deductible has been met

questions.explanation: A is correct: with the deductible met, only coinsurance applies, and 25% of $180 is $45, which is the patient's estimated cost for the service. B is wrong because $180 is the full fee schedule amount before the plan's payment is considered. C is wrong because $135 is the payer's 75% share, not the patient's share. D is wrong because meeting a deductible does not eliminate coinsurance; the patient still owes the coinsurance percentage.

questions.question: For an upcoming service, the allowed amount in the EHR is $240, the patient's verified benefits show $90 of deductible remaining, and after the deductible the patient pays 20% coinsurance on the rest of the amount. Regarding calculating the estimated patient cost from those figures, which amount is correct?

answers.text: $240, because the patient owes the full fee schedule amount
$90, because only the deductible counts toward the estimate
$30, because only the coinsurance counts toward the estimate
$120, from the $90 deductible plus 20% of the remaining $150, which is $30

questions.explanation: D is correct: the patient first owes the $90 of remaining deductible, and 20% coinsurance on the remaining $150 ($240 minus $90) is $30, so the estimate is $90 plus $30, or $120. A is wrong because it ignores the payer's payment of the portion above the patient's deductible and coinsurance share. B is wrong because it omits the coinsurance the patient owes after the deductible is met. C is wrong because it omits the deductible the patient must pay before coinsurance applies.

questions.question: Shortly after a documentation template update, an incentive-program measure that had been stable drops sharply, while staff report the underlying care has not changed. What should the EHR specialist do to address the reporting problem?

answers.text: Accept the lower rate as the new baseline without investigating, since rates fluctuate
Restore the rate by editing past encounter records to match the new template
Validate the measure by checking whether the updated template still captures the required element in the fields the reporting logic reads, and escalate a capture defect through the EHR change process
Stop submitting that measure until the next template update is released

questions.explanation: C is correct: a sudden drop after a template change, with care unchanged, points to a data-capture problem, which is found by validating the fields the reporting logic reads and fixing the build through change control. A is wrong because accepting an unexplained drop leaves a likely system defect distorting reported performance. B is wrong because editing past records to fit a template alters the legal record to fix a reporting artifact. D is wrong because withholding a required measure does not fix the capture problem and creates a compliance gap.

questions.question: Concerning backups as part of EHR downtime and recovery readiness, which statement is correct?

answers.text: A backup is useful only for records older than one year that are no longer opened
Backups need to be made only after a system failure has already occurred
Data should be backed up on a regular schedule using approved methods, and recovery should be tested so records can actually be restored after a failure
Keeping one staff member's handwritten summary is an adequate substitute for system backups

questions.explanation: C is correct: scheduled backups with tested restoration are what make recovery possible after a failure or downtime event. A is wrong because current, active records are the ones most needed immediately after a failure. B is wrong because a backup created after a failure cannot restore data that was lost in that failure. D is wrong because a personal summary is incomplete, uncontrolled, and cannot restore the EHR's data.

questions.question: Following a contract renegotiation, a finance director asks a one-time question: how much was written off as contractual adjustments for one payer during the first month under the new contract, a breakdown no standard report provides. How should the EHR specialist produce that information?

answers.text: Run the standardized carrier report for the full year and highlight the payer's rows
Build an ad hoc financial report querying the payer, adjustment, and date fields for that payer and that month
Wait for the next standardized report cycle in case the breakdown is added then
Send the aging report, since adjustments reduce the balances it shows

questions.explanation: B is correct: an ad hoc financial report is built for a specific nonroutine question by querying the EHR fields the question defines — here payer, contractual adjustment amounts, and the dates of the first contract month. A is wrong because a full-year standardized report buries the one-month figure in excess data and does not isolate adjustments. C is wrong because a standardized cycle may never add this one-time breakdown. D is wrong because an aging report groups unpaid balances by age and does not report adjustment amounts for a payer.

cmaa.quiz_title: CMAA Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: When a patient checks in, the practice's system displays an alert that the patient is due for a preventive screening the provider tracks annually, and it flags the chart for the care team. Regarding EHR components, which function produced this alert?

answers.text: The audit trail, which logs every user who viewed or edited the chart
The electronic prescribing function, which transmits prescriptions to a pharmacy
The clinical decision support and health maintenance function, which flags care that is due
The demographics module, which stores the patient's contact and insurance information

questions.explanation: C is correct: decision support and health maintenance functions track preventive care that is due and alert the team at the point of service. A is wrong because an audit trail records access history; it does not generate due-care alerts. B is wrong because electronic prescribing sends medication orders to pharmacies and is unrelated to screening reminders. D is wrong because the demographics module stores identifying and insurance details rather than evaluating clinical due dates.

questions.question: A provider's preparation sheet for a scheduled test tells patients to ask the provider's office about any medicines they take before the test. The patient asks the assistant directly, 'Should I stop taking mine before the test?' Analyzing the assistant's scope, what is the correct response?

answers.text: Advise the patient to stop the medicine to be safe
Advise the patient to keep taking the medicine, since stopping is riskier
Decline to advise on stopping or continuing, route the question promptly to the provider or clinical staff, and document that the question was referred
Tell the patient to decide based on how they feel on the day of the test

questions.explanation: C is right because whether to stop a medicine is a clinical decision; the assistant's role is to connect the patient with the provider, as the sheet itself directs, and record the referral. A is wrong because advising a stop is a clinical judgment outside the assistant's scope and could cause harm. B is wrong for the same reason in the opposite direction. D is wrong because it leaves a clinical decision to guesswork instead of the provider.

questions.question: An upset patient moves from raised voice to profanity and a statement that staff 'will be sorry.' The assistant's de-escalation attempts are not working. Which response best fits this point in the encounter?

answers.text: Set a calm, clear boundary about acceptable language, disengage from the argument, and alert the supervisor and follow office safety procedures
Continue debating the original complaint until the patient runs out of energy
Respond with sarcasm so the patient realizes how unreasonable they sound
Physically block the doorway so the patient cannot leave before the issue is settled

questions.explanation: A is correct because once language turns threatening, staff safety governs: a firm boundary, disengagement, and immediate involvement of supervision follow established safety practice. B is wrong because continuing to argue with a threatening person prolongs exposure and rarely resolves anything. C is wrong because sarcasm is provocative and unprofessional. D is wrong because physically blocking or restraining a patient is dangerous and far outside the assistant's role.

questions.question: Regarding disclosures to family members, a patient is present in the exam area and tells the assistant, in front of their adult child, that it is fine to go over the appointment summary together. The assistant must decide how much may be shared. Which approach is correct?

answers.text: Share nothing, because family members may never hear PHI under any circumstance
Share the patient's full lifetime record, because permission was given once
Refuse until the adult child provides written proof of the relationship
Share the information relevant to the current visit, consistent with the patient's stated agreement

questions.explanation: D is correct: when a patient is present and agrees, information relevant to the person's involvement in the patient's care may be shared, limited to what fits that agreement. A is wrong because the Privacy Rule does allow sharing with family when the patient agrees or does not object. B is wrong because a one-time verbal agreement about a visit summary does not open the entire lifetime record. C is wrong because written proof of relationship is not required when the patient personally confirms the arrangement.

questions.question: Regarding mobile-device safeguards, the assistant realizes at the end of the day that a work tablet used for patient check-in cannot be found. What should the assistant do first?

answers.text: Wait a full week to see whether it turns up before saying anything
Buy a replacement tablet so the loss is not noticed
Assume no risk exists, because check-in tablets hold no clinical notes
Report the loss immediately to the supervisor or privacy officer so the device can be located, locked, or wiped and the incident assessed

questions.explanation: D is correct: a missing device that may hold PHI is a potential security incident and must be reported at once so safeguards such as remote lock or wipe and a risk assessment can begin. A is wrong because delay lets any exposure continue and weakens the response. B is wrong because quietly replacing the device hides an incident that must be documented and evaluated. C is wrong because check-in devices can hold names, appointment details, and other identifiers, which are PHI even without clinical notes.

questions.question: For a school-physical block scheduled from 9:00 a.m. to noon, each physical is allotted 30 minutes and the block is booked back to back with no gaps. How many patients can the medical administrative assistant book into this block?

answers.text: Five patients
Six patients
Seven patients
Nine patients

questions.explanation: B is correct: the block runs 3 hours, which is 180 minutes, and 180 minutes divided by 30 minutes per physical gives 6 patients booked back to back. A is wrong because five patients would use only 150 minutes and leave half an hour of the block unbooked. C is wrong because seven patients would need 210 minutes, half an hour more than the block contains. D is wrong because nine patients would need 270 minutes, which is the answer obtained by dividing by 20 minutes rather than the allotted 30.

questions.question: A service runs a morning clinic made up almost entirely of brief, highly predictable three-to-five-minute injections, and keeping patients moving on a precise timetable matters more than absorbing unpredictable visit lengths. Which scheduling system best fits this clinic?

answers.text: Wave scheduling, with all morning patients arriving at the top of the first hour
Open booking, with patients arriving whenever they choose during the morning
Double booking every slot, so two injection patients share each time
Time-specified scheduling, with each patient given their own exact appointment time

questions.explanation: The key is right because time-specified scheduling assigns each patient a specific time and fits brief, predictable visits where a precise timetable can actually be kept. A is wrong because wave scheduling is designed to absorb variable visit lengths by front-loading arrivals, which this predictable clinic does not need. B is wrong because open booking gives up the precise timetable the clinic is trying to maintain. C is wrong because double booking is for interleaving a brief visit into another visit's waiting time, not for pairing identical short visits that both need attention at once.

questions.question: With the deductible confirmed as met, a plan pays 80% of the allowed amount while the patient pays 20% coinsurance. An outpatient service has an allowed amount of $600. Regarding the patient's coinsurance for this service, what is the amount?

answers.text: $480, because the patient pays the plan's 80% share when the deductible is met
$120, because 20% of the $600 allowed amount is the patient's share
$600, because coinsurance means the patient pays the entire allowed amount
$20, because the coinsurance percentage itself is collected as a flat dollar amount

questions.explanation: B is correct: with the deductible met, coinsurance is the stated percentage of the allowed amount, and 20% of $600 is $120 owed by the patient while the plan pays the remaining $480. A is wrong because $480 is the plan's 80% share, not the patient's 20% share. C is wrong because coinsurance is a shared percentage, not full payment of the allowed amount. D is wrong because 20% is a rate applied to the allowed amount, not a $20 flat fee.

questions.question: After completing intake forms through the patient portal the night before a visit, a patient arrives expecting a shorter check-in. Regarding completion of required intake for this visit, what should the assistant do?

answers.text: Hand the patient the full paper packet anyway, because portal submissions never count toward required intake
Confirm the portal forms are present and complete in the record, verify identity and demographics, obtain any missing signatures or acknowledgments, and then proceed with check-in
Assume every required form was completed correctly online and skip reviewing the submission entirely
Delete the portal submission and have the patient restart intake so the paper trail stays uniform

questions.explanation: B is correct because portal-submitted intake counts when it is actually in the record, so the assistant confirms completeness, verifies identity and demographics at arrival, and collects only what is still missing, such as a required signature or acknowledgment. A is wrong because completed portal intake does not need to be duplicated on paper. C is wrong because assuming completeness without review risks a missing required form reaching the encounter. D is wrong because deleting a valid submission wastes the patient's completed work and creates extra burden with no benefit.

questions.question: Regarding what makes a claim a clean claim at submission, which description is accurate?

answers.text: A complete and accurate claim with all required fields and supporting information, able to pass payer edits without correction
Any claim that is submitted on the same day the patient was seen
A claim the payer has already paid in full
A claim submitted on paper rather than electronically

questions.explanation: A is correct because a clean claim is defined by completeness and accuracy at submission, so it passes edits and is processed without needing correction. B is wrong because same-day submission says nothing about whether the claim's fields are complete or correct. C is wrong because payment is the outcome of processing, not the definition of a clean claim at submission. D is wrong because the submission medium does not determine cleanliness; an electronic claim can be incomplete and a paper claim complete.

questions.question: Regarding petty cash control, a staff member asks the assistant to hand over $20.00 from the fund and leave a signed personal IOU in the box instead of a receipt. The correct response is to:

answers.text: Accept the IOU as a voucher because it is signed
Take the $20.00 from the day's cash collections instead
Decline to disburse on an IOU alone and require the approved voucher-and-receipt process for the purchase
Count the IOU as cash on hand so the box still balances at reconciliation

questions.explanation: Every petty cash disbursement must be supported by an approved voucher with a receipt for an actual practice purchase; an IOU is not documentation of an expense, so the assistant declines and routes the request through the proper process. A is wrong because a signature alone does not turn a personal loan into a documented disbursement. B is wrong because patient collections are never a substitute fund and must be deposited intact. D is wrong because counting an IOU as cash conceals a shortage rather than reconciling the fund.

questions.question: A stack of loose result reports is ready to be scanned into electronic charts. Regarding the check the medical administrative assistant performs before scanning each report into a chart, what is the correct practice?

answers.text: Match the report to the chart using the patient's surname alone
Verify at least two patient identifiers on the report against the chart so the result is filed for the correct patient
Scan all reports into the most recently opened chart and sort them later
Hold the reports until the patient confirms which chart they belong in

questions.explanation: B is correct: verifying at least two identifiers before filing prevents results from entering the wrong patient's record. A is wrong because a surname alone is not sufficient and names are commonly shared. C is wrong because bulk-scanning into one chart guarantees misfiles that compromise record accuracy and safety. D is wrong because filing is matched against record identifiers by staff, not deferred to patient confirmation.

part-107.quiz_title: Part 107 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A crew attaches an external sensor pod to an aircraft with a loose strap. During a test hover, the pod shifts and the aircraft's handling changes noticeably. What does the preflight rule require?

answers.text: The pod is acceptable because it stayed attached during the hover

Before flight, the remote pilot in command must ensure that any object attached to the aircraft is secure and does not adversely affect the flight characteristics or controllability of the aircraft, so this installation must be corrected
The pod may be carried if the visual observer holds a backup strap ready
The pod may be carried only on flights shorter than 10 minutes

questions.explanation: Prior to flight, the remote pilot in command must ensure that any object attached or carried by the small unmanned aircraft is secure and does not adversely affect the flight characteristics or controllability of the aircraft; a pod that shifts and changes handling fails both halves of that test and must be fixed before flight. Staying attached during one hover does not show the load is secure or that handling is unaffected. A crew member's readiness does not restrain the load in flight. Flight duration does not excuse an installation that degrades controllability.

questions.question: A drone strikes a client's parked vehicle. Repair of the vehicle, which was not the drone, is estimated at $650, and no one is hurt. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: No report is ever required when there are no injuries
A report to the FAA is required within 10 calendar days because damage to property other than the small unmanned aircraft exceeds $500
A report is required only if repair exceeds $5,000
A report is required only if the drone itself costs more than $500 to repair

questions.explanation: Property damage of at least $500 to property other than the small unmanned aircraft triggers the 10-calendar-day accident report, even without injuries. The threshold is $500, not $5,000. Damage to the small unmanned aircraft itself is excluded from that property-damage calculation, so the drone's own repair cost is not the test here. The $650 vehicle repair satisfies the trigger.

questions.question: A receiver application displays the altitude reported by a standard remote identification aircraft. Which altitude does the broadcast message element report for the aircraft?

answers.text: The aircraft's height above the launch point, expressed as a radio altimeter reading
The geometric altitude of the unmanned aircraft
The pressure altitude assigned by air traffic control for the flight
The altitude of the control station repeated a second time

questions.explanation: Standard remote identification broadcasts an indication of the geometric altitude of the unmanned aircraft, alongside its latitude and longitude, and separately reports the geometric altitude of the control station. A height above the launch point or a radio altimeter reading is not the defined element. Air traffic control does not assign altitudes to these broadcasts. The aircraft's altitude element is the aircraft's own, distinct from the control station element reported with it.

questions.question: A university team wants to test a prototype aircraft without remote identification as part of a genuine aeronautical research program. What pathway does part 89 provide?

answers.text: Operations conducted for aeronautical research may be excepted from remote identification when they comply with the conditions part 89 sets for such operations, including operating within a FRIA or under an FAA authorization as applicable
None; research aircraft must always broadcast remote identification
Any flight labeled research is automatically excepted with no conditions
Research operations are excepted only if the aircraft weighs more than 55 pounds

questions.explanation: Part 89 excepts certain operations from remote identification, including operations for aeronautical research and operations to show compliance with requirements, when conducted under the conditions the rule prescribes, such as within an FAA-recognized identification area or as otherwise authorized. The exception is real but conditional, so a bare research label is not enough, and it has nothing to do with aircraft over the 55-pound part 107 ceiling.

questions.question: Mid-flight, a client urges the remote pilot in command to keep filming even though a crewed helicopter is approaching the work area. Who has final authority and direct responsibility for the operation?

answers.text: The remote pilot in command
The client paying for the job
The visual observer, in all cases
The helicopter pilot, for every decision about the drone flight

questions.explanation: The remote pilot in command is directly responsible for, and has final authority over, the operation of the small unmanned aircraft system. A paying client cannot override safety or regulatory duties. A visual observer supports the operation but does not automatically assume that authority. The helicopter pilot controls the helicopter, while responsibility for the drone's operation remains with its remote pilot in command.

questions.question: A company produced a declared model for operations over people and stopped producing it in March 2024. In January 2026, the FAA asks for the information that supported the declaration. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The company may refuse because all record duties ended the day production stopped
The company must produce the records only if it resumes production

The company must retain the supporting information for two years after cessation of production and make it available to the Administrator on request, so the January 2026 request is within the retention period
The company could lawfully have destroyed the records after 90 days

questions.explanation: A person who produces a small unmanned aircraft system covered by a declaration of compliance must retain the information supporting the declaration for two years after cessation of production of that system and make it available to the Administrator upon request. Ending production starts the two-year clock rather than ending the duty at once, the duty does not depend on resuming production, and a 90-day destruction period is far shorter than the required retention.

questions.question: A remote pilot reviewing the general airspace structure for a high-altitude balloon-recovery planning exercise asks what class of airspace lies above flight level 600. The correct answer is

answers.text: Class A, which extends upward without limit
Class G, because controlled airspace ends at FL600
No airspace classification applies above FL600
Class E airspace

questions.explanation: Airspace above FL600 is classified as Class E airspace. Class A airspace tops out at FL600 rather than extending without limit. Class G is uncontrolled airspace found below controlled-airspace floors, not above FL600. The classification structure does apply above FL600, and it assigns that region to Class E.

questions.question: (Scenario) A sectional chart shows a blue-hatched area labeled with a P number over a sensitive federal installation, and a client asks a remote pilot to overfly it at 200 feet AGL with the landowner's written consent. Which response is correct?

answers.text: The flight may not be conducted; a prohibited area bars flight of aircraft, and neither landowner consent nor an ATC authorization opens it
The flight may be conducted with the landowner's consent alone
The flight may be conducted if LAANC grants an automated authorization for the site
The flight may be conducted below 400 feet AGL because prohibited areas protect only high-altitude traffic

questions.explanation: A prohibited area is established for security or national welfare reasons and flight within it is prohibited, full stop. Consent from a surface landowner does not lift a federal airspace prohibition, LAANC authorizations address controlled airspace rather than prohibited areas, and the prohibition is not limited to high-altitude traffic.

questions.question: (Scenario) An airport has a field elevation of 3,850 feet, the altimeter setting is 29.52 inches, and the outside air temperature is 33 degrees Celsius. Using a pressure altitude correction of about 1,000 feet per inch and an increase of about 120 feet of density altitude per degree Celsius above standard, the density altitude is closest to

answers.text: 3,850 feet, because density altitude always equals field elevation
5,200 feet, from correcting only for the low altimeter setting
7,400 feet, from a pressure altitude near 4,250 feet and a temperature roughly 26 degrees above standard at that altitude
9,800 feet, because the temperature correction alone is added to sea level

questions.explanation: Pressure altitude is field elevation plus the correction for a setting 0.40 inch below standard, about 400 feet, giving roughly 4,250 feet. Standard temperature at that altitude is about 6 to 7 degrees Celsius, so 33 degrees is about 26 degrees above standard, adding roughly 26 times 120, or about 3,100 feet, for a density altitude near 7,400 feet. Density altitude equals field elevation only on a standard day. Correcting only for pressure ignores the large temperature effect, and the temperature correction is added to pressure altitude, not to sea level.

questions.question: (Scenario) A crew member monitoring traffic hears a pilot identify an aircraft with the spoken suffix Seven Whiskey Romeo. In digits and letters, what suffix did the pilot state?

answers.text: 7WR
7MR, because Whiskey stands for the letter M
N7R, because the spoken digit begins the registration prefix
7WS, because Romeo is spoken for the letter S

questions.explanation: In the phonetic alphabet Whiskey is the letter W and Romeo is the letter R, so Seven Whiskey Romeo is the digit 7 followed by W and R. M is spoken as Mike, not Whiskey. The spoken sequence is transcribed in the order heard, so the digit stays where it was spoken rather than moving to the front. S is spoken as Sierra, not Romeo.

questions.question: (Scenario) Tracking a moving boat for a client, a remote pilot's whole attention narrows onto keeping the boat framed while the aircraft follows it toward a bridge the pilot scouted an hour ago and has stopped thinking about. What is degrading, and what restores it?

answers.text: Nothing is degrading, because framing the subject is the pilot's whole job
The camera is degrading, and a faster gimbal restores it
Situational awareness is degrading through channelized attention on the subject; deliberate periodic scans of the wider scene - position, obstacles, battery, traffic - restore the full picture
The observer's awareness replaces the pilot's, so the pilot need not scan

questions.explanation: Framing a moving subject channels attention onto one element while the rest of the operation goes unwatched, and only deliberate full-scene scans by the pilot rebuild awareness. The paying shot is one task among several the pilot owns. The failure is attentional, not mechanical. An observer supplements the pilot's awareness and can never substitute for the person flying the aircraft.

questions.question: (Scenario) A crew monitoring a small airport's UNICOM frequency in the early morning hears no station operator answering pilots, although pilots are announcing to each other on the same frequency. What is the most likely explanation and the correct practice?

answers.text: Silence from the station means the airport is closed until the operator arrives
The UNICOM station is simply unattended at that hour; pilots self-announce to each other on the frequency, and the crew should rely on those announcements
The pilots are on the wrong frequency, because UNICOM frequencies carry no pilot-to-pilot calls
The crew should transmit a warning that the airport is unstaffed

questions.explanation: Many UNICOM stations are attended only part of the day, and outside those hours the frequency still serves pilot-to-pilot self-announcing, which is what the crew should monitor. An unattended station does not close the airport. Pilot-to-pilot calls on that frequency are normal practice. A drone crew has no business broadcasting staffing warnings.

virginia-real-estate.quiz_title: Virginia Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A borrower obtains a loan of $530,000.00 and pays 1 discount points. What is the dollar cost of the points?
questions.explanation: The points cost is the loan amount times the points as a percentage, here $530,000 times 1 point, which equals $5,300. The $2,650 figure is half the cost, while $7,950 and $10,600 are one and one-half times and double the cost.

questions.question: A $1900000 Virginia property’s building earns $87605 NOI capitalized at 10.5%. By the building residual technique, the land is worth
questions.explanation: Under the building residual technique, the building value is its income divided by its capitalization rate, 87,605 dollars divided by 10 and one half percent, or about 834,333 dollars, leaving land value of about 1,065,667 dollars from the 1,900,000 dollar total. The 834,333 dollar figure is the building value rather than the land value, 532,833 dollars is about half the land value, and 1,812,395 dollars merely subtracts the income itself from the total price.

questions.question: A short-term loan used until long-term financing or a sale closes is commonly called a

answers.text: construction draw
bridge loan
graduated payment loan
reverse annuity loan

questions.explanation: A bridge loan is short-term financing used until long-term financing is arranged or a sale closes. A construction draw is a disbursement under a construction loan rather than a bridge, a graduated payment loan is a long-term loan whose payments rise over time, and a reverse annuity loan pays a homeowner instead of bridging to permanent financing.

questions.question: The escalation provision increases the bid $6,000 beyond competing offers, never above $415,750. Competition comes in at $406,750. The buyer's final price is
questions.explanation: The escalation price is the competing offer plus the increment, capped at the stated maximum: $406,750 plus $6,000 is $412,750, which is below the $415,750 cap. Matching the competing offer at $406,750 ignores the increment, $413,750 adds too much, and $415,750 is the ceiling rather than the computed price.

questions.question: With 15% down on $697,000, plus $8,100 in buyer closing costs, less the $1,600 earnest money already paid, the buyer needs
questions.explanation: Cash to close is the down payment plus closing costs minus earnest money already paid: 15 percent of $697,000 is $104,550, plus $8,100, minus $1,600, equals $111,050. The $112,050 and $112,650 figures overstate that arithmetic, and $98,050 understates it by effectively subtracting the closing costs instead of adding them.

questions.question: Among common residential property conditions, which one presents a classic example of a latent defect

answers.text: peeling exterior paint
a concealed structural failure not discoverable through ordinary inspection
a broken window
a stained carpet

questions.explanation: A latent defect is a hidden problem that ordinary inspection does not reveal, and a concealed structural failure fits that definition. Peeling paint, a broken window, and a stained carpet are visible conditions a buyer can discover by looking, so they are patent rather than latent.

questions.question: EPA's recommended radon action level is

answers.text: 20 pCi/L
2 pCi/L
0.5 pCi/L
4 picocuries per liter (pCi/L)

questions.explanation: Federal environmental guidance recommends action to reduce radon at a level of 4 picocuries per liter. Levels of 2 picocuries per liter and one-half picocurie per liter are below that action level, while 20 picocuries per liter is far above the level at which action is recommended.

questions.question: The remaining 20% in a 55+ community

answers.text: may include younger occupants without losing the exemption
must be 55+
must be empty
violates the Act

questions.explanation: Because the older-persons occupancy element requires 80 percent occupancy by persons 55 or older, the remaining 20 percent may include younger occupants without losing the exemption. That remainder need not be 55 or older, need not be empty, and does not by itself violate the Act.

questions.question: A borrower's monthly PITI is $3,050 and gross monthly income is $18,000. What is the front-end (housing) debt-to-income ratio?
questions.explanation: The front-end ratio is monthly housing expense divided by gross monthly income: $3,050 divided by $18,000 equals about 16.9 percent. The 16.1 percent figure is slightly low, while 19.7 percent and 21.9 percent overstate the housing burden.

questions.question: Licensing a new branch office costs what?
questions.explanation: Virginia's Real Estate Board fee schedule sets the branch office license application fee at $265, payable with the application for a license for each additional place of business the principal broker maintains.

questions.question: A buyer asks about extra district taxes in a community development authority district. The disclosure statement references which body of law?

answers.text: the federal empowerment zone program
the Code's community development authority provisions
the state enterprise zone act only
the housing authorities law

questions.explanation: The disclosure statement's list of buyer due-diligence items includes community development authority districts and the added district taxes they can impose, pointing buyers to Virginia's community development authority provisions. The federal empowerment zone program, the state enterprise zone act standing alone, and the housing authorities law govern different programs and are not the body of law the statement references for these district taxes.

questions.question: A property manager asks about the rent target under Virginia agency law. Which statement is true?

answers.text: Terms are the agent's choice
Market rent is mandatory
The agent seeks the rent and terms in the brokerage agreement or otherwise acceptable to the landlord
The agent sets the rent

questions.explanation: A landlord's agent must seek the rent and terms stated in the brokerage agreement or otherwise acceptable to the landlord, because the landlord, not the agent, sets the rental objectives. Market rent is not automatically mandatory regardless of the agreement, and the agent may not choose or set the rent and terms independently.

massachusetts-real-estate.quiz_title: Massachusetts Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about determinable vs condition subsequent and one about vendor's lien — contains two true statements?

answers.text: The determinable estate uses words like 'while' or 'during' and ends automatically; the condition-subsequent estate uses 'on condition that' and requires the grantor to act. A vendor's lien secures unpaid purchase money owed to a seller who financed the sale.
The determinable and condition-subsequent estates are identical and both require court action to terminate. A vendor's lien is a tax imposed on vendors selling goods at a flea market.
The determinable and condition-subsequent estates are identical and both require court action to terminate. A vendor's lien secures unpaid purchase money owed to a seller who financed the sale.

The determinable estate uses words like 'while' or 'during' and ends automatically; the condition-subsequent estate uses 'on condition that' and requires the grantor to act. A vendor's lien is a tax imposed on vendors selling goods at a flea market.

questions.explanation: Durational words like 'while' or 'during' create the determinable estate that ends automatically, while 'on condition that' creates the condition-subsequent estate that requires the grantor to act to reclaim the land. A vendor's lien secures unpaid purchase money owed to a seller who financed the sale, not a flea-market tax, so only the first pairing states both points correctly.

questions.question: If NOI is $50,000 and the cap rate is 10%, what is the indicated value?
questions.explanation: Value under the income approach equals net operating income divided by the capitalization rate, so $50,000 divided by ten percent gives $500,000. The other figures come from multiplying instead of dividing or from misplacing the decimal.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about mortgagor vs mortgagee and one about TILA — contains two true statements?

answers.text: The mortgagor is the borrower who gives the mortgage; the mortgagee is the lender who receives it. The Truth in Lending Act requires disclosure of credit terms including the APR.
The mortgagor is the borrower who gives the mortgage; the mortgagee is the lender who receives it. TILA prohibits all consumer lending.
The mortgagor is the lender and the mortgagee is the borrower. The Truth in Lending Act requires disclosure of credit terms including the APR.
The mortgagor is the lender and the mortgagee is the borrower. TILA prohibits all consumer lending.

questions.explanation: The mortgagor is the borrower who gives the mortgage, and the mortgagee is the lender who receives it, not the reverse. The Truth in Lending Act requires disclosure of credit terms including the annual percentage rate so borrowers can compare cost, rather than prohibiting consumer lending.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about option and one about gross lease — contains two true statements?

answers.text: An option is a separate contract keeping an offer open for a period, supported by consideration. In a gross lease the tenant pays all expenses.
An option is a free promise with no consideration. In a gross lease the tenant pays all expenses.
An option is a separate contract keeping an offer open for a period, supported by consideration. In a gross lease the tenant pays one rent and the landlord pays operating expenses.
An option is a free promise with no consideration. In a gross lease the tenant pays one rent and the landlord pays operating expenses.

questions.explanation: An option is a separate contract, supported by consideration, that keeps an offer open for a stated period — not a free promise. In a gross lease the tenant pays one rent and the landlord pays operating expenses, so the tenant does not pay all expenses.
