questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about executory and one about void — contains two false statements?

answers.text: An executory contract is fully performed. A void contract is fully enforceable.
An executory contract is fully performed. A void contract lacks legal effect from the start.
An executory contract still has performance remaining. A void contract lacks legal effect from the start.
An executory contract still has performance remaining. A void contract is fully enforceable.

questions.explanation: An executory contract still has performance remaining on one or both sides, so describing it as fully performed is backwards. A void contract has no legal effect from the beginning, which is the opposite of being fully enforceable.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about implied agency and one about renunciation — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Implied agency can arise from conduct, creating unintended duties. The agent can never withdraw.
Implied agency can arise from conduct, creating unintended duties. The agent may renounce the agency, subject to contract liability.
Agency can never arise by implication. The agent can never withdraw.
Agency can never arise by implication. The agent may renounce the agency, subject to contract liability.

questions.explanation: Agency can arise by implication when conduct creates it, which is how unintended duties sneak in, so agency is not limited to signed agreements. An agent may also renounce the agency and withdraw, though doing so can carry contract liability.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about HIV/AIDS and one about water — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Federal and many state laws prohibit disclosing that an occupant had HIV/AIDS. A failing septic system need not be disclosed.
Federal and many state laws prohibit disclosing that an occupant had HIV/AIDS. Water source, quality problems, and well/septic issues should be disclosed.
An occupant's HIV status must be disclosed to buyers. Water source, quality problems, and well/septic issues should be disclosed.
An occupant's HIV status must be disclosed to buyers. A failing septic system need not be disclosed.

questions.explanation: An occupant's illness, including HIV status, is treated as a stigmatized, nonmaterial matter that disclosure law shields rather than broadcasts to buyers. By contrast, problems with water source, quality, wells, or septic systems affect the property itself and should be disclosed.

questions.question: A Boston attorney reviewing title for a buyer discovers an undisclosed 40-year-old mortgage that was never discharged. What does this defect affect?

answers.text: The property's assessed value for tax purposes
The seller's homestead exemption amount
Marketability of title, which the buyer's attorney must certify before closing
The broker's commission entitlement

questions.explanation: An old mortgage that was never discharged remains a cloud on the seller's title, and a buyer cannot receive clean, marketable title until it is dealt with. That is a title problem for the closing attorney to resolve, not a matter of tax assessment, homestead protection for the seller, or the broker's right to a commission.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about license required and one about do not practice law — contains two false statements?

answers.text: Anyone may perform brokerage for a fee. Agents may give legal advice freely.
Anyone may perform brokerage for a fee. Licensees must not practice law; they use approved forms and refer legal questions to attorneys.
A license is required to perform brokerage acts for another for compensation. Agents may give legal advice freely.
A license is required to perform brokerage acts for another for compensation. Licensees must not practice law; they use approved forms and refer legal questions to attorneys.

questions.explanation: Brokerage for another for compensation requires a license, so anyone may not perform it for a fee. Licensees must not practice law either; in Massachusetts closings and conveyancing belong to attorneys, and licensees use approved forms and refer legal questions out, so the pairing joining the anyone-may-broker claim with the free-legal-advice claim holds the two untrue statements.

questions.question: A $992,000.00 property generates $97,000.00 of annual net operating income. Regarding rates of return, what is the capitalization rate?
questions.explanation: Divide the net operating income by the value: $97,000.00 ÷ $992,000.00 = 0.0978, a capitalization rate of 9.78%. The figure above one thousand percent comes from inverting the relationship, and the lower percentages do not match the division the stem's numbers produce.

questions.question: A broker applicant in Springfield submits proof of experience as an active Massachusetts salesperson. What affiliation history must a broker applicant show?

answers.text: 1 year of part-time affiliation under any broker
5 years as an unlicensed assistant
2 years of affiliation with no minimum weekly hours
3 years affiliation as an active MA salesperson under an active MA broker, at minimum 25 hours per week

questions.explanation: Broker applicants must show three years as an active Massachusetts salesperson affiliated under an active Massachusetts broker, working at least twenty-five hours per week. Shorter periods, unlicensed assisting, and affiliation without the weekly-hours minimum do not qualify.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about discriminatory terms and one about human models — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Charging higher rent because of a tenant's religion is lawful. Housing ads should use models suggesting only one group is welcome.
Imposing different terms, conditions, or privileges based on a protected class is prohibited. Housing ads should use models suggesting only one group is welcome.
Imposing different terms, conditions, or privileges based on a protected class is prohibited. Human models in housing ads should reflect diversity and avoid signaling exclusion.
Charging higher rent because of a tenant's religion is lawful. Human models in housing ads should reflect diversity and avoid signaling exclusion.

questions.explanation: Imposing different terms, conditions, or privileges because of a protected class is prohibited, so charging higher rent because of a tenant's religion is unlawful. Housing advertising should likewise avoid signaling exclusion: human models in ads should reflect diversity rather than suggest only one group is welcome.

georgia-insurance.quiz_title: Georgia Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A customer is injured in a fall at a store in March while an occurrence-based commercial general liability policy is in effect. The customer does not file a claim until the following year, after that policy has expired. Which event determines whether that expired policy responds?

answers.text: The date the claim was first reported to any insurer
The date the injured person first hired an attorney
The date the bodily injury occurred
The date a lawsuit was served on the store

questions.explanation: An occurrence policy responds based on when the bodily injury or property damage occurred during the policy period, even if the claim is made later. A first-made or first-reported date is the trigger concept for a claims-made policy, not an occurrence policy.

questions.question: A landlord leases a building it owns to a nightclub and does not itself sell or serve any alcohol. A claim seeks to hold the landlord liable by reason of the club's overservice. Which concept-level caution applies?

answers.text: A landlord can never be affected by the liquor exclusion under any facts

Only the person who physically poured the drink can be an insured affected, in accordance with the policy conditions, and taking the policy's definitions and conditions as they are written in the form
Premises ownership converts the landlord into the alcohol manufacturer
The exclusion can also reach an insured that owns or leases out premises used by others for alcohol business purposes, so the landlord's non-pouring role is not automatically dispositive

questions.explanation: The exclusion's reach is not limited to the hand that poured the drink; it addresses insureds in the alcohol business and, in the form's framing, those whose premises role is tied to that business. Ownership does not make the landlord a manufacturer, but it also does not end the inquiry.

questions.question: Must a disease be an occupational disease of the claimant's own job to count as disease within the bodily injury definition?

answers.text: Yes; diseases of members of the public never qualify
No, but only diseases that are also sicknesses in name
No; the definition says disease sustained by a person without limiting it to occupational disease
Yes; only diseases listed as occupational qualify

questions.explanation: The definition is unqualified as to whose job produced the disease. Reading in an occupational-only limit would narrow words the definition does not narrow.

questions.question: A delivery company's insurer pays an injured customer after its insured driver and a road contractor share fault, then seeks recovery from the contractor for the contractor's share. This pursuit is

answers.text: Subrogation against the party whose negligence contributed to the loss
A first-party bad faith claim
An IBNR reserve estimate
A covenant not to execute

questions.explanation: After paying, the insurer pursues the outside party responsible for part of the loss through subrogation. No settlement promise or reserve estimate describes that recovery action.

questions.question: An insured transfers its interest in the business to a buyer and assumes the CGL policy itself was sold with the business. Separately, a claim the insurer already paid generated recovery rights against a third party. Which statement keeps the two transfer concepts straight?

answers.text: Both transfers are the same condition with the same consent rules
Transfer of recovery rights after payment is the insurer's subrogation right; assigning the policy itself to a new owner is a different matter that generally requires the insurer's written consent
Recovery rights belong to whoever buys the business automatically

Policy assignment and recovery transfer are both prohibited in all cases, consistent with the wording of the form edition in effect during the policy period, and as stated in the applicable policy form

questions.explanation: The transfer of rights of recovery condition moves the insured's claim against a wrongdoer to the paying insurer. Transferring the policy itself to another party is an assignment issue governed by a different condition and consent requirement.

questions.question: A contents claim is filed under a broad named-perils form for an item that stopped working for unknown reasons. Which statement correctly places the burden regarding cause of loss?

answers.text: The insurer must prove an exclusion applies before the insured identifies any cause at all.
The insured must show that the loss was caused by a peril named in the policy; an unknown cause is not enough.
Coverage is automatic whenever the cause cannot be determined.
The burden is decided by whichever party files the claim first.

questions.explanation: Named-perils coverage is triggered only by a listed cause, so the insured bears the burden of tying the loss to one. An unknown cause therefore fails at the threshold, unlike an open-perils claim where the insurer must raise an exclusion.

questions.question: An earthquake endorsement defines a period, often 72 hours, during which related shocks are treated in a particular way. What is that treatment?

answers.text: Each aftershock is a new occurrence with a new deductible every hour
The period determines when the policy automatically renews after a quake
Aftershocks after the first shock are never covered under any circumstance, including when the underlying event involves more than one location, vehicle, or injured person
Shocks within the defined period are generally treated as a single occurrence, so one earthquake deductible applies to the combined loss

questions.explanation: The single-occurrence window prevents a separate deductible for every tremor in one seismic event. Aftershocks are not automatically uncovered.

questions.question: A homeowner carries less than 80% of the dwelling's replacement cost when a covered partial loss occurs. Under the homeowners loss settlement condition, the insurer will pay the greater of which two amounts, less the deductible?

answers.text: The full replacement cost of the damaged part, or the original purchase price of the home, whichever amount the insured happens to prefer at claim time
The mortgage balance, or the tax-assessed value of the dwelling
The actual cash value of the damaged part, or the proportion of the loss that the limit carried bears to 80% of the replacement cost
The limit of insurance, or twice the actual cash value of the damaged part

questions.explanation: Falling short of the 80% threshold gives the greater of ACV or the proportionate share (did divided by 80% of replacement cost, times the loss), less the deductible. Full replacement cost is available only when the threshold is met, so that option is wrong.

questions.question: An 1890s commercial building has ornate handcrafted features. Reproducing them exactly would cost far more than the building contributes in use or income. Why might functional replacement cost be selected for this building?

answers.text: It guarantees payment of the full cost of reproducing every ornate feature by hand
It converts the policy into a valued policy that pays the limit for any partial loss, as shown in the schedule of covered locations attached to the policy at inception
It removes the need for any limit of insurance on the building
It bases the value on putting back a building that serves the same function with standard modern construction, rather than reproducing the costly ornate work

questions.explanation: Functional replacement cost fits older buildings whose exact reproduction cost is out of proportion to their use, by valuing a functionally equivalent rebuild. It does not promise hand reproduction of the ornate features.

questions.question: How does an exclusion differ from a condition in the work each does inside a policy?

answers.text: An exclusion defines risks the insurer has not assumed, while a condition sets a requirement that governs the parties' rights
An exclusion sets requirements, while a condition removes perils
Both provisions do the same work and differ only in placement
A condition removes coverage permanently, while an exclusion is temporary and lasts only until the insurer chooses to reinstate the coverage

questions.explanation: Exclusions mark the boundary of assumed risk; conditions impose requirements attached to the contract's operation. Reversing those roles misreads both provisions.

questions.question: A broker placed surplus lines coverage using a certificate because the policy was unavailable. The insured now asks for the actual policy. What is the broker's duty?

answers.text: Deliver the policy only at the first renewal, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Explain that the certificate is legally the same as the policy and refuse, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Deliver the policy within one year of the request, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
As soon as reasonably possible, procure and deliver the policy in replacement of the certificate

questions.explanation: On the insured's request, the broker must procure and deliver the policy as soon as reasonably possible in place of the certificate; the certificate is interim evidence, not a permanent substitute.

questions.question: An insurer unreasonably delays a claim by demanding both a formal proof of loss and later verification duplicating the same information. What does Georgia say, and what remains allowed?

answers.text: The insurer may duplicate demands without limit, demanding the same information over and over without any limit at all
Sworn statements are prohibited in all cases, so no sworn statement may be obtained even when the policy permits it
The duplicative demand is a listed practice, but the insurer may still obtain sworn statements if the policy permits them
All proof of loss demands are prohibited, so an insurer may never demand a formal proof of loss from an insured

questions.explanation: Duplicative verification delay is listed, while policy-permitted sworn statements remain available. Banning all proof demands overreads the rule.

texas-water-operator-class-d.quiz_title: Texas Water Operator Class D Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A groundwater treatment system serves 820 people through only 210 connections. A former Class D holder applies for a new Class D license to operate that system. What is the result?

answers.text: The application is approved, because the connection count is under 250 and that is the only size test that is ever applied
The application is approved, because population limits apply only when a license is renewed
The application is approved if a supervisor co-signs the application form
The new Class D application is barred, because a groundwater treatment system serving 750 or more people is one of the categories closed to a new Class D license

questions.explanation: The population category stands on its own: serving 750 or more people bars a previous holder from a new Class D license for that system even with fewer than 250 connections. The bar is not limited to renewal situations.

questions.question: An operator arrives to read a meter inside a fenced yard. A large dog inside the fence charges the gate, barking and lunging, and no one answers at the house. What should the operator do?

answers.text: Stay out of the yard, back away safely, and arrange through the customer or a supervisor for the visit to happen when the dog is secured
Enter quickly and finish the reading before the dog reaches the far side of the yard
Offer the dog treats from the truck until it calms down and accepts the operator, then enter the yard and take the reading as planned without further delay
Open the gate and use a garden hose to keep the dog at a distance while reading

questions.explanation: An unrestrained, aggressive dog is a reason not to enter: the operator withdraws and the reading is rescheduled for when the animal is secured. Racing the dog, feeding it, or hosing it all put the operator inside the fence with an aroused animal.

questions.question: A Texas operator records how much of each chemical the system uses. How long must those chemical-amount records be kept?

answers.text: At least two years.
At least three years.
At least five years.
At least ten years.

questions.explanation: Chemical amounts used are in the two-year retention group, together with water volumes, the complaint log, and maintenance records. Calibration and residual records run three years, and chemical analysis results run ten.

questions.question: What is the multiple-barrier principle in drinking-water protection?

answers.text: Running all of the water through the same treatment process twice to be doubly sure it works
Relying on disinfection alone because it is the strongest step
Layering source protection, treatment, and disinfection so each barrier backs up the others
Testing the finished water more often instead of improving treatment

questions.explanation: Safe water is not entrusted to any single step: protecting the source, treating the water, disinfecting it, and keeping the distribution system secure are independent barriers that back each other up. Testing alone detects problems but is not itself a barrier.

questions.question: A system plans extra surface-protection vigilance for wells drilled in cracked limestone country full of sinkholes. Why do these wells need the extra vigilance?

answers.text: Openings and fractures let spilled or surface contaminants reach the groundwater quickly, with little natural filtering along the way.
Limestone groundwater in contact with the casing slowly dissolves the steel casing from the outside inward until the casing wall fails and the well begins taking in surface water.
Sinkholes drain the water table downward so the wells run dry every summer season.
Fractured rock formations make the groundwater far too hard for customers to use.

questions.explanation: Karst and fractured formations are fast pathways: contamination can travel through cracks and solution openings to a well far faster than through granular soil that filters it. That travel speed, not casing corrosion, water level, or hardness, is why surface protection matters most there.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a watertight well cap on top of a well casing?

answers.text: To carry the full weight of the pump, motor, and drop pipe assembly hanging inside the well casing
To give the operator a way to measure the depth of water standing in the well
To vent air freely in and out of the casing whenever the pump starts and stops
To seal the top of the casing so insects, debris, and surface water cannot enter the well

questions.explanation: A watertight well cap seals the casing top against insects, debris, and surface water entering the well. Venting is handled by a separate screened vent opening, and carrying the pump's weight is the job of the well seal and support fittings, not the cap.

questions.question: Heavy rain falls across the watershed overnight, and by morning the raw water arriving at a plant's intake has turned brown and its turbidity has climbed sharply. What should the crew expect and do?

answers.text: Expect a much heavier solids load on the treatment processes, and keep the operator in charge informed as raw-water conditions change.
Expect the heavy rain to improve the raw water by diluting everything dissolved in the river, so the plant can relax its treatment and monitoring until the river settles back down.
Expect no change at the plant, because turbidity is a problem only in groundwater systems.
Expect the plant to need no extra monitoring until the river water clears up on its own.

questions.explanation: Storm runoff washes soil and debris into the source, so raw-water turbidity and the solids load on coagulation, settling, and filtration all rise, and changing source conditions must be reported up. Rain does not dilute a river clean, and turbidity matters greatly in surface water treatment.

questions.question: Before deciding whether to start a second well, an operator checks how much finished water is in storage by reading the tank's level gauge at ground level. What has the gauge provided?

answers.text: The pressure in the distribution zone served by the tank at the far end of the zone during the morning peak demand period
The current water level, and therefore the stored volume available, without climbing the tank
The chlorine residual of the water stored in the tank
The flow rate at which the tank is filling

questions.explanation: A level gauge or indicator shows the water level in the tank, from which the operator knows the stored volume on hand. It does not measure residual or zone pressure, which require their own instruments and samples.

questions.question: While repairing a copper service line, an operator finds the only solder on the truck is labeled as containing 0.3 percent lead. What should the operator do?

answers.text: Use it, because the 0.25 percent limit for pipes and fittings is the limit that governs the repair
Not use it, because solder and flux must not exceed 0.2 percent lead
Use it on the hot-water side only, where the water sits in contact with the joint for less time
Use it to finish the repair, then flush the service line for ten minutes before returning it

questions.explanation: Solder and flux containing more than 0.2 percent lead are prohibited, so the 0.3 percent solder cannot be used on the potable service. The 0.25 percent figure is the limit for pipes and fittings, and flushing afterward does not make a prohibited material acceptable.

questions.question: A hypochlorite solution feeder is running, but no chlorine is reaching the water and the residual is dropping. The operator finds the solution tank nearly empty and the suction line drawing air. What is the correct diagnosis and fix?

answers.text: The water has stopped exerting demand, so no chlorine feed is needed
The DPD reagent has expired, and the actual residual in the system is unchanged from yesterday's reading
The distribution system is full, so chlorine can no longer enter it
Refill the solution tank and restore the suction feed so the feeder regains prime

questions.explanation: A solution feeder cannot deliver chlorine from an empty tank, and air in the suction line breaks its prime, so refilling the tank and restoring suction returns the feed. A falling residual with no feed reaching the water is an equipment supply problem, not a testing artifact.

questions.question: An operator is about to open an ultraviolet disinfection unit to replace a lamp. What safety step comes first?

answers.text: Leave the lamps lit so the operator can see which one has failed
Look directly into the lit lamp to check that it is still producing light
Shut off power to the lamps and let them cool before opening the unit
Spray the lit lamps with water to cool them before touching the unit

questions.explanation: Ultraviolet light injures eyes and skin and the lamps run hot, so the unit is de-energized and allowed to cool before service. Viewing or spraying an energized lamp risks burns and eye damage.

questions.question: A system treats 0.53 MGD and applies a chlorine dose of 4.2 mg/L. How many pounds of chlorine per day are required?

answers.text: 2.23 lb/day
17.81 lb/day
18.56 lb/day
20.03 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = 0.53 MGD × 4.2 mg/L × 8.34 = 18.56 lb/day. The 2.23 lb/day result omits the 8.34 factor, and the others use the wrong factor.

california-wastewater-grade-5.quiz_title: California Wastewater Grade 5 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Three eyewash stations fail activation checks in one quarter, each in a different building. What does the chief operator treat as the finding?

answers.text: A run of defective eyewash units that the manufacturer should replace under warranty
An ownership gap in the inspection program — no position clearly accountable for those stations — corrected by assigning and tracking the inspections
Evidence that activation checks are being done too often and wearing the valves out
A training issue for the three operators who happened to find the failures on their rounds, with responsibility assigned to the shift supervisor on duty at the time

questions.explanation: The same failure appearing across separate buildings points past the individual units to the program element that was supposed to catch it. When inspection ownership is unassigned, completion is nobody's measured job; the chief operator fixes the assignment and tracks closure rather than replacing hardware one station at a time.

questions.question: Paired samples for a capacity review show primary influent suspended solids of 312 mg/L and primary effluent suspended solids of 118 mg/L. What is the percent removal across the stage?
questions.explanation: Percent removal = (in − out) / in × 100 = (312 − 118) / 312 × 100 = 62.18%. The 37.82% figure is the share of solids remaining, not the share removed, and the other figures use effluent values of 90 and 142 mg/L that the samples did not show.

questions.question: A plant's anoxic zone receives plenty of nitrate but too little carbon, and the chief operator evaluates buying an external carbon source for denitrification. Which evaluation is complete?

answers.text: Compare carbon products on price per gallon only, since denitrification has no other plant effects, with the supporting paperwork filed alongside the year's capital correspondence
Reject purchased carbon in all cases, because carbon must come only from the influent
Weigh the carbon cost together with the alkalinity denitrification returns and the aeration oxygen credit it creates downstream
Buy enough carbon to keep the anoxic zone fully aerobic at all times

questions.explanation: Denitrification needs an anoxic zone and available carbon, and it returns part of the alkalinity nitrification consumed while its oxygen credit lowers downstream aeration demand. A chief-level decision weighs those axes together with the purchase cost, not the invoice alone.

questions.question: A plant serving a food-processing town faces a short, intense seasonal load peak each year and moderate loads the rest of the year. How does that pattern shape the expansion evaluation?

answers.text: The plant is sized for the peak week alone, because idle capacity the rest of the year carries no cost worth weighing in the evaluation
The seasonal peak is ignored in planning because annual average load is the only figure an evaluation may use
The processor is simply told to stop discharging during its season, which closes the evaluation without a project
Paths are compared on how they carry a brief peak without stranding oversized capacity all year — equalization and flexible configurations are weighed alongside raw added volume

questions.explanation: Process selection at planning scale compares modification and expansion paths on capacity gained, energy, sludge production, and operability. A short sharp peak changes the comparison: load equalization or a flexible process configuration may carry the season at far lower year-round cost than concrete sized for the peak week alone.

questions.question: A chief operator budgets alkalinity consumption for a basin that will oxidize 31 mg/L of ammonia nitrogen. How much alkalinity will nitrification consume?

answers.text: 142.6 mg/L as CaCO3
186.0 mg/L as CaCO3
221.34 mg/L as CaCO3
275.9 mg/L as CaCO3

questions.explanation: Alkalinity CONSUMED by nitrification = 7.14 × ammonia nitrogen = 7.14 × 31 = 221.34 mg/L as CaCO3. The 7.14 factor is the ALKALINITY factor; the 4.6 factor (which would give 142.6) belongs to oxygen demand, not alkalinity. This item keys the amount consumed, not the residual remaining.

questions.question: A membrane train's permeability recovers fully after each chemical cleaning in its early years, but the recovery after cleaning shrinks year by year despite correct cleaning practice. What does that pattern support?

answers.text: A lifecycle replacement argument for the membranes, built on declining cleaning recovery
A conclusion that the cleaning chemicals should be doubled in strength until full recovery returns
A finding that the membranes are improving, because less recovery means they were never very fouled
No action, because permeability trends are operating trivia that never justify capital planning

questions.explanation: Membrane assets are lifecycle-managed by tracking cleaning effectiveness through permeability recovery. Declining recovery after correctly performed cleaning is the replacement argument.

questions.question: During a screw press dewatering campaign, the plant feeds 96 lb/day of polymer while processing 7.4 dry tons of solids per day. What is the polymer dose?

answers.text: 9.73 lb/ton
16.21 lb/ton
12.97 lb/ton
710.40 lb/ton

questions.explanation: Polymer dose = polymer fed ÷ dry solids processed = 96 lb/day ÷ 7.4 ton/day = 12.97 lb/ton. The 710.40 figure multiplies the two quantities instead of dividing; the dose is always expressed per dry ton processed.

questions.question: A refilled contact structure holds 0.85 MG of water that is to be disinfected at a dose of 9 mg/L using calcium hypochlorite rated at 68% available chlorine. How many pounds of the dry product are required?
questions.explanation: Pounds (solid) = volume × dose × 8.34 ÷ (strength/100) = 0.85 × 9 × 8.34 ÷ 0.68 = 63.80 ÷ 0.68 = 93.82 lb. Because the product is only 68% available chlorine, more dry product is needed than the uncorrected gas-form figure of 63.80 lb.

questions.question: A pond plant supplies polished, disinfected effluent for restricted irrigation. Demand peaks hard in the dry season, while pond production is steadiest in the wet season, and storage is limited. What does chief-level planning require?

answers.text: Evaluate treatment capacity, storage, and delivery together against the customers' seasonal demand pattern, surfacing a dry-season shortfall early as a capacity and storage question
Promise customers the full dry-season demand, since pond effluent volume roughly balances over a whole year, and make up any shortfall by drawing storage below its normal minimum operating level
Hold pond levels as high as possible all winter regardless of freeboard, to bank water for the dry season
Reduce wet-season treatment so the ponds rest before the irrigation season begins each year

questions.explanation: Pond-to-reuse service is planned against seasonal demand and storage together: the mismatch between when water is produced and when customers need it is a capacity question to surface early, not a promise to make on an annual average while storage runs out mid-season.

questions.question: In the nitrification analysis set, ammonia is falling but nitrite is accumulating while nitrate rises only slowly. What does the nitrite accumulation mark?

answers.text: Complete nitrification, since the appearance of any nitrite proves the full pathway is finished and the alkalinity is no longer being consumed
Denitrification in the sample bottle, which manufactures nitrite from nitrate after collection
A preservation failure, because nitrite cannot exist in a properly collected effluent sample
Oxidation stalled between its two steps: ammonia is being converted to nitrite faster than nitrite is being converted onward to nitrate

questions.explanation: Nitrification is a two-step autotrophic oxidation — ammonia to nitrite, then nitrite to nitrate — which is why the set is read together. Accumulating nitrite with slow nitrate formation shows the second step lagging the first, a different finding from either healthy nitrification or no nitrification at all.

questions.question: During a plant performance review, the effluent channel is carrying 13.9 cubic feet per second through a cross-sectional area of 3.6 square feet. What is the flow velocity in the channel?

answers.text: 3.86 ft/sec
50.04 ft/sec
7.72 ft/sec
0.26 ft/sec

questions.explanation: Velocity = flow ÷ area = 13.9 cfs ÷ 3.6 sq ft = 3.86 ft/sec. Multiplying flow by area gives 50.04 ft/sec, and inverting the ratio gives 0.26 ft/sec; neither is a velocity for this channel.

questions.question: A desert plant's total operating cost for a year is $7,293,000, and it treated 2,431 million gallons that year. What is the cost per million gallons?

answers.text: $2,550.00 per MG, and the matter is treated as closed for the rest of the year

questions.explanation: Cost per MG = total cost ÷ volume = $7,293,000 ÷ 2,431 MG = $3,000.00 per MG.

california-wastewater-grade-4.quiz_title: California Wastewater Grade 4 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An inspection lists a failed ventilation fan in a chlorine room and peeling paint in a break room, but funds cover only one job this month. What should the program do?

answers.text: Repair the paint first because it is the cheaper and quicker job
Split the funds so both jobs are partly completed this month
Repair the ventilation fan first, because it controls a severe hazard, and defer the cosmetic work
Defer both jobs until the next annual budget is approved

questions.explanation: Corrective spending is ranked by hazard severity. Ventilation in a chlorine room is a working control against a severe hazard, so it is funded first; peeling paint is cosmetic and can wait without exposing anyone to serious harm.

questions.question: A primary clarifier holds 412,000 gallons and the flow through it is 920 gallons per minute. How many hours of detention does the tank provide?

answers.text: 3.73 hours
14.93 hours
7.46 hours
447.83 hours

questions.explanation: Detention time = volume / flow = 412,000 gal / 920 gpm = 447.83 minutes, and 447.83 / 60 = 7.46 hours. The 447.83-hour figure skips the minutes-to-hours conversion, and the others use half or double the stated flow.

questions.question: What does a routine microscopic examination program add to secondary process control?

answers.text: An early warning: filament abundance and floc character can be seen trending before settleability and effluent quality deteriorate
A replacement for settleability testing, which it makes unnecessary, and note the action in the shift log for the following crew to review
A method for measuring the dissolved oxygen profile of the basin
A count of the bacteria present that sets the wasting rate directly

questions.explanation: The microscope shows the biology changing before the numbers do. Trending filament abundance and floc character on a routine schedule warns of a developing bulking condition while there is still time to act, instead of discovering it when settling already fails.

questions.question: On afternoon rounds, a one-liter settleability sample drawn from an aeration basin settles to 310 mL after 30 minutes. The laboratory reports mixed liquor suspended solids of 2,400 mg/L for that basin. What sludge volume index do these results give?

answers.text: 155 mL/g

questions.explanation: SVI = settled volume x 1,000 / MLSS = 310 x 1,000 / 2,400 = 129.17 mL/g. The 12.92 figure uses 100 instead of 1,000 in the numerator, and the others divide by MLSS values of 4,000 and 2,000 mg/L instead of the stated 2,400 mg/L.

questions.question: An influent carries 27 mg/L of ammonia nitrogen that the plant fully nitrifies. How much alkalinity does nitrification consume?

answers.text: 124.20 mg/L as CaCO3
96.39 mg/L as CaCO3
27.00 mg/L as CaCO3
192.78 mg/L as CaCO3

questions.explanation: This computes the ALKALINITY consumed by nitrification, which uses the 7.14 alkalinity factor: 7.14 x 27 mg/L = 192.78 mg/L as CaCO3. (The 4.6 factor belongs to oxygen-demand calculations, not alkalinity.)

questions.question: Each backwash from one tertiary filter carries noticeably more media away than the backwash from its sister cells, and the bed level in that cell is falling month by month. What is the sound response?

answers.text: Top the bed up to level on a fixed schedule and record nothing, because media loss at any rate is normal wear
Investigate and correct the bed condition causing the loss — media loss is a recognized filter bed defect — instead of only replacing what was carried away
Raise that cell's backwash rate further, because a stronger wash will settle the remaining media more firmly in place

Lower the filtration rate permanently and accept the lost capacity, because a losing bed can never be returned to service, with the lost capacity written off in the annual report as a permanent reduction

questions.explanation: Media loss is one of the classic tertiary filter bed defects, alongside mudballs, bed cracking, and air binding. A defect has a cause in the bed or its washing; simply topping up treats the symptom while the cause keeps consuming the bed, so the operator finds and corrects the condition.

questions.question: During a cold snap, gas production cannot cover both the digester boilers and the engine-generator. How should the gas be allocated, and why?

answers.text: To the engine-generator first, because electricity production is the highest-value use of the gas in every season of the year

Equally to both, because splitting a shortage evenly is the standard allocation whenever two uses compete for the same gas supply under an allocation rule the plant applies to every shared utility regardless of process criticality
To neither, with all gas flared, because operating either use on a partial supply damages the equipment it serves
To the boilers first, because holding digester temperature steady protects the methane formers, and generation takes what gas remains

questions.explanation: Digester temperature must be held steady — the methane formers the whole process depends on are harmed by swings. In a shortage the heat account is settled first and engine generation, a valuable but deferrable use, takes the remainder.

questions.question: A plant will disinfect 0.48 million gallons of effluent at a dose of 6.2 mg/L using calcium hypochlorite that is 65% available chlorine. How many pounds of the product are required?
questions.explanation: Pounds of solid product = Volume × Dose × 8.34 ÷ (Strength ÷ 100) = 0.48 × 6.2 × 8.34 ÷ 0.65 = 24.82 ÷ 0.65 = 38.18 lb. Leaving out the strength division gives only the pounds of chlorine itself, not the pounds of product to weigh out.

questions.question: A long cold period is forecast for a pond plant that is already carrying a heavy load in its first cell. Which action applies seasonal capacity planning correctly?

answers.text: Add the season's heaviest industrial load now, because cold water will preserve it until spring
Wait for the effluent to fail, then judge from that single reading how much loading to remove, because a cold forecast alone never justifies changing a load
Drain the first cell completely, because an empty cell insulates the remaining cells from the cold
Trim and redistribute the loading ahead of the cold so the slowed biology is not asked to carry a summer load

questions.explanation: Seasonal planning acts before the season arrives: because cold-season biology treats more slowly, the load is trimmed and spread while there is still time. Waiting for a failure reading abandons the plan for a reaction.

questions.question: At a quarterly laboratory review, no single quality check has failed outright, but blanks have crept up, duplicate agreement has widened, and spike recoveries have drifted over three months. What is the program-level conclusion?

answers.text: No action is warranted, because only an outright failure of a single check can ever justify a change
Each analyst should be told privately to be more careful, with no change to methods or training made

The quality checks should be run less often, so their trends stop suggesting problems that are not real, a step that will bring the blank, duplicate, and spike trends back into line without any change in how the work is done
The drift across all three checks is itself the finding: the method or its execution is degrading, and retraining or a method fix is assigned before the drift produces failed results

questions.explanation: Data quality is managed as a program, not check by check. Blanks, duplicates, and spikes each passed individually, but their trends moving together show the measurement system degrading — a management finding that assigns a corrective action, the same discipline the plant's safety and evaluation programs use.

questions.question: An effluent channel carries 11.25 cubic feet per second through a flow area of 3.0 square feet. What is the velocity in the channel?

answers.text: 3.75 ft/sec
33.75 ft/sec
0.27 ft/sec
8.25 ft/sec

questions.explanation: Velocity = flow / area = 11.25 / 3.0 = 3.75 ft/sec. Multiplying flow by area gives 33.75, inverting the division gives 0.27, and subtracting gives 8.25; velocity is the flow divided by the area it passes through.

questions.question: Which description best fits supervision at the Grade IV level, beyond the shift-lead duties of assigning rounds and checking work?

answers.text: Directing the laboratory's analytical methods in detail and approving each reported result personally before its release to the operating crew
Program-level management: energy management, safety program development, operator training, and budget development and control
Serving as the plant's purchasing agent for all of its chemicals, equipment, and contracted services
Setting the discharge limits that the plant must meet under its waste discharge requirements

questions.explanation: Grade IV supervision is defined by the management functions: the shift-lead base is assumed, and the Grade IV operator manages programs — energy, the safety program, operator training, and the budget — at the level of the whole plant.

california-wastewater-grade-3.quiz_title: California Wastewater Grade 3 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A pump coupling guard was removed so the coupling could be inspected. The inspection is finished and the pump is needed. What comes first?

answers.text: The pump is run for a trial shift without the guard to confirm it runs true
The guard is refitted securely before the pump is returned to service
The guard is left off because the coupling area is rarely visited by anyone
The guard is propped beside the pump as a reminder to refit it next week

questions.explanation: Rotating equipment is a mechanical hazard; a guard removed for inspection is replaced before the equipment restarts, so no one is exposed to the moving coupling.

questions.question: Over one day, 13,260 pounds of solids are applied to a primary clarifier whose surface area is 1,560 square feet. What solids loading rate does that produce?

answers.text: 8.5 lb/day/sq ft
6.63 lb/day/sq ft
10.63 lb/day/sq ft
11.05 lb/day/sq ft

questions.explanation: Solids loading rate = solids applied ÷ surface area = 13,260 lb/day ÷ 1,560 sq ft = 8.5 lb/day/sq ft. The other figures come from dividing by the wrong area or inflating the solids load.

questions.question: During the storm peak, solids are washing into the primary clarifiers faster than usual and blankets are climbing. Besides evening out the flow, what withdrawal move helps?

answers.text: Stop sludge withdrawal entirely so the blankets can compact in place
Increase sludge withdrawal to keep the blankets from building too deep
Withdraw scum only, and leave the sludge blankets untouched for now
Drain one clarifier completely and let the others take the whole flow

questions.explanation: Increased sludge withdrawal is part of the wet-weather response: heavier solids inflow builds blankets faster, and stepping up withdrawal holds them at a workable depth. Stopping withdrawal, skimming only, or draining a unit all surrender blanket control during the peak.

questions.question: A clarifier's effluent carries a fine turbidity made of tiny, dense floc particles even though most of the sludge settles. The floc in the basin looks small and compact rather than open and fluffy. Which condition fits?

answers.text: Pin floc, the small compact floc associated with an over-aged sludge
Filamentous bulking, which always produces a large, open, slow-compacting blanket in the clarifier
Dispersed growth, in which no floc particles of any size ever form in the mixed liquor sample
Sludge washout, in which whole formed floc is carried over the weirs only during storm flows

questions.explanation: Pin floc is on the recognised abnormal-condition list: tiny compact particles from an old sludge settle out but leave a turbid effluent, unlike the open blanket of a bulking sludge.

questions.question: Each time operators raise MLSS to hold more treatment capacity, the secondary clarifier begins carrying solids over well before its hydraulic limit is reached. What governs how much inventory this system can hold?

answers.text: The weir overflow rate alone, since hydraulic figures are the only loading a clarifier ever experiences and the solids applied to its surface each day have no bearing on performance at all
The length of the aeration basin, which fixes the inventory regardless of clarifier performance
The dissolved oxygen setpoint, which determines how many solids the clarifier can settle per hour
The solids loading on the secondary clarifier, which limits the solids flux the clarifier can pass downward

questions.explanation: The clarifier is the process's bottleneck: its solids loading governs how much inventory the system can hold. A clarifier can be within hydraulic limits and still fail on solids loading.

questions.question: A microscopic examination of mixed liquor shows abundant stalked ciliates, firm floc with few filaments, and very few free-swimming organisms. How should the operator read this?

answers.text: A stable, older, well-oxidizing system in good operating condition
A young, dispersed sludge that needs its wasting rate cut sharply today
A bulking sludge in which filamentous organisms are taking over the floc
A septic mixed liquor that needs immediate chlorination of the return sludge

questions.explanation: Higher organisms are age indicators in microscopic examination. Stalked ciliates signal a stable, older, well-oxidizing system with firm floc; free-swimming organisms dominate young, dispersed sludge instead.

questions.question: During inspection of a drained filter cell, the operator finds balled clumps of media and solids, bare patches where media depth is low, and cracks at the bed surface. Which set of classic bed defects is present?

answers.text: Sloughing, ponding, and icing of the media surface during cold weather
Denitrification, luxury uptake, and precipitation within the media bed
Ripening, breakthrough, and short-circuiting of the underdrain system
Mudballs, media loss, and cracking or shrinkage of the filter bed

questions.explanation: The classic granular-bed defects are mudballs (media cemented with trapped solids from inadequate backwash), media loss during backwash, and cracking or shrinkage of the bed, with air binding as the fourth common fault. Each is corrected through proper backwash practice and bed maintenance.

questions.question: A digester's volatile acids have climbed for several days, alkalinity and gas production are falling, and the feed log shows the volatile-solids loading was recently stepped up sharply. What is the best first response?

answers.text: Increase the feed rate further so the methane-forming organisms receive more food and recover faster
Raise the digester temperature well above its normal heated range to speed up the slowed organisms
Stop mixing entirely and let the digester rest undisturbed until the volatile acids consume themselves
Cut back the feed, hold heating and mixing steady, and reseed if suitable seed sludge is available

questions.explanation: Rising volatile acids with falling alkalinity and gas is the overload picture, read against the loading figure. The carried response is to cut feed, hold heat and mixing steady, and reseed; adding feed, overheating, or stopping mixing all deepen the upset.

questions.question: How many pounds of chlorine are needed to dose 0.28 million gallons of effluent at 2.4 mg/L?
questions.explanation: Pounds = volume in million gallons × dose × 8.34 = 0.28 × 2.4 × 8.34 = 5.60 lb. Omitting the 8.34 conversion gives only 0.67 lb.

questions.question: What physically happens in a pond at seasonal turnover?

answers.text: Cooling surface water becomes denser than the water below and sinks, mixing the pond's layers and stirring settled material back through the water column
The pond's algae suddenly die off and release their oxygen
Wind pushes the entire pond volume through the outlet in one surge
The bottom sludge layer floats to the surface as a single mat

questions.explanation: Turnover is a density event: as the surface layer cools in the fall it grows denser than the warmer water beneath, sinks, and mixes the whole pond — which is why effluent quality is upset until the pond restratifies.

questions.question: To judge how much load one treatment stage is actually removing, which analyses does the operator pair?

answers.text: The stage's influent and effluent analyses for the same period, compared against each other
Two effluent analyses taken a month apart, with the difference between them reported as the stage's removal performance
The influent analysis and the chemical feed record
The effluent analysis and the flow totalizer reading alone

questions.explanation: Removal across a stage is judged from paired analyses: what entered the stage and what left it over the same period. Unpaired or mismatched results cannot show the stage's removal.

questions.question: During performance testing, a pump delivers 850 gpm against a total head of 115 ft while its driver supplies 42 brake horsepower. What is the pump efficiency?
questions.explanation: Water horsepower = flow x head / 3,960 = 850 x 115 / 3,960 = 24.68 hp. Efficiency = water hp / brake hp x 100 = 24.68 / 42 x 100 = 58.77%. Reporting 24.68% mistakes the water horsepower for the efficiency, and inverting the ratio gives 170.14%.

california-wastewater-grade-2.quiz_title: California Wastewater Grade 2 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Pathogens carried in wastewater belong to which class of plant hazard?

answers.text: Electrical hazard
Mechanical hazard
Biological hazard
Physical noise hazard

questions.explanation: Disease-causing organisms in wastewater are a biological hazard, one of the recognized hazard classes in plant operations alongside chemical, confined-space, electrical, mechanical, and physical hazards.

questions.question: A clarifier with 900 square feet of surface area receives 877,500 gallons per day. What is its overflow rate?

answers.text: 975 gpd/sq ft
487.5 gpd/sq ft
1,462.5 gpd/sq ft
1,950 gpd/sq ft

questions.explanation: Overflow rate = flow ÷ surface area = 877,500 gpd ÷ 900 sq ft = 975 gpd/sq ft. Watching this rate tells the operator how hydraulically loaded the clarifier is.

questions.question: During a digester cleaning, the crew finds a deep layer of grit that has steadily reduced the tank's working volume. Which upstream check does this finding call for?

answers.text: Check whether the chlorine contact basin residual has been high enough over the past operating season
Check digester heating and mixing first
Evaluate grit removal performance, since grit that passes fills downstream tanks
Check the effluent weirs on the primary clarifiers

questions.explanation: Grit that is not removed upstream wears pumps and fills tanks, so grit banked in a digester is evidence the grit stage is passing material it should capture. Chlorine residual, digester heating, and effluent weirs do not explain grit arriving from the headworks.

questions.question: The sludge blanket in a secondary clarifier is deepening while the aeration basin MLSS is dropping. Which adjustment moves the solids back where they belong?

answers.text: Waste much more sludge each shift so that less sludge remains anywhere in the system at all
Increase the return activated sludge rate to transfer settled solids from the clarifier back to the basin
Decrease the return rate further so the clarifier can compact a much thicker blanket
Stop aeration for a while so the floc in the basin settles and the blanket stabilizes without waiting for any laboratory result to come back first

questions.explanation: The solids have not disappeared — they are sitting in the clarifier instead of the basin. Raising the return rate pumps them back to the aeration basin, lowering the blanket and restoring basin MLSS. Wasting more or returning less pushes the system further in the wrong direction.

questions.question: Settleability tests over several days show settling getting poorer and the clarifier blanket climbing, a bulking pattern. Which response follows sound Grade II practice?

answers.text: Double the wasting rate and halve the return rate on the same day so the correction takes effect quickly during the busiest part of the operating shift
Stop all wasting for two weeks so the organisms can recover without disturbance
Drain the aeration basin and reseed it with sludge hauled from the nearest neighboring plant
Verify dissolved oxygen, follow the SVI trend, and adjust return or wasting gradually — one change at a time, then observe

questions.explanation: Bulking — high SVI and poor settling, classically from filamentous growth — is worked methodically: verify DO is present, track settleability and the SVI trend, and make gradual return or wasting adjustments one at a time, observing the result before the next change. Simultaneous large changes destroy the evidence of what worked.

questions.question: Primary clarifier percent removal dips on a day when a larger-than-usual volume of digester supernatant was returned to the influent, while flows and blanket depths stayed normal. How should the lead operator interpret this?

answers.text: As proof the clarifier scrapers have failed and must be replaced that same shift and the clarifier must be drained for a full internal inspection before the next shift
As an added load effect from the returned supernatant, to be weighed before faulting the clarifier itself
As a disinfection problem, since supernatant return sets the chlorine demand
As normal wet-weather washout, even though no storm flows occurred that day

questions.explanation: Supernatant returned to the influent carries load back into the plant, so a removal dip coinciding with a large supernatant return is first interpreted as that added load effect before the clarifier itself is faulted.

questions.question: At the recognition level expected at Grade II, polymer in solids handling is understood as what?

answers.text: A conditioning practice sometimes applied to dewatering feeds before mechanical dewatering
A disinfectant added to digested sludge to destroy pathogens before hauling off site
A heating fuel burned in the digester boiler in place of collected digester gas
A coagulant dosed to the gravity thickener to settle incoming raw wastewater

questions.explanation: Polymer conditioning of dewatering feeds is recognized as a practice at Grade II: polymer may condition sludge ahead of mechanical dewatering equipment. Polymer doses are a higher-grade calculation and are not part of Grade II operation.

questions.question: A plant disinfects 0.042 million gallons of effluent in a day at a chlorine dose of 9.5 mg/L using chlorine gas. How many pounds of chlorine are used that day?
questions.explanation: Pounds = volume (MG) × dose (mg/L) × 8.34 = 0.042 × 9.5 × 8.34 = 3.33 lb of chlorine for the day.

questions.question: Dye added at a pond inlet reaches the outlet far sooner than the detention time suggests, and large areas of the pond look stagnant. What corrective approach fits this problem?

answers.text: Deepen the stagnant areas by adding fill until the pond holds twice its present working volume
Raise the chlorine dose at the outlet
Use baffles or multiple cells in series to prevent short-circuiting
Stop all influent flow for a full week

questions.explanation: Flow reaching the outlet too soon with dead zones elsewhere is short-circuiting. Baffles and multiple cells operated in series force the wastewater through the full pond volume and prevent it.

questions.question: A final effluent result comes back wildly out of line, but the plant looks normal and no process change was made. What is the first thing to check?

answers.text: Whether the influent pumps need repacking
Whether the aeration basins need new diffusers, new blowers, and a full process audit this week
The chlorine supplier's delivery schedule
Sampling error, such as the wrong point, a dirty bottle, or a stale sample

questions.explanation: Abnormal results are first checked against sampling error — wrong point, dirty bottle, or stale sample — before process changes are made. Equipment overhauls are not the first response to one suspect result.

questions.question: During a loading check, flow through a grit channel is 8.0 cubic feet per second and the channel cross-sectional area is 1.5 square feet. What is the flow velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity = flow ÷ area = 8.0 cfs ÷ 1.5 sq ft = 5.33 ft/s. Multiplying gives 12.00 ft/s, using flow alone gives 8.00 ft/s, and inverting the division gives 0.19 ft/s.

questions.question: How can education figure into qualifying for a higher wastewater certification grade, at the program-structure level?

answers.text: Education cannot count toward qualification in any circumstance at all
Education replaces the examination requirement for the higher grade
Education can substitute for part of the experience requirement
Education raises the plant's classification instead of the operator's grade

questions.explanation: At the program-structure level, education can substitute for part of the experience requirement for a higher grade. It does not replace the examination, and it affects the operator's qualification, not the plant's classification.

california-wastewater-grade-1.quiz_title: California Wastewater Grade 1 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: When an unsafe condition is found during a plant round, what is the correct response?

answers.text: Work around the condition and finish the round without mentioning it to anyone else on shift
Wait until the condition causes an injury or equipment damage before reporting it to a supervisor
Report the condition so it can be corrected rather than working around it
Cover the condition with equipment or materials so it is no longer visible during inspections

questions.explanation: Unsafe conditions are reported and corrected rather than worked around. Hiding a condition, waiting for an injury, or simply avoiding the spot leaves the hazard in place for the next worker.

questions.question: A primary clarifier influent sample shows 235 mg/L suspended solids and the effluent shows 98 mg/L. What is the percent removal?
A supervisor asks an operator to schedule lubrication for the clarifier drives using plant records. Which record directly supports that scheduling?

answers.text: The daily influent flow totals recorded at the Parshall flume over the same period as the maintenance
The laboratory suspended solids results for the primary effluent samples collected during the prior week
The count of loads of screenings hauled away from the headworks since the drives were last serviced fully
The equipment run hours logged for the drives on every shift

questions.explanation: Flows, sludge pumping times and volumes, equipment run hours, and unusual conditions are logged every shift. The logged run hours for the drives are the record that times their inspection and lubrication.

questions.question: The sludge blanket in a primary clarifier is rising toward the surface. What is the best first operating response?

answers.text: Increase the sludge pumping or withdrawal rate
Stop all sludge pumping until the blanket settles
Raise the effluent weirs above the water level
Add more influent flow to the clarifier

questions.explanation: A rising sludge blanket means settled solids are accumulating faster than they are removed. Increasing sludge pumping or withdrawal rate draws the blanket down.

questions.question: A plant flow of 0.47 MGD carries a solids concentration of 185 mg/L. How many pounds per day of solids are in the flow?

answers.text: 86.95 lb/day
725.16 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = Flow in MGD x concentration in mg/L x 8.34 = 0.47 x 185 x 8.34 = 725.16 lb/day.

questions.question: A plant produces more digester gas than it needs for heating on a given day. How is the excess gas properly handled?

answers.text: It is released raw at ground level beside the digester building
It is burned in a flare (waste gas burner) or used as fuel
It is piped into a confined space to displace stale air there
It is stored in an open tank until the pressure builds up again

questions.explanation: Digester gas is used as fuel, for example for heating or engines, and gas that cannot be used is wasted to a flare (waste gas burner) rather than released raw.

questions.question: A drum of sodium hypochlorite solution has been stored warm, near acid containers, for a long period. What should the operator expect and do?

answers.text: Expect gained strength; warm storage near acids improves the solution when checked during a normal working shift
Expect lost strength; store hypochlorite away from acids and heat and check its condition
Use it without checking, since hypochlorite never changes in storage
Mix it with acid to restore strength before feeding it

questions.explanation: Hypochlorite solutions are stored away from acids and heat and lose strength with time, so aged warm-stored solution should be expected to be weaker and handled accordingly.

questions.question: A pond receives a BOD load of 186 lb/day over a surface area of 6.2 acres. What is the organic loading?

answers.text: 24 lb/day/acre
37.2 lb/day/acre
18.6 lb/day/acre
30 lb/day/acre

questions.explanation: Organic loading = BOD load ÷ Area = 186 ÷ 6.2 = 30 lb/day/acre. This pond-frame loading is the controlling duty for stabilization ponds.

questions.question: Why is a flow-proportional composite preferred for representing loading?

answers.text: It can be stored warm without changing
It eliminates the need to label the sample bottle with location, date, or time
Its portions vary with flow, matching the load carried
It measures chlorine residual at one instant

questions.explanation: In a flow-proportional composite the portion sizes vary with flow, so the combined sample matches the load actually carried during the period.

questions.question: A 150 mL portion of a well-mixed sludge sample is filtered and dried, leaving a residue of 36.9 mg. What is the solids concentration?

answers.text: 246 mg/L

questions.explanation: Solids concentration = residue (mg) x 1000 / sample volume (mL) = 36.9 x 1000 / 150 = 246 mg/L.

questions.question: One primary clarifier is taken out of service for maintenance while the plant keeps treating wastewater through the remaining units. Does the certified-staffing requirement still apply during this period?

answers.text: No, staffing rules pause whenever any unit is down
Only if the maintenance lasts longer than one shift
Only the maintenance crew needs to be certified during the work, and then only while the removed unit is actually open for repair
Yes; the plant is still operating, so it must remain properly staffed by certified operators

questions.explanation: A plant that is treating wastewater is operating, even with a unit out of service. Every plant must be properly staffed by certified operators when operating, so the requirement continues throughout the maintenance period.

questions.question: A storm causes a bypass of untreated wastewater at a plant. What duty does this event trigger for the operating staff?

answers.text: Wait a full month before mentioning it to anyone, so the monthly summary can be prepared first and the event described in general terms only
Notification to the overseeing authorities, as the permit requires for bypasses
Record it only in a private notebook kept at home
Report it only if a neighbor happens to complain

questions.explanation: Effluent violations, bypasses, and spills trigger notification duties to the overseeing authorities, reported as the permit requires.

excpt.quiz_title: ExCPT Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: The technician finds an expired hazardous medication in segregated stock, and a coworker suggests tossing it into the regular pharmacy trash to clear the holding area before an inspection. Regarding disposal of this product, what is the best action?

answers.text: Place the product in the designated hazardous-waste container following pharmacy procedure and its safety information, notify the pharmacist, and document the handling
Follow the coworker's suggestion, since the quantity is small
Pour the medication out and place only the empty container in the regular trash
Return the expired hazardous medication to the active shelf until a waste pickup is scheduled

questions.explanation: A is correct: hazardous medications require the designated hazardous-waste stream, pharmacist notification, and documentation, regardless of quantity. B is wrong because regular trash does not contain or lawfully dispose of hazardous pharmaceutical waste. C is wrong because pouring out the contents spreads the hazard and still leaves improper disposal of the residue. D is wrong because returning expired stock to the active shelf risks it being dispensed.

questions.question: Working the weekly order for a maintenance medication, the technician uses the item's par level of 120 units. The shelf count is 35 units and 20 units are already on order and in transit. Regarding order-quantity calculation in inventory management, how many additional units should the technician order to bring the item up to par?

answers.text: 105 units, by adding the on-order quantity to the shelf count and ordering that total
65 units, because par minus the combined shelf count and on-order quantity is 120 minus 55
85 units, because only the shelf count is subtracted from par and stock in transit is ignored
120 units, because a full par quantity is ordered whenever the shelf count falls below par

questions.explanation: The key is right because the quantity needed is par (120) minus everything already available or arriving (35 on the shelf plus 20 on order = 55), which equals 65 units. Option A is wrong because it adds the available stock to par instead of subtracting it, over-ordering badly. Option C is wrong because ignoring the 20 units already in transit would duplicate stock the pharmacy is about to receive. Option D is wrong because ordering a full par quantity regardless of stock on hand ignores both the shelf count and the pending shipment.

questions.question: At the drive-through window, a patient asks the technician to increase a noncontrolled refill from a 30-day quantity to a 90-day quantity, saying the prescriber mentioned the change during a visit but no new prescription or authorization has reached the pharmacy. Regarding this quantity-change request for a noncontrolled refill, what should the technician do?

answers.text: Increase the quantity, because the patient is reporting what the prescriber said
Dispense the 30-day quantity twice and document the second fill as part of the requested change
Keep the authorized quantity unchanged and refer the request to the pharmacist so the change can be confirmed with the prescriber
Refuse to process any refill for the patient until they bring a handwritten note from the prescriber

questions.explanation: The key is correct because a technician may not change the authorized quantity of a refill on a patient's report alone; the pharmacist must confirm any change with the prescriber. A is wrong because a patient's account of a conversation is not prescriber authorization. B is wrong because manufacturing an extra fill misrepresents what was authorized and corrupts the dispensing record. D is wrong because the original authorized refill can still be addressed through the pharmacist rather than being blocked outright by the technician.

questions.question: A patient asks that their noncontrolled prescription, which still has refills, be transferred out to a pharmacy closer to their new home. Regarding the technician's role in this transfer request, which action is correct?

answers.text: Collect the receiving pharmacy's information and the prescription details and bring the request to the pharmacist so the transfer is completed and documented as required
Tell the patient transfers are not allowed for any prescription with refills remaining
Hand the patient a photocopy of the original prescription and tell them that serves as the transfer
Delete the prescription from the profile once the patient says they are leaving

questions.explanation: A is correct because the technician gathers the receiving pharmacy's information and prescription details and brings the request to the pharmacist so the transfer is properly completed and documented. B is wrong because a noncontrolled prescription with refills remaining can be transferred. C is wrong because a photocopy handed to the patient is not a pharmacy-to-pharmacy transfer. D is wrong because deleting the record destroys documentation the transfer and the patient's history require.

questions.question: Regarding routes of administration for insulin injected into the fatty tissue just under the skin of the abdomen, which route does this administration use?

answers.text: Subcutaneous route
Intramuscular route
Intravenous route
Intradermal route

questions.explanation: A is correct because injection into the fatty tissue just under the skin is the subcutaneous route, the usual route for insulin. B is wrong because intramuscular injection delivers medication deep into a muscle. C is wrong because intravenous administration delivers medication directly into a vein. D is wrong because intradermal injection is placed within the skin layers, as for certain skin tests, not into subcutaneous fat.

questions.question: Interpreting percent strength for a solution labeled 8% w/v, the technician must state how much drug is contained in 200 mL. Percent w/v means grams of drug per 100 mL of solution. How many grams are in 200 mL?

answers.text: 8 g

questions.explanation: An 8% w/v solution contains 8 g per 100 mL, so 200 mL contains 8 x (200/100) = 16 g, so A is correct. B (8 g) is only the amount in 100 mL and ignores the 200 mL volume. C (20 g) would correspond to a 10% solution, not 8%. D (25 g) comes from dividing 200 by 8, which is not the percent w/v relationship.

questions.question: A patient brings back unused tablets of a medication identified as hazardous and asks the technician to put them back on the shelf so another patient can use them. Regarding these returned hazardous tablets, what should the technician do?

answers.text: Return the tablets to stock if the vial seal still looks intact
Segregate the returned tablets and route them to hazardous waste disposal under the pharmacist's direction, without returning them to stock
Place the tablets in the ordinary trash so they leave the pharmacy quickly
Hold the tablets at the counter to hand to the next patient with the same prescription

questions.explanation: B is correct because medication returned from a patient cannot go back into dispensing stock, and a hazardous product must be segregated and disposed of as hazardous waste under the pharmacist's direction. A is wrong because an intact-looking seal does not restore a returned medication to stock; its storage history outside the pharmacy is unknown. C is wrong because hazardous drugs must never enter ordinary trash. D is wrong because dispensing one patient's returned medication to another patient is unsafe and prohibited.

questions.question: With alligation, a technician must prepare 240 mL of a 4% solution by mixing an 8% solution and a 2% solution. In alligation, parts of the higher strength equal the desired strength minus the lower strength, and parts of the lower strength equal the higher strength minus the desired strength. How many milliliters of the 8% solution are needed?

answers.text: 120 mL
80 mL
160 mL
40 mL

questions.explanation: B is correct: parts of the higher strength = 4 - 2 = 2 parts, parts of the lower strength = 8 - 4 = 4 parts, for 6 total parts, and 2/6 x 240 mL = 80 mL of the 8% solution. A is wrong because it splits the total evenly, ignoring the alligation parts. C is wrong because it gives the volume of the 2% solution (4/6 x 240 mL), not the 8% solution asked for. D is wrong because it uses 1 part of the total instead of the calculated 2 parts.

questions.question: A claim rejects because the submitted package code for a 100-count bottle is not covered, while the plan covers the same drug and strength in a 30-count package. Analyzing this formulary coverage situation, what should the technician do?

answers.text: Alert the pharmacist, and if the pharmacist approves using the covered package, update the claim to the package code of the product actually dispensed and resubmit
Submit the covered 30-count package code but dispense from the 100-count bottle to save time
Switch the prescription to a different covered drug in the same class without contacting anyone
Split the claim into several smaller claims under the uncovered package code until it pays

questions.explanation: A is correct because coverage here turns on the package actually dispensed; with pharmacist approval the technician can dispense the covered package and submit its matching code. B is wrong because submitting one package code while dispensing another misrepresents the product dispensed. C is wrong because changing the drug is a prescriber and pharmacist decision, not a technician substitution. D is wrong because splitting claims to bypass a coverage rule misrepresents the transaction.

questions.question: Checking a gravity IV flow rate, a technician verifies an infusion of 900 mL to run over 3 hours using a set with a drop factor of 20 gtt/mL. Using gtt/min = (mL/hr x drop factor) / 60, what is the flow rate in drops per minute?

answers.text: 25 gtt/min
50 gtt/min
75 gtt/min
100 gtt/min

questions.explanation: First, 900 mL / 3 hours = 300 mL/hr. Then (300 x 20) / 60 = 6,000 / 60 = 100 gtt/min, so D is correct. A (25 gtt/min) understates the rate fourfold. B (50 gtt/min) results from halving the correct rate, as if the infusion ran over 6 hours. C (75 gtt/min) would fit a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL, not the stated 20 gtt/mL.

questions.question: Shortly after receiving a vaccination at the pharmacy, a patient reports an unexpected serious reaction to the technician at the counter before the pharmacist is aware of it. Regarding external adverse event reporting for vaccines, what should the technician do?

answers.text: Reassure the patient that post-vaccination reactions are routine and make no record of the report
Document the report promptly with the details provided and bring it to the pharmacist without delay, so the pharmacist can assess it and handle reporting to the national vaccine adverse event system
Complete and submit the national vaccine adverse event report on their own and take no action inside the pharmacy
Record the report in a personal note and raise it at the next monthly staff meeting

questions.explanation: B is correct because the technician's role is to capture the report accurately in the pharmacy record and escalate it promptly to the pharmacist, who assesses the event and handles external reporting to the vaccine adverse event reporting system. A is wrong because dismissing a serious reported reaction without a record prevents any assessment. C is wrong because submitting the external report independently, with no internal record or pharmacist involvement, bypasses the assessment step. D is wrong because a serious reaction report cannot wait for a monthly meeting or live outside the pharmacy record.

questions.question: An order for a medication scheduled on three set days each week arrives with its frequency written only as 'TIW.' Analyzing the risk in this error-prone abbreviation, what should the technician do?

answers.text: Interpret it as twice weekly, since that reading uses fewer doses and is safer
Interpret it as three times a day, since daily schedules are more common
Recognize that 'TIW' can be misread as three times daily or as twice weekly, and seek clarification so the intended frequency is written out in full
