questions.question: Accuracy testing shows one meter size class failing low in large numbers while other classes test well. How should the chief operator direct the replacement budget?

answers.text: Spread the replacement money evenly across every size class in the system, regardless of what the accuracy test results actually showed
Replace only the meters of customers who dispute their bills
Postpone all replacement until every class fails at the same rate
Concentrate replacement on the failing size class, where lost registration is actually occurring

questions.explanation: Test results identify where registration is being lost, so the budget follows that evidence to the failing class. Even spreading ignores the test data, complaint-driven replacement misses silent under-registration, and waiting for uniform failure leaves known losses in place.

questions.question: A growing utility assembling its rate case groups the coming year's spending into four amounts: $3,150,000 to operate and maintain the system, $1,120,000 of capital spending, $640,000 of debt service, and $390,000 to build reserves. How much must its rates recover in all over the year?
questions.explanation: Total annual expenditures = operations and maintenance + capital expenditures + debt service + reserve contributions = $3,150,000 + $1,120,000 + $640,000 + $390,000 = $5,300,000. Leaving out the reserve contributions gives $4,910,000 and leaving out debt service gives $4,660,000; counting the capital expenditures twice gives $6,420,000.

questions.question: A water system's annual figures are: operations and maintenance expenditures $1,840,000; capital expenditures $625,000; debt service $412,500; reserve contributions $260,000. What are the system's total annual expenditures?
questions.explanation: Total annual expenditures = operations and maintenance + capital expenditures + debt service + reserve contributions = $1,840,000 + $625,000 + $412,500 + $260,000 = $3,137,500. Leaving out the reserve contributions gives $2,877,500 and leaving out debt service gives $2,725,000; counting the capital expenditures twice gives $3,762,500.

questions.question: A system contracts with an outside firm to prepare a cost-of-service rate study and with outside counsel to review the adoption documents. In the operations and maintenance budget, those contracted costs belong to which component?

answers.text: Professional services, because specialized work is being purchased from outside firms
Supplies, because the firms will deliver printed reports
Water, because the study concerns the water the system sells, in all cases, whether or not the system's own experience supports doing so
Labor, because system staff will read the finished study

questions.explanation: Contracted engineering, analytical, and legal work is professional services in the operations and maintenance component list. The reports' paper does not make them supplies, the subject matter does not move them to the water component, and staff time spent reading them does not convert a contract into labor.

questions.question: Planners sizing supply for a new development phase expect the area to house 42,000 people at build-out, and they apply a per-capita use figure of 125 gallons per person daily. How much water should they expect the built-out area to need each day, expressed in MGD?

answers.text: 5.25 MGD
4.20 MGD
6.30 MGD
5.75 MGD

questions.explanation: Future needs = population x per-capita use = 42,000 people x 125 gallons per person per day = 5,250,000 gallons per day = 5.25 MGD. The lower and higher figures come from using a smaller or larger per-capita value than the one given, not from the stated inputs.

questions.question: A system buys wholesale water from a neighboring agency to supplement its own sources. In the operations and maintenance budget, that purchase belongs to which component?

answers.text: Supplies, because the water is a material the system takes into stock
Energy, because the water arrives under pressure from the agency
Water, the component covering purchased or wholesale water
Capital improvement, because the purchased water becomes a system asset

questions.explanation: The water component of the operations and maintenance budget exists for purchased and wholesale water. Supplies covers materials and chemicals consumed, energy covers power, and capital improvement covers building or upgrading facilities; bought water is an operating purchase, not a facility.

questions.question: A service-line renewal program routinely joins new copper services to older galvanized piping left in place at some homes. Which program requirement best protects those joints?

answers.text: Separate them with a dielectric fitting to interrupt galvanic action
Paint the outside of the completed joint so the metals blend in appearance
Join the metals directly and rely on high flow to wash corrosion products away
Wrap the joint tightly in metal tape so both sides stay in firm electrical contact

questions.explanation: Copper joined directly to galvanized steel sets up galvanic action that attacks the more active metal at the joint; a dielectric separation interrupts that cell. Paint and appearance do not stop the reaction, flow does not prevent it, and metal tape preserves the very electrical contact that must be broken.

questions.question: A saturated formation sample with a total volume of 82,000 gal drains 18,500 gal of water by gravity. What is the specific yield, as a percent?

answers.text: About 18.05%
About 22.56%
About 27.07%
About 77.44%

questions.explanation: Specific yield = volume released / total volume x 100 = 18,500 / 82,000 x 100 = about 22.56%. The other values come from using the wrong volume in the numerator or from reporting the retained share instead of the share that drained by gravity.

questions.question: Which group consists of human-made organic chemicals most associated with industrial and degreasing activity reaching groundwater?

answers.text: Calcium and magnesium salts dissolved from limestone, on the assumption that no follow-up verification will be needed afterward
Iron and manganese released from aquifer minerals
Solvents and related synthetic organic chemicals from industrial use and spills
Sand and silt carried in by a flooded wellhead

questions.explanation: Industrial solvents are synthetic organic chemicals that reach groundwater through use, disposal, and spills. Calcium, magnesium, iron, and manganese are inorganic minerals, and sand and silt are physical sediment, not organic contamination.

california-water-distribution-d4.quiz_title: California Water Distribution D4 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Winter water is cold and disinfection is slower, but a contact tank cannot be held longer this week because the system needs its storage back for supply security each morning. The residual, however, has room to rise within its normal operating band. What is the chief operator's soundest way to protect the disinfection credit?

answers.text: Accept the lower credit, because cold water also preserves the residual longer
Raise the residual during the hold so the residual-times-time product is restored at the shorter contact time
Warm the tank contents with the building heating system before each hold period and keep them warm until the tank returns to service each morning
Credit the tank with summer contact-time values until the weather turns warmer

questions.explanation: CT is the product of residual and contact time. When cold water slows disinfection and the available contact time is capped by storage needs, raising the residual during the hold restores the product honestly. Crediting time or performance the water never received is not an option.

questions.question: The crew disinfecting a coastal well will chlorinate from the liquid product on the truck: sodium hypochlorite at 10% available chlorine, weighing 9.8 lb per gallon. The job covers 0.09 MG of water and the foreman has set the dose at 26 mg/L. How many gallons of the liquid product must the crew draw?

answers.text: 16.58 gallons
23.90 gallons
21.75 gallons
19.91 gallons

questions.explanation: Gallons = volume (MG) x dose (mg/L) x 8.34 / (strength x solution weight) = 0.09 x 26 x 8.34 / (0.10 x 9.8) = 19.91 gallons.

questions.question: Before cleaning, a main at a set flow had a steep hydraulic gradient. After the main is cleaned and the same flow is restored, its gradient is noticeably flatter. What is the sound conclusion?

answers.text: Cleaning reduced the friction in the main, so less head is now consumed per unit length at that flow
Cleaning raised the friction in the main, and the flatter line is only an error in the new gauge readings
The gradient change proves the main's diameter was permanently enlarged by the cleaning equipment used
No conclusion is possible, because a gradient measured after cleaning can never be compared with one before

questions.explanation: At the same flow, a flatter gradient means less head loss per unit length. Cleaning removed interior roughness and deposits, so friction fell and more head survives to the far end of the main.

questions.question: What do accumulated run-time records for pumps and motors primarily enable a chief operator to do?

answers.text: Prove that a pump has never operated outside its warranty period
Schedule inspections, lubrication, and overhauls by actual use rather than by guesswork or breakdown
Replace the need for any pressure or flow testing of the equipment
Set the retail water rate charged to customers served by the station under all operating conditions the station will ever be expected to see

questions.explanation: Run-time records convert maintenance from calendar guesswork or failure response into use-based scheduling. They show which units are carrying the load and when inspections and overhauls are actually due.

questions.question: A well pump must deliver 620 gallons per minute against a total head of 140 feet. Its efficiency at that duty is 72 percent. Calculate the brake horsepower required.
questions.explanation: Water horsepower = 620 x 140 / 3960 = 21.92 hp. Brake horsepower = 21.92 / 0.72 = 30.44 hp.

questions.question: Under the Lead and Copper Rule, an action-level exceedance is judged on what basis?

answers.text: The 90th-percentile value of the tap samples, compared against the action level
The single highest tap sample collected anywhere in the system during the round
The average of every tap sample collected during the monitoring round
The result from the sample collected closest to the treatment plant entry point

questions.explanation: An action-level exceedance is judged on the 90th-percentile value of the tap samples compared against the action level — neither the single highest sample nor a simple average of all results. An exceedance is not itself a violation, but it triggers required follow-up actions under the Lead and Copper Rule.

questions.question: A confirmed result establishes a maximum contaminant level violation. A sample taken weeks later is below the level. What is the status of the violation?

answers.text: It stands — the violation must still be addressed through the required notification and correction, despite the later lower result
It is cancelled automatically, because any later passing result erases an earlier violation
It never existed, because the later result is the most recent information about the system

It converts into a secondary-standard issue, because time has passed since the confirmed result, because the newest laboratory report is always the one that decides whether a violation ever existed in the first place

questions.explanation: A later lower sample does not erase a confirmed violation; the violation stands and the required notification and correction still apply. The later result is useful operating information, not a cancellation.

questions.question: A Grade D4 distribution operator is planning continuing education for the upcoming renewal and wants the total for the full cycle. The certificate renews on a 3-year cycle — how many contact hours in total must be completed during that cycle?

answers.text: 12 contact hours per 3-year renewal cycle, which is the requirement associated with the lowest distribution grade level in California
16 contact hours per 3-year renewal cycle, which is the requirement associated with the second distribution grade level in California
24 contact hours per 3-year renewal cycle, which is the requirement associated with the third distribution grade level in California
36 contact hours per 3-year renewal cycle

questions.explanation: Grade D4 renewal requires 36 contact hours per 3-year cycle. The 12-, 16-, and 24-hour figures belong to the lower distribution grades.

questions.question: A planning study projects a population of 72,500 people using 120 gallons per person per day. What is the estimated future water need?

answers.text: 6.04 MGD
8.70 MGD
9.60 MGD
7.25 MGD

questions.question: A recently lined main has picked up loose sediment and stale water after a repair shutdown, and the lining must not be damaged by aggressive scraping. Which cleaning choice is proportionate?

answers.text: Drive a hard pig through the lined section repeatedly until the walls are scraped bare, because lining damage is an acceptable cost of cleaning
Use air scouring at maximum intensity as the first step, before trying any gentler method on a main whose deposits are loose and light
Cut out the lined section and replace it, because loose sediment after a shutdown can never be removed by any cleaning method available
Flush the main with system water to carry out the loose material without attacking the lining

questions.explanation: The deposit is loose and the pipe is lined, so flushing — the gentlest method — fits: it carries sediment and stale water out without scraping at the lining. Aggressive pigging belongs to heavy deposits in sound pipe.

questions.question: A crew verifying a new source meter runs water through a short test spool fitted with a velocity probe. The spool's cross-section measures 0.85 sq ft and the probe reads 2.35 ft/s. How much water is the spool passing, in gallons per minute?

answers.text: 2.00 gpm

questions.explanation: Flow = area x velocity x 448.8 = 0.85 sq ft x 2.35 ft/s x 448.8 = 896.46 gpm. Omitting the 448.8 conversion leaves only the cubic-feet-per-second figure.

questions.question: Which description fits a confined aquifer?

answers.text: It lies open to the ground surface along its whole length, so rain anywhere above it enters the formation immediately
It is a layer of clay at the surface that stores water tightly and is pumped directly as the producing formation
It is sandwiched between low-permeability layers, and its water is under pressure within the formation
It has no confining beds and no pressure, so a well in it can never rise above the top of the formation

questions.explanation: A confined aquifer is sandwiched between low-permeability layers (aquitards or confining beds), and its water is under pressure.

california-water-distribution-d3.quiz_title: California Water Distribution D3 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: The free chlorine in a sample consists of the sum of which two chemical forms?

answers.text: Chloramine plus ammonia
Hypochlorous acid plus hypochlorite ion
Hydrochloric acid plus chloride under the conditions described in this situation
Ozone plus dissolved oxygen

questions.explanation: Free chlorine is defined as the hypochlorous acid and hypochlorite ion present together; the acid form is the strong disinfectant and the ion is the weaker form.

questions.question: As part of a recoating estimate for a round tank 28 ft in diameter, the crew needs the interior side-wall area that stays submerged when the tank carries 12 ft of water. Compute that submerged wall area.

answers.text: 527.79 sq ft
336.00 sq ft

questions.explanation: Wall area = 3.1416 x diameter x depth = 3.1416 x 28 x 12 = 1,055.58 sq ft. The 336.00 figure multiplies diameter by depth alone, omitting the circumference factor.

questions.question: Heavy tuberculation has shrunk the open bore of a main, yet the system keeps pushing the same flow through it. Beyond the added roughness, why does head loss climb even further in this main?

answers.text: The smaller bore slows the water down, and slow water drags against the pipe wall for a longer time before it can get through the narrowed reach of pipe
The deposits give off heat as they grow, and warmer water always loses more head in a main
The flow begins to run uphill through the deposits, adding elevation lift that was not there before
The same flow squeezed through a smaller bore must move faster, and the higher velocity raises friction loss still more

questions.explanation: Squeezed through a smaller bore, the same flow must move faster, and the higher velocity raises friction loss still more, on top of the loss added by roughness. The water does not slow down, heat up, or gain elevation inside the deposits.

questions.question: An atmospheric vacuum breaker protects a connection by doing what when supply pressure is lost?

answers.text: Opening an air inlet that admits air and breaks the siphon before contaminated water can be drawn back
Closing a spring-loaded check that seals the outlet against any pressure coming from downstream and holds it closed until a worker resets the assembly by hand
Discharging water from a relief port until the downstream pressure falls below the supply pressure
Raising the outlet above the flood rim of the fixture so a physical air gap is formed in the piping

questions.explanation: When supply pressure is lost, the atmospheric vacuum breaker opens an air inlet that admits air and breaks the siphon before contaminated water can be drawn back. It has no check-and-relief arrangement, and it does not work by raising the outlet into an air gap.

questions.question: A well pump delivers 850 gpm against a total head of 118 ft at a pump efficiency of 74 percent. Calculate the brake horsepower required.
questions.explanation: Water hp = 850 x 118 / 3960 = 25.33 hp; brake hp = 25.33 / 0.74 = 34.23 hp. Multiplying by the efficiency instead of dividing understates the input power the driver must supply.

questions.question: On a gas chlorinator, what operating loss will stop chlorine feed even when the cylinder still holds gas?

answers.text: Loss of the paint finish on the outside of the cylinder
A rise in the temperature of the room housing the feeder during a warm afternoon
Loss of the vacuum that draws the gas through the chlorinator
A change in the color of the solution in the sight glass

questions.explanation: Gas feeders depend on vacuum to draw gas through the injector system, so a loss of vacuum stops feed despite gas in the cylinder. Room temperature, paint, and sight-glass color do not drive the feed.

questions.question: When a replacement pump is being selected from manufacturers' curves, what must its curve do at the station's required duty?

answers.text: Reach the highest shutoff head of any pump offered, regardless of the flow delivered at duty
Stay below the system curve at every flow, so the pump is never asked to work very hard
Pass through the required flow and head duty point
Match the physical casing dimensions of the old pump, which guarantees the duty is met

questions.explanation: The selected pump's curve must pass through the required flow and head duty point; that crossing is where the pump will actually operate in the system. Shutoff head or casing size alone does not prove the duty is met.

questions.question: A cylindrical tank is 9 ft in diameter with a water depth of 11 ft. How many gallons of water does it hold?
questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 x diameter squared x depth x 7.48 = 0.785 x 81 x 11 x 7.48 = 5,231.77 gal. Omitting the 7.48 conversion leaves cubic feet, not gallons.

questions.question: A sampling crew arrives at a selected high-risk home and, out of habit, flushes the tap for several minutes before filling the lead and copper sample bottle. Why is that sample compromised?

answers.text: The sample is fine because flushing is required before every sample of every kind in distribution work
The sample is compromised only because the bottle was filled during daylight rather than at night
Flushing improves the sample by removing the water that had contacted the household lead plumbing
Lead and copper samples must be first-draw after standing in the plumbing

questions.explanation: Lead and Copper Rule samples are first-draw samples taken after the water has stood in the plumbing. Flushing first removes exactly the standing water the sample is meant to capture.

questions.question: Operators checking a transmission main read the master meter: 900 gallons per minute are passing through pipe whose inside bore is 1.25 ft across. From these readings, find how fast the water is traveling, in feet per second.
questions.explanation: Velocity = (flow / 448.8) / (0.785 x D^2) = (900 / 448.8) / (0.785 x 1.25^2) = 1.63 ft/s. Forgetting to square the diameter understates the velocity, and using the radius in place of the diameter overstates it.

questions.question: A contractor excavates a trench for a new main: 52 ft in length, 4 ft across, and 5 ft deep. Billing is per cubic yard of soil removed. How many cubic yards should appear on the bill?

answers.text: 1040.00 cubic yards
19.26 cubic yards
38.52 cubic yards
77.04 cubic yards

questions.explanation: Volume = length x width x depth / 27 = 52 x 4 x 5 / 27 = 38.52 cubic yards. Skipping the division by 27 leaves the answer in cubic feet, not cubic yards.

questions.question: Which activity is a recognized source of organic contaminants in a water supply?

answers.text: Groundwater dissolving calcium and magnesium out of limestone as it moves through the formation over many years
Industrial discharges releasing organic chemicals into the water
Corrosion of household plumbing slowly releasing dissolved metals into water standing in the pipes
Rainwater picking up dissolved minerals from bare rock on hillsides far above the intake structure

questions.explanation: Industrial discharges are a recognized source of organic contaminants, alongside fuels, solvents, and pesticides reaching water through spills, leaks, and runoff.

california-water-distribution-d2.quiz_title: California Water Distribution D2 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An operator needs both the free and the total chlorine of a distribution sample using DPD. How are the two values obtained?

answers.text: By a single DPD reading, which reports free and total chlorine as the same number whenever the sample comes from a system that uses chlorine in any form at all
By measuring free chlorine with DPD and estimating total chlorine from the chlorine dose applied at the plant, since total chlorine cannot be measured in the field
By filtering the sample to remove the combined chlorine and then reading the filtrate twice, once for the free portion and once for the portion removed by the filter
By DPD colorimetric readings for free chlorine and for total chlorine on the sample, with combined chlorine taken as the difference

questions.explanation: The DPD colorimetric method measures free chlorine and total chlorine; combined chlorine is the difference between the total and free readings on the same sample.

questions.question: About how much available chlorine does calcium hypochlorite (HTH) contain?

answers.text: About 5 to 10 percent
About 25 percent
About 65 to 70 percent
Essentially 100 percent

questions.explanation: Calcium hypochlorite is a solid carrying roughly 65 to 70 percent available chlorine, which is why dosage calculations for it divide by the product strength.

questions.question: Which set contains only disadvantages or risks of chloramination?

answers.text: Weaker and slower disinfection, a residual that disappears faster than free chlorine, and trihalomethane formation higher than with free chlorination of the same water
Nitrification risk, complete inability to maintain any residual at dead ends, and a requirement to dechlorinate all water before it can be served to customers
Taste or odor if di- or trichloramine forms, formation of ozone in the mains, and a residual that cannot be measured by any chlorine test available to operators
Weaker and slower disinfection, nitrification risk, and taste or odor if di- or trichloramine forms

questions.explanation: The disadvantages are the weak, slow disinfection (far more contact is needed), the nitrification risk from excess ammonia, and taste and odor when dichloramine or trichloramine forms instead of monochloramine.

questions.question: An 18-inch transmission main (1.5 ft in diameter) carries 2,000 gallons per minute. What is the velocity of the water in the main?
questions.explanation: Flow = 2,000 / 448.8 = 4.46 cfs. Area = 0.785 x 1.5^2 = 1.766 sq ft. Velocity = 4.46 / 1.766 = 2.52 ft/s. The 4.46 value is the flow in cubic feet per second, not the velocity, because it was never divided by the area.

questions.question: A pressure gauge on a distribution main reads 31 psi. How many feet of head does that pressure represent?

answers.text: 62 ft
93 ft

questions.explanation: Head = psi x 2.31 = 31 x 2.31 = 71.61 ft. Dividing by 2.31 gives 13.42 ft, and using a factor of 2.0 or 3.0 gives the other incorrect figures.

questions.question: To report the average rate at which water left a storage facility during a drawdown period, which approach is correct?

answers.text: Divide the tank's total rated capacity by its age in years of service
Read the static pressure at the base of the tank one single time
Multiply the tank diameter by the depth of water inside the tank
Divide the volume change by the time it took

questions.explanation: A storage facility flow rate comes from a known volume change over a known time: rate equals volume divided by time. A single pressure reading gives head, not a rate, and tank dimensions alone give volume, not flow.

questions.question: What does an in-line (continuous) chlorine analyzer do during normal operation?

answers.text: It continuously samples the flowing water and reports the residual, alarming on out-of-range values
It samples the water once a month and mails the result away
It adds chlorine to the water whenever the flow increases so the residual never falls at peak demand
It stores a day's flow so it can be analyzed the next morning

questions.explanation: An in-line analyzer continuously samples the water and reports values such as chlorine residual, alarming on out-of-range readings. It measures rather than feeds chemical, and its whole purpose is continuous rather than monthly or next-day information.

questions.question: Chemical solution is metered into a flow of 0.85 MGD at a booster station to deliver a dose of 3.1 mg/L. The product's purity is 55 percent and each gallon of it weighs 9.6 lb. How many gallons per day must the feeder deliver?

answers.text: 4.16 gal/day
2.29 gal/day
7.92 gal/day
1.85 gal/day

questions.explanation: Solution feed = MGD x mg/L x 8.34 / [(purity as decimal) x lb/gal] = 0.85 x 3.1 x 8.34 / (0.55 x 9.6) = 21.98 / 5.28 = 4.16 gal/day. The 2.29 figure omits the purity correction.

questions.question: What do the records of a fire hydrant testing program document?

answers.text: Only the names of the crew members who attended the testing that day and signed the work order before leaving the site
The water rates charged in the surrounding blocks
The flow-test results and the condition found for each hydrant tested
The age of the pavement around each hydrant

questions.explanation: Testing records capture what the program found: how each hydrant flowed and what condition it was in. Those records are what let the system follow up on weak hydrants and show the program was carried out.

questions.question: Which list contains only recognized procedures for cleaning the inside of a water main?

answers.text: Flushing, sandblasting the outside of the barrel, and repainting the hydrants
Pigging, jetting the service laterals with a garden hose, and vacuuming the trench, none of which is a recognized way to clean the inside of a main in service
Air scouring, ice pigging, and relining the street above the main
Flushing, swabbing or pigging, air scouring, and ice pigging

questions.explanation: The recognized in-main cleaning procedures are flushing, swabbing or pigging, air scouring, and ice pigging; exterior surface work and street work are not pipe cleaning procedures.

questions.question: Water moves through a pipe 0.5 ft in diameter at 5.2 ft per second. How many gallons per minute is the pipe carrying at that velocity?
questions.explanation: Capacity Q = A x V = 0.785 x 0.5^2 x 5.2 = 1.02 cu ft per sec; x 448.8 = 458.00 gpm. The distractors use a wrong velocity, a wrong diameter, or a wrong conversion factor and do not equal the result.

questions.question: What is a presumptive result in water quality testing?

answers.text: A final verified result that closes out the sample, with no further testing of any kind needed afterward
A result the laboratory reports only after repeat sampling
A preliminary positive indication from an initial test, before confirmation
A negative result that presumes the water is safe

questions.explanation: A presumptive result is the preliminary indication from an initial test; it is not final until confirmatory testing verifies it. Treating a presumptive positive as already confirmed overstates what the first test shows.

california-water-distribution-d1.quiz_title: California Water Distribution D1 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A reservoir is refilled after cleaning, but loose debris and organic material were left on the floor. What effect does that material have on disinfection?

answers.text: None, because material on the floor cannot react with chlorine dissolved in the water stored above it during the holding period before sampling
It exerts chlorine demand, consuming disinfectant that would otherwise remain as a residual
It manufactures chlorine, so the measured residual rises on its own
It seals the floor so well that no disinfection is needed at all

questions.explanation: Organic matter and other reacting material consume chlorine. Debris left in a reservoir raises demand and leaves less of the dose available as a protective residual.

questions.question: A well contains 0.028 MG of water and is to be disinfected at a given dose of 60 mg/L using calcium hypochlorite that is 70% available chlorine. How many pounds of the solid product are required?
questions.explanation: Pounds (solid) = volume (MG) x dose x 8.34 / (strength/100) = 0.028 x 60 x 8.34 / 0.70 = 20.02 lb. Multiplying by the strength instead of dividing, or skipping the strength correction, both give too little product.

questions.question: A crew must shut off water to one house for a plumbing repair without disturbing the main or neighboring services. The shutoff at the property line, ahead of the meter, is operated. Which fitting is this, and what is its role?

answers.text: The corporation stop, which is the valve used to tap the main under pressure
The meter stop inside the building, which isolates a single fixture branch
A gate valve on the arterial main, which isolates the whole street segment
The curb stop, which shuts off the individual service at the property line

questions.explanation: The curb stop sits at the property line and shuts off the individual service, so one customer can be isolated without disturbing the main. The corporation stop is back at the main itself.

questions.question: While reading meters, an operator sees a garden hose from a house bibb lying submerged in a backyard tank of mixed pesticide solution, with no device on the bibb. How should this be reported?

answers.text: As routine yard use, because a hose bibb is part of the house plumbing and the tank is on private property
As an unprotected cross-connection, because the submerged hose links the potable supply to a contamination source
As a meter problem, because flow through a hose cannot be registered accurately
As a dead-end condition, because the hose is the last outlet on that service

questions.explanation: A hose submerged in a pesticide tank links the potable supply directly to a contamination source with no protection in between. That is an unprotected cross-connection and a backflow hazard if supply pressure drops.

questions.question: How much does 1 gallon of water weigh?
questions.explanation: The Equivalents sheet gives 1 gal of water = 8.34 lb. The 62.38 lb figure is the weight of one cubic foot of water, and 7.48 is the number of gallons in a cubic foot.

questions.question: A commercial meter showed 29,600 gallons at one reading and 87,200 gallons at a reading 32 days later. What was the average use in gallons per day?

answers.text: 1,800 gal/day
57,600 gal/day
900 gal/day
3,650 gal/day

questions.explanation: GPD = (read 2 − read 1) ÷ days = (87,200 − 29,600) ÷ 32 = 57,600 ÷ 32 = 1,800 gal/day. The 57,600 figure is the total for the whole period, not the daily average.

questions.question: Customers on a dead-end street report discolored water and a stale taste after a quiet period with little use on that street. What hydrant action addresses this?

answers.text: Paint the hydrant a bright color and return it to service at once, since appearance is what customers judge the water quality by
Close the hydrant's main valve and leave the street as is
Remove the hydrant caps and leave them off overnight
Flush the main through the hydrant to scour out sediment and stale water

questions.explanation: Flushing through a hydrant scours sediment and stale water from the main, which is the usual cause of discolored, stale-tasting water at a dead end. Painting or capping does nothing for the water in the main.

questions.question: A homeowner offers to run the kitchen tap for a while before you collect the lead and copper sample so the water is fresh. What should you do?

answers.text: Collect the sample first-draw, without flushing the tap beforehand
Flush the tap thoroughly, then collect the sample in the bottle
Collect the sample from the garden hose bib instead of the tap
Run the hot water tap until it is warm, then collect the sample

questions.explanation: The D1 skill is taking the sample first-draw, with no flushing first, at the approved site. Letting the homeowner flush first would change what the sample represents.

questions.question: A crew member must move a container of a hazardous material and notices its label is damaged. What is the safe course of action?

answers.text: Move it quickly to the truck so the damaged label is out of public view, and sort out what it was once it is safely inside the truck bed
Guess at the contents from the container shape and handle it as usual
Stop, identify the material and its handling requirements before moving it, using its safety information
Pour the contents into a clean unlabeled container for the trip back

questions.explanation: Hazardous material safety requires knowing what the material is and how it must be handled before moving it. Guessing, hiding the label problem, or transferring it to an unlabeled container creates new hazards.

questions.question: Where a pipeline steps down from a larger diameter to a smaller one and keeps running straight, which fitting makes that size change?

answers.text: Branch a side line off the main while the main continues through the junction
Close the end of a dead-end main so it can be reopened for a future extension
Connect a larger pipe to a smaller pipe, stepping the run down in size at the fitting
Join two plain pipe ends of the same size in the middle of a straight repair

questions.explanation: A reducer changes pipe size — that is its application among fittings. Branching is a tee's work, closing an end is a cap's, and joining equal plain ends is a coupling's.

questions.question: A trench 25 ft long, 4 ft wide, and 3 ft deep must be filled with water for a test. How many gallons of water will fill the trench?

answers.text: 300 gallons
1,122 gallons
2,244 gallons
7,480 gallons

questions.explanation: Rectangular volume in gallons = length x width x depth x 7.48 = 25 ft x 4 ft x 3 ft x 7.48 = 2,244 gal. The 300 figure is the cubic-foot volume before the gallons conversion.

questions.question: A presence/absence coliform test on a distribution sample reports absence. What does that result mean?

answers.text: The entire distribution system is guaranteed free of bacteria
The sample contained E. coli but at a level too low to report
No coliform was detected in the sample volume tested
No further routine monitoring is needed for the rest of the year

questions.explanation: Presence/absence testing reports presence or absence in the sample tested, so absence means no coliform was detected in that sample. It does not guarantee the whole system or end routine monitoring.

wastewater-collection-class-4.quiz_title: Wastewater Collection Class IV Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: In a utility's equipment standard, critical stations that use a variable frequency drive on a pump also specify a drive bypass. What operating need does the bypass provision serve?

answers.text: It lets the drive run at two different carrier frequencies during a single pumping cycle on alternating weeks so that each drive carries the station load equally often
It raises the pump's peak efficiency whenever the wet well is near its high level
It lets the pump keep running at full speed if the drive itself fails or is taken out of service
It replaces the need for a standby generator during a utility power outage at the station

questions.explanation: The bypass is a continuity provision: if the drive fails, the motor can run across the line at full speed so a critical station keeps pumping. It does not tune the drive, raise efficiency, or substitute for standby power, which addresses a different failure entirely.

questions.question: A chemical feed system doses odor-control chemical into a flow of 0.42 MGD at a dose of 16 mg/L. How many pounds of chemical per day must the feed system deliver?

answers.text: About 56.04 lb/day
About 6.72 lb/day
About 112.10 lb/day
About 28.02 lb/day

questions.explanation: lb/day = flow (MGD) x dose (mg/L) x 8.34 = 0.42 x 16 x 8.34 = 56.04 lb/day. Omitting the 8.34 factor gives 6.72, and doubling or halving the flow gives the other values; the feed system must be sized and stocked for the full daily requirement.

questions.question: Drone crews begin delivering sharp video of trunk structures, but the files sit in a separate folder system that the asset program cannot search or trend. What direction should the program head give?

answers.text: Let the drone files stay separate, since video quality matters more than whether the asset program can retrieve the records later
Delete drone findings that cannot be coded, so the asset database never shows a gap between inspected and recorded structures
Have each drone operator keep personal copies as backup, and treat those copies as the official record of each inspection performed
Require drone deliverables in the standard coding and asset record system, so findings trend with other inspection data

questions.explanation: Inspection data has program value only when it joins the common record: coded the same way, tied to the same assets, and retrievable beside CCTV and field findings. A separate silo of video cannot support trending, comparisons, or capital defense, no matter how sharp the footage is.

questions.question: An undersized main must be replaced with a larger pipe where it passes beneath a rail crossing, and the crossing owner will not permit open excavation in the crossing. What method direction should the director give?

answers.text: Line the existing pipe and accept the smaller diameter, since no other method can work under a crossing
Renew by pipe bursting, which replaces the host with a larger pipe along the existing alignment without open excavation
Reroute the main around the crossing at whatever length and cost the detour requires
Defer the renewal indefinitely, since an upsized replacement under a crossing is not achievable

questions.explanation: Pipe bursting is the trenchless replacement method that can increase diameter: the bursting head breaks the host outward while the new, larger pipe is pulled in behind it along the same alignment. Lining would preserve the undersized diameter that is the problem.

questions.question: A CSO basin returns stored flow through a conduit with a cross-sectional area of 4.1 square feet at a velocity of 3.85 feet per second. What flow is the conduit carrying, in gallons per minute?

answers.text: 7,084.3 gallons per minute
15.8 gallons per minute
1,577.0 gallons per minute
3,542.2 gallons per minute

questions.explanation: Step 1: Multiply area by velocity: 4.1 sq ft x 3.85 ft/s = 15.785 cubic feet per second. Step 2: Convert using 448.8 gallons per minute per cubic foot per second: 15.785 x 448.8 = 7,084.3 gallons per minute. Knowing the return conduit's carried flow lets the operator set a return rate the downstream system can accept.

questions.question: Plan drawings show the proposed trenchless renewal reach crossing beneath a pressurized water main, but the recorded depth of that main varies between two plan sets. Approving the method depends on the clearance. What should the director order?

answers.text: Expose the crossing by careful vacuum excavation and confirm its true depth and position before the method is approved
Approve the method using the shallower of the two recorded depths, since that is the more recent plan set
Move the renewal reach to a different street so the crossing never has to be dealt with
Let the renewal crew proceed slowly and stop only if they feel resistance at the crossing

questions.explanation: Conflicting record depths cannot settle a clearance question on which method approval depends. Vacuum excavation exposes the crossing safely and gives a measured depth and position, so the trenchless method is approved, modified, or rejected on fact.

questions.question: A proposed annexation would hand the utility a group of privately built stations of unknown condition, controls, and capacity. What direction protects the utility before it accepts operating responsibility?

answers.text: Accept the stations immediately, at the closing ceremony, and discover their true condition gradually through day-to-day operations over the following years
Refuse all annexations that include lift stations, whatever the area's needs
Require a pre-acceptance assessment of condition, capacity, and control compatibility, with upgrades and funding identified before transfer
Accept the stations but decline to maintain any equipment that is not already standard

questions.explanation: Acceptance transfers every hidden liability with the assets; assessing condition, capacity, and compatibility first lets the utility price the upgrade program and negotiate it as part of the transfer instead of inheriting surprises.

questions.question: A force main's air valves pass normal operating flows of air but are far too small to admit air fast enough when the main is drained, risking vacuum damage during maintenance. What does the fleet design standard need to require?

answers.text: Air valve sizing checked for both operating release and the large air flows of filling and draining, not just operation
A standing rule that force mains may never be drained for maintenance under any circumstances at any station in the fleet, ever
Larger pumps so the main refills before a vacuum can form
Removal of the undersized valves so the main can breathe through the station

questions.explanation: The governing air flow for a valve is often the filling or draining case, not steady operation; a standard that checks both prevents vacuum collapse risk from being designed into every new main.

questions.question: On a sewer installation project, the contractor's grade records conflict with the utility's check survey at several reaches, and backfilling is proceeding quickly. What should the monitoring and inspection program direct?

answers.text: Require independent grade verification of the remaining reaches before they are covered, and resolve the conflicting reaches before acceptance
Accept the contractor's records, because the installing party's paperwork is presumed correct whenever a conflict with the owner's survey appears during a project of this kind
Average the two sets of elevations and record the midpoint as the as-built grade for every reach in dispute
Stop all inspection on the project, since conflicting records mean inspection can no longer serve any useful purpose there

questions.explanation: Grade determines whether the line will drain and self-cleanse for its whole life, and backfill permanently hides the evidence. When records conflict, independent verification before covering is the only point where the truth is still cheap to establish.

questions.question: Two hydrogen sulfide loggers a short distance apart on the same trunk have tracked each other almost exactly for a full season, while a concrete trunk with known corrosion has no sulfide monitoring at all. What is the best direction?

answers.text: Redeploy one logger to the unmonitored corrosion reach, keeping the other as the continuing record at the original location
Add a third logger beside the first two, so the agreement between instruments at that location becomes even stronger even if doing so leaves the underlying condition completely unmeasured
Leave both loggers in place, because moving any instrument would break the continuity of both records at once
Remove both loggers and rely on odor complaints to describe sulfide conditions on both trunks from now on

questions.explanation: Duplicated coverage that adds no new information wastes scarce instruments. Keeping one logger preserves the original trend while the second starts building the missing record where corrosion risk is currently unmeasured.

questions.question: A corrosion-control feed on a large interceptor treats 2.05 MGD at a dose of 2.8 mg/L. How many pounds of chemical are fed per day?

answers.text: 45.87 lb/day
47.87 lb/day
49.87 lb/day
51.87 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow (MGD) x dose (mg/L) x 8.34. 2.05 x 2.8 = 5.74, times 8.34 = 47.87 lb/day (rounded).

questions.question: A sulfide-control feed serves a force-main discharge carrying 0.85 MGD, dosed at 5.2 mg/L. How many pounds of chemical are fed per day?

answers.text: 36.86 lb/day
34.86 lb/day
38.86 lb/day
40.86 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow (MGD) x dose (mg/L) x 8.34. 0.85 x 5.2 = 4.42, times 8.34 = 36.86 lb/day.

wastewater-collection-class-3.quiz_title: Wastewater Collection Class III Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Maintenance logs for one pump show repeated overload trips spread over months, each reset and returned to service, while the station's other pump never trips. What does that logged pattern most directly indicate?

answers.text: A recurring mechanical or load problem on that pump, not random events
Proof that the overload device itself should be removed from the circuit
A level sensor reading higher than the true wet well level
Normal operation that needs no program attention at any point

questions.explanation: One trip can be an event; the same protection tripping on the same machine over months is a trend with an address. Repetition on one pump while its partner runs clean points to a load that keeps returning, such as drag, binding, or a passing obstruction. A program that trends trip logs treats the pattern as a work order, not a reset routine.

questions.question: After a pump rehabilitation, a duty check measures flow in a force main section with a flow area of 1.45 square feet and a velocity of 3.7 feet per second. What is the flow through the section?

answers.text: 5.37 gpm

questions.explanation: Use Q = A x V x 448.8 from the formula table. Step 1: multiply area by velocity, 1.45 x 3.7 = 5.365 cubic feet per second. Step 2: convert with 448.8, 5.365 x 448.8 = 2,407.81. Step 3: state the flow with its unit, 2,407.81 gpm. Skipping the conversion leaves 5.37, and doubling the area gives 4,815.62 gpm.

questions.question: A manager is setting CCTV inspection frequencies for a new program covering both large trunk sewers and small residential lines. What principle should set the frequencies?

answers.text: Residential lines are inspected most often because they are shortest, while trunk lines wait the longest
Every line in the system is inspected on the same fixed cycle, regardless of size, age, or consequence
Only lines that have already overflowed are inspected, and all other lines wait until a problem is reported
Trunk and high-consequence lines are inspected most often, with longer cycles for low-risk local lines

questions.explanation: A defensible program tiers frequency by risk: large, deep, or high-consequence lines whose failure would cause the greatest harm are inspected most often, while low-risk lines can carry longer cycles. A single uniform cycle wastes effort on low-risk pipe and under-inspects the lines that matter most.

questions.question: Why does a preventive program schedule periodic pigging of a force main that is still flowing without complaint?

answers.text: To pressure-test the main to destruction so weak points reveal themselves during the run and can be marked for later repair
To flush the main backward toward the station wet well
To give a new crew practice inserting equipment into a live line
To wipe wall buildup away before it narrows the main and cuts its capacity

questions.explanation: Buildup grows on a force-main wall gradually and steadily reduces the flow area. Pigging on a preventive cycle wipes that buildup out while the loss is still small, preserving the main's capacity instead of waiting until pumping can no longer keep up.

questions.question: Before a reach is moved to a longer cleaning cycle, its supervisor verifies carrying velocity. The reach carries 7.6 cubic feet per second through a flow area of 2.0 square feet. What is the velocity?

answers.text: 3.8 ft/s
5.6 ft/s

questions.explanation: Velocity = flow / area. Step 1: 7.6 cfs / 2.0 sq ft = 3.8. The velocity is 3.8 ft/s, comfortably above the self-cleansing range, which supports the longer cycle.

questions.question: What is the main program reason structure inspections use a standard set of defect codes rather than free-form descriptions?

answers.text: Free-form descriptions are prohibited in the field because writing narrative notes during an inspection is unsafe
Standard codes make condition data comparable across crews, structures, and years, so trends and priorities can be built from it
Standard codes are shorter to type, and saving keystrokes is the primary reason the coding system was adopted
Standard codes allow the inspection to be completed without actually observing the defect being recorded

questions.explanation: Program decisions depend on comparing condition across hundreds of structures inspected by different crews over many years. Standard defect codes create that comparability; free-form notes, however careful, cannot be aggregated into trends, rankings, or defensible nominations.

questions.question: Discharge pressures at one station have crept upward at unchanged flow over several years, suggesting the force main's interior is roughening or narrowing. Before funding a full cleaning program, what evidence should the manager require?

answers.text: Vendor assurances that cleaning always restores at least half of lost capacity
A single pressure reading taken on the day the contractor visits
The age of the main alone, since old mains always benefit equally
A pilot cleaning judged by before-and-after measurements

questions.explanation: A measured pilot converts a plausible theory into a defensible program: if pressures and drawdown rates recover, the case for cleaning the remaining reaches is evidence; if not, the money goes elsewhere.

questions.question: Storage between control levels matters at a small neighborhood station. Its round wet well measures 5 feet across; how many gallons are stored in 7 feet of its depth?

answers.text: About 1,027.6 gallons
About 822 gallons
About 1,336.5 gallons
About 1,542 gallons

questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 x diameter squared x depth x 7.48 gallons per cubic foot. 0.785 x 5 x 5 x 7 = 137.38 cubic feet. 137.38 x 7.48 = about 1,027.6 gallons. Small-well volumes like this set how much storage a station really has between its control levels.

questions.question: In long-term defect analysis, a capacity defect is distinguished from a condition defect by which difference?

answers.text: A capacity defect appears only in summer, while a condition defect appears only in winter, a distinction based on the season in which the defect was first noticed by a maintenance crew
A capacity defect means sound pipe is being asked to carry more flow than it can, while a condition defect means the pipe itself has deteriorated
A capacity defect is found by flow meters, while a condition defect can never be detected by any instrument
A capacity defect requires no action, while a condition defect always requires emergency repair

questions.explanation: The distinction decides the remedy. Sound but undersized pipe needs relief or added capacity, while deteriorated pipe needs rehabilitation or replacement; treating one as the other spends capital without fixing the limitation the data revealed.

questions.question: Evening solvent odors recur at one trunk junction, but routine daytime samples there are always clean. The program adds a conductivity-triggered automatic sampler at the junction. What does this design accomplish that the old program could not?

answers.text: It guarantees the discharger will be identified by name from the sample alone, without any upstream tracing work by the field crews
It captures the discharge while it is passing, at whatever hour it occurs, instead of sampling the junction only when it runs clean
It prevents the discharge from occurring, because automatic samplers deter dischargers who learn that a sampler is present
It replaces the need for any field response to odor complaints at that junction for the rest of the program year

questions.explanation: The old program proved only that the junction is clean at midday. Event-triggered sampling aligns collection with the discharge's own schedule, producing the physical evidence that tracing, source control, and any enforcement then build on.

questions.question: The utility buys its first units of a new type of inspection equipment. No maintenance procedure exists for it. What must the manager's new procedure include to be complete at the program level?

answers.text: Only the manufacturer's warranty terms, so crews know which repairs the vendor will pay for during the term of coverage
Only a cleaning schedule, because inspection electronics rarely need any other scheduled care or checking
Only the purchase price and delivery date, filed with the equipment record for future replacement planning
Scheduled tasks and intervals, required parts and calibration, safety precautions, and the records to be kept

questions.explanation: A complete procedure covers what is done, how often, with what parts and calibration, under what safety precautions, and what is recorded. Warranty, cleaning, or purchase data alone leaves the program undefined.

questions.question: Year-to-date reports show lift station power costs running well above budget while flows are near normal. What is the manager's best response?

answers.text: Ignore the variance until year end, since power bills are outside the program's control entirely
Order crews to run stations less often, even if wet-well levels rise above normal operating ranges
Transfer money from the training budget without documenting the change or its effect on the program or on staffing, schedules, or the service levels the program is expected to maintain
Investigate the cause, forecast the year-end impact, and adjust the budget plan through proper channels

questions.explanation: A variance is a management signal: find whether equipment condition, rates, or operating settings are driving it, forecast where the year will land, and make any budget adjustment openly and with documentation.

wastewater-collection-class-2.quiz_title: Wastewater Collection Class II Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Camera work from the main shows a leaking tap connection, but a lateral camera pushed up the service line finds the lateral itself cracked and root-filled for most of its length. Why is a top-hat liner alone the wrong rehabilitation here?

answers.text: A top-hat seals only the connection area and a short piece of lateral, leaving the damaged lateral unrepaired
A top-hat liner can be installed only in manholes, so it can never be used at any lateral connection at all
A top-hat would add so much thickness that the main would be blocked for its entire remaining length
A top-hat requires the lateral to be in perfect condition at the connection, which is the opposite of this case

questions.explanation: A top-hat liner is a tap device: it seals the lateral-to-main connection and a short section of the lateral beside it. Damage running most of the lateral's length is beyond its reach, so the lateral itself needs repair or renewal in addition to, or instead of, the connection seal.

questions.question: Before a wet well is taken out of service for rehabilitation, the crew must know how much wastewater the well holds so it can be pumped down and hauled. The cylindrical wet well is 11 ft in diameter and holds a depth of 9 ft. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume of a cylinder in gallons = 0.785 x diameter squared x depth x 7.48. Step 1: square the diameter, 11 x 11 = 121. Step 2: find the cross-sectional area factor, 0.785 x 121 = 94.985. Step 3: multiply by the depth, 94.985 x 9 = 854.865 cubic ft. Step 4: convert to gallons, 854.865 x 7.48 = 6,394.39 gal. Stopping after Step 3 gives the cubic-foot value, 854.87, not gallons.

questions.question: Two air tools must run at the same time from one compressor, and together they draw more air than the compressor can deliver at working pressure. What happens in operation, and what selection fixes it?

answers.text: Working pressure holds steady, because pneumatic tools share a supply without any loss
Both tools run noticeably faster than normal when they are fed from the shared supply
Pressure falls and tools weaken; a larger-delivery compressor is needed
The receiver tank alone makes up the whole difference for as long as the job continues

questions.explanation: When combined tool demand exceeds compressor delivery, the system cannot hold working pressure: pressure falls and the tools lose power. A receiver only buffers brief draws, so the lasting fix is a compressor whose delivery matches the combined demand.

questions.question: Before a crew can repair a leaking tap, the exact position of the lateral where it meets the main must be confirmed in a yard crossed by other buried services. Which excavation approach best fits?

answers.text: Open a wide trench with an excavator bucket across the whole yard so every buried service in the area is uncovered at once
Probe blindly with a steel bar until the lateral is struck
Hydro excavate a narrow exposure that daylights the tap and the nearby services
Jet the main from inside and judge the tap position from the surface

questions.explanation: Hydro excavation removes soil with water and vacuum in a narrow, controlled exposure, so the tap and the other buried services can be daylighted and seen before repair work begins. That precision is what a congested yard crossing calls for.

questions.question: Flow in a trunk channel measures 24 cubic feet per second through a flow area of 3.0 square feet. What is the velocity?

answers.text: 72 ft/s
4.0 ft/s
8.0 ft/s

questions.explanation: Velocity = flow / area. Step 1: V = 24 cfs / 3.0 sq ft. Step 2: V = 8.0 ft/s. Multiplying flow by area gives 72, which is not a velocity, and dividing area by flow inverts the relationship.

questions.question: A reach drops 2.1 ft over a run of 300 ft. What is the slope of the reach?
questions.explanation: Slope = fall / run x 100. Step 1: 2.1 ft / 300 ft = 0.007. Step 2: 0.007 x 100 = 0.7%. The slope is 0.7%.

questions.question: A lift station pump motor runs at full speed but the pump delivers no flow, and the condition began after the wet well was drawn down unusually low. What condition inside the pump best explains this?

answers.text: The pump has become air-bound, with air trapped in the casing preventing it from moving liquid
The force main has become too clean for the pump to work against
The check valve has opened too far and cannot be slowed
The wet well has gained volume while the pump was off

questions.explanation: A pump moves liquid, not air. Drawing the well down too far can let air into the casing, and an air-bound pump spins without developing flow until the trapped air is cleared and the pump is again full of liquid.

questions.question: Wastewater moves through a force main at 4.2 ft/s, and the pipe offers 1.5 square feet of flow area. How many gallons per minute pass a given point in the line?

answers.text: About 2,827 gpm
About 2,262 gpm
About 3,392 gpm
About 1,979 gpm

questions.explanation: Flow = area x velocity x 448.8. 1.5 square feet x 4.2 ft/s = 6.3 cubic feet per second. 6.3 x 448.8 = about 2,827 gpm.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a deadband built into a SCADA level alarm setting?

answers.text: It silences every alarm at the station automatically during the nighttime hours, on the assumption that no genuine emergency can develop while the crew is off site
It keeps the alarm from chattering on and off when the level hovers right at the alarm point
It delays every alarm by one full day so a supervisor can review it first
It disconnects the level sensor whenever the measured level is holding steady

questions.explanation: A deadband makes the level move a small set distance past the alarm point before the alarm clears. Without it, ordinary ripples around the setpoint would cycle the alarm repeatedly and flood the operator with nuisance calls.

questions.question: Dry-weather flow from one basin has declined steadily for a year while customer counts and neighboring basins stayed stable. Which defect should the operator investigate?

answers.text: The basin's manholes have begun taking in far too much storm water lately
The treatment plant is drawing extra flow out of that basin every night
Wastewater may be leaking out of the basin's pipes through defects — exfiltration — or being diverted before the meter
The basin's residents are all using less water for no identifiable reason

questions.explanation: A real, sustained drop with no change in customers means flow is leaving the system somewhere — leaking out through cracked pipe or broken joints where the sewer lies above the water table (exfiltration), or escaping through an unknown connection before it reaches the meter.

questions.question: A repair will close one lane of a busy street for most of a day. What is the best traffic-control action?

answers.text: Configure the plan and signs in advance, coordinate the detour with city or agency contacts, and brief the crew
Place cones when the crew arrives and let traffic sort itself out, with drivers choosing whatever route around the work they prefer
Close both lanes without notice to shorten the job
Rely on the truck's flashing lights as the only traffic control

questions.explanation: A planned lane closure needs a configured plan: signs and layout set in advance, the detour and timing coordinated with the responsible contacts, and the crew briefed. Improvised cones and unannounced closures endanger workers and drivers alike.

questions.question: A crew finds drums of unknown material dumped beside a manhole, with liquid pooled nearby. What is the best program response?

answers.text: Have the crew open a drum to identify the contents by smell
Load the drums onto the crew truck and haul them to the yard, where they can be stored until someone has time to look at them properly and decide
Wash the pooled liquid into the manhole so the area looks clean
Keep the crew back, secure the area, and coordinate the response through the program's hazardous-materials and emergency contacts

questions.explanation: Unknown material is not handled, opened, or washed into the sewer by the collection crew. The program response is to keep people back, secure the area, bring in the designated hazardous-materials and emergency contacts, and document the find.

wastewater-collection-class-1.quiz_title: Wastewater Collection Class I Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: During calibration, a gas detector exposed to span gas of known concentration will not adjust to the correct reading. What should the operator do?

answers.text: Use the detector anyway and note the problem at the end of the shift
Zero it again in fresh air and skip the span step
Take the detector out of service for service or sensor replacement and use a detector that calibrates correctly before any entry work
Turn the alarm volume up so the error is easier to hear

questions.explanation: A detector that cannot be spanned to a known gas cannot be trusted to read that gas correctly, so it is removed from service and a properly calibrated instrument is used instead.

questions.question: Calculate the volume in gallons of a circular wet well 4 ft in diameter and 12 ft deep. Use Volume = 0.785 × D² × depth × 7.48.
questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 × 4² × 12 × 7.48 = 0.785 × 16 × 12 × 7.48 ≈ 1,127.4 gal. The 150.7 figure is the volume in cubic feet, before converting to gallons.

questions.question: Why is temperature measured during equipment inspection?

answers.text: Temperature readings replace the need to check lubrication during routine collection system operations
Overheating is an early sign of problems in motors, bearings, and electrical parts
A cool motor always means the pump is delivering full flow
Temperature must be recorded before any gauge may be read

questions.explanation: Measuring temperature during inspection reveals overheating in motors, bearings, and electrical components before failure. It complements, rather than replaces, other checks.

questions.question: A reach of pipe is crushed and offset so badly that no liner can be pulled or inverted through it, and the utility wants the same size pipe in the same alignment without open-cut digging. Which method fits?

answers.text: Pipe bursting, which breaks up the old pipe in place while pulling the new pipe in behind the bursting head
Cured-in-place lining, because a soft liner can always be forced through a fully collapsed section
Joint grouting, because sealing the joints will push a crushed pipe back into its round shape
Smoke testing, because pressurized smoke will gradually reinflate the collapsed section

questions.explanation: Pipe bursting does not depend on the old pipe's shape: the head fractures it outward and pulls in the replacement, making it the trenchless choice for a collapsed line.

questions.question: Wastewater flows at 5 cubic feet per second through a cross-sectional area of 2 square feet. What is the velocity?

answers.text: 0.4 ft/s
10 ft/s
7.5 ft/s
2.5 ft/s

questions.explanation: Velocity = flow ÷ area = 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 ft/s. The 0.4 value inverts the division and 10 multiplies flow by area instead.

questions.question: What is a corkscrew attachment on a rodder used for?

answers.text: Threading a new service lateral into the side of the main without excavation
Drilling pilot holes through concrete pipe so grout can be injected from outside
Winding the rod back onto its reel evenly at the end of the job
Boring through soft blockages and retrieving rags and similar material

questions.explanation: The corkscrew head twists into soft obstructions to open a passage and can snag and pull back rags and wipes.

questions.question: Why are lift station wet wells and dry wells ventilated?

answers.text: To cool the standby generator so it can run longer during a power failure event
To dry out the control panel wiring between pump cycles at the station
To increase the pressure in the force main so the pumps work less hard
To remove hazardous gases and supply fresh air for worker safety

questions.explanation: Ventilation dilutes and removes gases that accumulate in station structures and brings in fresh air, making the atmosphere safer for operators who work there.

questions.question: A cylindrical wet well is 12 feet in diameter. How many gallons does a 5-foot depth hold?

answers.text: 565 gallons
352 gallons
1,057 gallons
4,228 gallons

questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 x D^2 x depth x 7.48 = 0.785 x 144 x 5 x 7.48 = about 4,228 gallons. Leaving out the 7.48 conversion gives about 565 gallons, and using the radius squared in place of the diameter squared gives about 1,057 gallons.

questions.question: How is cleaning effectiveness best evaluated after a sewer is cleaned?

answers.text: By assuming the line is clean because the jet truck was present
By inspecting the line and confirming debris is removed
By checking only the amount of fuel the cleaning truck consumed
By repainting the manhole cover and calling the work complete

questions.explanation: Cleaning is evaluated by inspecting the result, for example by visual or camera inspection, and confirming debris was removed and flow is restored. Presence of equipment alone proves nothing.

questions.question: How is poor performance of an inverted siphon most often recognized?

answers.text: By a rattling manhole cover nearby
By clear water flowing freely
By solids depositing and flow being restricted in a barrel
By smoke appearing at a roof vent

questions.explanation: Inverted siphons are clog-prone and need frequent cleaning and inspection. Deposition that restricts a barrel is the recognized sign of poor siphon performance.

questions.question: A lift station preventive maintenance list has 80 scheduled tasks for the month, and the crew has completed 48 of them. What percent of the scheduled tasks are done?
questions.explanation: Percent done = part ÷ total × 100 = 48 ÷ 80 × 100 = 60%. The crew has completed 60% of the scheduled tasks.

questions.question: A crew is about to power-rod a blocked sewer where records suggest a gas line may have been bored through the pipe. What is the safest course?

answers.text: Treat it as a possible cross bore and verify before cutting or rodding
Rod the line at full power first, since a cutting head will pass a plastic gas line without damaging it
Jet the line at maximum pressure to clear the blockage before checking whether a cross bore is present
Have a worker enter the downstream manhole to watch the cutter pass so any gas line can be seen in time

questions.explanation: A gas line bored through a sewer is a cross bore; cutting or rodding through it can rupture the gas line, so the line must be verified before mechanical cutting.

wastewater-treatment-class-4.quiz_title: Wastewater Treatment Class IV Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Chemical deliveries twice arrived after tanks ran dry during peak-demand weeks, while other months carry heavy surplus. What inventory direction corrects the pattern?

answers.text: Reduce all doses slightly whenever inventory looks low, whatever the process effect
Order every chemical on the same calendar day each month for administrative simplicity
Keep tanks as full as possible all year so a dry tank can never happen again, even though surplus chemicals age in storage through the low-demand months
Set reorder points and storage targets from each chemical's seasonal dose curve, so peak weeks are stocked before they arrive

questions.explanation: Chemical programs fail at predictable peaks when ordering ignores the dose curve. Reorder points keyed to seasonal demand stock the plant ahead of high-use weeks without carrying year-round surplus, and dose decisions stay with the process instead of the tank gauge.

questions.question: During irrigation season the operations plan loads one polishing filter of 270 sq ft at 1,026 gpm. Compute the filtration rate for that filter.

answers.text: 3.8 gpm/sq ft
0.26 gpm/sq ft
2.9 gpm/sq ft
4.7 gpm/sq ft

questions.explanation: Filtration rate = flow / area = 1,026 gpm / 270 sq ft = 3.8 gpm/sq ft. Dividing area by flow gives about 0.26, which inverts the ratio.

questions.question: What is the defining role of tertiary media filtration in this plant's process train?

answers.text: It grows the biomass that consumes most of the incoming organic load and produces the plant's secondary effluent
It polishes remaining effluent solids so disinfection and reuse receive a consistent, low-solids stream
It settles raw wastewater solids before any biological treatment occurs
It destroys pathogens by chemical oxidation as water passes through the bed

questions.explanation: Tertiary media filtration is a polishing step: sand, anthracite, or disc media remove residual solids after biological treatment. That consistent low-solids effluent is what makes downstream disinfection reliable and reuse quality steady.

questions.question: A nitrifying plant holds one sludge-age target all year: winter ammonia margins are thin, while summer operation carries far more inventory than nitrification needs. What is the best direction-level change?

answers.text: Keep the single target, because changing targets seasonally is inconsistent
Lower the target in winter to save wasting effort when operators are busy
Adopt seasonal sludge-age bands in the annual plan: a higher winter band to protect slow-growing nitrifiers and a lower summer band when warm water supports them
Set the target by whichever month last produced the best effluent

questions.explanation: Nitrifiers grow slowly and are most vulnerable in cold water, so sludge-age direction follows the season. Planned seasonal bands protect winter ammonia margin without carrying unneeded inventory, and its aeration cost, all summer.

questions.question: What does the percent volatile figure express for a sludge or digester solids sample?

answers.text: The share of the sample that is grit and other heavy inorganic material
The share of the sample already converted to digester gas during feeding
The share of the sample that is water removable by gravity thickening alone
The volatile, organic fraction of the total solids in the sample

questions.explanation: Percent volatile is the volatile solids divided by the total solids, expressed as a percent: it states how much of the solids mass is organic material. Digester and sludge programs track it because that organic fraction is what digestion can reduce; grit is part of the fixed, non-volatile remainder.

questions.question: A plant converts its disinfection to ozonation. What must the director account for regarding protection of the water after the ozone contactor?

answers.text: Ozone leaves a long-lasting residual in the effluent that must be chemically removed before discharge, so a deozonation feed system has to be installed and paced to the ozone dose at all times
Ozone residual persists for days and protects a reuse distribution system
Ozone can be stored in the contactor to cover the following day's demand
Ozone leaves no residual, so a residual disinfectant may need to follow where downstream residual protection is required

questions.explanation: Ozone is a strong oxidant that reacts and disappears in the contactor, leaving no residual behind. Where a distribution or reuse system needs continuing residual protection, a residual disinfectant must be applied after ozonation.

questions.question: A circular primary clarifier is 47 feet in diameter with an 11-foot water depth. What is its volume, for comparison with the unit that would remain in service during an outage?

answers.text: 114,143 gallons
142,679 gallons
128,411 gallons
171,215 gallons

questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 x D^2 x depth x 7.48 = 0.785 x 47^2 x 11 x 7.48 = 0.785 x 2,209 x 11 x 7.48 = 142,679 gallons. The single-unit volume anchors the firm-capacity comparison.

questions.question: An ozonation system has two generators, each sized for 60 percent of peak ozone demand. Both must run at peak, and any generator outage during a peak event cuts the applied dose well below target. How should the director treat this in capital planning?

answers.text: Treat the system as fully redundant because two generators are installed, and count the pair as backed up whenever both machines are capable of running, regardless of how much of peak demand one unit covers alone
Recognize there is no generator redundancy at peak demand and plan added capacity, demand management, or an accepted risk decision
Overspeed the remaining generator to full peak output whenever its twin is down
Store liquid ozone ahead of forecast peaks to cover generator outages

questions.explanation: Two units that must both run at peak provide no spare capacity — firm capacity is what remains with one unit out, here only 60 percent of peak demand. The director either funds capacity, manages peak demand, or documents the accepted risk; calling the pair redundant hides the gap.

questions.question: Why must compliance results come from an approved analytical method for that parameter and matrix?

answers.text: Approved methods are always the fastest methods available to the laboratory based on convenience for the reporting schedule rather than data quality
Approved methods never require quality control samples in the batch
Only an approved method has demonstrated performance and quality requirements that make results comparable and defensible
An approved method guarantees the result will fall within the permit limit

questions.explanation: Approval means the method was validated for that use with defined quality controls. A scientifically reasonable but unapproved procedure does not produce compliance-grade data.

questions.question: A QA audit discovers that an expired calibration standard was used for a week of metals analyses before anyone noticed. What is the correct program response?

answers.text: Identify every batch and result produced with the standard, assess and qualify or reanalyze the affected data, and document corrective action
Say nothing, because the standard was only slightly past its date and probably still good and the analyses were probably still good enough for reporting purposes
Throw away the expired standard and continue reporting the week's results as they stand
Recalculate the week's results using the ratio between the old and new standard prices

questions.explanation: The impact of a quality failure has to be bounded honestly: trace every result the bad standard touched, qualify or redo what cannot be trusted, and document the corrective action so the lapse cannot quietly repeat.

questions.question: A security summary counts 200 documented security rounds in a quarter, of which 58 covered remote unstaffed sites. What percent of the rounds covered remote unstaffed sites?
