questions.explanation: Percent of total = part / total x 100 = 58 / 200 x 100 = 0.29 x 100 = 29%. The summary uses this share to judge whether the round program gives unstaffed sites their intended coverage.

questions.question: Why does the safety program for an ozonation plant plan around generator rooms and contactor areas rather than around bulk chemical storage?

answers.text: Ozone is delivered in bulk tankers and stored for months at a time
Ozone is generated on site as it is needed for use
Ozone areas are hazardous only because of noise from the generators
Ozone is stored as a liquid under pressure in outdoor tanks

questions.explanation: Ozone is generated on site rather than delivered and stored in bulk, so the program concentrates monitoring, ventilation, and access control on the generator and contactor areas where the hazard is produced.

wastewater-treatment-class-3.quiz_title: Wastewater Treatment Class III Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: During storm peaks the primary clarifiers lose capture badly for about two hours, forwarding a solids surge that upsets the aeration basins for the rest of the day. Equalization volume is available upstream. What is the best wet-weather strategy?

answers.text: Push the full peak through the primaries as fast as possible so the basins empty sooner, and accept the capture loss as the unavoidable price of wet weather
Raise primary sludge withdrawal to its maximum for the whole storm so the blankets stay thin, even though the withdrawn sludge runs dilute for many hours
Shave the hydrograph peak into equalization so the primaries see a capped, steadier flow
Take one primary clarifier out of service during the peak so the remaining units run deeper and settle the storm solids by gravity over a longer path

questions.explanation: Primary capture collapses when the surface overflow rate spikes. Capping the forward flow with equalization holds the primaries near the rate where they capture, and the stored flow returns at a pace the plant can treat.

questions.question: A plant flowing 3.12 MGD sets a ferric dose of 14 mg/L from its effluent phosphorus trend. How many pounds of chemical per day does this dose represent?

answers.text: 43.7 lb/day
364.3 lb/day
261.3 lb/day
3,643 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow x dose x 8.34 = 3.12 x 14 x 8.34 = 364.29 lb/day, reported as 364.3 lb/day. Omitting the 8.34 factor gives 43.7 lb/day, a common miscalculation.

questions.question: With one secondary clarifier out of service, 1,330,000 gpd passes over the remaining 1,520 sq ft of clarifier surface. The operator is judging whether the peak can be held or must be shaved. What is the surface overflow rate?

answers.text: 700 gpd/sq ft
1,050 gpd/sq ft
875 gpd/sq ft
1,400 gpd/sq ft

questions.explanation: Surface overflow rate = flow (gpd) / surface area (sq ft) = 1,330,000 / 1,520 = 875 gpd/sq ft. That loading, judged with the current settling condition, decides whether equalization must shave the peak.

questions.question: Effluent solids have risen steadily over three shifts toward the discharge limit, traced to a clarifier upset that is now being corrected. Equalization storage with spare capacity is available upstream of discharge. What is the best effluent-disposal decision?

answers.text: Discharge at full rate until the limit is actually exceeded
Dilute the effluent with plant water at the outfall to lower the measured solids concentration, and continue discharging at the full permitted flow rate
Discharge the poorest effluent at night when fewer people see it
Temporarily hold or reduce discharge using the available storage while the clarifier recovers, releasing the stored effluent once quality returns

questions.explanation: Surface-water discharge is governed by permit limits judged on effluent quality. Using storage to ride out a known, recovering upset protects the discharge; dilution at the outfall and timing games do not change the solids load delivered.

questions.question: When biosolids are land applied at agronomic rates, what primarily limits how much can be applied to a field?

answers.text: The total volume of storage the farm has available that season, since chemical and energy costs are treated as secondary concerns here
The number of truck trips the hauler can make in one day, because that response has worked at this plant in past seasons
The nitrogen the crop can use, so application does not exceed crop nutrient need
The phosphorus already present in the receiving stream nearby, and let the following shift decide whether the change helped

questions.explanation: Agronomic-rate application is nitrogen-limited: solids are spread at the rate that supplies the crop's nitrogen need without excess. That limit, not hauling convenience or storage volume, sets the application rate.

questions.question: Two identical centrifugal pumps discharge into a common header. With both running, total flow is well short of twice the single-pump flow, and both pumps test healthy. What explains the shortfall?

answers.text: As combined flow rises, system head rises with it, moving each pump back on its curve to a lower individual output
One of the two pumps must be rotating backwards whenever both pumps are running together on the common discharge header
Parallel pumps can never add flow to a header
The header gauge is the only thing that changed

questions.explanation: A pump delivers where its curve meets the system curve. Doubling flow through the same piping raises friction head, so each pump settles at a lower rate — parallel pumps share the system, they do not simply double it.

questions.question: Two parallel mechanically cleaned bar screens serve one channel. Screen 1 rakes three times as often as Screen 2 and shows a higher upstream level, while total plant flow is steady. What is the best optimization move?

answers.text: Take Screen 2 out of service to force all flow through Screen 1 according to the trend recorded over the past several operating shifts
Slow the rake on Screen 1 to match Screen 2
Rebalance the split so both screens share the flow and debris load more evenly
Raise the rake speed on Screen 2 only

questions.explanation: Unequal raking frequency and upstream level at steady total flow show an unbalanced split, with one screen carrying most of the debris load. Evening the split shares wear and headloss instead of overloading one unit.

questions.question: A dissolved air flotation recycle pump must deliver 960 gpm against 144 ft of head. The pump efficiency at this duty is 80%. What brake horsepower must the motor supply?
questions.explanation: Water hp = (960 x 144) / 3,960 = 138,240 / 3,960 = 34.91 hp. Brake hp = water hp / efficiency = 34.91 / 0.80 = 43.64 hp. The motor must be sized to the brake horsepower, not the water horsepower.

questions.question: What role do written laboratory standard operating procedures play in producing defensible data?

answers.text: So every analyst works the same documented way, making results reproducible and traceable
They encourage each analyst to improvise an individual technique for routine tests
They replace the need for the laboratory to run any quality control samples, standards, or duplicates with its routine batches
They are written only to satisfy safety inspections and are not used in analysis

questions.explanation: Defensible data rest on documented, consistently followed procedures: identical sampling, preservation, analysis, and QC steps make results reproducible by any analyst and traceable when a result is questioned.

questions.question: A plant-wide metals balance shows effluent metals low and steady, influent metals gradually rising, and sludge metals rising in step with influent. What does the balance demonstrate?

answers.text: The metals are being destroyed by biological treatment by the biological treatment process and converted to harmless gases in the aeration basins
The effluent metals results must be wrong
Metals pass through the plant unchanged in the effluent
The metals are being removed from the water by accumulation in the solids, so sludge quality and source control need attention

questions.explanation: Metals are not destroyed in treatment; a balance that closes through the sludge shows removal by transfer to the solids. Rising sludge metals shift the concern to solids quality and to finding the source.

questions.question: A monthly maintenance report lists 400 total completed work orders, of which 190 were preventive maintenance work orders. What percent of the work orders were preventive maintenance?
questions.explanation: Percent of total = part divided by total, times 100: 190 divided by 400 = 0.475, times 100 = 47.5%.

questions.question: A digester shows grit and foam accumulating, dead zones suspected, and gas production falling. Two mixing systems are proposed for replacement. How should performance data guide the choice?

answers.text: Choose the system with the lowest purchase price, since mixing performance cannot be judged until it is installed
Compare verified mixing performance at the digester's size and duty, since restoring full-volume mixing addresses the failure
Choose the system whose motor is largest, because motor size alone guarantees the whole tank contents will move
Keep the existing mixers and raise the feed rate, since more feed will stir the tank through gas production alone

questions.explanation: The evidence - dead zones, grit and foam accumulation, falling gas - defines the duty: the replacement is judged on verified ability to mix the full tank volume at that duty, not on price or motor size alone.

wastewater-treatment-class-2.quiz_title: Wastewater Treatment Class II Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A plant feeds 118 lb/day of chlorine (as chlorine) to a flow of 1.05 MGD. Using the feed records, what applied dose is the plant actually achieving?

answers.text: 112.4 mg/L, without checking whether the loading has actually changed

questions.explanation: Dose from feed = feed lb/day / (flow in MGD x 8.34) = 118 / (1.05 x 8.34) = 118 / 8.757 = 13.48 mg/L. Dividing by flow alone, without the 8.34 conversion, gives the unrealistic 112.4 mg/L.

questions.question: After a new industry connects, a plant treats 1.35 MGD of wastewater with an influent BOD of 165 mg/L. How many pounds of BOD enter the plant each day?

answers.text: 223 lb/day
1,376 lb/day
2,228 lb/day
1,858 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow (MGD) x concentration (mg/L) x 8.34 = 1.35 x 165 x 8.34 = 1,858 lb/day. Omitting the 8.34 conversion factor gives only 223 lb/day.

questions.question: Effluent ammonia is well within limits at average flow but spikes during each day's peak-flow hours, and sludge age and DO are both adequate. Equalization volume is available. What adjustment addresses the pattern?

answers.text: Waste heavily on peak days so the remaining sludge is younger and more active, because young sludge always nitrifies faster than an established population
Raise the RAS rate only during the ammonia spikes and leave flow unaltered
Use equalization to shave the peaks and feed flow forward steadily, restoring aeration detention time during the hours that now spike
Lower the basin DO during peaks so the nitrifiers rest between surges

questions.explanation: Adequate sludge age and DO with ammonia failure only at peak flow points to hydraulics: detention time collapses during the surge. Equalizing the peak restores the contact time nitrification needs without changing the biology.

questions.question: MLSS has drifted slightly this week, but SVI is 95, the effluent is clear, and microscopic examination shows firm floc with many stalked ciliates and very few filaments. What is the best evaluation?

answers.text: The sludge is young and dispersed, so wasting should stop until floc firms up
Stalked ciliates signal an old, failing sludge, so wasting should double
Filaments must be treated immediately even though few were seen before it can spread through the basin
The biology is healthy and stable — hold the current RAS, WAS, and air setpoints and keep trending

questions.explanation: Firm floc, abundant stalked ciliates, few filaments, a good SVI, and clear effluent together describe healthy, stable sludge. Evaluation sometimes concludes that no adjustment is the right adjustment.

questions.question: Nitrification is consuming alkalinity and the operator will feed an alkalinity chemical at 27 mg/L to a flow of 1.35 MGD. How many pounds per day of chemical (as the dosed compound) are required?

answers.text: 303.94 lb/day
36.45 lb/day, found by multiplying flow by dose without the weight conversion
253.3 lb/day
364.7 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow x dose x 8.34 = 1.35 MGD x 27 mg/L x 8.34 = 303.94 lb/day. Omitting the 8.34 conversion gives only the 36.45 figure.

questions.question: A standby generator starts and runs smoothly through every weekly no-load exercise, but during a loaded transfer test it bogs down, frequency sags, and it nearly stalls. What does this evidence show?

answers.text: The transfer switch is the only defective component in the standby system, and the engine's behavior under load is a normal characteristic that requires no further investigation
No-load runs cannot prove generating capacity; the engine or fuel system is failing under real load and loaded exercising is what exposes it
The generator is oversized for the plant and should be downsized
The weekly exercise period should simply be lengthened at no load, running the engine for several hours unloaded until it is thoroughly warmed and able to accept the plant load

questions.explanation: An unloaded engine only has to turn itself, so governor, fuel delivery, and cooling faults stay hidden. Sagging frequency under load is the classic finding that loaded exercise and load-bank testing exist to reveal, and the fuel and engine systems are evaluated from there.

questions.question: An RBC shaft develops a rhythmic knock once per revolution and the shaft sits visibly lower at one bearing. Growth is even and drive current is normal. What is the most likely equipment finding?

answers.text: The biomass has become too heavy for the shaft according to the gauge readings taken during the most recent rounds
The trough water level is too high when checked against the performance baseline for this equipment
The media discs are out of round from age under the loading conditions the unit has seen this operating week
A worn or failing shaft bearing is letting the shaft drop

questions.explanation: A once-per-revolution knock tied to a visibly dropped shaft localizes the fault to the bearing supporting that end, independent of growth or drive load. Bearing inspection and planned replacement prevent shaft and media damage.

questions.question: A wet-well drawdown test on a centrifugal pump measures output about 18% below its commissioning value. Suction and discharge valves are verified fully open, the piping is unchanged, and discharge head reads the same as at commissioning. What is the best evaluation?

answers.text: The discharge pressure gauge has drifted over time and should be recalibrated first, after which the drawdown result will likely return to its original value
The pump is air-bound and only needs its casing vented
The system head has increased because of changes elsewhere in the plant, and a larger motor must be installed before the pump can deliver its rated flow again
Worn impeller and wear-ring clearances are allowing internal recirculation inside the pump

questions.explanation: A drawdown test measures true delivered volume. With valves, piping, and head unchanged, a large output loss points inside the pump: enlarged wear-ring clearances let discharge water recirculate to suction instead of leaving the pump.

questions.question: An aerobic digester's temperature has fallen steadily for two weeks. Air supply and mixing check out normal, volatile reduction is slipping, and the heat exchanger's outlet temperature difference has narrowed. What is the best evaluation?

answers.text: The digester blower is undersized for the tank and must be replaced with a larger unit, because the falling temperature shows the biology is no longer receiving enough air
The temperature probe is the only thing that can produce this pattern
The digester is being fed far too much volatile solids for its volume, and the excess feed is absorbing all the heat the exchanger can deliver faster than it can be replaced
The heat exchanger is fouling and transferring less heat, so it is cleaned and its flows verified

questions.explanation: A narrowing temperature difference across the exchanger, alongside a real fall in digester temperature and process performance, shows heat transfer itself is failing. Fouled exchanger surfaces are the equipment cause to correct before the digester cools further.

questions.question: Seeded BOD bottles for a disinfected effluent show depletion in the valid range, but the seed control run beside them shows the seed alone consumed a large share of that oxygen. What must the analyst do before reporting the effluent BOD?

answers.text: Report the bottle depletion as the effluent BOD without adjustment
Discard the run, because seeded samples can never be reported
Add the seed control depletion to each sample bottle depletion
Correct each result for the oxygen uptake of the seed itself

questions.explanation: Seed adds its own oxygen demand to every seeded bottle. The seed control measures that uptake so sample results can be corrected for it; skipping the correction overstates the effluent BOD.

questions.question: For the monthly report, a plant treated 900,000 gallons total, of which 117,000 gallons came from one industrial customer. What percent of the total flow came from that customer?
questions.explanation: Percent of total = part divided by total, times 100: 117,000 / 900,000 x 100 = 13%. The industrial customer contributed 13% of the month's flow.

questions.question: What does a supervisor verify when checking readiness of the chlorine emergency repair kit and breathing equipment stored for a gas leak?

answers.text: Only that the kit box is present in the chlorine building and its lid is closed
That the kit is the correct type for the containers in use, its contents are complete and undamaged, and the breathing equipment is inspected and ready for trained responders
That the kit has been opened recently, because frequent opening proves the crew is familiar with it
That one kit can serve both the chlorine and sulfur dioxide rooms regardless of container fittings

questions.explanation: Emergency equipment is ready only if it fits the actual containers, is complete and serviceable, and is paired with inspected breathing equipment for trained responders. Presence of a box alone proves nothing about readiness.

wastewater-treatment-class-1.quiz_title: Wastewater Treatment Class I Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Why is wastewater effluent dechlorinated before discharge to surface water?

answers.text: Because chlorine residual is toxic to aquatic life
Because chlorine residual makes the effluent too clear to sample accurately
Because dechlorination restores dissolved oxygen consumed in the aeration basin
Because chlorine must be recovered and reused in the headworks chemical tank

questions.explanation: Chlorine remaining in discharged effluent can harm fish and other aquatic life, so a dechlorination chemical is fed to remove the residual before discharge.

questions.question: Digested sludge shows a much lower percent volatile solids than the raw sludge fed to the digester. What does this indicate?

answers.text: The digester added organic matter to the sludge while it was being stored
Percent volatile rises whenever digestion is working as it should perform
The laboratory ignition step created new volatile solids in the dried sample
Digestion destroyed a portion of the organic solids

questions.explanation: Volatile solids represent the organic fraction. A lower percent volatile in digested sludge shows organisms converted part of that organic material during digestion.

questions.question: Sludge on a drying bed drains very slowly and stays wet on top after several days. What is a likely process cause to investigate?

answers.text: Blinded bed media or clogged underdrains that are slowing drainage through the bed
Excess grit lightening the sludge
Too much chlorine in the effluent
Uneven sunlight on the bed surface

questions.explanation: Drying beds depend on drainage through media to underdrains. When drainage slows, check for blinded media or clogged underdrains and for sludge applied too thickly.

questions.question: A contact basin operates with a chlorine residual of 1.4 mg/L and provides 25 minutes of contact time. What is the CT value?

answers.text: 26.4 mg-min/L
3.5 mg-min/L
350 mg-min/L
35 mg-min/L

questions.explanation: CT = residual x contact time = 1.4 mg/L x 25 min = 35 mg-min/L.

questions.question: A progressing-cavity pump feeding sludge to a press has lost output over several weeks. Discharge pressure pulsates, the suction supply is good, and the drive speed has not changed. What should the operator suspect?

answers.text: Worn stator and rotor surfaces are letting sludge slip back inside the pump instead of moving forward with each turn
The polymer conditioning system has failed, which prevents a positive displacement pump from moving any sludge at all
The drive motor is running far above its rated speed, which makes this type of pump deliver less sludge per revolution
The discharge line is completely blocked solid, which normally makes this pump run quietly with a smooth, low output

questions.explanation: Progressing-cavity pumps depend on a tight seal between the rotor and the stator. As those surfaces wear, sludge slips back through the pump, output falls, and discharge pressure begins to pulsate.

questions.question: What is the main operational difference between coarse-bubble and fine-bubble diffusers?

answers.text: Coarse-bubble diffusers are used only in grit chambers and are never used in aeration basins
Fine-bubble diffusers never require cleaning during their service life
Coarse-bubble diffusers transfer oxygen more efficiently than fine-bubble units
Fine-bubble diffusers make smaller bubbles and transfer oxygen more efficiently

questions.explanation: Fine bubbles present far more surface area per volume of air than coarse bubbles, so fine-bubble diffusers transfer a greater share of their oxygen into the mixed liquor. Coarse-bubble units are sturdier but less efficient.

questions.question: What does the unloader valve on a plant air compressor do?

answers.text: It raises the receiver pressure above the compressor's rated limit so the stored air can do more work before the compressor has to restart and refill the receiver tank again
It relieves pressure from the compressor head at shutdown or cut-out so the motor can restart without fighting trapped pressure
It drains condensed water from the receiver tank on a timed cycle
It filters oil out of the compressed air before the air dryer unit

questions.explanation: The unloader bleeds off head pressure when the compressor stops or unloads, so the motor is not trying to start against a pressurized cylinder on the next start.

questions.question: During rounds, an operator hears a grinding noise from a motor that was quiet last week, and the bearing housing feels hotter than usual. What is the best response?

answers.text: Report it and schedule bearing inspection soon
Wait a few months to see if the noise goes away
Add extra grease until the housing overflows out
Run the motor faster so the noise blends in well

questions.explanation: New grinding noise plus a hot bearing housing signals bearing wear. Reporting it promptly allows planned repair before the bearing fails and damages the motor.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the silencer on a blower's air inlet?

answers.text: To filter grit and sand out of the air before it reaches the basin
To cool the incoming air so the blower discharge stays at setpoint
To reduce the intake noise produced as air is drawn into the blower
To measure the volume of air the blower delivers to the aeration grid

questions.explanation: Inlet silencers muffle the pulsation and intake noise of the blower. Many combine silencing with inlet filtration, but their named job is noise reduction.

questions.question: Influent TSS is 200 mg/L and effluent TSS is 30 mg/L. What is the percent removal across the plant?

answers.text: 15 percent removal based only on the effluent value divided by the influent value alone
170 percent removal across the plant
70 percent removal across the plant
85 percent

questions.explanation: Percent removal = (influent - effluent) / influent x 100 = (200 - 30) / 200 x 100 = 85%.

questions.question: After locks and tags are applied to a pump's energy sources, what final lockout/tagout step confirms the equipment is safe to service?

answers.text: Removing the lock so the start switch can be tested freely
Trying the controls and checking that no stored or residual energy remains
Asking a coworker who watched the shutdown whether it looked complete and taking their word for it without checking anything yourself
Signing the work order to show the job is ready to begin

questions.explanation: Verification confirms isolation worked: the operator tries the controls and checks for stored or residual energy before servicing begins.

questions.question: Where should a worker look for hazard and safe-handling information on a laboratory chemical?

answers.text: On the product marketing sheet kept in the front office reception area drawer
In the monthly discharge monitoring report filed for the treatment facility
In the safety data sheet for that chemical
On the shipping invoice that lists only the price and delivery date information

questions.explanation: Safety data sheets provide hazards, PPE, handling, storage, and emergency information for chemicals. They must be readily accessible to workers.

water-distribution-class-4.quiz_title: Water Distribution Class IV Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Why does a water-age limit act as a binding constraint on a production schedule, even when a cheaper way to run the sources is available?

answers.text: Stored water loses quality as it ages, so storage must be cycled even when holding it longer would cost less
Older water raises the pumping head in every main in the system, which is why the age limit must be enforced daily
The age limit is what determines the correct size of customer service lines
Water age is recorded only because it is needed for customer billing

questions.explanation: Stored water ages, loses residual, and loses quality, so tanks must be cycled within age limits even when a cheaper schedule would hold water longer. At the directing level the age limit overrides a purely cost-based running order.

questions.question: A peak-shaving plan depends on a transfer section with a flow area of 1.85 square feet carrying water at 3.62 feet per second. What flow rate, in gallons per minute, does that section deliver?

answers.text: About 3,006 gpm
About 2,405 gpm
About 3,607 gpm
About 1,503 gpm

questions.explanation: Flow = area x velocity x 448.8 = 1.85 sq ft x 3.62 ft/s x 448.8 = 6.697 x 448.8 = 3,006 gpm (approximately). The plan may only count this deliverable rate, not the station's nameplate rate, when it assigns the peak gap to this transfer.

questions.question: A hydraulic model predicts adequate pressures in a zone, but field gauges there read much lower. What is the directing operator's first response?

answers.text: Approve replacement of the zone's oldest mains on the strength of the model alone, without any field check
Verify field conditions first, checking for a closed valve, bad data, or changed demand
Raise production until the model prediction and the field readings happen to match
Lower the zone's pressure target so the existing readings comply on paper

questions.explanation: When a model or record prediction disagrees with field pressures, the operator verifies field conditions first, looking for a closed valve, bad data, or changed demand. A construction conclusion is not defensible until the disagreement itself is explained.

questions.question: A new rectangular ground reservoir is 24 ft long, 15 ft wide, and 8 ft deep. What is its volume in gallons?
questions.explanation: Volume = length x width x depth x 7.48. So 24 x 15 x 8 x 7.48 = 21,542.4 gal.

questions.question: A well pump delivers 480 gpm against 135 ft of head at 75 percent efficiency. What brake horsepower must the motor supply?
questions.explanation: Brake horsepower = (flow x head / 3,960) / efficiency. Water horsepower is 480 x 135 / 3,960 = 16.36 hp, and 16.36 / 0.75 = 21.82 hp.

questions.question: At a program audit, a booster station's feeder delivers 34.7 lb/day into a flow of 2.05 MGD. What dose is the station actually applying?
questions.explanation: Dose from feed = feed (lb/day) / (flow (MGD) x 8.34) = 34.7 / (2.05 x 8.34) = 34.7 / 17.097 = 2.03 mg/L.

questions.question: What makes a sampling site representative when a program is redesigned for a grown system?

answers.text: It is the site easiest for the sampler to reach each morning, and no follow-up sampling or verification is needed afterward
It reflects the water actually delivered to a real service area, including its age and flow conditions
It is any hydrant, since all distribution water is identical
It is the site closest to the treatment plant, where water is freshest, regardless of what the rest of the system's monitoring shows that month

questions.explanation: Representative sites mirror delivered water across the system's zones, ages, and storage influences, so results describe what customers actually receive.

questions.question: During a quality response, a station feeds a flow of 1.45 MGD at a chlorine dose of 4.2 mg/L. How many pounds per day are applied?

answers.text: 60.9 lb/day
42.3 lb/day
50.77 lb/day
6.09 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow (MGD) x dose (mg/L) x 8.34 = 1.45 x 4.2 x 8.34 = 50.77 lb/day.

questions.question: How do grab samples and continuous analyzers complement each other in a monitoring program?

answers.text: Grab samples are only for training new operators
Analyzers show the pattern between visits at one location, while grab samples verify analyzer accuracy and cover the wider system
Analyzers make grab sampling unnecessary at every location
Grab samples calibrate themselves against the analyzer automatically because it has been the utility's long-standing practice in similar cases

questions.explanation: Continuous data reveal trends and excursions at instrumented points; verified grab results keep those instruments honest and extend coverage beyond them.

questions.question: A validated top-down water audit shows real losses dominate the system's losses, but it cannot say where in the system the water is escaping. What program step should be directed next?

answers.text: Fund additional leak repair crews evenly across every district at once, and record that decision in the program file for the next scheduled review
Use district metering and night-flow analysis to locate where real losses are concentrated before committing repair resources
Raise the apparent-loss program's funding, since its work is better understood, while noting the choice in the quarterly program report sent to utility leadership
Set a lower loss target and wait for the next annual audit to clarify the picture, and leave the underlying program arrangements unchanged for the rest of the operating year

questions.explanation: A top-down audit sizes a problem; it does not locate it. District-level measurement and night-flow analysis show where the real losses are, so repair money is spent where the water is.

questions.question: Pumping energy cost $132,000 of a distribution operating budget totaling $300,000 for the year. What percent of the operating budget is pumping energy?
questions.explanation: Worked math: percent = (part / total) x 100 = (132,000 / 300,000) x 100 = 0.44 x 100 = 44%. The 56% figure is the remainder of the budget, and 22% results from halving the correct share.

questions.question: A flood forces one of the system's two sources out of service for at least two days during a high-demand week, while storage is near normal. What is the directing operator's first plan-level action?

answers.text: Activate the emergency response plan, shifting zones and storage to the remaining source under its pre-set priorities
Ask customers system-wide to stop all outdoor use indefinitely, with no end condition stated and no review date set, until someone remembers to lift the request
Wait for storage to fall to its lowest level before changing any system operations
Continue the routine plan unchanged because the remaining source is still producing water

questions.explanation: Loss of a source is exactly the condition the emergency response plan is written for, with pre-set priorities for zones and storage. Waiting for storage to empty or improvising restrictions discards that preparation.

water-distribution-class-3.quiz_title: Water Distribution Class III Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Every tank is full, demand is moderate, and pressures at low-elevation services are climbing above the normal working range while hilltop pressures remain comfortable. What adjustment should the senior operator make?

answers.text: Reduce the feed into the low area and trim production until pressures return to the normal range
Start another booster pump so the low area has even more water available
Open a tank drain and waste water until the low-elevation pressures look better
Take no action at all, because high pressure simply means customers have plenty of water and pressure can never be too high in a distribution system

questions.explanation: With storage full and demand only moderate, excess feed is what is pushing low-elevation pressures above the normal range. Trimming production and reducing the feed into that area brings pressures back into range; adding pumping would raise them further and wasting water treats the symptom instead of the cause.

questions.question: To measure how much water a district actually uses overnight, an operator isolates the district so its tank is the only supply, holds all pumps off for a timed period, and records the tank level drop and the tank dimensions. What does this test determine?

answers.text: The C-factor of the oldest main in the district, from the speed of the level drop
The specific capacity of the well that normally feeds the tank during the day
The pressure that will be available at the highest service in the district during the next fire event
The district's actual flow rate over the test period, from the volume that left storage

questions.explanation: With the tank as the only source, the volume that leaves storage during the timed period is the district's use, so volume divided by time gives its flow rate. The test says nothing direct about pipe roughness, well performance, or fire pressure.

questions.question: To plan a turnover cycle, a senior operator will draw a storage tank holding 297,000 gallons at an average rate of 550 gpm. How long will it take to exchange that volume at that draw rate?

answers.text: About 9.0 hours
About 5.4 hours
About 18.0 hours
About 540 hours

questions.explanation: Turnover time = volume / flow = 297,000 gal / (550 gpm x 60 min/hr) = 297,000 / 33,000 = 9.0 hours. The 540 figure divides gallons by gpm and stops at minutes without converting to hours.

questions.question: A repaired main section is ready for its post-repair flush. From which direction should flushing flow be moved through the section?

answers.text: From the repaired section outward into the clean system on both sides
From a clean, unaffected part of the system toward and past the repair, carrying debris out at the discharge point
From the nearest dead end back toward the repair, to save water
Direction does not matter as long as the velocity is high

questions.explanation: Post-repair flushing moves clean water through the work area so loosened debris and any remaining contamination are carried to the discharge point, not pushed into clean piping.

questions.question: A station pump delivers 480 gpm against 142 feet of head at 72 percent efficiency. What brake horsepower must the motor supply?

answers.text: About 17.2 hp
About 12.4 hp
About 33.2 hp
About 23.9 hp

questions.explanation: Water horsepower = (480 x 142) / 3,960 = 68,160 / 3,960 = about 17.2 hp. Brake horsepower = 17.2 / 0.72 = about 23.9 hp. The motor must be sized for the brake horsepower, which includes the pump's losses.

questions.question: Pipe and fittings for a repair were disinfected early in the shift, then left open and uncovered in the trench while the crew was pulled to an emergency, returning the next morning to dusty, open pipe ends. Before assembly, what must happen?

answers.text: The parts may be assembled as disinfected, because the previous day's chlorine treatment remains effective on the surfaces
Only the pipe ends need a freshwater rinse, since dust on an interior surface flushes out harmlessly at startup
The parts must be scrapped and replaced with new stock, because once disinfected parts sit overnight they cannot be re-treated
The parts must be cleaned and disinfected again immediately before they are assembled

questions.explanation: Disinfection protects only until the surface is exposed again. Parts left open to trench dust and air are cleaned and re-disinfected right before assembly; they are not scrapped, but the earlier treatment no longer counts.

questions.question: What is the purpose of routine maintenance on chemical feed equipment in a distribution disinfection program?

answers.text: To allow longer intervals between residual samples, since maintained feeders cannot drift, even though the same approach has not corrected it before
To keep feeders, lines, and injectors clean and calibrated so the applied dose stays accurate and uninterrupted
To document equipment age for the asset inventory, with no effect on dosing accuracy
To reduce chemical usage by intentionally restricting the maximum feed rate of each pump

questions.explanation: Fouled lines, worn pump parts, and clogged injectors quietly change the delivered dose; scheduled cleaning and calibration keep feed accurate between verification checks.

questions.question: A station treats 0.72 MGD and must apply a dose of 1.8 mg/L using a product that is 65% available chlorine. How many pounds of product must be fed per day?

answers.text: 10.81 lb/day
7.02 lb/day
16.63 lb/day
21.55 lb/day

questions.explanation: Feed with purity = flow x dose x 8.34 / (purity as a decimal). So 0.72 x 1.8 x 8.34 / 0.65 = 16.63 lb/day of product.

questions.question: A repaired main has been disinfected and flushed, and the first bacteriological set is satisfactory. A supervisor presses to return it to service before the second set to restore a detour route sooner. What should the senior operator do?

answers.text: Return it to service; one clean set is enough when traffic is waiting, and treat the result as settled without further checking
Hold it out of service until the second consecutive satisfactory set is in hand
Return it but tell customers not to drink the water
Skip sampling and rely on the chlorine residual instead

questions.explanation: Return to service rests on the full satisfactory sampling sequence, not on schedule pressure. A single clean set does not complete the verification the disinfection was performed to achieve.

questions.question: In a planned traffic control setup, what is the purpose of the open buffer area between the end of the taper and the start of the actual work area?

answers.text: It gives an errant or slow-stopping vehicle room to stop or recover before reaching the crew and the excavation
It is the designated place to park the crew truck and stage pipe where it is closest to the trench
It is extra pavement kept clear so flaggers can step back and talk with the crew between traffic cycles
It is a storage lane for signs and cones that will be needed when the closure is taken down at the end of the day

questions.explanation: The buffer is empty recovery space that protects the crew if a driver fails to merge or stop in time. Using it for parking, staging, or standing removes the protection it is there to provide.

questions.question: A distribution maintenance budget totals $300,000 for the year. The meter change-out program accounts for $51,000 of that budget. What percent of the maintenance budget does the meter change-out program represent?
questions.explanation: Percent of total = (part / total) x 100 = ($51,000 / $300,000) x 100 = 0.17 x 100 = 17.0%. The 83.0% figure is the share remaining for everything else, not the change-out share.

questions.question: A program evaluation shows the testing compliance rate has dropped sharply over two quarters. Review finds the assemblies were installed and inventoried correctly, but reminder notices were mailed to outdated addresses copied from an old billing list, and many owners never learned their tests were due. What is the correct program fix?

answers.text: Extend every affected assembly's testing due date by a full additional year to clear the backlog, and suspend new notices in that area until the following cycle
Record the untested assemblies as passing for this cycle so the compliance rate returns to normal
Begin formal enforcement proceedings against all of the affected property owners at the same time
Correct the address records against current account data and reissue the notices with a new deadline

questions.explanation: The compliance failure originated in the program's own records, so enforcement against owners who were never properly notified would be misplaced. Correcting the addresses and reissuing notices with a fair deadline restores the process.

water-distribution-class-2.quiz_title: Water Distribution Class II Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: One street reports low pressure while surrounding streets on the same main are normal, and a recent repair occurred on that street. Which cause should field verification check first?

answers.text: A valve left partially closed after the recent repair work
System-wide tuberculation affecting every main throughout the entire pressure zone
A citywide drop in source water production
Normal aging of the elevated storage tank coating

questions.explanation: A localized low-pressure pocket right after nearby repair work points first to a valve not fully reopened. Zone-wide or system-wide causes would affect surrounding streets as well, so the data pattern directs the first check.

questions.question: Water moves at 3.5 feet per second through a main section with a cross-sectional area of 1.25 square feet. What is the flow in gpm? Use Flow (gpm) = area (sq ft) x velocity (fps) x 448.8.

answers.text: 4.4 gpm

questions.explanation: Flow = 1.25 sq ft x 3.5 fps x 448.8 = 1,963.5 gpm. The 4.4-gpm distractor is the flow in cubic feet per second before the 448.8 conversion to gallons per minute is applied.

questions.question: Homes below a pressure-reducing valve report pressures well above the valve's set point at night, but normal pressures during the busy morning. What does the timing of the complaint indicate?

answers.text: The valve is failing to close down and hold its set point when downstream demand is low
The upstream zone is over-pumping only at night, which no valve setting can influence
Customer meters below the valve are under-registering and creating false pressure data
The valve is working correctly, because downstream pressure should always equal upstream at night

questions.explanation: A reducing valve must throttle down as demand falls and hold downstream pressure at its set point. Pressure that creeps up only under low-demand conditions shows the valve is not controlling at low flow and needs service, not a higher plant output.

questions.question: A cross-connection survey finds a chemical mixing tank on a double-check assembly. The contents would be a health hazard if they entered the main. What decision follows from the survey?

answers.text: Leave the assembly, because any testable assembly satisfies every hazard level equally
Replace it with a vacuum breaker, because the tank is vented to the atmosphere at the top
Upgrade to a reduced-pressure assembly or an air gap, because double-check assemblies are for low hazards only
Replace it with a hose-bib protector, because the fill line enters through a threaded fitting

questions.explanation: Protection must match the hazard: double-check assemblies are limited to low-hazard connections. A health-hazard chemical connection needs high-hazard protection — a reduced-pressure assembly or an air gap — regardless of how well the existing device tests.

questions.question: A disinfection fill uses 0.06 MG of water in one day at a dose of 25 mg/L, but the chlorine product available is only 65% pure. How many pounds of that product must be fed?

answers.text: About 12.5 lb
About 29.6 lb
About 19.2 lb
About 8.1 lb

questions.explanation: Pure chlorine needed = 0.06 x 25 x 8.34 = 12.51 lb. Correcting for purity: 12.51 / 0.65 = 19.2 lb of the 65% product must be fed.

questions.question: An operator approaches a gate valve with a rising stem and can see the stem standing well up out of the valve. What does the stem's position tell the operator?

answers.text: That the valve was exercised on schedule this year
How far open or closed the valve is
That the valve is a butterfly valve, not a gate valve
How much pressure is standing in the main right now

questions.explanation: On a rising-stem gate valve, the stem rises as the valve opens and lowers as it closes. The exposed stem height is therefore a direct visual indication of the valve's position, letting the operator read how far open or closed it is without turning it or counting handwheel rotations.

questions.question: A hydrant inspection finds deep pitting and heavy rust on the barrel right at the ground line, while the upper barrel coating is sound. The hydrant operates normally. What is the best evaluation and next step?

answers.text: Judge it cosmetic, because corrosion at the ground line never affects the barrel's strength
Cover the rust with a heavier coat of paint and close the inspection with no further digging in this case
Condemn the whole hydrant immediately, because any visible rust means the barrel has failed
Excavate enough to inspect the buried barrel and flange area, since ground-line attack is hidden

questions.explanation: The ground line is where moisture and oxygen meet, and the worst attack is often just below grade where it cannot be seen. Excavating to inspect the buried barrel and flange turns a surface finding into a real condition decision.

questions.question: A booster station treats an average flow of 0.85 MGD and applies a chlorine dose of 0.9 mg/L. How many pounds of chlorine does it feed per day?

answers.text: About 0.77 lb per day
About 12.76 lb per day
About 6.38 lb per day
About 63.8 lb per day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow (MGD) x dose (mg/L) x 8.34 = 0.85 x 0.9 x 8.34 = 6.38 lb per day. Omitting the 8.34 factor gives 0.77, and doubling the flow gives 12.76.

questions.question: Water entering a tank carries a good residual, but water leaving the same tank reads much lower. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: The inlet sample must have been wrong
The tank is adding chlorine demand at the outlet only first
Residual decayed during storage, consistent with water age
The outlet tap needs a longer flush only

questions.explanation: A drop across storage shows decay while the water was held, a water-age effect addressed by cycling and turnover.

questions.question: Discolored-water calls from one neighborhood begin within an hour of a pump trip that briefly reversed flow in the area, then fade over two days. What is the best evaluation of this pattern?

answers.text: The flow disturbance likely shook deposits loose, a temporary event effect rather than steady corrosion
The treatment plant most likely changed its chemical feed rates during that same hour without telling anyone
Every caller most likely has a failing water heater at the same time
The pattern proves a coliform problem is developing in that main

questions.explanation: Complaints that start with a flow reversal and fade as the water clears fit disturbed deposits. Timing tied to an operational event is a key evaluation clue.

questions.question: A booster station feeds chlorine into 0.60 MGD of flow at a dose of 1.8 mg/L. How many pounds of chlorine does the station use per day?

answers.text: About 1.1 lb per day
About 9.0 lb per day
About 90.1 lb per day
About 5.0 lb per day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow (MGD) x dose (mg/L) x 8.34 = 0.60 x 1.8 x 8.34 = 9.01, about 9.0 lb per day. Daily use figures drive chemical inventory and reorder planning.

questions.question: By mid-year, a crew leader's tracking shows repair and overtime spending in the crew's work areas running well ahead of the budget pace. What should the crew leader do?

answers.text: Spend the remaining funds quickly before they are taken away at year end by the finance office
Stop tracking spending until the final quarter figures are available
Compare spending in the work areas against the budget and adjust work planning early
Move the overrun into a different work area without telling anyone

questions.explanation: Operators who participate in the budget process track spending in their own work areas against the budget, so a mid-year overrun is addressed in work planning rather than hidden or ignored.

water-distribution-class-1.quiz_title: Water Distribution Class I Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: At a bend in a crowded utility corridor there is no room for a proper thrust block. What is an appropriate alternative for restraint?

answers.text: Leave the joint unrestrained and lower pressure for a day
Use restrained joints to hold the fitting against thrust
Wrap the joint in plastic sheeting and backfill it loosely
Move the bend to the middle of the nearest straight section

questions.explanation: Thrust at bends must be restrained by thrust blocks or by restrained joints. Where a block cannot be placed, restrained joints lock the fitting and pipe together so pressure cannot push the joint apart.

questions.question: A gauge reads 75 psi at the base of a standpipe. How many feet of head does this pressure represent?

answers.text: About 32.5 ft of head
About 75.0 ft of head
About 173.3 ft of head
About 346.5 ft of head

questions.explanation: Head = pressure x 2.31. Head = 75 psi x 2.31 = 173.25, about 173.3 ft of head.

questions.question: Why are dry-barrel hydrants used in cold climates?

answers.text: The barrel drains after use and the main valve sits below the frost line
The barrel stays full so it can freeze solid without any damage occurring
The top is painted red so crews can find it easily in deep winter snow
The flange is made to break away whenever a vehicle strikes the hydrant

questions.explanation: Dry-barrel hydrants drain after use and the main valve is below the frost line, preventing a full barrel of water from freezing.

questions.question: What is backpressure in backflow prevention?

answers.text: Downstream pressure exceeding the supply pressure
Negative pressure in a main after a large break occurs
The normal working pressure in a residential service line
Air pressure trapped at a high point in a distribution main

questions.explanation: Backpressure occurs when downstream pressure, from sources such as boilers, pumps, or elevated tanks, exceeds the supply pressure and can push water backward.

questions.question: How much water fills a 24-inch main section that is 50 feet long? The pipe diameter is 2.0 feet.

answers.text: 157 gal

questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 x D squared x length x 7.48 = 0.785 x 4.0 x 50 x 7.48 = 1,174 gal in the section.

questions.question: A vehicle strikes a hydrant and the upper barrel shears cleanly off without flooding the street. What design feature worked as intended?

answers.text: The breakaway flange, which lets the hydrant shear without flooding
The thrust block, which absorbed the full force of the impact at the base
The corporation stop, which closed when the barrel separated
The air-release valve, which vented pressure from the barrel

questions.explanation: Breakaway flanges let a struck hydrant shear at ground level while the main valve stays closed below, preventing flooding and limiting the repair.

questions.question: Records and wet pavement show a leak somewhere along a 300-foot block, but no water is surfacing at one spot. What should the crew do before opening the street?

answers.text: Excavate the whole block in sections until the leak appears
Wait for the leak to surface so its position is easy to see
Use listening equipment on fittings to pinpoint the leak area
Raise zone pressure overnight to force the leak to show itself

questions.explanation: Listening devices and correlators pick up leak sound at valves, hydrants, and services, narrowing the dig to the actual leak instead of opening the whole block.

questions.question: How much water is needed to fill a new 12-inch main section that is 100 feet long? The pipe diameter is 1.0 foot.

answers.text: 78.5 gal
587 gal
785 gal

questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 x D squared x length x 7.48 = 0.785 x 1.0 x 100 x 7.48 = 587 gal to fill the section.

questions.question: Which locations should be used for routine distribution system sampling?

answers.text: Designated sites including dead ends and far reaches
Only taps located closest to the treatment plant and main office building
Random garden hoses chosen on the day of collection
Hydrants selected because they are easiest to park beside

questions.explanation: Regulatory and informational samples come from designated sites representative of the whole system, including dead ends and far reaches where water is oldest.

questions.question: Before filling a bacteriological bottle at a designated site, the operator runs the tap for a period first. Why?

answers.text: To warm the sample so bacteria grow more quickly
To rinse the disinfectant out of the sterile sample bottle before filling it
To flush the line so the sample represents water in the main
To lower the pressure so the bottle fills more slowly

questions.explanation: The line is flushed before sampling so stagnant water in the service and faucet is cleared and the sample represents water in the distribution main.

questions.question: A customer reports having no water at all, and no outage is posted for the area. What should the operator check first?

answers.text: Whether the customers bill shows a balance from two billing cycles ago today
Whether a plumber has visited the home at any time during the past year
Whether unreported system work or a closed valve is affecting the service, and the state of its service valves
Whether the customer has recently installed a new irrigation system that could have been tied into the service line incorrectly

questions.explanation: A no-water report is worked from the system side first: area work, valve positions, and the corporation and curb stops on the service determine whether the cause is the utilitys or the homes.

questions.question: A worn booster pump is replaced with a new unit at a station. What should the operator do in the asset records?

answers.text: Leave the old pumps record untouched so the station history looks unchanged
Delete the station from the inventory until its next scheduled inspection
Update the asset record to reflect the new pump and the start of its service history
Record the replacement only in the crews personal notebook for future reference during later repairs

questions.explanation: Asset management depends on a current inventory with maintenance history. A replacement that is never recorded leaves the program planning around equipment that no longer exists.

water-treatment-class-4.quiz_title: Water Treatment Class IV Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A residuals discharge is scheduled, but the effluent quality from the residuals stream has degraded and releasing it now would exceed the permit limits that govern that discharge. What should the operator in charge do?

answers.text: Release it during a period of high receiving-water flow so dilution keeps the exceedance from being noticed
Release half now and half later so each release looks smaller
Release it at night when the discharge is least likely to be sampled
Hold and manage the residuals on site until the discharge can meet its permit limits

questions.explanation: Permit limits govern residual effluent quality returned or discharged, and they are not waived by dilution, splitting, or timing tricks. The compliant course is to hold and manage the residuals until a lawful discharge can be made.

questions.question: A day tank feeds 585.5 lb/day of coagulant product (taken as 100% chemical for this check) while the plant treats 3.9 MGD. What dose is actually being delivered?

answers.text: 9.0 mg/L
1.8 mg/L

questions.explanation: Dose from feed = feed (lb/day) / (flow (MGD) x 8.34). Substituting: 585.5 / (3.9 x 8.34) = 585.5 / 32.53 = 18.0 mg/L delivered.

questions.question: Over several weeks a membrane train needs steadily rising transmembrane pressure to hold its flux as fouling builds. What is the proper operating response sequence?

answers.text: Hold the pressure where it is and let the train run at rising pressure until it can no longer produce its share of plant flow
Use backpulse to restore recovery during operation and schedule chemical cleaning as the pressure trend continues
Defeat the pressure alarms so the trend stops interrupting operations
Swap the train's feed to the permeate header to reverse the fouling

questions.explanation: As fouling builds, flux declines and transmembrane pressure rises. Recovery is restored by backpulse during operation and by chemical cleaning when the trend calls for it — not by running the train to failure or silencing its alarms.

questions.question: To avoid starting a fourth train, operators have run three trains well above design flux for months. Cleanings are now needed far more often and run lengths keep shrinking. What is the root problem and the correction?

answers.text: The membranes have reached end of life together; replace all three trains at once
Sustained over-flux is fouling the trains faster; return to design flux by using all trains and storage as intended
The cleaning chemical has weakened in storage; order fresh chemical at the same strength and keep the same flux schedule
Raw water quality has worsened; raise the coagulant dose until the run lengths recover

questions.explanation: Flux pushed above design drives fouling faster, which shows up as ever-shorter runs and more frequent cleanings across all the over-run trains at once. The correction is operational: restore design flux by bringing the fourth train and storage back into the production plan.

questions.question: Raw water enters treatment at 210 color units and finished water leaves at 18.9 color units. What percent of the color was removed?
questions.explanation: Use pct_removal: (210 - 18.9) / 210 x 100 = 91%. Only 9% of the incoming color remains in the finished water.

questions.question: Which laboratory measurement distinguishes a chloramine-decay problem from a dosing problem in a chloraminated system?

answers.text: Total alkalinity at the plant effluent tap
Free ammonia at the affected distribution sites
Raw-water turbidity at the intake structure
Finished-water hardness leaving the clearwell

questions.explanation: Free ammonia distinguishes a chloramine-decay problem from a dosing problem. Excess free ammonia at the far ends points to decay feeding nitrification, while a dosing problem shows a different ammonia picture.

questions.question: A routine check shows the control system's backup power batteries can no longer carry the PLC and instruments for their rated time. What is the correct maintenance action?

answers.text: Leave them in place, because controls draw almost no power during an outage
Test them again in a year to confirm the decline is real before spending money for the record
Replace or restore the batteries promptly, before an outage tests them in service
Remove the batteries so a weak set cannot drag down the control voltage

questions.explanation: Backup power keeps controls, instruments, and alarms alive through an outage; a set that already fails its load check must be restored promptly, not left to fail when it is actually needed.

questions.question: A discharge gauge on a booster pump reads 58 psi during an efficiency test. How many feet of head does this represent?
questions.explanation: Head = psi x 2.31 = 58 x 2.31 = 134.0 ft. Test heads must be in feet before they are plotted against the manufacturer's pump curve.

questions.question: Heavy algae growth noted during a reservoir inspection warns the operator to expect which combination at the plant?

answers.text: Taste and odor complaints, higher daytime pH, and shorter filter runs
Lower raw-water pH at midday and steadily lengthening filter runs
Falling iron and manganese with no change in raw-water turbidity
Rising well yields and a falling demand for coagulant chemicals

questions.explanation: Algae raise pH during daylight photosynthesis, produce taste and odor compounds, and load filters so runs shorten. Growth seen at the reservoir is therefore an early warning of treatment effects, not just a cosmetic condition of the source.

questions.question: A utility-sponsored household hazardous-waste collection day supports source water protection mainly by doing what?

answers.text: Testing each resident's well water while chemicals are dropped off
Giving residents a proper disposal route for chemicals kept at home
Replacing the watershed protection plan with a one-day cleanup event
Removing sediment that has accumulated in the raw-water reservoir

questions.explanation: Education on chemical storage and disposal works when residents have somewhere proper to take leftover chemicals instead of pouring them out or storing them indefinitely. A collection day turns the protection message into an action residents can complete.

questions.question: A plant's annual operating budget is $625,000, and $187,500 has been spent by the end of the first quarter review. What percent of the operating budget has been expended?

answers.text: 33.33% of the budget
70.00% of the budget
30.00% of the budget
25.00% of the budget

questions.explanation: Percent expended = part / total x 100 = 187,500 / 625,000 x 100 = 30.00%. The plant has expended 30.00% of its operating budget.

questions.question: Preparing an annual evaluation, a supervisor realizes the file holds only notes from a difficult incident last month, though the operator performed well most of the year. What should the supervisor do?

answers.text: Write the evaluation around the incident because it is best documented
Give the operator the same rating as last year to avoid the missing data
Reconstruct the full-year record from logs and notes before evaluating
Skip the evaluation this year because the documentation is incomplete

questions.explanation: An evaluation must reflect documented performance across the whole review period. The supervisor rebuilds the record from operating logs and notes rather than letting one recent incident stand in for the year.

water-treatment-class-3.quiz_title: Water Treatment Class III Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: What is the sedimentation step in a conventional plant designed to accomplish?

answers.text: To disinfect the water before it reaches the filters and the clearwell, replacing the need for a separate disinfection step later in the treatment train
To remove, by gravity, the settleable floc formed during coagulation and flocculation
To soften the water by precipitating calcium and magnesium hardness
To add alkalinity back to water that coagulation has depleted

questions.explanation: Sedimentation removes settled floc by gravity, taking out the bulk of the solids before filtration. Disinfection, softening, and alkalinity replacement are separate steps elsewhere in the train.

questions.question: A plant treating 1.85 MGD needs a pure chemical dose of 31 mg/L, but the dry product on hand is only 82% pure. How many pounds of the product must be fed per day?

answers.text: 392.2 lb/day
478.3 lb/day
583.3 lb/day
711.3 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pure chemical needed = 1.85 x 31 x 8.34 = 478.3 lb/day, and dividing by the purity as a decimal, 478.3 / 0.82 = 583.3 lb/day of product. Feeding only the pure-chemical weight would underdose the water because part of every pound of product is inactive material.

questions.question: A SCADA trend shows one process value locked at exactly the same reading for hours while related flows and levels move normally, punctuated by occasional out-of-range spikes. What should the operator conclude and do?

answers.text: The process has reached a perfect steady state, so the value can be removed from the rounds sheet entirely
The process is upset in a way no local instrument can confirm, so chemical doses should be doubled as a precaution
The alarm system itself has failed plant-wide, so all SCADA values should be ignored until the next software update
The sensor has likely failed — a frozen value with spikes — so the instrument is corrected while the process is verified locally

questions.explanation: A failed sensor is recognized by a frozen value or out-of-range spikes, and the correction is to the instrument, not the process. Operators acknowledge and verify alarms against local instruments before acting on them.

questions.question: Two parallel treatment trains receive the same raw water at the same coagulant dose. Over several days, one train's settled turbidity steadily worsens while the other's stays at its normal level. What does the comparison tell the supervisor?

answers.text: The raw water must have changed, because both trains would otherwise perform identically at all times
The problem is specific to the worsening train — its mixing, flocculation, or settling equipment — rather than the shared chemistry or raw water, so that train is where the investigation belongs
The good train is being underdosed and should have its dose cut until the two trains match again

Both trains should have their coagulant doses raised together, in equal steps, and kept there until the poorer train recovers, whatever the underlying cause of its decline turns out to be when the maintenance crew finally gets a chance to look into it

questions.explanation: When shared inputs are identical, a one-train decline isolates the fault to that train's own equipment or hydraulics. Comparing parallel units this way keeps the supervisor from changing plant-wide chemistry for a unit-specific problem.

questions.question: Laboratory turbidity results show raw water entering clarification at 160 NTU and settled water leaving at 12 NTU. What is the percent removal across the clarifier?
questions.explanation: Percent removal = (in - out) / in x 100 = (160 - 12) / 160 x 100 = 148 / 160 x 100 = 92.50%. The 7.50% figure is the share of turbidity remaining, not the share removed.

questions.question: For protozoa monitoring, which set of duties belongs to the plant operator rather than the specialized laboratory?

answers.text: Performing the immunomagnetic separation and microscopic identification of every organism recovered
Sampling, preservation, chain of custody, and interpreting results for the plant
Designing the analytical method and certifying the specialized laboratory's quality system each year
Counting oocysts under the microscope and signing the specialized laboratory's final report as analyst

questions.explanation: The operator's role in protozoa monitoring is sampling, preservation, chain of custody, and interpreting the results for treatment decisions. The specialized separation and identification work is performed by the laboratory equipped for it.

questions.question: A thermography scan finds one connection in a motor starter running much hotter than the identical connections beside it, while the motor itself runs normally. What does this indicate and require?

answers.text: Proof that the motor is oversized for its pump, without documenting the work, the readings, or the reason for the decision in the maintenance record
A need to raise the starter's overload setting
Normal operation, because starters always have one hot connection
A loose or deteriorating connection that should be corrected before it fails or damages the starter

questions.explanation: Thermography is a predictive tool that finds hot spots in electrical gear before failure. A single hot connection among identical neighbors points to that connection, not to the motor.

questions.question: A pump delivers 540 gpm against 130 ft of head and tests at 72% efficiency. What brake horsepower must the motor supply?
questions.explanation: Water horsepower = (540 x 130) / 3,960 = 17.73 hp, and brake horsepower = 17.73 / 0.72 = 24.62 hp. Dividing by the efficiency as a decimal accounts for the power lost inside the pump.

questions.question: A core sample shows filter media depth has fallen well below the design depth, though the remaining media is clean and properly graded. What is the appropriate response?

answers.text: Raise the filtration rate to compensate for the shallow bed and no further checking or follow-up of any kind is needed
Remove the filter from service permanently
Top up the media to restore the design depth and investigate where media is being lost
Replace the entire bed immediately in all such cases

questions.explanation: Clean, well-graded media that is simply short on depth needs topping up, not wholesale replacement. The loss pathway, such as carryover during backwash, should be found so the depth holds.

questions.question: Chlorinating raw-water lines is used at mussel-prone intakes for what purpose?

answers.text: To soften the raw water before it reaches treatment at any time during the operating year
To control mussel settlement and growth in the lines
To raise raw-water pH ahead of the coagulation step
To dissolve eroded bank sediment in the reservoir

questions.explanation: Chlorine applied in raw-water lines discourages mussels from settling and growing there. It complements coatings, mechanical removal, and veliger monitoring.

questions.question: Brushing, as a well rehabilitation method, works by doing what?

answers.text: Adding a new gravel pack around the screen
Scrubbing deposits and growth from the casing and screen surfaces
Pumping the well at a very low rate for a week, whether or not the watershed has changed at all in recent years
Heating the well water to kill bacteria

questions.explanation: Brushing mechanically scrubs the inside of the casing and screen to loosen deposits and growth. The loosened material is then removed so flow into the well improves.

questions.question: A supervisor is estimating a monthly chemical order for a plant treating 2.7 MGD at a dose of 6 mg/L. How many pounds per day is the plant feeding?

answers.text: 16.20 lb/day
135.11 lb/day
48.60 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow x dose x 8.34 = 2.7 MGD x 6 mg/L x 8.34 = 135.11 lb/day. The order estimate is built from this verified daily feed rate.

water-treatment-class-2.quiz_title: Water Treatment Class II Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Over several weeks a membrane unit shows declining flux and rising transmembrane pressure at the same flow. What does this indicate?

answers.text: The membranes are becoming cleaner with use
Fouling is building up on the membranes
Recovery has improved beyond its design value
The permeate quality has stopped mattering

questions.explanation: Flux declines and transmembrane pressure rises as fouling builds. Backpulse and chemical cleaning are used to restore recovery.

questions.question: Raw water entering an iron-removal filter contains 2.0 mg/L of iron, and the filter effluent contains 0.10 mg/L. What is the percent removal?
questions.explanation: Percent removal = (in - out) / in x 100 = (2.0 - 0.10) / 2.0 x 100 = 95%.

questions.question: In a jar test, how is the coagulant dose selected?

answers.text: Lowest dose with well-formed floc and lowest settled turbidity
Highest dose tested, regardless of settled turbidity results
Dose producing the largest floc, even if turbidity stays higher
Average of all doses that formed any visible floc at all

questions.explanation: A jar test runs samples through rapid mix, tapered flocculation, and settling. The operator selects the lowest dose that forms good floc and gives the lowest settled turbidity.

questions.question: Why are storage tank levels deliberately cycled up and down in a chloraminated system?

answers.text: To exercise the altitude valve once each shift
To keep the tank as full as possible at all times
To reduce detention time, which otherwise drives residual loss and nitrification
To increase the pressure and storage available to the system during hours of peak demand

questions.explanation: Long detention lets chloramine decay and lets ammonia-oxidizing bacteria nitrify the water. Cycling levels turns the stored water over, limiting age, residual loss, and nitrification.

questions.question: Lab results show a process stream entering at 85 mg/L TSS and leaving at 5 mg/L TSS. What is the percent removal?
The designated distribution sampling tap is locked inside a closed building, so the sampler collects from a garden hose bib next door instead. Why is that sample unacceptable?

answers.text: Hose bibs always contain much more chlorine than regularly flushed service taps, so the sample would show a falsely high residual and hide any problem
Samples must come from the cold-water kitchen tap only
The laboratory cannot analyze water collected outdoors
Distribution samples must come from representative, regularly flushed service taps at designated sites — not hoses or substitute fixtures

questions.explanation: Sample plans designate representative sites in advance, and samples are drawn from regularly flushed service taps. Hoses, swivel faucets, and leaking or substitute fixtures do not represent the distribution system.

questions.question: A high-service pump delivers 1,188 gpm against 75 ft of head. What is the water horsepower?
A pump delivers 600 gpm against 150 ft of head at 75% efficiency. What brake horsepower must the motor supply?
questions.explanation: Water hp = (600 x 150) / 3,960 = 22.7 hp. Brake hp = water hp / efficiency = 22.7 / 0.75 = 30.3 hp. The 22.7 hp choice forgets the efficiency loss.

questions.question: A SCADA chlorine reading has not changed at all for hours while plant flow and dose have varied. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: The sensor or signal has likely failed and shows a frozen value
The process is perfectly stable, so no field check is needed
The chlorine dose should be doubled until the reading moves again
The contact basin has suddenly gained extra baffling efficiency

questions.explanation: A value that never moves while conditions change indicates a failed sensor or signal, not a stable process. The instrument is corrected and the fault documented, not the process.

questions.question: A long dry forecast shows demand staying high while reservoir inflow stays near zero. The best release plan is to:

answers.text: Release at the normal rate until storage is nearly empty
Hold all water and supply the system from wells only
Pace releases against forecasted demand and remaining storage so the supply lasts through the dry period
Release extra water now to lower the pool before drought

questions.explanation: Stored-water release is managed against forecasted demand. In a drought, pacing releases to the forecast and the storage remaining stretches the supply instead of exhausting it early.

questions.question: How do wellhead protection areas restrict activities around a well?

answers.text: They ban all pumping within a fixed distance of every well in the area
They restrict activities by groundwater travel-time zones
They apply only to surface reservoirs, never to groundwater well fields
They restrict activities based on the age of the pump motor in the well

questions.explanation: Wellhead protection areas are drawn around travel time — how long groundwater takes to reach the well — with tighter restrictions closer in.

questions.question: A contractor crew arrives to work near chemical storage. What is the supervisor's best action before work starts?

answers.text: Assume the contractor's own company has covered all plant hazards fully
Brief the crew on plant hazards, safety rules, and emergency actions
Let the crew start and correct any unsafe practice if it is noticed later
Limit the briefing to parking and break areas to keep the crew on schedule

questions.explanation: Class II duties include training staff and contractors on site hazards and safe work practices before work begins. Waiting for an unsafe act leaves people exposed to plant-specific risks.

water-treatment-class-1.quiz_title: Water Treatment Class I Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: In a conventional surface-water plant, which step immediately follows flocculation in the normal treatment train?

answers.text: Filtration through a rapid sand bed
Sedimentation in a clarification basin
Disinfection in a chlorine contact tank
Storage in a finished-water clearwell

questions.explanation: After gentle mixing builds floc, the water moves to sedimentation or clarification, where the floc settles out before filtration and disinfection.

questions.question: Water flows through a channel with a cross-sectional area of 3 square feet at a velocity of 2 feet per second. What is the flow in gallons per minute?

answers.text: 6.00 gpm

questions.explanation: Flow Q = A x V = 3 sq ft x 2 ft/s = 6 cfs. Convert to gpm: 6 x 448.8 = 2,692.80 gpm.

questions.question: What distinguishes a solids-contact clarifier from a conventional clarifier?

answers.text: It removes the need for any coagulant chemical because solids alone destabilize colloids
It settles solids only by spinning the water at high speed in a cylindrical steel tank
It combines mixing, flocculation, and clarification together inside a single unit
It filters water through a sand bed before any flocculation or settling can take place

questions.explanation: Solids-contact units carry out rapid mixing, flocculation, and clarification in one basin, using contact with previously formed solids to help build floc.

questions.question: Which features protect a finished-water storage tank or clearwell from contamination?

answers.text: Screened vents and a screened, flap-covered overflow pipe
Open vents and an overflow pipe left unprotected at the top
Unlocked hatches and lighting left off around the tank site
Cracked coatings and standing water pooled on the tank roof
