questions.explanation: Storage tanks are protected by screened vents and a screened overflow with a flap, which keep insects, birds, and debris out while still letting the tank breathe and drain.

questions.question: A presence/absence test comes back positive, and a supervisor asks how many coliform organisms the sample contained. What is the correct response?

answers.text: The count can be estimated reasonably well from how quickly the test changed color after incubation
A positive result always means the count exceeded one thousand
The test cannot say; it only shows presence, so a quantitative method would be needed
The number can be read from the turbidity of the incubated sample

questions.explanation: Presence/absence methods give a yes-or-no answer; a number requires a quantitative method such as membrane filter counts or an MPN determination.

questions.question: Hardness in water is caused mainly by which dissolved minerals?

answers.text: Sodium thiosulfate and DPD
Iron and aluminum sulfate
Calcium and magnesium
Natural organic matter and algae

questions.explanation: Hardness is caused mainly by calcium and magnesium and is reported as mg/L CaCO3.

questions.question: Inline turbidimeters, chlorine analyzers, and pH meters require which routine attention?

answers.text: Calibration only when a reading looks unusual
No calibration after installation
Calibration with finished water only, never standards
Routine calibration against standards

questions.explanation: Inline instruments need routine calibration against standards to keep their readings trustworthy.

questions.question: Calculate the water horsepower for a pump delivering 500 gpm against 100 ft of head.
After cleaning battery terminals on a backup system, what step protects against repeat corrosion and poor contact?

answers.text: Leave the connections finger-tight so they can be removed quickly by hand
Paint the cable ends the same color so either cable fits either terminal
Wrap the terminals in dry rags to keep dust from settling on the bare metal
Tighten connections securely and apply a protective coating to the terminals

questions.explanation: Clean, tight, protected terminals keep resistance low and corrosion down, so the battery delivers full current when the backup system is called on.

questions.question: A raw-water sample is cloudy and measures high in turbidity. Turbidity is classified as which type of characteristic?

answers.text: A physical characteristic
A biological characteristic
A chemical characteristic
A radiological characteristic

questions.explanation: Turbidity reflects suspended material clouding the water, a physical property rather than a dissolved chemical or a living organism.

questions.question: Raw water turbidity entering a presedimentation step is 48 NTU and the settled water leaving it is 6 NTU. What is the percent removal?
A tanker arrives with a chemical delivery the plant was expecting. What should happen first?

answers.text: The driver checks in, the delivery is verified, and staff direct the unloading process
The driver unloads wherever the hose reaches while staff finish their other rounds
The driver is given a plant key so future deliveries can be made without checking in
The driver drains the remaining heel of the last product into the new storage tank

questions.explanation: Deliveries are controlled events: the driver checks in, staff verify the product and paperwork, and plant personnel direct unloading so the right chemical goes into the right tank.

texas-mpje.quiz_title: Texas MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Pharmacist-in-charge Robert Hale gives notice that his last day is Friday. The regional manager plans to leave the position vacant for about a month while interviewing candidates, with staff pharmacists simply covering shifts in the meantime. What must the pharmacy do instead?

answers.text: Continue operating indefinitely with rotating staff pharmacists, since each shift has a licensed pharmacist
Ask the DEA to appoint an interim pharmacist-in-charge from its registrant list
Close the pharmacy permanently, because a departing pharmacist-in-charge can never be replaced
Designate a successor pharmacist-in-charge so that accountability for the pharmacy's compliance, security, records, and supervision continues without a gap

questions.explanation: When a pharmacist-in-charge leaves, the pharmacy must designate a successor so the accountability attached to that role continues without interruption. A licensed pharmacist covering individual shifts does not fill the designated in-charge role, the DEA does not appoint pharmacy managers, and replacing a departing pharmacist-in-charge is routine rather than a reason the pharmacy must close for good.

questions.question: A patient advocate in Houston asks how many members of the Texas State Board of Pharmacy represent the general public rather than the profession. What is the correct number?

answers.text: One public member
Two public members
Four public members
Three public members

questions.explanation: Three board members are public members, providing a non-professional perspective. One and two understate public representation, and four overstates it and would displace a pharmacist or technician seat.

questions.question: A pharmacist in El Paso argues that because his violation involved diverting a controlled substance for personal use, the board can fine him up to $10,000 per violation, and he asks the board to treat that higher figure as the governing cap. How should the board respond?

answers.text: Accept the figure, because diversion doubles the usual cap
Reject it, because diversion cases carry no administrative penalty at all
Reject it, because the cap remains $5,000 per violation and expressly covers violations involving diversion
Accept it only if the drug was a Schedule II substance

questions.explanation: The administrative penalty cap is $5,000 per violation, and the cap expressly includes violations involving diversion of a controlled substance, so diversion neither raises the ceiling nor removes penalty authority. The schedule of the drug involved does not change the cap.

questions.question: Last week in Corpus Christi, an adult patient agreed to have refills of a non-psychotropic dangerous drug consolidated. Before the consolidated fill is dispensed, the patient phones pharmacist Irene and clearly withdraws that agreement, saying she wants her refills kept separate. All other consolidation conditions could be met. What should Irene do?

answers.text: Not consolidate the refills, because the patient's consent is required and has been withdrawn
Consolidate anyway, because consent given once cannot be taken back
Consolidate half the supply as a compromise between the two instructions
Consolidate if the prescriber, rather than the patient, gives a fresh approval

questions.explanation: Refill consolidation requires the patient's consent, and this patient withdrew consent before the consolidated fill was dispensed, so a required condition is no longer met. Consent to consolidation is not irrevocable once given. Consolidating even part of the supply would still be consolidation against the patient's current instruction, and a prescriber's approval or notification cannot replace the patient's own consent.

questions.question: A patient in Weatherford takes one tablet of a non-Schedule II maintenance drug every 12 hours. Pharmacist June lawfully dispenses a 72-hour emergency supply at 6 p.m. on Friday. How much did June dispense, and when does the supply run out?

answers.text: 3 tablets, lasting until Sunday evening
12 tablets, lasting until the following Friday evening
72 tablets, lasting until the prescriber's office reopens the next month
6 tablets, lasting until Monday evening

questions.explanation: A 72-hour supply is measured by the drug's dosing interval: at one tablet every 12 hours, 72 hours requires six tablets. Counted from Friday at 6 p.m., six doses carry the patient through Monday at 6 p.m. Three tablets would cover only 36 hours, and twelve or seventy-two tablets would far exceed the 72-hour cap that limits an emergency refill.

questions.question: Patient Selma Ortiz shows pharmacist Kurt Weiss her printed profile, which lists a blood pressure medication she has never taken; the entry came from another patient's order entered in error. Selma asks that the record be corrected. What is the correct response?

answers.text: Tell her profile entries can never be changed once entered
Delete her entire prescription history so the error disappears with it
Treat her request as a request for amendment and handle it under the pharmacy's privacy procedures so the erroneous entry is addressed
Tell her only the prescriber who supposedly ordered the drug can raise the issue

questions.explanation: Patients have the right to request amendments to their records, and a demonstrably erroneous entry about a medication never taken is exactly the kind of request the pharmacy must handle under its privacy procedures. Refusing all changes leaves false information in a record used for screening and counseling. Deleting the entire history destroys accurate records along with the error, and the right to request an amendment belongs to the patient, not only to a prescriber.

questions.question: At 6 p.m. in Amarillo, pharmacist Noah is asked for a refill of a non-Schedule II maintenance drug that ran out today, and a treatment gap would harm the patient. He calls the prescriber's office once, hears a recorded message giving a pager number for the covering prescriber, and does not use it. Has Noah satisfied the contact condition for a Texas emergency refill?

answers.text: Yes, because a single unanswered call always counts as reasonable effort
No, because an available route to reach the covering prescriber remains untried, so reasonable effort has not been completed
Yes, if the patient signs a statement waiving any further contact attempts
No, because emergency refills are barred whenever a covering prescriber exists in the practice

questions.explanation: The contact condition requires that the prescriber cannot be contacted after reasonable effort. The recorded message supplied a working route to the covering prescriber, and Noah did not try it, so the prescriber cannot yet be treated as unreachable. One call is not automatically reasonable effort when the recording provides the next step, and a patient waiver cannot substitute for contacting the prescriber. The existence of a covering prescriber does not bar emergency refills in general; if reasonable efforts through that route also failed, the condition could be met.

questions.question: A man representing an unfamiliar company offers a pharmacy deeply discounted brand-name medication, but the pharmacy cannot confirm the seller is an authorized trading partner. A buyer argues the sealed packaging looks genuine. What is the status of product from this source?

answers.text: It is suspect product from an unverified source and may not be dispensed
It is acceptable stock because sealed packaging proves legitimacy
It may be dispensed to cash-paying patients only
It may be dispensed if the price savings are passed to patients

questions.explanation: Pharmacies must deal only with authorized trading partners, and product offered by a seller whose authorized status cannot be verified is suspect product that must not enter dispensing stock. Intact-looking packaging does not establish a legitimate source, and neither the patient's payment method nor a lower price cures a broken chain of custody.

questions.question: Before dispensing an opioid in Texas, pharmacist Lena performs the required prescription monitoring check. Which program does she check, and who administers it?

answers.text: PMP AWARE, administered by the Texas State Board of Pharmacy
PMP AWARE, administered by the federal Drug Enforcement Administration
A national insurer database, administered by the patient's health plan
The state immunization registry, administered by the state health department

questions.explanation: The Texas prescription monitoring program is PMP AWARE, and it is administered by the Texas State Board of Pharmacy. The Drug Enforcement Administration does not administer the Texas program. An insurer database and the immunization registry serve different purposes and are not the Texas prescription monitoring program.

questions.question: A prescription in Texarkana bears the prescriber's handwritten words 'Brand Medically Necessary' on its face. At pickup, the patient asks the pharmacist to dispense the cheaper generic instead and offers to sign a waiver accepting the switch. What must the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Dispense the generic once the patient signs the waiver
Dispense the generic because the patient's choice always controls
Dispense the brand, because the practitioner's handwritten certification blocks substitution and the patient cannot overrule it
Hold the prescription until the board approves the switch

questions.explanation: When the practitioner handwrites 'Brand Necessary' or 'Brand Medically Necessary' on the face of the prescription, the pharmacist shall dispense that brand. A patient's waiver or preference does not override the practitioner's certification, and board approval is not the route for resolving the request.

questions.question: To save data-entry time, a Class A pharmacy in Alvin keeps a single monthly tally stating how many refills were dispensed that month, with no entry identifying any individual refill, patient, or prescription. An inspector reviewing a complaint about one patient's refill finds nothing to review. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The tally is sufficient, because refill records may be kept in aggregate form
The tally is sufficient, because a monthly total proves the pharmacy's overall refill volume
The tally is sufficient as long as the original prescription files are complete
The tally is not sufficient, because refill records must capture each refill event, and an aggregate monthly count leaves no record of the individual refill the inspector needs to examine

questions.explanation: Refill records serve as the record of each refill dispensed, so they must capture individual refill events rather than a monthly aggregate. A total count may describe overall volume, but it creates no audit trail for a particular patient's refill. Complete original prescription files do not fill that gap, because they do not record the later refill events themselves.

questions.question: A Texas community pharmacy is purging old files. How long must prescription records be retained under board rule?

answers.text: Six months from the date of dispensing
One year from the date of dispensing
Until the end of the calendar year in which they were dispensed
At least two years

questions.explanation: Texas prescription records must be retained for at least two years, which is the board-rule floor for prescription records. Six months, one year, and the end of the dispensing calendar year all fall short of that minimum and would destroy records that must still be available.

nbrc-rte.quiz_title: NBRC RTE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A patient with advanced lung disease reports now needing to sit down to dress, stopping twice while showering because of breathlessness, and no longer being able to carry groceries into the house. How should these reports be interpreted in the assessment?

answers.text: They show the disease has minimal functional impact because the patient still completes these tasks
They document a substantial decline in functional capacity, with dyspnea now limiting basic self-care activities
They indicate the patient is exaggerating, because dressing should not cause breathlessness
They are irrelevant to a respiratory assessment and should not be recorded

questions.explanation: The key is right: when breathlessness forces rest breaks during dressing and showering and prevents carrying groceries, basic activities of daily living are compromised — a substantial functional decline that belongs in the assessment and care plan. The minimal-impact distractor is wrong because completing tasks only with repeated stops is itself evidence of major limitation. The exaggeration distractor is wrong because the energy cost of dressing and showering is genuinely significant for patients with severe ventilatory limitation. The irrelevant distractor is wrong because functional status is a core element of respiratory assessment and of decisions about rehabilitation and support.

questions.question: A patient with COPD and chronic CO2 retention is receiving oxygen at 3 L/min by nasal cannula with an SpO2 of 97%, and the care plan specifies a target saturation range of 88–92%. Which titration action is correct?

answers.text: Increase the flow to keep the saturation above 98% at all times
Remove the oxygen completely and recheck in one hour
Reduce the oxygen flow stepwise, rechecking saturation, to bring SpO2 down into the 88–92% target range
Leave the flow unchanged because a higher saturation is always safer

questions.explanation: The key is right: oxygen titration means adjusting flow to the prescribed target range; at 97% on 3 L/min this patient is above the 88–92% target set for chronic CO2 retainers, so flow is reduced in steps with saturation rechecked after each change. The increase distractor drives saturation further above target and increases the risk of worsening hypercapnia in this population. The remove-completely distractor overshoots in the other direction and risks rebound hypoxemia; titration is stepwise, not on-off. The leave-it distractor ignores that the target range exists precisely because more oxygen is not always safer for these patients.

questions.question: An arterial blood gas shows pH 7.28, PaCO2 58 mm Hg, PaO2 62 mm Hg, and HCO3- 27 mEq/L in a patient with an acute COPD exacerbation. How should this gas be interpreted?

answers.text: Fully compensated respiratory acidosis
Acute metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation
Acute respiratory alkalosis with hypoxemia
Acute (largely uncompensated) respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia

questions.explanation: Key D is correct: pH is acidemic, PaCO2 is elevated as the primary disorder, and HCO3- is only slightly above normal, consistent with acute respiratory acidosis without full renal compensation, plus a low PaO2. A is wrong because full compensation would return pH to the normal range. B is wrong because HCO3- is not low and PaCO2 is high, not compensatorily low. C is wrong because both pH direction and PaCO2 direction are opposite to alkalosis.

questions.question: A wall suction setup has its regulator set and the gauge near the wall holding at the set vacuum, but vacuum at the catheter is feeble and secretions barely move. The collection canister lid is missing its gasket and sits slightly askew. Trace the discrepancy.

answers.text: A missing gasket raises the vacuum at the catheter, so weak suction must come from the regulator
The gauge reading proves full vacuum is present at the catheter, so the catheter itself must be oversized
Air leaks in at the unsealed lid, so vacuum is lost at the canister and little of the regulator's vacuum reaches the catheter, even though the gauge at the source reads normally
Lid leaks affect only the measurement of collected fluid volume and never the transmitted vacuum

questions.explanation: The key is right: the system is a series path — regulator, canister, tubing, catheter — and a leak at the canister admits room air that collapses the vacuum downstream of the leak while the upstream gauge still shows its set point. The raised-vacuum distractor inverts leak physics; an inward leak always reduces transmitted vacuum. The gauge-proves distractor is wrong because the gauge samples the source side of the leak, not the catheter tip. The volume-only distractor is wrong because the lid seal is part of the vacuum path, not just a fluid container closure.

questions.question: A galvanic fuel-cell oxygen analyzer still calibrates correctly in room air, but in 100% oxygen it now reads only in the low 80s and takes far longer than usual to stabilize after any change in concentration. The sensor is near the end of its rated service life. What does this pattern indicate?

answers.text: The analyzer needs a fresh two-point calibration with a higher span gas
Water vapor in the span gas is diluting the reading, and drying the gas will restore it
The fuel cell is exhausted - its chemical output can no longer track high oxygen levels - and the cell must be replaced
The display electronics are failing, and the analyzer should be returned for board repair

questions.explanation: The key is right: a galvanic cell generates current proportional to oxygen partial pressure only while its anode and electrolyte last; an aging cell keeps a plausible room-air point but its output saturates and slows at high oxygen, which is the classic end-of-life signature calling for cell replacement. The recalibration distractor is wrong because calibration cannot restore chemical capacity the cell no longer has - the room-air point already passes. The water-vapor distractor is wrong because humidification would lower readings proportionally at all concentrations and would not slow the response this way. The electronics distractor is wrong because a board failure would not produce this concentration-dependent, slow-response pattern with a normal air reading.

questions.question: A unit's practice has been to change every ventilator circuit on a fixed every-few-days schedule 'to prevent infection.' A therapist reviewing the ventilator-associated event prevention protocol notes the circuits are clean and functioning. What does current prevention practice direct?

answers.text: Continue fixed-schedule changes, but change the circuits at night so patients sleep through them
Change circuits twice as often, since each new circuit is sterile
Add a second circuit in parallel so one can rest while the other is used

Do not change circuits on a routine fixed schedule; change a circuit when it is visibly soiled or malfunctioning, because unnecessary circuit breaks increase contamination risk without reducing events

questions.explanation: The key is right: ventilator circuits are not changed on a routine schedule — they are changed for visible soiling or malfunction, because opening the circuit repeatedly introduces contamination and evidence shows scheduled changes do not lower ventilator-associated events. Changing at night is wrong because timing does not fix a practice whose frequency itself is the problem. Doubling the frequency is wrong because it doubles circuit breaks and cost with no preventive benefit. A parallel resting circuit is wrong because ventilator circuits are single-patient systems and no such rotation practice exists.

questions.question: A patient with a known difficult intubation still requires ventilation, but the endotracheal tube must be changed because of a damaged cuff causing a large leak that cannot be corrected. Which approach best preserves airway access during the exchange?

answers.text: Remove the tube first and attempt a fresh intubation without any guide
Deflate the cuff further and ignore the leak because exchange is always riskier than a leak
Use an airway exchange catheter (with visualization/experienced help as available) so the new tube can be railroaded and reintubation access is maintained
Replace the endotracheal tube with an oropharyngeal airway for long-term ventilation

questions.explanation: In a difficult airway, an airway exchange catheter maintains a conduit through the glottis, allowing the new tube to be railroaded and oxygenation/reintubation access to be preserved if the first pass fails. A discards the only secured access. B leaves an uncorrectable leak that compromises ventilation. D is not a ventilation airway for ongoing support.

questions.question: A patient with a COPD exacerbation on heated high-flow nasal therapy for one hour has worsening hypercapnia with pH 7.26, increasing drowsiness, and rising work of breathing, although SpO2 is 93%. What is the most appropriate escalation?

answers.text: Escalate to bilevel noninvasive ventilation, which provides ventilatory assistance for hypercapnic failure, with close monitoring for intubation need
Continue high-flow therapy unchanged because oxygen saturation is acceptable
Increase FiO2 on high-flow therapy to raise SpO2 to 100%
Switch to a partial rebreather mask to rest the patient

questions.explanation: The key is right: this is ventilatory (hypercapnic, acidemic) failure, not primarily an oxygenation problem; bilevel noninvasive ventilation unloads the respiratory muscles and augments alveolar ventilation, which high-flow therapy cannot do to the same degree. Continuing unchanged is wrong because acidemia and mental status are worsening. Raising FiO2 to 100% is wrong because saturation is already adequate and over-oxygenation can worsen CO2 retention. A partial rebreather is wrong because it provides oxygen only and no ventilatory support.

questions.question: A patient with a chest tube for pneumothorax has a large continuous air leak on day 6, incomplete lung expansion, and increasing subcutaneous emphysema despite a patent, correctly positioned drain on appropriate suction. Which recommendation is most appropriate?

answers.text: Recommend removing the chest tube because 6 days is the maximum allowed
Recommend clamping the tube permanently to stop the leak
Recommend thoracic surgery consultation for the persistent air leak and incomplete expansion, since prolonged leaks often need procedural or operative solutions
Recommend doubling ventilator tidal volumes to force the lung fully open

questions.explanation: The key is right: a large air leak persisting near a week with incomplete expansion despite a functioning drain defines a prolonged air leak/bronchopleural problem that warrants thoracic surgery evaluation for options beyond drainage. Removing the tube is wrong because the leak and unexpanded lung would leave an untreated pneumothorax. Permanent clamping is wrong because it traps escaping air and risks tension pneumothorax. Doubling tidal volume is wrong because higher volumes drive more air through the fistula and injure the lung without sealing the leak.

questions.question: A newborn at 30 weeks' gestation requires positive-pressure ventilation at delivery. What initial oxygen concentration should be used, with titration by preductal oximetry?

answers.text: 100% oxygen from the outset
A fixed 65% concentration throughout the resuscitation
21-30% (room air to low-concentration oxygen)
No oxygen may be used at any point in a preterm resuscitation

questions.explanation: The key is right: infants born before 35 weeks start resuscitation at 21-30% oxygen and are titrated to the minute-specific preductal targets, because preterm infants are especially vulnerable to oxygen toxicity. The 100% distractor is wrong because high initial oxygen in a preterm newborn increases oxidative injury without improving resuscitation success. The fixed-65% distractor is wrong because no fixed mid-range concentration is the starting standard and it removes titration. The no-oxygen distractor is wrong because oxygen remains available and is increased as needed if saturations or heart rate do not respond.

questions.question: After being turned for a procedure, a ventilated 60-year-old man with COPD becomes hypoxemic with SpO2 88%. Breath sounds are loud over the right chest and nearly absent over the left, and chest rise is asymmetric. The endotracheal tube depth marking at the lips reads 4 cm deeper than the value documented after intubation, and the capnogram is present. What is the most appropriate action?

answers.text: Suction the tube for a presumed left-sided mucus plug
Withdraw the tube to the previously documented depth, then re-auscultate and confirm position
Increase PEEP to recruit the left lung
Order a bronchoscopy to evaluate the left main bronchus

questions.explanation: Key B is correct: the deeper depth marking plus unilateral (right-sided) ventilation and a present capnogram indicate the tube has advanced into the right mainstem bronchus; withdrawing it to the documented depth and reconfirming position is the immediate corrective action. A is wrong because suctioning does not correct tube malposition and the depth change is the diagnostic clue. C is wrong because adding PEEP to a one-lung-ventilated patient overdistends the ventilated lung without fixing the cause. D is wrong because bronchoscopy is unnecessarily slow and invasive when the bedside findings and depth marking already identify the problem.

questions.question: During compressions for a newborn, the ECG monitor displays a heart rate of 140/min, but the pulse oximeter reads 68/min, the infant's perfusion is poor, and a team member cannot feel a brachial pulse. How should this discrepancy be interpreted?

answers.text: The ECG rate proves the heart is perfusing well, so compressions should stop immediately
The pulse oximeter rate is always the most accurate during resuscitation, so the ECG leads should be removed
Both devices must be replaced before any clinical decision can be made

Electrical activity on ECG does not guarantee effective perfusion, and pulse oximetry under-reads with poor perfusion and motion, so the team should judge the response by the ECG rate together with auscultation and clinical signs rather than stopping compressions on the oximeter number alone

questions.explanation: D is correct: during resuscitation the ECG gives the most reliable continuous heart-rate display, pulse oximetry is prone to under-reading when perfusion is poor, and neither number alone proves effective circulation, so assessment combines the ECG, auscultation, pulses, and response. A is wrong because an ECG rate can exist without adequate mechanical output. B is wrong because the oximeter is the least reliable signal in a poorly perfused, moving infant. C is wrong because the discrepancy is physiologic and technical, not a reason to halt assessment and replace both monitors mid-resuscitation.

umpje.quiz_title: UMPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A pharmacist sends a patient's prescription history to the patient's other treating clinician so that clinician can adjust therapy, and a staff member worries that a signed patient authorization and a minimum-necessary review are both legally required first. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Both a signed authorization and a minimum-necessary limit always apply to every disclosure
Treatment disclosures need a signed authorization, but payment disclosures do not
Disclosures for treatment may be made without patient authorization, and the minimum necessary standard does not apply to treatment uses and disclosures
No information may ever be shared with another clinician without a court order

questions.explanation: Health information may be used and disclosed for treatment, payment, and health care operations without patient authorization, and the minimum necessary standard applies to payment and operations but not to treatment, so C is correct. A wrongly imposes authorization and minimum-necessary limits on treatment. B reverses the rule by requiring authorization for treatment. D invents a court-order requirement that does not govern ordinary treatment sharing.

questions.question: During a genuine emergency, a prescriber gives a pharmacist oral authorization for a Schedule II medicine but asks the pharmacist to dispense a full month's supply so the patient will not need to return. The emergency itself is expected to last only a few days, and no alternative treatment will work. How much may the pharmacist dispense on the oral authorization?

answers.text: The full month's supply, because the prescriber authorized that amount by phone
The full month's supply, if the patient signs a statement accepting the emergency dispensing
Only the amount needed for the emergency period, with the prescriber required to deliver the covering written or electronic prescription within 7 days
Nothing, because a Schedule II medicine can never be dispensed on an oral authorization even in an emergency

questions.explanation: C is correct because in a true emergency a pharmacist may dispense a Schedule II medicine on a prescriber's oral authorization, but the quantity is limited to the emergency period, and the prescriber must deliver the covering written or electronic prescription within 7 days. A is wrong because the prescriber's request for a larger amount does not expand the emergency oral authority beyond the emergency period. B is wrong because a patient's signed statement cannot expand that authority either. D is wrong because emergency oral dispensing is permitted within those limits; it is not barred outright.

questions.question: A pharmacist compounds a preparation for a named patient with a valid prescription. At pickup, that patient's spouse asks for a supply of the same preparation for himself, saying he has the same condition, but the pharmacy has no prescription for the spouse. What should the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Give him part of the batch, because the formulation has already been made for the household
Relabel a container with the spouse's name written over the first patient's name
Sell it to him without a prescription, since a compounded preparation for one spouse may be shared with the other
Decline to dispense it to the spouse until a patient-specific prescription for the spouse is received

questions.explanation: D is correct because traditional compounding is patient-specific: each dispensing must be supported by a prescription for that identified patient, and the spouse has none. A is wrong because shared household or condition does not transfer one patient's prescription to another person. B is wrong because relabeling does not create a valid prescription, and C is wrong because a compounded prescription preparation does not become an over-the-counter product by being shared within a family.

questions.question: On a holiday weekend, an established patient runs out of a daily non-controlled maintenance medicine, has no refills left, and will miss doses because the prescriber cannot be reached. Under the prevailing emergency-refill principle, the pharmacist dispenses a limited 72-hour emergency supply. Which steps complete the pharmacist's obligations for that dispensing?

answers.text: Document the circumstances of the emergency dispensing in the patient's record and notify the prescriber of the emergency supply
Record the supply as an ordinary authorized refill so the patient's refill count stays accurate
Add a new refill authorization to the prescription so the patient is covered next month as well
No documentation or prescriber notice is needed when the supply is this small

questions.explanation: A is correct: the prevailing emergency-refill principle permits a limited supply to prevent interruption of maintenance therapy only with the circumstances documented and the prescriber notified. B is wrong because an emergency supply is not an authorized refill and recording it as one falsifies the prescription record. C is wrong because the pharmacist's emergency authority covers the immediate limited supply only; it does not create ongoing refill authorization. D is wrong because the small quantity does not waive the documentation and notification conditions that make the dispensing permissible.

questions.question: A prescriber writes a Schedule III prescription with the words 'refills for one year.' Four months later the patient has used two refills and asks how much refill authority actually remains under federal limits. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Up to three more refills remain, and only until six months from the original prescription date, because the prescriber's wording cannot extend the five-refills-in-six-months limits
Refills are unlimited for the full year, exactly as the prescriber wrote
Ten more refills remain, because a one-year period allows two successive six-month refill cycles on the same prescription
No refills remain, because writing 'for one year' voided the refill authorization entirely

questions.explanation: A is correct because Schedule III refills are limited to five refills within six months regardless of broader wording on the prescription; with two used at four months, at most three remain and they lapse at six months. B is wrong because a prescriber's wording cannot override the federal refill ceiling. C is wrong because the limits do not renew on the same prescription for a second cycle; continued therapy after the limits requires a new prescription. D is wrong because the overbroad wording does not void the authorization; the refills are simply effective only within the federal limits.

questions.question: A pharmacy relocated to a new street address last month. A technician filling a prescription reaches for the remaining stock of pre-printed container labels bearing the pharmacy's former address. At final verification, the pharmacist should:

answers.text: Hold the fill and relabel it with the pharmacy's current name and address before dispensing.
Dispense it, because the pharmacy's address on a label matters only for insurance billing.
Dispense the old label stock until it runs out, because the labels were accurate when they were printed.
Dispense it, because a dispensed container label is required to show only the prescription number and the patient's name.

questions.explanation: A is correct: prevailing dispensed-container labeling requirements include the pharmacy's name and address, and the label must be accurate for the pharmacy dispensing the medication. B is wrong because the pharmacy name and address are required label elements, not billing details. C is wrong because accuracy is judged at the time of dispensing, not when the label stock was printed. D is wrong because the label must also carry elements such as the date of fill, directions, and the drug name and strength.

questions.question: A discount supplier offers the pharmacy a case of an over-the-counter cough product whose cartons are printed only in a foreign language and omit required label information for buyers in this country, including adequate directions in a form buyers can use. The supplier suggests the pharmacist can explain everything verbally at the counter. How should the pharmacy treat the product?

answers.text: Stock it, because a pharmacist's verbal explanation cures any gap in over-the-counter labeling
Stock it if a technician adds a handwritten English directions sticker to each carton
Treat it as misbranded and do not sell it in that condition, because its labeling is missing required information and lacks adequate directions for use
Treat it as adulterated, because missing label information changes the product's strength and quality

questions.explanation: C is correct because false or misleading labeling, missing required label information, and inadequate directions for use for an over-the-counter product make it misbranded, and it should not be sold in that condition. A is wrong because counter counseling does not cure a labeling defect in a self-service over-the-counter product. B is wrong because a technician's handwritten sticker does not supply the manufacturer's required labeling. D is wrong because adulteration concerns contamination, decomposition, insanitary preparation, or strength and quality differing from standards, not missing label information.

questions.question: A Schedule IV prescription authorized five refills. The patient took two refills at her current pharmacy and now transfers the prescription to your pharmacy. How many refills may your pharmacy dispense under the transferred prescription?

answers.text: The three refills that remain from the prescriber's original authorization
Five fresh refills, because the transfer restarts the authorization
Six refills, counting the transfer itself as one authorization
Two refills, matching the number already taken at the other pharmacy

questions.explanation: A is correct: a transfer moves the refill authority that remains; two of five authorized refills are used, so three remain, still subject to the prescription's original limits. B is wrong because a transfer does not restart or expand the prescriber's authorization. C is wrong because a transfer is a movement of records, not an additional refill authorization. D is wrong because the number already dispensed reduces the balance rather than setting it.

questions.question: A board receives a complaint that a pharmacist filed several required records late over one quarter. The pharmacist is cooperating, there is no allegation of impairment, diversion, or dispensing errors, and no evidence that patients face an immediate risk. Which board approach best fits these facts?

answers.text: Summarily suspend the license today, because summary suspension is the required first step for every board complaint
Take no action of any kind, because late records can never be a board concern
Ask the federal drug enforcement authority to impose the state discipline, because a board cannot investigate its own licensees
Investigate the complaint and pursue any discipline through the board's ordinary process, reserving summary suspension for situations involving imminent danger

questions.explanation: D is correct because boards investigate complaints and may discipline for violating board rules, while summary suspension is the tool reserved for imminent danger, which these facts do not show. A is wrong because not every complaint presents the immediate risk that justifies summary action. B is wrong because record violations are within the board's disciplinary grounds, and C is wrong because the board investigates and disciplines its own licensees rather than delegating that role.

questions.question: A pharmacist dispenses the correct drug at the correct strength after a screening that shows no problem, but provides no counseling at all. The patient misses a dose, does not know what to do about a missed dose, doubles the next dose to catch up, and is harmed. The pharmacist argues there can be no liability because the fill itself was perfect. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A counseling failure can support liability, because the pharmacist's duty extends beyond accurate filling to counseling, including what to do if a dose is missed
There can be no liability whenever the drug and strength dispensed were correct
Only the prescriber can be liable, because the prescriber chose the therapy and its schedule
Liability requires proof that the pharmacist intended the patient to be harmed

questions.explanation: A is correct: the duty extends beyond accurate filling, and counseling points include what to do if a dose is missed, so omitting counseling entirely can support negligence liability when the omission contributes to harm. B is wrong because an accurate fill does not exhaust the pharmacist's duties. C is wrong because the prescriber's choice of therapy does not erase the pharmacist's independent counseling duty. D is wrong because negligence is judged by the care used, not by intent to harm.

questions.question: A buyer signed electronic controlled-substance orders for a pharmacy during March. In April, managers prepare the power-of-attorney document authorizing those signatures and date it back to March 1 so the file matches the orders. What is the compliance problem?

answers.text: Power of attorney must be executed before it is relied on and retained as executed; backdating the document does not retroactively authorize the March signatures
There is no problem, because a power of attorney may be dated to match any earlier orders it is meant to cover
The only problem is that the document was prepared in April rather than on a business day
The problem is cured if the buyer also signs the April document a second time

questions.explanation: A is correct: a power of attorney for controlled-substance ordering must be executed and retained, and the authority it grants runs from its actual execution; backdating it does not retroactively authorize signatures made before it existed. B is wrong because matching the date to earlier orders is exactly the falsification that makes the document unreliable. C is wrong because the day of the week has nothing to do with the defect, which is the false effective date. D is wrong because an extra signature does not change when the authority was actually granted.

questions.question: A board-authorized remote dispensing site in a small town is staffed on site by a pharmacy technician, with a pharmacist at the main pharmacy reviewing and verifying each prescription through a secure electronic link before anything is handed out. One afternoon the link fails, and the site manager proposes that the technician hand out prescriptions that are already packaged and labeled while the link is down, since the labels 'look right.' What must happen?

answers.text: The technician may hand out the labeled prescriptions, because packaging and labeling are the only steps that matter
The technician may hand out noncontrolled prescriptions only, without any pharmacist verification
The site may keep dispensing as long as the pharmacist reviews everything the next morning
No prescription may be released until pharmacist verification through the authorized arrangement is restored; dispensing waits for the pharmacist's review

questions.explanation: D is correct because remote and telepharmacy arrangements operate under board authorization with pharmacist verification retained, so a link outage removes the verification the model depends on and releases must pause. A is wrong because accurate-looking labels do not replace pharmacist verification. B is wrong because the verification requirement is not limited to controlled substances in this arrangement. C is wrong because next-day review is not the prospective verification the arrangement requires before a patient receives a prescription.

us-history-survey.quiz_title: US History Survey Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Cacao beans circulated in Mesoamerica not only as the basis of a prized drink but also as small-denomination money used in market purchases, while lengths of cotton cloth served as larger units of value. This dual use most directly demonstrates that Mesoamerican economies included

answers.text: barter only, with no standardized media of exchange
commodity money that made everyday market transactions possible at varied price levels
coinage struck by imperial mints on the European model
a prohibition on markets outside the imperial capital

questions.explanation: Beans for small purchases and cloth for larger ones are commodity money: standardized, divisible value that greased market exchange well beyond simple barter. No European-style mint existed, and markets flourished in many towns, not only the capital.

questions.question: In several Eastern Woodlands societies, dreams were treated as communications carrying obligations: a dream of receiving a gift or of a feast could require the dreamer to hold that feast or give that gift publicly. This practice indicates that in these societies dreams functioned as

answers.text: private entertainment with no social consequences
a socially binding source of guidance that could obligate public generosity and ritual action
evidence used in courts to convict people of witchcraft
a skill restricted to a hereditary priestly caste

questions.explanation: Dreams carried duties enforceable by community expectation, channeling generosity and ceremony rather than remaining private experience. They were not courtroom evidence in this setting, and dreaming and interpretation were broadly shared, not caste monopolies.

questions.question: After the Stuart restoration, Charles II rewarded a group of courtiers with a vast proprietary grant for Carolina, whose Fundamental Constitutions envisioned hereditary nobility with titled ranks and large seigniories. In practice the colony developed instead around

answers.text: exact implementation of the titled-nobility plan for two centuries
a single royal governor ruling without any assembly
small farms in the north and Barbadian-style plantations in the south, while the elaborate constitution failed to take root
the immediate abolition of proprietary government in 1670

questions.explanation: The paper constitution's hereditary lords and leet-men never materialized; actual settlement followed the Albemarle small-farm pattern and the lowcountry plantation pattern. An assembly existed from early on, and proprietary rule lasted until 1719-1729.

questions.question: In 1692-1693, courts in and around Salem, Massachusetts, admitted testimony about spectral appearances — harm allegedly done by an accused person's spirit, visible only to the afflicted — and hanged nineteen people before the governor halted the proceedings. The episode's collapse came largely when

answers.text: spectral testimony was discredited after accusations reached prominent families and ministers pressed evidentiary objections
all accused persons confessed and were pardoned
Parliament passed a law abolishing all colonial courts
the accused were rescued by an armed uprising of their neighbors

questions.explanation: Once accusations touched the governor's own household and leading clergy questioned evidence no bystander could verify, the proceedings lost legitimacy and were shut down. Most of the condemned had maintained innocence, and neither Parliament nor an uprising ended the trials.

questions.question: Under the task system used on many lowcountry rice estates, an enslaved worker who completed an assigned daily task — a measured portion of field or dike work — could use remaining daylight for provision grounds and family plots, whereas Chesapeake field hands typically worked gang labor from sunup to sundown under direct supervision. The contrast shows that

answers.text: labor organization within slavery varied by crop and ecology, with consequences for enslaved families' time and informal economies
all enslaved work regimes in British America were identical
task workers were legally free once their task was done
gang labor was used only on small farms with few workers

questions.explanation: Crop requirements shaped supervision: measurable rice tasks could be assigned individually, while tobacco's continuous care favored gangs — and the difference governed enslaved people's discretionary time and garden production. Task completion conferred no legal freedom, and gangs were the large plantations' norm.

questions.question: Bills of exchange drawn on London or Glasgow merchants circulated among colonial merchants as a means of paying debts across the Atlantic, while colonial assemblies issued paper currency for local use of widely varying reliability. The two instruments coexisted because colonies chronically lacked

answers.text: any form of money whatsoever before 1750
specie — gold and silver coin — which drained away to pay for imports in a persistently unfavorable balance of trade
laws permitting contracts between private parties
merchants willing to trade beyond their own colony

questions.explanation: Coin left as fast as it arrived because imports exceeded staple earnings in coin terms, so credit paper filled the gap: sterling bills for Atlantic settlement, local paper for internal trade. Contracts and intercolonial merchants were abundant; it was hard money that was scarce.

questions.question: In the war that opened in the Ohio Country in 1754, the French position in the interior rested on a chain of forts and trading posts staffed by small garrisons and sustained by alliances with Native nations who valued French trade goods and the French presence as a counterweight to British settler expansion. France's structural weakness in that contest was that

answers.text: it possessed no navy capable of reaching North America
Native nations uniformly refused to trade with the French
its forts were all located on the Atlantic coast
its Canadian settler population was a small fraction of British America's, so it could not match British colonial manpower and had to depend on Native allies and regulars shipped across the Atlantic

questions.explanation: Roughly seventy thousand French colonists faced well over a million British Americans, so French strategy hinged on alliance diplomacy and metropolitan troops vulnerable to naval interdiction. France did field a navy, Native trade with France was extensive, and the fort chain ran through the interior, not the coast.

questions.question: The Pennsylvania constitution of 1776 created a single-house legislature elected annually, a plural executive council instead of a governor, no property qualification for voting by taxpayers, and required that bills wait for public consideration before final passage. Contemporaries and historians treat it as the era's most democratic frame chiefly because it

answers.text: dispersed and slowed power through annual elections, a weak plural executive, and the broadest male suffrage of any state
concentrated power in a strong single executive
copied the British House of Lords into American government
gave the judiciary final authority over all legislation

questions.explanation: Unicameralism, annual terms, taxpayer suffrage, and the publication delay all move authority toward the voting public and away from a single magistrate. A strong executive and a lords-like chamber are precisely what the design rejected, and courts held no such veto.

questions.question: The excise on distilled spirits fell hardest on western farmers for a concrete economic reason: grain was bulky and expensive to haul over the mountains, while the same grain distilled into whiskey concentrated its value into a form pack animals could carry to market, and whiskey also served as a medium of exchange on the frontier. Taxing whiskey therefore amounted, in western eyes, to

answers.text: a tax on imported luxury goods consumed in eastern cities
a tax that western farmers could pass entirely to British buyers
a tax on the only practical way to get their staple crop to market and on their local currency itself
a tax identical in burden to the stamp taxes on paper

questions.explanation: Distilling was transport economics, not indulgence: it converted unsalable bulk into a portable, storable, spendable commodity, so the levy struck income and exchange medium together. The buyers were domestic, the burden could not be exported, and the grievance was livelihood rather than paperwork.

questions.question: When the federal government built a reservation dam and claimed a tribe's senior water allocation was limited to the small acreage it actually farmed, the Supreme Court's Winters v. United States (1908) protected tribal water through a distinctive interpretive move: it held that

answers.text: water rights in the West belong entirely to whoever files first with the state engineer
tribes hold no water rights unless a treaty names a specific river and quantity
the treaty reserving the land had impliedly reserved sufficient water to make the reservation livable, since a reservation of arid land without water would defeat the agreement's purpose
the federal government may extinguish reserved water rights at will without compensation

questions.explanation: Winters read silence purposefully: because the Fort Belknap agreement aimed at an agricultural homeland, water sufficient for that purpose was reserved by implication with a treaty-date priority, defeating later state-law appropriators. The doctrine rejects both pure prior-appropriation control over reservations and the demand for explicit textual mention — implication tied to the treaty's purpose is the mechanism.

questions.question: When a 1970s household faced prices rising about eight percent a year while its earner's pay rose five percent, the household's real purchasing power

answers.text: rose by three percent
stayed exactly level
could not be estimated from these figures
fell by roughly three percent a year, the gap between nominal pay growth and inflation

questions.explanation: Real change approximates nominal growth minus inflation: five minus eight is negative three percent, the lived squeeze of stagflation-era budgets. Purchasing power fell rather than rose or held level, and the figures are exactly what the calculation requires.

questions.question: During the mid-2000s housing boom, many borrowers took out interest-only adjustable-rate mortgages of the kind that later figured in the 2008 financial crisis. A borrower holds a 200,000 dollar interest-only adjustable-rate mortgage. At a six percent annual rate the monthly interest payment is 1,000 dollars. If the rate resets to nine percent, the new interest-only monthly payment would be

answers.text: 1,500 dollars
1,000 dollars
1,250 dollars
2,000 dollars

questions.explanation: Two hundred thousand times nine percent is 18,000 dollars a year, divided by twelve equals 1,500 dollars a month. The payment cannot stay at 1,000 when the rate rises, 1,250 would correspond to seven and a half percent, and 2,000 would require a twelve percent rate.

pennsylvania-insurance.quiz_title: Pennsylvania Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A hospital's negligent delay in treatment combines with a patient's pre-existing condition to produce an injury that neither would have produced as severely on its own. The delay can still be a cause in fact if it qualifies as what?

answers.text: The sole cause of every part of the injury
A superseding cause of the pre-existing condition
An intentional cause of the condition
A substantial factor in producing the injury

questions.explanation: When causes combine, conduct that is a substantial factor in producing the result can be a cause in fact without being the sole cause. The delay did not create the pre-existing condition, so it cannot be a superseding cause of it.

questions.question: An underlying aggregate is $2,000,000. Covered payments so far are $1,200,000 and $500,000, with defense payable outside the limits. How much aggregate remains before the umbrella attaches?
questions.explanation: Covered payments total $1,200,000 plus $500,000, which is $1,700,000, and $2,000,000 minus $1,700,000 leaves $300,000. The aggregate is not yet exhausted, so the umbrella has not attached on an aggregate basis.

questions.question: Early reports suggest an injury claim will settle well within underlying limits, but one claimant's condition worsens and surgery is now expected. Must the insured wait for certainty that underlying limits will be pierced before notifying the umbrella carrier?

answers.text: Yes, because umbrella notice is proper only after the amount is known to the dollar
No, because notice is required when it becomes reasonably possible the claim may involve the umbrella
Yes, because early notice forfeits the underlying insurer's duty to defend
No, but only if the claimant's attorney demands umbrella notice in writing

questions.explanation: The standard is possibility, not certainty, so a serious turn in a claimant's condition is the time to notify the umbrella carrier. Giving early notice does not disturb the underlying insurer's defense duty.

questions.question: A report is prepared after interviews with an applicant's neighbors and associates about the applicant's character and lifestyle. What kind of report is this?

answers.text: A standard billing report
An investigative consumer report
A motor vehicle abstract only
A plain consumer report with no interviews

questions.explanation: An investigative consumer report gathers information on character, general reputation, personal characteristics, or mode of living through personal interviews. A report built only from records and transactions is not investigative in this sense.

questions.question: An applicant asks an agent to write a property policy that falsely describes a building used for an unlawful operation as a vacant office so coverage can be obtained. Why would a contract formed on that basis fail an essential element?

answers.text: It lacks an offer because no application was completed
It lacks consideration because no premium was quoted yet
It lacks competent parties because the agent is licensed
It lacks a legal purpose because the object is unlawful

questions.explanation: A valid contract requires a legal purpose, and an agreement to insure or conceal an unlawful operation fails that element. Licensing of the agent concerns competence to act rather than curing an unlawful purpose.

questions.question: A hobby model aircraft that cannot carry people or cargo is damaged at the dwelling by a covered peril. The adjuster notes that aircraft are property not covered. What is the correct refinement?

answers.text: Model or hobby aircraft not used or designed to carry people or cargo are an exception and can be covered
The adjuster is right, and no aircraft of any kind can be covered
The model is covered only under Coverage A
The model is covered only while it is in flight

questions.explanation: The aircraft exclusion in Coverage C does not apply to model or hobby aircraft that are not used or designed to carry people or cargo. A full-size aircraft designed to carry people would remain property not covered.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is prohibited under Pennsylvania law on unfair discrimination in homeowners insurance?

answers.text: An insurer declines a new application that fails its filed underwriting standards
An insurer cancels during the first sixty days on a lawful ground with the required notice
An insurer nonrenews a policy at expiration for a statutory reason
An insurer cancels a homeowners policy during the first sixty days for a reason that amounts to unfair discrimination under the unfair practices law

questions.explanation: No; the regulation expressly conditions investigation-period cancellations on not violating the unfair discrimination provision.

questions.question: A producer pays the lapsed renewal fee instead of the resident renewal fee. How much more is the lapsed fee than the resident renewal fee?

answers.text: Fifty-five dollars more
One hundred ten dollars more
Two hundred dollars more
No difference

questions.explanation: Pennsylvania's resident producer renewal fee is $55 and the lapsed-license renewal fee is $165 (40 P.S. 310.8(f)), so the lapsed fee is $165 - $55 = $110 more than the resident renewal fee.

questions.question: Regarding advertising for unauthorized entity, what may happen to a producer who violates the Pennsylvania rule?

answers.text: Suspension of the license only, because revocation is not an available sanction
Revocation, suspension or refusal to renew the license
Denial of the license application
Refusal to renew only, because suspension and revocation are not available sanctions

questions.explanation: Under 40 P.S. 310.91, a Pennsylvania producer who violates the insurance laws, including advertising for an unauthorized entity, is subject to revocation, suspension, or refusal to renew the license - the full triad of sanctions is available, not any single one of them alone.

questions.question: A facility's safety officer logs a near-miss incident. Which outside body receives that report?

answers.text: Incidents are reported to the Department of Health only
Incidents are never reported outside the facility
Incidents are reported to the Patient Safety Authority only, without patient-identifying information
Incidents are reported to both agencies within twenty-four hours

questions.explanation: Incidents go to the Patient Safety Authority only, under the same ban on patient-identifying information.

questions.question: An insured loses $2,500 of gross income from a crash injury. Applying the income loss percentage, how much does the benefit address?

answers.text: $2,500, which is 100 percent of $2,500
$1,667, which is two-thirds of $2,500
$2,000, which is 80 percent of $2,500
$1,250, which is 50 percent of $2,500

questions.explanation: Pennsylvania first-party income loss benefits pay 80 percent of actual gross income loss: 80 percent of the $2,500 loss is $2,000. The benefit does not replace the full amount.

questions.question: A licensing candidate is studying notice of ability to return to work contents. Which statement should they learn as the correct Pennsylvania rule?

answers.text: A brief phone call telling the claimant benefits will probably stop
A prompt written notice on the prescribed form covering the medical change, the duty to seek work, the risk to benefits, and the right to consult an attorney
A notice sent only to the employer, never to the claimant
A notice that omits any mention of the right to consult an attorney

questions.explanation: The insurer must promptly give written notice on the department-prescribed form with the four required statements, including the right to consult an attorney.

new-york-insurance.quiz_title: New York Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: What is an anti-indemnity statute, at the concept level?

answers.text: A federal law requiring every contract to contain a broad form clause transferring all liability to the party with the least fault
A law that forbids parties from buying liability insurance
An insurance policy condition that excludes all contract claims
A state law that limits or voids certain indemnity promises, especially broad form promises in construction contracts

questions.explanation: Anti-indemnity statutes restrict how far a party can contractually shift liability, with broad form construction clauses a common target. They regulate contract promises; they do not ban insurance or require broad clauses.

questions.question: A buyer takes a car from a dealer after paying with a fraudulent check, and the car is never recovered. Why does dealers open lot coverage typically not pay this loss?

answers.text: Because theft is never covered under open lot coverage, as stated in the applicable policy form, and under the terms and conditions stated in the applicable policy form
Loss from false pretense, trick, or device, including voluntarily parting with an auto based on a bad payment, is excluded from dealer physical damage
Because the car was worth more than the lot limit
Because only collisions are covered on an open lot

questions.explanation: Explanation: Dealer physical damage excludes losses where the dealer is induced by false pretense to part with an auto, such as a bad-check purchase. Ordinary theft of a car from the lot, without the dealer's voluntary parting, is a different and covered kind of loss.

questions.question: Why are a spouse's consortium and services claims usually described as derivative?

answers.text: Because they can only be brought after retirement
Because they depend on the employee having a covered bodily injury from which the spouse's loss flows
Because they are paid from a separate property policy
Because the spouse must first be hired by the employer before the spouse can claim consortium or services losses of any kind

questions.explanation: Derivative claims stand or fall with the underlying injury to the employee; without that covered bodily injury there is no flowing family loss to claim. The spouse need not be an employee or retiree.

questions.question: Why do insurers steer an older home whose replacement cost is several times its market value toward the modified coverage form instead of a standard owner form?

answers.text: Insuring far more than the home's market value creates an overinsurance problem the modified form's functional, value-aligned basis is meant to control
Older homes are legally barred from every other homeowners form
Standard owner forms exclude any dwelling built before a fixed calendar year, as recorded in the recorded statement taken from the insured after the accident
The modified form pays more than replacement cost for historic features

questions.explanation: When the amount needed to rebuild dwarfs what the home would sell for, a standard form invites overinsurance concerns; the modified form aligns the settlement basis with functional value. No rule bars older homes from other forms outright — the value relationship drives the choice.

questions.question: A warehouse is covered by Policy A with a $150,000 limit and Policy B with a $50,000 limit. A covered loss of $80,000 occurs and pro rata sharing applies. How much does Policy A pay?
questions.explanation: Policy A's share is $150,000 divided by $200,000 in total limits, or three-fourths, times the $80,000 loss, which equals $60,000. Policy B pays the remaining one-fourth, or $20,000.

questions.question: An applicant asks a producer about minimum property damage limit. Which response states the New York rule correctly?

answers.text: $10,000 per accident
$50,000 per accident
$5,000 per accident
$25,000 per accident

questions.explanation: The property damage minimum is $10,000 per accident. Higher figures appear in bills that were proposed but not enacted, so they are not the current minimum.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding insurer options after paying mortgagee in New York?

answers.text: The insurer must absorb the payment with no recourse of any kind
The insurer may cancel the mortgage itself
On paying the mortgagee despite no liability to the owner, the insurer is subrogated to the mortgagee's recovery rights or may pay off the mortgage and take an assignment
The mortgagee loses its right to sue once the insurer is subrogated

questions.explanation: The insurer is subrogated, to the extent of its payment, to the mortgagee's rights of recovery without impairing the mortgagee's right to sue, or it may pay off the mortgage debt and require an assignment of the debt and mortgage. It is not left without recourse.

questions.question: A homeowner cannot obtain homeowners coverage in the voluntary market because of where the home is located, and the refusal was not grounded in loss-experience principles. What remedy does the law give the homeowner?

answers.text: The insured's only remedy is to accept association coverage
The insured must sue the insurer before contacting the regulator
Agents may file the complaint but insureds may not
The insured may file a complaint with the superintendent on the prescribed form

questions.explanation: The aggrieved insured may file a complaint with the superintendent on the prescribed form. Accepting association coverage is not the only remedy, and no lawsuit is a prerequisite.

questions.question: An insurer sent an escrow-account nonpayment cancellation notice to the homeowner but not to the mortgage institution, then treated the policy as cancelled. What is the status of that notice?

answers.text: The notice takes effect thirty days later than planned
Missing either required recipient makes the escrow cancellation notice of no force and effect
The notice remains effective but the insurer owes a small fee
Only the mortgagee's copy matters to the notice's effectiveness

questions.explanation: The statute makes the notice of no force and effect when either required copy is not sent. The cancellation cannot stand on that notice.

questions.question: Regarding unlicensed activity penalty ceiling, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: up to five hundred dollars per transaction
up to twenty-five hundred dollars in total for all transactions
up to five thousand dollars per transaction
up to one hundred dollars per day of violation

questions.explanation: Up to five hundred dollars per transaction is correct because it states the verified rule. The alternative 'up to five thousand dollars per transaction' is wrong because it reverses, misstates or mis-times that rule.

questions.question: A member's deficit share equals two percent of its surplus. How much must it reimburse that year under the cap rule?

answers.text: Cap of five percent of surplus
Cap measured by premium volume
No cap on yearly reimbursement
Deficit reimbursement capped at one percent of surplus

questions.explanation: Only up to one percent, with the excess reallocated as described. Premium volume sets shares, surplus sets this cap.

questions.question: A worker's disability begins and no controversy exists. When is the first payment due and how often do payments follow?

answers.text: Payments are always monthly
First payment due on day fourteen, paid within four days, then biweekly
First payment due on day thirty
First payment due on the first day of disability

questions.explanation: Day fourteen is the due date with payment within four days and biweekly payment after. Day thirty is wrong because the first due date is the fourteenth day.

california-insurance.quiz_title: California Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: How does lending a covered auto to a friend for a week differ from selling that auto to the friend?

answers.text: There is no difference, because the friend has possession in both cases, for the insured, premises, and policy period identified in the declarations, and as the form itself provides
Both require the friend to be named on the title
Lending leaves ownership with the insured, so the auto remains a covered auto used by a permissive user, while selling transfers ownership and ends that auto's covered status
Lending ends coverage, while selling keeps it

questions.explanation: Possession is not ownership. A loan keeps the auto owned and covered, with the borrower as a permissive user, while a sale moves ownership and with it the basis for covered auto status.

questions.question: One injured person incurs $3,000 of eligible medical expenses, and another incurs $9,000. The per person medical expense limit is $5,000. How much is paid in total?
questions.explanation: The first person is paid in full at $3,000 and the second is capped at $5,000, for $3,000 + $5,000 = $8,000. Applying one $5,000 cap to both together would underpay the first person.

questions.question: A bookkeeper diverts customer payments to a personal account over several months, intending to keep the funds. Which element makes this an Employee Theft loss rather than a bookkeeping error?

answers.text: The bookkeeper was a long-service employee
The payments were received on different dates
The bookkeeper unlawfully took the insured's money with intent to deprive the insured and gain personally
The customers paid by check instead of by cash, regardless of whether the event took place on the described premises or at another covered location

questions.explanation: Explanation: The unlawful taking with intent to deprive the insured and obtain a personal benefit is the core of employee theft. Length of service, payment method, and timing across months do not turn an error into theft or theft into an error.

questions.question: A volunteer worker helping at the insured's charity bake sale, who is not an employee, is burned and treated at an urgent care clinic. Which statement about the Coverage C insured exclusion is correct for this volunteer?

answers.text: The volunteer is treated as the named insured for every purpose under Coverage C
The volunteer is barred because every helper is an insured under Coverage C
The volunteer is covered only if the volunteer also bought a ticket to the sale
The volunteer is excepted from the insured exclusion, so the claim is not barred on that ground

questions.explanation: The Coverage C insured exclusion carves out volunteer workers, so a volunteer is not excluded as an insured. That exception does not make the volunteer an insured for all purposes, which is why the broader distractor overstates it.

questions.question: A tenant secretly builds a permanent recording studio inside rented space at the tenant's expense, without telling the landlord, and asks whether the build-out can be improvements and betterments. Which element deserves the closest look?

answers.text: Whether the studio equipment has Bluetooth capability, under the policy form in effect, and as set out in the policy form, declarations, and applicable endorsement schedule
Whether studio sessions are booked on weekends
Whether the tenant's customers like the studio
Whether the work qualifies as a permanent alteration made by the tenant at the tenant's expense to the rented premises, and whether policy and lease terms recognize it

questions.explanation: The classification turns on the nature of the work, permanent alterations by the tenant at the tenant's expense to the rented space, plus what the lease and policy say about it. Secrecy and scheduling do not define the category.

questions.question: A delivery company's driver, who is insured under the company's own separate commercial policy with a different insurer, negligently damages a florist's insured greenhouse. The florist's insurer pays and seeks recovery from the driver. Does the no-subrogation-against-an-insured rule block this recovery?

answers.text: Yes, because the driver has insurance somewhere
No, because the driver is not an insured under the florist's policy that paid the claim
Yes, because all negligent drivers are treated as insureds
No recovery is possible from any individual, only from corporations

questions.explanation: The shield applies only to persons insured under the paying policy; the driver is insured elsewhere, which is irrelevant to the florist's insurer. A different insurer's policy does not extend the protection.

questions.question: Suspecting arson, an insurer lawfully requires an examination under oath. The insured refuses to appear at all, without explanation. What is the likely consequence?

answers.text: Nothing, because examinations under oath are always optional
Refusal breaches a policy condition and can support denial of the claim
The insurer must pay the claim in full within ten days
Refusal converts the claim into a liability claim

questions.explanation: Appearing for a required examination under oath is a condition of recovery, so an unexplained refusal can defeat the claim. It is not an optional courtesy.

questions.question: A tenant's clothing, dishes, and electronics are damaged by a covered peril in the rented unit. Which coverage in the tenants policy pays for those belongings?

answers.text: Coverage A, dwelling
Coverage C, personal property, which is the main property coverage on a tenants policy
Coverage B, other structures
The landlord's loss of rents coverage, which pays the tenant for clothing and electronics damaged inside the rented unit

questions.explanation: On a tenants policy, Coverage C carries the property protection because the tenant owns contents, not the building. There is no dwelling limit for the tenant to claim against, and the landlord's rental income coverage protects the landlord, not the tenant's belongings.

questions.question: A BOP-insured building has sat completely empty and unused for well beyond the policy's vacancy period when vandals damage it and a pipe bursts. How does prolonged vacancy affect the claim?

answers.text: Certain losses, such as vandalism and water damage, can be excluded or reduced after the building has been vacant beyond the stated period
Vacancy has no effect on any BOP property claim
