The insurer must pay double because vacant buildings face higher risk, as described in the application and the agent's notes taken when the coverage was placed
The claim converts to a liability claim because no one was present

questions.explanation: BOP vacancy provisions restrict coverage for causes such as vandalism, sprinkler leakage, and water damage, and can reduce other payments, once a building is vacant beyond the stated period. Vacancy is not irrelevant, which is why the no-effect option is wrong.

questions.question: A licensee moves the agency to a new building and changes a home address. Which changes trigger the immediate electronic notice duty?

answers.text: Only the business move, as the complete answer for the situation described in the question
Only the home move, as the complete and controlling answer for the situation described in the question
Neither until renewal, as the sole answer governing the matter that is described in the question
Changes in email, residence, principal business, or mailing address

questions.explanation: The current duty covers email, residence, principal business, and mailing addresses alike.

questions.question: A borrower buys more hazard coverage than the loan agreement requires, from an acceptable insurer, and the lender refuses it solely because the limit is higher than required. The extra coverage is property coverage only. May the lender refuse on that ground?

answers.text: Yes, lenders may cap coverage at the required amount, because that single ground or statement is treated as enough by itself to decide the matter, without regard to any other fact mentioned in the question

Yes, unless the borrower complains to the Commissioner, and that answer is not qualified by any condition drawn from the surrounding facts, the identity of the parties involved, or the stage at which the matter arises in this case
No. A lender may not refuse insurance from an acceptable insurer merely because it provides more coverage than required, unless the additional coverage is automobile, life, or disability insurance

No rule addresses excess coverage, with the same answer applying whether the matter arises before, during, or after the transaction, event, or proceeding that the question describes in its facts, as the complete answer for the situation described in the question

questions.explanation: Excess property coverage alone is not a lawful ground for refusal; the exception covers additional automobile, life, or disability coverage.

questions.question: Under the standard fire policy, the amount of loss for which the company may be liable becomes payable:

answers.text: Only after the insured rebuilds the entire structure, and the rule cannot be changed by a side agreement
Immediately when the fire department leaves the scene, and it applies to every policyholder in the same position, even when the insured requests different treatment in writing
30 days after the policy is issued each year, with no exception allowed for any insured
60 days after the proof of loss is received and the loss is ascertained by written agreement or by filing of an appraisal award

questions.explanation: Loss is payable 60 days after proof of loss is received and ascertainment is made by written agreement between the parties or by filing of an award. Rebuilding first is not the form's payment trigger.

florida-insurance.quiz_title: Florida Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Participants allege that plan fiduciaries allowed the retirement plan to pay excessive recordkeeping fees for years without shopping for alternatives, reducing participant account balances. Which policy responds to this allegation?

answers.text: Medical professional liability insurance
Fiduciary liability insurance
An umbrella policy with no underlying coverage for the claim
A license and permit bond

questions.explanation: Allowing a plan to pay excessive fees is alleged to be an imprudent fiduciary act that harms participants, a fiduciary liability claim. A license bond guarantees compliance with a licensing law and does not defend plan fee claims.

questions.question: A booster club that normally runs school concessions buys a one-weekend permit, sells beer at a fair as its main fundraiser activity that weekend, and a buyer it served injures a third party after becoming intoxicated. What is the key liquor exclusion question?

answers.text: Whether the club's school concessions usually sell soft drinks during the school year or sells during the school year, and that usual activity alone decides whether the club was in the business of selling alcohol at the fair
Whether the fairground was owned by a public school district
Whether, for that activity, the club was in the business of selling or furnishing alcohol, judged by the selling role it took on rather than its usual school purpose
Whether the beer was sold in cans rather than in cups

questions.explanation: The exclusion asks about the insured's role in the alcohol activity that produced the claim, so selling beer as the fundraiser's business that weekend is the relevant role. The club's usual soft drink sales and the container type do not decide whether it was selling alcohol for this event.

questions.question: On a liability application, a business states that it believes it had no losses in the past three years, answering to the best of its knowledge. That statement, if later shown to be mistaken, is most accurately classified as which of the following?

answers.text: A warranty
Concealment
An endorsement
A representation

questions.explanation: A representation is a statement the applicant believes to be true to the best of knowledge and belief. A warranty is guaranteed true, and concealment is the withholding of a material fact rather than a stated belief.

questions.question: A liability policy lists a first named insured and several other named insureds. Notice of cancellation is properly given to the first named insured only. What is the effect on the other named insureds?

answers.text: Each other named insured keeps a separate, uncancelled policy
The notice is effective for policy purposes, because the first named insured acts on behalf of all insureds for notices and cancellation
The other insureds automatically become first named insureds
The cancellation applies to no one until each insured is separately served, even if a similar approach is sometimes followed under a different form, endorsement, or coverage

questions.explanation: The first named insured is the conduit for policy notices and cancellation. Separate service on every insured is not required, contrary to that distractor.

questions.question: A man buys a condominium unit as an investment and rents it to a tenant year-round while living elsewhere. Why does the unit-owners form not fit him as an occupant's policy?

answers.text: His unit lost its condominium status when a tenant moved in
The unit-owners form is written for an owner who occupies the unit; he is a non-occupying landlord
Unit-owners forms may never be sold in buildings that contain tenants
He must instead insure the entire condominium building himself

questions.explanation: Like the other owner forms, the unit-owners form follows owner occupancy. Renting the unit out full time makes him a landlord for that unit, and one rented unit does not make him responsible for insuring the whole building.

questions.question: An employee of an independent contractor, over whom the insured had no direction or control, leaves a valve open and causes covered water damage. The insurer argues the insured should lose coverage because of that person's neglect. Which condition answers the insurer's argument?

answers.text: The Control of Property condition, because another person's neglect beyond the insured's direction or control does not affect the insurance
The No Benefit to Bailee condition, because the contractor held the property, even where the insured relied on advice from an agent or broker in expecting that result to follow
The vacancy condition, because the premises were partly unattended
The coinsurance condition, because the loss involves water

questions.explanation: Control of Property is written for exactly this fact pattern, an act or neglect by someone outside the insured's direction or control. No Benefit to Bailee addresses a custodian claiming a benefit, which is not this dispute.

questions.question: Under the federal concept governing risk retention groups, what kind of insurance may a risk retention group provide?

answers.text: Liability insurance for its members
Property insurance for any member of the public
Workers' compensation insurance for unrelated employers
Life insurance for its members' employees

questions.explanation: Risk retention groups are limited to liability coverage for their members. They do not write property, workers' compensation, or life insurance.

questions.question: A homeowner applies for a new policy while knowing that an unrepaired fire last month damaged wiring inside the walls. The homeowner reports no prior damage because the earlier fire was never claimed. Which element makes this concealment rather than a simple lack of a claim history?

answers.text: Unrepaired damage is material only if a neighbor reports it
The homeowner knowingly withheld existing material damage that increased the risk
A prior event only matters if a claim was paid on it
The homeowner made a warranty by not filing the earlier claim

questions.explanation: What matters is the known, existing, unrepaired damage and the added risk it presents, not whether an earlier claim was filed or paid. Deliberately withholding that known condition is concealment.

questions.question: An insured's check to the finance company bounces for insufficient funds and the agreement provides for a charge. What may be imposed?

answers.text: A $15 charge
A $50 charge
A charge equal to the installment
No charge is ever allowed

questions.explanation: The returned-check charge is $15 when the agreement so provides. An installment-sized charge far exceeds the stated amount.

questions.question: A limited customer representative in Florida may assist the appointing general lines agent or agency only with:

answers.text: Commercial property insurance for small businesses
All personal and commercial lines the agency writes
Life and health insurance sold from the agency office
Private passenger motor vehicle insurance

questions.explanation: A limited customer representative assists only with private passenger motor vehicle insurance from the appointing agent's or agency's office. The limited license does not extend to the agency's full book of business.

questions.question: A Florida homeowners policy has a dwelling limit of $400,000 and a 2 percent hurricane deductible. What is the dollar amount of the hurricane deductible?
questions.explanation: 2 percent of $400,000 is $8,000. The deductible is a percentage of the dwelling limit, not of the loss.

questions.question: A newly eligible foreign surplus lines insurer asks what comes next with the office. Florida law provides that:

answers.text: The insurer's continued eligibility, and the office's authority to remove eligibility, are governed by the statutory eligibility framework and its withdrawal provisions
Eligibility is permanent once granted, with no exception for the situation described, under any reading of the facts presented
The insurer must reapply from scratch every year, in each instance of the conduct described, without regard to the surrounding circumstances
Eligibility ends automatically after three years, in every case, with no qualification of any kind

questions.explanation: Eligibility is an ongoing status: the insurer must continue to satisfy the eligibility requirements, and the office retains statutory authority over continued eligibility and withdrawal. It is neither a one-time permanent grant nor an annual fresh application.

intro-psychology.quiz_title: Introductory Psychology Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: In the self-correcting process of science, an explanation that organizes observations and generates testable predictions is called a(n):

answers.text: Case study
Operational definition
Illusory correlation
Theory

questions.explanation: A theory is an explanation that organizes observations and predicts behaviors or events, and it is refined as evidence accumulates.

questions.question: Psychologists who conduct research with animals are required to justify the work and to ensure humane care and treatment because:

answers.text: Animal studies never cause any discomfort
Animals have given informed consent
Animal research is exempt from review
Ethical standards require minimizing animal suffering and ensuring the knowledge gained warrants the research

questions.explanation: Ethical guidelines require that animal research be justified by its potential value and that animals receive humane housing, care, and treatment with suffering minimized.

questions.question: A lab studies only how often a rat presses a lever after different reward schedules, deliberately avoiding any claims about the rat's thoughts. This restriction to observable events defines:

answers.text: Cognitive psychology
Psychoanalytic theory
Humanistic psychology
Behaviorism

questions.explanation: Behaviorism redefined psychology as the scientific study of observable behavior and rejected reliance on unobservable mental processes.

questions.question: A clinician explains a patient's depression by considering brain chemistry, negative thought patterns, and a recent loss of social support together. The clinician is using:

answers.text: The behaviorist approach alone
The structuralist approach
The biopsychosocial approach
A single-level explanation

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial approach integrates biological, psychological, and social-cultural levels of analysis instead of relying on one factor alone.

questions.question: A psychologist spends two years documenting the language recovery of one patient with a rare brain injury. A key limitation of this case study is that:

answers.text: The study lacks any detailed information
The results must be statistically significant
The findings may not generalize to other people
The patient cannot be observed over time

questions.explanation: Case studies offer depth on an individual case but a single atypical person may not represent the wider population, limiting generalizability.

questions.question: If adopted children resemble their biological parents more than their adoptive parents on a trait, that pattern most directly suggests:

answers.text: A genetic influence on the trait
That the trait is entirely determined at birth
That adoptive homes were unusually uniform
That adoption has no environmental effect

questions.explanation: Adoption studies separate heredity from shared home environment; resemblance to biological parents points toward genetic influence.

questions.question: To untangle genetic and environmental influences, behavior geneticists rely most heavily on studies of:

answers.text: Single case studies
Opinion surveys
Brain imaging alone
Twins and adopted individuals

questions.explanation: Twin and adoption studies are the core methods of behavior genetics because they allow comparisons that separate shared genes from shared environments.

questions.question: A lottery winner reports a surge of joy, but a year later her overall happiness is close to what it was before winning. This return toward a baseline illustrates the:

answers.text: Relative deprivation effect
Adaptation-level phenomenon
Fight-or-flight response
General adaptation syndrome

questions.explanation: The adaptation-level phenomenon is our tendency to judge new circumstances relative to a neutral level set by prior experience, so happiness gains from changed circumstances often fade.

questions.question: Regular brisk walking and cycling are associated with lower depression and anxiety, better stress management, and increased longevity. Such sustained activity that raises heart rate is called:

answers.text: Aerobic exercise
Anaerobic resistance only
Biofeedback training
The general adaptation syndrome

questions.explanation: Aerobic exercise — sustained activity that increases heart and lung fitness — is linked to reduced stress, depression, and anxiety and to longer life.

questions.question: An earthquake destroys homes across a region, and months later many residents still report anxiety and sleep problems. Earthquakes are examples of which type of stressor?

answers.text: Significant life changes only
Catastrophes — large-scale events that threaten many people at once
Daily hassles
Approach-approach conflicts

questions.explanation: Catastrophes are sudden, unpredictable, large-scale events such as natural disasters that can produce lasting stress in entire communities.

questions.question: When stimulation reaches a minimum threshold, a neuron fires at full strength; stronger stimulation does not make that single impulse stronger. This describes the action potential's:

answers.text: graded response that grows with input
partial firing proportional to stimulus size
continuous leak of charge
all-or-none response

questions.explanation: An action potential is all-or-none: once threshold is reached the neuron fires fully, and intensity is instead coded by firing rate and number of neurons.

questions.question: A drug eases pain because its molecules closely resemble endorphins and activate the same receptors, increasing their activity. In pharmacology terms, this drug is an:

answers.text: agonist
antagonist
reuptake pump
enzyme that destroys receptors

questions.explanation: Agonists increase a neurotransmitter's action by mimicking it or by blocking its reuptake so it stays active longer.

calculus-i-iii.quiz_title: Calculus I-III Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: What is the average rate of change of f(x) = x^2 on [1, 3]?
questions.explanation: The average rate is (f(3) - f(1)) / (3 - 1) = (9 - 1) / 2 = 4.

questions.question: How is f(x) = x^2 + 2x classified by symmetry?

answers.text: Neither even nor odd
Even, because the squared term is unchanged when x is replaced by its negative value
Odd, because the linear term changes sign when x is replaced by its negative value
Both even and odd, because it contains one term of each symmetry type together

questions.explanation: f(-x) = x^2 - 2x, which equals neither f(x) = x^2 + 2x nor -f(x), so the function is neither even nor odd.

questions.question: Why does the intermediate value theorem show that x^3 + x - 1 = 0 has a solution between 0 and 1?

answers.text: The polynomial has degree three, and every cubic equation has three real solutions in total
The polynomial is increasing, and increasing functions always cross every horizontal line
The polynomial changes sign on [0, 1]
The value at x = 1 is exactly zero, so the endpoint itself is the required solution point

questions.explanation: At x = 0 the polynomial equals -1 and at x = 1 it equals 1; being continuous and changing sign, it must equal 0 somewhere between them.

questions.question: What is lim (x -> 0-) |x| / x?

answers.text: The expression is undefined at every point

questions.explanation: For x < 0, |x| = -x, so |x| / x = -x / x = -1 on the whole left side.

questions.question: What is the derivative of 4 sqrt(x)?

answers.text: 2 / sqrt(x)
4 / sqrt(x), from keeping the original coefficient in front of the root unchanged
2 sqrt(x), from multiplying the coefficient by the root instead of dividing by it
1 / (2 sqrt(x)), from dropping the coefficient four before applying the root rule

questions.explanation: The derivative of sqrt(x) is 1 / (2 sqrt(x)), and multiplying by the constant 4 gives 2 / sqrt(x).

questions.question: What is the derivative of e^x?

answers.text: x e^(x - 1), by applying the power rule to the exponent
e^(x - 1), by reducing the exponent by one in the answer
0, because the base of the exponential is a constant number
e^x

questions.explanation: e^x is its own derivative: the derivative of e^x is e^x.

questions.question: What is the derivative of x^2 sin x?

answers.text: 2x cos x, from differentiating both factors and multiplying the results together
2x sin x + x^2 cos x
2x sin x - x^2 cos x, from subtracting the second term of the product rule formula
x^2 cos x alone, because only the trigonometric factor is differentiated in a product

questions.explanation: By the product rule the derivative is (2x)(sin x) + (x^2)(cos x) = 2x sin x + x^2 cos x.

questions.question: What is the equation of the tangent line to y = x^3 at x = 2?

answers.text: y = 12x - 8, obtained by subtracting the function value only once from the product
y = 8x - 16, obtained by using the function value as the slope of the tangent line
y = 12x + 16, obtained by reversing the sign of the intercept in the final equation

questions.explanation: The slope is f'(2) = 3(4) = 12 and the point is (2, 8), so the line is y - 8 = 12(x - 2), that is, y = 12x - 16.

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = cos(x^2)?

answers.text: -sin(x^2)
2x sin(x^2)
-2x sin(x^2)
-2x sin(x^2) cos(x^2)

questions.explanation: The derivative of cos u is -sin u times u prime; with u = x^2, u prime is 2x.

questions.question: For x^2 + xy = 6, what is dy/dx at the point (2, 1)?
questions.explanation: Differentiate: 2x + y + x(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = -(2x + y)/x; at (2, 1) this is -(4 + 1)/2 = -5/2.

questions.question: A spherical balloon's radius is increasing at (1/2) cm/s. How fast is its volume increasing when the radius is 3 cm?

answers.text: 6pi cm^3/s
18pi cm^3/s
36pi cm^3/s
18pi cm^3/s plus 4pi cm^3/s

questions.explanation: V = (4/3)pi r^3, so dV/dt = 4pi r^2 (dr/dt) = 4pi(9)(1/2) = 18pi cm^3/s.

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = sqrt(e^x + x)?

answers.text: (e^x + 1)/sqrt(e^x + x)
1/(2 sqrt(e^x + x))
(e^x + 1)/(2 sqrt(e^x + x))
(e^x + 1)/(2 sqrt(e^x + x)) + x

questions.explanation: Write the root as (e^x + x)^(1/2); the chain rule gives (1/2)(e^x + x)^(-1/2) times (e^x + 1).

general-chemistry.quiz_title: General Chemistry Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Convert 250 cm to meters using 100 cm = 1 m.
What factor does the prefix mega- represent?
questions.explanation: Mega- means one million, a factor of 10^6.

questions.question: A sample of gold contains only gold atoms and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means. How is gold classified?

answers.text: A compound
A homogeneous mixture
A heterogeneous mixture
An element

questions.explanation: A substance containing only one kind of atom that cannot be chemically broken down further is an element.

questions.question: A liquid has a density of 4.0 g/mL and a mass of 36 g. What is its volume?

answers.text: 144 mL
9.0 mL
40 mL

questions.explanation: Volume = mass / density = 36 g / 4.0 g/mL = 9.0 mL.

questions.question: Iron forms FeCl3, in which iron carries a 3+ charge to balance three 1- chloride ions. What is the correct name?

answers.text: Iron chloride with no charge indicated
Iron(I) chloride
Iron(III) chloride
Trichloride iron

questions.explanation: A variable-charge metal needs a Roman numeral for its charge: iron(III) chloride.

questions.question: HNO3 contains the nitrate ion. What is the name of this acid?

answers.text: Nitrous acid
Nitric acid
Hydronitric acid
Nitrogen acid

questions.explanation: Acids from -ate ions take the -ic ending without hydro-: nitric acid.

questions.question: Calcium is in Group 2. What charge does a calcium ion most commonly carry?
questions.explanation: Group 2 atoms lose two electrons, so calcium most commonly forms a 2+ ion.

questions.question: What is the formula and charge of the ammonium ion?

answers.text: NH3 with a 1+ charge
NH4 with a 1- charge
NH4 with a 1+ charge
NH4 with a 2+ charge

questions.explanation: Ammonium is NH4 with a 1+ charge.

questions.question: How many moles are in 90.10 g of H2O? Use a molar mass of 18.02 g/mol.

answers.text: 5.00 mol
2.50 mol
4.00 mol

questions.explanation: Moles = 90.10 g / 18.02 g/mol = 5.00 mol.

questions.question: What is the coefficient of O2 when this equation is balanced with the smallest whole numbers? __ C3H8 + __ O2 -> __ CO2 + __ H2O
questions.explanation: C3H8 gives 3 CO2 and 4 H2O. Oxygen atoms in products = 3(2) + 4(1) = 10, which is 5 O2 molecules.

questions.question: Using H = 1.008 and O = 16.00, what is the molar mass of H2O?

answers.text: 18.02 g/mol
17.01 g/mol
18.00 g/mol
20.02 g/mol

questions.question: What is the percent by mass of chlorine in CaCl2? Use Cl = 35.45 and a molar mass of 110.98 g/mol.

english-composition-i.quiz_title: English Composition I Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An essay gives cost data, quotes affected students fairly, and presents the writer's careful research process. Its persuasion is strongest because what?

answers.text: Three appeals used at once cancel the need for any one of them to be well supported
Logos, pathos, and ethos reinforce one another
Readers cannot distinguish the appeals, so weaknesses in the evidence will go unnoticed
Genre conventions require every persuasive essay to display all three appeals in equal length

questions.explanation: Effective rhetoric usually blends appeals: sound reasoning, credible presentation, and human significance make each element harder to dismiss.

questions.question: Mara writes a campus essay for first-year students who have never used the tutoring center. Those students are her what?

answers.text: Intended audience, the readers she actually aims to reach
Invoked audience, because she pictures readers who share the values she wants them to display
Discourse community, because any group of readers automatically shares goals and specialized language
Secondary audience, because students reading a campus essay are never its primary readership group

questions.explanation: The intended audience is the real readership the writer targets and designs the text to reach and affect.

questions.question: An essay opens with a concrete scene of a student studying in a cold car between work shifts to show what housing costs mean. This primarily uses which appeal?

answers.text: Logos, because a detailed scene functions as a measured data set about regional housing prices
Ethos, because describing another person's hardship proves the writer's professional qualifications
Pathos, engaging readers' emotions through a vivid human situation
Genre, because opening with a scene converts any argumentative essay into a work of short fiction

questions.explanation: Pathos appeals to emotion, and a relevant concrete human scene can make an issue felt as well as understood.

questions.question: Which opening most responsibly uses pathos for an essay on food insecurity?

answers.text: A stock photograph of strangers crying, captioned as though they were students at this college
A fabricated statistic about hunger presented in an emotional font and repeated three times
A threat that readers who disagree will be named publicly as indifferent to student suffering
A specific student's real, permitted account of skipping meals

questions.explanation: Responsible pathos uses truthful, relevant human detail connected to the claim, not manufactured images, invented figures, or intimidation.

questions.question: Two essays both support a new bike-share program; one sounds measured, the other mocking toward critics. The essays most clearly differ in what?

answers.text: Stance, because a mocking style proves the second writer opposes the program being discussed
Genre, because a change in attitude automatically moves a text into a different text category
Tone, while sharing the same basic stance
Audience, because an author who mocks critics must be writing for an entirely different readership

questions.explanation: Stance is the position taken on the subject, which both essays share; tone is the attitude conveyed toward readers and critics, which differs.

questions.question: A writer places 'community gardens' in a center circle and draws branches to 'cost,' 'health,' and 'campus land.' This strategy is what?

answers.text: Freewriting, because drawing circles for a fixed time without stopping is its defining technique
Proofreading, because checking how ideas connect is a final-stage correction of surface errors
Clustering, or mapping, ideas to reveal connections
Formal outlining, because branches arranged by size are equivalent to headings and subheadings

questions.explanation: Clustering maps ideas spatially, letting a writer see relationships and possible subtopics radiating from a central subject.

questions.question: Cubing asks a writer to examine a topic from six sides, such as describing, comparing, and arguing about it. Its purpose is to do what?

answers.text: Generate varied perspectives on a single subject
Assign the six paragraphs of a finished essay so each performs exactly one prescribed function
Evaluate sources for a research paper using a six-point scale of credibility and relevance
Divide a workshop group into six roles that rotate each time the class meets for peer review

questions.explanation: Cubing is an invention heuristic: viewing one subject through several lenses produces angles and material a single viewpoint would miss.

questions.question: A writer schedules four short drafting sessions across a week instead of one all-night session. The chief process advantage is what?

answers.text: Short sessions eliminate the need for revision, since rested writers produce final-quality prose
Spreading work out guarantees the essay will match the formal outline with no changes needed
Frequent sessions count as peer review, because the writer returns to the draft as a new reader
Time between sessions lets ideas develop and problems become visible

questions.explanation: Spacing drafting creates room for incubation and fresh seeing, making both invention and revision more productive than a single marathon.

questions.question: What is the writer's proper standard for deciding which peer suggestions to adopt?

answers.text: Whether the reviewer is the strongest writer in the class, regardless of the suggestion's content
Whether each change serves the essay's purpose and readers
Whether adopting the change is the fastest way to finish the assignment and submit the draft
Whether the suggestion changes the largest possible number of sentences in the existing draft

questions.explanation: Feedback is advice, not instruction; the writer tests each suggestion against purpose, audience, and the essay's own aims before adopting it.

questions.question: Moving a background section before the problem discussion and cutting a repeated example is an act of what?

answers.text: Structural, or global, revision
Proofreading, because any change made near the end of the process counts as final checking
Sentence-level editing, because paragraphs are composed of sentences and so count as sentences
Focused freewriting, because rearranging existing material generates new ideas about the topic

questions.explanation: Reordering major sections and removing redundancy changes the draft's architecture, which is global revision rather than surface editing.

questions.question: Which description best captures active, critical reading?

answers.text: Engaging the text by questioning and testing its ideas
Accepting a text's claims as settled whenever its author holds academic credentials
Reading as quickly as possible so that more pages can be covered in one sitting
Memorizing a text's wording so that it can be reproduced exactly on an examination

questions.explanation: Critical reading is active engagement: the reader questions, connects and evaluates rather than simply absorbing what is printed.

questions.question: Before arguing against a source, a fair disagreeing response should first do what?

answers.text: Announce that the source's author is unqualified to write on the topic under discussion
Select the source's weakest sentence and treat it as the whole of its argument
Restate the source's claim in exaggerated terms so that it is easier to refute
Represent the source's position accurately

questions.explanation: Disagreement is credible only when the position being answered is the one the source actually took, fairly and accurately stated.

ohio-real-estate.quiz_title: Ohio Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Two partners buy a rental property with partnership funds. On a partner's death, what happens to the interest?

answers.text: Goes to the spouse automatically
Escheats to the state
Is partitioned by a court
Passes under partnership rules, not survivorship

questions.explanation: A partner's interest is governed by the partnership agreement and partnership law when a partner dies; it does not pass automatically by survivorship the way a joint-tenancy interest does. It also does not automatically go to a spouse, escheat to the state, or require partition in every case.

questions.question: Under 12 CFR 1024.17(c)(1), the cushion a servicer may require a borrower to deposit into an escrow account for a federally related mortgage loan may not exceed what amount?

answers.text: One-sixth of the estimated total annual payments from the escrow account
One month of the borrower's total housing payment
Five per cent of the loan balance
One-quarter of the estimated total annual payments from the escrow account

questions.explanation: For federally related mortgage loans, the escrow cushion a servicer may require is capped at one-sixth of the estimated total annual payments from the escrow account, which equals about two months of escrow payments. The larger fractions and the loan-balance or housing-payment measures exceed or misstate that cap.

questions.question: A construction loan includes an interest reserve. What is it?

answers.text: Funds set aside from the loan to pay interest during construction, so the borrower has no out-of-pocket payments while building.
Short-term financing that lets a buyer purchase a new home before selling the current one, similar to a bridge loan.
The lender, who receives the mortgage.
A conventional loan is made by a private lender without government insurance or guarantee, and must meet investor guidelines.

questions.explanation: An interest reserve is money held back from construction loan proceeds to pay interest while the building is underway, sparing the borrower out-of-pocket interest payments during construction. A bridge loan, the lender, and a conventional loan definition describe different financing concepts.

questions.question: Robin writes a Kettering offer contingent on the buyer's condo sale. Under the rules of sale-of-home contingency, what should happen?

answers.text: Include clear timelines and any kick-out rights for the seller
Leave the timeline open-ended
Hide the contingency from the seller
Promise the buyer's home will sell

questions.explanation: A sale-of-home contingency needs clear deadlines and, where agreed, a kick-out right so the seller can keep marketing and require the buyer to act if another offer arrives. Leaving timing open-ended, hiding the contingency, or guaranteeing the buyer's home sale misstates how the protection works.

questions.question: A seller gives their sibling a general, non-durable power of attorney to sign their closing documents. Before closing, the seller becomes incapacitated. Which of the following happens to the power of attorney?

answers.text: Remains fully valid through closing
Transfers automatically to the listing broker
Becomes irrevocable once signed
Terminates upon the principal's incapacity

questions.explanation: A non-durable power of attorney terminates when the principal becomes incapacitated, because durability is what allows an agency document to survive incapacity. It therefore does not remain valid through closing, does not transfer to the broker, and does not become irrevocable merely by being signed.

questions.question: An underground storage tank was removed from the property ten years ago. What should the seller do about the former tank?

answers.text: Disclose it only if the buyer is obtaining an FHA loan
Stay silent, because a removed tank cannot affect the property
Disclose the tank's existence and removal, since residual contamination is a material concern
Report it to the fire department instead of disclosing to the buyer

questions.explanation: A removed underground storage tank is still a material fact because residual contamination may remain in the soil, so the seller should disclose both its existence and its removal. Silence is improper precisely because the risk can outlast the tank, and disclosure to the buyer cannot be replaced by a report to an agency or tied only to one loan type.

questions.question: Business plan is best described as which of the following?

answers.text: New-construction buyers need builder-contract review, upgrade negotiation, and independent inspections
The agent's strategy for success
The sphere of influence — past clients and contacts — is the highest-converting lead source
Luxury properties need professional photography, staging, targeted exposure, and price-positioning expertise

questions.explanation: A business plan is the agent's strategy for success: the goals and methods the agent will use to build the business. The other choices describe services for particular client types and lead sources, not the plan itself.

questions.question: Compound appreciation: $671,000, 5% per year, 3 years. How much value added?
questions.explanation: Compound growth applies the rate to the growing balance each year: $671,000 multiplied by 1.05 three times reaches about $776,766. Subtracting the original $671,000 leaves about $105,766 of added value. Adding three years of simple interest would understate the gain because it ignores growth on prior growth.

questions.question: Can excess CE carry to the next cycle?

answers.text: Yes — up to 10 excess hours may be carried into the next reporting period.
No; out-of-state licensees must satisfy Ohio's education, exam, and character requirements.
Orientation on the brokerage's policies, the license law, and compliance duties.
Through the broker, with intra-team splits set by the team agreement.

questions.explanation: Ohio Adm. Code 1301:5-7-02(H) allows a licensee to carry up to 10 excess continuing education hours into the next reporting period; any hours beyond 10 do not carry over.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes for-sale signs in Ohio?

answers.text: are optional
need no permission
are prohibited
are placed with authority

questions.explanation: For-sale signs are placed with the property owner's authority; putting marketing on someone's property is not a matter of the licensee's personal choice. Signs are not prohibited altogether, but permission is what separates an authorized sign from an unauthorized one.

questions.question: A parcel of 6.5 acres is priced at $11,000 per acre. What is the total price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the acreage by the price per acre: six and one-half acres times eleven thousand dollars per acre equals seventy-one thousand five hundred dollars.

questions.question: Ohio consent and dual is best described as which of the following?

answers.text: Informed and written
The listing where the broker keeps amounts above the seller's net price, restricted or prohibited in many states.
Verbal consent is sufficient
Same rules

questions.explanation: Ohio dual agency must be informed and written: both the seller and the purchaser must give full knowledge and consent in writing on the agency disclosure statement before one brokerage or licensee represents both. Verbal consent is not sufficient.

general-biology.quiz_title: General Biology Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Many archaea live in hot springs or very salty water, but their cells still lack a membrane-bound nucleus. Archaea are therefore:

answers.text: Eukaryotic because they live in extreme places
Prokaryotic members of a domain distinct from Bacteria
Nonliving chemical systems
Members of domain Bacteria

questions.explanation: Archaea are prokaryotic, yet they form their own domain separate from Bacteria.

questions.question: A formula that reliably describes how the period of a pendulum relates to its length under stated conditions illustrates a scientific:

answers.text: Law, because it describes a consistent pattern
Hypothesis, because it explains why the pattern occurs
Theory, because it is broad and unifying
Control, because it holds variables constant

questions.explanation: Scientific laws describe consistent relationships or patterns, often mathematically.

questions.question: How does a biological community differ from a population?

answers.text: A population is larger than the biosphere, while a community is smaller
A community includes multiple species in an area, while a population is one species
A community includes abiotic factors, while a population does not
A population includes multiple species, while a community is one species

questions.explanation: A community is the collection of all populations of different species in an area.

questions.question: A sunflower turns its leaves toward light during the day. Which property of life does this best illustrate?

answers.text: Heredity through DNA
Homeostasis of internal temperature
Photosynthesis as a form of reproduction
Responsiveness to stimuli

questions.explanation: Responding to an environmental signal, such as light, is a hallmark property of living organisms.

questions.question: A group written as -COOH that can donate a hydrogen ion and make a molecule act as an acid is the:

answers.text: Hydroxyl group
Phosphate group
Methyl group
Carboxyl group

questions.explanation: Carboxyl groups can release H+, giving carboxylic acids their acidic behavior.

questions.question: A neutral atom has 17 protons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

questions.question: Two atoms both have 6 protons, so they must be the same element because an element's identity is determined by:

answers.text: Number of electron shells
Number of neutrons
Number of protons
Total number of bonds formed

questions.explanation: The proton count, or atomic number, defines the element; 6 protons is carbon.

questions.question: Human blood must stay near pH 7.4. If a small amount of acid enters the blood, a buffer such as bicarbonate helps by:

answers.text: Turning blood into a strong base
Raising pH immediately to 14
Removing all carbon dioxide instantly
Binding some of the added H+ so pH changes only slightly

questions.explanation: Bicarbonate can accept hydrogen ions, dampening the pH drop from added acid.

questions.question: In a molecule of H2, the two hydrogen atoms are held together by:

answers.text: A hydrogen bond between molecules
A van der Waals attraction only
A single covalent bond sharing one pair of electrons
An ionic bond between opposite charges

questions.explanation: Each hydrogen contributes one electron, forming one shared pair: a single covalent bond.

questions.question: Joining 10 glucose units into a single chain by dehydration synthesis (ignoring branching) releases how many water molecules?
questions.explanation: Each new glycosidic bond formed between two units releases one water molecule. A chain of 10 units has 9 bonds linking them.

questions.question: A molecule contains carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and phosphorus, and is built from nucleotides. It must be what?

answers.text: A nucleic acid
A lipid
A carbohydrate
A protein only

questions.explanation: The combination of phosphorus and nucleotide subunits is diagnostic of nucleic acids (DNA or RNA).

questions.question: Sucrose, common table sugar, is formed from which pair of monomers?

answers.text: Glucose + glucose
Glucose + fructose
Fructose + galactose
Glucose + ribose

questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide composed of one glucose unit joined to one fructose unit by a glycosidic linkage.

nce.quiz_title: NCE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A new supervisor asks where ultimate responsibility for the welfare of clients seen by supervisees rests. The accurate answer is that

answers.text: Responsibility rests entirely with each supervisee
The supervisor shares responsibility for client welfare in supervisee cases and must monitor the care provided
Responsibility rests with the agency's insurer
Responsibility begins only after the supervisee is licensed

questions.explanation: Supervision carries vicarious responsibility: the supervisor oversees and answers for the quality and safety of care supervisees deliver, which is why monitoring, review, and intervention are supervisory duties. The supervisee's developing status does not shift that responsibility away, an insurer handles liability rather than clinical welfare, and oversight applies throughout training, not only after licensure.

questions.question: Before a second round of counseling begins, a client describes the relaxation training from earlier therapy as genuinely useful and the nightly written journals as something she dreaded and skipped. Asking about experiences like these during the treatment history is most useful because it:

answers.text: proves whether the earlier counselor practiced competently
determines whether the client is likely to resist this time
replaces the need to explore the current presenting concern
shows which approaches to build on and which unhelpful strategies to avoid repeating

questions.explanation: Prior response to treatment is practical evidence: approaches that helped can be built on, and strategies the client experienced as unhelpful can be avoided or adapted. It does not judge the earlier clinician, does not brand the client as resistant, and never substitutes for exploring the current concern.

questions.question: Unable to be in the same room without fighting, divorced parents of a nine-year-old agree to communicate only in writing about logistics, attend school events separately, and each run their own household routines without consulting the other. This high-conflict co-parenting arrangement is known as what?

answers.text: Cooperative co-parenting
Coparent triangulation
Parallel parenting
Conflict-free joint custody

questions.explanation: Parallel parenting lets high-conflict parents disengage from each other while each parents independently, using structured, businesslike communication limited to essentials. Cooperative co-parenting involves the joint consultation these parents cannot manage, triangulation would pull the child into the conflict rather than structuring around it, and the arrangement manages conflict rather than eliminating it.

questions.question: Since returning from an overseas deployment, a veteran sits facing doors, scans rooms constantly, and jumps at sudden noises at home. Which symptom group do these behaviors most directly reflect?

answers.text: Negative mood symptoms only
Compulsive rituals
Manic impulsivity
Arousal and reactivity changes, including hypervigilance and exaggerated startle

questions.explanation: Hypervigilance and exaggerated startle response are arousal and reactivity changes commonly seen after trauma, reflecting a persistently activated threat system. They are distinct from ritualized behavior aimed at preventing a feared outcome and from the disinhibition of elevated mood states.

questions.question: An intake screening scale returns a 'moderate' score for a client whose interview reveals recent losses, new insomnia, and a brother who died by suicide, while another client with the same score appears stable and well supported. How should the score be used?

answers.text: The score alone should set the same disposition for both clients
Scores inform, but do not replace, a clinical formulation weighing acute and chronic factors for each person
A moderate score rules out serious risk, so the interview findings can be set aside
Scores are meaningless and should never be administered at all

questions.explanation: Standardized scores contribute one data point, but disposition rests on an individualized formulation that weighs static history against current, changeable warning signs and supports — which clearly differ between these two clients. Identical scores with different clinical pictures demand different plans. Discarding instruments entirely would throw away useful structured information.

questions.question: One patient secretly injects insulin to produce symptoms and seeks admission after admission, wanting the care and attention of the sick role; another fabricates symptoms only to obtain a settlement payment and avoid work. What distinguishes the second patient's behavior?

answers.text: It is factitious disorder because all deception about illness is factitious
It is malingering, because the deception serves clear external incentives
It is somatic symptom disorder because symptoms are reported
It cannot be classified because motives are unknowable

questions.explanation: Malingering involves intentional production or exaggeration of symptoms motivated by external incentives such as money, avoiding work, or obtaining drugs. Factitious disorder involves deceptive presentation of illness even without obvious external rewards, with gratification tied to occupying the sick role itself. Somatic symptom disorder does not require intentional deception at all, so deliberate fabrication for payment falls outside it.

questions.question: A 6-year-old's successful treatment is ending. Which termination approach fits the child's development?

answers.text: End without telling the child, to spare the child sadness
Hold an adult-style verbal review of treatment goals
Use a planned goodbye activity the child can understand, mark the progress made, and prepare caregivers that brief clinginess or regression can follow endings
Extend treatment indefinitely because children cannot tolerate endings

questions.explanation: Young children process endings concretely, so a planned goodbye ritual and caregiver preparation for transient regression fit their development. Disappearing without a goodbye undermines trust and the child's understanding, abstract verbal goal reviews exceed a young child's processing, and children can tolerate well-managed endings that are part of healthy care.

questions.question: Having listed several ways to handle a neighbor dispute, a client and counselor rate each option against criteria the client chose, select one, and agree to test it for two weeks and review the result. This step in problem solving is best described as:

answers.text: Brainstorming options without any structure
Terminating treatment because a decision was reached
Evaluating options against chosen criteria and piloting the selected one as a trial
Interpreting the dispute as a family-of-origin repetition

questions.explanation: Rating options against chosen criteria, selecting one, and testing it for a set period is the evaluation-and-trial step of problem solving. Generation of options happened earlier and was structured, a single decision does not end treatment, and no transference-style interpretation of family patterns is involved.

questions.question: A school counselor chooses a structured peer group, rather than only individual sessions, for a 13-year-old struggling to make friends, reasoning that peer belonging is especially salient at this age. The choice reflects alignment with:

answers.text: Infant attachment formation
Later-life generativity
Preoperational thought
Adolescents' heightened peer orientation

questions.explanation: Early adolescents are intensely oriented toward peer acceptance, so a well-run peer group offers practice and belonging where they matter most. Attachment formation in infancy, midlife generativity, and preschool cognition do not explain this modality choice.

questions.question: Saying no without aggression is the skill practiced in a counselor-led module using scripts, role play, and feedback. Which training is this?

answers.text: Assertiveness training delivered as psychoeducation
Exposure therapy for a specific phobia
Play therapy for young children
Biofeedback using physiological monitoring equipment

questions.explanation: Assertiveness training teaches clients to express needs and limits directly and respectfully, commonly through instruction and role play in a psychoeducational format. It involves no feared-stimulus exposure, no child play medium, and no physiological equipment. Scripted practice of respectful self-expression is its hallmark.

questions.question: Awareness is the goal when a counselor asks a client to exaggerate a nervous foot-tapping until its meaning in the present moment becomes clear. Which approach uses such experiments?

answers.text: Adlerian therapy, which would interpret the movement as lifestyle expression
Behavior therapy, which would count the movement as a baseline frequency
Existential therapy, which would link the movement to death anxiety
Gestalt therapy, which builds here-and-now awareness through experiments such as exaggeration

questions.explanation: Gestalt counselors use experiments like exaggeration to heighten present-moment awareness of how a behavior expresses current experience. Adlerian work would fold the behavior into lifestyle interpretation, behavior therapy would measure it as data, and existential work would address ultimate concerns. Deliberate exaggeration for awareness is a Gestalt experiment.

questions.question: Treating self-awareness as a professional competency means viewing it as what?

answers.text: A trait counselors either possess at graduation or lack permanently
An ongoing practice of reflection, feedback, and supervision across the counselor's career
A private matter with no bearing on client outcomes
A requirement satisfied by completing one personal therapy course

questions.explanation: Self-awareness develops continuously through reflection, client feedback, supervision, and personal work, because new clients and life stages keep activating new material. It is neither fixed at graduation nor a one-time credential, and it directly affects the quality clients experience.

aswb-clinical.quiz_title: ASWB Clinical Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Before a joint meeting that includes her probation officer, a court-involved client assumes everything said will stay in therapy. What should the clinician do FIRST?

answers.text: Promise the client the officer will keep the discussion confidential
Ask the officer to leave the room whenever treatment topics arise
Let the meeting proceed and clarify afterward if problems arise
Explain before the meeting what may be shared with the officer, what the officer may do with it, and what choices the client has about participating

questions.explanation: NASW Standard 1.07 requires clarifying, before disclosure occurs, who will receive information and how it may be used, especially where a third party's duties differ from the clinician's. The officer cannot promise therapeutic confidentiality, excluding the officer defeats the meeting's purpose, and after-the-fact clarification comes too late.

questions.question: Stabilized after months of skills work, a client with complex trauma tells her clinician she is not ready to construct a trauma narrative and wants to continue stabilization-focused work. The clinician believes narrative work is eventually indicated. The clinician should:

answers.text: Explain that treatment cannot continue unless she follows the model's sequence
Begin narrative work gradually without labeling it, so she adjusts
Schedule the narrative work and let her cancel if she objects
Respect her pacing, continue the stabilization work she chooses, and revisit readiness together over time

questions.explanation: Pacing in trauma treatment belongs substantially to the client; forcing or disguising exposure undermines safety and consent under NASW Code of Ethics 1.02 and trauma-informed practice. Ultimatums convert a clinical recommendation into a condition of care, unlabeled exposure is deception about the treatment itself, and pre-scheduling puts the burden of refusal on the client at every step.

questions.question: A burst pipe soaks a storage room of archived paper charts, many past their active use but within retention periods. The practice should:

answers.text: Secure and salvage what can be saved, and document any destruction of unsalvageable records according to retention law and policy
Use the flood as an occasion to discard all archived charts
Leave the wet charts to dry in an open hallway
Scan the damaged charts to a personal cloud account for safekeeping

questions.explanation: Damaged records remain confidential records: salvage, secure handling, and documented, rule-compliant destruction protect both privacy and legal retention duties. Wholesale discarding destroys records the practice must keep, open drying exposes contents, and personal cloud storage removes records from controlled systems.

questions.question: Adopted across cultures as an infant and raised without contact with her community of origin, an adult client wants to explore that heritage but fears betraying her adoptive family. The clinician should:

answers.text: Discourage exploration because it usually destabilizes adoptive bonds
Support her exploration at her own pace, treating curiosity about origins as a legitimate identity task
Require a family session with her adoptive parents before she begins
Interpret the wish as evidence of unresolved attachment disorder

questions.explanation: Identity formation can include reclaiming a heritage from which a person was separated; the clinician's role is support, not gatekeeping. Discouragement protects one bond by suppressing another part of identity, mandatory family sessions make her exploration conditional on others' comfort, and pathologizing the wish medicalizes a developmental task.

questions.question: During a crisis assessment, a client who lost housing this week is panicked, sleepless, and unable to outline next steps, though she managed a household and job for years before. Which interpretation is MOST sound?

answers.text: Her reaction reveals a lifelong pattern of poor coping
Panic after housing loss indicates a primary anxiety disorder
Her prior functioning was likely overstated by history
Acute crisis can temporarily overwhelm established coping in a previously well-functioning person

questions.explanation: Crisis theory holds that acute disequilibrium can swamp ordinarily adequate coping for a limited period. Lifelong-deficit, instant-diagnosis, or history-dismissing readings each convert a situational collapse into a trait or disorder.

questions.question: Ten days after a severe assault, Marcus has intrusive memories, nightmares, avoidance, negative mood, and hypervigilance that began within a day of the event. Which diagnosis is MOST accurate now?

answers.text: Posttraumatic stress disorder
Adjustment disorder with anxiety
Acute stress disorder
Generalized anxiety disorder

questions.explanation: Acute stress disorder covers trauma symptoms lasting from three days to one month after a qualifying trauma, and Marcus is at ten days with symptoms across intrusion, avoidance, mood, and arousal clusters. Posttraumatic stress disorder requires duration of more than one month, so it is premature at ten days. Adjustment disorder is excluded when the stressor and symptom pattern meet criteria for a trauma disorder. Generalized anxiety disorder involves six months of excessive worry about multiple domains, not an acute post-trauma syndrome.

questions.question: Vera, 30, has severe ambivalence about substance-use treatment; she attends intake but rejects homework-based approaches and says she may not return. Which sequencing is BEST?

answers.text: Assign a structured homework program immediately
Begin with motivational work to resolve ambivalence before skills-heavy treatment
Discharge her for low motivation
Start with confrontational group feedback

questions.explanation: High ambivalence predicts dropout from action-oriented treatment, so resolving ambivalence and building intrinsic motivation comes first in the sequence. Immediate homework demands and confrontational feedback amplify the ambivalence, and discharging her treats a treatable engagement problem as disqualification.

questions.question: An insurer's reviewer questions continued therapy for a client whose scores improved but who still cannot work full shifts due to panic. Which documentation BEST supports continued care?

answers.text: A statement that the client enjoys therapy and wishes to continue
Copies of every session note since intake with no summary
A diagnosis list alone, since diagnosis establishes necessity
Current functional impairments, treatment response so far, specific remaining goals, and the plan and expected timeframe to reach them

questions.explanation: Utilization review turns on documented function, response, and a forward plan, which is how policy requirements shape clinical documentation. Enjoyment of therapy is not a necessity criterion, an unsummarized record dump buries the relevant facts, and a diagnosis without functional impact does not justify a level or duration of care.

questions.question: Feedback in a new interpersonal group has turned global and personal ('you're just needy'). Which norm should the leader teach and model?

answers.text: Feedback that is specific, behavioral, and about the here-and-now interaction, offered after checking the receiver is ready to hear it
Feedback only about events members describe from outside the group
Feedback delivered anonymously in writing to avoid discomfort
Feedback reserved for the leader, since members are not therapists

questions.explanation: Interpersonal group learning depends on feedback about observable in-room behavior, given with attention to the receiver's readiness. Outside events cannot be examined live by the group, anonymity removes the relational learning feedback creates, and restricting feedback to the leader wastes the group's central therapeutic resource — each other.

questions.question: Two sessions into couples therapy for 'communication problems,' one partner privately reports being afraid to disagree at home, describes monitoring of her movements, and begs the therapist not to repeat this. What should the therapist do NEXT?

answers.text: Raise her disclosure in the next joint session so both can address it openly
Pause conjoint work, assess safety with her individually, and shift to individual support and safety planning rather than couples techniques
Continue couples therapy but focus on neutral topics
Teach her assertiveness skills to use with her partner at home

questions.explanation: Disclosed coercive control and fear make conjoint therapy unsafe; the work becomes individual safety assessment and planning. Repeating her disclosure in session exposes her to retaliation, neutral-topic couples work pretends the central danger is absent, and assertiveness coaching sends her to practice skills against a partner she fears, which can raise risk.

questions.question: A utilization reviewer questions whether a client's continued intensive outpatient level of care is supported. What is the MOST appropriate basis for the review decision?

answers.text: Whether the treating clinician has a long-standing relationship with the client
Documented symptoms, functional impairment, and progress measured against established level-of-care criteria, discussed clinician-to-clinician when needed
Whether the program currently has empty seats to fill
Whether the client's family prefers the higher level of care

questions.explanation: Utilization review rests on documented clinical need weighed against explicit level-of-care criteria, with peer discussion available when documentation and judgment diverge. Length of the treatment relationship is not a necessity criterion, census pressure is a financial consideration that must not drive clinical decisions, and family preference informs care planning but cannot substitute for documented need.

questions.question: A specialty clinic's waiting list now holds 90 names, some added eight months ago, with no contact since intake. What is the MOST responsible waitlist management practice?

answers.text: Close the list permanently so no one else can join it
Serve clients strictly in order of referral date regardless of changing risk
Re-triage the list at set intervals, contact waiting clients to update risk and need, offer interim supports or alternatives, and remove those who no longer need or want the service
Charge a fee to remain on the list so only serious clients stay

questions.explanation: Waiting clients' risk and circumstances change, so responsible management periodically re-triages, maintains contact, and offers interim options rather than treating the list as static. Permanent closure denies access to everyone new, rigid first-come order ignores deteriorating risk, and a holding fee rations care by ability to pay rather than need.

aswb-masters.quiz_title: ASWB Masters Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An agency wants a culture that supports self-care. Which policy change BEST reflects that goal?

answers.text: A poster reminding staff that self-care is their sole responsibility
Requiring staff to log personal wellness activities for review
Awarding prizes for never taking sick days
Protected lunch breaks, realistic caseload standards, and leadership modeling of leave use

questions.explanation: Organizational self-care support, per NASW guidance, is structural: time, workload, and modeled norms. Posters that individualize the issue change nothing material. Monitoring private wellness activity is intrusive. Rewarding unused sick leave discourages recovery and spreads illness.

questions.question: A client who submits claims herself asks the practitioner to list a different, better-reimbursed service on her superbill than the one provided. What should the practitioner do?

answers.text: Comply, because the client bears responsibility for her own claims
Refuse to give her any superbill in the future
Provide a superbill that accurately describes the services, dates, and diagnoses supported by the record, and explain why it cannot be altered
Change the dates instead, which is less serious

questions.explanation: Standard 1.13 and Standard 5.01 make the practitioner responsible for the accuracy of documents she issues, whoever submits them; a knowingly false superbill is participation in misrepresentation. Withholding future superbills punishes the client for asking, and substituting a different falsehood does not reduce the dishonesty.

questions.question: A private-practice client is surprised at her third session by a cancellation fee and an out-of-network deductible never mentioned earlier. What standard was breached?

answers.text: Fees may be introduced whenever the practice updates its policies
Fees, billing practices, and payment expectations must be disclosed and agreed as part of informed consent before services begin
Surprise charges are acceptable if they are customary in the area
Clients are responsible for discovering all fees on their own

questions.explanation: Responsible billing begins with transparent fee disclosure clients can weigh before committing to care. Custom and later policy changes do not substitute for the advance agreement the standard requires.

questions.question: A supervisee hides a documentation mistake from her supervisor, who also writes her annual evaluation, fearing it will end her career. The dynamic MOST illustrates how:

answers.text: Supervisees generally prefer to work without oversight
Documentation errors are too minor to discuss in supervision
Evaluative power can suppress the disclosure supervision needs in order to protect clients
Supervisors should never evaluate their own supervisees

questions.explanation: When the same person judges performance and receives disclosures, power predictably chills the openness that safe practice depends on. Nothing suggests a preference against oversight, error disclosure is exactly what supervision exists for, and separating evaluation from supervision entirely is neither required nor the dynamic described.

questions.question: A client's supervisor has warned him about Monday absences; his wife reports he drinks nightly until he falls asleep, has tried to cut down twice, and becomes irritable and shaky on mornings he does not drink. Taken together, these details indicate:

answers.text: Indicators of an alcohol use problem, including unsuccessful efforts to cut down, role impairment, and possible withdrawal symptoms
Normal social drinking that his wife is exaggerating
A sleep disorder that explains every reported feature
That he simply needs a less demanding job

questions.explanation: Failed attempts to cut down, drinking to the point of passing out, occupational consequences, and morning tremor and irritability suggesting withdrawal form a convergent picture of problematic alcohol use. Social drinking does not produce this constellation. A sleep disorder cannot explain the drinking pattern or withdrawal signs, and job stress does not account for the physiological features.

questions.question: Before asking a new client about alcohol and drug use, a practitioner says, "I ask everyone about this because it affects health and planning." This preamble serves to:

answers.text: Guarantee the client will answer fully
Satisfy a billing requirement for the session
Test whether the client is paying attention
Normalize the inquiry and reduce the sense of being singled out or judged

questions.explanation: A normalizing preamble frames sensitive questions as routine and purposeful, lowering defensiveness. It cannot guarantee candor, is not a billing device, and is not an attention test.

questions.question: Evidence on modality selection for moderate-to-severe major depression generally supports:

answers.text: Psychotherapy alone in all cases regardless of severity
Delaying any treatment until one modality clearly outperforms the other
Supportive listening only, avoiding referral for medication evaluation
Considering combined medication and psychotherapy, coordinated between prescriber and therapist

questions.explanation: For moderate-to-severe depression, combined pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy is commonly supported and requires coordination between prescriber and therapist. Insisting on one modality for every severity, delaying treatment pending perfect comparative evidence, and withholding medication evaluation all under-serve a severity level where combination treatment is a standard consideration.

questions.question: Trying a small step comes next after a client agrees to make one phone call about childcare before the following visit, with a review of what happened. The main purpose of that review step is to:

answers.text: Determine whether the client complied with the worker's instructions
Learn from the attempt, including partial success or obstacles, and adjust the plan accordingly
Assign a grade to the client's effort for the progress note
Confirm that the original problem definition was correct all along

questions.explanation: Problem solving is iterative: trying a manageable action generates information that refines the next step, whether the attempt succeeded, partly worked, or revealed barriers. Framing review as compliance checking or grading turns learning into surveillance, and the attempt may legitimately show the problem definition itself needs revision.

questions.question: Screening a primary care patient, a worker uses a brief validated questionnaire about drinking quantity and consequences, then discusses the score with the patient. This activity is part of:

answers.text: Diagnosis of alcohol use disorder by questionnaire alone
A legal determination of intoxication
Mandatory reporting
Screening within a brief intervention and referral framework using a validated tool and feedback

questions.explanation: Validated brief screening with feedback to the patient is the screening step of evidence-based brief intervention practice. A questionnaire alone does not establish a diagnosis, a legal finding, or a reportable event.

questions.question: Applying for replacement benefit cards, confirming a pharmacy transfer, and verifying a bus pass are all arranged before a patient leaves a psychiatric unit. Attending to these details in discharge planning prevents:

answers.text: Continuity failures in the first days after discharge, when lapsed basics can undo clinical stabilization
The need for any follow-up appointment after discharge
Disagreement among team members about the discharge date
The patient from ever requiring readmission in the future

questions.explanation: Discharge succeeds or fails on logistics: medication access, benefits, and transportation gaps in the first days are common, preventable drivers of rapid deterioration. Practical continuity supports rather than replaces follow-up, it does not settle team disagreements, and no planning can guarantee against readmission.

questions.question: Instead of counting only how many clients were served, funder guidelines require a shelter program to report how many residents moved into stable housing and remained housed six months later. The funder is emphasizing what?

answers.text: Outputs that tally service volume
Inputs such as staff hours and budget size
Outcomes reflecting lasting change in client status
Activities performed during staff training

questions.explanation: Stable placement and retention represent outcomes, meaning durable changes in client condition attributable to the program's purpose. Service counts are outputs, staff and budget resources are inputs, and training tasks are activities; none of these show lasting client-level change.

questions.question: Staff at a rural program regularly drive clients to medical appointments in personal cars, sometimes for hours, with no agency guidance. Which policy response BEST minimizes the risk involved?

answers.text: Set clear requirements for approved drivers and vehicles, verified insurance, trip authorization, and what to do in an emergency
Advise staff informally to drive carefully and avoid discussing the arrangement
Require clients to sign a note absolving the agency of any responsibility
Ban clients from attending appointments that require transportation

questions.explanation: Client transportation policies reduce risk by defining driver and vehicle standards, insurance verification, authorization, and emergency procedures. Informal advice leaves the exposure unmanaged, a client waiver does not substitute for safe practice, and denying appointment access harms clients instead of managing the risk.

nremt-paramedic.quiz_title: NREMT Paramedic Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: During an interfacility transfer, a ventilated patient now opens his eyes to command, follows instructions, and has a strong voluntary cough with good spontaneous tidal volumes. What do these combined cues indicate?

answers.text: He has failed ventilation and needs a surgical airway now
He should be deeply sedated again before any assessment
He requires an immediate increase in his paralytic dose
He is approaching readiness for a trial of extubation

questions.explanation: Correct answer: He is approaching readiness for a trial of extubation. Extubation readiness is a bundle of cues, not one number: neurologic ability to follow commands, airway protection shown by a strong cough, and adequate spontaneous breathing. The receiving team uses these trends to time a spontaneous breathing trial rather than pulling the tube on a single sign.

questions.question: A patient with a confirmed STEMI has an oxygen saturation of 97% on room air and no respiratory distress. What is the correct oxygen decision?

answers.text: Apply oxygen at 15 liters per minute by nonrebreather mask
Withhold supplemental oxygen and monitor the saturation
Apply oxygen at 6 liters per minute by nasal cannula
Place the patient on CPAP for the entire transport

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Withhold supplemental oxygen and monitor the saturation. Withhold supplemental oxygen and monitor the saturation. Oxygen in acute coronary syndrome is a drug for hypoxemia; routine oxygen in a normoxic patient offers no benefit and hyperoxia may worsen outcomes, so it is given only when saturation is low or distress is present.

questions.question: Dopamine is ordered at 5 micrograms per kilogram per minute for an 80 kg adult with symptomatic bradycardia. What total dose per minute must the infusion deliver?

answers.text: 400 micrograms per minute, from 5 times the 80 kg weight
80 micrograms per minute, from 1 times the 80 kg weight
800 micrograms per minute, from 10 times the 80 kg weight
200 micrograms per minute, from 2.5 times the 80 kg weight

questions.explanation: Correct answer: 400 micrograms per minute, from 5 times the 80 kg weight. Worked dose: 5 mcg/kg/min x 80 kg = 400 mcg/min. Weight-based infusions are always converted to a total dose per minute first, then to a pump rate from the bag concentration, so a decimal slip in either step is caught at the other.

questions.question: During procedural sedation of a spontaneously breathing patient who is receiving supplemental oxygen, which monitor usually warns of hypoventilation earliest?

answers.text: Continuous waveform capnography showing rising values
Pulse oximetry, which falls within a few seconds
The blood pressure cuff cycling every five minutes
Skin color changes observed across the procedure room

questions.explanation: Continuous waveform capnography showing rising values. With supplemental oxygen, saturation can stay normal while ventilation fails; capnography reveals hypoventilation and rising carbon dioxide promptly, which is why it is a procedural-sedation monitoring standard alongside a dedicated observer, suction, and airway equipment.

questions.question: A 70 kg adult is being treated for methanol poisoning, and fomepizole is ordered at a loading dose of 15 mg per kilogram IV. How many milligrams make up the loading dose?

answers.text: 350 mg, from 5 times the 70 kg weight
700 mg, from 10 times the 70 kg weight
1,050 mg, from 15 times the 70 kg weight
1,500 mg, given as a fixed loading dose for all adults

questions.explanation: Correct answer: 1,050 mg, from 15 times the 70 kg weight. Worked arithmetic: 15 mg/kg x 70 kg = 1,050 mg. Fomepizole blocks alcohol dehydrogenase, preventing methanol from being converted into its toxic metabolites (formic acid) while the parent compound is cleared, ideally alongside haemodialysis in significant poisonings. The loading dose is strictly weight-based, so the fixed-dose and lower per-kilogram options underdose this patient.

questions.question: A haemodynamically unstable patient has just been found to have a ruptured ectopic pregnancy. A junior colleague asks whether methotrexate could avoid surgery. What is correct?

answers.text: Yes; methotrexate works faster in unstable patients than in stable ones
Methotrexate is preferred whenever the ectopic has already ruptured
