A loan guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs
Lets the lender demand the full balance on default
Pre-approval is a verified commitment; pre-qualification is an estimate

questions.explanation: Describing a loan's approval process as evaluating the borrower's credit and the collateral identifies underwriting. A loan guaranteed by the veterans' agency describes a specific loan program, demanding the full balance on default is an acceleration clause, and the pre-approval versus pre-qualification distinction concerns borrower screening terms rather than the underwriting evaluation itself.

questions.question: In a discussion of breach and remedies, which statement is TRUE?

answers.text: Death never affects contractual duties
New laws never excuse contracts
Impracticability requires extreme, unforeseen difficulty
The promisor must still perform after destruction

questions.explanation: Impracticability excuses performance only when an extreme and unforeseen difficulty makes performance essentially impossible, not merely harder or more expensive. Death can affect contractual duties, new laws can excuse performance they make illegal, and destruction of the subject matter can relieve the promisor, so the absolute statements fail.

questions.question: Scenario: A buyer signs a written offer and the seller signs acceptance without changes. Which contract concept best describes this situation?

answers.text: Listing commission
Earnest money
Bilateral contract
Counteroffer

questions.explanation: When a seller accepts a buyer's written offer without changes, each side has promised to perform, which is a bilateral contract. It is not a counteroffer because nothing was changed, and commission and earnest money are related subjects rather than the name for this two-sided promise structure.

questions.question: Regarding this situation — Joseph Weber tells a Ridgemont seller about a higher backup offer. — all of the following are correct about Duty of disclosure EXCEPT:

answers.text: The principal decides with full information
Material facts shape decisions
Agents may hide defects to protect deals
All offers must be disclosed to the seller

questions.explanation: Agents may not hide defects to protect deals, because known defects are material facts the duty of disclosure requires them to reveal to the principal, making the hiding claim the exception. The principal is entitled to decide with full information, material facts shape decisions, and all offers must be disclosed to the seller.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Termite and wood-destroying insect disclosure?

answers.text: A New Jersey seller disclosing aluminum wiring
A New Jersey seller disclosing a fence dispute
A New Jersey seller disclosing septic age and condition
A New Jersey seller disclosing termite treatment records

questions.explanation: Disclosing termite treatment records is the example because it directly concerns wood-destroying insects and their treatment history. Aluminum wiring, a fence dispute, and septic age and condition are each different disclosure subjects, not termite disclosure.

questions.question: Scenario: Dorothy Pruitt explains the lender's policy to an Oakdale borrower. Regarding Lender's title policy, the legal result is: A lender's title policy protects the lender's lien priority and validity. Why does this result follow?

answers.text: Because idem sonans rules forgive minor variations
Because personal debts are not title links
Because the lender's risk shrinks with the balance
Because the record must link the correction to the original

questions.explanation: The lender's policy protects the lien because the lender's exposure is tied to the loan: as the balance is paid down, the lender's risk and policy amount shrink, leaving coverage matched to the remaining lien. Name-variation rules, personal debts as title links, and linking a correction to the original deed concern other title matters.

questions.question: Which statement about Open listing is true under New Jersey law?

answers.text: Open listings pay all brokers
Open listings pay whoever procures
Wholesalers must hold a broker license
Amendments are effective when one party signs

questions.explanation: An open listing pays the broker who is the procuring cause of the sale, and only that broker, rather than every broker who showed the property. Wholesaling licensure addresses a different activity than the open listing's payment rule, and an amendment binds only when all parties to the agreement sign it.

questions.question: A rental property in Ridgemont has gross monthly rent of $1,800 and similar properties sell at a gross rent multiplier of 125. What is the indicated sale price?
questions.explanation: The gross rent multiplier method multiplies monthly rent by the multiplier: $1,800 times 125 equals $225,000. The other figures come from arithmetic slips, such as using a slightly higher or lower multiplier, and do not match the stated rent and multiplier.

questions.question: Scenario: A homeowner sells her own house without a broker and without a license. Which statement correctly describes the homeowner’s position under New Jersey law?

answers.text: Hosting open houses and discussing terms for another's property is brokerage activity requiring a license
A salesperson (referral) must include on all advertisements, except business cards, the clear and conspicuous statement: 'Services limited to referring prospects to broker'
A licensee may not advertise another broker's exclusive listing without that broker's prior written consent
An owner selling or leasing the owner's own property is exempt from licensure

questions.explanation: An owner selling or leasing the owner's own property is exempt from licensure, because the licensing law governs acting for another. Hosting open houses and discussing terms for another's property describes activity that does require a license, not the owner's position; the referral salesperson advertising statement concerns a limited licensee's advertising, not an owner selling her own home; and the ban on advertising another broker's exclusive listing without written consent concerns licensee advertising, not the owner's exemption.

questions.question: Which statement about MLS is true under New Jersey law?

answers.text: MLS rules are optional
MLS participation follows rules
The municipality exception applies only to magazine or newspaper ads published under municipality headings
Dual broker affiliation is prohibited for referral licensees

questions.explanation: MLS participation is rule-bound: a participant takes part under the multiple listing service's rules rather than treating them as optional. The municipality-heading exception concerns print advertising identification, and referral-licensee affiliation limits concern a different license type; neither displaces the rule that MLS participation follows MLS rules.

georgia-real-estate.quiz_title: Georgia Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: A federal estate tax lien attaches

answers.text: Only to cash accounts
To property in the gross estate
To neighboring parcels
After 50 years

questions.explanation: The federal estate tax lien attaches to property in the decedent's gross estate to secure the estate tax. It is not limited to cash accounts, because real and personal property in the estate are covered; it does not reach neighboring parcels that were never part of the estate; it attaches at death rather than arising only after 50 years.

questions.question: A Marietta apartment complex has potential gross income of $200,000, a 10% vacancy rate, and operating expenses of $60,000. Capitalized at 7%, the indicated value by the income approach is closest to
questions.explanation: Effective gross income is $180,000 after the 10% vacancy loss, net operating income is $120,000 after $60,000 in expenses, and $120,000 divided by 7% gives $1,714,286. $1,731,429 is $17,143 too high; $1,697,143 is $17,143 too low; $1,748,572 is $34,286 too high.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE?

answers.text: Seller financing should use a note and security instrument.
A loan commitment is not the lender's promise to fund.
A payment cap cannot cause negative amortization.
The secondary market does not give lenders liquidity.

questions.explanation: Seller financing should truly use a note and a security instrument, so the debt and the lien securing it are both documented. The loan-commitment statement is false because a commitment is the lender's promise to fund; the payment-cap statement is false because a payment cap can cause negative amortization when the payment does not cover interest; the secondary-market statement is false because that market does give lenders liquidity by letting them sell loans.

questions.question: Nadia asks about contract law. Which of the following correctly states the rule?

answers.text: An 'as-is' sale still does not need the seller's honest disclosure.
A counteroffer does not create a new offer.
An 'as-is' sale still needs the seller's honest disclosure.
Fraud makes a contract automatically void.

questions.explanation: An as-is sale still needs the seller's honest disclosure, because selling as-is does not excuse concealing known material defects. Saying an as-is sale still does not need honest disclosure is wrong for that same reason, since the disclosure duty survives the as-is term; saying a counteroffer does not create a new offer is wrong because a counteroffer is itself a new offer that rejects the original; saying fraud makes a contract automatically void is wrong because fraud makes the contract voidable at the wronged party's election.

questions.question: A $542,000 transaction at 6% produces a total commission of $32,520. If split evenly, each side receives
questions.explanation: The exact equal share is $16,260 because the stated total commission of $32,520 divided by two is $16,260. $32,520 is $16,260 above the exact result because it is the unsplit total; $19,512 is $3,252 above the exact result; $13,008 is $3,252 below the exact result.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE?

answers.text: HOA info is irrelevant.
Future developments near a property can never affect its value or desirability.
Only facts about the property itself can be material; projects planned nearby are not.
Future developments may be material.

questions.explanation: Future developments may be material, because a planned project near a property can change its use, value, and desirability. The claim that homeowners association information is irrelevant is wrong because dues, rules, and assessments affect cost and use; the claim that a related principle applies in every transaction states no substantive rule at all; the claim that the opposite principle governs this situation likewise states no substantive rule at all.

questions.question: Which of these statements about real estate practice is accurate?

answers.text: The relocation department is regularly balancing escrow records against bank statements
Oral leases for a year or less are generally enforceable.
Boot received in an exchange is never taxable.
Capital gains on a home sale can never be excluded.

questions.explanation: Oral leases for a year or less are generally enforceable because the writing requirement for real estate contracts reaches leases longer than one year. Calling the relocation department the activity of regularly balancing escrow records against bank statements splices a business unit together with trust-account reconciliation, which is a broker accounting duty; boot received in an exchange can be taxable, so saying it is never taxable is wrong; capital gains on a home sale can be excluded within the principal-residence limits, so saying they can never be excluded is wrong.

questions.question: Jordan sells a home in Marietta for $195,000. The mortgage payoff is $130,000, the brokerage commission is 7.0% of the sale price, and other closing costs total $3,300. What are the seller's approximate net proceeds?
questions.explanation: The seller's net is the $195,000 sale price minus the $13,650 commission (7% of the price), the $130,000 mortgage payoff, and $3,300 in other closing costs, which comes to $48,050. The $61,700 figure leaves out the $13,650 commission entirely, overstating the net by $13,650; the $54,650 figure adds the $3,300 in other closing costs instead of subtracting them, overstating the net by $6,600; the $178,050 figure leaves out the $130,000 mortgage payoff entirely, overstating the net by $130,000.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Georgia real estate license law is FALSE?

answers.text: Georgia licensees must disclose dual agency and obtain written consent.
The landlord's lien is the instrument conveying foreclosed property to the purchaser
No person may receive more than $25,000 from the fund in a lifetime.
The salesperson exam allows 4 hours of testing time.

questions.explanation: The false statement pairs the landlord's lien with the instrument conveying foreclosed property to the purchaser, because that instrument is the deed given after a foreclosure sale, not a landlord's lien. Dual agency requires disclosure and written consent, no person may receive more than $25,000 from the fund in a lifetime, and the salesperson exam allows four hours.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Georgia real estate practice is TRUE?

answers.text: A Georgia manager must not report income and expenses to the owner.
A Georgia buyer's agent who shows 20 homes and writes the offer is not the procuring cause.
A Georgia buyer who does not terminate in due diligence generally gets earnest money back.
A Georgia inspection objection should be delivered before the deadline.

questions.explanation: An inspection objection should be delivered before the deadline is true, because objections delivered late lose the contract's inspection protection. A manager must report income and expenses to the owner, a buyer's agent who shows twenty homes and writes the offer can be the procuring cause, and a buyer who does not terminate during due diligence does not generally recover the earnest money, so those statements are false.

questions.question: An Athens broker drives a buyer to see five listings; no written agreement exists. When the buyer asks which home is the best investment, the broker

answers.text: Must recommend the best investment
Must not give investment advice; a transaction broker performs only ministerial acts
Must refuse to show more homes
Becomes a dual agent automatically

questions.explanation: Without a written agreement the broker is a transaction broker who performs only ministerial acts, so the broker must not give investment advice or recommend which home is the best investment. Giving such advice would risk creating an agency relationship the parties never agreed to, and the broker neither must stop showing homes nor becomes a dual agent automatically.

questions.question: Andre's Savannah property has an assessed value of $76,000 and the millage rate is 37 mills. The yearly ad valorem tax is closest to
questions.explanation: At 37 mills the tax is 37 dollars for each one thousand dollars of assessed value, so the assessed value of $76,000 yields $2,812.00 exactly. $1,406.00 is $1,406.00 below that exact tax; $7,030.00 is $4,218.00 above that exact tax; $28,120.00 is $25,308.00 above that exact tax.

new-york-real-estate.quiz_title: New York Real Estate FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which term is described as follows: the requirement that the broker's license be conspicuously displayed at the place of business

answers.text: pocket card display
license display
associated licensee
trade name

questions.explanation: The requirement that the broker's license be conspicuously displayed at the place of business is license display. Pocket card display confuses the wall display with the pocket card a licensee carries, an associated licensee is a person affiliated with the broker rather than a display rule, and a trade name is the business name the brokerage operates under rather than a posting requirement.

questions.question: While representing a client, Lily Evans as the property manager in Oneonta, did not provide the tenant with a security deposit accounting. Which duty does this breach?

answers.text: accounting
disclosure
confidentiality
reasonable care

questions.explanation: Failing to provide an accounting of a tenant's security deposit breaches the duty of accounting, which requires a clear accounting for money held for another. The other duties concern revealing material facts, protecting confidences, and exercising competent care, while an unrendered deposit accounting is specifically a failure to account for funds.

questions.question: Under the license regulations, the sponsoring broker's supervision duty means the broker

answers.text: need only review files after a complaint arrives
must supervise the real estate activities of associated licensees and remains responsible for their compliance
may delegate all supervision to an unlicensed manager
supervises only transactions over $1 million

questions.explanation: The sponsoring broker must supervise the real estate activities of associated licensees and remains responsible for their compliance with license law. Reviewing files only after a complaint arrives is reactive rather than ongoing supervision, delegating all supervision to an unlicensed manager abdicates a broker duty, and supervising only transactions over $1 million wrongly limits supervision by price when associated licensees must be supervised generally.

questions.question: Which statement about recording practice is TRUE?

answers.text: A lis pendens is recorded to warn the public that litigation affects title to the parcel.
A lis pendens is recorded to pay taxes.
A lis pendens is recorded to transfer ownership.
A lis pendens is recorded to create an easement.

questions.explanation: A lis pendens is a recorded notice warning the public that litigation is pending that affects title to the parcel, so a buyer takes with notice of the suit. It does not pay taxes, transfer ownership, or create an easement.

questions.question: A property closes at $805,000. If the brokerage's commission is 5.0% of the closing price, what amount does the brokerage earn?
questions.explanation: The brokerage earns 5.0% of $805,000, which is $805,000 times 0.05, or $40,250. The other choices are wrong for distinct reasons: $36,225 is 4.5% of the price; $44,275 is 5.5% of the price; and $32,200 is 4.0% of the price.

questions.question: A unilateral mistake by one party to a contract generally

answers.text: always voids the contract
doubles the damages
is a criminal matter
does not excuse performance unless the other party knew or should have known of the mistake

questions.explanation: A unilateral mistake generally does not excuse performance unless the other party knew or should have known of the mistake. It does not automatically void the contract, double the damages, or create a criminal matter.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines "loan estimate"?

answers.text: a closed-end second mortgage on the equity of the borrower
the federal form disclosing estimated loan terms and costs within three business days of application
the mortgage insurance premium on FHA loans
a loan with a lower rate in exchange for a share of appreciation

questions.explanation: A loan estimate is the federal disclosure form that gives a borrower estimated loan terms and costs within three business days after application. A closed-end second mortgage describes a home equity loan product, the mortgage insurance premium belongs to federal housing loans, and a loan trading a lower rate for a share of appreciation is a shared appreciation mortgage.

questions.question: A building lot is 80 feet wide and 410 feet deep. What is its area in acres, rounded to two decimal places?

answers.text: 0.68 acres
0.75 acres
0.83 acres
0.60 acres

questions.explanation: The lot contains eighty feet times four hundred ten feet, which is thirty-two thousand eight hundred square feet, and dividing by forty-three thousand five hundred sixty square feet per acre gives zero point seven five acres when rounded to two decimal places. Zero point six eight acres and zero point six zero acres each understate the quotient, and zero point eight three acres overstates it.

questions.question: True or false: A deck ledger attaches the deck to the house.

answers.text: True only for new homes
False
Cannot be determined
True

questions.explanation: A deck ledger does attach the deck to the house, transferring the deck's load to the house structure, so the statement is true. That function is not limited to new homes, denying the attachment is false, and the ledger's function can be determined rather than being indeterminate.

questions.question: True or false: Brokerage services must not be denied by protected class.

answers.text: True
True only in New York
Cannot be determined
False

questions.explanation: The statement is true: brokerage services must not be denied because of a person's protected class, under fair housing law generally and in New York. It is not a New York-only rule, and it is a settled prohibition rather than something that cannot be determined.

questions.question: Total common-area maintenance charges for a shopping center are $680,000 for the year. One tenant's proportionate share is 13.5%. What is that tenant's annual share of the charges?
questions.explanation: The tenant's share is thirteen point five percent of $680,000, which equals $91,800. The $82,620 figure understates that percentage share, $100,980 overstates it, and $73,440 understates it by an even wider margin.

questions.question: Before-tax cash flow of $68,000 on a cash investment of $420,000 is a cash-on-cash return of
questions.explanation: $68,000 / $420,000 = about 16.19%, the before-tax cash-on-cash return. 8.10% is roughly half the correct rate, 14.19% understates the quotient, and 18.19% overstates it.

texas-insurance.quiz_title: Texas Insurance FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: An insured is deciding between forms and wants coverage that looks to the year the injury happens, even if claims emerge years later. Which form identity matches that preference?

answers.text: The occurrence form
The claims-made form
The medical payments form
The reporting-endorsement form

questions.explanation: The occurrence form keys coverage to injury or damage during the policy period regardless of when the claim later emerges. The claims-made form keys coverage to when the claim is first made, which is a different selection rule.

questions.question: While a tenant is away, a landlord's agent enters the leased apartment without permission or emergency justification to show it to prospective renters. Which Coverage B offense is implicated?

answers.text: Slogan infringement
Malicious prosecution
Quality failure exclusion
Wrongful entry into a premises that another occupies

questions.explanation: Entering leased premises the tenant occupies, without right, is wrongful entry, part of the eviction and entry offense group. No legal proceeding or advertisement is involved.

questions.question: An insurer groups many similar small liability losses that have occurred but have not been individually reported and holds one combined estimate for them. That combined estimate is an example of

answers.text: A separate case reserve for each claimant
A bulk reserve
A full release of the group
A high-low settlement range

questions.explanation: A bulk reserve is a single aggregate estimate for a group of losses, often serving the IBNR function. It is not a separate, file-specific case reserve.

questions.question: A masked person uses a weapon to take cash directly from a store clerk, while another person secretly picks a customer's pocket with no confrontation. The first taking, contrasted with secret taking without force, is best defined as which of the following?

answers.text: Burglary
Robbery
Mysterious disappearance
Embezzlement

questions.explanation: Robbery is the taking of property from a person or that person's presence by force or threat of force. Burglary generally involves unlawful entry into premises, and a secret taking without force is theft rather than robbery.

questions.question: A cleaning company knows a client slipped on a freshly mopped floor in March but gives the insurer no notice until the client files suit the following January, reasoning that notice is only due once a lawsuit exists. What is wrong with that reasoning?

answers.text: Nothing, because the duties condition is triggered only by a suit
The January notice is timely because it preceded the trial date
The duty attaches at the occurrence and, if a claim develops, the insured must notify as soon as practicable rather than waiting for suit papers
The company should have notified the client's health insurer instead about the slip and fall, because the client's own health insurer is the party the duties condition requires the company to notify

questions.explanation: The condition covers occurrences and offenses that may result in a claim, and separately covers claims and suits when they arrive. Waiting for a lawsuit to report a known occurrence breaches the earlier, occurrence-based notice duty.

questions.question: One person insured under a homeowners policy deliberately damages covered property, while another insured on the same policy is innocent and files the claim. Standard intentional loss wording is written to apply based on the acts of which person?

answers.text: Only the named insured's acts can ever matter, never any other insured's conduct.
An act of any insured under the policy can trigger the intentional loss exclusion as the standard wording frames it.
Intentional acts are excluded only when committed by a guest.
Intentional loss applies only when both insureds acted together.

questions.explanation: Standard intentional loss language is keyed to acts done by or at the direction of an insured, and is commonly phrased to reach the conduct of any insured. That breadth is precisely what makes the innocent co-insured situation difficult under the standard form.

questions.question: A client says flood pricing should be the same for every house on the street. Which reply best explains current NFIP pricing?

answers.text: Each house is rated on its own risk, so elevation, distance to water, and rebuilding cost can make premiums differ house by house
Every house on a street is legally required to pay the same premium, whether or not the insurer has already made a partial payment on some other part of the same claim
Premiums differ only because agents charge different commissions
Premiums are random and cannot be explained

questions.explanation: Risk Rating 2.0 prices individual property characteristics, so neighboring homes can legitimately differ. Premiums are not street-uniform, commission-driven, or random.

questions.question: A tenant is legally responsible for negligent damage the tenant causes to a landlord's building. That responsibility supports the tenant having an insurable interest in what sense?

answers.text: The tenant becomes owner of the building
Responsibility eliminates the need for the landlord's own policy
The landlord loses all interest in the building
The tenant faces financial loss if the building is damaged through the tenant's responsibility

questions.explanation: Potential liability for damage is a financial stake supporting an interest. It coexists with, rather than replaces, the landlord's ownership interest.

questions.question: A project owner asks, after a covered loss has already occurred and been paid, whether the property insurer will now add a waiver of subrogation protecting the contractor whose negligence caused that loss. What is the realistic answer?

answers.text: The contractor can add the waiver without the insurer
The waiver becomes unnecessary because the loss is paid

Yes, waivers are routinely added retroactively after losses, based on the facts presented and recorded when the claim was submitted for review, and under the terms and conditions stated in the applicable policy form
A waiver of subrogation is arranged before the loss, typically by endorsement for an additional charge; an insurer will not ordinarily surrender an existing recovery right after the loss

questions.explanation: Waivers are prospective bargains priced and endorsed before a loss occurs. After payment, the insurer already holds a valuable recovery right and has no reason to give it away, and the contractor cannot create the waiver unilaterally.

questions.question: Which conviction falls within the guideline's list of serious offenses because it involves a breach of a position of trust?

answers.text: An overdue library fine
A first speeding ticket
A felony involving moral turpitude or breach of fiduciary duty
A misdemeanor littering conviction

questions.explanation: A felony involving moral turpitude or breach of fiduciary duty is expressly listed among the serious offenses in the guideline. The minor matters listed are not.

questions.question: A lender files a claim under a mortgage guaranty policy after a borrower defaults, and later seeks prompt payment damages for slow claim handling. What is the correct response?

answers.text: Those damages do not arise under the prompt payment law, because mortgage guaranty insurance is excepted from its provisions
The prompt payment law covers mortgage guaranty insurance only for loans under $100,000
The damages apply, but at half the usual interest rate
The lender recovers the damages, because mortgage guaranty claims are the law's central subject

questions.explanation: Mortgage guaranty insurance is an express exception to the prompt payment subchapter, so its damages do not apply.

questions.question: A member insurer with large Texas premiums asks for its maximum regular assessment exposure for the year. Which cap applies?

answers.text: Assessments are capped at five percent of net direct written premiums
There is no cap on assessments in any year
Assessments during a calendar year generally may not exceed two percent of the insurer's net direct written premiums for the preceding calendar year in the lines assessed
Assessments are capped at one percent of the insurer's surplus

questions.explanation: The regular calendar-year cap is two percent of the insurer's preceding-year net direct written premiums in the assessed lines.

questions.question: A home health LPN arrives and finds the client's visit note from another agency nurse is missing from the home chart, and the client cannot recall what was taught. What should the LPN do?

answers.text: Assume nothing was taught and start initial teaching yourself
Skip documentation for this visit as well
Contact the agency and RN supervisor to obtain the visit information before proceeding with teaching reinforcement
Ask the client's neighbor what the nurse said

questions.explanation: Continuity in home care depends on shared visit records; the LPN obtains the missing information through the agency rather than guessing. Initial teaching is the RN's role, missing documentation compounds the gap, and a neighbor is not a reliable or confidential source.

questions.question: A client restraint order expired 40 minutes ago, and the client remains in restraints while the LPN notices during rounds. What should the LPN do?

answers.text: Leave the restraints on until the next routine check
Renew the order herself and note it in the chart
Remove the restraints and say nothing further
Notify the RN immediately that the order has expired and follow RN direction about the client status

questions.explanation: Restraints without a current order are a legal and safety problem requiring immediate RN notification. The LPN cannot renew orders, and neither leaving restraints on silently nor removing them without communication addresses the client status lawfully.

questions.question: Which practices protect client confidentiality? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Discussing client details only in private areas with those involved in care
Sharing your password with a trusted coworker during a busy shift
Verifying a fax number before sending client information
Posting a thank-you note from a client with her full name on social media
Shredding printed handoff sheets per policy at shift end

questions.explanation: Private discussion, verifying fax destinations, and secure disposal of printed information protect confidentiality. Passwords are never shared, and posting an identifiable client's name publicly discloses her care relationship without authorization.

questions.question: Case study: At an assisted-living facility in January, three residents on the same wing develop fever of 101.4-101.8 F (38.6-38.8 C), cough, and muscle aches within 24 hours. One resident has just tested positive for influenza A. Several other residents on the wing are over age 80 and have chronic lung or heart disease. The LPN/VN is working under the direction of the RN supervisor. Droplet precautions, cohorting, and symptom monitoring have been in place for 48 hours. Which outcome indicates the measures are effective?

answers.text: All symptomatic residents stopped coughing within one hour of precautions starting
No new residents have developed fever or respiratory symptoms, and symptomatic residents are being monitored with findings reported to the RN
Residents on the wing no longer need hand hygiene because they were cohorted
The facility can stop monitoring because one resident's fever resolved

questions.explanation: Absence of new cases over the monitoring period, with ongoing data collection and reporting, shows transmission is being controlled. Cohorting does not end hand hygiene or monitoring, and symptoms are not expected to vanish within an hour.

questions.question: An LPN/VN collects data on a client who started a new blood pressure medication yesterday and reports dizziness on standing; the sitting blood pressure is notably lower than the client's usual readings. What should the LPN/VN do?

answers.text: Have the client sit or lie down, recheck as directed, and report the dizziness and readings promptly to the RN
Encourage the client to walk the hallway to work through the dizziness
Tell the client dizziness is expected and needs no follow-up
Give an extra dose of the medication to stabilize the pressure

questions.explanation: Dizziness on standing with lower-than-usual readings suggests orthostatic hypotension and a fall risk, so the client should be seated or lying down and the findings reported promptly. Walking it off risks a fall, and changing doses is outside PN scope.

questions.question: The LPN/VN reinforces the RN's teaching to a healthy 70-year-old about maintaining bone health with aging. Which client plan shows correct understanding?

answers.text: I will avoid all exercise because activity wears out aging joints
I will get weight-bearing activity most days and eat calcium-rich foods as my plan outlines
Vitamin D has no role in bone health after age 70
Bed rest during the winter will protect my bones from fractures

questions.explanation: Weight-bearing activity plus adequate calcium (with vitamin D per the plan) slows age-related bone loss. Inactivity and bed rest accelerate bone loss and deconditioning, and vitamin D remains important for calcium absorption in older adults.

questions.question: An Orthodox Jewish client in a rehab unit is served a tray with shrimp and a milk-based dessert alongside meat, and quietly pushes it away uneaten. Which action by the LPN/VN is most appropriate?

answers.text: Encourage the client to eat the meat and simply leave the rest
Remove the tray, report the error to the RN and dietary department so a kosher meal can be provided, and document the missed meal
Tell the client the kitchen cannot accommodate religious diets
Mix the foods together so the client does not notice them

questions.explanation: Kosher dietary laws prohibit shellfish and mixing meat with dairy; the respectful action is to report the tray error so a compliant meal is provided and to document intake. Pressuring the client or concealing the foods violates religious practice and trust.

questions.question: A client with arthritis finds cold packs helpful for a swollen knee but asks to leave one on all afternoon. Which reinforcement by the LPN/VN is correct?

answers.text: Agree that longer cold application always gives more benefit
Tell the client to place the cold pack directly on skin under a tight wrap
Advise alternating cold with a heating pad every 5 minutes all day
Explain cold is applied for limited periods as prescribed, with a barrier and skin checks, and report swelling or skin changes

questions.explanation: Time-limited cold with a barrier and skin monitoring prevents cold injury while relieving swelling. Prolonged or direct tightly wrapped cold damages skin, and rapid unplanned alternation is not the prescribed regimen.

questions.question: A resident taking donepezil for dementia has fainted once and now has a pulse of 48 beats/min. What should the licensed practical nurse do?

answers.text: Give the next donepezil dose early so the level stays steady
Reinforce that fainting is unrelated to memory medication and needs no report
Encourage the resident to get up and walk to raise the pulse
Keep the resident safe in bed, collect vital signs, and report the fainting and slow pulse to the registered nurse promptly

questions.explanation: Donepezil can slow the heart rate and cause fainting, so a pulse of 48 with syncope requires prompt reporting and fall precautions. Giving more drug or ambulating the resident worsens the risk.

questions.question: A client taking phenytoin has swollen, overgrown gums. Which teaching should the licensed practical nurse reinforce?

answers.text: Gum overgrowth means the client should stop brushing to rest the gums
Meticulous oral hygiene and regular dental visits help reduce gum overgrowth, and the finding should be reported
The finding proves the dose is too low and should be increased at home
Only the front teeth are affected, so no report is needed

questions.explanation: Gingival hyperplasia is a known phenytoin effect managed partly with careful oral hygiene and dental care, and it should be reported. Stopping brushing worsens it, and dose changes are the provider's decision.

questions.question: A client is scheduled for pulmonary function tests this afternoon and asks about using his prescribed bronchodilator inhaler this morning. Which response by the LPN is correct?

answers.text: Use it right before the test so the numbers look their best
Use a neighbor's inhaler instead so his own record stays clear
Skip the test if he used the inhaler yesterday
Follow the provider's written instructions about holding the inhaler before the test, because the test measures breathing with and without medication effects as directed

questions.explanation: Pulmonary function testing follows specific instructions about which inhalers to hold and for how long, so results reflect the client's true lung function as the provider intends. Using the inhaler against instructions, or someone else's inhaler, distorts the results and is unsafe.

questions.question: The LPN/VN monitors Mrs. Rosa Delgado, 79, in a skilled nursing facility. Which findings should be reported to the RN as possible cues of sepsis? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Temperature of 101.9 F with a heart rate of 118/min
Respiratory rate of 26/min, increased from her baseline of 16/min
New confusion and difficulty staying awake during conversation
Blood pressure of 92/58 mmHg, down from her usual 138/84 mmHg
A surgical incision that is pink at the edges with mild tenderness on day 2

questions.explanation: Fever with tachycardia, new tachypnea, altered mental status, and a falling blood pressure form the systemic response pattern of sepsis and each element strengthens the need for prompt reporting and evaluation. Mild pinkness and tenderness at a day-2 incision are expected healing findings, not systemic cues.

florida-real-estate.quiz_title: Florida FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: The exam is administered by

answers.text: the FREC
Pearson VUE
the DBPR
a school

questions.explanation: The licensing exam is administered by Pearson VUE, the testing vendor that delivers the examination. It is not administered by the commission, the licensing department itself, or a real estate school.

questions.question: A broker acting as a transaction broker in a commercial deal, where both customers have over $1 million in assets, designates one associate to advocate solely for the buyer. The associate

answers.text: owes fiduciary duties to both sides
acts as a single agent for the buyer, with single-agent duties
is the buyer's dual agent
needs no disclosures to either party

questions.explanation: For a nonresidential transaction where both customers meet the stated asset threshold, the broker may designate one associate to act as a single agent for the buyer, and that associate owes single-agent duties to the buyer. Florida does not permit dual agency, and the designated associate does not owe fiduciary duties to both sides at once.

questions.question: Which of the following means: the FREC's directive on disputed funds?

answers.text: partnership
interpleader
group boycott
Escrow Disbursement Order

questions.explanation: An Escrow Disbursement Order is the Commission's directive telling the broker how to disburse disputed escrow funds. A partnership is a business form, an interpleader is a court action the broker may file instead, and a group boycott is an antitrust violation, so none of those is the Commission's order.

questions.question: A life tenant who mortgages the property

answers.text: cannot mortgage
must get the remainderman's consent always
encumbers only the life-estate interest, not the remainder
encumbers the fee simple

questions.explanation: A life tenant owns only an interest lasting for the measuring life, so a mortgage the tenant grants can encumber only that life-estate interest. It cannot pledge the remainder interest or the fee simple, which belong to others.

questions.question: A buyer signs a developer contract for a new Florida condominium unit on June 23, 2026 and receives all required documents that day. Until when is the agreement voidable by the buyer?
questions.explanation: For a developer sale of a new condominium unit, the buyer may void the contract within fifteen days after signing and receiving all required documents. Counting fifteen days from the late-June signing reaches July eighth. The shorter periods belong to other types of sales, and the longest date exceeds the developer-sale period.

questions.question: A chain of title is

answers.text: a title insurance policy
a lien
a survey
the history of conveyances and encumbrances affecting the property

questions.explanation: A chain of title is the recorded history of conveyances and encumbrances affecting a property, traced from owner to owner. It is a historical record rather than an insurance policy, a lien, or a survey.

questions.question: A rectangular lot 90 feet by 230 feet is valued at $8 per square foot. What is the lot's value?
questions.explanation: The lot area is ninety times two hundred thirty, or twenty thousand seven hundred square feet. At $8 per square foot, the value is $165,600.

questions.question: A buyer offers $350,000 with a 3% earnest money deposit. The deposit is
questions.explanation: Earnest money is a percentage of the offer price: three percent of $350,000 equals $10,500. The other figures double that percentage, halve it, or use a different rate than the one stated.

questions.question: The borrower may reinstate the loan by

answers.text: paying one payment
paying arrears and costs before the foreclosure sale
selling the home
filing bankruptcy only

questions.explanation: A borrower in default can cure and reinstate by paying the past-due amounts plus permitted costs before the foreclosure sale occurs. Paying only one installment leaves other arrears unpaid, and selling the home or filing bankruptcy is not the stated reinstatement method.

questions.question: The best description of 'Freddie Mac' is

answers.text: the party taking the security interest
a multi-property mortgage
a major loan purchaser and securitizer
an interim improvement loan

questions.explanation: Freddie Mac operates in the secondary mortgage market, buying loans from lenders and pooling them into securities. The party taking a security interest is a mortgagee, a multi-property mortgage is a blanket mortgage, and an interim improvement loan is construction financing, none of which describes a major loan purchaser and securitizer.

questions.question: The seller prepaid a $3,650 annual hazard insurance policy. Using a 365-day year, with closing on day 172 (buyer owns closing day), how much does the buyer reimburse the seller for the unused portion?
questions.explanation: The daily insurance amount is $10, found by dividing $3,650 by three hundred sixty-five days, and with the buyer owning the closing day, the unused portion runs for one hundred ninety-four days from day one hundred seventy-two through the end of the year. The buyer therefore reimburses the seller $1,940.

questions.question: Competition holds that

answers.text: excess profit attracts competition, which tends to reduce returns
profits are guaranteed
monopolies raise value
competition is illegal

questions.explanation: Under the principle of competition, excess profit in a market attracts new competition, and that added competition tends to drive returns back down. Profits are therefore not guaranteed, monopolies are not what competition describes, and competition itself is lawful.

nclex-rn.quiz_title: NCLEX-RN FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which elements are part of safe delegation? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Giving clear directions, including what changes must be reported immediately
Delegating the nursing process itself, including initial assessment and care planning
Assuming that once a task is delegated, the RN no longer needs to review the result
Delegating the right task, for the right client, under the right circumstances
Following up to evaluate the outcome of the delegated task

questions.explanation: Safe delegation requires the right task, person, circumstance, communication, and supervision, with RN follow-up and evaluation. The nursing process cannot be delegated, and accountability for reviewing results stays with the RN.

questions.question: A client admitted with a stroke is medically stable, but the team notes the client cannot swallow safely and lives alone. What is the most important next management step?

answers.text: Schedule discharge for tomorrow morning to free the bed for admissions
Ensure swallowing evaluation and discharge planning begin now, including support services, rather than waiting until discharge is imminent
Teach the client to eat slowly and document the teaching as complete
Ask the client's neighbor to check in occasionally after discharge

questions.explanation: Unsafe swallowing plus living alone is a high-risk discharge combination; evaluation and structured planning must start immediately. Rushed discharge, superficial teaching, and informal neighbor checks do not manage aspiration and support risks.

questions.question: Case study: Marcus Bell, age 62, is scheduled for a non-contrast MRI of the lumbar spine for persistent leg pain. Screening notes: he worked 22 years as a sheet-metal fabricator and was treated at age 24 for a metal fragment in his left eye; no eye imaging was ever done afterward. He wears an insulin pump. A transdermal patch with a metallic foil backing is on his upper arm. He carries a card documenting MRI-conditional titanium spinal hardware placed in 2019. He ate breakfast this morning. Which actions should be completed before Mr. Bell's scan proceeds? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Remove the insulin pump, store it as directed, and arrange glucose monitoring during the scan period
Obtain orbital radiographs and documented MRI-safety clearance for the possible retained eye fragment
Leave the foil-backed patch in place but cover it with a thick gauze dressing
Remove the foil-backed patch, clean the skin site, and have Mr. Bell change into approved metal-free clothing
Proceed immediately, because screening is unnecessary for a non-contrast study

questions.explanation: The pump must come off with a glucose-monitoring plan, the possible eye fragment needs orbital imaging and clearance, and the foil-backed patch must be removed with the site cleaned and metal-free clothing confirmed. Covering a foil-backed patch does not remove its heating risk, and screening is required for every MRI regardless of contrast.

questions.question: Case study: Leo M., age 4 years, is brought to a pediatric clinic with 3 days of fever to 103.1 F (39.5 C), cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes, followed today by a blotchy red rash spreading from the hairline down the face and small white spots on the inside of his cheeks. He has received no childhood vaccines. Before being roomed, he spent 45 minutes in the shared waiting room with a 5-month-old infant, a pregnant parent, and a child who is receiving chemotherapy. Which additional findings support the nurse's concern about this situation? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Leo has had no measles-containing vaccine, so he had no protection against this infection
The 5-month-old in the waiting room is younger than the routine age for the first measles vaccine dose
Measles virus can remain infectious in a room's air for up to 2 hours after an infected person leaves
Only children who touched Leo or shared his toys could have been exposed
The child receiving chemotherapy and the pregnant parent are at higher risk for severe measles

questions.explanation: Leo's unvaccinated status, the infant who is too young for routine measles vaccination, the 2-hour persistence of measles virus in air, and the presence of immunocompromised and pregnant contacts all raise the concern. Measles spreads through the air, so direct touch or shared toys are not required for exposure.

questions.question: A sedentary adult client asks how much aerobic activity to aim for each week for substantial health benefits. Which target is correct?

answers.text: 30 minutes of activity once a month
At least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week, plus muscle strengthening twice weekly
Vigorous activity only counts if done for 3 hours at a time
Activity benefits only begin after 1 year of training

questions.explanation: Adults gain substantial benefits from 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity (or 75–150 minutes vigorous) aerobic activity weekly plus twice-weekly muscle strengthening. Benefits begin well before a year, and activity can be accumulated in shorter sessions.

questions.question: A school nurse sees a 7-year-old for the third time this month. The child has bruises in various stages of healing on the torso and upper arms, flinches when an adult raises a hand to reach a shelf, and says a caregiver gets angry when the child spills food. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Ask the child open-ended questions and document statements in the child's own words
Report the findings to the child protective agency as required for suspected abuse
Confront the caregiver in the hallway and demand an explanation
Photograph and document the size, color, and location of each bruise objectively
Promise the child that nothing they say will be shared with anyone

questions.explanation: Objective documentation, non-leading questioning, and mandated reporting are required responses to suspected child abuse. Confronting the caregiver can endanger the child and compromise the investigation, and the nurse cannot promise secrecy because reporting is legally required.

questions.question: A nurse must verify placement of a newly inserted nasogastric tube before the first feeding. Which method is the most reliable initial bedside confirmation strategy?

answers.text: Inject air and listen for a whoosh over the stomach
Confirm with the insertion radiograph as the gold standard, then use aspirate pH testing for ongoing bedside checks
Place the tube end in water and watch for bubbles
Ask the client to speak; a clear voice confirms placement

questions.explanation: Radiographic confirmation is the gold standard before first use of a blindly inserted tube; aspirate pH (typically 5.5 or less for gastric contents) is the accepted ongoing bedside check. The air-whoosh, water-bubbling, and voice tests are unreliable and have all missed misplacements.

questions.question: Shortly after a nurse gives an IV medication by rapid push, a client reports a pounding headache and a feeling of tightness in the chest, feels flushed, and the blood pressure drops. Which complication should the nurse suspect and act on?

answers.text: Speed shock from the medication entering the circulation too quickly; stop further administration, assess airway and circulation, and notify the prescriber
A normal drug effect that should be documented without assessment
Fluid overload from the small push volume, treated by sitting the client up only
An air embolism, treated by placing the client flat on the right side

questions.explanation: Speed shock is a systemic reaction to a drug or solution infused too rapidly, causing headache, flushing, chest tightness, and hypotension. Administration is stopped, the client is assessed and supported, and the prescriber is notified.

questions.question: A nurse is setting up a total parenteral nutrition solution that contains dextrose and amino acids without lipids. Which filter is correct for this solution?

answers.text: No filter is ever used with parenteral nutrition
A filter borrowed from the client's enteral feeding set
A blood filter with a 170-micron screen
A 0.22-micron in-line filter, which is used for non-lipid parenteral nutrition solutions

questions.explanation: Non-lipid parenteral nutrition is infused through a 0.22-micron filter, which removes particulate matter and most bacteria. Lipid-containing admixtures require a larger 1.2-micron filter, and blood or enteral filters are never substituted.

questions.question: A potassium result of 5.7 mEq/L is reported for a comfortable client with a normal ECG. The specimen note says the sample was hemolyzed and difficult to draw. Which action is most appropriate?

answers.text: Give IV insulin and dextrose immediately based on this single result
Assess the client and ECG, notify the provider of the result and the hemolysis, and obtain a careful repeat specimen drawn without prolonged tourniquet time or fist pumping before treating the number
Ignore potassium results for the rest of the admission
Tell the client to stop eating potassium-containing foods permanently

questions.explanation: Hemolysis releases intracellular potassium and commonly causes a falsely high result, so verification with a properly drawn repeat sample (alongside clinical assessment) precedes treatment. Treating a spurious value with insulin can cause dangerous hypoglycemia and hypokalemia.

questions.question: A client with potassium 6.2 mEq/L and no ECG changes is receiving an IV insulin-and-dextrose infusion to shift potassium into cells. Which monitoring is most important during this therapy?

answers.text: Check blood glucose frequently, because insulin can cause hypoglycemia after the potassium shifts
Check the temperature hourly for infusion-related fever
Measure urine output every 15 minutes to time the potassium excretion
Monitor the client's pain level as the main indicator of effectiveness

questions.explanation: Insulin drives both potassium and glucose into cells, so delayed hypoglycemia is the key hazard of this temporizing therapy and glucose is checked frequently. The therapy shifts rather than excretes potassium, so urine output and pain do not gauge its effect or its main risk.

questions.question: A 4-year-old sits leaning forward, drooling, with a muffled voice, high fever, and a soft inspiratory stridor. The throat has not been examined. Which action is correct?

answers.text: Use a tongue depressor to look for a swollen epiglottis
Keep the child calm with the parent, do not inspect the throat or place a tongue blade, and summon the airway/anesthesia and provider team for a controlled airway evaluation
Lay the child flat for a throat culture
Give oral fluids to soothe the throat

questions.explanation: Drooling, tripod posture, and stridor in a febrile child suggest acute epiglottitis, where any throat instrumentation can trigger complete obstruction. The airway must be secured by the most skilled team in a controlled setting, with the child kept calm and upright.

california-real-estate.quiz_title: California FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: The primary purpose of the conservation-easement law is:

answers.text: Requires zoning ordinances to be consistent with the general plan
Establishes the Subdivided Lands Law requiring DRE public reports
Authorizes conservation easements for preserving natural and scenic values
Authorizes eminent domain takings for public use with just compensation

questions.explanation: The conservation-easement law authorizes landowners to place conservation easements on property to preserve natural, scenic, and open-space values. Requiring zoning to match a general plan is planning law, the Subdivided Lands Law and its public reports are a separate subdivision statute, and eminent domain is the government's taking power, so those are different laws.

questions.question: Matthew must net $430,000 after a 5.5% commission. The sale price needed is:
questions.explanation: If the seller must keep $430,000 after paying a five and a half percent commission, the price must satisfy ninety-four and a half percent of price equal to $430,000, so the needed sale price is $455,026.46. Simply adding the commission percentage to the net, as the lower figures do, understates the price.

questions.question: Thomas buys 190 front feet for $565,000. The per-front-foot price equals:
questions.explanation: The per-front-foot price is $565,000 divided by 190 front feet, which equals $2,973.68. The other figures divide by the wrong frontage or double-count the stated front feet.

questions.question: A property's value drops from $500,000 to $465,000. The percentage decline is:
questions.explanation: The decline is $500,000 minus $465,000, or $35,000, and $35,000 divided by the original $500,000 value equals seven percent. The other percentages use the new value or an unrelated base and overstate or understate the drop.

questions.question: A biweekly mortgage makes how many half-payments per year:
questions.explanation: A biweekly plan makes a half-payment every two weeks, which is twenty-six half-payments in a fifty-two-week year. That schedule equals thirteen full monthly payments a year, not one, two, or four half-payments.

questions.question: Rent $3,075/month; April has 30 days; seller owned 28 days. The seller's rent proration is:
questions.explanation: April rent is $3,075 for 30 days, or $102.50 per day, and 28 days at that rate equals $2,870 for the seller. The other amounts use fewer days than the seller owned.

questions.question: A tenant is served a 3-day notice on Monday. The notice period generally:

answers.text: Includes the day of service
Starts next month
Is 30 days
Excludes the day of service

questions.explanation: When counting a notice period, the day of service is excluded and counting begins the next day. Including the day of service would shorten the tenant's time, and the period is not 30 days or delayed to next month.

questions.question: Elizabeth's $475,000 loan at 5%; 12 days of prepaid interest (365-day year) equals:
questions.explanation: Prepaid interest is $475,000 multiplied by five percent, divided by three hundred sixty-five days, multiplied by twelve days, which equals $780.82. The smaller and larger figures use the wrong number of days or rate.

questions.question: Which requirement applies under CEQA's trigger?

answers.text: Discretionary government approval
The recorded subdivision creating legal lots
The locality's comprehensive planning blueprint
The entity enforcing CC&Rs and managing common areas

questions.explanation: CEQA review is triggered by a discretionary government approval of a project, the keyed answer. A recorded subdivision map creates legal lots, a general plan is the locality's comprehensive planning blueprint, and a homeowners association enforces CC&Rs; none of those is CEQA's trigger.

questions.question: Which term matches the following: requires a branch license?

answers.text: reasonable accommodation
customer vs client
contingency removal
branch office

questions.explanation: A branch office is the additional licensed location that requires a branch license under California brokerage law. Reasonable accommodation, the customer-versus-client distinction, and contingency removal involve other duties and contract events.

questions.question: An Oxnard property sells for $1,615,000. At 5% commission, the brokerage earns:
questions.explanation: Five percent of $1,615,000 is $80,750, found by multiplying the sale price by 0.05. The other amounts reflect using a lower or higher percentage than the stated commission rate.

questions.question: Which statement about A tenant's repair-and-deduct remedy is correct?

answers.text: The tenant may deduct the full cost of any repair from the rent, even if the cost exceeds several months' rent.
Repairing and deducting cost after the landlord's neglect, within limits
The landlord pays operating expenses
One month's rent, twice in 12 months

questions.explanation: The repair-and-deduct remedy lets a tenant, after proper notice and the landlord's failure to fix a habitability defect, pay for the repair and deduct the cost from rent within statutory limits. The other choices are a stray date, a landlord expense rule, and a bare limit fragment that does not describe the remedy.

pennsylvania-real-estate.quiz_title: Pennsylvania FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Concerning township and range notation, which of the following statements is wrong?

answers.text: 'T3N, R2W' means Township 3 North, Range 2 West.
Township numbers increase with distance from the base line.
Ranges are measured from the Atlantic Ocean.
Range numbers increase with distance from the principal meridian.

questions.explanation: Township and range are measured from a base line and a principal meridian, with range numbers increasing with distance from that meridian. Ranges are not measured from the Atlantic Ocean, so that statement is wrong.

questions.question: Concerning pretermitted heir, which of the following statements is TRUE?

answers.text: A pretermitted heir is a child explicitly disinherited in the will.
A pretermitted heir is a child born or adopted after the will was executed who may claim a share despite being omitted.
Pretermitted heir statutes protect the testator's creditors.
An omitted child has no rights if the will leaves everything to charity.

questions.explanation: A pretermitted heir is a child born or adopted after the will was executed who was omitted and may claim a share despite the omission. Such a child is not one explicitly disinherited, and the protection is for the omitted child, not the testator's creditors or a charity.

questions.question: A pre-licensing class in Altoona covers USPAP. Each of the following is true EXCEPT:

answers.text: Market value assumes a willing buyer and seller, both knowledgeable, acting prudently without undue pressure, with reasonable market exposure.
A higher capitalization rate indicates greater risk and produces a lower indicated value for a given income stream.
The intended use of an appraisal, such as mortgage underwriting, need not be identified so the appraiser can determine the appropriate scope of work.
A state-licensed appraiser has lower transaction-value limits than a certified appraiser.

questions.explanation: The exception is the claim that the intended use need not be identified, because the intended use, such as mortgage underwriting, must be identified so the appraiser can determine the appropriate scope of work. Market value does assume knowledgeable, prudent parties without undue pressure and reasonable exposure, a higher capitalization rate signals greater risk and lowers value for a given income, and licensed appraisers have lower transaction-value limits than certified appraisers.

questions.question: A client asks Devon about governing law. Which of the following answers is correct?

answers.text: It specifies the court and county where any lawsuit over the contract must be filed.
A governing-law clause specifies which state's law controls interpretation of the contract's terms.
It allows either party to assign the contract to a third party without the other party's consent.
It sets the amount of the earnest money deposit the buyer must pay.

questions.explanation: A governing-law clause exists to name which state's law controls how the contract's terms are interpreted. Denying that function leaves the clause with no purpose.

questions.question: A buyer contracts with an agent who was secretly acting for an undisclosed seller-principal. After closing, the buyer discovers the principal's identity. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The buyer may hold either the agent or the discovered principal liable on the contract, but may obtain only one satisfaction
The buyer may collect full damages from both the agent and the principal for the same loss
Discovery of the principal automatically releases the agent and voids the contract
The principal can never be liable because the buyer did not know the principal existed when contracting

questions.explanation: When an undisclosed principal is discovered after contracting, the buyer may elect to hold either the agent or the principal liable on the contract. The buyer gets only one satisfaction, so collecting full damages twice for the same loss is not allowed, and discovery does not void the contract.

questions.question: Concerning property manager's role for Jordan's apartment building, which of the following is NOT true?

answers.text: The property manager acts as the owner's agent for the apartment building.
Market knowledge is irrelevant to managing the apartment building.
Maximizing the apartment building's income while preserving its condition is the manager's goal.
The manager should understand the apartment building's market and applicable laws.

questions.explanation: A property manager acts as the owner's agent, must understand the market and applicable laws, and aims to maximize income while preserving the property's condition. Market knowledge is therefore essential, not irrelevant.

questions.question: In a transaction involving lead paint disclosure, Jamie needs the right rule. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The applicable rule is that buyers of pre-1978 homes get a ten-day opportunity to test for lead-based paint unless they waive it in writing.
Buyers of pre-1978 homes get a twenty-day opportunity to test for lead-based paint unless they waive it in writing.
Buyers of pre-1978 homes get a ten-day opportunity to test for lead-based paint, which they may waive verbally at any time.
sellers of pre-1978 homes get a ten-day opportunity to test for lead-based paint unless they waive it in writing.

questions.explanation: Buyers of pre-1978 homes get a ten-day opportunity to test for lead-based paint unless they waive it in writing. The period is ten days, not twenty, and the testing right belongs to the buyers, not the sellers.

questions.question: An exam candidate is asked about down payment and LTV for Jordan's rectangular lot at 25%. Which of the following is right?

answers.text: LTV plus down payment equals 50% on the rectangular lot.
Lenders use LTV to gauge risk on Jordan's rectangular lot loan.
LTV is value divided by the loan for the rectangular lot.
Lenders ignore LTV on Jordan's rectangular lot.

questions.explanation: Lenders use loan-to-value to gauge the risk of a loan, comparing the loan amount against the property's value. With a twenty-five percent down payment the loan-to-value is seventy-five percent, so the two add to one hundred percent, not fifty, and loan-to-value is loan divided by value rather than the reverse.

questions.question: Monthly rent is $2,065. Using a 30-day month, what is the prorated rent for 15 days of occupancy?
questions.explanation: Divide the monthly rent by thirty days and multiply by fifteen days of occupancy. That gives one half of the monthly rent, or one thousand thirty-two dollars and fifty cents.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about reactivating Casey's vacant lot license is FALSE?

answers.text: An inactive licensee may reactivate the license.
Inactive licenses cannot be reactivated.
Fees apply to a license reactivation.
Reactivation restores full practice authority.

questions.explanation: The false statement is that inactive licenses cannot be reactivated — an inactive licensee may reactivate, paying the applicable fees, and reactivation restores full practice authority. Saying reactivation is impossible contradicts that process.

questions.question: At the initial interview, Maya, a Pennsylvania broker, describes to a consumer the business relationships a broker may have with the consumer and the duties owed in each relationship, as provided for in RELRA. Did Maya comply with the Pennsylvania initial-interview disclosure rule?

answers.text: No. Maya violated the initial-interview disclosure rule.
No. Maya was required to describe only the business relationship she recommended, not each relationship.
The initial-interview disclosure rule does not apply to Maya.
Yes. Maya complied with the Pennsylvania initial-interview disclosure rule.

questions.explanation: Yes, she complied, because the stem states that she did describe the business relationships a broker may have with a consumer and the duties owed in each. That description is exactly what the initial-interview disclosure requires, so the rule does apply and was not breached.

questions.question: On the topic of escrow dispute hold, which of the following is wrong?

answers.text: Retain the money in escrow until the dispute is resolved.
Under the cited rule, the broker must not disburse disputed escrow funds without a court order or the written agreement of the parties.
The rule provides that, if the dispute remains unresolved, the broker may deposit the funds with the court through interpleader.
It is wrong to claim that the money need not be retained in escrow until the dispute is resolved.

questions.explanation: The wrong statement is the one denying that disputed escrow money stays in escrow until the dispute is resolved, because holding the funds untouched is exactly what protects both parties. The other choices all state that hold requirement.

sat.quiz_title: SAT (Digital SAT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: The function f(x) = 1x^2 - 10x + 24 has its vertex at (h, k). What is the value of h?
questions.explanation: For a quadratic in standard form, the vertex's x-coordinate is -b/(2a) = 10/(2) = 5. Using b/(2a) without the negative sign gives -5, the trap option.

questions.question: What is the distance between the points (-4, 2) and (1, 14) in the xy-plane?
questions.explanation: The horizontal change is 5 and the vertical change is 12, so the distance is sqrt(25 + 144) = 13. Adding the changes directly gives 17, the trap value.

questions.question: A bike rental shop charges a flat pickup fee of $15 plus $3 per hour. If a customer's total charge was $36, for how many hours was the customer charged?
questions.explanation: Subtract the one-time fee first: 36 - 15 = 21. Then divide by the rate of 3 per unit: (36 - 15) / 3 = 7. Dividing the whole total by the rate ignores the fee and overstates the answer.

questions.question: The graph of y = g(x) is the graph of y = f(x) shifted 3 units to the left and 6 units down. Which equation defines g?
questions.explanation: A shift left by 3 replaces x with x + 3 inside the function, and a shift down by 6 subtracts 6 outside: g(x) = f(x + 3) - 6. The horizontal replacement moves opposite to the sign students expect, which is the trap in the other options.

questions.question: In a survey of 400 voters, 200 said they support a measure. If the survey is representative, about how many of the 5000 voters in the town would be expected to support the measure?
questions.explanation: The sample proportion is 200/400 = 0.5. Scaling to the town: 0.5 × 5000 = 2500 voters. Reporting the raw count 200 ignores the scaling to the full population.

questions.question:
6x + 2y = 2
2x + 1y = 3

If (x, y) is the solution to the system of equations above, what is the value of x + y?
questions.explanation: The system solves to (-2, 7). Therefore x + y = 5. Stopping at one coordinate, such as -2, is the trap — the question asks for the combination x + y.

questions.question:
The weather service issued a detailed forecast for the regatta on the bay. The starting time _____ depends on the morning fog, which usually lifts by nine when the sea breeze begins to build.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

answers.text: (originally set for eight o'clock)
(originally set for eight o'clock),
(originally set for eight o'clock) —
; originally set for eight o'clock;

questions.explanation: A parenthetical phrase in parentheses is followed directly by the verb depends, with no added punctuation. The comma after the parenthesis is the strongest distractor because it separates subject from verb.

questions.question:
Certain bacteria living in the roots of peas and beans take nitrogen gas from the air, which plants cannot use directly, and convert it into compounds the plants can absorb. In return, the plants supply the bacteria with sugars and a protected home inside root nodules. Farmers value the partnership because it reduces how much nitrogen fertilizer a field needs.

According to the text, what do the bacteria receive from the plants they live in?

answers.text: Nitrogen gas converted from compounds in root nodules
Protection from ladybirds and other insect predators
Fertilizer that farmers apply to the field each season
Sugars and a protected home inside root nodules

questions.explanation: The passage says plants supply sugars and a protected home in root nodules, while usable nitrogen flows from bacteria to plants. Choice A reverses that exchange and misstates the form of nitrogen.

questions.question:
A bakery's croissant sales rose from 160 per day to 200 per day after a price change in the opposite direction of what a manager expected, prompting a review of the data.

By what percentage did daily croissant sales increase?

answers.text: 40 percent
20 percent
25 percent
200 percent

questions.explanation: Sales rose by 200 minus 160, or 40, and 40 divided by the original 160 is 0.25, or a 25 percent increase. Choice A mistakes the increase of 40 croissants for a percentage without dividing by the starting sales.

questions.question:
A flock of geese landed on the pond just before sunset last night. Their honking echoed across the water as they settled for the evening. Soon the geese were drifting quietly, _____ heads tucked beneath their wings.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

answers.text: there
they're
them
their

questions.explanation: The possessive adjective 'their' modifies 'heads' and refers to the geese; 'they're' fails because 'they are heads tucked' does not make grammatical sense in this clause.

questions.question:
Text 1: Mandatory voting raises turnout, and high turnout makes election results more representative. Countries that require citizens to vote, with small fines for abstaining, routinely see participation above ninety percent.

Text 2: Turnout purchased with fines is a hollow victory. A ballot cast to avoid a penalty expresses no judgment about the candidates, and a democracy should want engaged citizens, not merely counted ones.

Based on the texts, what is the central disagreement between the authors?

answers.text: Whether fines for abstaining are usually large or small
Whether other countries have ever tried mandatory voting
Whether high turnout achieved by compulsion is a genuine democratic good
Whether election results are announced on the same day as voting

questions.explanation: Text 1 treats compelled high turnout as more representative while Text 2 calls it hollow, a direct clash over its value. Choice A focuses on fine size, which neither author treats as the heart of the issue.

questions.question:
The survey uncovered a significant change in commuting habits. Within five years, the share of residents cycling to work had tripled, a shift large enough to prompt the city to redesign several major intersections.

Based on the passage, 'significant' most nearly means
